  [NormedSpace ℝ X] {A : ApproximationScheme X} {s₀ s₁ η : ℝ} {q q₀ q₁ : ℝ≥0∞} (hs₀ : 0 < s₀)

**The reiteration theorem for approximation spaces** (DeVore–Lorentz, Chapter 7; Pietsch
1981; DeVore–Popov, LNM 1302 (1988)): for `0 < s₀ < s₁`, `0 < η < 1` and `1 ≤ q₀, q₁, q ≤ ∞`,
`(A^{s₀}_{q₀}, A^{s₁}_{q₁})_{η,q} = A^{(1-η)s₀+ηs₁}_q`.  The proof represents both spaces in the
couple `(X, A^r_∞)` with `r = s₁ + 1` and applies `InterpCouple.memKMethod_kCouple_iff`.

**Approximation spaces are interpolation spaces** (Pietsch 1981; DeVore–Popov, LNM 1302
(1988)): for every scheme, `0 < s < r` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `A^s_q = (X, A^r_∞)_{s/r,q}`, the real
interpolation space of the continuous K-method of the couple `(X, A^r_∞)`.

`A 0 ⊆ A 1 ⊆ ⋯` in a real normed space, starting with `A 0 = {0}`, closed under real
multiples, and with `A m + A n ⊆ A (m + n)`.

  {Y : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [NormedAddCommGroup Y] [NormedSpace ℝ Y]
  {ι : Y →L[ℝ] X} {A : ApproximationScheme X} {α C s : ℝ} {q : ℝ≥0∞} [CompleteSpace Y]
  (hι : Function.Injective ⇑ι) (hN : ApproximationScheme.LiftBound ι A α C) (hC : 0 ≤ C)
  (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hαs : α < s) (hq : 1 ≤ q) {f : X} (hf : A.MemApprox s q f) :
  ∃ y,
    ι y = f ∧
      (A.comap (↑ι) hι).approxNormDyadic (s - α) q y ≤
        ApproximationScheme.nikolskiiConst C α s * A.approxNormDyadic s q f

inequality of exponent `α` for `A`, `0 ≤ α < s` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, every `f ∈ A^s_q(X)` is

is the scheme `ι⁻¹(A n)` in `Y`.

nodes.title: A^s_q is a real interpolation space

lean.name: ApproximationScheme.memApprox_iff_memInterp_of_jacksonBound_of_liftBound
lean.docstring:
**The representation theorem**: under Jackson's and Bernstein's inequalities of order `r`
and for `0 < s < r`, `f ∈ A^s_q` if and only if `f ∈ (X, Y)_{s/r,q}`, the real interpolation
space of the discrete K-method on the grid `t = 2^(-kr)`.

lean.name: FunctionScheme.MemBesov.exists_boundedContinuous_of_nikolskii
lean.docstring:
**Embedding into bounded continuous functions**, for `0 < p ≤ ∞` and `0 < q ≤ ∞`: if `Ω` is
a topological space with its Borel `σ`-algebra, `μ` charges every nonempty open set, the scheme
has continuous approximants and the Nikolskii bound of dimension `D ≥ 0` at `p`
(`FunctionScheme.HasNikolskiiAt`), for instance the Nikolskii property, and `s > D/p`, every
`f ∈ B^s_{p,q}` has a bounded continuous representative. The class `g ∈ L_∞` of
`FunctionScheme.MemBesov.exists_inclusion_eq_top` lies in `B^{s - D/p}_{∞,∞}`
(`FunctionScheme.MemBesov.mono`), the approximation space of `S` in `L_∞`
(`FunctionScheme.memBesov_iff_memApprox`), so it is a limit of approximants
(`ApproximationScheme.mem_closure_iUnion_of_memApprox`); these are classes of bounded continuous
functions, which form a closed subset of `L_∞`
(`BoundedContinuousFunction.isClosed_range_toLp_top`).

lean.signature:
theorem FunctionScheme.MemBesov.exists_inclusion_eq_of_nikolskii.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {S : FunctionScheme μ} {D : ℝ} {p r : ℝ≥0∞} {s : ℝ} {q : ℝ≥0∞}
  (h : S.HasNikolskiiAt D p) (hD : 0 ≤ D) (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hpr : p ≤ r)
  (hs : nikolskiiExponent D p r < s) (hq0 : q ≠ 0) {f : ↥(Lp ℂ p μ)} (hf : S.MemBesov p s q f) :
  ∃ g, (Lp.inclusionOfExponentLeLinear μ hpr) g = f ∧ S.MemBesov r (s - nikolskiiExponent D p r) q g
lean.name: FunctionScheme.MemBesov.exists_inclusion_eq_of_nikolskii
lean.docstring:
**The Besov embedding** `B^s_{p,q} ↪ B^{s - α}_{r,q}`, `α = D(1/p - 1/r)`, for
`0 < p ≤ r ≤ ∞`, `0 < q ≤ ∞` and `s > α`, for a scheme with the Nikolskii bound of
dimension `D ≥ 0` at the source exponent `p` (`FunctionScheme.HasNikolskiiAt`), for instance a
scheme with the Nikolskii property: every `f ∈ B^s_{p,q}` is the inclusion of some `g ∈ L_r`
lying in `B^{s - α}_{r,q}`. Since `s > α ≥ 0`, membership in both Besov spaces is the finiteness
of the dyadic norms of the couples (`FunctionScheme.memBesov_iff_eNormDyadic_lt_top`), which the
norm bound `FunctionScheme.exists_uniform_inclusion_eq_of_nikolskii` compares.

lean.name: FunctionScheme.memKMethod_besovCouple_iff
lean.docstring:
**Besov spaces interpolate**: for every scheme of functions, every exponent `p`,
`0 < s₀ < s₁`, `0 < η < 1` and `1 ≤ q₀, q₁, q ≤ ∞`,
`(B^{s₀}_{p,q₀}, B^{s₁}_{p,q₁})_{η,q} = B^{(1-η)s₀+ηs₁}_{p,q}`: the reiteration theorem for
E-spaces (`InterpCouple.memKMethod_eCouple_iff`) for the couple of `S` in `L_p`, which is
quasi-normed with subadditive complexity (`FunctionScheme.isQuasiNormed_lpCouple`,
`FunctionScheme.lpCouple_norm1_add_le`), and the description of the Besov space by the dyadic
norm (`FunctionScheme.memBesov_iff_eNormDyadic_lt_top`). For the classical Besov spaces this is
DeVore–Popov, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 305 (1988), Corollary 6.2, which holds for every fine
index.

  [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {S : FunctionScheme μ} {p : ℝ≥0∞} {s₁ η : ℝ} {q q₁ : ℝ≥0∞} (hs₁ : 0 < s₁)
  (hη : 0 < η) (hη' : η < 1) (hq₁ : q₁ ≠ 0) (hq : q ≠ 0) {f : ↥(Lp ℂ p μ)} :
  (S.lpBesovCouple p s₁ q₁).MemKMethod η q f ↔ S.MemBesov p (η * s₁) q f
lean.name: FunctionScheme.memKMethod_lpBesovCouple_iff
lean.docstring:
**`L_p` and a Besov space interpolate**: for every scheme of functions, every exponent `p`,
`s₁ > 0`, `0 < η < 1` and `0 < q₁, q ≤ ∞`, `(L_p, B^{s₁}_{p,q₁})_{η,q} = B^{ηs₁}_{p,q}`: the
representation of E-spaces as interpolation spaces (`InterpCouple.memKMethod_leftECouple_iff`)
for the couple of `S` in `L_p`, and the description of the Besov space by the dyadic norm
(`FunctionScheme.memBesov_iff_eNormDyadic_lt_top`).

lean.signature:
structure FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
  (S : FunctionScheme μ) (D : ℝ) : Prop where
  exists_const : ∀ (p : ℝ≥0∞),
  1 ≤ p →
    ∃ C,
      0 ≤ C ∧
        ∀ (n : ℕ),
          1 ≤ n →
            ∀ a ∈ S.sets n,
              (eLpNorm ↑↑a ∞ μ).toReal ≤ C * ↑n ^ (D * p.toReal⁻¹) * (eLpNorm (↑↑a) p μ).toReal
lean.name: FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii
lean.docstring:
The **Nikolskii property of dimension `D`**: for every `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`,
`‖a‖_∞ ≤ C n^(D/p) ‖a‖_p` for all approximants `a ∈ S n`, `n ≥ 1`, with the norm `‖a‖_∞` of the
class `a` in `L_∞(μ)`. A hypothesis on the scheme; the trigonometric polynomials on the torus
(`Torus.trigScheme_hasNikolskii`) and the dyadic step functions on `[0, 1)`
(`Haar.hasNikolskii_haarScheme`) have it. The property asks `p ≥ 1` only, since the bound at
`p = 1` gives the bound for every `0 < p < 1`
(`FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii.exists_eLpNorm_top_le`). It is meant for a finite measure, where
all the quasi-norms are finite; on an infinite measure the real form forces every approximant to
lie in every `L_p`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`: if `‖a‖_p = ∞`, then `(‖a‖_p).toReal = 0`, so `‖a‖_∞ = 0`, and
then `a = 0` and `‖a‖_p = 0`.

lean.name: FunctionScheme.SobolevSpace

A **Sobolev space** inside `L_p(μ)` for the scheme `S`: a smoothness space for `S` in
`L_p(μ)`, that is, a normed space `W` with an injective bounded linear map into `L_p(μ)` and
Jackson's and Bernstein's inequalities of some order. It is a hypothesis structure; the instances
are `Torus.periodicSobolevSpace` and `ContinuousSpectralBasis.sobolevSpace`, both for `p = 2`.

**The Besov embedding into `L_r`**: for `1 ≤ p ≤ r ≤ ∞`, `p < ∞`,
`s > α = n(1/p - 1/r)`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and `f ∈ B^s_{p,q}` (band-limited approximation in `L_p`),

`‖g‖_r ≤ K_{V,p,r,s} ‖(2^(js) ‖Δ_j f‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`. The blocks lie in `L_r`, their series
converges absolutely in `L_r` (`Rd.tsum_eLpNorm_blockFun_le`), its sum `g` is the almost
everywhere limit of the series (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Lp.hasSum_coeFn_tsum`), and so is `f`
(`Rd.ae_hasSum_blockFun`).

`Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_zero_two_le` and `Rd.enorm_le_triebelLizorkinNorm_zero_two`.

theorem Rd.memTriebelLizorkin_iff_atomic.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V] {p : ℝ≥0∞} [Fact (1 ≤ p)] (hp1 : 1 < p)
  (hp : p ≠ ∞) {q : ℝ≥0∞} (hq1 : 1 < q) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) {L : ℕ} (hsL : s < ↑L)
  (F : ↥(Lp ℂ p volume)) :
  Rd.MemTriebelLizorkin s q F ↔
    ∃ d A coef a f,
      0 ≤ d ∧
        (∀ (j : ℕ) (m : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ V) → ℤ),
            Rd.IsSmoothAtom Set.univ L d A j (Rd.cellCenter j m) (a j m)) ∧
          (∀ (j : ℕ),
              ∀ᵐ (x : V), ↑↑(f j) x = ∑' (m : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ V) → ℤ), coef j m * a j m x) ∧

              Rd.tlCoeffNorm p s q coef < ∞

lean.docstring:
**The atomic characterisation of Triebel–Lizorkin spaces** for `1 < p < ∞`, `1 < q ≤ ∞`
and `s > 0`, with atoms normalised in `L_∞` and the weights `2^(js)` in `f^s_{p,q}`; for `s > 0`
the atoms carry no moment conditions. Triebel, *Theory of Function Spaces II*, states it with
`(s,p)`-atoms normalised in `L_p`; the coefficients `λ_{j,m}` here correspond to his
coefficients `2^(j(s - n/p)) λ_{j,m}`, `n = dim V`. For an order `L` with `0 < s < L`,
`F ∈ F^s_{p,q}` iff `F = ∑_j f_j` in `L_p` with `f_j = ∑_m λ_{j,m} a_{j,m}` almost everywhere for
smooth atoms `a_{j,m}` on `V` of level `j` and order `L` centred at the cells, with a common
radius factor `d ≥ 0` and constant `A`, and `‖λ‖_{f^s_{p,q}} < ∞`. The atoms of `F` are the cell
atoms of `η_j ⋆ (k_j ⋆ F)` (`Rd.LocalMeansBump.tl_atomic_decomposition`); the converse is the
synthesis `Rd.LocalMeansBump.tlLocalMeansNorm_le_tlCoeffNorm`. The Besov analogue is
`Rd.LocalMeansBump.besov_iff_atomic`.

nodes.title: Sobolev space H^s(Ω) on an open set

the orthogonal complement in `H^s(V)` of the elements vanishing on `Ω`. It is isometric to the
quotient of `H^s(V)` by them (`Rd.quotientEquivRestrictionSpace`), so its norm is the infimum
of the norms of all extensions (`Rd.norm_restrictProj_le_of_mem`,
`Rd.exists_norm_restrictProj_eq`); this is the space `H^s(Ω)` of Chandler-Wilde, Hewett and
Moiola (§3.1.4) and of McLean (Chapter 3).

`dim V = n`: the `(n-1)`-dimensional Hausdorff measure restricted to `Γ`, normalised as Mathlib's
`μHE[n-1]`, so that it is the volume on hyperplanes. In each chart it is the measure with density
`√(1 + ‖∇φ_j‖²)` on the hyperplane
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_surfaceMeasure_of_support`).

theorem Torus.periodic_memKMethod_modCouple_iff.{u_1} {d : Type u_1} [Fintype d] {p : ℝ≥0∞} [Fact (1 ≤ p)]
  {s₀ s₁ η : ℝ} {q₀ q₁ q : ℝ≥0∞} (hp : p ≠ ∞) {r : ℕ} (hs₀ : 0 < s₀) (hs : s₀ < s₁) (hs₁ : s₁ < ↑r)
  (hη : 0 < η) (hη' : η < 1) (hq₀ : 1 ≤ q₀) (hq₁ : 1 ≤ q₁) (hq : 1 ≤ q) {f : ↥(Lp ℂ p volume)} :
  ((Torus.trigLpModulusData d hp r).modCouple s₀ q₀ s₁ q₁).MemKMethod η q f ↔
    (‖f‖ₑ + q.lqNorm fun k ↦ dyadicWeight ((1 - η) * s₀ + η * s₁) k * Rd.lpModulus p r f k) < ∞
lean.name: Torus.periodic_memKMethod_modCouple_iff
lean.docstring:
**Besov spaces on the torus by differences interpolate**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, an order `r`,
`0 < s₀ < s₁ < r`, `0 < η < 1` and `1 ≤ q₀, q₁, q ≤ ∞`, `f ∈ L_p(𝕋^d)` lies in the real
interpolation space of the couple of the quasi-norms
`‖f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks_i) ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_{q_i}}` iff
`‖f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞` with `s = (1-η)s₀ + ηs₁`.

lean.name: Torus.memBesov_iff_periodicLittlewoodPaleyNorm_lt_top
lean.docstring:
**Besov spaces on the torus by Littlewood–Paley blocks**: for every `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `s > 0` and
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `f ∈ B^s_{p,q}(𝕋^d)` (the approximation space of the trigonometric polynomials in
`L_p`) iff `(2^(js) ‖ψ_j ⋆ f‖_p)_j ∈ ℓ_q`.

lean.signature:
theorem Torus.memBesov_iff_modNorm_lt_top_lp.{u_1} {d : Type u_1} [Fintype d] {p : ℝ≥0∞} [Fact (1 ≤ p)]
  (hp : p ≠ ∞) {r : ℕ} {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hsr : s < ↑r) {q : ℝ≥0∞} (hq : 1 ≤ q)
  (f : ↥(Lp ℂ p volume)) :
  (Torus.trigScheme d).MemBesov p s q f ↔
    (‖f‖ₑ + q.lqNorm fun k ↦ dyadicWeight s k * Rd.lpModulus p r f k) < ∞
lean.name: Torus.memBesov_iff_modNorm_lt_top_lp
lean.docstring:
**Besov spaces on the torus by moduli of smoothness, for all `1 ≤ p < ∞`**: for `0 < s < r`
and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `f ∈ B^s_{p,q}(𝕋^d)` (the approximation space of the trigonometric
polynomials in `L_p`) iff `‖f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`.

lean.signature:
theorem Torus.trigScheme_hasNikolskii.{u_1} {d : Type u_1} [Fintype d] :
  (Torus.trigScheme d).HasNikolskii ↑(Fintype.card d)
lean.name: Torus.trigScheme_hasNikolskii
lean.docstring:
**The trigonometric polynomials have the Nikolskii property of dimension `d`**: the sup-norm
bound of `Torus.norm_le_rpow_mul_eLpNorm` for the uniform trigonometric scheme, passed to its
scheme of functions by `FunctionScheme.hasNikolskii_ofContinuous`.

lean.signature:
theorem Torus.norm_le_rpow_mul_eLpNorm.{u_1} {d : Type u_1} [Fintype d] {n : ℕ} {T : UnitAddTorus d →ᵇ ℂ}
  (hT : T ∈ Torus.trigPoly d n) {p : ℝ≥0∞} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (hp' : p ≠ ∞) :
  ‖T‖ ≤
    (2 * ↑⌈p.toReal / 2⌉₊) ^ (↑(Fintype.card d) * p.toReal⁻¹) *
        ↑n ^ (↑(Fintype.card d) * p.toReal⁻¹) *
      (eLpNorm (⇑T) p volume).toReal
lean.name: Torus.norm_le_rpow_mul_eLpNorm
lean.docstring:
**The Nikolskii inequality** for trigonometric polynomials: for `T` of degree `< n` and
`1 ≤ p < ∞`, `‖T‖_∞ ≤ (2⌈p/2⌉)^(d/p) n^(d/p) ‖T‖_p`.

lean.name: Torus.memPeriodicTriebelLizorkin_iff_memBesov
lean.docstring:
**`F^s_{p,p}(𝕋^d) = B^s_{p,p}(𝕋^d)`**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `s > 0`, `f ∈ F^s_{p,p}` iff `f`
lies in the Besov space `B^s_{p,p}(𝕋^d)`, the approximation space of the trigonometric
polynomials.

lean.signature: def Torus.trigPoly.{u_1} (d : Type u_1) [Fintype d] (n : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ (UnitAddTorus d →ᵇ ℂ)
lean.name: Torus.trigPoly
lean.docstring: The **trigonometric polynomials of degree `< n`**, `span_ℂ {e_k : deg k < n}`.

one_le_of_nikolskiiExponent_lt.name: one_le_of_nikolskiiExponent_lt
one_le_of_nikolskiiExponent_lt.docstring:
A natural number `m` above the Nikolskii exponent is at least `1`: for `D ≥ 0`,
`0 < p ≤ r ≤ ∞` and `m ∈ ℕ` with `m > D(1/p - 1/r)`, `m ≥ 1`, since the exponent is
nonnegative (`nikolskiiExponent_nonneg`).

ofReal_two_rpow_half_mul_self.name: ofReal_two_rpow_half_mul_self
ofReal_two_rpow_half_mul_self.docstring:
**The square of the normalising factor**: `2^(j/2) · 2^(j/2) = 2^j` for every `j ∈ ℕ`, as
complex numbers (Mathlib's `Real.rpow_add` and `add_halves`).

nikolskiiExponent_nonneg.name: nikolskiiExponent_nonneg
nikolskiiExponent_nonneg.docstring:
`D(1/p - 1/r) ≥ 0` for `D ≥ 0` and `0 < p ≤ r ≤ ∞`, since then `1/r ≤ 1/p`
(`ENNReal.one_div_toReal_sub_one_div_toReal_nonneg`).

nikolskiiExponent_eq_mul_one_sub_div.name: nikolskiiExponent_eq_mul_one_sub_div
nikolskiiExponent_eq_mul_one_sub_div.docstring:
**The Nikolskii exponent as an interpolated exponent**: for `0 < p ≤ r ≤ ∞`,
`D(1/p - 1/r) = (D/p)(1 - p/r)`, with `1/∞ = 0` and `p/∞ = 0`. This is the exponent of `n` that
interpolation between `L_p` and `L_∞` produces from a bound `‖a‖_∞ ≤ C n^(D/p) ‖a‖_p`.

nikolskiiExponent.name: nikolskiiExponent
nikolskiiExponent.docstring:
The **Nikolskii exponent** `D (1/p - 1/r)`.  With `1/∞ = 0` (in Lean `∞.toReal = 0` and
`0⁻¹ = 0`) it is `D/p` for `r = ∞`.

intervalIntegral.hasFDerivAt_integral_of.name: intervalIntegral.hasFDerivAt_integral_of_contDiff
intervalIntegral.hasFDerivAt_integral_of.docstring:
**Differentiation under the integral sign** for a jointly `C^1` integrand: if
`(x, t) ↦ F x t` is `C^1` on `H × ℝ`, then `x ↦ ∫_a^b F x t dt` has the derivative
`∫_a^b D_x F x₀ t dt` at every `x₀`. The partial derivative is bounded on the compact set
`B̄(x₀, 1) × [a, b]`, so Mathlib's `intervalIntegral.hasFDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_of_fderiv_le`
applies.

intervalIntegral.fderiv_integral_apply_o.name: intervalIntegral.fderiv_integral_apply_of_contDiff
intervalIntegral.fderiv_integral_apply_o.docstring:
**The derivative of a parametric integral, applied to a vector**: for a jointly `C^1`
integrand, `D(∫_a^b F(·, t) dt)(x) v = ∫_a^b D_x F(x, t) v dt`
(`intervalIntegral.hasFDerivAt_integral_of_contDiff` and Mathlib's
`ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_apply`).

intervalIntegral.continuous_fderiv_fst_o.name: intervalIntegral.continuous_fderiv_fst_of_contDiff
intervalIntegral.continuous_fderiv_fst_o.docstring: The partial derivative `(x, t) ↦ D_x F(x, t)` of a jointly `C^1` integrand is continuous.

intervalIntegral.contDiff_parametric_int.name: intervalIntegral.contDiff_parametric_intervalIntegral_of_contDiff_aux
intervalIntegral.contDiff_parametric_int.docstring:
Smoothness of parametric integrals with values in a space of the universe of `H` or above,
by induction on the order: the derivative of `x ↦ ∫_a^b F x t dt` is again a parametric integral
of a smooth integrand (`intervalIntegral.hasFDerivAt_integral_of_contDiff`).

intervalIntegral.contDiff_parametric_int.name: intervalIntegral.contDiff_parametric_intervalIntegral_of_contDiff
intervalIntegral.contDiff_parametric_int.docstring:
**Smoothness of parametric integrals**: if `(x, t) ↦ F x t` is smooth on `H × ℝ`, `H` finite
dimensional, then `x ↦ ∫_a^b F x t dt` is smooth. Mathlib has the derivative under the integral
sign (`intervalIntegral.hasFDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_of_fderiv_le`) and the continuity
(`intervalIntegral.continuous_parametric_intervalIntegral_of_continuous'`); the induction on the
order runs in one universe
(`intervalIntegral.contDiff_parametric_intervalIntegral_of_contDiff_aux`), reached through
`ULift`.

enorm_two_rpow_half.name: enorm_two_rpow_half
enorm_two_rpow_half.docstring:
**The normalising factor in extended norm**: `‖2^(j/2)‖ = 2^(j/2)` for every `j ∈ ℕ`, written
as the dyadic weight `ENNReal.dyadicWeight (1/2) j`.

enorm_sum_mul_sq_le.name: enorm_sum_mul_sq_le
enorm_sum_mul_sq_le.docstring:
**The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for finite sums of products**:
`|∑_{j ∈ s} a_j b_j|² ≤ (∑_{j ∈ s} |a_j|²) (∑_{j ∈ s} |b_j|²)` in every seminormed ring, such
as `ℂ`, with values in `[0, ∞]` (Mathlib's `Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq` for the norms, after
the triangle inequality and `‖a b‖ ≤ ‖a‖ ‖b‖`).

TranslationAlgebra.translHom.name: TranslationAlgebra.translHom
TranslationAlgebra.translHom.docstring: The translations form a monoid homomorphism from `G`, written multiplicatively.

TranslationAlgebra.transl.name: TranslationAlgebra.transl
TranslationAlgebra.transl.docstring: The **translation** `τ_v f(x) = f(x + v)`, a linear map of functions on `G`.

TranslationAlgebra.sum_letterCount.name: TranslationAlgebra.sum_letterCount
TranslationAlgebra.sum_letterCount.docstring: The multiplicities of a word add up to its length.

TranslationAlgebra.single_sub_one_pow_eq.name: TranslationAlgebra.single_sub_one_pow_eq_sum
TranslationAlgebra.single_sub_one_pow_eq.docstring:
**The expansion in the translation algebra**:
`(δ_h - 1)^r = ∑_α δ_{s_α} ∏_i (δ_{h_i e_i} - 1)^{m_i(α)}`, summed over the words
`α : Fin r → Fin d`.

TranslationAlgebra.single_sub_one_eq_sum.name: TranslationAlgebra.single_sub_one_eq_sum
TranslationAlgebra.single_sub_one_eq_sum.docstring:
**The first-order telescoping**: `δ_h - 1 = ∑_i (δ_{h_i e_i} - 1) δ_{∑_{j<i} h_j e_j}`
(Mathlib's `Finset.prod_add_ordered` for `∏_i (1 + (δ_{h_i e_i} - 1))`).

TranslationAlgebra.shiftVec_apply.name: TranslationAlgebra.shiftVec_apply
TranslationAlgebra.shiftVec_apply.docstring: The coordinates of the shift: `(s_α)_c = #{l : c < α_l} h_c`.

TranslationAlgebra.shiftVec.name: TranslationAlgebra.shiftVec
TranslationAlgebra.shiftVec.docstring: The shift `s_α = ∑_l ∑_{j < α_l} h_j e_j` of the term of a word `α`.

TranslationAlgebra.prod_lt_single.name: TranslationAlgebra.prod_lt_single
TranslationAlgebra.prod_lt_single.docstring: The lower products: `∏_{j < i} δ_{h_j e_j} = δ_{∑_{j<i} h_j e_j}`.

TranslationAlgebra.letterCount.name: TranslationAlgebra.letterCount
TranslationAlgebra.letterCount.docstring: The multiplicities `m_i(α) = #{l : α_l = i}` of a word `α : Fin r → Fin d`.

TranslationAlgebra.higherDiff_eq_diffAct.name: TranslationAlgebra.higherDiff_eq_diffAct
TranslationAlgebra.higherDiff_eq_diffAct.docstring: **The difference is a power in the translation algebra**: `Δ_h^r = (δ_h - 1)^r`.

TranslationAlgebra.diffAct.name: TranslationAlgebra.diffAct
TranslationAlgebra.diffAct.docstring:
The **action of the translation algebra** `ℂ[G]` on functions on `G`: `δ_v` acts by the
translation `τ_v` (Mathlib's `AddMonoidAlgebra.lift`).

TranslationAlgebra.coordElem.name: TranslationAlgebra.coordElem
TranslationAlgebra.coordElem.docstring:
The element `δ_{h_i e_i} - 1` of the translation algebra, the first difference in
coordinate `i`.

TranslationAlgebra.card_lt_add_letterCou.name: TranslationAlgebra.card_lt_add_letterCount_le
TranslationAlgebra.card_lt_add_letterCou.docstring:
The shift and the multiplicity of a coordinate add up to at most the length of the word:
`#{l : c < α_l} + #{l : α_l = c} ≤ r`.

TorusHaar.isProbabilityMeasure.name: TorusHaar.isProbabilityMeasure
TorusHaar.isProbabilityMeasure.docstring: The normalised Haar measure on the circle is a probability measure.

TorusHaar.isAddHaarMeasure.name: TorusHaar.isAddHaarMeasure
TorusHaar.isAddHaarMeasure.docstring: The normalised Haar measure on the circle is a Haar measure.

Torus.uniformTrigScheme.name: Torus.uniformTrigScheme
Torus.uniformTrigScheme.docstring:
The **uniform trigonometric scheme** on `𝕋^d`: the trigonometric polynomials of degree `< n`,
`n ∈ ℕ`, form an approximation scheme in the bounded continuous functions with the sup norm.

Torus.trigScheme.name: Torus.trigScheme
Torus.trigScheme.docstring:
The **trigonometric scheme** on `𝕋^d`, the scheme of functions of the uniform trigonometric
scheme: `trigScheme d n` consists of the classes in `L_∞(𝕋^d)` of the trigonometric polynomials
of degree `< n`.

Torus.trigPoly_zero.name: Torus.trigPoly_zero
Torus.trigPoly_zero.docstring: There are no nonzero trigonometric polynomials of degree `< 0`.

Torus.trigPoly_mul_le.name: Torus.trigPoly_mul_le
Torus.trigPoly_mul_le.docstring: **Products of trigonometric polynomials**: degrees `< m` and `< n` give degree `< m + n`.

Torus.trigPoly_mono.name: Torus.trigPoly_mono
Torus.trigPoly_mono.docstring: The spaces of trigonometric polynomials increase with the degree.

Torus.trigPolyLp_eq_span.name: Torus.trigPolyLp_eq_span
Torus.trigPolyLp_eq_span.docstring:
The trigonometric polynomials of degree `< n` in `L_p(𝕋)` are spanned by the characters
`e_m`, `deg m < n`.

Torus.trigPolyLp.name: Torus.trigPolyLp
Torus.trigPolyLp.docstring: The **trigonometric polynomials of degree `< n` in `L_p(𝕋)`**.

Torus.trigMonomial.name: Torus.trigMonomial
Torus.trigMonomial.docstring:
The **trigonometric monomial** `e_k(x) = exp(2πi ⟨k, x⟩)`, as a bounded continuous
function on the torus.

Torus.trigLpModulusData.name: Torus.trigLpModulusData
Torus.trigLpModulusData.docstring:
**The modulus of order `r` is compatible with the trigonometric polynomials in `L_p(𝕋^d)`**,
with inverse order `r`: Jackson's inequality from level `1` on, and the inverse inequality.

Torus.trigDeg_le_norm_latticeVec.name: Torus.trigDeg_le_norm_latticeVec
Torus.trigDeg_le_norm_latticeVec.docstring: **The degree is at most the norm**: `max_i |m_i| ≤ ‖m‖`.

Torus.trigDeg_le_iff.name: Torus.trigDeg_le_iff
Torus.trigDeg_le_iff.docstring: `deg k ≤ n` iff `|k_i| ≤ n` for every `i`.

Torus.trigDeg.name: Torus.trigDeg
Torus.trigDeg.docstring: The **degree** `deg k = max_i |k_i|` of a frequency `k ∈ ℤ^d`.

Torus.tendsto_sum_periodicLpBlock.name: Torus.tendsto_sum_periodicLpBlock
Torus.tendsto_sum_periodicLpBlock.docstring:
**Reconstruction**: the partial sums of the blocks converge to `f` in `L_p(𝕋^d)`, since
`Φ_J ⋆ f → f` (`Torus.tendsto_periodicEconvLp_dilatedLpKernel`).

Torus.tendsto_periodicEconvLp_of_fourier.name: Torus.tendsto_periodicEconvLp_of_fourier
Torus.tendsto_periodicEconvLp_of_fourier.docstring:
**Approximate identities on the torus**: let `Φ_i` be integrable kernels on `ℝ^d` with
`∫ |Φ_i| ≤ C < ∞` and `𝓕Φ_i(m) → 1` for every lattice point `m`. Then `Φ_i ⋆ f → f` in
`L_p(𝕋^d)` for every `f`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`. The `f` with `Φ_i ⋆ f → f` form a subspace that contains
every character; it is closed since the operators are uniformly bounded, hence equicontinuous
(Mathlib's `Equicontinuous.isClosed_setOfPred_tendsto`), and the characters span a dense
subspace.

Torus.tendsto_periodicEconvLp_dilatedLpK.name: Torus.tendsto_periodicEconvLp_dilatedLpKernel
Torus.tendsto_periodicEconvLp_dilatedLpK.docstring:
**The Littlewood–Paley kernels are an approximate identity on the torus**: `Φ_J ⋆ f → f`
in `L_p(𝕋^d)` as `J → ∞`, for `1 ≤ p < ∞`.

Torus.tendsto_periodicEconvLp_dilate.name: Torus.tendsto_periodicEconvLp_dilate
Torus.tendsto_periodicEconvLp_dilate.docstring:
**Dilations are approximate identities on the torus**: for an integrable kernel `K` on `ℝ^d`
with `∫ K = 1` and scales `c_i > 0` with `c_i → ∞` along a filter, `K_{c_i} ⋆ f → f` in
`L_p(𝕋^d)`. The Fourier transforms `𝓕K_{c_i}(m) = 𝓕K(m / c_i)` tend to `𝓕K(0) = ∫ K = 1`, and
`‖K_{c_i}‖_1 = ‖K‖_1`.

Torus.sum_periodicLpBlock.name: Torus.sum_periodicLpBlock
Torus.sum_periodicLpBlock.docstring: **The blocks telescope**: `∑_{j ≤ J} Δ_j f = Φ_J ⋆ f`.

Torus.quotientProj.name: Torus.quotientProj
Torus.quotientProj.docstring: The **quotient map** `π : ℝ^d → 𝕋^d`, `π x = (x_i mod 1)_i`.

Torus.pow_mem_trigPoly.name: Torus.pow_mem_trigPoly
Torus.pow_mem_trigPoly.docstring:
**Powers of trigonometric polynomials**: `T` of degree `< n` gives `T^(m+1)` of degree
`< (m+1) n`.

Torus.periodic_smoothnessModulus_nat_mul.name: Torus.periodic_smoothnessModulus_nat_mul_le
Torus.periodic_smoothnessModulus_nat_mul.docstring:
**Scaling the modulus of order `r`**: `ω_r(f, m t)_p ≤ m^r ω_r(f, t)_p` on the torus for
`m ≥ 1` and `1 ≤ p`, since every `h` with `‖h‖ ≤ m t` is `m h'` with `‖h'‖ ≤ t`
(`Torus.exists_coe_eq_abs_eq_norm`, `Rd.smoothnessModulus_nat_mul_le_of_forall_exists_nsmul`).

Torus.periodic_smoothnessModulus_mul_le.name: Torus.periodic_smoothnessModulus_mul_le
Torus.periodic_smoothnessModulus_mul_le.docstring:
**The modulus of order `r` grows polynomially**: `ω_r(f, c t)_p ≤ (1 + c)^r ω_r(f, t)_p` on the
torus for `c, t ≥ 0` (`Torus.periodic_smoothnessModulus_nat_mul_le`,
`Rd.smoothnessModulus_mul_le_of_nat_mul_le`).

Torus.periodic_norm_toLp_sum_sq.name: Torus.periodic_norm_toLp_sum_sq
Torus.periodic_norm_toLp_sum_sq.docstring:
**Parseval for trigonometric polynomials**: `‖∑ c_k e_k‖_2² = ∑ |c_k|²` (Mathlib's
`OrthogonalFamily.norm_sum` for the orthonormal characters).

Torus.periodic_ae_integrable_dilate_mul.name: Torus.periodic_ae_integrable_dilate_mul
Torus.periodic_ae_integrable_dilate_mul.docstring:
**The averaged translates are integrable**: for integrable `Φ`, `f ∈ L_1(𝕋)`, `c > 0` and
almost every `t`, `z ↦ Φ(z) f(t - π(c^(-1) z))` is integrable.

Torus.periodicTriebelLizorkinNorm_eq_per.name: Torus.periodicTriebelLizorkinNorm_eq_periodicLittlewoodPaleyNorm
Torus.periodicTriebelLizorkinNorm_eq_per.docstring:
**For `q = p` the two quasi-norms agree**: for every `s ∈ ℝ`,
`‖f‖_{F^s_{p,p}} = ‖(2^(js) ‖Δ_j f‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_p}` on `L_p(𝕋^d)`, by Tonelli's theorem
(`L_p(ℓ_p) = ℓ_p(L_p)`).

Torus.periodicTriebelLizorkinNorm.name: Torus.periodicTriebelLizorkinNorm
Torus.periodicTriebelLizorkinNorm.docstring:
The **Triebel–Lizorkin quasi-norm** `‖ t ↦ ‖(2^(js) |ψ_j ⋆ f(t)|)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p` of
`f ∈ L_p(𝕋^d)`: the `ℓ_q` norm of the weighted blocks at each point, then the `L_p` norm.

Torus.periodicLpBlock_mem_trigPolyLp.name: Torus.periodicLpBlock_mem_trigPolyLp
Torus.periodicLpBlock_mem_trigPolyLp.docstring:
**The blocks are trigonometric polynomials**: `Δ_j f` has degree `< 2^(j+1)`, since
`𝓕ψ_j(m) ≠ 0` forces `deg m ≤ |m| < 2^(j+1)`.

Torus.periodicLpBlock_eq_zero_of_mem.name: Torus.periodicLpBlock_eq_zero_of_mem
Torus.periodicLpBlock_eq_zero_of_mem.docstring:
**High blocks of trigonometric polynomials vanish**: `Δ_j a = 0` for a trigonometric
polynomial `a` of degree `< 2^i` and `j ≥ i + #d + 1`, since `𝓕ψ_j = 0` on the ball of radius
`2^(j-1)` and `|m| ≤ #d deg m < 2^(i + #d)`.

Torus.periodicLpBlock_ae_eq_periodicBloc.name: Torus.periodicLpBlock_ae_eq_periodicBlockFun
Torus.periodicLpBlock_ae_eq_periodicBloc.docstring: The block `Δ_j f ∈ L_p(𝕋^d)` is represented by the pointwise convolution `ψ_j ⋆ f`.

Torus.periodicLpBlock.name: Torus.periodicLpBlock
Torus.periodicLpBlock.docstring:
The **Littlewood–Paley block** `Δ_j f = ψ_j ⋆ f` of `f ∈ L_p(𝕋^d)`, with the kernel `ψ_j` of
`Rd.lpBlockKernel` on `ℝ^d`.

Torus.periodicLittlewoodPaleyNorm_le_app.name: Torus.periodicLittlewoodPaleyNorm_le_approxNormDyadic_trigScheme
Torus.periodicLittlewoodPaleyNorm_le_app.docstring:
**The Littlewood–Paley quasi-norm is controlled by the approximation norm**: for `s ≥ 0`,
`‖(2^(js) ‖Δ_j f‖_p)_j‖_q ≤ 2 (#d + 1) 2^((#d + 1) s) ‖Φ‖_1 ‖f‖^dyadic` for every
`f ∈ L_p(𝕋^d)`, with the scheme of trigonometric polynomials. The first `#d + 1` blocks are
bounded by `‖f‖`, the block `Δ_{j + #d + 1} f` by `E_{2^j}(f)`.

Torus.periodicLittlewoodPaleyNorm_eq_lqN.name: Torus.periodicLittlewoodPaleyNorm_eq_lqNorm_eLpNorm
Torus.periodicLittlewoodPaleyNorm_eq_lqN.docstring:
The Littlewood–Paley quasi-norm on the torus in terms of the pointwise blocks:
`‖(2^(js) ‖Δ_j f‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q} = ‖(2^(js) ‖ψ_j ⋆ f‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`.

Torus.periodicJacksonApprox_mem_trigPoly.name: Torus.periodicJacksonApprox_mem_trigPolyLp
Torus.periodicJacksonApprox_mem_trigPoly.docstring:
**The Jackson approximant is a trigonometric polynomial of degree `< 2^(k+1)`**:
`𝓕Φ_c(ξ) = 𝓕Φ(ξ/c) = 0` for `‖ξ‖ ≥ 2c`, `c = 2^k/(l+1)`, and `‖m‖ ≥ deg m`.

Torus.periodicJacksonApprox.name: Torus.periodicJacksonApprox
Torus.periodicJacksonApprox.docstring:
The **Jackson approximant on the torus** `J_k f = ∑_{l<r} (-1)^l C(r, l + 1) Φ_{2^k/(l+1)} ⋆ f`,
with the kernel `Φ` of `Rd.lpKernel` on `ℝ^d` acting by `Torus.periodicEconvLp`.

Torus.periodicEconv_smul.name: Torus.periodicEconv_smul
Torus.periodicEconv_smul.docstring:
**The convolution is homogeneous**: `Φ ⋆ (c f) = c (Φ ⋆ f)` at every point, for every
`c ∈ ℂ`.

Torus.periodicEconv_mFourier.name: Torus.periodicEconv_mFourier
Torus.periodicEconv_mFourier.docstring: **The characters are eigenfunctions**: `Φ ⋆ e_m = 𝓕Φ(m) e_m`.

Torus.periodicEconv_dilate_apply.name: Torus.periodicEconv_dilate_apply
Torus.periodicEconv_dilate_apply.docstring:
**Convolution with a dilation**: `(Φ_c ⋆ f)(t) = ∫ Φ(z) f(t - π(c^(-1) z)) dz` for `c > 0`
(substitute `y = c^(-1) z`).

Torus.periodicEconv_congr_ae.name: Torus.periodicEconv_congr_ae
Torus.periodicEconv_congr_ae.docstring:
**The convolution sees only classes**: `f = g` almost everywhere gives `Φ ⋆ f = Φ ⋆ g`
almost everywhere, since `f(t - π y) = g(t - π y)` for almost every `(t, y)`.

Torus.periodicEconv_add_quotientProj.name: Torus.periodicEconv_add_quotientProj
Torus.periodicEconv_add_quotientProj.docstring:
**Translation**: `(Φ ⋆ f)(t + π h) = (Φ(· + h) ⋆ f)(t)`, by the translation invariance of the
Lebesgue measure.

Torus.periodicEconv_add_ae.name: Torus.periodicEconv_add_ae
Torus.periodicEconv_add_ae.docstring:
**The convolution is additive almost everywhere** for integrable `f, g` on the torus:
`Φ ⋆ (f + g) = Φ ⋆ f + Φ ⋆ g` almost everywhere, where both integrals converge absolutely
(`Torus.ae_integrable_econv`).

Torus.periodicEconvLp_sub_kernel.name: Torus.periodicEconvLp_sub_kernel
Torus.periodicEconvLp_sub_kernel.docstring: **Subtractivity in the kernel**: `(K - L) ⋆ f = K ⋆ f - L ⋆ f` on `L_p(𝕋^d)`.

Torus.periodicEconvLp_mem_trigPolyLp.name: Torus.periodicEconvLp_mem_trigPolyLp
Torus.periodicEconvLp_mem_trigPolyLp.docstring:
**Band-limited kernels map `L_p(𝕋)` into trigonometric polynomials**: if `𝓕Φ(m) = 0` for
`deg m ≥ n`, then `Φ ⋆ f` has degree `< n`. The operator maps every `e_m` into the closed subspace
of trigonometric polynomials of degree `< n`, and the `e_m` span a dense subspace (Mathlib's
`span_mFourierLp_closure_eq_top`).

Torus.periodicEconvLp_mFourierLp.name: Torus.periodicEconvLp_mFourierLp
Torus.periodicEconvLp_mFourierLp.docstring: **The characters are eigenfunctions in `L_p`**: `Φ ⋆ e_m = 𝓕Φ(m) e_m`.

Torus.periodicEconvLp_eq_zero_of_mem.name: Torus.periodicEconvLp_eq_zero_of_mem
Torus.periodicEconvLp_eq_zero_of_mem.docstring:
**Kernels with `𝓕Φ = 0` on the low frequencies annihilate trigonometric polynomials**: if
`𝓕Φ(m) = 0` for `deg m < n`, then `Φ ⋆ a = 0` for every trigonometric polynomial `a` of degree
`< n`.

Torus.periodicEconvLp_eq_self_of_mem.name: Torus.periodicEconvLp_eq_self_of_mem
Torus.periodicEconvLp_eq_self_of_mem.docstring:
**Kernels with `𝓕Φ = 1` on the low frequencies reproduce trigonometric polynomials**: if
`𝓕Φ(m) = 1` for `deg m < n`, then `Φ ⋆ a = a` for every trigonometric polynomial `a` of degree
`< n`.

Torus.periodicEconvLp_dilatedBandKernel_.name: Torus.periodicEconvLp_dilatedBandKernel_eq_self
Torus.periodicEconvLp_dilatedBandKernel_.docstring:
**The band-limiting kernel reproduces trigonometric polynomials**: `Θ_{j+#d} ⋆ a = a` for `a`
of degree `< 2^j`, since `‖m‖ ≤ #d deg m < 2^(#d) 2^j` and `𝓕Θ_J = 1` on `‖ξ‖ ≤ 2^(J+1)`.

Torus.periodicEconvLp_apply_ae.name: Torus.periodicEconvLp_apply_ae
Torus.periodicEconvLp_apply_ae.docstring: The operator `periodicEconvLp` is the convolution, almost everywhere.

Torus.periodicEconvLp.name: Torus.periodicEconvLp
Torus.periodicEconvLp.docstring:
**Convolution with an integrable kernel on `ℝ^d` as a bounded operator on `L_p(𝕋)`**,
`1 ≤ p < ∞`, of norm at most `‖Φ‖_1`.

Torus.periodicEconv.name: Torus.periodicEconv
Torus.periodicEconv.docstring:
The **convolution with a kernel on `ℝ^d`**: `(Φ ⋆ f)(t) = ∫ Φ(y) f(t - π y) dy` for a function
`f` on the torus.

Torus.periodicBlockFun.name: Torus.periodicBlockFun
Torus.periodicBlockFun.docstring:
The **Littlewood–Paley block at every point**, `t ↦ (ψ_j ⋆ f)(t) = ∫ ψ_j(y) f(t - π y) dy`,
with a representative of `f ∈ L_p(𝕋^d)`. Its class in `L_p` is the block `Torus.periodicLpBlock`
(`Torus.periodicLpBlock_ae_eq_periodicBlockFun`).

Torus.periodicBernsteinConst_ne_top.name: Torus.periodicBernsteinConst_ne_top
Torus.periodicBernsteinConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of the inverse inequality is finite.

Torus.periodicBernsteinConst.name: Torus.periodicBernsteinConst
Torus.periodicBernsteinConst.docstring: The **constant of the inverse inequality on the torus**, `2^r + (2^(#d) #d)^r ‖D^r Θ‖_1`.

Torus.norm_trigMonomial_apply.name: Torus.norm_trigMonomial_apply
Torus.norm_trigMonomial_apply.docstring: A trigonometric monomial has modulus `1` everywhere.

Torus.norm_toLp_two_pow.name: Torus.norm_toLp_two_pow
Torus.norm_toLp_two_pow.docstring: The `L_2` norm of `T^m` is the `m`-th power of the `L_{2m}` norm of `T`.

Torus.norm_sq_le_card_mul_norm_toLp_sq.name: Torus.norm_sq_le_card_mul_norm_toLp_sq
Torus.norm_sq_le_card_mul_norm_toLp_sq.docstring:
**The Nikolskii inequality from `L_2` to `L_∞`**: for a trigonometric polynomial of degree
`< n`, `‖T‖_∞² ≤ (2n)^d ‖T‖_2²`.

Torus.norm_rpow_le_card_mul_eLpNorm_rpow.name: Torus.norm_rpow_le_card_mul_eLpNorm_rpow
Torus.norm_rpow_le_card_mul_eLpNorm_rpow.docstring:
**The Nikolskii inequality from `L_p` to `L_∞`** for trigonometric polynomials: for
`T` of degree `< n`, `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `m = ⌈p/2⌉`,
`‖T‖_∞^p ≤ (2mn)^d ‖T‖_p^p`.

Torus.norm_quotientProj_le.name: Torus.norm_quotientProj_le
Torus.norm_quotientProj_le.docstring: `‖π x‖ ≤ ‖x‖` for the sup norm of the torus.

Torus.norm_pow_le_norm_pow.name: Torus.norm_pow_le_norm_pow
Torus.norm_pow_le_norm_pow.docstring: For a bounded continuous function, `‖T‖^m ≤ ‖T^m‖` (in fact equality holds).

Torus.norm_periodicEconvLp_le.name: Torus.norm_periodicEconvLp_le
Torus.norm_periodicEconvLp_le.docstring:
**A uniform bound for convolution operators**: if `∫ |Φ| ≤ C < ∞`, then
`‖Φ ⋆ g‖_p ≤ C ‖g‖_p` in real norms.

Torus.norm_le_card_mul.name: Torus.norm_le_card_mul
Torus.norm_le_card_mul.docstring: **A norm bound by the coordinates**: `‖x‖ ≤ #d · M` if `|x_i| ≤ M` for every `i`.

Torus.norm_latticeVec_le.name: Torus.norm_latticeVec_le
Torus.norm_latticeVec_le.docstring: **The norm is at most `#d` times the degree**.

Torus.norm_coe_le_abs.name: Torus.norm_coe_le_abs
Torus.norm_coe_le_abs.docstring: The norm on the circle is at most the absolute value of a representative.

Torus.neg_one_pow_mul_higherDiff_quotien.name: Torus.neg_one_pow_mul_higherDiff_quotientProj
Torus.neg_one_pow_mul_higherDiff_quotien.docstring:
**Averaged differences on the torus**: `(-1)^r Δ^r_{π(-c^(-1) z)} f(t) =
f(t) - ∑_{l<r} (-1)^l C(r, l + 1) f(t - π((c/(l+1))^(-1) z))`.

Torus.mul_mem_trigPoly.name: Torus.mul_mem_trigPoly
Torus.mul_mem_trigPoly.docstring: The product of polynomials of degree `< m` and `< n` has degree `< m + n`.

Torus.mem_uniformTrigScheme.name: Torus.mem_uniformTrigScheme
Torus.mem_uniformTrigScheme.docstring:
The approximants of complexity `n` of the uniform trigonometric scheme are the trigonometric
polynomials of degree `< n`.

Torus.mem_toLp_trigScheme_iff.name: Torus.mem_toLp_trigScheme_iff
Torus.mem_toLp_trigScheme_iff.docstring:
**The trigonometric polynomials of the scheme in `L_p`**: the approximants of degree `< n`
of `(trigScheme d).toLp p` are the trigonometric polynomials of degree `< n` in `L_p`.

Torus.mem_boxLt.name: Torus.mem_boxLt
Torus.mem_boxLt.docstring: `k` lies in the box of size `n` iff `deg k < n`.

Torus.memLp_periodicEconv.name: Torus.memLp_periodicEconv
Torus.memLp_periodicEconv.docstring: The convolution of `f ∈ L_p(𝕋)` with an integrable kernel is in `L_p(𝕋)`.

Torus.measurable_comp_sub_quotientProj.name: Torus.measurable_comp_sub_quotientProj
Torus.measurable_comp_sub_quotientProj.docstring: The integrand `(t, y) ↦ f(t - π y)` is measurable.

Torus.mFourier_neg_quotientProj.name: Torus.mFourier_neg_quotientProj
Torus.mFourier_neg_quotientProj.docstring: **The characters along the quotient map**: `e_m(-π y) = e^(-2πi⟨y, m⟩)`.

Torus.mFourier_add_apply.name: Torus.mFourier_add_apply
Torus.mFourier_add_apply.docstring: A trigonometric monomial is a character: `e_k(x + h) = e_k(x) e_k(h)`.

Torus.mFourierLp_mem_trigPolyLp.name: Torus.mFourierLp_mem_trigPolyLp
Torus.mFourierLp_mem_trigPolyLp.docstring: `e_m` is a trigonometric polynomial of degree `< n` for `deg m < n`.

Torus.lpModulus_le_two_pow_mul_succ.name: Torus.lpModulus_le_two_pow_mul_succ
Torus.lpModulus_le_two_pow_mul_succ.docstring:
**Halving the step**: `ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p ≤ 2^r ω_r(f, 2^(-(k+1)))_p` on the torus
(`Torus.periodic_smoothnessModulus_nat_mul_le` with `m = 2`).

Torus.lpModulus_le_of_mem_trigPolyLp.name: Torus.lpModulus_le_of_mem_trigPolyLp
Torus.lpModulus_le_of_mem_trigPolyLp.docstring:
**The inverse inequality on the torus** (Bernstein): for a trigonometric polynomial `a` of
degree `< 2^j`, `ω_r(a, 2^(-k))_p ≤ C 2^(-(k-j) r) ‖a‖_p` (with `k - j` truncated at `0`). For
`k ≥ j` and `‖h‖ ≤ 2^(-k)`, `h = π x` with `‖x‖ ≤ #d ‖h‖`, `Δ^r_h a = (Δ^r_x Θ_J) ⋆ a`, and Young's
inequality gives `‖Δ^r_h a‖_p ≤ (2^J ‖x‖)^r ‖D^r Θ‖_1 ‖a‖_p`.

Torus.isClosed_trigPolyLp.name: Torus.isClosed_trigPolyLp
Torus.isClosed_trigPolyLp.docstring:
The trigonometric polynomials of degree `< n` form a closed subspace of `L_p(𝕋)`, being
finite-dimensional.

Torus.integral_mul_mFourier_neg_quotient.name: Torus.integral_mul_mFourier_neg_quotientProj
Torus.integral_mul_mFourier_neg_quotient.docstring: **The Fourier transform at the lattice points**: `∫ Φ(y) e_m(-π y) dy = 𝓕Φ(m)`.

Torus.higherDiff_periodicEconv_ae.name: Torus.higherDiff_periodicEconv_ae
Torus.higherDiff_periodicEconv_ae.docstring:
**Differences of the convolution**: `Δ^r_{π h} (Φ ⋆ f) = (Δ^r_h Φ) ⋆ f` almost everywhere,
for integrable `Φ` and `f ∈ L_1(𝕋)`.

Torus.hasSum_periodicLpBlock.name: Torus.hasSum_periodicLpBlock
Torus.hasSum_periodicLpBlock.docstring:
**A finite Littlewood–Paley quasi-norm gives an absolutely convergent decomposition**: for
`s > 0`, `‖Δ_j f‖_p ≤ 2^(-js) ‖f‖_{LP}`, so `f = ∑_j Δ_j f` converges absolutely in
`L_p(𝕋^d)`.

Torus.ext_mFourierLp.name: Torus.ext_mFourierLp
Torus.ext_mFourierLp.docstring:
**Bounded linear maps on `L_p(𝕋^d)` are determined by the characters**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`,
two bounded linear maps from `L_p(𝕋^d)` into a normed space that agree on every `e_m` are equal,
since the characters span a dense subspace (Mathlib's `span_mFourierLp_closure_eq_top`).

Torus.exists_sum_of_mem_trigPoly.name: Torus.exists_sum_of_mem_trigPoly
Torus.exists_sum_of_mem_trigPoly.docstring:
A trigonometric polynomial of degree `< n` is a combination of the monomials of degree
`< n`.

Torus.exists_quotientProj_eq.name: Torus.exists_quotientProj_eq
Torus.exists_quotientProj_eq.docstring:
**Every point of the torus is `π x` with `‖x‖ ≤ #d ‖h‖`**: choose representatives
`|x_i| = ‖h_i‖` (`Torus.exists_coe_eq_abs_eq_norm`).

Torus.exists_coe_eq_abs_eq_norm.name: Torus.exists_coe_eq_abs_eq_norm
Torus.exists_coe_eq_abs_eq_norm.docstring: Every point of the circle has a representative `x ∈ ℝ` with `|x| = ‖u‖`.

Torus.enorm_sub_periodicJacksonApprox_le.name: Torus.enorm_sub_periodicJacksonApprox_le
Torus.enorm_sub_periodicJacksonApprox_le.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality on the torus**: for `f ∈ L_p(𝕋^d)`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`,
`‖f - J_k f‖_p ≤ C ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p`, with the constant `Rd.bandJacksonConst` of `ℝ^d`: by the
weighted averages of `Rd.eLpNorm_integral_lpKernel_mul_le` and
`ω_r(f, 2^(-k) |z|)_p ≤ (1 + |z|)^r ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p`.

Torus.enorm_periodicLpBlock_le_approxErr.name: Torus.enorm_periodicLpBlock_le_approxError
Torus.enorm_periodicLpBlock_le_approxErr.docstring:
**Blocks see only the error of trigonometric approximation**: for `j ≥ i + #d + 1`,
`‖Δ_j f‖_p ≤ 2 ‖Φ‖_1 E_{2^i}(f)_p`.

Torus.enorm_periodicLpBlock_eq_eLpNorm_p.name: Torus.enorm_periodicLpBlock_eq_eLpNorm_periodicBlockFun
Torus.enorm_periodicLpBlock_eq_eLpNorm_p.docstring: `‖Δ_j f‖_p` is the `L_p` norm of the pointwise block `ψ_j ⋆ f`.

Torus.enorm_periodicEconvLp_le.name: Torus.enorm_periodicEconvLp_le
Torus.enorm_periodicEconvLp_le.docstring: **Young's inequality on `L_p(𝕋)`** in extended norms: `‖Φ ⋆ f‖_p ≤ ‖Φ‖_1 ‖f‖_p`.

Torus.eLpNorm_periodicEconv_le.name: Torus.eLpNorm_periodicEconv_le
Torus.eLpNorm_periodicEconv_le.docstring:
**Young's inequality on the torus**: `‖Φ ⋆ f‖_{L_p(𝕋)} ≤ ‖Φ‖_{L_1(ℝ^d)} ‖f‖_p`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`,
since every translate `f(· - π y)` has the norm of `f`.

Torus.eLpNorm_comp_sub.name: Torus.eLpNorm_comp_sub
Torus.eLpNorm_comp_sub.docstring: Translations keep `L_p` norms on the torus.

Torus.card_boxLt_le.name: Torus.card_boxLt_le
Torus.card_boxLt_le.docstring: There are at most `(2n)^d` frequencies of degree `< n`.

Torus.boxLt_zero.name: Torus.boxLt_zero
Torus.boxLt_zero.docstring: The box of size `0` is empty.

Torus.approxNormDyadic_trigScheme_le.name: Torus.approxNormDyadic_trigScheme_le
Torus.approxNormDyadic_trigScheme_le.docstring:
**The approximation norm is controlled by the Littlewood–Paley quasi-norm**: for `s > 0`,
`‖f‖^dyadic ≤ 2 · 2^s (1 - 2^(-s))⁻¹ ‖(2^(js) ‖Δ_j f‖_p)_j‖_q` for every `f ∈ L_p(𝕋^d)`, with
the scheme of trigonometric polynomials. The blocks moved up by one level,
`0, Δ_0 f, Δ_1 f, …` (`ApproximationScheme.shiftSeq 1`), lie in `𝒯_{2^k}` and form a block
decomposition (`ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_of_hasSum`).

Torus.approxError_trigScheme_le.name: Torus.approxError_trigScheme_le
Torus.approxError_trigScheme_le.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality for the trigonometric polynomials**:
`E_{2^(k+1)}(f)_p ≤ C ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p` in `L_p(𝕋^d)`.

Torus.ae_sub_periodicJacksonApprox_eq.name: Torus.ae_sub_periodicJacksonApprox_eq
Torus.ae_sub_periodicJacksonApprox_eq.docstring:
**The Jackson approximant as an averaged difference**: for almost every `t`,
`f(t) - J_k f(t) = ∫ Φ(z) (-1)^r Δ^r_{π(-2^(-k) z)} f(t) dz`.

Torus.ae_integrable_econv.name: Torus.ae_integrable_econv
Torus.ae_integrable_econv.docstring:
**The convolution integral converges absolutely almost everywhere** for `f ∈ L_1(𝕋)`:
`∫∫ |Φ(y)| |f(t - π y)| dy dt = ‖Φ‖_1 ‖f‖_1` by Tonelli's theorem.

Torus.MemPeriodicTriebelLizorkin.name: Torus.MemPeriodicTriebelLizorkin
Torus.MemPeriodicTriebelLizorkin.docstring: `f ∈ F^s_{p,q}(𝕋^d)`: the Triebel–Lizorkin quasi-norm of `f` is finite.

TestFunction.lineDerivOp_iteratedLineDer.name: TestFunction.lineDerivOp_iteratedLineDerivOp_comm
TestFunction.lineDerivOp_iteratedLineDer.docstring:
A directional derivative commutes with every iterated directional derivative of a test
function: `∂_a ∂^v φ = ∂^v ∂_a φ`.

TestFunction.lineDerivOp_comm.name: TestFunction.lineDerivOp_comm
TestFunction.lineDerivOp_comm.docstring:
Directional derivatives of a test function commute: `∂_a ∂_b φ = ∂_b ∂_a φ`, read off the
complex Schwartz function `Rd.testSchwartz φ` (`SchwartzMap.lineDerivOp_comm`).

TemperedDistribution.memSobolev_add_one_.name: TemperedDistribution.memSobolev_add_one_of_lineDerivOp
TemperedDistribution.memSobolev_add_one_.docstring:
**`H^{s+1,p}` from first derivatives along a basis**: for `1 < p < ∞`, if `f ∈ H^{s,p}` and
the derivatives of `f` along an orthonormal basis lie in `H^{s,p}`, then `f ∈ H^{s+1,p}`. Here
`J_1 f = J_{-1}(J_2 f) = J_{-1} f - (2π)^{-2} ∑_i J_{-1} ∂_{b_i} ∂_{b_i} f`
(`TemperedDistribution.besselPotential_two_eq_sub_laplacian`, Mathlib's
`TemperedDistribution.laplacian_eq_sum`), and `J_{-1}` maps `f` and each `∂_{b_i} ∂_{b_i} f` into
`H^{s,p}`. Mirrored from TauCeti.

TemperedDistribution.memSobolev_add_one_.name: TemperedDistribution.memSobolev_add_one_iff
TemperedDistribution.memSobolev_add_one_.docstring:
**The derivative characterisation of `H^{s+1,p}`**: for `1 < p < ∞` and every real `s`, a
tempered distribution lies in `H^{s+1,p}` iff it and all its first directional derivatives lie in
`H^{s,p}` (`TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.mono_of_one_lt`,
`TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.lineDerivOp_of_one_lt`,
`TemperedDistribution.memSobolev_add_one_of_lineDerivOp`). Mirrored from TauCeti.

TemperedDistribution.iteratedLineDerivOp.name: TemperedDistribution.iteratedLineDerivOp_toTemperedDistributionCLM_eq
TemperedDistribution.iteratedLineDerivOp.docstring:
The distributional derivative `∂^v S_u` of the tempered distribution `S_u` of a Schwartz
function `u` is the tempered distribution `S_{∂^v u}` of its classical derivative `∂^v u` (the
iterated form of Mathlib's `TemperedDistribution.lineDerivOp_toTemperedDistributionCLM_eq`).

TemperedDistribution.iteratedLineDerivOp.name: TemperedDistribution.iteratedLineDerivOp_apply_apply
TemperedDistribution.iteratedLineDerivOp.docstring:
The **transpose formula** for iterated derivatives of a tempered distribution: for directions
`v = (v_0, …, v_{k-1})`, `∂^v T (u) = T((-1)^k ∂^v u)` for every Schwartz function `u`. Mathlib
defines `∂_w T (u) = T(-∂_w u)` (`TemperedDistribution.lineDerivOp_apply_apply`); the order of
the derivatives on `u` is irrelevant because they commute
(`SchwartzMap.lineDerivOp_iteratedLineDerivOp_comm`).

TemperedDistribution.besselPotential_two.name: TemperedDistribution.besselPotential_two_eq_sub_laplacian
TemperedDistribution.besselPotential_two.docstring:
**`J_2 = 1 - (2π)^{-2} Δ`**: the Bessel potential of order `2` is the identity minus
`(2π)^{-2}` times the Laplacian; the factor comes from Mathlib's normalisation of the Fourier
transform. Mirrored from TauCeti.

TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.sum.name: TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.sum
TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.sum.docstring:
**Finite sums in `H^{s,p}`**: a finite sum of tempered distributions in `H^{s,p}` lies in
`H^{s,p}`. Mirrored from TauCeti.

TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.mono_of_.name: TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.mono_of_one_lt
TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.mono_of_.docstring:
**`H^{s,p}` decreases in `s`**: for `1 < p < ∞`, `H^{s,p} ⊆ H^{s',p}` whenever `s' ≤ s`. Here
`f ∈ H^{s',p}` iff `J_{s'-s} f ∈ H^{s,p}` (Mathlib's
`TemperedDistribution.memSobolev_besselPotential_iff`), and `⟨ξ⟩^{s'-s}` is a symbol of order
`s' - s ≤ 0` (`Rd.hasSymbolGrowth_besselWeight`), hence of order `0`. Statement mirrored from
TauCeti; for `p = 2` this is Mathlib's `TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.mono`.

TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.lineDeri.name: TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.lineDerivOp_of_one_lt
TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.lineDeri.docstring:
**Derivatives on Bessel potential spaces**: for `1 < p < ∞` and every direction `v`, the
derivative `∂_v` maps `H^{s,p}` into `H^{s-1,p}`, since `∂_v = 2πi ⟪ξ, v⟫(D)` (Mathlib's
`TemperedDistribution.lineDeriv_eq_fourierMultiplierCLM`) with the symbol `⟪ξ, v⟫` of order `1`
(`Rd.hasSymbolGrowth_inner`). Statement mirrored from TauCeti; for `p = 2` this is Mathlib's
`TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.lineDerivOp`.

TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.fourierM.name: TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.fourierMultiplierCLM_of_hasSymbolGrowth
TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.fourierM.docstring:
**Fourier multipliers on Bessel potential spaces**: for `1 < p < ∞`, a symbol `m` of order
`σ` and every real `s`, `m(D)` maps Mathlib's Bessel potential space `H^{s,p}(V)` into
`H^{s-σ,p}(V)`. In dimension `n ≥ 1`, `H^{s,p} = F^s_{p,2}`
(`Rd.memSobolev_bessel_iff_memTriebelLizorkinDistr`) and `m(D)` maps `F^s_{p,2}` into
`F^{s-σ}_{p,2}` (`Rd.MemTriebelLizorkinDistr.fourierMultiplierCLM`); dimension `0` is
`Rd.memSobolev_fourierMultiplierCLM_of_subsingleton`.

SchwartzMap.lineDerivOp_iteratedLineDeri.name: SchwartzMap.lineDerivOp_iteratedLineDerivOp_comm
SchwartzMap.lineDerivOp_iteratedLineDeri.docstring:
A directional derivative commutes with every iterated directional derivative of a Schwartz
function: `∂_a ∂^v u = ∂^v ∂_a u`.

SchwartzMap.lineDerivOp_compSubConstCLM.name: SchwartzMap.lineDerivOp_compSubConstCLM
SchwartzMap.lineDerivOp_compSubConstCLM.docstring:
**Derivatives commute with translations**: `∂_v (η(· - y)) = (∂_v η)(· - y)` for a Schwartz
function `η` (Mathlib's `SchwartzMap.compSubConstCLM` and `fderiv_comp_sub`).

SchwartzMap.lineDerivOp_comm.name: SchwartzMap.lineDerivOp_comm
SchwartzMap.lineDerivOp_comm.docstring:
Directional derivatives of a Schwartz function commute: `∂_a ∂_b u = ∂_b ∂_a u`. This is the
symmetry of the second derivative of a `C^2` function (Mathlib's
`ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt`), read through `∂^{(a, b)} u(x) = D^2 u(x)(a, b)`
(`SchwartzMap.iteratedLineDerivOp_eq_iteratedFDeriv`).

SchwartzMap.iteratedLineDerivOp_compSubC.name: SchwartzMap.iteratedLineDerivOp_compSubConstCLM
SchwartzMap.iteratedLineDerivOp_compSubC.docstring: Iterated derivatives commute with translations: `∂^w (η(· - y)) = (∂^w η)(· - y)`.

SchwartzMap.fourier_iteratedLineDerivOp_.name: SchwartzMap.fourier_iteratedLineDerivOp_apply
SchwartzMap.fourier_iteratedLineDerivOp_.docstring:
**The Fourier transform of an iterated derivative**: for every Schwartz function `G` on `V`
with values in a complex normed space `E` and directions `w ∈ V^k`, with
`∂^w = ∂_{w_0} ⋯ ∂_{w_{k-1}}`, `𝓕(∂^w G)(ξ) = (∏_l 2πi ⟪ξ, w_l⟫) 𝓕G(ξ)`, by induction from
Mathlib's `SchwartzMap.fourier_lineDerivOp_eq`.

Real.tsum_comp_add_int_eq_integral.name: Real.tsum_comp_add_int_eq_integral
Real.tsum_comp_add_int_eq_integral.docstring:
**Poisson summation when the Fourier transform vanishes at the nonzero integers**: let
`f : ℝ → ℂ` be continuous and vanish outside a bounded interval `[a, b]`, with `𝓕 f(n) = 0` for
every integer `n ≠ 0`. Then the periodisation of `f` is the constant `∫ f`:
`∑_{n ∈ ℤ} f(x + n) = ∫ f(y) dy` for every `x ∈ ℝ`. Poisson summation (Mathlib's
`Real.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier`) writes the periodisation as the Fourier series
`∑_n 𝓕 f(n) e^(2πinx)`, whose only nonzero term is `𝓕 f(0) = ∫ f`
(`Real.real_fourier_apply_zero`).

Real.summable_norm_restrict_comp_addRigh.name: Real.summable_norm_restrict_comp_addRight
Real.summable_norm_restrict_comp_addRigh.docstring:
For a continuous function `f : ℝ → E` vanishing outside a bounded interval `[a, b]` and a
compact set `K ⊆ ℝ`, the sup norms over `K` of the translates `x ↦ f(x + n)`, `n ∈ ℤ`, are
summable: only the finitely many `n` with `K + n` meeting `[a, b]` give a translate that is
nonzero on `K`. This is the hypothesis of Mathlib's Poisson summation formula
`Real.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier`.

Real.smoothTransition.exists_abs_deriv_l.name: Real.smoothTransition.exists_abs_deriv_le
Real.smoothTransition.exists_abs_deriv_l.docstring:
**The derivative of `Real.smoothTransition` is bounded**: it is continuous and vanishes
outside `[0, 1]` (Mathlib's `Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support`).

Real.smoothTransition.deriv_eq_zero_of_o.name: Real.smoothTransition.deriv_eq_zero_of_one_lt
Real.smoothTransition.deriv_eq_zero_of_o.docstring:
The derivative of Mathlib's `Real.smoothTransition` vanishes for `x > 1`, where the function
is constantly `1`.

Real.smoothTransition.deriv_eq_zero_of_n.name: Real.smoothTransition.deriv_eq_zero_of_neg
Real.smoothTransition.deriv_eq_zero_of_n.docstring:
The derivative of Mathlib's `Real.smoothTransition` vanishes for `x < 0`, where the function
is constantly `0`.

Real.real_integral_fourier_mul.name: Real.real_integral_fourier_mul
Real.real_integral_fourier_mul.docstring:
**The multiplication formula** `∫ 𝓕 f · g = ∫ f · 𝓕 g` for integrable `f, g`
(`Rd.integral_fourier_mul` on `ℝ`).

Real.real_integral_fourierInv_mul.name: Real.real_integral_fourierInv_mul
Real.real_integral_fourierInv_mul.docstring:
The multiplication formula for the inverse transform: `∫ 𝓕⁻ f · g = ∫ f · 𝓕⁻ g` for
integrable `f, g` (`Rd.integral_fourierInv_mul` on `ℝ`).

Real.real_fourier_apply_zero.name: Real.real_fourier_apply_zero
Real.real_fourier_apply_zero.docstring:
**The Fourier transform at `0` is the integral**: `𝓕 f(0) = ∫ f(x) dx` for every
`f : ℝ → ℂ` (`Rd.fourier_apply_zero` on `ℝ`).

Real.real_continuous_fourier_of_integrab.name: Real.real_continuous_fourier_of_integrable
Real.real_continuous_fourier_of_integrab.docstring:
The Fourier transform `𝓕 f(ξ) = ∫ e^(-2πixξ) f(x) dx` of an integrable function is
continuous (`Rd.continuous_fourier_of_integrable` on `ℝ`).

Real.real_continuous_fourierInv_of_integ.name: Real.real_continuous_fourierInv_of_integrable
Real.real_continuous_fourierInv_of_integ.docstring:
The inverse Fourier transform `𝓕⁻ f(x) = ∫ e^(2πixξ) f(ξ) dξ` of an integrable function is
continuous (`Rd.continuous_fourierInv_of_integrable` on `ℝ`).

Real.integral_mul_schwartz_eq.name: Real.integral_mul_schwartz_eq
Real.integral_mul_schwartz_eq.docstring:
**Testing against a Schwartz function** `ψ`: `∫ f · ψ = ∫ 𝓕 f · 𝓕⁻ ψ` for integrable `f`,
the multiplication formula for `f` and `𝓕⁻ ψ` together with `𝓕 (𝓕⁻ ψ) = ψ` (Fourier inversion on
the Schwartz space). Here `𝓕⁻ ψ` is the inverse transform of `ψ` as a Schwartz function.

Real.integral_mul_conj_eq_integral_fouri.name: Real.integral_mul_conj_eq_integral_fourier
Real.integral_mul_conj_eq_integral_fouri.docstring:
**Parseval's identity** `∫ f · conj g = ∫ 𝓕 f · conj (𝓕 g)` for integrable `f` and a
continuous integrable `g` with integrable transform. The sesquilinear multiplication formula
(Mathlib's `VectorFourier.integral_sesq_fourierIntegral_eq_neg_flip`) applied to `f` and `𝓕 g`
gives `∫ 𝓕 g · conj (𝓕 f) = ∫ 𝓕⁻ (𝓕 g) · conj f`, and `𝓕⁻ (𝓕 g) = g` by the inversion theorem
(Mathlib's `Continuous.fourierInv_fourier_eq`, which needs the hypotheses on `g`).

Real.fourier_sum_apply.name: Real.fourier_sum_apply
Real.fourier_sum_apply.docstring:
The Fourier transform of a finite sum of integrable functions is the sum of the
transforms.

Real.fourier_exp_mul_apply.name: Real.fourier_exp_mul_apply
Real.fourier_exp_mul_apply.docstring:
**Modulation becomes translation**: `𝓕[e^(2πib·) f](ξ) = 𝓕 f(ξ - b)`, since
`e^(-2πixξ) e^(2πibx) = e^(-2πix(ξ - b))`.

Real.fourier_const_mul_apply.name: Real.fourier_const_mul_apply
Real.fourier_const_mul_apply.docstring:
The Fourier transform commutes with multiplication by a constant, `𝓕[c f] = c 𝓕 f`, for
every `f` (Mathlib's `VectorFourier.fourierIntegral_const_smul`).

Real.fourier_comp_sub_right_apply.name: Real.fourier_comp_sub_right_apply
Real.fourier_comp_sub_right_apply.docstring: **Translation becomes modulation**, subtraction form: `𝓕[f(· - a)](ξ) = e^(-2πiaξ) 𝓕 f(ξ)`.

Real.fourier_comp_mul_sub_apply.name: Real.fourier_comp_mul_sub_apply
Real.fourier_comp_mul_sub_apply.docstring:
Dilation and translation together, `a > 0`:
`𝓕[f(a · - b)](ξ) = a⁻¹ e^(-2πibξ/a) 𝓕 f(ξ / a)`. This is the form met by the cascade
`η_{n+1}(x) = ∑_k c_k η_n(2x - k)`.

Real.fourier_comp_mul_left_apply_of_ne_z.name: Real.fourier_comp_mul_left_apply_of_ne_zero
Real.fourier_comp_mul_left_apply_of_ne_z.docstring:
**Dilation** by `a ≠ 0`: `𝓕[f(a ·)](ξ) = |a|⁻¹ 𝓕 f(ξ / a)`, by the substitution `y = a x`
(Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_comp_mul_left`).

Real.fourier_comp_add_right_apply.name: Real.fourier_comp_add_right_apply
Real.fourier_comp_add_right_apply.docstring:
**Translation becomes modulation**: `𝓕[f(· + a)](ξ) = e^(2πiaξ) 𝓕 f(ξ)`, by the substitution
`y = x + a` (Mathlib's `VectorFourier.fourierIntegral_comp_add_right`).

Real.fourierInv_sum_apply.name: Real.fourierInv_sum_apply
Real.fourierInv_sum_apply.docstring:
The inverse Fourier transform of a finite sum of integrable functions is the sum of the
inverse transforms.

Real.fourierInv_exp_mul_apply.name: Real.fourierInv_exp_mul_apply
Real.fourierInv_exp_mul_apply.docstring: Modulation for the inverse transform: `𝓕⁻[e^(2πib·) f](x) = 𝓕⁻ f(x + b)`.

Real.fourierInv_const_mul_apply.name: Real.fourierInv_const_mul_apply
Real.fourierInv_const_mul_apply.docstring: The inverse Fourier transform commutes with multiplication by a constant.

Real.fourierInv_comp_mul_left_apply.name: Real.fourierInv_comp_mul_left_apply
Real.fourierInv_comp_mul_left_apply.docstring: Dilation for the inverse transform, `a > 0`: `𝓕⁻[f(a ·)](x) = a⁻¹ 𝓕⁻ f(x / a)`.

Real.eqOn_zero_of_integral_mul_schwartz_.name: Real.eqOn_zero_of_integral_mul_schwartz_eq_zero
Real.eqOn_zero_of_integral_mul_schwartz_.docstring:
**Fundamental lemma**: a continuous `f` with `∫ ψ f = 0` for every Schwartz function `ψ`
with compact support in an open set `U` vanishes at every point of `U`. Almost everywhere this
is `Real.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_mul_schwartz_eq_zero`; two continuous functions that agree almost
everywhere on an open set agree on it (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Measure.eqOn_open_of_ae_eq`,
nonempty open sets have positive Lebesgue measure).

Real.conj_fourierInv.name: Real.conj_fourierInv
Real.conj_fourierInv.docstring:
Conjugation for the inverse transform: `conj (𝓕⁻ f(x)) = 𝓕[conj ∘ f](x)`
(`Rd.conj_fourierInv_apply` on `ℝ`).

Real.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_mul_schwartz.name: Real.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_mul_schwartz_eq_zero
Real.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_mul_schwartz.docstring:
**Fundamental lemma, almost everywhere form**: if `f` is locally integrable on an open set `U`
and `∫ ψ f = 0` for every Schwartz function `ψ` with compact support in `U`, then `f = 0` almost
everywhere on `U`. Mathlib's `IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero` tests with
real smooth compactly supported `g`; the function `x ↦ (g x : ℂ)` is such a Schwartz function
(`HasCompactSupport.toSchwartzMap`).

Rd.zcell_succ_subset_cubeParent.name: Rd.zcell_succ_subset_cubeParent
Rd.zcell_succ_subset_cubeParent.docstring: Every cube of level `k + 1` lies in its parent of level `k`.

Rd.zcell_subset_czSet.name: Rd.zcell_subset_czSet
Rd.zcell_subset_czSet.docstring: Every maximal big cube lies in the exceptional set.

Rd.zcell_subset_cubeAncestor.name: Rd.zcell_subset_cubeAncestor
Rd.zcell_subset_cubeAncestor.docstring: Every cube of level `k + l` lies in its ancestor of level `k`.

Rd.zcell_subset_closedBall.name: Rd.zcell_subset_closedBall
Rd.zcell_subset_closedBall.docstring:
**Outer ball**: the cube `Q_{k,m}` lies in the closed ball of radius `n 2^(-k)` around its
centre.

Rd.zcell_natCast.name: Rd.zcell_natCast
Rd.zcell_natCast.docstring: For natural levels the cubes are the cells of `Rd.dyadicCell`.

Rd.zcell_eq_preimage.name: Rd.zcell_eq_preimage
Rd.zcell_eq_preimage.docstring:
In the coordinates of the grid (`Rd.gridCoord`), the cube `Q_{k,m}` is the box
`∏_i [m_i 2^(-k), (m_i + 1) 2^(-k))`.

Rd.zcell_disjoint.name: Rd.zcell_disjoint
Rd.zcell_disjoint.docstring:
Cubes of the same level with different indices are disjoint: they are the fibres of the
cube index (Mathlib's `pairwise_disjoint_fiber`).

Rd.zcellIndex.name: Rd.zcellIndex
Rd.zcellIndex.docstring: The index `(⌊2^k x_i⌋)_i` of the dyadic cube of level `k ∈ ℤ` containing `x`.

Rd.zcellCenter_natCast.name: Rd.zcellCenter_natCast
Rd.zcellCenter_natCast.docstring: For natural levels the centres are those of `Rd.cellCenter`.

Rd.zcellCenter.name: Rd.zcellCenter
Rd.zcellCenter.docstring: The **centre** of the dyadic cube `Q_{k,m}`, with the coordinates `(m_i + 1/2) 2^(-k)`.

Rd.zcell.name: Rd.zcell
Rd.zcell.docstring:
The **dyadic cube** `Q_{k,m}` of level `k ∈ ℤ` and index `m ∈ ℤ^n`: the points whose scaled
coordinates `2^k x_i` have the integer parts `m_i`.

Rd.withDensity_maximalFunction_gt_mul_le.name: Rd.withDensity_maximalFunction_gt_mul_le
Rd.withDensity_maximalFunction_gt_mul_le.docstring:
The integrand of the layer cake formula for `M g` in the measure `w dx`, for measurable `g`
and `t > 0`: `|{M g > t}|_w t^(p-1) ≤ 2 · 5^n (∫_{g > t/2} g M w) t^(p-2)`.

Rd.weakTypeConst.name: Rd.weakTypeConst
Rd.weakTypeConst.docstring:
The constant of the vector-valued weak type `(1,1)`:
`(2n)^n |B(0,1)| + (1 + 3^n)^q 2^(n(q-1)) C_{n,q}`.

Rd.weakSobolevJet.snd_eq_of_fst_eq.name: Rd.weakSobolevJet.snd_eq_of_fst_eq
Rd.weakSobolevJet.snd_eq_of_fst_eq.docstring:
**The derivatives of a jet of `W^1_p(O)` are determined by its value**: two jets with the same
value have the same derivatives (`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.unique`).

Rd.weakSobolevJet.ext_of_fst_eq.name: Rd.weakSobolevJet.ext_of_fst_eq
Rd.weakSobolevJet.ext_of_fst_eq.docstring:
Two jets of `W^1_p(O)` with the same value are equal
(`Rd.weakSobolevJet.snd_eq_of_fst_eq`).

Rd.weakSobolevJet.name: Rd.weakSobolevJet
Rd.weakSobolevJet.docstring:
The **jets of `W^1_p(O)`**: the pairs `(f, (g_i)_i)` of elements of `L_p(O)` with
`g_i = ∂_{e_i} f` weakly on `O`, `e_i = Rd.gridBasis V i`; a complex linear subspace of
`L_p(O) × L_p(O)^n`.

Rd.weakDeriv_ae_zero_of_mem_vanishOn.name: Rd.weakDeriv_ae_zero_of_mem_vanishOn
Rd.weakDeriv_ae_zero_of_mem_vanishOn.docstring:
**Weak derivatives of an element vanishing on `Ω`**: for `W ∈ H^1(V)` vanishing on `Ω`, every
weak derivative on `V` of the `L_2` function of `W` vanishes almost everywhere on `Ω`.

Rd.weakDerivL2_restrictProj_ae_eq.name: Rd.weakDerivL2_restrictProj_ae_eq
Rd.weakDerivL2_restrictProj_ae_eq.docstring:
**A restriction has the same weak derivatives on `Ω`**: for an open `Ω`, `U ∈ H^1(V)` and every
direction `v`, `∂_v(U|_Ω) = ∂_v U` almost everywhere on `Ω`, since `U|_Ω` and `U` have the same
`L_2` function on `Ω` (`Rd.sobolevToL2_restrictProj_ae_eq`) and weak derivatives of `H^1(V)` are
local (`Rd.weakDerivL2_ae_eq_of_ae_eq`).

Rd.weakDerivL2_ofSchwartz.name: Rd.weakDerivL2_ofSchwartz
Rd.weakDerivL2_ofSchwartz.docstring:
**The weak derivative of a Schwartz function in `H^1(V)`** is its classical derivative:
`∂_v (ofSchwartz 1 w) = ∂_v w` in `L_2(V)` (`Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_schwartz`).

Rd.weakDerivL2_eq.name: Rd.weakDerivL2_eq
Rd.weakDerivL2_eq.docstring:
Every weak derivative `g ∈ L_2(V)` of the `L_2` function of `U` along `v` is
`weakDerivL2 v U`.

Rd.weakDerivL2_ae_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_zero.name: Rd.weakDerivL2_ae_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_zero
Rd.weakDerivL2_ae_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_zero.docstring:
**The weak derivatives of `H^1(V)` are local**: if the `L_2` function of `U ∈ H^1(V)`
vanishes almost everywhere on an open set `O`, so does its weak derivative `∂_v U`
(`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.ae_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_zero`).

Rd.weakDerivL2_ae_eq_of_ae_eq.name: Rd.weakDerivL2_ae_eq_of_ae_eq
Rd.weakDerivL2_ae_eq_of_ae_eq.docstring:
**Weak derivatives of functions that agree on an open set agree there**: if the `L_2`
functions of `U, W ∈ H^1(V)` agree almost everywhere on an open set `O`, so do `∂_v U` and
`∂_v W` (`Rd.weakDerivL2_ae_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_zero` for `U - W`).

Rd.weakDerivL2Linear.name: Rd.weakDerivL2Linear
Rd.weakDerivL2Linear.docstring:
The weak derivative `∂_v` of the `L_2` functions of `H^1(V)` as a linear map: `U` goes to the
weak derivative chosen in `Rd.exists_hasWeakLineDeriv_toL2`, which is linear in `U` because weak
derivatives on `V` are unique classes (`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.eq_of_top`).

Rd.weakDerivL2.name: Rd.weakDerivL2
Rd.weakDerivL2.docstring:
**The weak derivative `∂_v` as an operator** `H^1(V) → L_2(V)`, of norm at most `2π ‖v‖`
(`Rd.norm_le_of_hasWeakLineDeriv_toL2`): `∂_v U` is the weak derivative on `V` of the `L_2`
function of `U` (`Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_weakDerivL2`).

Rd.volume_zcell_sub.name: Rd.volume_zcell_sub
Rd.volume_zcell_sub.docstring:
**Coarser cubes are larger**: a cube of level `k - l` has `2^(ln)` times the volume of a cube
of level `k`, for all indices.

Rd.volume_zcell_cubeParent.name: Rd.volume_zcell_cubeParent
Rd.volume_zcell_cubeParent.docstring: The parent cube has `2^n` times the volume of its child.

Rd.volume_zcell.name: Rd.volume_zcell
Rd.volume_zcell.docstring:
**The volume of a cube**: `|Q_{k,m}| = 2^(-kn)`, since the coordinates of the grid preserve
Lebesgue measure (`Rd.measurePreserving_gridCoord`).

Rd.volume_switchSet_le.name: Rd.volume_switchSet_le
Rd.volume_switchSet_le.docstring:
**The switch set has volume at most `2 |U|`**: it lies in `U ∪ (U - h)`
(`Rd.switchSet_eq_symmDiff`, Mathlib's `Set.symmDiff_subset_union`), and translations preserve
the Lebesgue measure (Mathlib's `measure_preimage_add_right`).

Rd.volume_setOf_dist_add_smul_lt_le.name: Rd.volume_setOf_dist_add_smul_lt_le
Rd.volume_setOf_dist_add_smul_lt_le.docstring:
For `l ≥ 1` the steps `v` with `‖x + l v - w‖ < ρ` form a set of measure at most
`|B(0,ρ)|`, a ball of radius `ρ / l`.

Rd.volume_restrict_top.name: Rd.volume_restrict_top
Rd.volume_restrict_top.docstring:
Lebesgue measure restricted to the whole space `Ω = V` is Lebesgue measure, so that
`L_p(Ω) = L_p(V)` for `Ω = V`; a rewrite form of Mathlib's simp lemmas `Opens.coe_top` and
`Measure.restrict_univ`.

Rd.volume_real_zcell.name: Rd.volume_real_zcell
Rd.volume_real_zcell.docstring: The real volume of a cube is `2^(-kn)`.

Rd.volume_real_closedBall_div_cubeAt.name: Rd.volume_real_closedBall_div_cubeAt
Rd.volume_real_closedBall_div_cubeAt.docstring:
The closed ball of radius `(n+1) 2^(-k)` around the centre of the cube of level `k`
containing `x` has `(n+1)^n |B(0,1)|` times the volume of that cube.

Rd.volume_orthogonal_singleton_eq_zero.name: Rd.volume_orthogonal_singleton_eq_zero
Rd.volume_orthogonal_singleton_eq_zero.docstring:
**A hyperplane is a null set**: `e^⊥` has Lebesgue measure zero for `e ≠ 0` (Mathlib's
`MeasureTheory.Measure.addHaar_submodule`).

Rd.volume_lt_mul_lqNorm_maximalFunction_.name: Rd.volume_lt_mul_lqNorm_maximalFunction_czGood_le
Rd.volume_lt_mul_lqNorm_maximalFunction_.docstring:
**Chebyshev's inequality for the good parts**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 < q < ∞`, almost
everywhere measurable `g_j` with `G = ‖(g_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q}` integrable, and `0 < t < ∞`, let `czGood`
be the good part of the decomposition of `G` at height `t` and `c = 1 + 3^n`. The set where
`c ‖(M(czGood g_j)(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}` exceeds `t` has measure at most `c^q 2^(n(q-1)) C_{n,q} t⁻¹ ∫ G`,
by the case `q = p` and the bound of the good parts.

Rd.volume_lqNorm_maximalFunction_gt_mul_.name: Rd.volume_lqNorm_maximalFunction_gt_mul_rpow_le
Rd.volume_lqNorm_maximalFunction_gt_mul_.docstring:
**The level sets of the vector-valued maximal function, weighted**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`,
for `p > 1`, `1 < q < ∞`, measurable `g_j` with `∫ G^p < ∞` for `G = ‖(g_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`, and
`τ > 0`, `|{‖(M g_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q} > τ}| τ^(p-1)` is at most
`2 C (∫_{G > τ} G) τ^(p-2) + 2^q C_{n,q} (∫_{G ≤ τ} G^q) τ^(p-1-q)` with
`C = weakTypeConst V q`: `Rd.volume_lqNorm_maximalFunction_gt_le_split` for the set `{G > τ}`, on
which `G` is integrable since `∫_{G > τ} G ≤ τ^(1-p) ∫ G^p`.

Rd.volume_lqNorm_maximalFunction_gt_le_s.name: Rd.volume_lqNorm_maximalFunction_gt_le_split
Rd.volume_lqNorm_maximalFunction_gt_le_s.docstring:
**The two pieces at a level**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 < q < ∞`, almost everywhere
measurable `g_j`, a measurable set `S` on which `G = ‖(g_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q}` is integrable, and
`0 < s < ∞`,
`|{‖(M g_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q} > s}| ≤ C (s/2)⁻¹ ∫ 1_S G + ((s/2)^q)⁻¹ C_{n,q} ∫ (1_{Sᶜ} G)^q` with
`C = weakTypeConst V q`: the vector-valued weak type for `1_S g_j` and Chebyshev's inequality
with the case `q = p` for `1_{Sᶜ} g_j`.

Rd.volume_lqNorm_maximalFunction_gt_le.name: Rd.volume_lqNorm_maximalFunction_gt_le
Rd.volume_lqNorm_maximalFunction_gt_le.docstring:
**The vector-valued weak type `(1,1)`** of the maximal function (Fefferman–Stein): in
dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 < q < ∞`, almost everywhere measurable `g_j : V → [0, ∞]` with
`G = ‖(g_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q}` integrable, and `0 < t < ∞`,
`|{x : ‖(M g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q} > t}| ≤ C t⁻¹ ∫ G` with `C = weakTypeConst V q`. The
Calderón–Zygmund decomposition of `G` at height `t` splits the level set into the enlarged
exceptional set `Ω*`, of measure at most `(2n)^n |B(0,1)| t⁻¹ ∫ G`, and the set where
`(1 + 3^n) ‖(M(czGood g_j))_j‖_{ℓ_q} > t`, which Chebyshev's inequality bounds.

Rd.volume_image_eq_zero_of_lipschitzWith.name: Rd.volume_image_eq_zero_of_lipschitzWith
Rd.volume_image_eq_zero_of_lipschitzWith.docstring:
**Lipschitz maps keep null sets** between finite-dimensional inner product spaces of the same
dimension: `μ_H^k (f '' N) ≤ K^k μ_H^k N` for the Hausdorff measure `μ_H^k`, a Haar measure in
dimension `k` (Mathlib's `isAddHaarMeasure_hausdorffMeasure`), and Haar measures have the same null
sets.

Rd.volume_dyadicCell_ne_top.name: Rd.volume_dyadicCell_ne_top
Rd.volume_dyadicCell_ne_top.docstring: The cells have finite volume: `P_{j,m}` lies in the closed ball `B̄(c_{j,m}, n 2^(-j))`.

Rd.volume_dyadicCell.name: Rd.volume_dyadicCell
Rd.volume_dyadicCell.docstring: The cells of level `j ∈ ℕ` have volume `2^(-jn)`.

Rd.volume_dyadicAnnulus_le.name: Rd.volume_dyadicAnnulus_le
Rd.volume_dyadicAnnulus_le.docstring:
The annulus `j` has volume at most `ρ^n 2^(-jn) |B_1|`, the volume of the closed ball of
radius `ρ 2^(-j)` (`Rd.volume_closedBall_div_two_pow`).

Rd.volume_czEnlarged_le.name: Rd.volume_czEnlarged_le
Rd.volume_czEnlarged_le.docstring:
**The measure of the enlarged exceptional set**: `|Ω*| ≤ (2n)^n |B(0,1)| t⁻¹ ∫ G` for every
height `t`, by `Rd.cz_volume_le`.

Rd.volume_closedBall_zcellCenter.name: Rd.volume_closedBall_zcellCenter
Rd.volume_closedBall_zcellCenter.docstring:
The closed ball of radius `2n 2^(-k)` around the centre of a cube `Q_{k,m}` has volume
`(2n)^n |B(0,1)| |Q_{k,m}|`.

Rd.volume_closedBall_div_two_pow.name: Rd.volume_closedBall_div_two_pow
Rd.volume_closedBall_div_two_pow.docstring: The volume of the closed ball of radius `d 2^(-j)` is `d^n |B_1| 2^(-jn)` for `d ≥ 0`.

Rd.volume_ball_ne_zero.name: Rd.volume_ball_ne_zero
Rd.volume_ball_ne_zero.docstring: The ball `B(0,r)` of radius `r > 0` has positive volume.

Rd.volume_ball_div_two_pow.name: Rd.volume_ball_div_two_pow
Rd.volume_ball_div_two_pow.docstring:
**Volumes of dyadic balls**: a ball of radius `ρ 2^(-j)`, `ρ > 0`, around any centre has
volume `ρ^n |B_1| 2^(-jn)`, where `|B_1|` is the volume of the unit ball.

Rd.vectorWeakConst_ne_top.name: Rd.vectorWeakConst_ne_top
Rd.vectorWeakConst_ne_top.docstring: The weak type constant is finite for finite `B` and `H`.

Rd.vectorWeakConst.name: Rd.vectorWeakConst
Rd.vectorWeakConst.docstring:
The constant of the weak type `(1,1)` of a Calderón–Zygmund family with overlap `B` and
Hörmander constant `H`: `4 · 2^n B + (2n)^n |B(0, 1)| + 4H`, where `|B(0, 1)|` is the volume of
the unit ball of `V`, from the good part, the enlarged exceptional set and the bad part.

Rd.vanishOn.name: Rd.vanishOn
Rd.vanishOn.docstring:
**The elements of `H^s(V)` vanishing on `Ω`**: the `U ∈ H^s(V)` whose tempered distribution
vanishes on every real test function of the open set `Ω`, `U(φ) = 0` for all `φ ∈ 𝓓(Ω)`
(`Rd.mem_vanishOn_iff`). It is a closed subspace (`Rd.isClosed_vanishOn`); for `s ≥ 0` it
consists of the `U` whose `L_2` function vanishes almost everywhere on `Ω`
(`Rd.mem_vanishOn_iff_sobolevToL2`).

Rd.two_pow_smul_lpBlockKernel_succ_eq_su.name: Rd.two_pow_smul_lpBlockKernel_succ_eq_sum
Rd.two_pow_smul_lpBlockKernel_succ_eq_su.docstring:
**The dilated identity**: for all `m, j ∈ ℕ`,
`2^{jm} ψ_{j+1} = ∑_{i : Fin m → Fin n} ∂_{e_{i_0}} ⋯ ∂_{e_{i_{m-1}}} ((η_i)_{2^j})`, from
`Rd.sum_iteratedLineDerivOp_derivKernel`, the chain rule for dilations
(`Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_schwartzDilate`) and `(ψ_1)_{2^j} = ψ_{j+1}`.

Rd.two_pow_mul_enorm_le_ofReal.name: Rd.two_pow_mul_enorm_le_ofReal
Rd.two_pow_mul_enorm_le_ofReal.docstring: A point of norm at most `ρ 2^(-k)` has `2^k ‖w‖ ≤ ρ`, in `[0, ∞]`.

Rd.two_pow_mul_blockFun_succ_ae.name: Rd.two_pow_mul_blockFun_succ_ae
Rd.two_pow_mul_blockFun_succ_ae.docstring:
**The blocks of `f` as convolutions with its derivatives**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, if
`g_α ∈ L_p(V)` is the weak derivative `∂_{e_{α_0}} ⋯ ∂_{e_{α_{m-1}}} f` for every multi-index
`α`, then for almost every `x` and every `j`,
`2^{jm} (ψ_{j+1} ⋆ f)(x) = ∑_α ((η_α)_{2^j} ⋆ g_α)(x)`.
This is the dilated identity `2^{jm} ψ_{j+1} = ∑_α ∂^α ((η_α)_{2^j})`
(`Rd.two_pow_smul_lpBlockKernel_succ_eq_sum`) with each derivative moved from the kernel to `f`
(`Rd.conv_eq_conv_iteratedLineDerivOp`).

Rd.two_ne_top.name: Rd.two_ne_top
Rd.two_ne_top.docstring:
`2 ≠ ∞` in `ℝ≥0∞` (Mathlib's `ENNReal.ofNat_ne_top` at `2`): the hypothesis `p ≠ ∞` of the
blocks and the band-limited scheme on `L_2`. Its type fixes `p = 2` before the remaining
arguments are elaborated.

Rd.tsupport_shiftReflect_subset.name: Rd.tsupport_shiftReflect_subset
Rd.tsupport_shiftReflect_subset.docstring:
The support of the reflected translate `y ↦ η(x - y)` lies in `S` if `x - y ∈ S` for every
`y` in the support of `η`.

Rd.tsupport_halfSpaceCutoff_subset.name: Rd.tsupport_halfSpaceCutoff_subset
Rd.tsupport_halfSpaceCutoff_subset.docstring: **The closed support of `η_n` lies in `H₊`**: it lies in `{⟪y, e⟫ ≥ 1/(n + 1)}`.

Rd.tsupport_dilate_two_pow_subset.name: Rd.tsupport_dilate_two_pow_subset
Rd.tsupport_dilate_two_pow_subset.docstring:
**Supports of dyadic dilates**: if `K` vanishes outside a closed set `S` with
`c y ∈ S ⇒ y ∈ S` for `c ≥ 1`, then every dilate `K_{2^j}` is supported in `S`.

Rd.tsupport_bumpMollifier_subset.name: Rd.tsupport_bumpMollifier_subset
Rd.tsupport_bumpMollifier_subset.docstring: The mollifier of a bump function has its closed support in `B̄(c, r_out)`.

Rd.tsum_tail_le.name: Rd.tsum_tail_le
Rd.tsum_tail_le.docstring:
**The tail of the rate series**: `∑_{n > N} 2^(-sn) (n + 1)^a ≤ C 2^(-sN) (N + 1)^a` with
`C = ∑_l 2^(-sl) (l + 1)^a`, from `n + 1 ≤ (n - N + 1)(N + 1)`.

Rd.tsum_setLIntegral_dyadicAnnulus_le.name: Rd.tsum_setLIntegral_dyadicAnnulus_le
Rd.tsum_setLIntegral_dyadicAnnulus_le.docstring:
The integrals over the disjoint annuli sum to at most the integral over `V`
(Mathlib's `lintegral_iUnion`).

Rd.tsum_setLIntegral_czMaximal.name: Rd.tsum_setLIntegral_czMaximal
Rd.tsum_setLIntegral_czMaximal.docstring:
The sum over the maximal big cubes of the integrals of `h : V → [0, ∞]` over the cubes is
the integral of `h` over the exceptional set `Ω`, since the cubes are disjoint.

Rd.tsum_prod_le_prod_tsum.name: Rd.tsum_prod_le_prod_tsum
Rd.tsum_prod_le_prod_tsum.docstring:
**Sums of products over `ℕ^d`**: `∑_k ∏_i f_i(k_i) ≤ ∏_i ∑_j f_i(j)`, from the finite boxes
(Mathlib's `Finset.prod_univ_sum`).

Rd.tsum_nikolskii_le.name: Rd.tsum_nikolskii_le
Rd.tsum_nikolskii_le.docstring:
**The Nikolskii bounds are summable**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, every `r`, `s ∈ ℝ`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and
`f ∈ L_p(V)`,
`∑_j N_p^(1-p/r) 2^(jα) ‖ψ_j ⋆ f‖_p ≤ K_{V,p,r,s} ‖(2^(js) ‖Δ_j f‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`, since the weights
`2^(-j(s-α))` absorb the `ℓ_q` norm (`ENNReal.tsum_le_lqNorm_dyadicWeight`).

Rd.tsum_lintegral_lqNorm_czBadPart_le.name: Rd.tsum_lintegral_lqNorm_czBadPart_le
Rd.tsum_lintegral_lqNorm_czBadPart_le.docstring:
**The total mass of the bad pieces of a family**: for `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and almost everywhere
strongly measurable `g_j`, `∑_Q ∫ ‖(‖czBadPart_Q g_j‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ 2 ∫ ‖(‖g_j‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`, the
sum over the maximal big cubes `Q` of any function at any height.

Rd.tsum_lintegral_enorm_czBadPart_le.name: Rd.tsum_lintegral_enorm_czBadPart_le
Rd.tsum_lintegral_enorm_czBadPart_le.docstring:
**The total mass of the bad pieces**: `∑_Q ∫ ‖czBadPart_Q f‖ ≤ 2 ∫ ‖f‖`, the sum over the
maximal big cubes `Q` of `G` at height `t`, for every `f : V → E`.

Rd.tsum_le_mul_lintegral_of_le_setLInteg.name: Rd.tsum_le_mul_lintegral_of_le_setLIntegral
Rd.tsum_le_mul_lintegral_of_le_setLInteg.docstring:
**Summing bounds over the maximal big cubes**: if numbers `a_Q ∈ [0, ∞]` indexed by the
maximal big cubes `Q` of `G` at height `t` satisfy `a_Q ≤ c ∫_Q H` for a function
`H : V → [0, ∞]`, then `∑_Q a_Q ≤ c ∫ H`, since the cubes are disjoint
(`Rd.tsum_setLIntegral_czMaximal`).

Rd.tsum_indicator_dyadicCell.name: Rd.tsum_indicator_dyadicCell
Rd.tsum_indicator_dyadicCell.docstring:
The cells split every function: `g(y) = ∑_m (1_{P_{j,m}} g)(y)`, where only the cell
containing `y` contributes.

Rd.tsum_fourier_lpBlockKernel_sq_le.name: Rd.tsum_fourier_lpBlockKernel_sq_le
Rd.tsum_fourier_lpBlockKernel_sq_le.docstring:
**Overlap of the blocks**: `∑_j |𝓕ψ_j(ξ)|² ≤ 2` for every `ξ`, the case `s = 0` of
`Rd.tsum_dyadicWeight_fourier_lpBlockKernel_sq_le`.

Rd.tsum_fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_sq_le.name: Rd.tsum_fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_sq_le
Rd.tsum_fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_sq_le.docstring:
**Overlap of the synthesis kernels**: `∑_j |𝓕ψ̃_j(ξ)|² ≤ 4` for every `ξ`: at most four
kernels are nonzero at `ξ` (`Rd.mem_Icc_of_fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_ne_zero`), each of modulus at
most `1`.

Rd.tsum_fourier_dilate_besselKernelFamil.name: Rd.tsum_fourier_dilate_besselKernelFamily_sq_le
Rd.tsum_fourier_dilate_besselKernelFamil.docstring:
**Overlap of the dilated Bessel kernels**: if `ω̂` vanishes outside the annulus
`{a ≤ ‖ζ‖ ≤ 2^N a}`, `a > 0`, then `∑_j |𝓕(K_j)_{2^j}(ξ)|² ≤ Rd.besselOverlap a N σ ω̂` for every
`ξ`: a nonzero term needs `‖ξ‖ / 2^j ∈ [a, 2^N a]`
(`Rd.mem_annulus_of_fourier_dilate_besselKernelFamily_ne_zero`), so at most `N + 1` terms are
nonzero (`ENNReal.tsum_le_of_dyadic_annulus`), each bounded by
`Rd.enorm_fourier_dilate_besselKernelFamily_le`.

Rd.tsum_fourier_derivKernelFamily_sq_le.name: Rd.tsum_fourier_derivKernelFamily_sq_le
Rd.tsum_fourier_derivKernelFamily_sq_le.docstring:
**Overlap of a derivative family**: `∑_j |𝓕(η_i)_{2^j}(ξ)|² ≤ 2` for every `ξ`, by comparison
with the blocks (`Rd.enorm_fourier_derivKernelFamily_le`, `Rd.tsum_fourier_lpBlockKernel_sq_le`).

Rd.tsum_fourier_derivDualFamily_sq_le.name: Rd.tsum_fourier_derivDualFamily_sq_le
Rd.tsum_fourier_derivDualFamily_sq_le.docstring:
**Overlap of a dual derivative family**:
`∑_j |𝓕(∂^w G̃_j)_{2^j}(ξ)|² ≤ 4 ((8π)^k ∏_l ‖w_l‖)²` for every `ξ`, by
comparison with the synthesis kernels (`Rd.enorm_fourier_derivDualFamily_le`,
`Rd.tsum_fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_sq_le`).

Rd.tsum_enorm_fourier_dilate_sq_le.name: Rd.tsum_enorm_fourier_dilate_sq_le
Rd.tsum_enorm_fourier_dilate_sq_le.docstring:
**The Fourier overlap of the dilates of a mean-zero kernel**: for a Schwartz function `G`
with `∫ G = 0` and every `ξ`, `∑_j |𝓕(G_{2^j})(ξ)|² ≤ 4 C²` (`Rd.meanZeroOverlap G`), since
`𝓕(G_{2^j})(ξ) = 𝓕G(2^(-j) ξ)` and `∑_j min(2^(-j) ‖ξ‖, 2^j ‖ξ‖⁻¹) ≤ 4`
(`ENNReal.tsum_min_two_pow_le`).

Rd.tsum_enorm_convLp_sq_le_of_fourier_bo.name: Rd.tsum_enorm_convLp_sq_le_of_fourier_bound
Rd.tsum_enorm_convLp_sq_le_of_fourier_bo.docstring:
**The analysis bound on `L_2`**: for integrable kernels `θ_j` with Fourier overlap `B`,
`∑_j |𝓕θ_j(ξ)|² ≤ B` for almost every `ξ`, and every `f ∈ L_2(V)`,
`∑_j ‖θ_j ⋆ f‖_2² ≤ B ‖f‖_2²`. By `Rd.enorm_convLp_sq` the left side is
`∫ (∑_j |𝓕θ_j|²) |𝓕f|²` (Mathlib's `lintegral_tsum`), and Plancherel's theorem gives
`∫ |𝓕f|² = ‖f‖_2²`.

Rd.tsum_eLpNorm_blockFun_le.name: Rd.tsum_eLpNorm_blockFun_le
Rd.tsum_eLpNorm_blockFun_le.docstring:
**The `L_r` norms of the blocks are summable**: for `1 ≤ p ≤ r ≤ ∞`, `p < ∞`, `s ∈ ℝ`,
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and `f ∈ L_p(V)`,
`∑_j ‖ψ_j ⋆ f‖_r ≤ K_{V,p,r,s} ‖(2^(js) ‖Δ_j f‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}` (the Nikolskii inequality for
blocks and `Rd.tsum_nikolskii_le`).
