Rd.tsum_dyadicWeight_mul_setLIntegral_cl.name: Rd.tsum_dyadicWeight_mul_setLIntegral_closedBall_le
Rd.tsum_dyadicWeight_mul_setLIntegral_cl.docstring:
**Hardy's inequality for the balls**: for `G : V → [0, ∞]` with `G(0) = 0` and `b > 0`,
`∑_k 2^(kb) ∫_{|z| ≤ 2^(1-k)} G ≤ (1 - 2^(-b))⁻¹ 2^b ∫ G(z) / |z|^b dz`: each ball is the union
of the annuli `2^(-j) < |z| ≤ 2^(1-j)`, `j ≥ k`, and `ENNReal.hardy_tail_le` sums the tails.

Rd.tsum_dyadicWeight_mul_rpow_ne_top.name: Rd.tsum_dyadicWeight_mul_rpow_ne_top
Rd.tsum_dyadicWeight_mul_rpow_ne_top.docstring:
**A polynomial times a geometric series converges**:
`∑_l 2^(-sl) (l + 1)^a < ∞` for `s > 0` and `a ≥ 0` (Mathlib's
`summable_pow_mul_geometric_of_norm_lt_one`).

Rd.tsum_dyadicWeight_fourier_lpBlockKern.name: Rd.tsum_dyadicWeight_fourier_lpBlockKernel_sq_le
Rd.tsum_dyadicWeight_fourier_lpBlockKern.docstring:
**The Littlewood–Paley symbol is at most the Bessel weight**: for `s ≥ 0` and every `ξ ∈ V`,
`∑_j 2^(2js) |𝓕ψ_j(ξ)|² ≤ 2 · 4^s ⟨ξ⟩^{2s}`. At most two terms are nonzero
(`Rd.exists_fourier_lpBlockKernel_window`), each at most `4^s ⟨ξ⟩^{2s}`.

Rd.truncL2_ae_eq_fourierInv_indicator.name: Rd.truncL2_ae_eq_fourierInv_indicator
Rd.truncL2_ae_eq_fourierInv_indicator.docstring:
**The truncation as an inverse Fourier integral**: `truncL2 K F` agrees almost everywhere with
the pointwise inverse Fourier integral `x ↦ ∫ e^(2πi⟪ξ, x⟫) 1_{B_K}(ξ) 𝓕(toL2 F)(ξ) dξ`, since
`1_{B_K} 𝓕(toL2 F)` is integrable (`Rd.integrable_indicator_closedBall`,
`Rd.fourierInv_Lp_ae_eq_of_integrable`).

Rd.truncL2.name: Rd.truncL2
Rd.truncL2.docstring:
**The frequency truncation**: `truncL2 K F = 𝓕⁻(1_{B_K} 𝓕(toL2 F))`, the part of `F` with
frequencies in the closed ball `B_K = {|ξ| ≤ K}`, where `1_{B_K}` acts by the project's
`Rd.indicatorLp`.

Rd.triebelLizorkinSpace.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinSpace
Rd.triebelLizorkinSpace.docstring:
The **Triebel–Lizorkin space** `F^s_{p,q}` as a subspace of `L_p`, for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `s ∈ ℝ`
and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, with real scalars as `FunctionScheme.besovSpace`.

Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_zero_two_le.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_zero_two_le
Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_zero_two_le.docstring:
**The upper square function bound**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 < p < ∞` and
`f ∈ L_p(V)`, `‖f‖_{F^0_{p,2}} ≤ Q_{V,p} ‖f‖_p` with `Q_{V,p} = Rd.squareFunctionConst V p`. This is
the strong type of the analysis operator of the Calderón–Zygmund family `(ψ_j)_j`.

Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_zero_left.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_zero_left
Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_zero_left.docstring:
**Smoothness `0`**: `‖f‖_{F^0_{p,q}} = ‖ x ↦ ‖((ψ_j ⋆ f)(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p` for every `q`,
since the weights `2^(j·0)` are `1`.

Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_two_sq.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_two_sq
Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_two_sq.docstring:
**The Triebel–Lizorkin norm for `p = q = 2` on the Fourier side**: for `f ∈ L_2(V)`,
`‖f‖_{F^s_{2,2}}² = ∫ (∑_j 2^(2js) |𝓕ψ_j(ξ)|²) |𝓕f(ξ)|² dξ`, by
`‖f‖_{F^s_{2,2}} = ‖(2^(js) ‖Δ_j f‖_2)_j‖_{ℓ_2}`, Plancherel for each block and Tonelli.

Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_smul.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_smul
Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_smul.docstring: **The quasi-norm is homogeneous**: `‖c f‖_{F^s_{p,q}} = |c| ‖f‖_{F^s_{p,q}}` for `c ∈ ℂ`.

Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_mono_smoothness.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_mono_smoothness
Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_mono_smoothness.docstring:
**The quasi-norm increases in `s`**: `‖f‖_{F^s_{p,q}} ≤ ‖f‖_{F^t_{p,q}}` for `s ≤ t`, since
`2^(js) ≤ 2^(jt)`.

Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_le_of_hasWeakLine.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_le_of_hasWeakLineDeriv
Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_le_of_hasWeakLine.docstring:
**`W^m_p ⊆ F^m_{p,2}` with named constants**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 < p < ∞` and
`f ∈ L_p(V)` whose weak derivatives `g_α = ∂_{e_{α_0}} ⋯ ∂_{e_{α_{m-1}}} f` along the orthonormal
basis `e` of `Rd.gridBasis` lie in `L_p(V)` for every multi-index `α`,
`‖f‖_{F^m_{p,2}} ≤ ‖Φ‖_1 ‖f‖_p + 2^m ∑_α K_α ‖g_α‖_p` with `K_α = Rd.sobolevToTLConst V p α`.
The block `j = 0` is split off from the `ℓ_2` norm
(`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeight_le_zero_add_succ`) and bounded by Young's inequality
(`Rd.eLpNorm_blockFun_zero_le`); the other blocks by `Rd.eLpNorm_lqNorm_blockFun_succ_le`.

Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_le_littlewoodPale.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_le_littlewoodPaleyNorm_min
Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_le_littlewoodPale.docstring:
**The upper bound of the Triebel–Lizorkin quasi-norm**, behind `B^s_{p,min(p,q)} ⊆ F^s_{p,q}`:
for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `s ∈ ℝ` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`,
`‖f‖_{F^s_{p,q}} ≤ ‖(2^(js) ‖Δ_j f‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_{min(p,q)}}`. For `q = 2`: the quasi-norm of
`F^s_{p,2}` is at most the Littlewood–Paley quasi-norm of `B^s_{p,min(p,2)}`.

Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_le_approxNormDyad.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_le_approxNormDyadic
Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_le_approxNormDyad.docstring:
**`B^s_{p,min(p,q)} ⊆ F^s_{p,q}` with a constant**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `s ≥ 0` and
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `‖f‖_{F^s_{p,q}} ≤ 8 · 2^(3s) ‖Φ‖_1` times the approximation norm of `f` in
`A^s_{min(p,q)}` of the band-limited scheme.

Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_eq_littlewoodPale.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_eq_littlewoodPaleyNorm
Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_eq_littlewoodPale.docstring:
**For `q = p` the two quasi-norms agree**: for every `s ∈ ℝ`,
`‖f‖_{F^s_{p,p}} = ‖(2^(js) ‖Δ_j f‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_p}`, by Tonelli's theorem (`L_p(ℓ_p) = ℓ_p(L_p)`).

Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_add_le.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_add_le
Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_add_le.docstring:
**The quasi-norm is subadditive**: for `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`,
`‖f + g‖_{F^s_{p,q}} ≤ ‖f‖_{F^s_{p,q}} + ‖g‖_{F^s_{p,q}}`, by the triangle inequalities in
`ℓ_q` at every point and in `L_p`.

Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr_toTemperedDi.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr_toTemperedDistribution
Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr_toTemperedDi.docstring:
**Compatibility with `L_p`**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `f ∈ L_p(V)`, the quasi-norm of the
tempered distribution of `f` is the Triebel–Lizorkin quasi-norm `‖f‖_{F^s_{p,q}}` of
`Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm`: the case of the kernel of the project
(`Rd.LPKernel.kernelTriebelLizorkinNormDistr_toTemperedDistribution`,
`Rd.LPKernel.standardKernel_kernelTriebelLizorkinNorm`).

Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr_le.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr_le
Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr_le.docstring:
The quasi-norm is at most that of any family of `L_p` functions representing the blocks
(`Rd.LPKernel.kernelTriebelLizorkinNormDistr_le`).

Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr_fourierMulti.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr_fourierMultiplier_le
Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr_fourierMulti.docstring:
**The multiplier bound for one family of blocks**: for a function `m` of temperate growth
with `m(D) ψ̃_j = 2^{jσ} (G_j)_{2^j}` and `(G_j)` uniformly Schwartz with bounds `A`, `1 < p < ∞`,
`1 < q ≤ ∞` and `N > n`, if the blocks of `u` are `L_p` functions `g_j`, then
`‖m(D) u‖_{F^{s-σ}_{p,q}} ≤ C_{n,N} C_{A,0,N} C_{FS} ‖ x ↦ ‖(2^{js} |g_j(x)|)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p`
with the Fefferman–Stein constant `C_{FS} = Rd.feffermanSteinConst V p q`. The blocks of
`m(D) u` are the convolutions `(m(D) ψ̃_j) ⋆ g_j`
(`Rd.distribBlock_fourierMultiplierCLM_eq_convLp`), bounded at almost every point by
`Rd.dyadicWeight_mul_enorm_conv_le_maximalFunction`, and
`Rd.eLpNorm_le_of_le_lqNorm_maximalFunction` applies.

Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr_eq_top.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr_eq_top
Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr_eq_top.docstring:
If some block of `u` is no `L_p` function, the quasi-norm is `∞`
(`Rd.LPKernel.kernelTriebelLizorkinNormDistr_eq_top`).

Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr_eq.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr_eq
Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr_eq.docstring:
**The quasi-norm of the representing family**: if the blocks of `u` are the `L_p` functions
`g_j`, the quasi-norm is `‖ x ↦ ‖(2^{js} |g_j(x)|)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p`
(`Rd.LPKernel.kernelTriebelLizorkinNormDistr_eq`).

Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr
Rd.triebelLizorkinNormDistr.docstring:
The **Triebel–Lizorkin quasi-norm of a tempered distribution** `u`, the quasi-norm
`Rd.LPKernel.kernelTriebelLizorkinNormDistr` of the kernel of the project
(`Rd.LPKernel.standardKernel`): `‖ x ↦ ‖(2^{js} |g_j(x)|)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p` when every block `Δ_j u` is
(the tempered distribution of) an `L_p` function `g_j`, and `∞` otherwise.

Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm.name: Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm
Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm.docstring:
The **Triebel–Lizorkin quasi-norm** `‖ x ↦ ‖(2^(js) |ψ_j ⋆ f(x)|)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p` of
`f ∈ L_p`: the `ℓ_q` norm of the weighted blocks at each point, then the `L_p` norm. The
Littlewood–Paley quasi-norm of the Besov spaces (`Rd.littlewoodPaleyNorm`) takes the two norms in
the other order. For `q = 0` the quasi-norm is `0`; the results assume `1 ≤ q`.

Rd.totallyBounded_setOf_lipschitzWith.name: Rd.totallyBounded_setOf_lipschitzWith
Rd.totallyBounded_setOf_lipschitzWith.docstring:
**Arzelà–Ascoli for Lipschitz functions**: on a compact metric space `X`, the bounded
continuous functions with `|g| ≤ C` that are Lipschitz with constant `L` form a totally bounded
set in the uniform norm (Mathlib's `BoundedContinuousFunction.arzela_ascoli`: the family is
equicontinuous and takes values in the compact disc of radius `C`).

Rd.toTemperedDistribution_weakDerivL2.name: Rd.toTemperedDistribution_weakDerivL2
Rd.toTemperedDistribution_weakDerivL2.docstring:
**Weak derivatives of `H^1(V)` are distributional derivatives**: for `U ∈ H^1(V)` and every
direction `v`, the tempered distribution of the weak derivative `∂_v U ∈ L_2(V)` is the derivative
`∂_v` of the distribution `U` (`Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_top_iff`, `Rd.toTemperedDistribution_toL2`).

Rd.toTemperedDistribution_toL2.name: Rd.toTemperedDistribution_toL2
Rd.toTemperedDistribution_toL2.docstring:
**`toL2 F` represents `F`**: the tempered distribution of the `L_2` function `toL2 F` is the
distribution `F.toDistr`. Indeed `F.toDistr = J_{-1}(J_1 F)` (Mathlib's
`BesselPotentialSpace.besselPotential_neg_toLp_eq`), and the Fourier transform of `J_{-1} g` is
`⟨ξ⟩⁻¹ 𝓕g`, which for `g ∈ L_2` is the distribution of the `L_2` function `⟨ξ⟩⁻¹ 𝓕g`
(`Rd.smulLeftCLM_toTemperedDistribution_eq`).

Rd.toTemperedDistribution_sobolevToL2.name: Rd.toTemperedDistribution_sobolevToL2
Rd.toTemperedDistribution_sobolevToL2.docstring:
**`ι_s U` represents `U`**: the tempered distribution of the `L_2` function `ι_s U` is `U`,
since `J_0` is the identity (Mathlib's `TemperedDistribution.besselPotential_zero`) and the
inclusion `ι_{0,s}` keeps the distribution (`Rd.toDistr_sobolevInclusion`).

Rd.toTemperedDistribution_eq_of_ae_eq.name: Rd.toTemperedDistribution_eq_of_ae_eq
Rd.toTemperedDistribution_eq_of_ae_eq.docstring:
**Almost everywhere equal classes are the same tempered distribution**: if `f ∈ L_p(V)` and
`g ∈ L_r(V)`, `1 ≤ p, r ≤ ∞`, have almost everywhere equal representatives, then
`∫ u g = ∫ u f` for every Schwartz function `u` (Mathlib's
`MeasureTheory.Lp.toTemperedDistribution_apply`, `MeasureTheory.integral_congr_ae`).

Rd.toReal_enorm_add_sum.name: Rd.toReal_enorm_add_sum
Rd.toReal_enorm_add_sum.docstring:
`(‖x‖ₑ + ∑_i ‖y_i‖ₑ).toReal = ‖x‖ + ∑_i ‖y_i‖` in a normed group: the norm
`‖x‖ + ∑_i ‖y_i‖` in `ℝ≥0∞` and in `ℝ`.

Rd.toLp_sobolevInclusion.name: Rd.toLp_sobolevInclusion
Rd.toLp_sobolevInclusion.docstring: The `L_2` function `J_t (ι_{t,s} U)` of the inclusion is `𝓕⁻(⟨ξ⟩^{t-s} 𝓕(J_s U))`.

Rd.toLp_sobolevConv.name: Rd.toLp_sobolevConv
Rd.toLp_sobolevConv.docstring: The `L_2` function `J_s (K ⋆ U)` of the convolution is `K ⋆ J_s U`.

Rd.toLp_schwartz.name: Rd.toLp_schwartz
Rd.toLp_schwartz.docstring:
**The `L_2` function of a Schwartz function in `H^t(V)`**: for a Schwartz function `u`, the
element `u ∈ H^t(V)` (Mathlib's `SchwartzMap.memSobolev`) has `J_t u` as its `L_2` function, since
`L_2` functions are determined by their distributions (`Rd.eq_of_toTemperedDistribution_eq`).

Rd.toLp_ofTest.name: Rd.toLp_ofTest
Rd.toLp_ofTest.docstring: The `L_2` function of a test function `φ` in `H^t(V)` is `J_t φ` (`Rd.toLp_schwartz`).

Rd.toL2_ofSchwartz.name: Rd.toL2_ofSchwartz
Rd.toL2_ofSchwartz.docstring:
The `L_2` function of a Schwartz function `w` in `H^1(V)` is `w`
(`Rd.toL2_eq_of_toDistr_eq`).

Rd.toL2_eq_of_toDistr_eq.name: Rd.toL2_eq_of_toDistr_eq
Rd.toL2_eq_of_toDistr_eq.docstring:
An `L_2` function `f` is `toL2 F` as soon as its tempered distribution is `F.toDistr`:
`L_2` functions are determined by their distributions (`Rd.eq_of_toTemperedDistribution_eq`).

Rd.toL2.name: Rd.toL2
Rd.toL2.docstring:
**An element of `H^1(V)` as an `L_2` function**: for `F ∈ H^{1,2}(V, ℂ)`, given by the
tempered distribution `u = F.toDistr` and the `L_2` function `J_1 u = F.toLp`, the `L_2`
function `𝓕⁻(⟨ξ⟩⁻¹ 𝓕(J_1 u))`, which is `u` (`Rd.toTemperedDistribution_toL2`).

Rd.toDistr_testSchwartz_eq_integral_sobo.name: Rd.toDistr_testSchwartz_eq_integral_sobolevToL2
Rd.toDistr_testSchwartz_eq_integral_sobo.docstring:
For `s ≥ 0`, `U ∈ H^s(V)` and a real test function `φ` of `Ω`, `U(φ) = ∫ φ · ι_s U`, the
integral of `φ` against the `L_2` function `ι_s U` of `U`
(`Rd.toTemperedDistribution_sobolevToL2`).

Rd.toDistr_sobolevInclusion.name: Rd.toDistr_sobolevInclusion
Rd.toDistr_sobolevInclusion.docstring:
**The inclusion keeps the distribution**: `ι_{t,s} U = U` as tempered distributions. The
`L_2` function of `ι_{t,s} U` is `J_{t-s}(J_s U)`
(`Rd.fourierMultiplierCLM_toTemperedDistribution_eq`), so the distribution of `ι_{t,s} U` is
`J_{-t} J_{t-s} J_s U = J_0 U = U` (Mathlib's
`TemperedDistribution.besselPotential_besselPotential_apply`,
`TemperedDistribution.besselPotential_zero`).

Rd.toDistr_ofTest.name: Rd.toDistr_ofTest
Rd.toDistr_ofTest.docstring: The tempered distribution of `ofTest s φ` is the Schwartz function `φ`.

Rd.toDistr_ofSchwartz.name: Rd.toDistr_ofSchwartz
Rd.toDistr_ofSchwartz.docstring:
The tempered distribution of `ofSchwartz s w` is the Schwartz function `w`, since
`J_{-s} J_s = J_0 = id` (Mathlib's `TemperedDistribution.besselPotential_besselPotential_apply`).

Rd.toDistr_besselShift_eq_besselPotentia.name: Rd.toDistr_besselShift_eq_besselPotential_toLp
Rd.toDistr_besselShift_eq_besselPotentia.docstring: The distribution of `besselShift s U` is `J_s` of the `L_2` function `J_s U`.

Rd.tlToSobolevConst_ne_top.name: Rd.tlToSobolevConst_ne_top
Rd.tlToSobolevConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant `Rd.tlToSobolevConst p w` is finite for `1 < p < ∞`.

Rd.tlToSobolevConst.name: Rd.tlToSobolevConst
Rd.tlToSobolevConst.docstring:
The constant `C_w = S_{V,p}(4 ((8π)^k ∏_l ‖w_l‖)², 4 H_{Ã^w})` of the bound
`F^k_{p,2} ⊆ W^k_p` for the directions `w ∈ V^k`: the strong type constant `Rd.czConst` of the
Calderón–Zygmund family `((∂^w G̃_j)_{2^j})_j` of the rescaled derivatives of the synthesis
kernels (`Rd.isCZFamily_derivDualFamily`).

Rd.tlDiffNorm.name: Rd.tlDiffNorm
Rd.tlDiffNorm.docstring:
The **ball means quasi-norm of Triebel–Lizorkin type**
`‖f‖_p + ‖ x ↦ ‖(2^(js) d_j f(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p` of `f ∈ L_p`, with the ball means of
differences of order `L`: the `ℓ_q` norm at each point, then the `L_p` norm.

Rd.tlCoeffNorm.name: Rd.tlCoeffNorm
Rd.tlCoeffNorm.docstring:
The **quasi-norm of the sequence space `f^s_{p,q}`**:
`‖λ‖_{f^s_{p,q}} = ‖ x ↦ ‖(2^(js) |λ_{j,m_j(x)}|)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p`, where `P_{j,m_j(x)}` is the cell
of level `j` containing `x`: the `ℓ_q` norm at each point, then the `L_p` norm.

Rd.tildeToRestrictionL.name: Rd.tildeToRestrictionL
Rd.tildeToRestrictionL.docstring:
**From `H̃^s(Ω)` to `H^s(Ω)`**: the restriction of the elements of `H̃^s(Ω)` to `Ω`, an
operator of norm at most `1` with values in `H^s_0(Ω)` (`Rd.range_tildeToRestrictionL_le`).

Rd.tildeToRestriction.name: Rd.tildeToRestriction
Rd.tildeToRestriction.docstring:
**Restriction as an isometry of `H̃^1(Ω)` into `H^1(Ω)`**: for every open set `Ω`, the
restriction `H̃^1(Ω) → H^1(Ω)` as a linear isometry (`Rd.norm_restrictProj_of_mem_tildeSpace`),
the case `s = 1` of `H̃^s(Ω) = H^s_0(Ω)`.

Rd.tildeEquivRestriction.name: Rd.tildeEquivRestriction
Rd.tildeEquivRestriction.docstring:
**`H̃^s(Ω) ≅ H^{-s}(Ω)` by `J_{2s}`**: for every open set `Ω` and every real `s`,
`besselShift s` restricts to an isometric isomorphism of `H̃^s(Ω)` onto `H^{-s}(Ω)`
(`Rd.map_tildeSpace_besselShift`, Mathlib's `LinearIsometryEquiv.submoduleMap`).

Rd.testSpan.name: Rd.testSpan
Rd.testSpan.docstring:
**The test functions of `Ω` in `H^s(V)`**: the complex linear span of the `ofTest s φ`,
`φ` a real test function of `Ω`.

Rd.testSchwartz_apply.name: Rd.testSchwartz_apply
Rd.testSchwartz_apply.docstring: The values of `Rd.testSchwartz φ` are those of `φ`.

Rd.testSchwartz.name: Rd.testSchwartz
Rd.testSchwartz.docstring:
A real test function `φ` on an open set `Ω` as a complex Schwartz function on `V`,
`x ↦ (φ x : ℂ)`: it is smooth with compact support (Mathlib's
`HasCompactSupport.toSchwartzMap`).

Rd.testFunctionMulOn.name: Rd.testFunctionMulOn
Rd.testFunctionMulOn.docstring:
The product `φ χ` of a real test function `φ` on `O` with a smooth real function `χ` whose
closed support lies in `B` is a test function on `O ∩ B`.

Rd.testFunctionMul.name: Rd.testFunctionMul
Rd.testFunctionMul.docstring:
The product `φ χ` of a real test function `φ` on `Ω` with a smooth real function `χ` is a test
function on `Ω`.

Rd.tensorKernel.name: Rd.tensorKernel
Rd.tensorKernel.docstring: The **tensor product** `(⊗K)(x) = ∏_i K_i(x_i)` of one-dimensional kernels.

Rd.tendsto_truncL2.name: Rd.tendsto_truncL2
Rd.tendsto_truncL2.docstring: **The truncations converge to `toL2`** in operator norm as `K → ∞`.

Rd.tendsto_sum_mixedBlock.name: Rd.tendsto_sum_mixedBlock
Rd.tendsto_sum_mixedBlock.docstring:
**The tensor Littlewood–Paley decomposition**: `∑_{k ≤ J} δ_k ⋆ f → f` in `L_p` over the boxes
`{k : k_i ≤ J}`.

Rd.tendsto_sum_lpBlock.name: Rd.tendsto_sum_lpBlock
Rd.tendsto_sum_lpBlock.docstring:
**Reconstruction**: the partial sums of the blocks converge to `f` in `L_p`, since
`Φ_J ⋆ f → f` (`Rd.tendsto_convLp_dilate` with `∫ Φ = 1`).

Rd.tendsto_sum_distribBlock.name: Rd.tendsto_sum_distribBlock
Rd.tendsto_sum_distribBlock.docstring:
**The Littlewood–Paley decomposition of tempered distributions**: for every tempered
distribution `u` on `V`, `∑_{j < J} Δ_j u → u` in `𝓢'(V, ℂ)`. Tested against a Schwartz function
`φ`, `∑_{j ≤ J} Δ_j u (φ) = u(𝓕(χ_J 𝓕⁻¹ φ))` with the cut-offs `χ_J = χ(2^{-J} ·)`
(`Rd.sum_distribBlock`, `Rd.smulLeftCLM_sum_fourier_lpBlockKernelS`), and `χ_J 𝓕⁻¹ φ → 𝓕⁻¹ φ` in the
Schwartz space (`Rd.tendsto_cutoffMul`); `𝓕` and `u` are continuous.

Rd.tendsto_sobolevConv_dilate.name: Rd.tendsto_sobolevConv_dilate
Rd.tendsto_sobolevConv_dilate.docstring:
**Mollification converges in `H^s(V)`**, for every real `s`: let `η` be integrable with
`∫ η = 1`, `c_i ≠ 0` dilation factors with `c_i → ∞` and `η_c(x) = c^n η(c x)`. Then
`η_{c_i} ⋆ U → U` in `H^s(V)` for every `U ∈ H^s(V)`, since `‖η_c ⋆ U - U‖_{H^s}` is the `L_2`
norm of `η_c ⋆ J_s U - J_s U` (`Rd.toLp_sobolevConv`, Mathlib's
`BesselPotentialSpace.norm_toLp_eq`) and approximate identities converge in `L_2(V)`
(`Rd.tendsto_convLp_dilate`).

Rd.tendsto_integral_testFunction_smul.name: Rd.tendsto_integral_testFunction_smul
Rd.tendsto_integral_testFunction_smul.docstring:
**Convergence in `L_p(Ω)` gives convergence of the pairings with a test function**: if
`h_i → h` in `L_p(Ω)`, `1 ≤ p`, with `h ∈ L_p(Ω)` and `h_i ∈ L_p(Ω)` eventually, then
`∫ φ h_i → ∫ φ h` for every test function `φ` on `Ω`.

Rd.tendsto_integral_halfSpaceCutoff_smul.name: Rd.tendsto_integral_halfSpaceCutoff_smul
Rd.tendsto_integral_halfSpaceCutoff_smul.docstring:
**The cutoffs in the limit**: for `F` integrable on `H₊`, `∫ η_n F → ∫_{H₊} F`, by dominated
convergence: `|η_n| ≤ 1`, `η_n → 1` on `H₊` and `η_n = 0` outside `H₊`.

Rd.tendsto_integral_deriv_halfSpaceCutof.name: Rd.tendsto_integral_deriv_halfSpaceCutoff_smul
Rd.tendsto_integral_deriv_halfSpaceCutof.docstring:
**The derivatives of the cutoffs in the limit**: if `c` is continuous with compact support and
`|c(y)| ≤ C ⟪y, e⟫` on `H₊`, and `u` is integrable on every bounded part `H₊ ∩ B(0, R)`, then
`∫ s'((n + 1)⟪y, e⟫ - 1) (n + 1) c(y) u(y) dy → 0`. By the strip estimate
(`Rd.abs_deriv_smoothTransition_mul_le`) the integrands are bounded by `2 D C |u|` on
`H₊ ∩ B(0, R)`, vanish elsewhere (`Rd.deriv_smoothTransition_mul_eq_zero`), and tend to `0`
pointwise, since `s' = 0` on `(1, ∞)`.

Rd.tendsto_halfSpaceCutoff.name: Rd.tendsto_halfSpaceCutoff
Rd.tendsto_halfSpaceCutoff.docstring: **The cutoffs tend to `1` on `H₊`**: `η_n(y) = 1` as soon as `(n + 1)⟪y, e⟫ ≥ 2`.

Rd.tendsto_eLpNorm_sum_conv_dualLpBlockK.name: Rd.tendsto_eLpNorm_sum_conv_dualLpBlockKernel_blockFun_sub
Rd.tendsto_eLpNorm_sum_conv_dualLpBlockK.docstring:
**The reproducing formula**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `f ∈ L_p(V)`,
`∑_{j < J} ψ̃_j ⋆ (ψ_j ⋆ f) → f` in `L_p(V)` as `J → ∞`, since the partial sums are the
partial sums `∑_{j < J} Δ_j f` of the Littlewood–Paley decomposition (`Rd.tendsto_sum_lpBlock`).

Rd.tendsto_eLpNorm_mollify_sub_restrict.name: Rd.tendsto_eLpNorm_mollify_sub_restrict
Rd.tendsto_eLpNorm_mollify_sub_restrict.docstring:
**Mollifiers converge in `L_1` of a set**: for an integrable `h` that agrees with `h'` almost
everywhere on `K`, the mollifications `η_{k+1} ⋆ h` with the standard bump
`η = Rd.LocalMeansBump.std` converge to `h'` in `L_1(K)` (`Rd.tendsto_eLpNorm_conv_dilate_sub`
with `p = 1`).

Rd.tendsto_eLpNorm_conv_dilate_sub.name: Rd.tendsto_eLpNorm_conv_dilate_sub
Rd.tendsto_eLpNorm_conv_dilate_sub.docstring:
**Approximate identities in `L_p`**: for an integrable `Φ` with `∫ Φ = 1` and `f ∈ L_p`,
`1 ≤ p < ∞`, `‖Φ_c ⋆ f - f‖_p → 0` as `c → ∞`.

Rd.tendsto_cutoffMul.name: Rd.tendsto_cutoffMul
Rd.tendsto_cutoffMul.docstring:
**The cut-offs converge in the Schwartz space**: `χ_n u → u` in `𝓢(V, ℂ)`, since every
Schwartz seminorm of `u - χ_n u` is `O(1/(n+1))` (`Rd.seminorm_sub_cutoffMul_le`, Mathlib's
`schwartz_withSeminorms`). Hence smooth compactly supported functions are dense in
`𝓢(V, ℂ)`.

Rd.tendsto_convLp_dilate.name: Rd.tendsto_convLp_dilate
Rd.tendsto_convLp_dilate.docstring:
**Approximate identities as operators on `L_p`**: for an integrable `Φ` with `∫ Φ = 1`,
dilation factors `c_i ≠ 0` with `c_i → ∞` and `f ∈ L_p`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `Φ_{c_i} ⋆ f → f` in `L_p`
(Mathlib's `Lp.tendsto_Lp_iff_tendsto_eLpNorm'`).

Rd.tendsto_areaFactor.name: Rd.tendsto_areaFactor
Rd.tendsto_areaFactor.docstring: The area factor tends to `1` as `ε → 0+`, by continuity.

Rd.tendsto_apply_apply_of_tendsto.name: Rd.tendsto_apply_apply_of_tendsto
Rd.tendsto_apply_apply_of_tendsto.docstring:
**Uniformly bounded operators applied twice**: if additive maps `T_i : E → E` satisfy
`‖T_i g‖ ≤ C ‖g‖` for all `i` and `g`, and `T_i f → f`, then `T_i (T_i f) → f`, since
`T_i (T_i f) - f = T_i (T_i f - f) + (T_i f - f)` has norm at most `(C + 1) ‖T_i f - f‖`.

Rd.tailConst_ne_top.name: Rd.tailConst_ne_top
Rd.tailConst_ne_top.docstring: The tail constant of a Schwartz function is finite.

Rd.tailConst_le_familyTailConst.name: Rd.tailConst_le_familyTailConst
Rd.tailConst_le_familyTailConst.docstring: Every member of a uniform family has tail constant at most that of the family.

Rd.tailConst.name: Rd.tailConst
Rd.tailConst.docstring:
The constant `schwartzDecayConst G 0 (N + r + n + 1) · ∫ (1 + ‖u‖)^(-(n+1)) du` of the
tails of a Schwartz function.

Rd.symbolKernelFamily.name: Rd.symbolKernelFamily
Rd.symbolKernelFamily.docstring: The **symbol kernel family** `K_j = 𝓕⁻¹[2^{-jσ} m(2^j ·) ω̂]` of a Schwartz function `ω̂`.

Rd.symbolFamily.name: Rd.symbolFamily
Rd.symbolFamily.docstring:
The **symbol family** of a Schwartz function `ω̂`: `j ↦ (ζ ↦ 2^{-jσ} m(2^j ζ) ω̂(ζ))`, a
Schwartz function when `m` has temperate growth (Mathlib's `SchwartzMap.smulLeftCLM`).

Rd.symbolBase.name: Rd.symbolBase
Rd.symbolBase.docstring:
The **symbol kernels of a family** `(ω_j)` of Schwartz functions:
`K_j = 𝓕⁻¹[2^{-jσ} m(2^j ·) 𝓕ω_j]`, the symbol kernel of `𝓕ω_j` at the scale `j`
(`Rd.symbolKernelFamily`), so that `m(D) (ω_j)_{2^j} = 2^{jσ} (K_j)_{2^j}`
(`Rd.fourierMultiplierCLM_schwartzDilate`).

Rd.switchSet_zero.name: Rd.switchSet_zero
Rd.switchSet_zero.docstring: There are no switch points for the zero step: `S_0(U) = ∅`.

Rd.switchSet_eq_symmDiff.name: Rd.switchSet_eq_symmDiff
Rd.switchSet_eq_symmDiff.docstring:
**The switch set is a symmetric difference**: `S_h(U) = U ∆ (U - h)`, where
`U - h = {x | x + h ∈ U}` (Mathlib's `symmDiff`, with `Set.mem_symmDiff`).

Rd.switchSet.name: Rd.switchSet
Rd.switchSet.docstring:
The **switch set** of `U` for the step `h`: the points `x` for which exactly one of `x` and
`x + h` lies in `U`. It is the set where `1_U(x + h) - 1_U(x) ≠ 0`.

Rd.summable_levelSum.name: Rd.summable_levelSum
Rd.summable_levelSum.docstring:
The pointwise sums of a level converge: at most `N` atoms of the level with nonzero
coefficients are nonzero at a point.

Rd.sum_tensorKernel_piFinset.name: Rd.sum_tensorKernel_piFinset
Rd.sum_tensorKernel_piFinset.docstring:
**Sums of tensor products over boxes**:
`∑_{k ∈ ∏_i t_i} ⊗(K_i(k_i)) = ⊗(∑_{j ∈ t_i} K_i(j))`.

Rd.sum_snoc_le.name: Rd.sum_snoc_le
Rd.sum_snoc_le.docstring:
**Words with a fixed last letter**: for nonnegative `a`, the sum over the words `(w, j)` of
length `k + 1` that end with `j` is at most the sum over all words of length `k + 1` (the map
`w ↦ (w, j)` is injective, Mathlib's `Fin.snoc_left_injective`).

Rd.sum_range_sum_snoc_le.name: Rd.sum_range_sum_snoc_le
Rd.sum_range_sum_snoc_le.docstring:
**The sums of the induction step**: the sum over the words of length `k' + 1 ≤ k + 1` that end
with `j` is at most the sum over all words of length at most `k + 1` (`Rd.sum_snoc_le`).

Rd.sum_range_fourier_lpBlockKernel.name: Rd.sum_range_fourier_lpBlockKernel
Rd.sum_range_fourier_lpBlockKernel.docstring:
**The Fourier transforms of the blocks telescope**:
`∑_{j ≤ J} 𝓕ψ_j(ξ) = 𝓕Φ_J(ξ)`.

Rd.sum_prod_mul_derivSymbol.name: Rd.sum_prod_mul_derivSymbol
Rd.sum_prod_mul_derivSymbol.docstring:
**The symbols invert the derivatives**: for every `ξ ≠ 0`,
`∑_i (∏_k 2πi ⟪ξ, e_{i_k}⟫) σ_i(ξ) = 1`, since each term is
`(∏_k ⟪ξ, e_{i_k}⟫)² / ‖ξ‖^{2m}` and these add up to `1` (`Rd.norm_pow_eq_sum_prod_inner`).

Rd.sum_mixedLpBlockKernel.name: Rd.sum_mixedLpBlockKernel
Rd.sum_mixedLpBlockKernel.docstring:
**The blocks sum to an approximate identity**: over the boxes `{k : k_i ≤ J}`,
`∑_k δ_k = (⊗Φ)_{2^J}`.

Rd.sum_lpBlockKernel.name: Rd.sum_lpBlockKernel
Rd.sum_lpBlockKernel.docstring: **The blocks add up to the dilated kernel**: `∑_{j ≤ J} ψ_j = Φ_J`.

Rd.sum_lpBlock.name: Rd.sum_lpBlock
Rd.sum_lpBlock.docstring: **The blocks telescope**: `∑_{j ≤ J} Δ_j f = Φ_J ⋆ f`.

Rd.sum_lineDerivOp_schwartzDilate_diverg.name: Rd.sum_lineDerivOp_schwartzDilate_divergenceSchwartz
Rd.sum_lineDerivOp_schwartzDilate_diverg.docstring:
**The divergence identity at every scale**: for `c ≠ 0`,
`∑_i ∂_{b_i} (K_{b_i})_c = c (m_2 - m)_c`, by the chain rule for dilations
(`Rd.lineDerivOp_schwartzDilate`).

Rd.sum_lineDerivOp_divergenceSchwartz.name: Rd.sum_lineDerivOp_divergenceSchwartz
Rd.sum_lineDerivOp_divergenceSchwartz.docstring:
**The divergence identity for Schwartz kernels**: `∑_i ∂_{b_i} K_{b_i} = m_2 - m` pointwise
(`Rd.sum_fderiv_divergenceKernel`).

Rd.sum_le_card_rpow_mul_lqNorm.name: Rd.sum_le_card_rpow_mul_lqNorm
Rd.sum_le_card_rpow_mul_lqNorm.docstring:
**Hölder's inequality on a finite set**: `∑_{k ∈ S} x_k ≤ #S^(1-1/q) ‖x‖_{ℓ_q}` for
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`.

Rd.sum_jacksonCoeff_smul_pow.name: Rd.sum_jacksonCoeff_smul_pow
Rd.sum_jacksonCoeff_smul_pow.docstring:
**The polynomial of the moment kernels**: in a commutative `ℂ`-algebra,
`∑_{l<L} (-1)^l C(L, l + 1) Y^(l+1) = 1 - (-1)^L (Y - 1)^L`, by the binomial theorem.

Rd.sum_jacksonCoeff.name: Rd.sum_jacksonCoeff
Rd.sum_jacksonCoeff.docstring:
**The coefficients add up to `1`**: `∑_{l<r} (-1)^l C(r, l + 1) = 1` for `r ≥ 1`, since
`∑_{l ≤ r} (-1)^(r-l) C(r, l) = (1 - 1)^r = 0`.

Rd.sum_iteratedLineDerivOp_derivKernel.name: Rd.sum_iteratedLineDerivOp_derivKernel
Rd.sum_iteratedLineDerivOp_derivKernel.docstring:
**`ψ_1` as a sum of derivatives**: for every `m ∈ ℕ`,
`∑_{i : Fin m → Fin n} ∂_{e_{i_0}} ⋯ ∂_{e_{i_{m-1}}} η_i = ψ_1` as Schwartz functions. Both sides
have the same Fourier transform: `(∑_i ∏_k 2πi ⟪ξ, e_{i_k}⟫ σ_i(ξ)) 𝓕ψ_1(ξ) = 𝓕ψ_1(ξ)` for
`ξ ≠ 0` (`Rd.sum_prod_mul_derivSymbol`), and `𝓕ψ_1(0) = 0`.

Rd.sum_fourier_lpBlockKernelS_apply.name: Rd.sum_fourier_lpBlockKernelS_apply
Rd.sum_fourier_lpBlockKernelS_apply.docstring:
**The Fourier transforms of the blocks add up to a cut-off**:
`∑_{j ≤ J} 𝓕ψ_j(ξ) = χ(2^{-J} ξ)` with `χ = Rd.cutoff 1 2` (`Rd.sum_range_fourier_lpBlockKernel`,
`Rd.fourier_dilatedLpKernel`).

Rd.sum_fderiv_inner_mul.name: Rd.sum_fderiv_inner_mul
Rd.sum_fderiv_inner_mul.docstring:
**The divergence of `x A(x)`**: for an orthonormal basis `(b_i)` of `V` and `A`
differentiable at `x`, `∑_i ∂_{b_i} (⟪b_i, ·⟫ A)(x) = n A(x) + DA(x) x`, since
`∑_i ⟪b_i, x⟫ b_i = x` (Mathlib's `OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr'`).

Rd.sum_fderiv_divergenceKernel.name: Rd.sum_fderiv_divergenceKernel
Rd.sum_fderiv_divergenceKernel.docstring:
**The divergence identity**: for an orthonormal basis `(b_i)` of `V` and `m ∈ C^1`,
`∑_i ∂_{b_i} K_{b_i}(x) = m_2(x) - m(x)` with the divergence kernels
`K_{b_i}(x) = ⟪b_i, x⟫ A_m(x)`: the left side is `n A_m(x) + D A_m(x) x`
(`Rd.sum_fderiv_inner_mul`), and `Rd.dilate_two_sub_eq`.

Rd.sum_distribBlock.name: Rd.sum_distribBlock
Rd.sum_distribBlock.docstring:
**Partial sums of the blocks as one multiplier**: `∑_{j ≤ J} Δ_j u` is the Fourier multiplier
with `χ(2^{-J} ·)` (Mathlib's `TemperedDistribution.fourierMultiplierCLM_sum`,
`Rd.sum_fourier_lpBlockKernelS_apply`).

Rd.sum_conv_dualLpBlockKernel_blockFun_a.name: Rd.sum_conv_dualLpBlockKernel_blockFun_ae
Rd.sum_conv_dualLpBlockKernel_blockFun_a.docstring:
**The reproducing sums**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `f ∈ L_p(V)` and every finite set `s ⊆ ℕ`,
`∑_{j ∈ s} ψ̃_j ⋆ (ψ_j ⋆ f) = ∑_{j ∈ s} Δ_j f` almost everywhere.

Rd.sum_choose_mul_succ_add.name: Rd.sum_choose_mul_succ_add
Rd.sum_choose_mul_succ_add.docstring:
**Pascal's rule for sums**:
`∑_{l ≤ r} C(r, l) F(l + 1) + ∑_{l ≤ r} C(r, l) F(l) = ∑_{l ≤ r+1} C(r + 1, l) F(l)`.

Rd.subsingleton_czMaximal_mem_zcell.name: Rd.subsingleton_czMaximal_mem_zcell
Rd.subsingleton_czMaximal_mem_zcell.docstring:
Every point lies in **at most one maximal big cube**, since these cubes are disjoint
(Mathlib's `Set.PairwiseDisjoint.elim_set`).

Rd.sub_restrictProj_mem.name: Rd.sub_restrictProj_mem
Rd.sub_restrictProj_mem.docstring: `U` and its restriction differ by an element vanishing on `Ω`.

Rd.sub_mem_of_lt_infDist_of_norm_le.name: Rd.sub_mem_of_lt_infDist_of_norm_le
Rd.sub_mem_of_lt_infDist_of_norm_le.docstring:
**Inner patches, the support condition for kernels in a ball**: if `δ < infDist(x, Oᶜ)` and
`‖y‖ ≤ δ`, then `x - y ∈ O`, since `x - y` lies in the ball `B(x, infDist(x, Oᶜ)) ⊆ O`
(Mathlib's `Metric.ball_infDist_compl_subset`).

Rd.sub_le_norm_sub_of_mem_ball.name: Rd.sub_le_norm_sub_of_mem_ball
Rd.sub_le_norm_sub_of_mem_ball.docstring:
**Points inside and outside two concentric balls are far apart**: for `y ∈ B(c, r)` and
`x ∉ B(c, R)`, `R - r ≤ |y - x|`, by the triangle inequality.

Rd.sub_conv_ae.name: Rd.sub_conv_ae
Rd.sub_conv_ae.docstring: **Convolution is subtractive in the kernel** almost everywhere.

Rd.stronglyMeasurable_czAverageC.name: Rd.stronglyMeasurable_czAverageC
Rd.stronglyMeasurable_czAverageC.docstring:
The signed averages are strongly measurable: they are the pointwise limit of the finite
partial sums, which are finite sums of constants times indicators of cubes.

Rd.stretch.name: Rd.stretch
Rd.stretch.docstring:
The **stretch** `D x = x + (c - 1) ⟪u, x⟫ u` by the factor `c` in the direction `u`: for a
unit vector `u` it multiplies `u` by `c` and fixes the vectors orthogonal to `u`. It is Mathlib's
`LinearMap.transvection` of the linear form `(c - 1) ⟪u, ·⟫` and the vector `u`.

Rd.stdBumpBase.name: Rd.stdBumpBase
Rd.stdBumpBase.docstring: The smooth bump around `0` with radii `1/2` and `1` (`Rd.centeredBumpBase` for `R = 1`).

Rd.squareFunctionConst_ne_top.name: Rd.squareFunctionConst_ne_top
Rd.squareFunctionConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant `Rd.squareFunctionConst V p` is finite for `1 < p < ∞`.

Rd.squareFunctionConst.name: Rd.squareFunctionConst
Rd.squareFunctionConst.docstring:
The constant `Q_{V,p}` of the **upper square function bound**
`‖f‖_{F^0_{p,2}} ≤ Q_{V,p} ‖f‖_p`: the strong type constant `Rd.czConst` of the
Calderón–Zygmund family of the blocks `ψ_j`, with overlap `2` and Hörmander constant
`4 H_{A^ψ}`, where `A^ψ = Rd.lpBlockKernelBaseBound V` (`Rd.isCZFamily_lpBlockKernel`).

Rd.sq_norm_eq_of_hasWeakLineDeriv.name: Rd.sq_norm_eq_of_hasWeakLineDeriv
Rd.sq_norm_eq_of_hasWeakLineDeriv.docstring:
**The `H^1(V)` norm by the weak gradient, in `ℝ`**: let `(e_i)` be an orthonormal basis of
`V`, `f` the `L_2` function of `U ∈ H^1(V)`, and `g_i ∈ L_2(V)` the weak derivatives
`∂_{e_i} f` on `V`. Then `‖U‖² = ‖f‖_2² + (2π)⁻² ∑_i ‖g_i‖_2²`
(`Rd.sq_norm_besselPotential_one_eq` with `J_1 f = U`).

Rd.sq_norm_besselPotential_one_eq.name: Rd.sq_norm_besselPotential_one_eq
Rd.sq_norm_besselPotential_one_eq.docstring:
**The `H^1` norm by the weak gradient, in `ℝ`**: under the hypotheses of
`Rd.enorm_besselPotential_one_sq_eq`, `(2π)² ‖h‖_2² = (2π)² ‖f‖_2² + ∑_i ‖g_i‖_2²`.

Rd.sq_norm_add_sum_sq_le.name: Rd.sq_norm_add_sum_sq_le
Rd.sq_norm_add_sum_sq_le.docstring: If `‖x‖ + ∑_i ‖y_i‖ ≤ K` in `ℝ≥0∞` with `K` finite, then `‖x‖² + ∑_i ‖y_i‖² ≤ K²` in `ℝ`.

Rd.sobolevToTLConst_ne_top.name: Rd.sobolevToTLConst_ne_top
Rd.sobolevToTLConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant `Rd.sobolevToTLConst V p α` is finite for `1 < p < ∞`.

Rd.sobolevToTLConst.name: Rd.sobolevToTLConst
Rd.sobolevToTLConst.docstring:
The constant `K_α = S_{V,p}(2, 4 H_{A^α})` of the bound `W^m_p ⊆ F^m_{p,2}` for the
multi-index `α`: the strong type constant `Rd.czConst` of the Calderón–Zygmund family of the
dilated derivative kernels `(η_α)_{2^j}`, with overlap `2` and Hörmander constant `4 H_{A^α}`
(`Rd.isCZFamily_derivKernelFamily`).

Rd.sobolevToL2_zero_surjective.name: Rd.sobolevToL2_zero_surjective
Rd.sobolevToL2_zero_surjective.docstring:
**Every `L_2` function is the `L_2` function of an element of `H^0(V)`**: for `F ∈ L_2(V)`,
the element `U = J_0⁻¹ F` of `H^0(V)` (Mathlib's isometry `BesselPotentialSpace.toLpₗᵢ` onto
`L_2(V)`) has `ι_0 U = J_0 (ι_{0,0} U) = J_0 U = F` (`Rd.sobolevInclusion_self`).

Rd.sobolevToL2_sobolevInclusion.name: Rd.sobolevToL2_sobolevInclusion
Rd.sobolevToL2_sobolevInclusion.docstring:
**The `L_2` function does not depend on the space**: for `0 ≤ t ≤ s` and `U ∈ H^s(V)`,
`ι_t (ι_{t,s} U) = ι_s U`.

Rd.sobolevToL2_sobolevConv.name: Rd.sobolevToL2_sobolevConv
Rd.sobolevToL2_sobolevConv.docstring:
**Convolution acts on the `L_2` functions**: for `s ≥ 0`, an integrable `K` and
`U ∈ H^s(V)`, `ι_s (K ⋆ U) = K ⋆ ι_s U`. Both sides have the Fourier transform
`𝓕K ⟨ξ⟩^{-s} 𝓕(J_s U)` almost everywhere (`Rd.fourier_toLp_sobolevInclusion_ae`,
`Rd.fourier_toLp_sobolevConv_ae`, `Rd.fourier_convLp`), and the Fourier transform of `L_2(V)` is
injective (Mathlib's `FourierTransform.fourierInv_fourier_eq`).

Rd.sobolevToL2_restrictProj_ae_eq.name: Rd.sobolevToL2_restrictProj_ae_eq
Rd.sobolevToL2_restrictProj_ae_eq.docstring:
**A restriction has the same `L_2` function on `Ω`**: for `s ≥ 0`, an open `Ω` and
`U ∈ H^s(V)`, `ι_s(U|_Ω) = ι_s U` almost everywhere on `Ω`, since `U - U|_Ω` vanishes on `Ω`
(`Rd.sub_restrictProj_mem`, `Rd.mem_vanishOn_iff_sobolevToL2`).

Rd.sobolevToL2_one.name: Rd.sobolevToL2_one
Rd.sobolevToL2_one.docstring:
**At `s = 1` the `L_2` function is `Rd.toL2`**: both represent the same distribution
(`Rd.toL2_eq_of_toDistr_eq`).

Rd.sobolevToL2_ofSchwartz.name: Rd.sobolevToL2_ofSchwartz
Rd.sobolevToL2_ofSchwartz.docstring:
**The `L_2` function of a Schwartz function** in `H^s(V)`, `s ≥ 0`, is the function itself:
`ι_s w = w` in `L_2(V)`, since both have the tempered distribution `w`
(`Rd.sobolevToL2_eq_of_toDistr_eq`; at `s = 1` this is `Rd.toL2_ofSchwartz`).

Rd.sobolevToL2_injective.name: Rd.sobolevToL2_injective
Rd.sobolevToL2_injective.docstring:
**`H^s(V)`, `s ≥ 0`, is determined by its `L_2` functions**: `U ↦ ι_s U` is injective
(`Rd.toTemperedDistribution_sobolevToL2`, Mathlib's `BesselPotentialSpace.ext`).

Rd.sobolevToL2_eq_of_toDistr_eq.name: Rd.sobolevToL2_eq_of_toDistr_eq
Rd.sobolevToL2_eq_of_toDistr_eq.docstring:
An `L_2` function `f` is `ι_s U` as soon as its tempered distribution is `U`: `L_2` functions
are determined by their distributions (`Rd.eq_of_toTemperedDistribution_eq`).

Rd.sobolevToL2_apply.name: Rd.sobolevToL2_apply
Rd.sobolevToL2_apply.docstring: `ι_s U` is the `L_2` function `J_0 (ι_{0,s} U)` of the inclusion of `U` into `H^0(V)`.

Rd.sobolevToL2_ae_eq_zero_of_mem_tildeSp.name: Rd.sobolevToL2_ae_eq_zero_of_mem_tildeSpace
Rd.sobolevToL2_ae_eq_zero_of_mem_tildeSp.docstring:
**The elements of `H̃^s(Ω)` vanish outside `Ω`**: for `s ≥ 0`, every open `Ω` and
`U ∈ H̃^s(Ω)`, the `L_2` function `ι_s U` vanishes almost everywhere outside `Ω`. The `U` with
this property form the kernel of `U ↦ (ι_s U)|_{V \ Ω}`, a closed subspace containing `T^s(Ω)`
(`Rd.exists_opens_sobolevToL2_ae_eq_zero`).

Rd.sobolevToL2.name: Rd.sobolevToL2
Rd.sobolevToL2.docstring:
**The `L_2` function `ι_s U` of an element `U` of `H^s(V)`, `s ≥ 0`**: the inclusion
`ι_{0,s}` into `H^0(V)`, followed by Mathlib's isometry `H^0(V) → L_2(V)`, `U ↦ J_0 U = U`. Its
distribution is `U` (`Rd.toTemperedDistribution_sobolevToL2`); at `s = 1` it is `Rd.toL2`
(`Rd.sobolevToL2_one`).

Rd.sobolevPairingCLM.name: Rd.sobolevPairingCLM
Rd.sobolevPairingCLM.docstring:
**The pairing as a bounded functional**: for `W ∈ H^{-s}(V)`, `U ↦ [W, U]` as a continuous
linear map `H^s(V) → ℂ`, the inner product with `J_{-s} W` (Mathlib's `innerSL`) after the
isometry `U ↦ J_s U` onto `L_2(V)`.

Rd.sobolevOneBesovConst_ne_top.name: Rd.sobolevOneBesovConst_ne_top
Rd.sobolevOneBesovConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of `H^1(V) ⊆ B^1_{2,2}(V)` is finite.

Rd.sobolevOneBesovConst.name: Rd.sobolevOneBesovConst
Rd.sobolevOneBesovConst.docstring:
**The constant of `H^1(V) ⊆ B^1_{2,2}(V)`**: `C_inv · 2 (1 - 2^(-1))⁻¹ · (2 · 4)^{1/2}`, the
product of the constants of the three inclusions behind `Rd.modNorm_two_le_norm`: the inverse
inequality for the moduli of order `2` (`ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.inverseConst` of
`Rd.bandModulusData`), `F^1_{2,2} ⊆ B^1_{2,2}` (`Rd.approxNormDyadic_le_triebelLizorkinNorm`) and
`H^1 ⊆ F^1_{2,2}` (`Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_le_of_besselPotential_eq`).

Rd.sobolevJet.snd_eq_of_fst_eq.name: Rd.sobolevJet.snd_eq_of_fst_eq
Rd.sobolevJet.snd_eq_of_fst_eq.docstring:
**The derivatives of a jet of `W^1_p(V)` are determined by its value**
(`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.eq_of_top`).

Rd.sobolevJet.restrictL.name: Rd.sobolevJet.restrictL
Rd.sobolevJet.restrictL.docstring:
**The restriction of jets** `(F, (G_i)_i) ↦ (F|_O, (G_i|_O)_i)` from `W^1_p(V)` to `W^1_p(O)`,
a bounded linear operator (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.LpToLpRestrictCLM` in each component; weak
derivatives restrict by `Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.mono`).

Rd.sobolevJet.liftJet_apply_snd.name: Rd.sobolevJet.liftJet_apply_snd
Rd.sobolevJet.liftJet_apply_snd.docstring:
The derivatives of `Rd.sobolevJet.liftJet L h u` are the weak derivatives of `L u`: every weak
derivative `G = ∂_{e_i} (L u)` in `L_p(V)` is the `i`-th one (`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.eq_of_top`).

Rd.sobolevJet.liftJet.name: Rd.sobolevJet.liftJet
Rd.sobolevJet.liftJet.docstring:
**Linear maps into the jets of `W^1_p(V)`**: a linear map `L` into `L_p(V)` whose values have
weak derivatives `∂_{e_i} (L u) ∈ L_p(V)` is the linear map `u ↦ (L u, (∂_{e_i} (L u))_i)` into
the jets; it is additive and homogeneous since the derivatives are determined by the value
(`Rd.sobolevJet.ext_of_fst_eq`).

Rd.sobolevJet.ext_of_fst_eq.name: Rd.sobolevJet.ext_of_fst_eq
Rd.sobolevJet.ext_of_fst_eq.docstring: Two jets of `W^1_p(V)` with the same value are equal (`Rd.sobolevJet.snd_eq_of_fst_eq`).

Rd.sobolevJet.name: Rd.sobolevJet
Rd.sobolevJet.docstring:
The **jets of `W^1_p(V)`**: the pairs `(F, (G_i)_i)` of elements of `L_p(V)` with
`G_i = ∂_{e_i} F` weakly on `V`, `e_i = Rd.gridBasis V i`; a complex linear subspace of
`L_p(V) × L_p(V)^n`.

Rd.sobolevInclusion_self.name: Rd.sobolevInclusion_self
Rd.sobolevInclusion_self.docstring:
**The inclusion `ι_{s,s}` is the identity** of `H^s(V)`: it keeps the tempered distribution
(`Rd.toDistr_sobolevInclusion`), which determines an element of `H^s(V)` (Mathlib's
`BesselPotentialSpace.ext`).

Rd.sobolevInclusion_ofTest.name: Rd.sobolevInclusion_ofTest
Rd.sobolevInclusion_ofTest.docstring:
**Test functions under the inclusions**: for `t ≤ s` and a real test function `φ` of an open
set `Ω`, `ι_{t,s} φ = φ` (`Rd.toDistr_sobolevInclusion`, `Rd.toDistr_ofTest`).

Rd.sobolevInclusion_ofSchwartz.name: Rd.sobolevInclusion_ofSchwartz
Rd.sobolevInclusion_ofSchwartz.docstring:
**Schwartz functions under the inclusions**: for `t ≤ s` and a Schwartz function `w`,
`ι_{t,s} w = w`, since both sides have the tempered distribution `w`
(`Rd.toDistr_sobolevInclusion`, `Rd.toDistr_ofSchwartz`).

Rd.sobolevInclusion_mem_vanishOn_iff.name: Rd.sobolevInclusion_mem_vanishOn_iff
Rd.sobolevInclusion_mem_vanishOn_iff.docstring:
**The inclusions detect vanishing on `Ω`**: for `t ≤ s` and `W ∈ H^s(V)`, `ι_{t,s} W ∈ H^t(V)`
vanishes on `Ω` iff `W` does, since both have the same tempered distribution
(`Rd.toDistr_sobolevInclusion`, `Rd.mem_vanishOn_iff`).

Rd.sobolevInclusion_mem_vanishOn.name: Rd.sobolevInclusion_mem_vanishOn
Rd.sobolevInclusion_mem_vanishOn.docstring:
**The inclusions keep vanishing on `Ω`**: for `t ≤ s`, if `W ∈ H^s(V)` vanishes on `Ω`, so
does `ι_{t,s} W ∈ H^t(V)` (`Rd.sobolevInclusion_mem_vanishOn_iff`).

Rd.sobolevInclusion_mem_testSpan.name: Rd.sobolevInclusion_mem_testSpan
Rd.sobolevInclusion_mem_testSpan.docstring:
**The inclusions keep the span of the test functions**: for `t ≤ s`,
`ι_{t,s}(T^s(Ω)) ⊆ T^t(Ω)`, since `ι_{t,s} φ = φ` for every test function `φ` of `Ω`
(`Rd.sobolevInclusion_ofTest`).

Rd.sobolevInclusion.name: Rd.sobolevInclusion
Rd.sobolevInclusion.docstring:
**The inclusion `H^s(V) ⊆ H^t(V)` for `t ≤ s`**: `U ↦ J_{-t} 𝓕⁻(⟨ξ⟩^{t-s} 𝓕(J_s U))`,
built from Mathlib's isometry `U ↦ J_s U` of `H^s(V)` onto `L_2(V)`
(`BesselPotentialSpace.toLpₗᵢ`), the Fourier transform of `L_2(V)` and the multiplier
`Rd.besselWeightMul (t - s)`. It keeps the distribution (`Rd.toDistr_sobolevInclusion`).

Rd.sobolevExtensionOp_of_cover.name: Rd.sobolevExtensionOp_of_cover
Rd.sobolevExtensionOp_of_cover.docstring:
**Pasting extension operators**: let `(U_k)` be a finite cover of `Ō` by bounded open sets and
let `E_k` be extension operators from `O ∩ U_k` with finite constants. Then there is an extension
operator from `O` with a finite constant (`Rd.SobolevExtensionOp.paste` with a smooth resolution of
unity, `Rd.exists_smooth_partition`).

Rd.sobolevConv.name: Rd.sobolevConv
Rd.sobolevConv.docstring:
**Convolution in `H^s(V)`**: for an integrable `K` and every real `s`, `U ↦ K ⋆ U`, the
element of `H^s(V)` whose `L_2` function `J_s (K ⋆ U)` is `K ⋆ J_s U`
(`Rd.toLp_sobolevConv`). It is a bounded operator, built from Mathlib's isometry
`U ↦ J_s U` of `H^s(V)` onto `L_2(V)` (`BesselPotentialSpace.toLpₗᵢ`) and Young's inequality
`‖K ⋆ g‖_2 ≤ ‖K‖_1 ‖g‖_2` (`Rd.convLp`).

Rd.sobolevBesovInvConst_ne_top.name: Rd.sobolevBesovInvConst_ne_top
Rd.sobolevBesovInvConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of the bound of `H^s(V)` by `B^s_{2,2}(V)` is finite.

Rd.sobolevBesovInvConst.name: Rd.sobolevBesovInvConst
Rd.sobolevBesovInvConst.docstring:
**The constant of the bound of `H^s(V)` by `B^s_{2,2}(V)` for the moduli of order `r`**:
`(2 · 5^s)^{1/2} · 8 · 2^{3s} ‖Φ‖_1 · D`, the product of the constants of the three inclusions
behind `Rd.enorm_le_modNorm_sobolevToL2`: `F^s_{2,2} ⊆ H^s`
(`Rd.enorm_besselPotential_le_triebelLizorkinNorm`), `A^s_2 ⊆ F^s_{2,2}` for the band-limited
approximation spaces, with the Littlewood–Paley kernel `Φ = Rd.lpKernel`
(`Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_le_approxNormDyadic`), and Jackson's direction for the moduli of order
`r` (`ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.directConst` of `Rd.bandModulusData`). At `s = 1`, `r = 2`
it is `Rd.sobolevOneInvConst V`.

Rd.sobolevBesovConst_ne_top.name: Rd.sobolevBesovConst_ne_top
Rd.sobolevBesovConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of `H^s(V) ⊆ B^s_{2,2}(V)` is finite for `0 < s < r`.

Rd.sobolevBesovConst.name: Rd.sobolevBesovConst
Rd.sobolevBesovConst.docstring:
**The constant of `H^s(V) ⊆ B^s_{2,2}(V)` for the moduli of order `r`**:
`C_inv · 2 (1 - 2^{-s})⁻¹ · (2 · 4^s)^{1/2}`, the product of the constants of the three inclusions
behind `Rd.modNorm_sobolevToL2_le`: the inverse inequality for the moduli of order `r`
(`ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.inverseConst` of `Rd.bandModulusData`), `F^s_{2,2} ⊆ B^s_{2,2}`
(`Rd.approxNormDyadic_le_triebelLizorkinNorm`) and `H^s ⊆ F^s_{2,2}`
(`Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_le_of_besselPotential_eq`). At `s = 1`, `r = 2` it is
`Rd.sobolevOneBesovConst V`.

Rd.smul_mem_tsupport_of_mem_tsupport_dil.name: Rd.smul_mem_tsupport_of_mem_tsupport_dilate
Rd.smul_mem_tsupport_of_mem_tsupport_dil.docstring:
**The support of a dilation**: if `x` lies in the closed support of `Φ_c`, `c ≠ 0`, then
`c x` lies in the closed support of `Φ`; the closed support of `Φ_c` lies in the preimage of that
of `Φ` under `x ↦ c x` (Mathlib's `tsupport_comp_eq_preimage`).

Rd.smul_mem_bandSpace.name: Rd.smul_mem_bandSpace
Rd.smul_mem_bandSpace.docstring: The band-limited classes are closed under complex scalars.

Rd.smul_conv.name: Rd.smul_conv
Rd.smul_conv.docstring: Convolution is homogeneous in the kernel.

Rd.smulLeftCLM_toTemperedDistribution_eq.name: Rd.smulLeftCLM_toTemperedDistribution_eq
Rd.smulLeftCLM_toTemperedDistribution_eq.docstring:
**Multiplying an `L_p` function by a temperate weight**: if `w` has temperate growth,
`g ∈ L_p(V)` and `w g ∈ L_q(V)`, `1 ≤ p, q ≤ ∞`, then the product of `w` with the tempered
distribution of `g` is the tempered distribution of `w g`.

Rd.smulLeftCLM_sum_fourier_lpBlockKernel.name: Rd.smulLeftCLM_sum_fourier_lpBlockKernelS
Rd.smulLeftCLM_sum_fourier_lpBlockKernel.docstring:
**The cut-off of the inverse Fourier transform**: multiplying a Schwartz function `w` by
`∑_{j ≤ J} 𝓕ψ_j = χ(2^{-J} ·)` is the cut-off `Rd.cutoffMul (2^J - 1) w` at radius `2^J`
(`Rd.sum_fourier_lpBlockKernelS_apply`, `Rd.cutoffMul_apply`).

Rd.smoothnessModulus_nat_mul_le_of_foral.name: Rd.smoothnessModulus_nat_mul_le_of_forall_exists_nsmul
Rd.smoothnessModulus_nat_mul_le_of_foral.docstring:
**Integer multiples of the scale, for divisible steps**: if every step `h` with
`‖h‖ ≤ m t` is `m h'` for a step `h'` with `‖h'‖ ≤ t`, then `ω_r(f, m t)_p ≤ m^r ω_r(f, t)_p`,
since `‖Δ^r_{m h'} f‖_p ≤ m^r ‖Δ^r_{h'} f‖_p` (`Rd.eLpNorm_higherDiff_nsmul_higherDiff_le`). The
hypothesis holds on every normed space and on the torus.

Rd.smoothnessModulus_nat_mul_le.name: Rd.smoothnessModulus_nat_mul_le
Rd.smoothnessModulus_nat_mul_le.docstring: **Integer multiples of the scale**: `ω_r(f, m t)_p ≤ m^r ω_r(f, t)_p` for `m ≥ 1`.

Rd.smoothnessModulus_mul_smooth_le.name: Rd.smoothnessModulus_mul_smooth_le
Rd.smoothnessModulus_mul_smooth_le.docstring:
**The modulus of a product**:
`ω_r(ψ F, t)_p ≤ ∑_{l ≤ r} C(r, l) C t^l ω_(r-l)(F, t)_p` for `t ≥ 0`.

Rd.smoothnessModulus_mul_le_of_nat_mul_l.name: Rd.smoothnessModulus_mul_le_of_nat_mul_le
Rd.smoothnessModulus_mul_le_of_nat_mul_l.docstring:
**From integer to real dilations of the scale**: if `ω_r(f, m t)_p ≤ m^r ω_r(f, t)_p` for
every integer `m ≥ 1`, then `ω_r(f, c t)_p ≤ (1 + c)^r ω_r(f, t)_p` for every `c ≥ 0`, with the
integer `m = ⌊c⌋ + 1 ≤ 1 + c` and the monotonicity of the modulus.

Rd.smoothnessModulus_mul_le.name: Rd.smoothnessModulus_mul_le
Rd.smoothnessModulus_mul_le.docstring:
**Dilating the scale**: `ω_r(f, c t)_p ≤ (1 + c)^r ω_r(f, t)_p` for `c, t ≥ 0`
(`Rd.smoothnessModulus_nat_mul_le`, `Rd.smoothnessModulus_mul_le_of_nat_mul_le`).

Rd.smoothnessModulus_const_smul.name: Rd.smoothnessModulus_const_smul
Rd.smoothnessModulus_const_smul.docstring:
**The modulus is homogeneous**: `ω_r(c f, t)_p = |c| ω_r(f, t)_p`, since
`Δ_h^r (c f) = c Δ_h^r f` (Mathlib's `fwdDiff_iter_const_smul`, `eLpNorm_const_smul`).

Rd.smoothnessModulus_congr_ae.name: Rd.smoothnessModulus_congr_ae
Rd.smoothnessModulus_congr_ae.docstring: **The modulus depends only on the class modulo null sets.**

Rd.smoothnessModulus.name: Rd.smoothnessModulus
Rd.smoothnessModulus.docstring: The **modulus of smoothness** `ω_r(f, t)_p = sup_{‖h‖ ≤ t} ‖Δ_h^r f‖_p`.

Rd.slobodeckijIntegrand_le_of_support.name: Rd.slobodeckijIntegrand_le_of_support
Rd.slobodeckijIntegrand_le_of_support.docstring:
**The Gagliardo integrand of a function supported in a ball**: if `f` vanishes outside
`B(c, r)` and `r ≤ R`, then for all `x, y`, `P > 0` and `a ≥ 0`,
`|f(y) - f(x)|^P / |y - x|^a ≤ 1_{B(c,R)²}(x, y) |f(y) - f(x)|^P / |y - x|^a +
|f(x)|^P / (R - r)^a + |f(y)|^P / (R - r)^a`. If one point lies outside `B(c, R)`, then `f`
vanishes there, and the other point is at distance at least `R - r` where `f` does not vanish
(`Rd.sub_le_norm_sub_of_mem_ball`).

Rd.slobodeckijForm_le.name: Rd.slobodeckijForm_le
Rd.slobodeckijForm_le.docstring:
**The Gagliardo form by the first-difference Besov norm**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `s > 0` and
`f ∈ L_p(V)`,
`∫∫ |f(y) - f(x)|^p / |y - x|^(n+sp) dy dx ≤ C (‖f‖_p^p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_1(f, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_p}^p)`
with `C = Rd.slobodeckijConstLower V p s`: the steps `|z| ≤ 1` are sorted into the dyadic annuli,
and the steps `|z| ≥ 1` give the tail.

Rd.slobodeckijForm_eq_lintegral_of_measu.name: Rd.slobodeckijForm_eq_lintegral_of_measurable
Rd.slobodeckijForm_eq_lintegral_of_measu.docstring:
**The Gagliardo form by the step**, for measurable `f`: the substitution `y = x + h`
(Mathlib's `lintegral_add_left_eq_self`) and Tonelli's theorem (`lintegral_lintegral_swap`) give
`∫∫ |f(y) - f(x)|^p / |y - x|^(n + sp) dy dx = ∫ ‖Δ_h f‖_p^p / |h|^(n + sp) dh`.

Rd.slobodeckijForm_eq_lintegral_eLpNorm.name: Rd.slobodeckijForm_eq_lintegral_eLpNorm
Rd.slobodeckijForm_eq_lintegral_eLpNorm.docstring:
**The Gagliardo form by the step**: for `0 < p < ∞` and a.e. strongly measurable `f`,
`∫∫ |f(y) - f(x)|^p / |y - x|^(n + sp) dy dx = ∫ ‖Δ_h f‖_p^p / |h|^(n + sp) dh`.

Rd.slobodeckijForm_congr_ae.name: Rd.slobodeckijForm_congr_ae
Rd.slobodeckijForm_congr_ae.docstring: The Gagliardo form depends only on the class of `f` modulo null sets.

Rd.slobodeckijForm.name: Rd.slobodeckijForm
Rd.slobodeckijForm.docstring:
The **Gagliardo form** `∫∫ |f(y) - f(x)|^p / |y - x|^(n + sp) dy dx` of `f : V → ℂ`, with
`n = dim V`: for `0 < p < ∞` the `p`-th power of the Gagliardo seminorm of the
Sobolev–Slobodeckij space `W^{s,p}(V)` (Gagliardo 1957). The exponent is the real number
`p.toReal`, which is `0` for `p = ∞`. For `p = 2`, `s = α/2` and measurable real-valued `f` it
agrees, by Tonelli's theorem, with the form `formHs univ α` of the Lean project
*quadratic-forms-sobolev-lean*, an integral for the product measure, with the same orientation
`f(y) - f(x)`.

Rd.slobodeckijConstUpper_ne_top.name: Rd.slobodeckijConstUpper_ne_top
Rd.slobodeckijConstUpper_ne_top.docstring: The constant `Rd.slobodeckijConstUpper V p s` is finite for `0 < p < ∞` and `s > 0`.

Rd.slobodeckijConstLower_ne_top.name: Rd.slobodeckijConstLower_ne_top
Rd.slobodeckijConstLower_ne_top.docstring: The constant `Rd.slobodeckijConstLower V p s` is finite for `0 < p < ∞` and `s > 0`.

Rd.slobodeckijConstLower.name: Rd.slobodeckijConstLower
Rd.slobodeckijConstLower.docstring:
The constant `2^(n+sp) |B_1| + 2^p Rd.complBallRpowConst V (n + sp)` of the bound of the
Gagliardo form by `‖f‖_p^p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_1(f, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_p}^p` (`Rd.slobodeckijForm_le`).

Rd.shiftReflect_apply.name: Rd.shiftReflect_apply
Rd.shiftReflect_apply.docstring: The values of the reflected translate: `y ↦ η(x - y)`.

Rd.shiftReflect.name: Rd.shiftReflect
Rd.shiftReflect.docstring:
The **reflected translate** `y ↦ η(x - y)` of a Schwartz function `η`, the Schwartz function
that tests the convolution `(η ⋆ f)(x) = ∫ η(x - y) f(y) dy`.

Rd.setOf_lt_maximalFunction_subset.name: Rd.setOf_lt_maximalFunction_subset
Rd.setOf_lt_maximalFunction_subset.docstring: The level set `{M g > t}` lies in the union of the sets `bigBallSet g t N`, `N ∈ ℕ`.

Rd.setOf_lt_infDist_compl_subset.name: Rd.setOf_lt_infDist_compl_subset
Rd.setOf_lt_infDist_compl_subset.docstring: Points at distance more than `r ≥ 0` from the complement of `s` lie in `s`.

Rd.setLIntegral_setLIntegral_ball_le.name: Rd.setLIntegral_setLIntegral_ball_le
Rd.setLIntegral_setLIntegral_ball_le.docstring:
**Averaging moving balls** (Tonelli): for `l ≥ 1`, every `a, ρ`, `x` and every almost
everywhere measurable `G : V → [0, ∞]`,
`∫_{B(0,a)} ∫_{B(x + l v, ρ)} G(w) dw dv ≤ |B(0,ρ)| ∫_{B(x, ρ + l a)} G`: a point `w` lies in
`B(x + l v, ρ)` only for `v` in a set of measure at most `|B(0,ρ)|`, and only if
`w ∈ B(x, ρ + l a)` (`Rd.setLIntegral_indicator_ball_add_smul_le`).

Rd.setLIntegral_maximalFunction_gt_le_in.name: Rd.setLIntegral_maximalFunction_gt_le_indicator
Rd.setLIntegral_maximalFunction_gt_le_in.docstring:
The weighted level sets of `M g` for measurable `g`:
`∫_{M g > s} w ≤ 2 · 5^n s⁻¹ ∫_{g > s/2} g M w` for `s > 0`, by the weighted weak type
applied to `1_{g > s/2} g`.

Rd.setLIntegral_maximalFunction_gt_le.name: Rd.setLIntegral_maximalFunction_gt_le
Rd.setLIntegral_maximalFunction_gt_le.docstring:
**Weighted weak type `(1,1)` of the maximal function** (Fefferman–Stein): for all
`g, w : V → [0, ∞]` and `t > 0`, `∫_{M g > t} w ≤ 5^n t⁻¹ ∫ g M w`. The level set is exhausted
by the sets `Rd.bigBallSet`, whose radii are bounded, and Vitali's covering lemma applies to each
of them.

Rd.setLIntegral_inter_ball_le.name: Rd.setLIntegral_inter_ball_le
Rd.setLIntegral_inter_ball_le.docstring:
The integral of `g` over the part of `Q ⊆ B̄(c, ρ)` in `B(x, r)`, for `x ∉ B̄(c, 2ρ)`, is at
most `(⨍_Q g) |Q ∩ B(x, 3r)|`: either the two sets are disjoint, or `Q ⊆ B(x, 3r)`.

Rd.setLIntegral_indicator_ball_add_smul_.name: Rd.setLIntegral_indicator_ball_add_smul_le
Rd.setLIntegral_indicator_ball_add_smul_.docstring:
**One point under moving balls**: for `l ≥ 1`, every `a, ρ` and points `x, w`,
`∫_{B(0,a)} 1_{B(x + l v, ρ)}(w) G(w) dv ≤ 1_{B(x, ρ + l a)}(w) G(w) |B(0,ρ)|`: the integrand is
at most `1_{B(x, ρ + l a)}(w) G(w)` times the indicator of the steps `v` whose ball contains `w`
(`Rd.indicator_ball_add_smul_le`), a set of measure at most `|B(0,ρ)|`
(`Rd.volume_setOf_dist_add_smul_lt_le`).

Rd.setLIntegral_eq_mul_ballMeanDiff.name: Rd.setLIntegral_eq_mul_ballMeanDiff
Rd.setLIntegral_eq_mul_ballMeanDiff.docstring: The integral of the differences over the ball is `|B(0, 2^(-j))| d_j f(x)`.

Rd.setLIntegral_enorm_dilate_sub_le_min.name: Rd.setLIntegral_enorm_dilate_sub_le_min
Rd.setLIntegral_enorm_dilate_sub_le_min.docstring:
**The Hörmander bound for one dilate**: for every Schwartz function `G`, `j ∈ ℕ` and
`y ∈ V`,
`∫_{‖x‖ > 2‖y‖} |G_{2^j}(x - y) - G_{2^j}(x)| dx ≤ H_G min(2^j ‖y‖, (2^j ‖y‖)⁻¹)` with
`H_G = Rd.hormanderConst G`; at `y = 0` both sides vanish, since `0⁻¹ = ∞` in `[0, ∞]`.

Rd.setLIntegral_enorm_dilate_sub_le_inv.name: Rd.setLIntegral_enorm_dilate_sub_le_inv
Rd.setLIntegral_enorm_dilate_sub_le_inv.docstring:
**Long steps**: `∫_{‖x‖ > 2‖y‖} |G_{2^j}(x - y) - G_{2^j}(x)| dx ≤ 2 T_G (2^j ‖y‖)^(-1)` with
`T_G = Rd.tailConst G 0 1`: both `x` and `x - y` lie outside the ball of radius `‖y‖`, where the
mass of `G_{2^j}` is at most `T_G (1 + 2^j ‖y‖)^(-1)`
(`Rd.setLIntegral_enorm_dilate_schwartz_le`).

Rd.setLIntegral_enorm_dilate_schwartz_le.name: Rd.setLIntegral_enorm_dilate_schwartz_le
Rd.setLIntegral_enorm_dilate_schwartz_le.docstring:
**Tails of dilated Schwartz functions**: for every real `a`,
`∫_{‖z‖ ≥ a} |G_{2^j}(z)| dz ≤ C (1 + max(2^j a, 0))^(-N)` with `C = Rd.tailConst G 0 N`, by the
substitution `u = 2^j z`.

Rd.setLIntegral_dyadicAnnulus_norm_rpow_.name: Rd.setLIntegral_dyadicAnnulus_norm_rpow_neg_le
Rd.setLIntegral_dyadicAnnulus_norm_rpow_.docstring:
On the annulus `R 2^(-(i+1)) < |z| ≤ R 2^(-i)`, `|z|^(-a)` has the integral at most
`(1 + 2^a) |B_1| R^(n-a) 2^(-i(n-a))`, for every real `a`.

Rd.setLIntegral_dyadicAnnulus_le_lpModul.name: Rd.setLIntegral_dyadicAnnulus_le_lpModulus
Rd.setLIntegral_dyadicAnnulus_le_lpModul.docstring:
**One annulus of the Gagliardo form**: for `s ≥ 0`, on `2^(-(i+1)) < |z| ≤ 2^(-i)`,
`∫ ‖Δ_z f‖_p^p / |z|^(n+sp) dz ≤ 2^(n+sp) |B_1| (2^(is) ω_1(f, 2^(-i))_p)^p`, since there
`‖Δ_z f‖_p ≤ ω_1(f, 2^(-i))_p` and `|z|^(-(n+sp)) ≤ 2^((i+1)(n+sp))`.

Rd.setLIntegral_compl_ball_le_enorm.name: Rd.setLIntegral_compl_ball_le_enorm
Rd.setLIntegral_compl_ball_le_enorm.docstring:
**The tail of the Gagliardo form**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `s > 0`,
`∫_{|z| ≥ 1} ‖Δ_z f‖_p^p / |z|^(n+sp) dz ≤ 2^p C ‖f‖_p^p` with
`C = Rd.complBallRpowConst V (n + sp)`, since `‖Δ_z f‖_p ≤ 2 ‖f‖_p`.

Rd.setLIntegral_compl_ball_inter_dyadicS.name: Rd.setLIntegral_compl_ball_inter_dyadicShell_le
Rd.setLIntegral_compl_ball_inter_dyadicS.docstring:
On the part of the dyadic shell `i` outside the ball of radius `R`, `|z|^(-a)` has the
integral at most `2^n |B_1| R^(n-a) 2^(-i(a-n))`, for `a ≥ 0`.

Rd.setLIntegral_comp_smul.name: Rd.setLIntegral_comp_smul
Rd.setLIntegral_comp_smul.docstring:
The set version of `Rd.lintegral_comp_smul`: `∫_s f(r x) dμ(x) = |r^(-n)| ∫_{r s} f dμ` for
every set `s`, since `x ↦ r x` is a measurable equivalence (Mathlib's
`MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map`).

Rd.setLIntegral_closedBall_le_tsum_dyadi.name: Rd.setLIntegral_closedBall_le_tsum_dyadicAnnulus
Rd.setLIntegral_closedBall_le_tsum_dyadi.docstring:
**An integral over a ball by the annuli**: for every `G : V → [0, ∞]`,
`∫_{|z| ≤ ρ 2^(-k)} G ≤ G(0) |{0}| + ∑_i ∫_{annulus (k + i)} G`.

Rd.setLIntegral_ball_le_mul_maximalFunct.name: Rd.setLIntegral_ball_le_mul_maximalFunction
Rd.setLIntegral_ball_le_mul_maximalFunct.docstring: `∫_{B(x,r)} g ≤ |B(0,r)| M g(x)` for every `g : V → [0, ∞]` and every `r > 0`.

Rd.setLIntegral_ball_comp_sub_le.name: Rd.setLIntegral_ball_comp_sub_le
Rd.setLIntegral_ball_comp_sub_le.docstring:
`∫_{|z| < t} G(h - z) dz ≤ ∫_{|z| < 2t} G(z) dz` for `|h| ≤ t` and every `G : V → [0, ∞]`:
the reflection `z ↦ h - z` preserves Lebesgue measure (Mathlib's `lintegral_sub_left_eq_self`)
and maps the ball of radius `t` into the ball of radius `2t`.

Rd.setLAverage_eq_ofReal_setAverage.name: Rd.setLAverage_eq_ofReal_setAverage
Rd.setLAverage_eq_ofReal_setAverage.docstring:
For an a.e.-measurable `G : α → ℝ≥0∞` with finite integral over `s`, the average of `G`
over `s` is `ENNReal.ofReal` of the average of the real function `G.toReal` (Mathlib's
`toReal_setLAverage`).

Rd.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_sum.name: Rd.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_sum
Rd.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_sum.docstring:
**Green's integrand is linear in the second function**: for a measurable set `s` and a finite
family `W_i ∈ H^1(V)`, `∫_s (∂_v U) ∑_i W_i + U ∂_v ∑_i W_i` is the sum of the integrals
(`Rd.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_eq`).

Rd.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_eq.name: Rd.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_eq
Rd.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_eq.docstring:
**The integral of Green's integrand as a pairing**: for a measurable set `s` and
`U, W ∈ H^1(V)`, `∫_s (∂_v U) W + U ∂_v W = ⟨1_s ∂_v U, W⟩ + ⟨1_s U, ∂_v W⟩` with the bilinear
pairing of `L_2(V)` with itself (`Rd.setIntegral_mul_eq_lpPairing`).

Rd.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_add.name: Rd.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_add
Rd.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_add.docstring:
**Green's integrand is additive in the second function**: for a measurable set `s`,
`∫_s (∂_v U)(W₁ + W₂) + U ∂_v (W₁ + W₂)` is the sum of the two integrals
(`Rd.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_eq`).

Rd.setIntegral_openHalfSpace_smul_add_eq.name: Rd.setIntegral_openHalfSpace_smul_add_eq
Rd.setIntegral_openHalfSpace_smul_add_eq.docstring:
**Integration by parts on the half-space with a vanishing boundary term**: let `g_k = ∂_{w_k} u`
weakly on `H₊` (`k = 1, 2`), with `u`, `g_1`, `g_2` integrable on every bounded part
`H₊ ∩ B(0, R)`, and let `χ_1`, `χ_2` be smooth with compact support and
`|⟪w_1, e⟫ χ_1(y) + ⟪w_2, e⟫ χ_2(y)| ≤ C ⟪y, e⟫` on `H₊`. Then
`∫_{H₊} (χ_1 g_1 + χ_2 g_2) = -∫_{H₊} ((∂_{w_1} χ_1) u + (∂_{w_2} χ_2) u)`. With the cutoffs
`η_n` (`Rd.integral_halfSpaceCutoff_smul_eq`), the boundary terms are
`∫ s'((n + 1)⟪y, e⟫ - 1) (n + 1) (⟪w_1, e⟫ χ_1 + ⟪w_2, e⟫ χ_2) u → 0`
(`Rd.tendsto_integral_deriv_halfSpaceCutoff_smul`), and the other terms converge by dominated
convergence (`Rd.tendsto_integral_halfSpaceCutoff_smul`). This is the half-space lemma of
Brezis (2011, Chapter 9) in a form with two test functions.

Rd.setIntegral_mul_eq_lpPairing.name: Rd.setIntegral_mul_eq_lpPairing
Rd.setIntegral_mul_eq_lpPairing.docstring:
**Integrals over a set as a pairing**: `∫_s a b = ⟨1_s a, b⟩` for `a, b ∈ L_2(μ)` and a
measurable set `s`, with Mathlib's bounded bilinear pairing of `L_2` with `L_2`
(`ContinuousLinearMap.lpPairing`).

Rd.setIntegral_eq_of_inter_eq.name: Rd.setIntegral_eq_of_inter_eq
Rd.setIntegral_eq_of_inter_eq.docstring:
**Sets that agree inside `B`**: if `s ∩ B = t ∩ B` and `F` vanishes almost everywhere outside
`B`, then `∫_s F = ∫_t F`.

Rd.seminorm_sub_cutoffMul_le.name: Rd.seminorm_sub_cutoffMul_le
Rd.seminorm_sub_cutoffMul_le.docstring:
**The cut-off estimate**: the Schwartz seminorm `p_{k,m}(u - χ_n u)` is at most
`Rd.cutoffMulConst k m u / (n + 1)`, because `u - χ_n u` vanishes on the ball of radius `n + 1`
and `‖x‖^k ≤ ‖x‖^(k+1)/(n+1)` outside it.

Rd.schwartzReflect.name: Rd.schwartzReflect
Rd.schwartzReflect.docstring: The **reflection of a Schwartz function**, `x ↦ G(-x)`.

Rd.schwartzDilate_sum.name: Rd.schwartzDilate_sum
Rd.schwartzDilate_sum.docstring: The dilation of Schwartz functions is additive: `(∑_i G_i)_c = ∑_i (G_i)_c`.

Rd.schwartzDilate.name: Rd.schwartzDilate
Rd.schwartzDilate.docstring:
The **dilation of a Schwartz function**: for `c ≠ 0`, the function
`G_c(x) = c^n G(c x)` is a Schwartz function, the composition of `G` with the linear
equivalence `x ↦ c x` (Mathlib's `SchwartzMap.compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv`) times `c^n`.

Rd.schwartzDecayConst_ne_top.name: Rd.schwartzDecayConst_ne_top
Rd.schwartzDecayConst_ne_top.docstring: The decay constant of a Schwartz function is finite.

Rd.schwartzDecayConst_le_familyDecayCons.name: Rd.schwartzDecayConst_le_familyDecayConst
Rd.schwartzDecayConst_le_familyDecayCons.docstring: Every member of a uniform family has decay constant at most that of the family.

Rd.schwartzDecayConst.name: Rd.schwartzDecayConst
Rd.schwartzDecayConst.docstring:
The constant `2^N (sup ‖D^r G‖ + sup ‖x‖^N ‖D^r G(x)‖)` of the decay of the derivatives of
order `r` of a Schwartz function `G`, through two of its seminorms.

Rd.scaledSymbol.name: Rd.scaledSymbol
Rd.scaledSymbol.docstring:
The **rescaled symbol** `ζ ↦ 2^{-jσ} m(2^j ζ)` of `m` at the dyadic level `j`. For a symbol
of order `σ` its derivatives are bounded on annuli uniformly in `j`
(`Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_scaledSymbol_le`).

Rd.rpow_neg_mul_pow_mul_one_add_sq_rpow.name: Rd.rpow_neg_mul_pow_mul_one_add_sq_rpow
Rd.rpow_neg_mul_pow_mul_one_add_sq_rpow.docstring:
**The dyadic weights of a rescaled symbol**: for `c > 0` and `x ≥ 0`,
`c^{-σ} c^k (1 + (c x)²)^{(σ-k)/2} = (c^{-2} + x²)^{(σ-k)/2}`, since
`c^{-2} + x² = c^{-2} (1 + (c x)²)` and `(c^{-2})^{(σ-k)/2} = c^{k-σ}`.

Rd.rpow_lintegral_Ioc_le.name: Rd.rpow_lintegral_Ioc_le
Rd.rpow_lintegral_Ioc_le.docstring:
**Jensen's inequality on the unit interval**: `(∫_0^1 φ)^p ≤ ∫_0^1 φ^p` for real `p ≥ 1` and
measurable `φ ≥ 0`. This is the weighted Jensen inequality `MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_rpow_le`
with the weight `1`, since `(0, 1]` has length `1`.

Rd.restrictionInclusion_restrictProj.name: Rd.restrictionInclusion_restrictProj
Rd.restrictionInclusion_restrictProj.docstring:
**The inclusion commutes with restriction**: for `t ≤ s` and `U ∈ H^s(V)`,
`ι_{t,s}(U|_Ω) = (ι_{t,s} U)|_Ω` in `H^t(Ω)`. `U|_Ω - U` vanishes on `Ω`
(`Rd.sub_restrictProj_mem`), hence so does its inclusion (`Rd.sobolevInclusion_mem_vanishOn`),
which the restriction maps to `0` (`Rd.restrictProj_eq_zero_iff`).

Rd.restrictionInclusion_mem_zeroBoundary.name: Rd.restrictionInclusion_mem_zeroBoundarySpace
Rd.restrictionInclusion_mem_zeroBoundary.docstring:
**The inclusion maps `H^s_0(Ω)` into `H^t_0(Ω)`**: for `t ≤ s`, the restriction of a test
span element `U ∈ T^s(Ω)` goes to `(ι_{t,s} U)|_Ω` (`Rd.restrictionInclusion_restrictProj`),
the restriction of an element of `T^t(Ω)` (`Rd.sobolevInclusion_mem_testSpan`); `H^s_0(Ω)` is the
closure of these restrictions, and the preimage of the closed `H^t_0(Ω)` is closed.

Rd.restrictionInclusion.name: Rd.restrictionInclusion
Rd.restrictionInclusion.docstring:
**The inclusion `H^s(Ω) ⊆ H^t(Ω)`** for `t ≤ s` and an open set `Ω`: `u ↦ (ι_{t,s} u)|_Ω`,
the inclusion `ι_{t,s}` of `u ∈ H^s(Ω) ⊆ H^s(V)` followed by the restriction to `Ω`. It is an
injective bounded operator of norm at most `1` (`Rd.restrictionInclusion_injective`,
`Rd.norm_restrictionInclusion_apply_le`) and commutes with restriction
(`Rd.restrictionInclusion_restrictProj`).

Rd.restrictProj_eq_zero_iff.name: Rd.restrictProj_eq_zero_iff
Rd.restrictProj_eq_zero_iff.docstring:
The kernel of the restriction consists of the elements vanishing on `Ω` (Mathlib's
`Submodule.orthogonalProjectionOnto_eq_zero_iff`, `Submodule.orthogonal_orthogonal`).

Rd.restrictProj_eq_restrictProj_of_ae_eq.name: Rd.restrictProj_eq_restrictProj_of_ae_eq
Rd.restrictProj_eq_restrictProj_of_ae_eq.docstring:
**Restrictions are determined by the `L_2` functions on `Ω`**: for `s ≥ 0`, an open `Ω` and
`U, U' ∈ H^s(V)` with `ι_s U = ι_s U'` almost everywhere on `Ω`, `U|_Ω = U'|_Ω`, since `U - U'`
vanishes on `Ω` (`Rd.mem_vanishOn_iff_sobolevToL2`), the kernel of the restriction
(`Rd.restrictProj_eq_zero_iff`).

Rd.restrictProj_eq_of_ae_eq.name: Rd.restrictProj_eq_of_ae_eq
Rd.restrictProj_eq_of_ae_eq.docstring:
**The restriction of an element that agrees with `u` on `Ω`**: if `U ∈ H^1(V)` and
`u ∈ H^1(Ω)` agree almost everywhere on `Ω`, then `U|_Ω = u`, since both have the restriction
`(ι U)|_Ω` in `L_2(Ω)` (`Rd.restrictL2_restrictProj`, `Rd.restrictL2_eq_iff_ae_eq`) and
`u ↦ u|_Ω` is injective (`Rd.restrictL2_injective`).

Rd.restrictProj_coe.name: Rd.restrictProj_coe
Rd.restrictProj_coe.docstring: The restriction is the identity on `H^s(Ω)`.

Rd.restrictProj.name: Rd.restrictProj
Rd.restrictProj.docstring:
**Restriction to `Ω`**: the orthogonal projection of `H^s(V)` onto `H^s(Ω)`, an operator of
norm at most `1` whose kernel is `Rd.vanishOn s Ω` (`Rd.restrictProj_eq_zero_iff`).

Rd.restrictL2_restrictProj.name: Rd.restrictL2_restrictProj
Rd.restrictL2_restrictProj.docstring:
The restriction to `L_2(Ω)` of `U|_Ω ∈ H^1(Ω)` is the restriction of the `L_2` function of
`U`, because `U - U|_Ω` vanishes on `Ω` (`Rd.sub_restrictProj_mem`).

Rd.restrictL2_injective.name: Rd.restrictL2_injective
Rd.restrictL2_injective.docstring:
**An element of `H^1(Ω)` is determined by its values on `Ω`**: `u ↦ u|_Ω` is injective,
since its kernel lies in `vanishOn 1 Ω ⊓ (vanishOn 1 Ω)ᗮ = ⊥`
(`Rd.mem_vanishOn_one_iff_restrict_eq_zero`, Mathlib's
`Submodule.inf_orthogonal_eq_bot`).

Rd.restrictL2_eq_iff_ae_eq.name: Rd.restrictL2_eq_iff_ae_eq
Rd.restrictL2_eq_iff_ae_eq.docstring:
**`u|_Ω = f|_Ω` as an equation of functions**: for `u ∈ H^1(Ω)` and `f ∈ L_2(V)`,
`restrictL2 Ω u` is the restriction of `f` to `Ω` iff the `L_2` function of `u` equals `f` almost
everywhere on `Ω` (Mathlib's `LpToLpRestrictCLM_coeFn`).

Rd.restrictL2_apply.name: Rd.restrictL2_apply
Rd.restrictL2_apply.docstring: `restrictL2 Ω u` is the restriction to `Ω` of the `L_2` function of `u`.

Rd.restrictL2.name: Rd.restrictL2
Rd.restrictL2.docstring:
**`H^1(Ω)` in `L_2(Ω)`**: the bounded operator `u ↦ u|_Ω` from `H^1(Ω)` to `L_2(Ω)`, the
restriction of the `L_2` function of `u ∈ H^1(V)` to `Ω`. It is injective
(`Rd.restrictL2_injective`), has norm at most `1` (`Rd.norm_restrictL2_apply_le`), and is compact
for bounded `Ω` (`Rd.isCompactOperator_restrictL2`).

Rd.restr_truncL2_mem_closureToLp_image.name: Rd.restr_truncL2_mem_closureToLp_image
Rd.restr_truncL2_mem_closureToLp_image.docstring:
**The truncations restricted to `Ω` are band-limited functions**: for `‖F‖_{H^1} ≤ 1`, the
restriction of `truncL2 K F` to a bounded set `Ω` is (the class of) a bounded continuous function
on `closure Ω` with `|g| ≤ |B_K|^{1/2}` that is Lipschitz with constant
`2π max(K, 0) |B_K|^{1/2}`: the function `𝓕⁻(1_{B_K} 𝓕(toL2 F))`
(`Rd.truncL2_ae_eq_fourierInv_indicator`, `Rd.norm_fourierInv_indicator_le`,
`Rd.lipschitzWith_fourierInv_indicator`), since `‖𝓕(toL2 F)‖_2 ≤ ‖F‖_{H^1} ≤ 1`.

Rd.repr_sub_zcellCenter.name: Rd.repr_sub_zcellCenter
Rd.repr_sub_zcellCenter.docstring: The `i`-th coordinate of `x - c_{k,m}` is `(2^k x_i - m_i - 1/2) / 2^k`.

Rd.reflectionConst_ne_top.name: Rd.reflectionConst_ne_top
Rd.reflectionConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of the boundary patches by reflection is finite for finite `d`.

Rd.reflectionConst.name: Rd.reflectionConst
Rd.reflectionConst.docstring:
The **constant of the boundary patches by reflection**: `2 + 2 n (1 + M)² (1 + d)` for the
dimension `n`, the Lipschitz constant `M` of the graph and the sum `d` of the bounds of the
derivatives of the cutoff
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_hasWeakLineDeriv_reflectionExtension_mul`).

Rd.reflectNeg_apply.name: Rd.reflectNeg_apply
Rd.reflectNeg_apply.docstring: The values of the reflection: `K^∨(x) = K(-x)`.

Rd.reflectNeg.name: Rd.reflectNeg
Rd.reflectNeg.docstring: The **reflection** `K^∨(x) = K(-x)` of a function `K : V → ℂ`.

Rd.rayIntegral.name: Rd.rayIntegral
Rd.rayIntegral.docstring:
The **ray integral** `Ψ(y) = ∫_0^∞ g(y + t w) dt` of `g` along the ray from `y` in the
direction `w`.

Rd.range_tildeToRestrictionL_le.name: Rd.range_tildeToRestrictionL_le
Rd.range_tildeToRestrictionL_le.docstring:
The restriction maps `H̃^s(Ω)` into `H^s_0(Ω)`, by continuity of the restriction (Mathlib's
`map_mem_closure`).

Rd.range_tildeToRestriction.name: Rd.range_tildeToRestriction
Rd.range_tildeToRestriction.docstring:
**The image of `H̃^1(Ω)` is `H^1_0(Ω)`**: the range of the isometry `tildeToRestriction` is
closed, since `H̃^1(Ω)` is complete (Mathlib's `Isometry.isClosedEmbedding`), and its closure is
`H^1_0(Ω)` (`Rd.closure_range_tildeToRestrictionL`).

Rd.prod_pi_norm_le_norm_fst_add_sum.name: Rd.prod_pi_norm_le_norm_fst_add_sum
Rd.prod_pi_norm_le_norm_fst_add_sum.docstring: The sup norm of `(x, (y_i)_i) ∈ E × F^ι` is at most `‖x‖ + ∑_i ‖y_i‖`.

Rd.prod_pi_norm_fst_add_sum_le.name: Rd.prod_pi_norm_fst_add_sum_le
Rd.prod_pi_norm_fst_add_sum_le.docstring:
`‖x‖ + ∑_i ‖y_i‖` is at most `(#ι + 1)` times the sup norm of `(x, (y_i)_i) ∈ E × F^ι`
(Mathlib's `Pi.sum_norm_apply_le_norm`, `∑_i ‖y_i‖ ≤ #ι ‖y‖`).

Rd.peetre_mul_peetre_le.name: Rd.peetre_mul_peetre_le
Rd.peetre_mul_peetre_le.docstring:
The integrand of the convolution of two Peetre bumps, pointwise: for `i ≤ j`,
`2^(jn) (1 + 2^j ‖y - w‖)^(-2N) 2^(in) (1 + 2^i ‖w‖)^(-N)` is at most
`2^(jn) (1 + 2^j ‖y - w‖)^(-N) 2^(in) (1 + 2^i ‖y‖)^(-N)`.

Rd.peetreIntegral_ne_top.name: Rd.peetreIntegral_ne_top
Rd.peetreIntegral_ne_top.docstring:
The integral of the Peetre weight is finite for `M > n` (Mathlib's
`finite_integral_one_add_norm`).

Rd.peetreIntegral.name: Rd.peetreIntegral
Rd.peetreIntegral.docstring: The integral `∫ (1 + ‖u‖)^(-M) du` of the Peetre weight, finite for `M > n`.

Rd.pasting_bound.name: Rd.pasting_bound
Rd.pasting_bound.docstring:
**The arithmetic of the pasting bound**: if `‖F‖ ≤ ∑_k a_k x_k`,
`‖G_i‖ ≤ ∑_k (a_k y_{k,i} + d_{k,i} x_k)` and `x_k + ∑_i y_{k,i} ≤ C_k Y`, then
`‖F‖ + ∑_i ‖G_i‖ ≤ (∑_k (a_k + ∑_i d_{k,i}) C_k) Y`.

Rd.pairwise_disjoint_dyadicAnnulus.name: Rd.pairwise_disjoint_dyadicAnnulus
Rd.pairwise_disjoint_dyadicAnnulus.docstring: For `ρ ≥ 0` the dyadic annuli are pairwise disjoint.

Rd.orthogonal_tildeSpace_eq_comap.name: Rd.orthogonal_tildeSpace_eq_comap
Rd.orthogonal_tildeSpace_eq_comap.docstring:
**The orthogonal complement of `H̃^t(Ω)` as a preimage**: for a linear isometry `e` of
`H^t(V)` onto `H^{t'}(V)` whose values are the distributions `J_t (J_t U)`, `H̃^t(Ω)^⊥` is the
preimage under `e` of the elements of `H^{t'}(V)` vanishing on `Ω`
(`Rd.mem_orthogonal_tildeSpace_iff_toLp`). The hypothesis determines `e`, and such an `e` exists
only for `t' = -t`; the lemma is stated with `t'` free so that it applies to both
`Rd.besselShift s` and its inverse.

Rd.orthogonal_singleton_ne_top.name: Rd.orthogonal_singleton_ne_top
Rd.orthogonal_singleton_ne_top.docstring:
For `e ≠ 0` the orthogonal complement `e^⊥` is a proper subspace: `Kᗮ = ⊤` only for `K = ⊥`
(Mathlib's `Submodule.orthogonal_eq_top_iff`), and `ℝ e = ⊥` only for `e = 0` (Mathlib's
`Submodule.span_singleton_eq_bot`).

Rd.openHalfSpace.name: Rd.openHalfSpace
Rd.openHalfSpace.docstring: The **open half-space** `H₊ = {y : 0 < ⟪y, e⟫}`, an open set.

Rd.one_le_two_mul_enorm_sq_add.name: Rd.one_le_two_mul_enorm_sq_add
Rd.one_le_two_mul_enorm_sq_add.docstring:
Two complex numbers with `x + y = 1` satisfy `1 ≤ 2(|x|² + |y|²)`: `1 ≤ |x| + |y|` by the
triangle inequality, and `(a + b)² ≤ 2(a² + b²)` (Mathlib's `add_sq_le`).

Rd.one_div_two_pow_pos.name: Rd.one_div_two_pow_pos
Rd.one_div_two_pow_pos.docstring: The radius `2^(-j)` of the balls of the ball means is positive.

Rd.one_add_norm_sq_rpow_le_one_add_norm_.name: Rd.one_add_norm_sq_rpow_le_one_add_norm_pow
Rd.one_add_norm_sq_rpow_le_one_add_norm_.docstring:
**The bracket below a polynomial weight**: `(1 + ‖ξ‖²)^{a/2} ≤ (1 + ‖ξ‖)^N` for `a ≤ N`, since
`1 + ‖ξ‖² ≥ 1` and `√(1 + ‖ξ‖²) ≤ 1 + ‖ξ‖` (Mathlib's `sqrt_one_add_norm_sq_le`).

Rd.one_add_norm_pow_mul_le_schwartz.name: Rd.one_add_norm_pow_mul_le_schwartz
Rd.one_add_norm_pow_mul_le_schwartz.docstring:
`(1 + ‖x‖)^N ‖D^r G(x)‖ ≤ 2^N (sup ‖D^r G‖ + sup ‖x‖^N ‖D^r G(x)‖)` for a Schwartz function
`G`, from `(1 + t)^N ≤ 2^N (1 + t^N)`. Mathlib's `SchwartzMap.one_add_le_sup_seminorm_apply` is
the same kind of bound with the supremum over a range of seminorms.

Rd.one_add_norm_le_mul_of_mem_Icc.name: Rd.one_add_norm_le_mul_of_mem_Icc
Rd.one_add_norm_le_mul_of_mem_Icc.docstring:
**Peetre's inequality along a segment**: `1 + ‖y‖ ≤ (1 + ‖y + t v‖)(1 + r ‖v‖)` for
`0 ≤ t ≤ r`.

Rd.ofTest_eq_ofSchwartz.name: Rd.ofTest_eq_ofSchwartz
Rd.ofTest_eq_ofSchwartz.docstring: A test function of `Ω` in `H^s(V)` is its Schwartz function: `ofTest s φ = ofSchwartz s φ`.

Rd.ofTest.name: Rd.ofTest
Rd.ofTest.docstring:
**A test function as an element of `H^s(V)`**: a real test function `φ` of `Ω`, as the
complex Schwartz function `Rd.testSchwartz φ`, lies in every `H^s(V)` (Mathlib's
`SchwartzMap.memSobolev`).

Rd.ofSchwartz_mem_testSpan.name: Rd.ofSchwartz_mem_testSpan
Rd.ofSchwartz_mem_testSpan.docstring:
**Compactly supported Schwartz functions in `Ω` lie in the span of the test functions**: a
Schwartz function `w` with compact support in the open set `Ω` is `Re w + i Im w` with real test
functions of `Ω` (`Rd.exists_testSchwartz_eq_of_tsupport_subset`), so `w ∈ testSpan s Ω` for every
real `s`.

Rd.ofSchwartz.name: Rd.ofSchwartz
Rd.ofSchwartz.docstring:
**Schwartz functions in `H^s(V)`, continuously**: `w ↦ w ∈ H^s(V)` as a continuous linear
map from the Schwartz space: `w` is the element of `H^s(V)` whose Bessel potential `J_s w ∈ L_2(V)`
(Mathlib's `BesselPotentialSpace.toLp`) is the Schwartz function `Rd.besselSchwartz s w`
(`Rd.toDistr_ofSchwartz`).

Rd.ofReal_two_pow_mul.name: Rd.ofReal_two_pow_mul
Rd.ofReal_two_pow_mul.docstring:
`2^(jn)` as an extended real is the dyadic weight `2^(jn)`, since `2^(jn) = (2^j)^n`
(`ENNReal.ofReal_two_pow_pow`).

Rd.ofReal_mul_enorm_mul_enorm_fourier_le.name: Rd.ofReal_mul_enorm_mul_enorm_fourier_le
Rd.ofReal_mul_enorm_mul_enorm_fourier_le.docstring:
**Fourier transforms of Schwartz functions decay like `1/‖ξ‖`**:
`2π ‖ξ‖ |𝓕G(ξ)| ≤ C_G` with the gradient mass `C_G = Rd.gradMassConst G`, since
`𝓕(∂_ξ G)(ξ) = 2πi ‖ξ‖² 𝓕G(ξ)` (Mathlib's `SchwartzMap.fourier_lineDerivOp_eq`) and
`∫ |∂_ξ G| ≤ ‖ξ‖ C_G` (`Rd.lintegral_enorm_lineDerivOp_le`).

Rd.ofReal_besselWeight_sq_le_tsum.name: Rd.ofReal_besselWeight_sq_le_tsum
Rd.ofReal_besselWeight_sq_le_tsum.docstring:
**The Bessel weight is at most the Littlewood–Paley symbol**: for `s ≥ 0` and every `ξ ∈ V`,
`⟨ξ⟩^{2s} ≤ 2 · 5^s ∑_j 2^(2js) |𝓕ψ_j(ξ)|²`. The two blocks `a`, `a + 1` of
`Rd.exists_fourier_lpBlockKernel_window` have `|𝓕ψ_a(ξ)|² + |𝓕ψ_{a+1}(ξ)|² ≥ 1/2`, and
`⟨ξ⟩^{2s} ≤ 5^s 2^(2js)` for both.

Rd.ofReal_besselWeight_one_sq.name: Rd.ofReal_besselWeight_one_sq
Rd.ofReal_besselWeight_one_sq.docstring:
**Parseval for the Bessel weight**: `⟨ξ⟩² = 1 + ∑_i ⟪ξ, e_i⟫²` for every orthonormal basis
`(e_i)` of `V` (Mathlib's `OrthonormalBasis.sum_sq_inner_left`).

Rd.ofReal_abs_inv_neg_inv_two_pow_pow.name: Rd.ofReal_abs_inv_neg_inv_two_pow_pow
Rd.ofReal_abs_inv_neg_inv_two_pow_pow.docstring: The scaling factor of the steps: `|((-2^(-m))^n)⁻¹| = 2^(mn)`.

Rd.ofFun_top_apply.name: Rd.ofFun_top_apply
Rd.ofFun_top_apply.docstring:
On `Ω = V`, the distribution of `f ∈ L_p(V)` applied to a test function `φ` is the tempered
distribution of `f` applied to the Schwartz function `φ`: both are `∫ φ f`.

Rd.ofFun_sum_smul.name: Rd.ofFun_sum_smul
Rd.ofFun_sum_smul.docstring:
The distribution of a finite combination `∑_i c_i g_i` with real `c_i` of locally integrable
functions is `∑_i c_i` times the distributions of the `g_i` (Mathlib's `Distribution.ofFun_add`
and `Distribution.ofFun_smul`).

Rd.norm_toLp_indicator_le.name: Rd.norm_toLp_indicator_le
Rd.norm_toLp_indicator_le.docstring: `‖1_s g‖_p ≤ ‖g‖_p` for the class of `1_s g`.

Rd.norm_toLp_conv_le.name: Rd.norm_toLp_conv_le
Rd.norm_toLp_conv_le.docstring:
**Young's inequality for the classes in `L_p`**:
`‖K ⋆ f‖_p ≤ ‖K‖_1 ‖f‖_p` for `f ∈ L_p`.

Rd.norm_toL2_sub_truncL2_le.name: Rd.norm_toL2_sub_truncL2_le
Rd.norm_toL2_sub_truncL2_le.docstring: **The truncations approximate in operator norm**: `‖toL2 - truncL2 K‖ ≤ K⁻¹` for `K > 0`.

Rd.norm_toL2_sub_truncL2_apply_le.name: Rd.norm_toL2_sub_truncL2_apply_le
Rd.norm_toL2_sub_truncL2_apply_le.docstring:
**The truncation error**: for `K > 0` and `F ∈ H^1(V)`,
`‖toL2 F - truncL2 K F‖_2 ≤ K⁻¹ ‖F‖_{H^1}`. By Plancherel the left side is the `L_2` norm of
`1_{|ξ| > K} ⟨ξ⟩⁻¹ 𝓕(J_1 F)`, and `⟨ξ⟩⁻¹ ≤ K⁻¹` for `|ξ| > K`.

Rd.norm_toL2_le.name: Rd.norm_toL2_le
Rd.norm_toL2_le.docstring:
**`‖F‖_2 ≤ ‖F‖_{H^1}`**: by Plancherel, `‖toL2 F‖_2 = ‖⟨ξ⟩⁻¹ 𝓕(J_1 F)‖_2 ≤ ‖𝓕(J_1 F)‖_2`
(`Rd.norm_besselInvMul_le_one`), and `‖𝓕(J_1 F)‖_2 = ‖F‖_{H^1}` (Mathlib's
`BesselPotentialSpace.norm_fourier_toLp_eq`).

Rd.norm_sub_halfSpaceReflection.name: Rd.norm_sub_halfSpaceReflection
Rd.norm_sub_halfSpaceReflection.docstring: **The distance to the reflected point**: `‖y - σ y‖ = 2 |⟪y, e⟫|` for a unit vector `e`.

Rd.norm_restrictProj_of_mem_tildeSpace.name: Rd.norm_restrictProj_of_mem_tildeSpace
Rd.norm_restrictProj_of_mem_tildeSpace.docstring:
**Restriction is isometric on `H̃^1(Ω)`**: for `U ∈ H̃^1(Ω)`, `‖U|_Ω‖ = ‖U‖`, by continuity
from the test functions (`Rd.norm_restrictProj_of_mem_testSpan`).

Rd.norm_restrictProj_of_mem_testSpan.name: Rd.norm_restrictProj_of_mem_testSpan
Rd.norm_restrictProj_of_mem_testSpan.docstring:
**Restriction preserves the norm of test functions**: for `U ∈ testSpan 1 Ω`,
`‖U|_Ω‖_{H^1(Ω)} = ‖U‖_{H^1(V)}`. The norm of `U|_Ω` is `‖U + W‖` for some `W` vanishing on `Ω`
(`Rd.exists_norm_restrictProj_eq`), which is at least `‖U‖`
(`Rd.norm_le_norm_add_of_mem_testSpan`).

Rd.norm_restrictProj_apply_le.name: Rd.norm_restrictProj_apply_le
Rd.norm_restrictProj_apply_le.docstring: The restriction has norm at most `1`: `‖U|_Ω‖ ≤ ‖U‖`.

Rd.norm_pow_succ_mul_cutoffMulBound_le.name: Rd.norm_pow_succ_mul_cutoffMulBound_le
Rd.norm_pow_succ_mul_cutoffMulBound_le.docstring:
The pointwise form of the cut-off estimate: `‖x‖^(k+1) B(x) ≤ Rd.cutoffMulConst k m u` for
