the pointwise bound `B = Rd.cutoffMulBound m u`.

Rd.norm_pow_eq_sum_prod_inner.name: Rd.norm_pow_eq_sum_prod_inner
Rd.norm_pow_eq_sum_prod_inner.docstring:
**Powers of the norm in coordinates**: with the orthonormal basis `e_0, …, e_{n-1}` of
`Rd.gridBasis`, `‖ξ‖^{2m} = ∑_{i : Fin m → Fin n} ∏_k ⟪ξ, e_{i_k}⟫²`, from
`‖ξ‖² = ∑_i ⟪ξ, e_i⟫²` (Mathlib's `OrthonormalBasis.sum_sq_inner_left`) and the expansion of an
`m`-th power of a sum (Mathlib's `Fintype.sum_pow`).

Rd.norm_lt_of_fourier_lpBlockKernel_ne_z.name: Rd.norm_lt_of_fourier_lpBlockKernel_ne_zero
Rd.norm_lt_of_fourier_lpBlockKernel_ne_z.docstring: `𝓕ψ_j` vanishes outside the ball of radius `2^(j+1)`.

Rd.norm_lt_of_fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_.name: Rd.norm_lt_of_fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_ne_zero
Rd.norm_lt_of_fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_.docstring: `𝓕ψ̃_j` vanishes outside the ball of radius `2^(j+2)`.

Rd.norm_lt_of_fourier_dilatedLpKernel_ne.name: Rd.norm_lt_of_fourier_dilatedLpKernel_ne_zero
Rd.norm_lt_of_fourier_dilatedLpKernel_ne.docstring: `𝓕Φ_k` vanishes outside the ball of radius `2^(k+1)`.

Rd.norm_lt_of_fourier_dilatedBandKernel_.name: Rd.norm_lt_of_fourier_dilatedBandKernel_ne_zero
Rd.norm_lt_of_fourier_dilatedBandKernel_.docstring: `𝓕Θ_k` vanishes outside the ball of radius `2^(k+2)`.

Rd.norm_lt_of_cutoff_ne_zero.name: Rd.norm_lt_of_cutoff_ne_zero
Rd.norm_lt_of_cutoff_ne_zero.docstring: Where the cut-off does not vanish, `‖ξ‖ < b`.

Rd.norm_le_one_of_forall_mem_Icc.name: Rd.norm_le_one_of_forall_mem_Icc
Rd.norm_le_one_of_forall_mem_Icc.docstring:
A real function with values in `[0, 1]`, such as the cutoffs of
`Rd.exists_contDiff_eventuallyEq_one`, has norm at most `1`.

Rd.norm_le_of_mem_tsupport_dilate.name: Rd.norm_le_of_mem_tsupport_dilate
Rd.norm_le_of_mem_tsupport_dilate.docstring:
**Dilated supports shrink**: if the closed support of `η` lies in `B̄(0, R)` and `c > 0`, the
closed support of `η_c` lies in `B̄(0, R/c)`.

Rd.norm_le_of_iteratedFDeriv_le.name: Rd.norm_le_of_iteratedFDeriv_le
Rd.norm_le_of_iteratedFDeriv_le.docstring: The bound `‖ψ‖ ≤ C` from `‖D^0 ψ‖ ≤ C`.

Rd.norm_le_of_hasWeakLineDeriv_toL2.name: Rd.norm_le_of_hasWeakLineDeriv_toL2
Rd.norm_le_of_hasWeakLineDeriv_toL2.docstring:
**The weak derivatives of `H^1(V)` are bounded**: if `g ∈ L_2(V)` is the weak derivative
`∂_v` on `V` of the `L_2` function of `U ∈ H^1(V)`, then `‖g‖_2 ≤ 2π ‖v‖ ‖U‖`
(`Rd.enorm_le_of_hasWeakLineDeriv` with `J_1 f = U`).

Rd.norm_le_norm_add_of_mem_testSpan.name: Rd.norm_le_norm_add_of_mem_testSpan
Rd.norm_le_norm_add_of_mem_testSpan.docstring:
**The `H^1(V)` norm of a test function of `Ω` is at most that of its sum with a function
vanishing on `Ω`**: for `U ∈ testSpan 1 Ω` and `W` vanishing on `Ω`, `‖U‖ ≤ ‖U + W‖`. With an
orthonormal basis `(e_i)`, `‖U‖² = ‖U‖_2² + (2π)⁻² ∑_i ‖∂_{e_i} U‖_2²`
(`Rd.sq_norm_eq_of_hasWeakLineDeriv`), and the same for `U + W`. `U` and its weak gradient vanish
near `V \ Ω` (`Rd.exists_opens_toL2_ae_eq_zero`), `W` and its weak gradient vanish on `Ω`
(`Rd.mem_vanishOn_one_iff`, `Rd.weakDeriv_ae_zero_of_mem_vanishOn`), so each `L_2` norm grows
(`Rd.norm_le_norm_add_of_ae_eq_zero`).

Rd.norm_le_norm_add_of_ae_eq_zero.name: Rd.norm_le_norm_add_of_ae_eq_zero
Rd.norm_le_norm_add_of_ae_eq_zero.docstring:
**Functions with disjoint supports**: in every `L_p(μ)` with values in a normed group, if
`a` vanishes almost everywhere outside a measurable set `S` and `b` vanishes almost everywhere on
`S`, then `‖a‖_p ≤ ‖a + b‖_p`, since `|a + b| ≥ |a|` almost everywhere (Mathlib's
`Lp.norm_le_norm_of_ae_le`).

Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_sub_cutoffMul_le.name: Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_sub_cutoffMul_le
Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_sub_cutoffMul_le.docstring:
The derivatives of `u - χ_n u` are bounded by the pointwise bound `Rd.cutoffMulBound`,
uniformly in `n`.

Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_schwartz_le_of_me.name: Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_schwartz_le_of_mem_Icc
Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_schwartz_le_of_me.docstring:
The derivatives of order `r` of a Schwartz function along the segment from `y` to `y + r v`
are at most `2^N (sup ‖D^r G‖ + sup ‖x‖^N ‖D^r G(x)‖) (1 + r ‖v‖)^N (1 + ‖y‖)^(-N)`.

Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_scaledSymbol_le.name: Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_scaledSymbol_le
Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_scaledSymbol_le.docstring:
**Bounds of a rescaled symbol**: if `‖D^k m(ξ)‖ ≤ C (1 + ‖ξ‖²)^{(σ-k)/2}`, then
`‖D^k (2^{-jσ} m(2^j ·))(ζ)‖ ≤ C (2^{-2j} + ‖ζ‖²)^{(σ-k)/2}`
(`Rd.iteratedFDeriv_scaledSymbol`, `Rd.rpow_neg_mul_pow_mul_one_add_sq_rpow`).

Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_mul_schwartz_le.name: Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_mul_schwartz_le
Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_mul_schwartz_le.docstring:
**The Leibniz bound against a Schwartz function**: if the derivatives of the smooth function
`g` at `x` of the orders `i ≤ l` are at most `C_i`, then
`‖D^l (g ω)(x)‖ ≤ ∑_{i ≤ l} C(l, i) C_i ‖ω‖_{0, l-i}` (Mathlib's `norm_iteratedFDeriv_mul_le`).

Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_line_le.name: Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_line_le
Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_line_le.docstring:
**The line `t ↦ x + t h`**: its derivatives of order `i ≥ 1` have norm at most `‖h‖^i`
(the first derivative is `h`, the higher ones vanish).

Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_fwdDiff_le_of_seg.name: Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_fwdDiff_le_of_segment
Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_fwdDiff_le_of_seg.docstring:
The derivative bound of one step of `Rd.norm_higherDiff_le_of_segment`: for `G` of class
`C^(l+1)`, if `‖D^(l+1) G‖ ≤ C` at the points `x + s h`, `0 ≤ s ≤ l + 1`, then
`‖D^l (Δ_h G)‖ ≤ C ‖h‖` at the points `x + t h`, `0 ≤ t ≤ l`, by the mean value inequality on the
segment from `x + t h` to `x + (t + 1) h`.

Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_dilate_le.name: Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_dilate_le
Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_dilate_le.docstring:
**Derivatives of a dilation**: `‖D^l (Φ_c)(x)‖ ≤ c^(n+l) ‖D^l Φ(c x)‖` for `c ≥ 0`, since
`Φ_c = c^n Φ(c ·)`.

Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_cutoff_comp_smul_.name: Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_cutoff_comp_smul_le
Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_cutoff_comp_smul_.docstring:
For `0 ≤ c ≤ 1` the derivatives of the rescaled cut-off `x ↦ χ(c x)` are bounded by the
Schwartz seminorms `p_{0,i}(χ) = sup ‖D^i χ‖` of `χ = Rd.cutoffSchwartz 1 2`, because
`D^i (χ(c ·))(x) = c^i D^i χ(c x)` (Mathlib's `iteratedFDeriv_comp_const_smul`).

Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_cutoffMul_le.name: Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_cutoffMul_le
Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_cutoffMul_le.docstring:
The **Leibniz bound** for the cut-off: `‖D^m (χ_n u)(x)‖ ≤ ∑_{i ≤ m} C(m,i) p_{0,i}(χ)
‖D^(m-i) u(x)‖`, uniformly in `n` (Mathlib's `norm_iteratedFDeriv_mul_le`).

Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_const_mul_conv_le.name: Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_const_mul_conv_le
Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_const_mul_conv_le.docstring:
**Bounds for the derivatives of a convolution**: if `‖D^n K‖ ≤ M` and `K = 0` outside
`B̄(0, ρ)`, the derivative of order `n` of `c (K ⋆ g)` is bounded through the convolutions with the
directional derivatives `(D^n K)(·)(v)`, which satisfy `|(D^n K)(·)(v)| ≤ M ∏ ‖v_i‖`.

Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_clm_le.name: Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_clm_le
Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_clm_le.docstring:
**Derivatives of a composition with a linear map**:
`‖D^i (f ∘ L)(x)‖ ≤ ‖D^i f(L x)‖ ‖L‖^i`.

Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_cellAtom_le.name: Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_cellAtom_le
Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_cellAtom_le.docstring:
**Derivatives of cell atoms**: if `K` is smooth, vanishes outside `B̄(0, ρ 2^(-j))` and
`‖D^l K‖ ≤ A 2^(j(n+l))`, then `‖D^l a_{j,m}‖ ≤ A 2^(jl) (ρ^n |B_1|)^(1-1/p)`.

Rd.norm_higherDiff_two_conv_le.name: Rd.norm_higherDiff_two_conv_le
Rd.norm_higherDiff_two_conv_le.docstring:
**Second differences of convolutions with Lipschitz functions**: for `K = 0` outside
`B̄(0, R)`, `‖Δ_h^2 (K ⋆ u)(x)‖ ≤ M (R + 2‖h‖) ‖Δ_h^2 K‖_1`, since
`Δ_h^2 (K ⋆ u) = (Δ_h^2 K) ⋆ u` and `∫ Δ_h^2 K = 0`.

Rd.norm_higherDiff_le_of_segment.name: Rd.norm_higherDiff_le_of_segment
Rd.norm_higherDiff_le_of_segment.docstring:
**Differences along a segment**: for `G` of class `C^l`, if `‖D^l G‖ ≤ C` at the points
`x + t h`, `0 ≤ t ≤ l`, then `‖Δ_h^l G(x)‖ ≤ C ‖h‖^l`. By induction on `l`: the derivatives of
order `l` of `Δ_h G` at `x + t h` are differences of those of `G`, bounded by the mean value
inequality on the segment from `x + t h` to `x + (t + 1) h`.

Rd.norm_higherDiff_le_of_iteratedFDerivW.name: Rd.norm_higherDiff_le_of_iteratedFDerivWithin
Rd.norm_higherDiff_le_of_iteratedFDerivW.docstring:
**Differences of order `r ≥ 1` within a convex set**: if `a` is of class `C^r` within the
convex set `Ω` with nonempty interior and `‖D^i a‖ ≤ C` on `Ω` for `i ≤ r`, then
`|Δ_h^r a(x)| ≤ 2^r r^(r+1) C ‖h‖^r` whenever `x, x + h, …, x + r h ∈ Ω`.

Rd.norm_higherDiff_le_of_iteratedFDeriv.name: Rd.norm_higherDiff_le_of_iteratedFDeriv
Rd.norm_higherDiff_le_of_iteratedFDeriv.docstring:
**Differences of smooth functions**: if `‖D^l G‖ ≤ C` everywhere, then
`‖Δ_h^l G(x)‖ ≤ C ‖h‖^l`, the case of `Rd.norm_higherDiff_le_of_segment` with the bound on the
whole space.

Rd.norm_fwdDiff_iter_le_of_iteratedDeriv.name: Rd.norm_fwdDiff_iter_le_of_iteratedDerivWithin
Rd.norm_fwdDiff_iter_le_of_iteratedDeriv.docstring:
**Differences of order `r` and the `r`-th derivative on an interval**: if `g` is of class
`C^r` on `[0, r]`, `r = n + 1`, and `‖g^(r)‖ ≤ C` there, then
`|Δ_1^r g(0)| ≤ 2^r r^r C / (r-1)!`.

Rd.norm_fourier_lpBlockKernel_le_one.name: Rd.norm_fourier_lpBlockKernel_le_one
Rd.norm_fourier_lpBlockKernel_le_one.docstring:
**The Fourier transforms of the blocks are bounded by `1`**: `|𝓕ψ_j(ξ)| ≤ 1`, since
`𝓕ψ_0 = χ(ξ)` and `𝓕ψ_{j+1} = χ(2^(-j-1) ξ) - χ(2^(-j) ξ)` with a cut-off `χ` with values in
`[0, 1]`.

Rd.norm_fourier_le_of_integral_eq_zero.name: Rd.norm_fourier_le_of_integral_eq_zero
Rd.norm_fourier_le_of_integral_eq_zero.docstring:
**Fourier transforms of mean-zero kernels vanish at `0` to first order**: for a Schwartz
function `G` with `∫ G = 0`, `|𝓕G(ξ)| ≤ 2π ‖ξ‖ ∫ ‖x‖ |G(x)| dx`, since
`𝓕G(ξ) = ∫ (e^(-2πi⟪x, ξ⟫) - 1) G(x) dx` and the character is `2π`-Lipschitz
(`Rd.norm_fourierChar_sub_le`).

Rd.norm_fourier_dilatedLpKernel_sub_le_o.name: Rd.norm_fourier_dilatedLpKernel_sub_le_one
Rd.norm_fourier_dilatedLpKernel_sub_le_o.docstring: `|𝓕Φ_k(ξ) - 𝓕Φ_l(ξ)| ≤ 1`, since both values lie in `[0, 1]`.

Rd.norm_fourierInv_sub_le.name: Rd.norm_fourierInv_sub_le
Rd.norm_fourierInv_sub_le.docstring:
**Band-limited functions are Lipschitz**: if `g` is integrable and `g(ξ) = 0` for almost
every `ξ` with `|ξ| > K`, then `|𝓕⁻g(x) - 𝓕⁻g(y)| ≤ 2πK |x - y| ∫ |g|` for all `x, y`, since
`|e^(2πi⟪ξ, x⟫) - e^(2πi⟪ξ, y⟫)| ≤ 2π |⟪ξ, x - y⟫| ≤ 2πK |x - y|` for `|ξ| ≤ K`.

Rd.norm_fourierInv_le_integral_norm.name: Rd.norm_fourierInv_le_integral_norm
Rd.norm_fourierInv_le_integral_norm.docstring:
The inverse Fourier transform is bounded by the `L_1` norm: `|𝓕⁻g(x)| ≤ ∫ |g|` for every
`x`.

Rd.norm_fourierInv_indicator_le.name: Rd.norm_fourierInv_indicator_le
Rd.norm_fourierInv_indicator_le.docstring:
**Band-limited functions are bounded**: for `h ∈ L_2(V)` and every `x`,
`|𝓕⁻(1_{B_K} h)(x)| ≤ |B_K|^{1/2} ‖h‖_2`.

Rd.norm_fourierChar_sub_le.name: Rd.norm_fourierChar_sub_le
Rd.norm_fourierChar_sub_le.docstring:
The character `t ↦ e^(2πit)` is `2π`-Lipschitz: `|e^(2πia) - e^(2πib)| ≤ 2π |a - b|`
(Mathlib's `Real.norm_exp_I_mul_ofReal_sub_one_le`).

Rd.norm_foldHalfSpace.name: Rd.norm_foldHalfSpace
Rd.norm_foldHalfSpace.docstring:
The folding preserves the norm: `‖x + c e‖² = ‖x‖² + c (2⟪x, e⟫ + c)` vanishes in the second
term for `c = |⟪x, e⟫| - ⟪x, e⟫`.

Rd.norm_extendClosure_sub_le.name: Rd.norm_extendClosure_sub_le
Rd.norm_extendClosure_sub_le.docstring:
The extensions by `0` of `g` and `g'` differ by at most the uniform distance of `g` and
`g'`.

Rd.norm_extendClosure_le.name: Rd.norm_extendClosure_le
Rd.norm_extendClosure_le.docstring: The extension by `0` is bounded by the uniform norm of `g`.

Rd.norm_derivSymbol_le.name: Rd.norm_derivSymbol_le
Rd.norm_derivSymbol_le.docstring:
**The symbols are bounded away from the origin**: `|σ_i(ξ)| ≤ 1` for `‖ξ‖ ≥ 1`, since
`|⟪ξ, e⟫| ≤ ‖ξ‖`, `‖ξ‖^m ≤ ‖ξ‖^{2m}` and `(2π)^m ≥ 1`.

Rd.norm_conv_sub_self_le.name: Rd.norm_conv_sub_self_le
Rd.norm_conv_sub_self_le.docstring:
**Convolution moves Lipschitz functions little**: for `∫ K = 1` and `K = 0` outside
`B̄(0, R)`, `‖(K ⋆ u)(x) - u(x)‖ ≤ M R ‖K‖_1`.

Rd.norm_conv_sub_conv_le.name: Rd.norm_conv_sub_conv_le
Rd.norm_conv_sub_conv_le.docstring:
**Convolution keeps Lipschitz bounds**: for `u` with `‖u(x) - u(y)‖ ≤ M ‖x - y‖`,
`‖(K ⋆ u)(x) - (K ⋆ u)(y)‖ ≤ M ‖K‖_1 ‖x - y‖`.

Rd.norm_besselWeight_neg_one_le_one.name: Rd.norm_besselWeight_neg_one_le_one
Rd.norm_besselWeight_neg_one_le_one.docstring: `|⟨ξ⟩⁻¹| ≤ 1` for the Bessel weight of order `-1` as a complex number.

Rd.norm_besselWeight_le_one.name: Rd.norm_besselWeight_le_one
Rd.norm_besselWeight_le_one.docstring: `|⟨ξ⟩^t| ≤ 1` for `t ≤ 0`, for the Bessel weight as a complex number.

Rd.norm_besselSymbol_le.name: Rd.norm_besselSymbol_le
Rd.norm_besselSymbol_le.docstring:
**Size of the shifted Bessel symbols on the annulus**: for `0 < a ≤ ‖ζ‖ ≤ b` and
`ε ∈ [0, 1]`, `|(ε + ‖ζ‖²)^{σ/2}| ≤ max((a²)^{σ/2}, (1 + b²)^{σ/2})`, since
`ε + ‖ζ‖² ∈ [a², 1 + b²]` and `t ↦ t^{σ/2}` is monotone.

Rd.norm_besselInvMul_le_one.name: Rd.norm_besselInvMul_le_one
Rd.norm_besselInvMul_le_one.docstring:
Multiplication by `⟨ξ⟩⁻¹` has operator norm at most `1` on `L_2(V)`, since `|⟨ξ⟩⁻¹| ≤ 1`
(Mathlib's `Lp.norm_le_norm_of_ae_le`).

Rd.nikolskiiBlockConst_ne_top.name: Rd.nikolskiiBlockConst_ne_top
Rd.nikolskiiBlockConst_ne_top.docstring: The Nikolskii constant `N_p` is finite for `p ≥ 1`.

Rd.nikolskiiBlockConst.name: Rd.nikolskiiBlockConst
Rd.nikolskiiBlockConst.docstring:
The **Nikolskii constant** `N_p = ‖Θ‖_1^(1-1/p) (sup |Θ|)^(1/p)` of the blocks, built from the
band-limiting kernel `Θ`.

Rd.neg_one_pow_mul_sum_higherDiff_coeff.name: Rd.neg_one_pow_mul_sum_higherDiff_coeff
Rd.neg_one_pow_mul_sum_higherDiff_coeff.docstring:
**The coefficients of the moment kernels** are those of `(-1)^r Δ^r` without its term
`l = 0`: `(-1)^r ∑_{l ≤ r} (-1)^(r-l) C(r, l) F(l) = F(0) - ∑_{l<r} a_l F(l + 1)`.

Rd.multiplierTotal_ne_top.name: Rd.multiplierTotal_ne_top
Rd.multiplierTotal_ne_top.docstring: The constant of `Rd.modNorm_mulLp_le` is finite for `s < r`.

Rd.multiplierTotal.name: Rd.multiplierTotal
Rd.multiplierTotal.docstring:
The **constant of the multiplier bound** `K = C + ∑_{l ≤ r} C(r, l) C K_l` for a bound `C` of
the derivatives up to order `r`, with the constants `K_l` of `Rd.multiplierConst`.

Rd.multiplierConst_ne_top.name: Rd.multiplierConst_ne_top
Rd.multiplierConst_ne_top.docstring: The constants of the multiplier bound are finite for `s < r`.

Rd.multiplierConst.name: Rd.multiplierConst
Rd.multiplierConst.docstring: The constant of the multiplier bound at the order `l`.

Rd.mul_setLIntegral_closedBall_le.name: Rd.mul_setLIntegral_closedBall_le
Rd.mul_setLIntegral_closedBall_le.docstring:
**One ball of the Vitali cover.** If `t |B(0,r)| ≤ ∫_{B(b,r)} g`, then
`t ∫_{B̄(b,4r)} w ≤ 5^n ∫_{B(b,r)} g M w`: the mass of `w` on the enlarged ball is spread over
`B(b,r)` with the weight `g`, at the price of `M w`.

Rd.mul_setLIntegral_bigBallSet_le.name: Rd.mul_setLIntegral_bigBallSet_le
Rd.mul_setLIntegral_bigBallSet_le.docstring:
**Vitali step.** `t ∫_{E_R} w ≤ 5^n ∫ g M w` for the set `E_R = bigBallSet g t R`: Vitali's
covering lemma selects countably many disjoint balls `B(b, r_b)` from the balls that define
`E_R` such that the balls `B̄(b, 4 r_b)` cover `E_R`, and each of them is estimated by
`Rd.mul_setLIntegral_closedBall_le`.

Rd.mul_ae_eq_of_tsupport_subset.name: Rd.mul_ae_eq_of_tsupport_subset
Rd.mul_ae_eq_of_tsupport_subset.docstring:
**Cutoffs see only the values on a set**: if `χ` has closed support in `B`, `s ∩ B ⊆ t` and
`f = f'` almost everywhere on `t`, then `χ f = χ f'` almost everywhere on `s`.

Rd.mulLp_sub.name: Rd.mulLp_sub
Rd.mulLp_sub.docstring: Multiplication by `ψ` is additive: `ψ (F - G) = ψ F - ψ G` in `L_p`.

Rd.mulLp_smul.name: Rd.mulLp_smul
Rd.mulLp_smul.docstring: Multiplication by `ψ` commutes with complex scalars: `ψ (c F) = c (ψ F)` in `L_p`.

Rd.mulLp_apply_ae.name: Rd.mulLp_apply_ae
Rd.mulLp_apply_ae.docstring: The product in `L_p` is `ψ F` almost everywhere.

Rd.mulLp_add.name: Rd.mulLp_add
Rd.mulLp_add.docstring: Multiplication by `ψ` is additive: `ψ (F + G) = ψ F + ψ G` in `L_p`.

Rd.mulLpL.name: Rd.mulLpL
Rd.mulLpL.docstring:
**Multiplication by a bounded continuous function** `ψ`, `‖ψ‖ ≤ C`, as a bounded linear
operator on `L_p` of norm at most `max C 0` (`Rd.mulLp`, `Rd.enorm_mulLp_le`). It is Mathlib's
`ContinuousLinearMap.holderL` with `q = ∞` and `B = ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℂ ℂ`, applied to the
`L_∞` class of `ψ`, packaged so that `Rd.mulLpL_apply` is `rfl` on the project's `Rd.mulLp`.

Rd.mulLp.name: Rd.mulLp
Rd.mulLp.docstring: The product `ψ F` of a bounded continuous function and an element of `L_p`.

Rd.momentKernel.name: Rd.momentKernel
Rd.momentKernel.docstring: The **moment kernel** of order `L`, `m = ∑_{l=1}^L (-1)^(l+1) C(L, l) g_{1/l}`.

Rd.modulusOn_univ.name: Rd.modulusOn_univ
Rd.modulusOn_univ.docstring: The modulus on `V` is the modulus.

Rd.modulusOn_mono_set.name: Rd.modulusOn_mono_set
Rd.modulusOn_mono_set.docstring: **The modulus on a set grows with the set**: `ω_r(f, t, U)_p ≤ ω_r(f, t, O)_p` for `U ⊆ O`.

Rd.modulusOn_levelSum_le.name: Rd.modulusOn_levelSum_le
Rd.modulusOn_levelSum_le.docstring:
**Moduli of the level sums on `Ω`**: `ω_r(∑_m λ_m a_m, 2^(-k), Ω)_p ≤
2^r N^(1-1/p) C 2^(-jn/p) ‖λ‖_{ℓ_p} c_{kj}` with `c_{kj} = 2^(-(k-j)σ)` for `j ≤ k` and `1`
otherwise, for regular atoms on `Ω`.

Rd.modulusOn_le_smoothnessModulus.name: Rd.modulusOn_le_smoothnessModulus
Rd.modulusOn_le_smoothnessModulus.docstring: **The modulus on `U` is at most the modulus on `V`**, `ω_r(f, t, U)_p ≤ ω_r(f, t)_p`.

Rd.modulusOn_indicator.name: Rd.modulusOn_indicator
Rd.modulusOn_indicator.docstring: **The modulus on `U` uses only the values on `U`**: `ω_r(1_U f, t, U)_p = ω_r(f, t, U)_p`.

Rd.modulusOn_const_smul.name: Rd.modulusOn_const_smul
Rd.modulusOn_const_smul.docstring: `ω_r(c f, t, U)_p = |c| ω_r(f, t, U)_p`.

Rd.modulusOn_congr_set.name: Rd.modulusOn_congr_set
Rd.modulusOn_congr_set.docstring:
**The modulus on a set does not see null sets**: `ω_r(f, t, U)_p = ω_r(f, t, U')_p` if `U`
and `U'` agree up to a null set.

Rd.modulusOn_congr_ae.name: Rd.modulusOn_congr_ae
Rd.modulusOn_congr_ae.docstring:
**The modulus on `U` depends only on the class of `f` on `U`**: if `1_U f = 1_U g` almost
everywhere, then `ω_r(f, t, U)_p = ω_r(g, t, U)_p`.

Rd.modulusOn.name: Rd.modulusOn
Rd.modulusOn.docstring:
The **modulus of smoothness on `U`**, `ω_r(f, t, U)_p = sup_{‖h‖ ≤ t} ‖Δ_h^r(f, ·, U)‖_p`,
with the restricted difference `Δ_h^r(f, ·, U) = 1_{U_{rh}} Δ_h^r f`.

Rd.modNorm_two_le_norm.name: Rd.modNorm_two_le_norm
Rd.modNorm_two_le_norm.docstring:
**`H^1(V) ⊆ B^1_{2,2}(V)` with an explicit constant**: for every `U ∈ H^1(V)` with `L_2`
function `ι U`, `‖ι U‖_2 + ‖(2^k ω_2(ι U, 2^(-k))_2)_k‖_{ℓ_2} ≤ C ‖U‖` with
`C = Rd.sobolevOneBesovConst V`: the moduli are bounded by the band-limited approximation norm
(`ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.modNorm_le_approxNormDyadic`), which is bounded by the norm of
`F^1_{2,2}` (`Rd.approxNormDyadic_le_triebelLizorkinNorm`), which is at most
`(2 · 4)^{1/2} ‖J_1 ι U‖_2` (`Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_le_of_besselPotential_eq`), and
`‖J_1 ι U‖_2 = ‖U‖` (`BesselPotentialSpace.enorm_toLp_eq`).

Rd.modNorm_toL2_lt_top.name: Rd.modNorm_toL2_lt_top
Rd.modNorm_toL2_lt_top.docstring:
**The hypothesis of the trace theorems for `H^1(V)`**: for every `U ∈ H^1(V)`,
`‖ι U‖_2 + ‖(2^(k(1/2 + 1/2)) ω_2(ι U, 2^(-k))_2)_k‖_{ℓ_2} < ∞`, the finiteness that the boundary
traces at `s = 1/2`, `p = q = 2` and order `L = 2` ask for (`Rd.modNorm_two_le_norm`).

Rd.modNorm_sobolevToL2_lt_top.name: Rd.modNorm_sobolevToL2_lt_top
Rd.modNorm_sobolevToL2_lt_top.docstring:
**The hypothesis of the trace theorems for `H^s(V)`, `1/2 < s < 2`**: for every
`U ∈ H^s(V)`, `‖ι_s U‖_2 + ‖(2^{k((s - 1/2) + 1/2)} ω_2(ι_s U, 2^{-k})_2)_k‖_{ℓ_2} < ∞`, the
finiteness that the boundary traces at smoothness `s - 1/2`, `p = q = 2` and order `L = 2` ask
for (`Rd.modNorm_sobolevToL2_le`). The finiteness holds for `0 < s < 2`; `s > 1/2` is the range of
the trace theorems. At `s = 1` this is `Rd.modNorm_toL2_lt_top`.

Rd.modNorm_sobolevToL2_le.name: Rd.modNorm_sobolevToL2_le
Rd.modNorm_sobolevToL2_le.docstring:
**`H^s(V) ⊆ B^s_{2,2}(V)` with an explicit constant**: for `0 < s < r` and every
`U ∈ H^s(V)` with `L_2` function `ι_s U`,
`‖ι_s U‖_2 + ‖(2^{ks} ω_r(ι_s U, 2^{-k})_2)_k‖_{ℓ_2} ≤ C ‖U‖` with
`C = Rd.sobolevBesovConst V s r`: the moduli are bounded by the band-limited approximation norm
(`ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.modNorm_le_approxNormDyadic`), which is bounded by the norm of
`F^s_{2,2}` (`Rd.approxNormDyadic_le_triebelLizorkinNorm`), which is at most
`(2 · 4^s)^{1/2} ‖J_s ι_s U‖_2` (`Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_le_of_besselPotential_eq`), and
`J_s ι_s U` is the `L_2` function of `U` (`Rd.besselPotential_sobolevToL2`).

Rd.modNorm_order_le_of_le.name: Rd.modNorm_order_le_of_le
Rd.modNorm_order_le_of_le.docstring:
The norm with moduli of order `L ≥ r` is at most `2^(L-r)` times that with order `r`
(`Rd.lpModulus_add_order_le`).

Rd.modNorm_one_tsum_le.name: Rd.modNorm_one_tsum_le
Rd.modNorm_one_tsum_le.docstring:
**The norm with moduli is countably subadditive in `ℓ_1`**: for a summable series in `L_p`
and `N(G) = ‖G‖ + ‖(2^(kσ) ω_L(G, 2^(-k)))_k‖_{ℓ_1}`, `N(∑ G_i) ≤ ∑_i N(G_i)`, by
`ENNReal.le_tsum_of_tendsto_sum` for the modulus at each scale.

Rd.modNorm_mulLp_lt_top.name: Rd.modNorm_mulLp_lt_top
Rd.modNorm_mulLp_lt_top.docstring:
**Multipliers keep the Besov spaces by differences**: if `ψ` is smooth with bounded
derivatives up to order `r`, `s < r` and `F` has a finite `(s, r)`-quasi-norm, so has `ψ F`.

Rd.modNorm_mulLp_le.name: Rd.modNorm_mulLp_le
Rd.modNorm_mulLp_le.docstring:
**Pointwise multipliers**: for a smooth `ψ` with `‖D^l ψ‖ ≤ C` for `l ≤ r`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`,
`s < r` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`,
`‖ψ F‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(ψ F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ K (‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})`
with `K = C + ∑_{l ≤ r} C(r, l) C K_l` (`Rd.multiplierTotal`, `Rd.multiplierConst`).

Rd.modNorm_level_le.name: Rd.modNorm_level_le
Rd.modNorm_level_le.docstring:
**Synthesis of one level**: for regular atoms of level `j` with overlap `N` and
`F = ∑_m λ_m a_m` in `L_p`, `0 < s < σ`:
`‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ K 2^(j(s - n/p)) ‖λ‖_{ℓ_p}`, the case of
`Rd.modNorm_le_coeffNorm` with one nonzero level.

Rd.modNorm_le_modNorm_of_lt.name: Rd.modNorm_le_modNorm_of_lt
Rd.modNorm_le_modNorm_of_lt.docstring:
**The order of the differences does not matter**: for `0 ≤ s < r'` and every order `r`,
`‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_{r'}(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C (‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})`,
through the band-limited approximation norm: the inverse direction of
`Rd.bandModulusData hp r'` and Jackson's direction of `Rd.bandModulusData hp r`.

Rd.modNorm_le_coeffNorm.name: Rd.modNorm_le_coeffNorm
Rd.modNorm_le_coeffNorm.docstring:
**Atomic synthesis** (Schneider–Vybíral, Theorem 2.6 and Corollary 2.8, direction ⇐): if the
centres of the atoms with nonzero coefficients have overlap at most `N` on balls of radius
`(d + r) 2^(-j)` at every level `j`,
`F = ∑_j f_j` in `L_p` with the level sums `f_j = ∑_m λ_{j,m} a_{j,m}` of regular atoms of
exponent `σ` and order `r`, and `0 < s < σ`, then
`‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ K ‖λ‖_{b^s_{p,q}}`, the case `Ω = V` of
`Rd.modNormOn_le_coeffNorm`.

Rd.modNorm_half_one_le_of_lt.name: Rd.modNorm_half_one_le_of_lt
Rd.modNorm_half_one_le_of_lt.docstring:
**`B^s_{p,2} ⊆ B^{1/2}_{p,1}` for `s > 1/2`, with the constant of the geometric sequence**:
for `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, every order `r` and every `F ∈ L_p(V)`,
`‖F‖_p + ∑_k 2^{k/2} ω_r(F, 2^{-k})_p ≤ c (‖F‖_p + ‖(2^{ks} ω_r(F, 2^{-k})_p)_k‖_{ℓ_2})` with
`c = ‖(2^{-k(s-1/2)})_k‖_{ℓ_2} = ENNReal.dyadicGeomConst (s - 1/2) 2`, by the Cauchy–Schwarz
inequality `∑_k 2^{-k(s-1/2)} (2^{ks} ω_k) ≤ ‖(2^{-k(s-1/2)})_k‖_{ℓ_2} ‖(2^{ks} ω_k)_k‖_{ℓ_2}`
(`ENNReal.lqNorm_one_mul_le`) and `c ≥ 1`. At `s = 1`, `r = 2`, `p = 2` this is
`Rd.modNorm_half_one_le` with `c = √2`.

Rd.modNorm_half_one_le_norm_of_lt.name: Rd.modNorm_half_one_le_norm_of_lt
Rd.modNorm_half_one_le_norm_of_lt.docstring:
**`H^s(V) ⊆ B^{1/2}_{2,1}(V)` with an explicit constant**, `1/2 < s < 2`: for every
`U ∈ H^s(V)` with `L_2` function `ι_s U` (`Rd.sobolevToL2`),
`‖ι_s U‖_2 + ∑_k 2^(k/2) ω_2(ι_s U, 2^(-k))_2 ≤ c C ‖U‖` with
`c = ‖(2^{-k(s-1/2)})_k‖_{ℓ_2}` (`Rd.modNorm_half_one_le_of_lt`) and
`C = Rd.sobolevBesovConst V s 2` (`Rd.modNorm_sobolevToL2_le`, differences of order `2 > s`). The
left side bounds the traces on Lipschitz graph domains (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.enorm_graphTrace_le`). At
`s = 1` the corresponding bound with `√2 Rd.sobolevOneBesovConst V` is
`Rd.modNorm_half_one_le_norm`.

Rd.modNorm_half_one_le_norm.name: Rd.modNorm_half_one_le_norm
Rd.modNorm_half_one_le_norm.docstring:
**`H^1(V) ⊆ B^{1/2}_{2,1}(V)` with an explicit constant**: for every `U ∈ H^1(V)` with `L_2`
function `ι U`, `‖ι U‖_2 + ∑_k 2^(k/2) ω_2(ι U, 2^(-k))_2 ≤ √2 C ‖U‖` with
`C = Rd.sobolevOneBesovConst V` (`Rd.modNorm_half_one_le`, `Rd.modNorm_two_le_norm`). The left
side bounds the traces on Lipschitz graph domains (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.enorm_graphTrace_le`).

Rd.modNorm_half_one_le.name: Rd.modNorm_half_one_le
Rd.modNorm_half_one_le.docstring:
**`B^1_{2,2}(V) ⊆ B^{1/2}_{2,1}(V)` with constant `√2`**: for every `F ∈ L_2(V)`,
`‖F‖_2 + ∑_k 2^(k/2) ω_2(F, 2^(-k))_2 ≤ √2 (‖F‖_2 + ‖(2^k ω_2(F, 2^(-k))_2)_k‖_{ℓ_2})`, by the
Cauchy–Schwarz inequality `∑_k 2^(-k/2) (2^k ω_k) ≤ ‖(2^(-k/2))_k‖_{ℓ_2} ‖(2^k ω_k)_k‖_{ℓ_2}`. The
left side is the norm in which the trace on a Lipschitz graph domain is bounded
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.enorm_graphTrace_le`).

Rd.modNorm_finsetSum_lt_top.name: Rd.modNorm_finsetSum_lt_top
Rd.modNorm_finsetSum_lt_top.docstring: **Finite sums keep the Besov spaces by differences** (`Rd.modNorm_finsetSum_le`).

Rd.modNorm_finsetSum_le.name: Rd.modNorm_finsetSum_le
Rd.modNorm_finsetSum_le.docstring:
**The Besov quasi-norm by differences of a finite sum** is at most the sum of the quasi-norms:
`‖∑_i G_i‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(∑_i G_i, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤
∑_i (‖G_i‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(G_i, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})` for `q ≥ 1`
(`Rd.lpModulus_finsetSum_le`, `ENNReal.lqNorm_sum_le`).

Rd.modNorm_const_smul.name: Rd.modNorm_const_smul
Rd.modNorm_const_smul.docstring:
**The Besov quasi-norm by differences is homogeneous**:
`‖c G‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(c G, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} =
|c| (‖G‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(G, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})`
(`Rd.lpModulus_const_smul`, `ENNReal.lqNorm_const_mul`).

Rd.modNorm_add_le.name: Rd.modNorm_add_le
Rd.modNorm_add_le.docstring:
**The Besov quasi-norm by differences is subadditive**:
`‖G + H‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(G + H, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤
(‖G‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(G, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q}) + (‖H‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(H, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})`
for `q ≥ 1` (`Rd.lpModulus_add_le`, `ENNReal.lqNorm_add_le`).

Rd.modNormOn_univ.name: Rd.modNormOn_univ
Rd.modNormOn_univ.docstring:
On `U = V` the intrinsic quasi-norm is the quasi-norm of `V`:
`N_V(f) = ‖f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q}` (`Rd.modulusOn_univ`).

Rd.modNormOn_mono_of_subset.name: Rd.modNormOn_mono_of_subset
Rd.modNormOn_mono_of_subset.docstring:
**The intrinsic quasi-norm grows with the set**: for measurable `T ⊆ U`,
`N_T(f) ≤ N_U(f)`, where `N_U(f) = ‖1_U f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k), U)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q}`
(`Rd.lpModulusOn_mono_set`).

Rd.modNormOn_le_modNorm_of_indicatorLp.name: Rd.modNormOn_le_modNorm_of_indicatorLp
Rd.modNormOn_le_modNorm_of_indicatorLp.docstring:
**Restrictions have finite intrinsic moduli**: if `1_O F = 1_O f` for a measurable `O`, the
intrinsic quasi-norm of `f` on `O` is at most the quasi-norm of `F` on `V`.

Rd.modNormOn_le_coeffNorm.name: Rd.modNormOn_le_coeffNorm
Rd.modNormOn_le_coeffNorm.docstring:
**Atomic synthesis on `Ω`**: if the centres of the atoms with nonzero coefficients have overlap
at most `N` on balls of radius `(d + r) 2^(-j)` at every level `j`, `F = ∑_j f_j` in `L_p` with the
level sums `f_j = ∑_m λ_{j,m} a_{j,m}` of regular atoms on `Ω` of exponent `σ` and order `r`, and
`0 < s < σ`, then
`‖F‖_{L_p(Ω)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(F, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ K ‖λ‖_{b^s_{p,q}}`.

Rd.modNormOn_finsetSum_le.name: Rd.modNormOn_finsetSum_le
Rd.modNormOn_finsetSum_le.docstring: **The intrinsic quasi-norm of a finite sum** is at most the sum of the quasi-norms.

Rd.modNormOn_const_smul.name: Rd.modNormOn_const_smul
Rd.modNormOn_const_smul.docstring: **The intrinsic quasi-norm is homogeneous**: `N_Ω(c G) = |c| N_Ω(G)`.

Rd.modNormOn_congr_set.name: Rd.modNormOn_congr_set
Rd.modNormOn_congr_set.docstring:
**Sets that agree up to a null set have the same intrinsic quasi-norm**: `N_U(G) = N_{U'}(G)`
if `U` and `U'` agree up to a null set (`Rd.indicatorLp_congr_set`, `Rd.lpModulusOn_congr_set`).

Rd.modNormOn_congr.name: Rd.modNormOn_congr
Rd.modNormOn_congr.docstring: **The intrinsic quasi-norm sees only `1_Ω G`**: equal cut-offs give equal quasi-norms.

Rd.modNormOn.name: Rd.modNormOn
Rd.modNormOn.docstring:
The **intrinsic Besov quasi-norm** on a measurable set `Ω`:
`N_Ω(G) = ‖1_Ω G‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(G, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q}`.

Rd.mixedSupp.name: Rd.mixedSupp
Rd.mixedSupp.docstring: The coordinates `e(k) = {i : k_i ≠ 0}` in which the index `k ∈ ℕ^d` takes differences.

Rd.mixedModulus_congr_ae.name: Rd.mixedModulus_congr_ae
Rd.mixedModulus_congr_ae.docstring: **The mixed modulus depends only on the class modulo null sets.**

Rd.mixedModulus.name: Rd.mixedModulus
Rd.mixedModulus.docstring:
The **mixed modulus of smoothness** `Ω^e_L(f, t)_p = sup ‖Δ^{L,e}_h f‖_p` over the steps with
`|h_i| ≤ t_i` for `i ∈ e`.

Rd.mixedModNorm.name: Rd.mixedModNorm
Rd.mixedModNorm.docstring:
The **Besov quasi-norm of dominating mixed smoothness by differences**,
`‖(2^(s|k|_1) Ω^{e(k)}_L(f, 2^(-k))_p)_{k ∈ ℕ^d}‖_{ℓ_q(ℕ^d)}`.

Rd.mixedLPNorm.name: Rd.mixedLPNorm
Rd.mixedLPNorm.docstring:
**Vybíral's quasi-norm** of the Besov spaces of dominating mixed smoothness,
`‖(2^(s|k|_1) ‖δ_k ⋆ f‖_p)_{k ∈ ℕ^d}‖_{ℓ_q(ℕ^d)}`.

Rd.mixedDiff_tensorKernel.name: Rd.mixedDiff_tensorKernel
Rd.mixedDiff_tensorKernel.docstring:
**Mixed differences of tensor products** act on the factors of the coordinates in `e`:
`Δ^{L,e}_h (⊗K) = ⊗K'` with `K'_i = Δ^L_{h_i} K_i` for `i ∈ e` and `K'_i = K_i` otherwise.

Rd.mixedDiff_insert.name: Rd.mixedDiff_insert
Rd.mixedDiff_insert.docstring: **Adding a coordinate**: `Δ^{L, e ∪ {i}}_h = Δ^L_{h_i e_i} Δ^{L,e}_h` for `i ∉ e`.

Rd.mixedDiff_empty.name: Rd.mixedDiff_empty
Rd.mixedDiff_empty.docstring: The mixed difference in no coordinate is the function itself.

Rd.mixedDiff_conv_ae.name: Rd.mixedDiff_conv_ae
Rd.mixedDiff_conv_ae.docstring:
**Mixed differences of convolutions** fall on the kernel:
`Δ^{L,e}_h (K ⋆ f) = (Δ^{L,e}_h K) ⋆ f` almost everywhere, for integrable `K` and `f ∈ L_p`.

Rd.mixedDiff_congr_ae.name: Rd.mixedDiff_congr_ae
Rd.mixedDiff_congr_ae.docstring: **Mixed differences depend only on the class modulo null sets.**

Rd.mixedDiff.name: Rd.mixedDiff
Rd.mixedDiff.docstring:
The **mixed difference** `Δ^{L,e}_h f = (∏_{i ∈ e} Δ^L_{h_i e_i}) f`, the action of
`∏_{i ∈ e} (δ_{h_i e_i} - 1)^L` in the algebra of translations.

Rd.mixedBlock.name: Rd.mixedBlock
Rd.mixedBlock.docstring: The **tensor Littlewood–Paley blocks** `f ↦ δ_k ⋆ f` on `L_p(ℝ^d)`.

Rd.min_one_rpow_mul_le.name: Rd.min_one_rpow_mul_le
Rd.min_one_rpow_mul_le.docstring: `min(1, s^a) min(1, s^b) ≤ min(1, s^(a+b))` for `a, b ≥ 0`.

Rd.min_one_mul_le.name: Rd.min_one_mul_le
Rd.min_one_mul_le.docstring: `min(1, K t) ≤ K min(1, t)` for `K ≥ 1`.

Rd.mem_zcell_zcellIndex.name: Rd.mem_zcell_zcellIndex
Rd.mem_zcell_zcellIndex.docstring: Every point lies in the cube of its index.

Rd.mem_vanishOn_one_iff_restrict_eq_zero.name: Rd.mem_vanishOn_one_iff_restrict_eq_zero
Rd.mem_vanishOn_one_iff_restrict_eq_zero.docstring:
For `s = 1`, `U` vanishes on `Ω` iff the restriction to `L_2(Ω)` of the `L_2` function of
`U` is zero.

Rd.mem_vanishOn_one_iff.name: Rd.mem_vanishOn_one_iff

Rd.mem_vanishOn_iff_sobolevToL2.name: Rd.mem_vanishOn_iff_sobolevToL2
Rd.mem_vanishOn_iff_sobolevToL2.docstring:
**Vanishing on `Ω` for `s ≥ 0`**: `U ∈ H^s(V)` vanishes on the open set `Ω` iff its `L_2`
function `ι_s U` (`Rd.sobolevToL2`) vanishes almost everywhere on `Ω`. `⇐`: the integrand
`φ · ι_s U` vanishes almost everywhere; `⇒`: a locally integrable function on `Ω` with vanishing
integrals against all smooth compactly supported real functions in `Ω` vanishes almost everywhere
on `Ω` (Mathlib's `IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero`).

Rd.mem_vanishOn_iff.name: Rd.mem_vanishOn_iff
Rd.mem_vanishOn_iff.docstring: `U` vanishes on `Ω` iff `U(φ) = 0` for every real test function `φ` of `Ω`.

Rd.mem_tildeSpace_of_isCompact_of_nonneg.name: Rd.mem_tildeSpace_of_isCompact_of_nonneg
Rd.mem_tildeSpace_of_isCompact_of_nonneg.docstring:
**Functions with compact support in `Ω` lie in `H̃^s(Ω)`, `s ≥ 0`**: for an open set `Ω`,
every `U ∈ H^s(V)` with `ι_s U = 0` almost everywhere outside a compact subset `S` of `Ω` lies in
`H̃^s(Ω)`. Some thickening `S_δ` lies in `Ω` (Mathlib's `IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open`),
and for the mollifier of the standard bump `Rd.stdBumpBase`, supported in `B̄(0, 1)`, eventually
`supp η_{2^n} + S ⊆ S_δ` (`Rd.eventually_tsupport_dilate_add_subset_thickening`,
`Rd.mem_tildeSpace_of_dilate_of_nonneg`). At `s = 1` this is `Rd.mem_tildeSpace_of_isCompact`.

Rd.mem_tildeSpace_of_dilate_of_nonneg.name: Rd.mem_tildeSpace_of_dilate_of_nonneg
Rd.mem_tildeSpace_of_dilate_of_nonneg.docstring:
**Mollified functions in `H̃^s(Ω)`, `s ≥ 0`**: let `Ω` be open, `U ∈ H^s(V)` with `ι_s U = 0`
almost everywhere outside a compact set `S`, and `η` a smooth function with compact support and
`∫ η = 1`. If `supp η_{2^n} + S ⊆ Ω` for all large `n`, then `U ∈ H̃^s(Ω)`: `η_{2^n} ⋆ U` has the
`L_2` function `η_{2^n} ⋆ ι_s U` (`Rd.sobolevToL2_sobolevConv`), a Schwartz function with compact
support in `supp η_{2^n} + S` (`Rd.exists_schwartz_eq_conv`), hence, for large `n`, in the span
of the test functions of `Ω` (`Rd.ofSchwartz_mem_testSpan`), and `η_{2^n} ⋆ U → U` in `H^s(V)`
(`Rd.tendsto_sobolevConv_dilate`). At `s = 1` this is `Rd.mem_tildeSpace_of_dilate`.

Rd.mem_orthogonal_tildeSpace_iff_toLp.name: Rd.mem_orthogonal_tildeSpace_iff_toLp
Rd.mem_orthogonal_tildeSpace_iff_toLp.docstring:
**The orthogonal complement of `H̃^t(Ω)`**: `U ∈ H^t(V)` is orthogonal to `H̃^t(Ω)` iff the
distribution `J_t (J_t U)` vanishes on every test function of `Ω`. The orthogonal complement of a
closure is that of the set (Mathlib's `Submodule.orthogonal_closure`), orthogonality to a span is
orthogonality to its generators, and `⟪φ, U⟫ = (J_t (J_t U))(φ)` (`Rd.inner_ofTest_left`).

Rd.mem_openHalfSpace.name: Rd.mem_openHalfSpace
Rd.mem_openHalfSpace.docstring: Membership in the open half-space: `y ∈ H₊` iff `0 < ⟪y, e⟫`.

Rd.mem_interior_closedHalfSpace.name: Rd.mem_interior_closedHalfSpace
Rd.mem_interior_closedHalfSpace.docstring: A nonzero `e` lies in the interior of its closed half-space.

Rd.mem_hyperbolicCross.name: Rd.mem_hyperbolicCross
Rd.mem_hyperbolicCross.docstring: `k` lies in the hyperbolic cross of level `N` iff `|k|_1 ≤ N`.

Rd.mem_gridLevelSet.name: Rd.mem_gridLevelSet
Rd.mem_gridLevelSet.docstring: `k` lies in the level set of `n` iff `|k|_1 = n`.

Rd.mem_dyadicCell_cellIndex.name: Rd.mem_dyadicCell_cellIndex
Rd.mem_dyadicCell_cellIndex.docstring: Every point lies in the cell of its index.

Rd.mem_diffStepSet_neg.name: Rd.mem_diffStepSet_neg
Rd.mem_diffStepSet_neg.docstring: **Negative steps**: `x ∈ U_{r(-h)}` iff `x - r h ∈ U_{rh}`, by `l ↦ r - l`.

Rd.mem_cubeAt.name: Rd.mem_cubeAt
Rd.mem_cubeAt.docstring: Every point lies in its cube.

Rd.mem_bandScheme_two_pow.name: Rd.mem_bandScheme_two_pow
Rd.mem_bandScheme_two_pow.docstring: The level `2^k` of the band-limited scheme is `E_k`.

Rd.mem_annulus_of_mem_tsupport.name: Rd.mem_annulus_of_mem_tsupport
Rd.mem_annulus_of_mem_tsupport.docstring:
If a function vanishes outside the closed annulus `{a ≤ ‖ζ‖ ≤ b}`, the closure of its support
lies in that annulus.

Rd.mem_annulus_of_fourier_lpBlockKernelO.name: Rd.mem_annulus_of_fourier_lpBlockKernelOneS_ne_zero
Rd.mem_annulus_of_fourier_lpBlockKernelO.docstring:
`𝓕ψ_1` vanishes outside the annulus `{1 ≤ ‖ζ‖ ≤ 2^2 · 1}`. The bound is written as `2^2 · 1`
to match the hypothesis of `Rd.exists_isCZFamily_besselKernelFamily` with `a = 1`, `N = 2`.

Rd.mem_annulus_of_fourier_lpBlockKernelB.name: Rd.mem_annulus_of_fourier_lpBlockKernelBase_ne_zero
Rd.mem_annulus_of_fourier_lpBlockKernelB.docstring:
`𝓕(lpBlockKernelBase (j+1)) = 𝓕(Φ - δ_{1/2} Φ)` vanishes outside the annulus
`{1/2 ≤ ‖ζ‖ ≤ 2^2 · 1/2}`: `lpBlockKernelBase (j+1) = lpBlockKernelBase 1` and
`ψ_1 = (lpBlockKernelBase 1)_2`, so `𝓕(lpBlockKernelBase 1)(ζ) = 𝓕ψ_1(2ζ)`
(`Rd.fourier_eq_fourier_dilate`) and `1 ≤ ‖2ζ‖ ≤ 4`. The bound is written as `2^2 · 2⁻¹` to match
the hypothesis of `Rd.exists_isCZFamily_besselKernelFamily` with `a = 1/2`, `N = 2`.

Rd.mem_annulus_of_fourier_dualLpBlockKer.name: Rd.mem_annulus_of_fourier_dualLpBlockKernelBase_ne_zero
Rd.mem_annulus_of_fourier_dualLpBlockKer.docstring:
`𝓕(dualLpBlockKernelBase (j+2)) = 𝓕(δ_2 Φ - δ_{1/4} Φ)` vanishes outside the annulus
`{1/4 ≤ ‖ζ‖ ≤ 2^4 · 1/4}`: `dualLpBlockKernelBase (j+2) = dualLpBlockKernelBase 2` and the
synthesis kernel `ψ̃_2 = Rd.dualLpBlockKernel 2` is `(dualLpBlockKernelBase 2)_4`, whose Fourier
transform vanishes outside `{1 < ‖ξ‖ < 16}`. The bound is written as `2^4 · 4⁻¹` to match the
hypothesis of `Rd.exists_isCZFamily_besselKernelFamily` with `a = 1/4`, `N = 4`.

Rd.mem_annulus_of_fourier_dilate_besselK.name: Rd.mem_annulus_of_fourier_dilate_besselKernelFamily_ne_zero
Rd.mem_annulus_of_fourier_dilate_besselK.docstring:
Where `𝓕(K_j)_{2^j}(ξ) ≠ 0`, the frequency `2^{-j} ξ` lies in the annulus
`{a ≤ ‖ζ‖ ≤ b}` outside which `ω̂` vanishes.

Rd.mem_Icc_of_fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_.name: Rd.mem_Icc_of_fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_ne_zero
Rd.mem_Icc_of_fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_.docstring:
**At most four synthesis kernels see a frequency**: with `a` the least index such that
`‖ξ‖ < 2^(a+1)`, `𝓕ψ̃_j(ξ) ≠ 0` forces `a - 1 ≤ j ≤ a + 2`.

Rd.memTriebelLizorkin_zero_two.name: Rd.memTriebelLizorkin_zero_two
Rd.memTriebelLizorkin_zero_two.docstring:
**`L_p ⊆ F^0_{p,2}`**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 < p < ∞`, every `f ∈ L_p(V)` has a
finite Triebel–Lizorkin norm `‖f‖_{F^0_{p,2}}`.

Rd.memTriebelLizorkin_of_memSobolevW.name: Rd.memTriebelLizorkin_of_memSobolevW
Rd.memTriebelLizorkin_of_memSobolevW.docstring:
**`W^m_p ⊆ F^m_{p,2}`**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 < p < ∞`, every `f ∈ W^m_p(V)` lies in
`F^m_{p,2}(V)`; the weak derivatives of order `m` along the basis vectors suffice
(`Rd.memTriebelLizorkin_of_hasWeakLineDeriv`).

Rd.memTriebelLizorkin_of_hasWeakLineDeri.name: Rd.memTriebelLizorkin_of_hasWeakLineDeriv
Rd.memTriebelLizorkin_of_hasWeakLineDeri.docstring:
**The weak derivatives of order `m` along the basis vectors give `f ∈ F^m_{p,2}`**: in
dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 < p < ∞`, if the weak derivatives `g_α = ∂^α f` of order `m` along the
basis `e` of `Rd.gridBasis` lie in `L_p(V)` for every multi-index `α`, then `f ∈ F^m_{p,2}(V)`,
since the bound `Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_le_of_hasWeakLineDeriv` is finite.

Rd.memSobolev_two_of_lintegral_lt_top.name: Rd.memSobolev_two_of_lintegral_lt_top
Rd.memSobolev_two_of_lintegral_lt_top.docstring:
**A sufficient condition for `H^s`**: if `f ∈ L_2(V)` has
`∫ ⟨ξ⟩^{2s} |𝓕f(ξ)|² dξ < ∞`, then `f ∈ H^s(V)`.

Rd.memSobolev_one_two_of_lineDerivOp_eq.name: Rd.memSobolev_one_two_of_lineDerivOp_eq
Rd.memSobolev_one_two_of_lineDerivOp_eq.docstring:
**A gradient in `L_2` gives `H^1`**: let `(e_i)` be an orthonormal basis of `V`. If
`∂_{e_i} f = g_i` as tempered distributions for every `i`, with `f, g_i ∈ L_2(V)`, then
`f ∈ H^1(V)`, since `(2π)² ∫ ⟨ξ⟩² |𝓕f|² = (2π)² ‖f‖_2² + ∑_i ‖g_i‖_2² < ∞`
(`Rd.lintegral_besselWeight_one_sq_eq`, `Rd.memSobolev_two_of_lintegral_lt_top`).

Rd.memSobolev_fourierMultiplierCLM_of_su.name: Rd.memSobolev_fourierMultiplierCLM_of_subsingleton
Rd.memSobolev_fourierMultiplierCLM_of_su.docstring:
**Fourier multipliers on `H^{s,p}` in dimension `0`**: on a space with one point every
function `m` is constant, `m(D) u = m(0) u`, and `H^{s,p} = H^{t,p}` for all `s`, `t`
(`Rd.besselPotential_of_subsingleton`).

Rd.memSobolev_bessel_weakDerivL2_sobolev.name: Rd.memSobolev_bessel_weakDerivL2_sobolevInclusion
Rd.memSobolev_bessel_weakDerivL2_sobolev.docstring:
**The weak derivatives of `H^s(V)`, `s ≥ 1`, lie in `H^{s-1}(V)`**: for `U ∈ H^s(V)` and every
direction `v`, the weak derivative `∂_v(ι_{1,s} U) ∈ L_2(V)` is, as a tempered distribution, the
derivative `∂_v U` (`Rd.toTemperedDistribution_weakDerivL2`, `Rd.toDistr_sobolevInclusion`), which
lies in `H^{s-1}(V)` (Mathlib's `TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.lineDerivOp`).

Rd.memSobolev_bessel_of_memTriebelLizork.name: Rd.memSobolev_bessel_of_memTriebelLizorkinDistr
Rd.memSobolev_bessel_of_memTriebelLizork.docstring:
**`F^s_{p,2} ⊆ H^{s,p}`**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 < p < ∞` and real `s`, every tempered
distribution `u ∈ F^s_{p,2}` lies in Mathlib's Bessel potential space: `J_s u ∈ L_p(V)`
(`Rd.exists_besselPotential_eq_of_memTriebelLizorkinDistr`).

Rd.memSobolev_bessel_of_memTriebelLizork.name: Rd.memSobolev_bessel_of_memTriebelLizorkin
Rd.memSobolev_bessel_of_memTriebelLizork.docstring:
**`F^s_{p,2} ⊆ H^{s,p}`**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 < p < ∞` and real `s`, every
`f ∈ F^s_{p,2}(V)` lies in Mathlib's Bessel potential space: `J_s f ∈ L_p(V)`
(`Rd.exists_besselPotential_eq_of_memTriebelLizorkin`).

Rd.memSobolev_bessel_iff_memTriebelLizor.name: Rd.memSobolev_bessel_iff_memTriebelLizorkinDistr
Rd.memSobolev_bessel_iff_memTriebelLizor.docstring:
**`H^{s,p} = F^s_{p,2}` for every real `s`**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 < p < ∞`, real `s`
and every tempered distribution `u` on `V`, `u` lies in Mathlib's Bessel potential space
`H^{s,p}(V)` iff it lies in `F^s_{p,2}` of tempered distributions
(`Rd.exists_triebelLizorkinNormDistr_le_of_besselPotential_eq`,
`Rd.memSobolev_bessel_of_memTriebelLizorkinDistr`).

Rd.memSobolev_bessel_iff_exists_sobolevT.name: Rd.memSobolev_bessel_iff_exists_sobolevToL2_eq
Rd.memSobolev_bessel_iff_exists_sobolevT.docstring:
**`L_2` functions in `H^s(V)`**: for `s ≥ 0`, the tempered distribution of `f ∈ L_2(V)` lies in
Mathlib's `H^s(V)` iff `f = ι_s U` for some `U ∈ H^s(V)`. Mathlib's
`TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.toBesselPotentialSpace` bundles the distribution, whose `L_2`
function is `f` (`Rd.sobolevToL2_eq_of_toDistr_eq`); conversely the distribution of `ι_s U` is `U`
(`Rd.toTemperedDistribution_sobolevToL2`).

Rd.memSobolevW_toL2.name: Rd.memSobolevW_toL2
Rd.memSobolevW_toL2.docstring:
**`H^1(V) ⊆ W^1_2(V)`**: the `L_2` function of every `U ∈ H^1(V)` lies in the Sobolev space
`W^1_2(V)` of weak derivatives (`Rd.memSobolevW_one_iff`).

Rd.memSobolevW_one_of_forall_hasWeakLine.name: Rd.memSobolevW_one_of_forall_hasWeakLineDeriv
Rd.memSobolevW_one_of_forall_hasWeakLine.docstring:
**`W^1_p(V)` from first-order weak derivatives**: a function `f ∈ L_p(V)`, `1 ≤ p`, with a
weak derivative `∂_v f ∈ L_p(V)` in every direction `v` lies in `W^1_p(V)`
(`Rd.memSobolevW_iff_exists_hasWeakLineDeriv`; the derivative of order zero is `f` itself).

Rd.memSobolevW_one_of_forall_gridBasis.name: Rd.memSobolevW_one_of_forall_gridBasis
Rd.memSobolevW_one_of_forall_gridBasis.docstring:
**`W^1_p(V)` from the basis derivatives**: a function `F ∈ L_p(V)`, `1 ≤ p`, with weak
derivatives `G_i ∈ L_p(V)` along the basis vectors `e_i` on `V` lies in `W^1_p(V)`; the
derivative along `v` is the class of `∑_i ⟪v, e_i⟫ G_i`
(`Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_forall_gridBasis`, `Rd.memSobolevW_one_of_forall_hasWeakLineDeriv`).

Rd.memSobolevW_one_iff_memApprox.name: Rd.memSobolevW_one_iff_memApprox
Rd.memSobolevW_one_iff_memApprox.docstring:
**`W^1_2 = B^1_{2,2}`**: `F ∈ L_2(V)` lies in the Sobolev space `W^1_2(V)` iff it lies in the
approximation space `A^1_2` of the band-limited functions, the Besov space `B^1_{2,2}(V)`. This
combines `W^1_2 = H^1` (`Rd.memSobolevW_one_iff`) and `H^1 = B^1_{2,2}`
(`Rd.memSobolev_two_iff_exists_memApprox`); an `L_2` function is determined by its tempered
distribution (`Rd.eq_of_toTemperedDistribution_eq`).

Rd.memSobolevW_of_memTriebelLizorkin.name: Rd.memSobolevW_of_memTriebelLizorkin
Rd.memSobolevW_of_memTriebelLizorkin.docstring:
**`F^m_{p,2} ⊆ W^m_p`**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 < p < ∞`, every `f ∈ F^m_{p,2}(V)` lies
in `W^m_p(V)` (`Rd.exists_hasWeakLineDeriv_of_memTriebelLizorkin_of_le`).

Rd.memSobolevW_of_forall_gridBasis_words.name: Rd.memSobolevW_of_forall_gridBasis_words
Rd.memSobolevW_of_forall_gridBasis_words.docstring:
**`W^m_p(V)` from the derivatives along words**: a function `F ∈ L_p(V)`, `1 ≤ p`, with a weak
derivative `G_w ∈ L_p(V)` on `V` along every word `w` of length `k ≤ m` lies in `W^m_p(V)`; the
derivative along `v ∈ V^k` is `∑_w ∏_l ⟪v_l, e_{w_l}⟫ G_w`
(`Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_gridBasis_words`). For `m = 1` this is
`Rd.memSobolevW_one_of_forall_gridBasis`.

Rd.memSobolevW_iff_tempered.name: Rd.memSobolevW_iff_tempered
Rd.memSobolevW_iff_tempered.docstring:
**Sobolev spaces by tempered distributions**: `f ∈ L_p(V)` lies in `W^m_p(V)` iff for every
order `k ≤ m` and all directions `v`, the tempered derivative `∂^v f` is an `L_p(V)` function
(`Rd.memSobolevW_iff_exists_hasWeakLineDeriv` and `Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_top_iff`).

Rd.memSobolevW_iff_exists_hasWeakLineDer.name: Rd.memSobolevW_iff_exists_hasWeakLineDeriv
Rd.memSobolevW_iff_exists_hasWeakLineDer.docstring:
**`W^m_p(V)` with derivatives in `L_p(V)`**: `f ∈ L_p(V)` lies in `W^m_p(V)` iff for every
order `k ≤ m` and all directions `v ∈ V^k` some class `g ∈ L_p(V)` is the weak derivative
`∂^v f` on `V`.

Rd.memLp_top_fourier.name: Rd.memLp_top_fourier
Rd.memLp_top_fourier.docstring:
The Fourier transform of an integrable function lies in `L_∞`: it is continuous
(`Rd.continuous_fourier_of_integrable`) and bounded by `‖K‖_1`.

Rd.memLp_top_besselWeight_neg_one.name: Rd.memLp_top_besselWeight_neg_one
Rd.memLp_top_besselWeight_neg_one.docstring: The Bessel weight `⟨ξ⟩⁻¹` of order `-1` is a bounded function, an element of `L_∞(V)`.

Rd.memLp_sum_conv_blockFun.name: Rd.memLp_sum_conv_blockFun
Rd.memLp_sum_conv_blockFun.docstring:
The **synthesis sums** `∑_{j ∈ t} K_j ⋆ (ψ_j ⋆ f)` of Schwartz kernels `K_j` and the blocks of
`f ∈ L_p(V)` lie in `L_p(V)` for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, by Young's inequality.

Rd.memLp_one_indicator_dyadicCell.name: Rd.memLp_one_indicator_dyadicCell
Rd.memLp_one_indicator_dyadicCell.docstring:
On a cell, `L_p` functions are integrable: `1_{P_{j,m}} g ∈ L_1` for `g ∈ L_p`, `p ≥ 1`,
since the cell has finite volume.

Rd.memLp_of_eLpNorm_add_sum_le.name: Rd.memLp_of_eLpNorm_add_sum_le
Rd.memLp_of_eLpNorm_add_sum_le.docstring:
**Finiteness from a bound**: if `‖F‖_p + ∑_i ‖G_i‖_p ≤ C X` with finite `C` and `X`, then `F`
and every `G_i` lie in `L_p(V)`.

Rd.memLp_mul_of_bound.name: Rd.memLp_mul_of_bound
Rd.memLp_mul_of_bound.docstring: Multiplication by a continuous function bounded by `C` keeps `L_p`.

Rd.memLp_indicator_restrict.name: Rd.memLp_indicator_restrict
Rd.memLp_indicator_restrict.docstring:
For `g ∈ L_p(μ|_O)` and a measurable `T ⊆ O`, the extension by zero `1_T g` lies in `L_p(μ)`
(Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.memLp_indicator_iff_restrict`).

Rd.memLp_extendClosure.name: Rd.memLp_extendClosure
Rd.memLp_extendClosure.docstring:
On a bounded set `Ω`, the extension by `0` lies in `L_2(Ω)`: it is measurable and bounded,
and `Ω` has finite volume.

Rd.memLp_conv.name: Rd.memLp_conv
Rd.memLp_conv.docstring: Convolution of an integrable kernel with an `L_p` function is in `L_p`.

Rd.memLp_blockFun_of_le.name: Rd.memLp_blockFun_of_le
Rd.memLp_blockFun_of_le.docstring:
**The blocks lie in `L_r`** for `1 ≤ p ≤ r ≤ ∞`, `p < ∞` and `f ∈ L_p(V)`, by the Nikolskii
inequality for blocks (`Rd.eLpNorm_blockFun_le_nikolskii`).

Rd.memLp_blockFun.name: Rd.memLp_blockFun
Rd.memLp_blockFun.docstring:
The pointwise blocks `ψ_j ⋆ f` of `f ∈ L_p(V)` lie in `L_p(V)`, for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, by Young's
inequality (`Rd.memLp_conv`).

Rd.memLp_besselWeight_mul_fourier.name: Rd.memLp_besselWeight_mul_fourier
Rd.memLp_besselWeight_mul_fourier.docstring: If `∫ ⟨ξ⟩^{2s} |𝓕f(ξ)|² dξ < ∞` for `f ∈ L_2(V)`, then `⟨ξ⟩^s 𝓕f ∈ L_2(V)`.

Rd.memApprox_of_memSobolevW.name: Rd.memApprox_of_memSobolevW
Rd.memApprox_of_memSobolevW.docstring:
**`W^m_p ⊆ B^m_{p,max(p,2)}`**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 < p < ∞` and `m ≥ 1`, every
`f ∈ W^m_p(V)` lies in the approximation space `A^m_{max(p,2)}` of the band-limited scheme, the
Besov space `B^m_{p,max(p,2)}(V)` (`Rd.memApprox_of_memTriebelLizorkin`).

Rd.memApprox_bandScheme_iff.name: Rd.memApprox_bandScheme_iff
Rd.memApprox_bandScheme_iff.docstring:
**Band-limited approximation and Littlewood–Paley blocks**: for `s > 0` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`,
`f ∈ A^s_q(L_p, (E_k))` iff `(2^(js) ‖Δ_j f‖_p)_j ∈ ℓ_q`.

Rd.measurePreserving_halfSpaceReflection.name: Rd.measurePreserving_halfSpaceReflection
Rd.measurePreserving_halfSpaceReflection.docstring:
The reflection preserves the Lebesgue measure (Mathlib's
`LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving`).

Rd.measurePreserving_gridCoord.name: Rd.measurePreserving_gridCoord
Rd.measurePreserving_gridCoord.docstring:
**The coordinates of the grid preserve Lebesgue measure**: the coordinates of an orthonormal
basis map the volume of `V` to that of `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` (Mathlib's
`OrthonormalBasis.measurePreserving_repr`), and the identification with `Fin n → ℝ` preserves
volume (Mathlib's `PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp`).

Rd.measurable_slobodeckijIntegrand.name: Rd.measurable_slobodeckijIntegrand
Rd.measurable_slobodeckijIntegrand.docstring:
The integrand `(x, y) ↦ |f(y) - f(x)|^p / |y - x|^b` of a Gagliardo form is measurable for
measurable `f`.

Rd.measurable_maximalFunction.name: Rd.measurable_maximalFunction
Rd.measurable_maximalFunction.docstring: The maximal function of every `g : V → [0, ∞]` is **measurable**.

Rd.measurable_lqNorm_ballMeanDiff.name: Rd.measurable_lqNorm_ballMeanDiff
Rd.measurable_lqNorm_ballMeanDiff.docstring: The pointwise `ℓ_q` norm of the weighted ball means is measurable.

Rd.measurable_indicator_half_lt.name: Rd.measurable_indicator_half_lt
Rd.measurable_indicator_half_lt.docstring: The function `(t, x) ↦ 1_{g > t/2}(x) g(x)` is measurable on `ℝ × V` for measurable `g`.

Rd.measurable_higherDiff.name: Rd.measurable_higherDiff
Rd.measurable_higherDiff.docstring: Differences of measurable functions are measurable.

Rd.measurable_extendClosure.name: Rd.measurable_extendClosure
Rd.measurable_extendClosure.docstring: The extension by `0` is measurable: `g` is continuous on the closed set `closure Ω`.

Rd.measurable_enorm_higherDiff_uncurry.name: Rd.measurable_enorm_higherDiff_uncurry
Rd.measurable_enorm_higherDiff_uncurry.docstring:
For measurable `f` the differences `(x, h) ↦ |Δ_h^r f(x)|` are jointly measurable, by the
expansion `Δ_h^r f(x) = ∑_{l ≤ r} (-1)^(r-l) C(r, l) f(x + l h)`.

Rd.measurable_enorm_higherDiff_step.name: Rd.measurable_enorm_higherDiff_step
Rd.measurable_enorm_higherDiff_step.docstring: For measurable `f` and fixed `x` the differences `h ↦ |Δ^L_h f(x)|` are measurable.

Rd.measurable_eLpNorm_fwdDiff_rpow.name: Rd.measurable_eLpNorm_fwdDiff_rpow
Rd.measurable_eLpNorm_fwdDiff_rpow.docstring:
For `0 < p < ∞` and a.e. strongly measurable `f`, the step function `h ↦ ‖Δ_h f‖_p^p` is
measurable, as the integral of a jointly measurable function of `(x, h)` (Mathlib's
`Measurable.lintegral_prod_left'`).

Rd.measurable_cellCoefFun.name: Rd.measurable_cellCoefFun
Rd.measurable_cellCoefFun.docstring:
The step function of the coefficients is measurable: it factors through the measurable cell
index, which takes values in a countable set.

Rd.measurable_ballMeanDiff.name: Rd.measurable_ballMeanDiff
Rd.measurable_ballMeanDiff.docstring:
The ball means of a measurable function are measurable (Tonelli's theorem, Mathlib's
`Measurable.lintegral_prod_right'`).

Rd.measurableSet_switchSet.name: Rd.measurableSet_switchSet
Rd.measurableSet_switchSet.docstring:
The switch set of a measurable set `U` is measurable, as the symmetric difference of `U` and
the measurable set `U - h` (`Rd.switchSet_eq_symmDiff`, Mathlib's `MeasurableSet.symmDiff`).

Rd.measurableSet_infDist_gt.name: Rd.measurableSet_infDist_gt
Rd.measurableSet_infDist_gt.docstring: The sets `{infDist(·, Oᶜ) > δ}` are measurable.

Rd.measurableSet_czEnlarged.name: Rd.measurableSet_czEnlarged
Rd.measurableSet_czEnlarged.docstring: The enlarged exceptional set is measurable.

Rd.meanZeroOverlap_ne_top.name: Rd.meanZeroOverlap_ne_top
Rd.meanZeroOverlap_ne_top.docstring: The overlap constant of a mean-zero Schwartz function is finite.

Rd.meanZeroOverlap.name: Rd.meanZeroOverlap
Rd.meanZeroOverlap.docstring:
The constant `4 (2π ∫ ‖x‖ |G(x)| dx + C_G / (2π))²` of the Fourier overlap of the dilates of a
mean-zero Schwartz function `G`, with the gradient mass `C_G = Rd.gradMassConst G`.

Rd.maximalFunction_mono.name: Rd.maximalFunction_mono
Rd.maximalFunction_mono.docstring: The maximal function is **monotone**: `g ≤ h` implies `M g ≤ M h`.

Rd.maximalFunction_le_of_forall.name: Rd.maximalFunction_le_of_forall
Rd.maximalFunction_le_of_forall.docstring: `M g(x) ≤ c` as soon as `∫_{B(x,r)} g ≤ |B(0,r)| c` for every `r > 0`.

Rd.maximalFunction_le_of_ae_le.name: Rd.maximalFunction_le_of_ae_le
Rd.maximalFunction_le_of_ae_le.docstring: If `g ≤ c` almost everywhere, then `M g ≤ c` everywhere.

Rd.maximalFunction_le_maximalFunction_in.name: Rd.maximalFunction_le_maximalFunction_indicator_add
Rd.maximalFunction_le_maximalFunction_in.docstring:
**Cutting `g` at the height `s`**: `M g ≤ M (1_{g > s} g) + s` for measurable `g`, since
`g ≤ 1_{g > s} g + s`.

Rd.maximalFunction_le_maximalFunction_cz.name: Rd.maximalFunction_le_maximalFunction_czGood
Rd.maximalFunction_le_maximalFunction_cz.docstring:
**The maximal function off `Ω*` is controlled by the good part**: for `x ∉ Ω*` and almost
everywhere measurable `g`, `M g(x) ≤ (1 + 3^n) M(czGood g)(x)`. Split `g = 1_{Ωᶜ} g + 1_Ω g`;
the first part is at most the good part, and `M(1_Ω g)(x) ≤ 3^n M(czAverage g)(x)` by
`Rd.maximalFunction_indicator_czSet_le`.

Rd.maximalFunction_indicator_iUnion_le.name: Rd.maximalFunction_indicator_iUnion_le
Rd.maximalFunction_indicator_iUnion_le.docstring:
**The maximal function off enlarged sets**: let `Q_i ⊆ B̄(c_i, ρ_i)` be countably many
measurable sets of positive finite measure and `x` a point outside every `B̄(c_i, 2ρ_i)`. Then
`M(1_{⋃ Q_i} g)(x) ≤ 3^n M g̃(x)` for every `g : V → [0, ∞]`, where `g̃ = ∑_i (⨍_{Q_i} g) 1_{Q_i}`
replaces `g` on each `Q_i` by its mean. A ball `B(x, r)` that meets `Q_i` has radius `r > ρ_i`
and `Q_i ⊆ B(x, 3r)`, so `∫_{B(x,r)} 1_{⋃ Q_i} g ≤ ∫_{B(x,3r)} g̃`. The bound holds for arbitrary,
possibly overlapping sets `Q_i` and every `g`.

Rd.maximalFunction_indicator_czSet_le.name: Rd.maximalFunction_indicator_czSet_le
Rd.maximalFunction_indicator_czSet_le.docstring:
**Positivity of the maximal function off `Ω*`**: for `x` outside the enlarged exceptional
set, `M(1_Ω h)(x) ≤ 3^n M(czAverage h)(x)` for every `h : V → [0, ∞]`, since every maximal big
cube `Q_{k,m}` lies in `B̄(c_{k,m}, n 2^(-k))` and `Ω*` contains the balls of twice this
radius.

Rd.maximalFunction_eq_self_of_subsinglet.name: Rd.maximalFunction_eq_self_of_subsingleton
Rd.maximalFunction_eq_self_of_subsinglet.docstring:
On a space with one point (`n = 0`) every function is its own maximal function: every ball
of positive radius is the whole space, of positive finite volume.

Rd.maximalFunction_const_mul.name: Rd.maximalFunction_const_mul
Rd.maximalFunction_const_mul.docstring: The maximal function is **homogeneous**: `M (c g) = c M g` for a finite constant `c`.

Rd.maximalFunction_const.name: Rd.maximalFunction_const
Rd.maximalFunction_const.docstring: The maximal function of a **constant** is that constant.

Rd.maximalFunction_congr_ae.name: Rd.maximalFunction_congr_ae
Rd.maximalFunction_congr_ae.docstring: Functions that agree almost everywhere have the **same maximal function**.

Rd.maximalFunction_add_le.name: Rd.maximalFunction_add_le
Rd.maximalFunction_add_le.docstring:
The maximal function is **subadditive**: `M (g + h) ≤ M g + M h`. One summand has to be
measurable, since the lower Lebesgue integral of a sum of two non-measurable functions can exceed
the sum of their integrals.

Rd.maximalFunction.name: Rd.maximalFunction
Rd.maximalFunction.docstring:
The **Hardy–Littlewood maximal function** of `g : V → [0, ∞]`:
`M g(x) = sup_{r > 0} |B(0,r)|⁻¹ ∫_{B(x,r)} g`, the supremum of the means of `g` over the open
balls centred at `x`. The volume `|B(0,r)| = |B(x,r)|` of the centred ball keeps the factor
independent of `x`.

Rd.maximalConst.name: Rd.maximalConst
Rd.maximalConst.docstring:
The constant `C_{n,p} = p 2^p 5^n / (p - 1)` of the strong type bound
`∫ (M g)^p w ≤ C_{n,p} ∫ g^p M w`.

Rd.map_tildeSpace_eq_orthogonal.name: Rd.map_tildeSpace_eq_orthogonal
Rd.map_tildeSpace_eq_orthogonal.docstring:
**The image of `H̃^t(Ω)`**: for `e` as in `Rd.orthogonal_tildeSpace_eq_comap`, `e(H̃^t(Ω))`
is `H^{t'}(Ω)`, the orthogonal complement of the elements of `H^{t'}(V)` vanishing on `Ω`. Since
`H̃^t(Ω)` is closed it is its double orthogonal complement, and `e` maps orthogonal complements
to orthogonal complements (Mathlib's `Submodule.map_orthogonal_equiv`). As there, `t'` is free
only so that the lemma applies to both `Rd.besselShift s` and its inverse.

Rd.map_tildeSpace_besselShift.name: Rd.map_tildeSpace_besselShift
Rd.map_tildeSpace_besselShift.docstring:
**`J_{2s}` maps `H̃^s(Ω)` onto `H^{-s}(Ω)`**: the image of `H̃^s(Ω)` under `besselShift s` is
the orthogonal complement of the elements of `H^{-s}(V)` vanishing on `Ω`.

Rd.lt_setLAverage_zcell_iff.name: Rd.lt_setLAverage_zcell_iff
Rd.lt_setLAverage_zcell_iff.docstring: A height `t` lies below the average of `G` over a cube `Q` exactly when `t |Q| < ∫_Q G`.

Rd.lt_norm_of_fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_.name: Rd.lt_norm_of_fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_ne_zero
Rd.lt_norm_of_fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_.docstring: `𝓕ψ̃_{m+2}` vanishes on the closed ball of radius `2^m`.

Rd.lqNorm_schur_le.name: Rd.lqNorm_schur_le
Rd.lqNorm_schur_le.docstring:
**The Schur test** on `ℓ_q`: if the row sums and the column sums of a nonnegative matrix `w` are
at most `A`, then `‖(∑_k w(m, k) b_k)_m‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ A ‖b‖_{ℓ_q}` for `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, by the weighted
Jensen inequality `(∑_k w b)^q ≤ (∑_k w)^(q-1) ∑_k w b^q`.

Rd.lqNorm_modulus_rpow_le_slobodeckijFor.name: Rd.lqNorm_modulus_rpow_le_slobodeckijForm
Rd.lqNorm_modulus_rpow_le_slobodeckijFor.docstring:
**The first-difference Besov norm by the Gagliardo form**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `s > 0` and
`f ∈ L_p(V)`,
`‖(2^(ks) ω_1(f, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_p}^p ≤ C ∫∫ |f(y) - f(x)|^p / |y - x|^(n+sp) dy dx`
with `C = Rd.slobodeckijConstUpper V p s`.

Rd.lqNorm_maximalFunction_le_indicator_a.name: Rd.lqNorm_maximalFunction_le_indicator_add
Rd.lqNorm_maximalFunction_le_indicator_a.docstring:
**Splitting a family along a set**: for almost everywhere measurable `g_j`, measurable `S` and
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `‖(M g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ‖(M(1_S g_j)(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q} + ‖(M(1_{Sᶜ} g_j)(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}`, by
the subadditivity of `M` and Minkowski's inequality in `ℓ_q`.

Rd.lqNorm_lpModulus_sub_le.name: Rd.lqNorm_lpModulus_sub_le
Rd.lqNorm_lpModulus_sub_le.docstring:
**Moduli of lower order**: for `l ≤ s < r`, the quasi-norm with smoothness `s - l` and order
`r - l` is at most a constant times the one with smoothness `s` and order `r`, since both equal
band-limited approximation spaces (`Rd.bandModulusData`) and `A^s_q ⊆ A^(s-l)_q`.

Rd.lqNorm_lpModulus_le_multiplierConst.name: Rd.lqNorm_lpModulus_le_multiplierConst
Rd.lqNorm_lpModulus_le_multiplierConst.docstring:
**The terms of order `l`**: `‖(2^(k(s-l)) ω_(r-l)(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ K_l ‖F‖_{s,r}` for
`l ≤ r`.

Rd.lqNorm_le_of_le_almostDiagonal_pi.name: Rd.lqNorm_le_of_le_almostDiagonal_pi
Rd.lqNorm_le_of_le_almostDiagonal_pi.docstring:
**The almost diagonal lemma for termwise bounds**: for `0 ≤ s`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and
`C ∈ [0, ∞]`, if `a_m ≤ C^d ∑_k ∏_i c(m_i, k_i) x_k` for every `m ∈ ℕ^d`, then
`‖(2^(s|m|_1) a_m)_m‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ (C C_s)^d ‖(2^(s|k|_1) x_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q}` with the constant `C_s` of
`Rd.lqNorm_almostDiagonal_pi_le`, by the homogeneity of the `ℓ_q` norm and that lemma.

Rd.lqNorm_czGood_le.name: Rd.lqNorm_czGood_le
Rd.lqNorm_czGood_le.docstring:
**The pointwise `ℓ_q` norm of the good parts**: for a family `g_j` of almost everywhere
measurable functions and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `‖(czGood g_j (x))_j‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ 1_{Ωᶜ} F(x) + czAverage F (x)`
with `F(x) = ‖(g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}`: off `Ω` both sides are `F(x)`, and on a maximal big cube `Q` the
left side is `‖(⨍_Q g_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ⨍_Q F` (`MeasureTheory.lqNorm_laverage_le`).

Rd.lqNorm_cellCoefFun_le_lqNorm_maximalF.name: Rd.lqNorm_cellCoefFun_le_lqNorm_maximalFunction
Rd.lqNorm_cellCoefFun_le_lqNorm_maximalF.docstring:
**The coefficients with exponent one in `f^s_{p,q}` by maximal functions**: for almost
everywhere strongly measurable functions `g_j`, the step functions of the coefficients
`λ_{j,m} = Rd.cellCoef 1 j g_j m` satisfy, at every point,
`‖(2^(js) |λ_{j,m_j(x)}|)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ (2n + 1)^n |B_1| ‖(M(2^(js) |g_j|)(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}`.

Rd.lqNorm_blockFun_succ_le_sum_ae.name: Rd.lqNorm_blockFun_succ_le_sum_ae
Rd.lqNorm_blockFun_succ_le_sum_ae.docstring:
**The pointwise bound of the higher blocks**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, under the hypotheses of
`Rd.two_pow_mul_blockFun_succ_ae`, for almost every `x`,
`‖(2^{(j+1)m} (ψ_{j+1} ⋆ f)(x))_j‖_{ℓ_2} ≤ 2^m ∑_α ‖(((η_α)_{2^j} ⋆ g_α)(x))_j‖_{ℓ_2}`, by
Minkowski's inequality in `ℓ_2` (`ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_succ_le_sum`).

Rd.lqNorm_almostDiagonal_pi_le.name: Rd.lqNorm_almostDiagonal_pi_le
Rd.lqNorm_almostDiagonal_pi_le.docstring:
**The almost diagonal lemma on `ℕ^d`**: for `0 < s < L` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`,
`‖(2^(s|m|_1) ∑_k ∏_i c(m_i, k_i) a_k)_m‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C^d ‖(2^(s|k|_1) a_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q}` with
`C = (1 - 2^(-(L-s)))⁻¹ + (1 - 2^(-s))⁻¹`, by the Schur test: the matrix
`2^(s|m|_1) ∏_i c(m_i, k_i) 2^(-s|k|_1) = ∏_i u(m_i - k_i)` has row and column sums at most `C^d`.

Rd.lpMoment.name: Rd.lpMoment
Rd.lpMoment.docstring:
The moment kernel `μ = ∑_{l<L} a_l Φ_{1/(l+1)}` of order `L` built from the
Littlewood–Paley kernel `Φ = Rd.lpKernel`.

Rd.lpModulus_rpow_le_average.name: Rd.lpModulus_rpow_le_average
Rd.lpModulus_rpow_le_average.docstring:
**The dyadic modulus by an average**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`,
`ω_1(f, 2^(-k))_p^p ≤ 2^p |B(0, 2^(-k))|⁻¹ ∫_{|z| < 2^(1-k)} ‖Δ_z f‖_p^p dz`
(`Rd.eLpNorm_fwdDiff_rpow_le_average` for every step of the supremum).

Rd.lpModulus_le_of_mem_bandSpace.name: Rd.lpModulus_le_of_mem_bandSpace
Rd.lpModulus_le_of_mem_bandSpace.docstring:
**The inverse inequality for band-limited functions**: for `a ∈ E_j`,
`ω_r(a, 2^(-k))_p ≤ C 2^(-(k-j) r) ‖a‖_p` with `C = 2^r + ‖D^r Θ‖_1` (and `k - j` truncated at
`0`). For `k ≥ j` and `‖h‖ ≤ 2^(-k)`, `Δ_h^r a = (Δ_h^r Θ_j) ⋆ a` and Young's inequality give
`‖Δ_h^r a‖_p ≤ (2^j ‖h‖)^r ‖D^r Θ‖_1 ‖a‖_p`.

Rd.lpModulus_finsetSum_le.name: Rd.lpModulus_finsetSum_le
Rd.lpModulus_finsetSum_le.docstring: The modulus of a finite sum is at most the sum of the moduli.

Rd.lpModulus_convLp_le.name: Rd.lpModulus_convLp_le
Rd.lpModulus_convLp_le.docstring:
**The modulus of a convolution**: if `‖Δ_v^r K‖_1 ≤ B` for `‖v‖ ≤ 2^(-k)`, then
`ω_r(K ⋆ h, 2^(-k))_p ≤ B ‖h‖_p`, since `Δ_v^r (K ⋆ h) = (Δ_v^r K) ⋆ h` (Young's inequality).

Rd.lpModulus_const_smul.name: Rd.lpModulus_const_smul
Rd.lpModulus_const_smul.docstring:
The dyadic moduli are homogeneous: `ω_r(c f, 2^(-k))_p = |c| ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p`
(`Rd.smoothnessModulus_const_smul`).

Rd.lpModulusOn_mono_set.name: Rd.lpModulusOn_mono_set
Rd.lpModulusOn_mono_set.docstring: The modulus on a set at the dyadic scales grows with the set.

Rd.lpModulusOn_le_tsum.name: Rd.lpModulusOn_le_tsum
Rd.lpModulusOn_le_tsum.docstring:
**The modulus on `Ω` of a series**: if `∑_{j ≤ J} f_j → F` in `L_p`, then
`ω_r(F, 2^(-k), Ω)_p ≤ ∑_j ω_r(f_j, 2^(-k), Ω)_p`.

Rd.lpModulusOn_const_smul.name: Rd.lpModulusOn_const_smul
Rd.lpModulusOn_const_smul.docstring: The dyadic moduli on `U` are homogeneous: `ω_r(c f, 2^(-k), U)_p = |c| ω_r(f, 2^(-k), U)_p`.

Rd.lpModulusOn_congr_set.name: Rd.lpModulusOn_congr_set
Rd.lpModulusOn_congr_set.docstring: The dyadic moduli on almost equal sets agree.

Rd.lpModulusOn_congr.name: Rd.lpModulusOn_congr
Rd.lpModulusOn_congr.docstring: Elements of `L_p` that agree on `U` have the same moduli on `U`.

Rd.lpModulusOn_add_le.name: Rd.lpModulusOn_add_le
Rd.lpModulusOn_add_le.docstring: The modulus on `U` of elements of `L_p` is subadditive.

Rd.lpModulusOn.name: Rd.lpModulusOn
Rd.lpModulusOn.docstring: The modulus on `U` of an element of `L_p` at the dyadic scale `2^(-k)`.

Rd.lpMixedModulus_add_le.name: Rd.lpMixedModulus_add_le
Rd.lpMixedModulus_add_le.docstring: The mixed modulus on `L_p` is subadditive.

Rd.lpMixedModulus.name: Rd.lpMixedModulus
Rd.lpMixedModulus.docstring:
The **mixed modulus at the dyadic scale `2^(-k)`** of `f ∈ L_p`,
`Ω^{e(k)}_L(f, 2^(-k))_p` with `e(k) = {i : k_i ≠ 0}`.

Rd.lpKernelS.name: Rd.lpKernelS
Rd.lpKernelS.docstring: The **Littlewood–Paley kernel** `Φ = 𝓕⁻¹ χ_{1,2}`, a Schwartz function.

Rd.lpKernel.name: Rd.lpKernel
Rd.lpKernel.docstring: The Littlewood–Paley kernel as a function.

Rd.lpBlock_mem_bandSpace.name: Rd.lpBlock_mem_bandSpace
Rd.lpBlock_mem_bandSpace.docstring: **The blocks are band-limited**: `Δ_j f ∈ E_j`, since `Θ_j ⋆ ψ_j = ψ_j`.

Rd.lpBlock_eq_zero_of_mem.name: Rd.lpBlock_eq_zero_of_mem
Rd.lpBlock_eq_zero_of_mem.docstring:
**High blocks of band-limited functions vanish**: `Δ_j g = 0` for `g ∈ E_i` and `j ≥ i + 3`,
since `ψ_j ⋆ Θ_i = 0`.

Rd.lpBlock_ae_eq_blockFun.name: Rd.lpBlock_ae_eq_blockFun
Rd.lpBlock_ae_eq_blockFun.docstring: The block `Δ_j f ∈ L_p` is represented by the pointwise convolution `ψ_j ⋆ f`.

Rd.lpBlockKernelS.name: Rd.lpBlockKernelS
Rd.lpBlockKernelS.docstring: The Littlewood–Paley block `ψ_j = (lpBlockKernelBase j)_{2^j}` as a Schwartz function.

Rd.lpBlockKernelOneS.name: Rd.lpBlockKernelOneS
Rd.lpBlockKernelOneS.docstring: The block `ψ_1 = Φ_1 - Φ` as a Schwartz function, `ψ_1 = δ_2 (lpBlockKernelBase 1)`.

Rd.lpBlockKernelDecayConst_ne_top.name: Rd.lpBlockKernelDecayConst_ne_top
Rd.lpBlockKernelDecayConst_ne_top.docstring: The decay constant of the blocks is finite.

Rd.lpBlockKernelDecayConst.name: Rd.lpBlockKernelDecayConst
Rd.lpBlockKernelDecayConst.docstring:
The constant `(1 + 2^N) C` of the decay of the blocks `ψ_j`, with
`C = Rd.schwartzDecayConst lpKernelS 0 N`.

Rd.lpBlockKernelBaseBound.name: Rd.lpBlockKernelBaseBound
Rd.lpBlockKernelBaseBound.docstring:
The seminorm bounds of the family `lpBlockKernelBase`, the larger of the seminorms of `Φ` and of
`Φ - δ_{1/2} Φ`.

Rd.lpBlockKernelBase.name: Rd.lpBlockKernelBase
Rd.lpBlockKernelBase.docstring:
The Schwartz functions behind the blocks: `lpBlockKernelBase 0 = Φ` and
`lpBlockKernelBase (j+1) = Φ - δ_{1/2} Φ`, with the dilation `δ_c F(x) = c^n F(c x)`, so that
`ψ_j = δ_{2^j} (lpBlockKernelBase j)` (`Rd.dilate_lpBlockKernelBase`).

Rd.lpBlock.name: Rd.lpBlock
Rd.lpBlock.docstring: The **Littlewood–Paley block** `Δ_j f = ψ_j ⋆ f` of `f ∈ L_p`.

Rd.lowerSemicontinuous_setLIntegral_ball.name: Rd.lowerSemicontinuous_setLIntegral_ball
Rd.lowerSemicontinuous_setLIntegral_ball.docstring:
For every `g : V → [0, ∞]` and every radius `r`, `x ↦ ∫_{B(x,r)} g` is **lower
semicontinuous**: the ball `B(x₀, r)` is the increasing union of the balls `B(x₀, r - 1/(m+1))`,
and each of them lies in `B(x, r)` for all `x` close to `x₀`.

Rd.lowerSemicontinuous_maximalFunction.name: Rd.lowerSemicontinuous_maximalFunction
Rd.lowerSemicontinuous_maximalFunction.docstring:
The maximal function of every `g : V → [0, ∞]` is **lower semicontinuous**, as a supremum of
the lower semicontinuous functions `x ↦ |B(0,r)|⁻¹ ∫_{B(x,r)} g`.

Rd.locallyLipschitzOn_inter.name: Rd.locallyLipschitzOn_inter
Rd.locallyLipschitzOn_inter.docstring:
A map of class `C^1` within a relatively open part `Ω ∩ U` of a convex set `Ω` is locally
Lipschitz there.

Rd.locallyIntegrable_indicator_add_indic.name: Rd.locallyIntegrable_indicator_add_indicator_comp_halfSpaceReflection
Rd.locallyIntegrable_indicator_add_indic.docstring:
**The two halves of a reflected function are locally integrable**: for a measurable set `s`,
if `a` and `b` are integrable on every bounded part `s ∩ B(0, R)` of `s`, then
`y ↦ 1_s a (y) + 1_s b (σ y)` is locally integrable on `V`; the reflection `σ` preserves Lebesgue
measure and the balls `B(0, R)`.

Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_top_Lp.name: Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_top_Lp
Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_top_Lp.docstring:
An `L_p(V)` function, `1 ≤ p`, is locally integrable on `V`: the case `Ω = V` of
`Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_of_memLp`.

Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_sum_smul.name: Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_sum_smul
Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_sum_smul.docstring:
Finite sums of locally integrable functions on `Ω` with coefficients in a normed field `𝕜`
acting on `ℂ`, such as `ℝ` or `ℂ`, are locally integrable on `Ω`, by induction over the sum as in
Mathlib's `locallyIntegrable_finsetSum'`.

Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_of_memLp.name: Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_of_memLp
Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_of_memLp.docstring: A function in `L_p(Ω)`, `1 ≤ p`, is locally integrable on `Ω`.

Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_of_forall_gridBas.name: Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_of_forall_gridBasis
Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_of_forall_gridBas.docstring:
**Local integrability from the basis derivatives**: if `f` has weak derivatives `g_i` along
the basis vectors `e_i` on `Ω`, then `f` is locally integrable on `Ω`; in dimension `0` every
function on `V` is constant, hence continuous.

Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_mul_of_tsupport_s.name: Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_mul_of_tsupport_subset
Rd.locallyIntegrableOn_mul_of_tsupport_s.docstring:
**Cutoff products are locally integrable on the larger set**: if `u` is locally integrable
on `O ∩ B` and `c` is continuous with closed support in `B`, then `c u` is locally integrable on
`O`; near points of `B` this is the product with a continuous function, and near the other points
of `O`, `c u` vanishes.

Rd.littlewoodPaleyNorm_max_le_triebelLiz.name: Rd.littlewoodPaleyNorm_max_le_triebelLizorkinNorm
Rd.littlewoodPaleyNorm_max_le_triebelLiz.docstring:
**The lower bound of the Triebel–Lizorkin quasi-norm**, behind `F^s_{p,q} ⊆ B^s_{p,max(p,q)}`:
for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `s ∈ ℝ` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`,
`‖(2^(js) ‖Δ_j f‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_{max(p,q)}} ≤ ‖f‖_{F^s_{p,q}}`. For `q = 2`: the Littlewood–Paley
quasi-norm of `B^s_{p,max(p,2)}` is at most the quasi-norm of `F^s_{p,2}`.

Rd.littlewoodPaleyNorm_le_approxNormDyad.name: Rd.littlewoodPaleyNorm_le_approxNormDyadic
Rd.littlewoodPaleyNorm_le_approxNormDyad.docstring:
**The Littlewood–Paley quasi-norm is controlled by the approximation norm**: for `s ≥ 0`,
`‖(2^(js) ‖Δ_j f‖_p)_j‖_q ≤ 8 · 2^(3s) ‖Φ‖_1 ‖f‖^dyadic`, with the band-limited scheme. The first
three blocks are bounded by `‖f‖`, the block `Δ_{j+3} f` by `E(f, E_j)`.

Rd.littlewoodPaleyNorm_eq_lqNorm_eLpNorm.name: Rd.littlewoodPaleyNorm_eq_lqNorm_eLpNorm
Rd.littlewoodPaleyNorm_eq_lqNorm_eLpNorm.docstring:
The Littlewood–Paley quasi-norm of the Besov spaces in terms of the pointwise blocks:
`‖(2^(js) ‖Δ_j f‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q} = ‖(2^(js) ‖ψ_j ⋆ f‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`.

Rd.lipschitzWith_fourierInv_indicator.name: Rd.lipschitzWith_fourierInv_indicator
Rd.lipschitzWith_fourierInv_indicator.docstring:
**Band-limited functions are Lipschitz**, with explicit constant: for `h ∈ L_2(V)`, the
function `𝓕⁻(1_{B_K} h)` is Lipschitz on `V` with constant `2π max(K, 0) |B_K|^{1/2} ‖h‖_2`
(`Rd.norm_fourierInv_sub_le` and Cauchy–Schwarz on the ball).

Rd.lipschitzWith_closureToLp.name: Rd.lipschitzWith_closureToLp
Rd.lipschitzWith_closureToLp.docstring:
The map `g ↦ g` from bounded continuous functions on `closure Ω` to `L_2(Ω)` is Lipschitz
with constant `|Ω|^{1/2}`.

Rd.lintegral_tail_schwartz_le.name: Rd.lintegral_tail_schwartz_le
Rd.lintegral_tail_schwartz_le.docstring:
**Tails of Schwartz functions**: for every real `ρ`,
`∫_{‖z‖ ≥ ρ} |G(z)| ‖z‖^r dz ≤ C (1 + max(ρ, 0))^(-N)` with `C = Rd.tailConst G r N`.

Rd.lintegral_rpow_sum_maximalFunction_ne.name: Rd.lintegral_rpow_sum_maximalFunction_ne_top
Rd.lintegral_rpow_sum_maximalFunction_ne.docstring:
**Finiteness for finitely many functions**: for `1 < q < p`, finitely many almost everywhere
measurable `g_j` and `∫ (∑_j g_j^q)^(p/q) < ∞`, also `∫ (∑_j (M g_j)^q)^(p/q) < ∞`: each `g_j^p`
is at most `(∑_j g_j^q)^(p/q)`, the maximal theorem bounds `∫ (M g_j)^p`, and
`(∑_{j ∈ S} a_j)^u ≤ |S|^(u-1) ∑_{j ∈ S} a_j^u`.

Rd.lintegral_rpow_sum_maximalFunction_le.name: Rd.lintegral_rpow_sum_maximalFunction_le_mul
Rd.lintegral_rpow_sum_maximalFunction_le.docstring:
**The duality step** for finitely many functions: for `q > 1`, conjugate exponents `u, u'`
and almost everywhere measurable `g_j`, with `H = ∑_{j ∈ S} (M g_j)^q`,
`∫ H^u ≤ C_{n,q} C_{n,u'}^{1/u'} (∫ (∑_{j ∈ S} g_j^q)^u)^{1/u} (∫ H^u)^{1/u'}`. With
`w = H^(u-1)`, `∫ H^u = ∑_j ∫ (M g_j)^q w ≤ C_{n,q} ∫ (∑_j g_j^q) M w` by the weighted strong type,
then Hölder's inequality and the maximal theorem for `w` in `L_{u'}`, where
`∫ w^{u'} = ∫ H^u`.

Rd.lintegral_rpow_sum_maximalFunction_le.name: Rd.lintegral_rpow_sum_maximalFunction_le
Rd.lintegral_rpow_sum_maximalFunction_le.docstring:
**The Fefferman–Stein inequality for `q < p` and finitely many functions**: for `1 < q < p` and
almost everywhere measurable `g_j`, `∫ (∑_{j ∈ S} (M g_j)^q)^(p/q) ≤ C ∫ (∑_{j ∈ S} g_j^q)^(p/q)`
with `C = dualityConst n p q`. The duality step `Rd.lintegral_rpow_sum_maximalFunction_le_mul` with
`u = p/q` and `u' = p/(p - q)` gives `X ≤ K A^{1/u} X^{1/u'}`, and since `X < ∞` the factor
`X^{1/u'}` cancels (`ENNReal.le_rpow_mul_of_le_mul_rpow`).

Rd.lintegral_rpow_div_norm_rpow_le.name: Rd.lintegral_rpow_div_norm_rpow_le
Rd.lintegral_rpow_div_norm_rpow_le.docstring:
**A radial integral of Lipschitz differences**: if `u(z) ≤ L |z|` and `u(z) ≤ S` for all
`z ∈ V`, `dim V = n`, then `∫ u(z)^p / |z|^a dz ≤ L^p c_1 + S^p c_2` for `p > 0` and
`a - p < n < a`, with the constants `c_1 = Rd.ballRpowConst V (a - p)` of the unit ball, where
`u^p / |z|^a ≤ L^p |z|^(-(a-p))`, and `c_2 = Rd.complBallRpowConst V a` of its complement, where
`u^p / |z|^a ≤ S^p |z|^(-a)`.

Rd.lintegral_peetre_mul_le.name: Rd.lintegral_peetre_mul_le
Rd.lintegral_peetre_mul_le.docstring:
**Convolution of two Peetre bumps**: for `i ≤ j`, the integral
`∫ 2^(jn) (1 + 2^j ‖y - w‖)^(-2N) 2^(in) (1 + 2^i ‖w‖)^(-N) dw` is at most
`(∫ (1 + ‖u‖)^(-N) du) 2^(in) (1 + 2^i ‖y‖)^(-N)`, by Peetre's inequality and the substitution
`u = 2^j (y - w)`.

Rd.lintegral_mul_peetre_le_of_support.name: Rd.lintegral_mul_peetre_le_of_support
Rd.lintegral_mul_peetre_le_of_support.docstring:
**Integrals against a kernel of small support**: if `η` vanishes outside
`B̄(0, ρ 2^(-k))` and `|ψ(z)| ≤ C 2^(kn) (1 + 2^k ‖z‖)^(-N)`, then
`∫ |η(w)| |ψ(y - w)| dw ≤ ‖η‖_1 C (1 + ρ)^N 2^(kn) (1 + 2^k ‖y‖)^(-N)`, by Peetre's inequality
`(1 + 2^k ‖y - w‖)^(-N) ≤ (1 + 2^k ‖w‖)^N (1 + 2^k ‖y‖)^(-N)`.

Rd.lintegral_mul_le_setLIntegral_ball.name: Rd.lintegral_mul_le_setLIntegral_ball
Rd.lintegral_mul_le_setLIntegral_ball.docstring:
**Kernels bounded by a ball, before the maximal function**: if `0 ≤ K ≤ A 1_{B(0,ρ)}`
with `A < ∞`, then `∫ K(y) g(x - y) dy ≤ A ∫_{B(x,ρ)} g` for every `g : V → [0, ∞]`, by the
translation invariance of the Lebesgue measure.

Rd.lintegral_mul_le_maximalFunction_of_o.name: Rd.lintegral_mul_le_maximalFunction_of_one_add_norm
Rd.lintegral_mul_le_maximalFunction_of_o.docstring:
**Kernels with Peetre decay.** If `K(y) ≤ A 2^(jn) (1 + 2^j ‖y‖)^(-N)` with `N > n`, then
`∫ K(y) g(x - y) dy ≤ C_{n,N} A M g(x)` for every `g : V → [0, ∞]`, with the constant
`C_{n,N} = decayMaximalConst V N` independent of the level `j`.

Rd.lintegral_mul_le_maximalFunction_of_d.name: Rd.lintegral_mul_le_maximalFunction_of_decay
Rd.lintegral_mul_le_maximalFunction_of_d.docstring:
**Kernels with a power tail.** If `K ≤ A` on `B̄(0,ρ)` and `K(y) ≤ A (ρ/‖y‖)^N` outside, with
`N > n`, then `∫ K(y) g(x - y) dy ≤ A |B(0,ρ)| 2^n (1 - 2^(-(N-n)))⁻¹ M g(x)` for every
`g : V → [0, ∞]`. The proof covers `V` by the ball `B(0,2ρ)` and the dyadic shells
`2^i ρ ≤ ‖y‖ < 2^(i+1) ρ`, `i ≥ 1`, applies the ball bound on each, and sums a geometric
series.

Rd.lintegral_mul_le_maximalFunction_of_b.name: Rd.lintegral_mul_le_maximalFunction_of_ball
Rd.lintegral_mul_le_maximalFunction_of_b.docstring:
**Kernels bounded by a ball.** If `0 ≤ K ≤ A 1_{B(0,ρ)}`, then
`∫ K(y) g(x - y) dy ≤ A |B(0,ρ)| M g(x)` for every `g : V → [0, ∞]` and every kernel `K`
(`Rd.lintegral_mul_le_setLIntegral_ball` and the definition of `M g`).

Rd.lintegral_maximalFunction_rpow_mul_le.name: Rd.lintegral_maximalFunction_rpow_mul_le_of_measurable
Rd.lintegral_maximalFunction_rpow_mul_le.docstring:
The **weighted strong type** for measurable `g` and `w`: `∫ (M g)^p w ≤ C_{n,p} ∫ g^p M w`
for `p > 1`, the case of `Rd.lintegral_maximalFunction_rpow_mul_le` before `g` and `w` are replaced
by measurable representatives.

Rd.lintegral_maximalFunction_rpow_mul_le.name: Rd.lintegral_maximalFunction_rpow_mul_le
Rd.lintegral_maximalFunction_rpow_mul_le.docstring:
**Weighted strong type of the maximal function** (Fefferman–Stein): for `1 < p < ∞` and
almost everywhere measurable `g, w : V → [0, ∞]`, `∫ (M g)^p w ≤ C_{n,p} ∫ g^p M w` with
`C_{n,p} = p 2^p 5^n / (p - 1)`. The bound holds for every such `g` and `w`, with both sides
possibly infinite. The proof is the layer cake formula in the measure `w dx`, the weighted weak
type for the part of `g` above half the height, and Tonelli's theorem.

Rd.lintegral_maximalFunction_rpow_le.name: Rd.lintegral_maximalFunction_rpow_le
Rd.lintegral_maximalFunction_rpow_le.docstring:
**The strong type in integral form**: `∫ (M g)^p ≤ C_{n,p} ∫ g^p` for `p > 1` and almost
everywhere measurable `g : V → [0, ∞]` (`Rd.lintegral_maximalFunction_rpow_mul_le` with `w = 1`).

Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_sub_le.name: Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_sub_le
Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_sub_le.docstring:
**The Hörmander condition for dilation families**: for a uniform family `(G_j)` with bounds
`A` and every `y ∈ V`,
`∫_{‖x‖ > 2‖y‖} ‖((G_j)_{2^j}(x - y) - (G_j)_{2^j}(x))_j‖_{ℓ_2} dx ≤ 4 H_A` with
`H_A = Rd.familyHormanderConst V A`. The `ℓ_2` norm is at most the `ℓ_1` norm
(`ENNReal.lqNorm_le_lqNorm_one`), each term is bounded by
`Rd.setLIntegral_enorm_dilate_sub_le_min`, and the dyadic sum by `ENNReal.tsum_min_two_pow_le`.

Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_maximalFunction_rpow.name: Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_maximalFunction_rpow_le_of_lt_of_measurable
Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_maximalFunction_rpow.docstring:
**The Fefferman–Stein inequality for `p < q` in integral form, measurable case**: in
dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 < p < q < ∞` and measurable `g_j : V → [0, ∞]`,
`∫ ‖(M g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}^p dx ≤ C ∫ G^p` with `G = ‖(g_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q}` and
`C = interpolationConst V p q`. The layer cake formula, the level estimate
`Rd.volume_lqNorm_maximalFunction_gt_mul_rpow_le` and the two Tonelli steps give it. The bound
`1 < p < q.toReal` forces `q < ∞`.

Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_maximalFunction_rpow.name: Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_maximalFunction_rpow_le_of_lt
Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_maximalFunction_rpow.docstring:
**The Fefferman–Stein inequality for `p < q` in integral form** (interpolation): in dimension
`n ≥ 1`, for `1 < p < q < ∞` and almost everywhere measurable `g_j : V → [0, ∞]`,
`∫ ‖(M g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}^p dx ≤ C ∫ ‖(g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}^p dx` with
`C = interpolationConst V p q`. At each level `τ` the family is split at `{G > τ}`; the
vector-valued weak type `(1,1)` controls the large part and the case `q = p` the small part, as
in Marcinkiewicz's interpolation theorem.

Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_maximalFunction_rpow.name: Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_maximalFunction_rpow_le_of_gt
