Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_maximalFunction_rpow.docstring:
**The Fefferman–Stein inequality for `q < p` in integral form** (duality): for
`1 < q < p < ∞` and almost everywhere measurable `g_j : V → [0, ∞]`, in every dimension,
`∫ ‖(M g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}^p dx ≤ C ∫ ‖(g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}^p dx` with `C = dualityConst n p q`. The
finite partial sums satisfy `Rd.lintegral_rpow_sum_maximalFunction_le`, and monotone convergence
passes to the series.

Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_maximalFunction_rpow.name: Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_maximalFunction_rpow_le
Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_maximalFunction_rpow.docstring:
**The Fefferman–Stein inequality for `q = p` in integral form**: for `1 < q < ∞` and almost
everywhere measurable `g_j : V → [0, ∞]`,
`∫ ‖(M g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}^q dx ≤ C_{n,q} ∫ ‖(g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}^q dx`. Both sides are `∑_j ∫ (·)^q`, and
the maximal theorem applies to each `j`.

Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czGood_rpow_le.name: Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czGood_rpow_le
Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czGood_rpow_le.docstring:
**The `q`-th power of the good parts**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 < q < ∞`, almost
everywhere measurable `g_j` with `G = ‖(g_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q}` integrable, and `0 < t`, the good parts
of the decomposition of `G` at height `t` satisfy
`∫ ‖(czGood g_j (x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}^q dx ≤ 2^(n(q-1)) t^(q-1) ∫ G`: their `ℓ_q` norm is bounded by
`2^n t` almost everywhere and has integral at most `∫ G`
(`MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_mul_lintegral_of_ae_le`).

Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czGood_le.name: Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czGood_le
Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czGood_le.docstring:
**The integral of the `ℓ_q` norm of the good parts is at most that of the family**:
`∫ ‖(czGood g_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ∫ ‖(g_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q}` for
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and almost everywhere measurable `g_j`, for the decomposition of any `G` at any
height.

Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czGoodC_sq_le.name: Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czGoodC_sq_le
Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czGoodC_sq_le.docstring:
**The square of the good parts of a family**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, almost
everywhere strongly measurable `g_j` with `G = ‖(‖g_j‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q}` integrable, and `0 < t`,
`∫ ‖(‖czGoodC g_j‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q}² ≤ 2^n t ∫ G` for the cubes of `G` at height `t`.

Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czGoodC_le.name: Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czGoodC_le
Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czGoodC_le.docstring:
**The integral of the `ℓ_q` norm of the good parts of a family is at most `∫ G`**:
`∫ ‖(‖czGoodC g_j‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ∫ G` with `G = ‖(‖g_j‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`, for `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, almost
everywhere strongly measurable `g_j`, and the cubes of any function at any height.

Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czBadPart_le.name: Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czBadPart_le
Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czBadPart_le.docstring:
**The mass of the bad pieces of a family on one cube**: for `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, almost everywhere
strongly measurable `g_j` and every cube `Q`,
`∫ ‖(‖czBadPart_Q g_j‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ 2 ∫_Q ‖(‖g_j‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`
(`MeasureTheory.setLIntegral_lqNorm_sub_setAverage_le`).

Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_conv_sq_le_of_fourie.name: Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_conv_sq_le_of_fourier_bound
Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_conv_sq_le_of_fourie.docstring:
**The analysis bound on `L_2`, for functions**: for integrable kernels `θ_j` with Fourier
overlap `B` (almost everywhere) and every `f ∈ L_2(V)`,
`∫ ‖((θ_j ⋆ f)(x))_j‖_{ℓ_2}² dx ≤ B ∫ |f|²` (`Rd.tsum_enorm_convLp_sq_le_of_fourier_bound`
for the class of `f`, and Mathlib's `lintegral_tsum`).

Rd.lintegral_lintegral_mul_indicator_le.name: Rd.lintegral_lintegral_mul_indicator_le
Rd.lintegral_lintegral_mul_indicator_le.docstring:
**The tail part of a Gagliardo form**: for `η > 0`, `a > n = dim V` and every
`u : V → [0, ∞]`, `∫∫ u(x) 1_{|y - x| ≥ η} |y - x|^(-a) dy dx ≤ c η^(n - a) ∫ u` with
`c = Rd.complBallRpowConst V a`: the inner integral is `∫_{|z| ≥ η} |z|^(-a) dz` by translation
(`Rd.lintegral_compl_ball_norm_rpow_neg_le`).

Rd.lintegral_lintegral_le_add_two_mul.name: Rd.lintegral_lintegral_le_add_two_mul
Rd.lintegral_lintegral_le_add_two_mul.docstring:
**A double integral by a pointwise bound with one-variable parts**: if
`F(x, y) ≤ T(x, y) + a(x) + a(y)` for measurable `a`, then
`∫∫ F ≤ ∫∫ T + 2 μ(univ) ∫ a` (`Rd.lintegral_lintegral_add_right`).

Rd.lintegral_lintegral_const_mul'.name: Rd.lintegral_lintegral_const_mul'
Rd.lintegral_lintegral_const_mul'.docstring:
`∫∫ c F = c ∫∫ F` for a finite constant `c`, measurable `F` or not (Mathlib's
`lintegral_const_mul'` twice).

Rd.lintegral_lintegral_add_right.name: Rd.lintegral_lintegral_add_right
Rd.lintegral_lintegral_add_right.docstring:
**Splitting a double integral**: `∫∫ (F + G) = ∫∫ F + ∫∫ G` for an s-finite measure and `G`
jointly measurable, whatever `F` (Mathlib's `lintegral_add_right'` for the inner and the outer
integral, with `Measurable.lintegral_prod_right'`).

Rd.lintegral_lintegral_Ioc_add_smul.name: Rd.lintegral_lintegral_Ioc_add_smul
Rd.lintegral_lintegral_Ioc_add_smul.docstring:
**Averages of translates along a segment**: for a measurable `φ : V → [0, ∞]` and `v ∈ V`,
`∫_V ∫_0^1 φ(x + t v) dt dx = ∫_V φ`, by Tonelli's theorem (Mathlib's `lintegral_lintegral_swap`)
and the translation invariance of Lebesgue measure.

Rd.lintegral_inner_sq_eq.name: Rd.lintegral_inner_sq_eq
Rd.lintegral_inner_sq_eq.docstring:
**A directional derivative by Plancherel**: if `∂_v f = g` as tempered distributions with
`f, g ∈ L_2(V)`, then `(2π)² ∫ ⟪ξ, v⟫² |𝓕f(ξ)|² dξ = ‖g‖_2²`.

Rd.lintegral_fin_nat_prod_volume_eq_prod.name: Rd.lintegral_fin_nat_prod_volume_eq_prod
Rd.lintegral_fin_nat_prod_volume_eq_prod.docstring:
**Tonelli's theorem for products of functions of one coordinate**: on `ℝ^d` with Lebesgue
measure, `∫⁻ ∏_i f_i(x_i) dx = ∏_i ∫⁻ f_i` for all almost everywhere measurable
`f_i : ℝ → [0, ∞]`. The induction on `d` is the one of Mathlib's `integral_fin_nat_prod_eq_prod`:
`measurePreserving_piFinSuccAbove` splits off the first coordinate and `lintegral_prod_mul`
integrates the product of a function of it and a function of the others. TauCeti has the form
for `Measure.pi` over any finite index type (`TauCeti.lintegral_fintype_prod_eq_prod`).

Rd.lintegral_enorm_tensorKernel.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_tensorKernel
Rd.lintegral_enorm_tensorKernel.docstring:
**The `L_1` norm of a tensor product**: `‖⊗K‖_1 = ∏_i ‖K_i‖_1`, Tonelli's theorem
`Rd.lintegral_fin_nat_prod_volume_eq_prod` for `f_i = |K_i|`.

Rd.lintegral_enorm_sum_conv_sq_le_of_fou.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_sum_conv_sq_le_of_fourier_bound
Rd.lintegral_enorm_sum_conv_sq_le_of_fou.docstring:
**The synthesis bound on `L_2`, for functions**: for integrable kernels `θ_j` with Fourier
overlap `B` (almost everywhere), functions `g_j ∈ L_2(V)` and every finite set `s` of indices,
`∫ |∑_{j ∈ s} θ_j ⋆ g_j|² ≤ B ∫ ‖(g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_2}² dx`
(`Rd.enorm_sum_convLp_sq_le_of_fourier_bound` for the classes of the `g_j`).

Rd.lintegral_enorm_sq_eq_enorm_toLp.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_sq_eq_enorm_toLp
Rd.lintegral_enorm_sq_eq_enorm_toLp.docstring:
**The `L_2` norm of a function through its class**: for a function `f` with
`∫ |f|² < ∞` (`MemLp f 2 μ`), `∫ |f|² = ‖[f]‖_2²` for the class `[f] = hf.toLp f` of `f` in
`L_2(μ)`, on every measure space (`Rd.enorm_sq_eq_lintegral` and `[f] = f` almost everywhere).

Rd.lintegral_enorm_ne_zero_of_integral_e.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_ne_zero_of_integral_eq_one
Rd.lintegral_enorm_ne_zero_of_integral_e.docstring: The `L_1` norm of a function with integral `1` does not vanish.

Rd.lintegral_enorm_lineDerivOp_le.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_lineDerivOp_le
Rd.lintegral_enorm_lineDerivOp_le.docstring:
**`L_1` norms of directional derivatives**: `∫ |∂_v G| ≤ ‖v‖ M_G` with the gradient mass
`M_G = Rd.gradMassConst G`.

Rd.lintegral_enorm_iteratedFDeriv_ne_top.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_iteratedFDeriv_ne_top
Rd.lintegral_enorm_iteratedFDeriv_ne_top.docstring: The derivatives of a Schwartz function are integrable: `‖D^r G‖_1 < ∞`.

Rd.lintegral_enorm_higherDiff_schwartz_l.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_higherDiff_schwartz_le
Rd.lintegral_enorm_higherDiff_schwartz_l.docstring: **`L_1` norms of differences of Schwartz functions**: `‖Δ_v^r G‖_1 ≤ ‖v‖^r ‖D^r G‖_1`.

Rd.lintegral_enorm_higherDiff_le.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_higherDiff_le
Rd.lintegral_enorm_higherDiff_le.docstring:
**Differences of order `r` are bounded by line derivatives of order `r` in `L_1`**:
`‖Δ_v^r G‖_1 ≤ ‖∂_v^r G‖_1`.

Rd.lintegral_enorm_fwdDiff_rpow_le.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_fwdDiff_rpow_le
Rd.lintegral_enorm_fwdDiff_rpow_le.docstring:
**A difference is bounded by the line derivative in `L_p`**: for a Schwartz function `G` and
real `p ≥ 1`, `∫ |Δ_v G|^p ≤ ∫ |∂_v G|^p`, that is `‖Δ_v G‖_p ≤ ‖∂_v G‖_p`. Integrate the
pointwise bound `Rd.enorm_fwdDiff_schwartz_rpow_le` over `x` and use
`Rd.lintegral_lintegral_Ioc_add_smul`.

Rd.lintegral_enorm_fwdDiff_le.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_fwdDiff_le
Rd.lintegral_enorm_fwdDiff_le.docstring:
**A difference is bounded by the line derivative in `L_1`**: `‖Δ_v G‖_1 ≤ ‖∂_v G‖_1` for a
Schwartz function `G`, the case `p = 1` of `Rd.lintegral_enorm_fwdDiff_rpow_le`.

Rd.lintegral_enorm_dilate_sub_le_mul.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_dilate_sub_le_mul
Rd.lintegral_enorm_dilate_sub_le_mul.docstring:
**Short steps**: `∫ |G_{2^j}(x - y) - G_{2^j}(x)| dx ≤ M_G 2^j ‖y‖` with the gradient mass
`M_G = Rd.gradMassConst G`: the difference is the dilate of the difference of `G` with step
`-2^j y` (`Rd.higherDiff_dilate`), dilations keep `L_1` norms, and a difference is at most the
directional derivative in `L_1` (`Rd.lintegral_enorm_fwdDiff_le`).

Rd.lintegral_enorm_dilate.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_dilate
Rd.lintegral_enorm_dilate.docstring:
**Dilations keep the `L_1` norm of every function**: `∫ |F_c| dμ = ∫ |F| dμ` for `c > 0` and
every `F : V → ℂ`, integrable or not, by the change of scale `u = c x`
(`Rd.lintegral_comp_smul`).

Rd.lintegral_enorm_czGoodC_sq_le.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_czGoodC_sq_le
Rd.lintegral_enorm_czGoodC_sq_le.docstring:
**The square of the good part**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for integrable `f` and `0 < t`, the
good part of `f` in the decomposition of `‖f‖` at height `t` satisfies
`∫ ‖czGoodC f‖² ≤ 2^n t ∫ ‖f‖`: it is bounded by `2^n t`, and the integral of its norm is at
most `∫ ‖f‖`.

Rd.lintegral_enorm_czGoodC_le.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_czGoodC_le
Rd.lintegral_enorm_czGoodC_le.docstring:
**The integral of the norm of the signed good part is at most that of `f`**:
`∫ ‖czGoodC f‖ ≤ ∫ ‖f‖` for every `f : V → E`, since the nonnegative good part keeps the integral
(`Rd.lintegral_czGood`).

Rd.lintegral_enorm_czBadPart_le.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_czBadPart_le
Rd.lintegral_enorm_czBadPart_le.docstring:
**The mass of a bad piece**: `∫ ‖czBadPart_Q f‖ ≤ 2 ∫_Q ‖f‖` for every cube `Q` and every
`f : V → E` (`MeasureTheory.setLIntegral_enorm_sub_setAverage_le`).

Rd.lintegral_enorm_conv_sq_eq.name: Rd.lintegral_enorm_conv_sq_eq
Rd.lintegral_enorm_conv_sq_eq.docstring:
**The `L_2` norm of a convolution through its class**: for integrable `K` and `f ∈ L_2(V)`,
`∫ |K ⋆ f|² = ‖K ⋆ f‖_2²` with the convolution operator `Rd.convLp` on `L_2(V)`.

Rd.lintegral_dilate_peetre.name: Rd.lintegral_dilate_peetre
Rd.lintegral_dilate_peetre.docstring:
The mass of the dilated Peetre weight:
`∫ 2^(jn) (1 + 2^j ‖u‖)^(-N) du = ∫ (1 + ‖u‖)^(-N) du`.

Rd.lintegral_czGood.name: Rd.lintegral_czGood
Rd.lintegral_czGood.docstring:
**The good part keeps the integral**: `∫ czGood h = ∫ h` for every `h : V → [0, ∞]`, since
`h` is kept outside `Ω` and the averages keep the integral over `Ω` (`Rd.lintegral_czAverage`).

Rd.lintegral_czAverage.name: Rd.lintegral_czAverage
Rd.lintegral_czAverage.docstring:
**The averages keep the integral**: `∫ czAverage h = ∫_Ω h` for every `h : V → [0, ∞]`, since
`|Q| ⨍_Q h = ∫_Q h` on each of the disjoint maximal big cubes `Q`.

Rd.lintegral_compl_ball_norm_rpow_neg_le.name: Rd.lintegral_compl_ball_norm_rpow_neg_le
Rd.lintegral_compl_ball_norm_rpow_neg_le.docstring:
**The radial integral outside a ball**: for `a > n = dim V` and `R > 0`,
`∫_{|z| ≥ R} |z|^(-a) dz ≤ 2^n |B_1| (1 - 2^(-(a-n)))⁻¹ R^(n-a)`, by the dyadic shells
`2^i R ≤ |z| < 2^(i+1) R` and a geometric series.

Rd.lintegral_comp_smul.name: Rd.lintegral_comp_smul
Rd.lintegral_comp_smul.docstring:
**Integrals under a change of scale**: `∫ f(r x) dμ(x) = |r^(-n)| ∫ f dμ` for `r ≠ 0`, every
additive Haar measure `μ` and every `f : V → [0, ∞]` (Mathlib's `Measure.map_addHaar_smul`).

Rd.lintegral_besselWeight_one_sq_eq.name: Rd.lintegral_besselWeight_one_sq_eq
Rd.lintegral_besselWeight_one_sq_eq.docstring:
**The `H^1` integral by the gradient**: let `(e_i)` be an orthonormal basis of `V`. If
`∂_{e_i} f = g_i` as tempered distributions for every `i`, with `f, g_i ∈ L_2(V)`, then
`(2π)² ∫ ⟨ξ⟩² |𝓕f(ξ)|² dξ = (2π)² ‖f‖_2² + ∑_i ‖g_i‖_2²`.

Rd.lintegral_ball_norm_rpow_neg_le.name: Rd.lintegral_ball_norm_rpow_neg_le
Rd.lintegral_ball_norm_rpow_neg_le.docstring:
**The radial integral over a ball**: for `a < n = dim V` and `R > 0`,
`∫_{|z| < R} |z|^(-a) dz ≤ (1 + 2^a) |B_1| (1 - 2^(-(n-a)))⁻¹ R^(n-a)`, by the dyadic annuli
`R 2^(-(i+1)) < |z| ≤ R 2^(-i)` and a geometric series; the centre is a null set for `n ≥ 1`,
and for `n = 0` the integrand vanishes.

Rd.lintegral_Ioi_lintegral_indicator_mul.name: Rd.lintegral_Ioi_lintegral_indicator_mul_rpow
Rd.lintegral_Ioi_lintegral_indicator_mul.docstring:
The **Tonelli step** of the strong type bound: for measurable `g, v : V → [0, ∞]` and
`p > 1`, `∫_0^∞ (∫_{g > t/2} g v) t^(p-2) dt = 2^(p-1)/(p-1) ∫ g^p v`.

Rd.lineDeriv_mul_schwartz.name: Rd.lineDeriv_mul_schwartz
Rd.lineDeriv_mul_schwartz.docstring:
The product rule for Schwartz functions: `∂_v (w₁ w₂) = (∂_v w₁) w₂ + w₁ ∂_v w₂`
(`Rd.lineDeriv_mul`, Mathlib's `SchwartzMap.lineDerivOp_apply`).

Rd.lineDeriv_mul.name: Rd.lineDeriv_mul
Rd.lineDeriv_mul.docstring:
**The product rule for line derivatives**: for `f, g : V → ℂ` differentiable at `x`,
`∂_v (f g)(x) = ∂_v f(x) g(x) + f(x) ∂_v g(x)` (Mathlib's `fderiv_fun_mul` and
`DifferentiableAt.lineDeriv_eq_fderiv`).

Rd.lineDeriv_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport.name: Rd.lineDeriv_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport
Rd.lineDeriv_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport.docstring:
**Line derivatives vanish outside the closed support**: `∂_v g(x) = 0` for `x ∉ tsupport g`,
since `g` vanishes on a neighbourhood of `x`.

Rd.lineDeriv_comp_eq_sum.name: Rd.lineDeriv_comp_eq_sum
Rd.lineDeriv_comp_eq_sum.docstring:
**The chain rule through the basis**: if `u` is differentiable at `Φ x` and `Φ` at `x`, then
`∂_v (u ∘ Φ)(x) = ∑_i ⟪DΦ(x) v, e_i⟫ Du(Φ x) e_i`, by `DΦ(x) v = ∑_i ⟪e_i, DΦ(x) v⟫ e_i`
(Mathlib's `OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr'`).

Rd.lineDerivOp_testSchwartz.name: Rd.lineDerivOp_testSchwartz
Rd.lineDerivOp_testSchwartz.docstring:
Passing to complex values commutes with directional derivatives:
`∂_a (φ : ℂ) = (∂_a φ : ℂ)`.

Rd.lineDerivOp_testFunction_apply.name: Rd.lineDerivOp_testFunction_apply
Rd.lineDerivOp_testFunction_apply.docstring:
The directional derivative of a test function is the derivative of the function:
`∂_a φ(x) = Dφ(x) a`.

Rd.lineDerivOp_testFunctionMul_apply.name: Rd.lineDerivOp_testFunctionMul_apply
Rd.lineDerivOp_testFunctionMul_apply.docstring: **The product rule for test functions**: `∂_w (φ χ) = (∂_w φ) χ + φ ∂_w χ`.

Rd.lineDerivOp_testFunctionMulOn_apply.name: Rd.lineDerivOp_testFunctionMulOn_apply
Rd.lineDerivOp_testFunctionMulOn_apply.docstring:
**The product rule for `Rd.testFunctionMulOn`**: `∂_w (φ χ) = (∂_w φ) χ + φ ∂_w χ`. As a
function, `φ χ` is the test function `Rd.testFunctionMul φ` on `O`, whose derivative is
`Rd.lineDerivOp_testFunctionMul_apply`.

Rd.lineDerivOp_schwartzDilate.name: Rd.lineDerivOp_schwartzDilate
Rd.lineDerivOp_schwartzDilate.docstring:
**The chain rule for dilations**: `∂_v (G_c) = c (∂_v G)_c` for every Schwartz function `G`
and every `c ≠ 0`, from Mathlib's `SchwartzMap.lineDerivOp_compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv` and
`∂_{c v} = c ∂_v`.

Rd.lineDerivOp_fwdDiffSchwartz.name: Rd.lineDerivOp_fwdDiffSchwartz
Rd.lineDerivOp_fwdDiffSchwartz.docstring: **Differences commute with line derivatives**: `∂_u (Δ_v G) = Δ_v (∂_u G)`.

Rd.levelNorm_mono.name: Rd.levelNorm_mono
Rd.levelNorm_mono.docstring: The `ℓ_p`-norm of the coefficients is monotone in their moduli.

Rd.levelNorm_cellCoef.name: Rd.levelNorm_cellCoef
Rd.levelNorm_cellCoef.docstring:
**The coefficients of one level**: `‖λ_{j,·}‖_{ℓ_p} = 2^(jn/p) ‖g‖_p`, since the cells
partition `V`.

Rd.levelNorm.name: Rd.levelNorm
Rd.levelNorm.docstring: The `ℓ_p`-norm `‖λ_{j,·}‖_{ℓ_p}` of the coefficients of one level.

Rd.leibnizConst_ne_top.name: Rd.leibnizConst_ne_top
Rd.leibnizConst_ne_top.docstring:
The Leibniz constant of a smooth function with compact support is finite: each derivative
`D^j χ` is continuous with compact support, hence bounded (Mathlib's
`Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support`).

Rd.leibnizConst_add_le.name: Rd.leibnizConst_add_le
Rd.leibnizConst_add_le.docstring:
**The Leibniz constants grow along the induction**: for a smooth `χ` and `‖v‖ ≤ 1`,
`C_k(χ) + C_k(∂_v χ) ≤ C_{k+1}(χ)`, since both suprema are at most
`sup_x ∑_{j ≤ k+1} ‖D^j χ(x)‖` (`Rd.enorm_iteratedFDeriv_fderiv_apply_le`).

Rd.leibnizConst.name: Rd.leibnizConst
Rd.leibnizConst.docstring:
The **Leibniz constant** `C_k(χ) = 2^k sup_x ∑_{j ≤ k} ‖D^j χ(x)‖` of a smooth function `χ`: the
weak derivatives of order `k` of `χ f` are bounded by `C_k(χ)` times the derivatives of `f` of order
at most `k` (`Rd.exists_hasWeakLineDeriv_mul_of_tsupport_subset`).

Rd.le_rpow_half_mul_of_sq_le.name: Rd.le_rpow_half_mul_of_sq_le
Rd.le_rpow_half_mul_of_sq_le.docstring: Taking square roots in `ℝ≥0∞`: `a² ≤ c b²` implies `a ≤ c^(1/2) b`.

Rd.le_of_rpow_le_overlap.name: Rd.le_of_rpow_le_overlap
Rd.le_of_rpow_le_overlap.docstring: From `X^p ≤ N^(p-1) ∑ (b_m |λ_m|)^p` with `b_m ≤ B` to `X ≤ N^(1-1/p) B ‖λ‖_{ℓ_p}`.

Rd.le_of_forall_pos_le_ofReal_mul_of_ten.name: Rd.le_of_forall_pos_le_ofReal_mul_of_tendsto
Rd.le_of_forall_pos_le_ofReal_mul_of_ten.docstring:
**Letting a factor tend to one**: if `a ≤ c(ε) b` for every `ε > 0` and `c(ε) → 1` as
`ε → 0+`, then `a ≤ b`.

Rd.le_mul_triebelLizorkinNormDistr.name: Rd.le_mul_triebelLizorkinNormDistr
Rd.le_mul_triebelLizorkinNormDistr.docstring:
**Bounding by the quasi-norm**: if `x ≤ C ‖ x ↦ ‖(2^{js} |g_j(x)|)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p` for every
family of `L_p` functions `g_j` representing the blocks of `u`, and `C ≠ 0`, then
`x ≤ C ‖u‖_{F^s_{p,q}}` (`Rd.LPKernel.le_mul_kernelTriebelLizorkinNormDistr`).

Rd.le_maximalFunction.name: Rd.le_maximalFunction
Rd.le_maximalFunction.docstring: Every mean over a ball centred at `x` is at most `M g(x)`.

Rd.le_gridLevel.name: Rd.le_gridLevel
Rd.le_gridLevel.docstring: A coordinate is at most the level.

Rd.kernel_le_of_mem_dyadicShell.name: Rd.kernel_le_of_mem_dyadicShell
Rd.kernel_le_of_mem_dyadicShell.docstring:
A kernel with the bound `A` on `B̄(0,ρ)` and the bound `A (ρ/‖y‖)^N` outside is at most
`A 2^(-iN)` on the shell `i`.

Rd.jacksonScale.name: Rd.jacksonScale
Rd.jacksonScale.docstring: The scales `2^k / (l + 1)` of the Jackson approximant.

Rd.jacksonCoeff.name: Rd.jacksonCoeff
Rd.jacksonCoeff.docstring:
The coefficients `a_l = (-1)^l C(r, l + 1)`, `l < r`, of the moment kernels and of the
Jackson approximant: those of `-(-1)^r Δ^r` without its term of order `0`.

Rd.jacksonApprox_mem_bandSpace.name: Rd.jacksonApprox_mem_bandSpace
Rd.jacksonApprox_mem_bandSpace.docstring: **The Jackson approximant is band-limited**: `J_k f ∈ E_k`.

Rd.jacksonApprox.name: Rd.jacksonApprox
Rd.jacksonApprox.docstring: The **Jackson approximant** `J_k f = ∑_{l<r} (-1)^l C(r, l + 1) Φ_{2^k/(l+1)} ⋆ f`.

Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_toLp_eq.name: Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_toLp_eq
Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_toLp_eq.docstring:
The iterated derivative `∂^v` of the `L_p(V)` class of a Schwartz function `η`, as a tempered
distribution, is the `L_r(V)` class of the Schwartz function `∂^v η`, as a tempered
distribution.

Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_testSchwartz.name: Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_testSchwartz
Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_testSchwartz.docstring:
Passing to complex values commutes with iterated directional derivatives:
`∂^v (φ : ℂ) = (∂^v φ : ℂ)`.

Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_shiftReflect.name: Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_shiftReflect
Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_shiftReflect.docstring:
**Iterated derivatives of a reflected translate**: `∂^w` of `y ↦ η(x - y)` is `(-1)^k` times
`y ↦ (∂^w η)(x - y)`, for `w ∈ V^k`.

Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_schwartzReflect.name: Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_schwartzReflect
Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_schwartzReflect.docstring:
**Iterated derivatives of a reflection**: `∂^w (η(-·)) = (-1)^k (∂^w η)(-·)` for
`w ∈ V^k`.

Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_schwartzDilate.name: Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_schwartzDilate
Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_schwartzDilate.docstring:
**Iterated derivatives of dilations**: for directions `w ∈ V^k`,
`∂_{w_0} ⋯ ∂_{w_{k-1}} (G_c) = c^k (∂_{w_0} ⋯ ∂_{w_{k-1}} G)_c`.

Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_ofFun_top_apply.name: Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_ofFun_top_apply
Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_ofFun_top_apply.docstring:
On `Ω = V`, the iterated derivatives of `f ∈ L_p(V)` as a distribution and as a tempered
distribution agree on test functions.

Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_fwdDiffSchwartz.name: Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_fwdDiffSchwartz
Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_fwdDiffSchwartz.docstring: Iterated line derivatives commute with differences.

Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_eq_sum_prod_smul.name: Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_eq_sum_prod_smul
Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_eq_sum_prod_smul.docstring:
**Iterated derivatives are multilinear in the directions**: if
`v_l = ∑_j c_{l,j} b_j` for `l < k`, then
`∂^v T = ∑_{i : Fin k → ι} (∏_l c_{l, i_l}) ∂_{b_{i_0}} ⋯ ∂_{b_{i_{k-1}}} T`, for every `T` in a
space with additive and homogeneous derivatives, such as distributions. By induction on `k`,
with Mathlib's `LineDeriv.lineDerivOp_left_sum` and the splitting of words by `Fin.consEquiv`.

Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_dualLpBlockKernel.name: Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_dualLpBlockKernelS
Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_dualLpBlockKernel.docstring:
**Derivatives of the synthesis kernels**:
`∂^w ψ̃_j = 2^{jk} (∂^w G̃_j)_{2^j}` as functions
(`Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_schwartzDilate` with `c = 2^j`).

Rd.iteratedFDeriv_sub_cutoffMul_eq_zero.name: Rd.iteratedFDeriv_sub_cutoffMul_eq_zero
Rd.iteratedFDeriv_sub_cutoffMul_eq_zero.docstring:
All derivatives of `u - χ_n u` vanish on the open ball of radius `n + 1`, where the cut-off
is `1`.

Rd.iteratedFDeriv_scaledSymbol.name: Rd.iteratedFDeriv_scaledSymbol
Rd.iteratedFDeriv_scaledSymbol.docstring:
**Derivatives of a rescaled symbol**:
`D^k (2^{-jσ} m(2^j ·))(ζ) = 2^{-jσ} 2^{jk} D^k m(2^j ζ)` (Mathlib's
`iteratedFDeriv_comp_const_smul` and `iteratedFDeriv_const_smul_apply'`).

Rd.iteratedFDeriv_conv_apply.name: Rd.iteratedFDeriv_conv_apply
Rd.iteratedFDeriv_conv_apply.docstring:
**Iterated derivatives of a convolution**: for a smooth kernel `K` of compact support and a
locally integrable `g`, `D^n (K ⋆ g)(x)(v) = ((D^n K)(·)(v) ⋆ g)(x)`.

Rd.iteratedFDerivWithin_eq_zero_of_eqOn.name: Rd.iteratedFDerivWithin_eq_zero_of_eqOn
Rd.iteratedFDerivWithin_eq_zero_of_eqOn.docstring:
**Derivatives of a function that vanishes near a point**: if `f = 0` on `s ∩ u` for an open
`u ∋ x`, then the derivatives of `f` within `s` vanish at `x ∈ s`.

Rd.ite_dyadicWeight_ne_top.name: Rd.ite_dyadicWeight_ne_top
Rd.ite_dyadicWeight_ne_top.docstring: The weights `c_{ji} = 2^(-(j-i)L)` for `i ≤ j` and `c_{ji} = 1` for `i > j` are finite.

Rd.isUniformSchwartz_lpBlockKernelBase.name: Rd.isUniformSchwartz_lpBlockKernelBase
Rd.isUniformSchwartz_lpBlockKernelBase.docstring:
The family `lpBlockKernelBase` is uniformly Schwartz with bounds
`Rd.lpBlockKernelBaseBound V`.

Rd.isUniformSchwartz_derivKernel.name: Rd.isUniformSchwartz_derivKernel
Rd.isUniformSchwartz_derivKernel.docstring: The constant family `j ↦ η_i` is uniformly Schwartz with bounds `Rd.derivKernelBound i`.

Rd.isUniformSchwartz_derivDualBase.name: Rd.isUniformSchwartz_derivDualBase
Rd.isUniformSchwartz_derivDualBase.docstring:
The dual derivative bases are uniformly Schwartz with bounds `Rd.derivDualBound w`: they take
the two values of `j = 0` and `j = 2`.

Rd.isSmoothAtom_zero.name: Rd.isSmoothAtom_zero
Rd.isSmoothAtom_zero.docstring: The zero function is a smooth atom.

Rd.isRegularAtom_of_pointwise.name: Rd.isRegularAtom_of_pointwise
Rd.isRegularAtom_of_pointwise.docstring:
**Atoms from pointwise bounds**: a function that vanishes outside `B̄(c, d 2^(-j))` with
`|a| ≤ A` and `|Δ_h^r a| ≤ A min(1, (2^j ‖h‖)^σ)` is a regular atom with the constant
`A ((r + 1) d^n |B_1|)^(1/p)`, the case `Ω = V` of `Rd.isRegularAtomOn_of_pointwise`.

Rd.isRegularAtom_cellAtom.name: Rd.isRegularAtom_cellAtom
Rd.isRegularAtom_cellAtom.docstring:
**Cell atoms are regular atoms** of order and exponent `r`, with radius factor `ρ + n` and the
constant `Rd.cellAtomConst`, for a continuous kernel `K` with `|Δ_h^l K| ≤ A 2^(jn) min(1,
(2^j ‖h‖)^l)` (`l = 0, r`) that vanishes outside `B̄(0, ρ 2^(-j))`.

Rd.isRegularAtomOn_zero.name: Rd.isRegularAtomOn_zero
Rd.isRegularAtomOn_zero.docstring: The zero function is a regular atom on every set at every level.

Rd.isRegularAtomOn_of_pointwise.name: Rd.isRegularAtomOn_of_pointwise
Rd.isRegularAtomOn_of_pointwise.docstring:
**Atoms on `Ω` from pointwise bounds**: a function that vanishes outside `B̄(c, d 2^(-j))`
with `|a| ≤ A` on `Ω` and `|Δ_h^r a(x)| ≤ A min(1, (2^j ‖h‖)^σ)` at the points `x` whose steps stay
in `Ω` is a regular atom on `Ω` with the constant `A ((r + 1) d^n |B_1|)^(1/p)`. The support of
`Δ_h^r a` lies in `r + 1` translated balls.

Rd.isRegularAtomOn_of_isSmoothAtom.name: Rd.isRegularAtomOn_of_isSmoothAtom
Rd.isRegularAtomOn_of_isSmoothAtom.docstring:
**Smooth atoms are regular atoms**: on a measurable convex set `Ω` with nonempty interior, a
smooth atom of order `K` is a regular atom on `Ω` of order and exponent `r` for `1 ≤ r ≤ K`, with
the constant `2^r r^(r+1) A ((r + 1) d^n |B_1|)^(1/p)`.

Rd.isCompact_frontier_of_isBounded.name: Rd.isCompact_frontier_of_isBounded
Rd.isCompact_frontier_of_isBounded.docstring:
In finite dimension the **frontier of a bounded set is compact**: it is a closed subset of the
compact closure (Mathlib's `Bornology.IsBounded.isCompact_closure`).

Rd.isCompactOperator_restr_truncL2.name: Rd.isCompactOperator_restr_truncL2
Rd.isCompactOperator_restr_truncL2.docstring:
**The truncated operators are compact on bounded sets**: for bounded `Ω ⊆ V` and every
`K`, `F ↦ (truncL2 K F)|_Ω` is a compact operator from `H^1(V)` to `L_2(Ω)`. The image of the
unit ball lies in the image, under the Lipschitz map `Rd.closureToLp`, of a set of uniformly
bounded and uniformly Lipschitz functions on the compact set `closure Ω`
(`Rd.restr_truncL2_mem_closureToLp_image`), which is totally bounded by Arzelà–Ascoli
(`Rd.totallyBounded_setOf_lipschitzWith`).

Rd.isClosed_vanishOn.name: Rd.isClosed_vanishOn
Rd.isClosed_vanishOn.docstring:
The elements of `H^s(V)` vanishing on `Ω` form a closed subspace: an intersection of kernels
of the continuous functionals `U ↦ U(φ)` (Mathlib's `ContinuousLinearMap.isClosed_ker`).

Rd.isCZFamily_lpBlockKernel.name: Rd.isCZFamily_lpBlockKernel
Rd.isCZFamily_lpBlockKernel.docstring:
**The blocks form a Calderón–Zygmund family** with overlap `2` and Hörmander constant
`4 H_{A^ψ}`, `H_{A^ψ} = Rd.familyHormanderConst V (Rd.lpBlockKernelBaseBound V)`.

Rd.isCZFamily_divergenceSchwartz.name: Rd.isCZFamily_divergenceSchwartz
Rd.isCZFamily_divergenceSchwartz.docstring:
**The divergence kernels form Calderón–Zygmund families**: if `m` is smooth, vanishes outside
a ball and has vanishing first moment in the direction `w`, the dilates `(K_w)_{2^j}` of the
divergence kernel form a Calderón–Zygmund family (`Rd.integral_divergenceKernel`,
`Rd.isCZFamily_dilate_of_integral_eq_zero`).

Rd.isCZFamily_dilate_of_integral_eq_zero.name: Rd.isCZFamily_dilate_of_integral_eq_zero
Rd.isCZFamily_dilate_of_integral_eq_zero.docstring:
**Dilates of a mean-zero Schwartz function form a Calderón–Zygmund family**: for
`G ∈ 𝓢(V, ℂ)` with `∫ G = 0`, the kernels `G_{2^j}` have the Fourier overlap
`Rd.meanZeroOverlap G` and the Hörmander constant `4 H_G` (`Rd.IsCZFamily.of_dilation` with the
constant family `Rd.IsUniformSchwartz.const`).

Rd.isCZFamily_derivKernelFamily.name: Rd.isCZFamily_derivKernelFamily
Rd.isCZFamily_derivKernelFamily.docstring:
**The derivative families are Calderón–Zygmund families** with overlap `2` and Hörmander
constant `4 H_{A^{η_i}}`, `H_{A^{η_i}} = Rd.familyHormanderConst V (Rd.derivKernelBound i)`.

Rd.isCZFamily_derivDualFamily.name: Rd.isCZFamily_derivDualFamily
Rd.isCZFamily_derivDualFamily.docstring:
**The dual derivative families are Calderón–Zygmund families** with overlap
`4 ((8π)^k ∏_l ‖w_l‖)²` (`Rd.derivDualOverlap`) and Hörmander constant `4 H_{A^w}`,
`H_{A^w} = Rd.familyHormanderConst V (Rd.derivDualBound w)`.

Rd.inv_one_add_two_pow_mul_pow_le.name: Rd.inv_one_add_two_pow_mul_pow_le
Rd.inv_one_add_two_pow_mul_pow_le.docstring:
The tail bound of the Peetre weight: for every `y ≠ 0`,
`(1 + 2^j ‖y‖)^(-N) ≤ (2^(-j)/‖y‖)^N`.

Rd.inv_one_add_mul_enorm_sub_pow_le.name: Rd.inv_one_add_mul_enorm_sub_pow_le
Rd.inv_one_add_mul_enorm_sub_pow_le.docstring:
Peetre's inequality for norms: `(1 + a ‖y - w‖)^(-N) ≤ (1 + a ‖w‖)^N (1 + a ‖y‖)^(-N)` for
`a < ∞`.

Rd.interpolationConst_ne_zero.name: Rd.interpolationConst_ne_zero
Rd.interpolationConst_ne_zero.docstring: `interpolationConst V p q` is positive for `0 < p` and `0 < q`.

Rd.interpolationConst_ne_top.name: Rd.interpolationConst_ne_top
Rd.interpolationConst_ne_top.docstring: `interpolationConst V p q` is finite for `1 < p < q`.

Rd.interpolationConst.name: Rd.interpolationConst
Rd.interpolationConst.docstring:
The constant of the interpolation for `p < q`:
`p (2 C^w_{n,q} / (p - 1) + 2^q C_{n,q} / (q - p))` with `C^w_{n,q} = weakTypeConst V q` and
`C_{n,q} = maximalConst n q`.

Rd.interior_patch_support.name: Rd.interior_patch_support
Rd.interior_patch_support.docstring:
**Interior patches, the support condition**: if the dual kernels vanish outside the ball of
radius `δ`, they see `{infDist(·, Oᶜ) > δ}` from points of `{infDist(·, Oᶜ) > 2δ}`.

Rd.interior_patch_step.name: Rd.interior_patch_step
Rd.interior_patch_step.docstring:
**Interior patches, the step condition**: steps of length at most `δ / L` take
`{infDist(·, Oᶜ) > δ}` into `O_{L h}`.

Rd.inter_frontier_nonempty_of_isPreconne.name: Rd.inter_frontier_nonempty_of_isPreconnected
Rd.inter_frontier_nonempty_of_isPreconne.docstring:
**A preconnected set that meets `U` and its complement meets the frontier of `U`**: otherwise
it would lie in the union of the disjoint open sets `int U` and `X \ cl U`, hence in one of them
(Mathlib's `IsPreconnected.subset_or_subset`), but it has points in `U` and outside `U`.

Rd.integral_weakDeriv_mul_add_eq_zero.name: Rd.integral_weakDeriv_mul_add_eq_zero
Rd.integral_weakDeriv_mul_add_eq_zero.docstring:
**Integration by parts in `H^1(V)`**: for `U, W ∈ H^1(V)` and every direction `v`,
`∫ (∂_v U) W + U ∂_v W = 0`. Both sides are continuous on `H^1(V) × H^1(V)`
(`Rd.continuous_integral_weakDeriv_mul_add`) and the identity holds for Schwartz functions
(`Rd.integral_lineDerivOp_mul_add_eq_zero`), which are dense (`Rd.denseRange_ofSchwartz`).

Rd.integral_testFunction_mul_lineDeriv.name: Rd.integral_testFunction_mul_lineDeriv
Rd.integral_testFunction_mul_lineDeriv.docstring:
**Integration by parts for a Lipschitz function and a test function**: for a Lipschitz
`u : V → ℝ` and every test function `φ` on an open set, `∫ φ ∂_v u = -∫ (∂_v φ) u`, Mathlib's
`LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq` with the Lipschitz function `φ` of compact support
(`ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport`).

Rd.integral_tensorKernel_mul_comp_eq_con.name: Rd.integral_tensorKernel_mul_comp_eq_conv
Rd.integral_tensorKernel_mul_comp_eq_con.docstring:
**Anisotropic substitution** in a tensor integral: for `a_i > 0`,
`∫ (⊗φ)(z) f(x - (a_i z_i)_i) dz = ((⊗ φ_i^{(1/a_i)}) ⋆ f)(x)` with `φ^{(c)}(t) = c φ(c t)`.

Rd.integral_tensorKernel.name: Rd.integral_tensorKernel
Rd.integral_tensorKernel.docstring:
**The integral of a tensor product**: `∫ ⊗K = ∏_i ∫ K_i` (Fubini, Mathlib's
`integral_fintype_prod_eq_prod`).

Rd.integral_smul_indicator_comp_halfSpac.name: Rd.integral_smul_indicator_comp_halfSpaceReflection
Rd.integral_smul_indicator_comp_halfSpac.docstring:
**The reflected half**: for a measurable set `s`,
`∫ c(y) 1_s b (σ y) dy = ∫_s c(σ y) b(y) dy`, since `σ` is an involution that preserves Lebesgue
measure (Mathlib's `MeasurePreserving.integral_comp`).

Rd.integral_smul_indicatorLp_eq_setInteg.name: Rd.integral_smul_indicatorLp_eq_setIntegral_mul
Rd.integral_smul_indicatorLp_eq_setInteg.docstring:
**Testing a zero extension**: for a measurable `s ⊆ V`, `F ∈ L_p(V)`, a real function `φ` and
a function `h` equal to `φ` almost everywhere, `∫_V φ · 1_s F = ∫_s F h`.

Rd.integral_smul_indicator.name: Rd.integral_smul_indicator
Rd.integral_smul_indicator.docstring: Multipliers of a function on a measurable set `s`: `∫ c 1_s b = ∫_s c b`.

Rd.integral_norm_indicator_closedBall_le.name: Rd.integral_norm_indicator_closedBall_le
Rd.integral_norm_indicator_closedBall_le.docstring: **Cauchy–Schwarz on a ball**, in `ℝ`: `∫ |1_{B_K} h| ≤ |B_K|^{1/2} ‖h‖_2` for `h ∈ L_2(V)`.

Rd.integral_momentKernel.name: Rd.integral_momentKernel
Rd.integral_momentKernel.docstring: **The moment kernel has integral `1`**: `∫ m = ∑_{l=1}^L (-1)^(l+1) C(L, l) ∫ g = 1`.

Rd.integral_lpKernel.name: Rd.integral_lpKernel
Rd.integral_lpKernel.docstring: **The Littlewood–Paley kernel has integral `1`**: `∫ Φ = 𝓕Φ(0) = χ_{1,2}(0) = 1`.

Rd.integral_lineDeriv_eq_zero_complex.name: Rd.integral_lineDeriv_eq_zero_complex
Rd.integral_lineDeriv_eq_zero_complex.docstring:
**The complex form**: for a compactly supported Lipschitz `f : F → ℂ`, `∫ ∂_v f = 0`. The
real and imaginary parts of `∂_v f` are almost everywhere the line derivatives of the real and
imaginary parts of `f` (`Rd.ae_re_lineDeriv_eq`, `Rd.ae_im_lineDeriv_eq`), whose integrals vanish
(`Rd.integral_lineDeriv_eq_zero`), and `∂_v f` is integrable (`Rd.integrable_lineDeriv`).

Rd.integral_lineDeriv_eq_zero.name: Rd.integral_lineDeriv_eq_zero
Rd.integral_lineDeriv_eq_zero.docstring:
**The line derivative of a compactly supported Lipschitz function integrates to zero**: for a
Lipschitz `f : F → ℝ` with compact support on a finite-dimensional space with a Haar measure,
`∫ ∂_v f = 0` for every direction `v`. This is Mathlib's integration by parts for Lipschitz
functions (`LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq`) against the constant `1`.

Rd.integral_lineDerivOp_mul_add_eq_zero.name: Rd.integral_lineDerivOp_mul_add_eq_zero
Rd.integral_lineDerivOp_mul_add_eq_zero.docstring:
**Integration by parts for Schwartz functions**: `∫ (∂_v w₁) w₂ + w₁ ∂_v w₂ = 0` for Schwartz
functions `w₁, w₂` (Mathlib's `SchwartzMap.integral_mul_lineDerivOp_right_eq_neg_left`).

Rd.integral_inner_mul_momentKernel_two.name: Rd.integral_inner_mul_momentKernel_two
Rd.integral_inner_mul_momentKernel_two.docstring:
**The moment kernel of order two has vanishing first moments**: for
`m = 2 g - g_{1/2}` (`Rd.momentKernel g 2`) and every `w`, `∫ ⟪w, x⟫ m(x) dx = 0`, since the first
moment of `g_c` is `c⁻¹` times that of `g` (`Rd.integral_inner_mul_dilate`).

Rd.integral_inner_mul_dilate.name: Rd.integral_inner_mul_dilate
Rd.integral_inner_mul_dilate.docstring:
**First moments of a dilate**: `∫ ⟪w, x⟫ m_c(x) dx = c⁻¹ ∫ ⟪w, x⟫ m(x) dx` for `c > 0`
and every additive Haar measure, since `⟪w, x⟫ m_c(x) = c⁻¹ (⟪w, ·⟫ m)_c(x)`
(`Rd.inner_mul_dilate_eq`, `Rd.integral_dilate`).

Rd.integral_higherDiff_eq_zero.name: Rd.integral_higherDiff_eq_zero
Rd.integral_higherDiff_eq_zero.docstring: `∫ Δ_h^r K = 0` for integrable `K` and `r ≥ 1`: a difference integrates to `0`.

Rd.integral_halfSpaceCutoff_smul_eq.name: Rd.integral_halfSpaceCutoff_smul_eq
Rd.integral_halfSpaceCutoff_smul_eq.docstring:
**The weak derivative tested against a cutoff product**: if `g = ∂_w u` weakly on `H₊` and
`χ` is smooth with compact support, then for every `n`
`∫ η_n χ g = -∫ η_n (∂_w χ) u - ∫ (∂_w η_n) χ u`: the product `η_n u` has the weak derivative
`η_n g + (∂_w η_n) u` on `V` (`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.mul_of_tsupport_subset`), tested against
`χ`.

Rd.integral_fourier_smul_eq_of_integrabl.name: Rd.integral_fourier_smul_eq_of_integrable
Rd.integral_fourier_smul_eq_of_integrabl.docstring:
**Duality for the Fourier transform** (the multiplication formula), `∫ 𝓕u · g = ∫ u · 𝓕g`,
for a Schwartz function `u` and an integrable function `g` (`Rd.integral_fourier_mul`).

Rd.integral_fourier_mul.name: Rd.integral_fourier_mul
Rd.integral_fourier_mul.docstring:
**The multiplication formula** `∫ 𝓕f · g = ∫ f · 𝓕g` for integrable `f, g : V → ℂ`: both
sides are the double integral `∫∫ e^(-2πi⟪x, ξ⟫) f(x) g(ξ) dx dξ` (Fubini, Mathlib's
`VectorFourier.integral_bilin_fourierIntegral_eq_flip` with the product as bilinear form).

Rd.integral_fourierInv_smul_eq_of_integr.name: Rd.integral_fourierInv_smul_eq_of_integrable
Rd.integral_fourierInv_smul_eq_of_integr.docstring:
**Duality for the inverse Fourier transform** (the multiplication formula),
`∫ 𝓕⁻u · g = ∫ u · 𝓕⁻g`, for a Schwartz function `u` and an integrable function `g`
(`Rd.integral_fourierInv_mul`).

Rd.integral_fourierInv_mul.name: Rd.integral_fourierInv_mul
Rd.integral_fourierInv_mul.docstring:
**The multiplication formula for the inverse transform** `∫ 𝓕⁻f · g = ∫ f · 𝓕⁻g` for
integrable `f, g : V → ℂ` (the pairing `-⟪ξ, x⟫` in Mathlib's
`VectorFourier.integral_bilin_fourierIntegral_eq_flip`).

Rd.integral_divergenceKernel.name: Rd.integral_divergenceKernel
Rd.integral_divergenceKernel.docstring:
**The divergence kernels have mean zero** if the first moments of `m` vanish:
`∫ K_w = ∫_0^{log 2} ∫ ⟪w, x⟫ m_{e^s}(x) dx ds = ∫_0^{log 2} e^{-s} ∫ ⟪w, x⟫ m(x) dx ds = 0`
(Fubini, Mathlib's `integral_integral_swap`, and `Rd.integral_inner_mul_dilate`).

Rd.integral_dilate.name: Rd.integral_dilate
Rd.integral_dilate.docstring:
**The dilation keeps the integral**: `∫ Φ_c = ∫ Φ` for `c > 0` (Mathlib's
`Measure.integral_comp_smul`).

Rd.integral_czBadPart.name: Rd.integral_czBadPart
Rd.integral_czBadPart.docstring:
**The bad pieces have mean zero**: `∫ czBadPart_Q f = 0` for every function `f : V → E` and
every cube `Q`. For `f` not integrable on `Q`, or `E` not complete, both the mean and the
integral are `0` by convention.

Rd.integral_conv_mul_conj.name: Rd.integral_conv_mul_conj
Rd.integral_conv_mul_conj.docstring:
**The adjoint identity with conjugation**: for integrable `K`, `f ∈ L_p` and `g ∈ L_q` with
`1/p + 1/q = 1`, `p < ∞`, `∫ (K ⋆ f) conj g = ∫ f conj(K^* ⋆ g)` with the adjoint kernel
`K^*(z) = conj K(-z)` (`Rd.integral_conv_mul` for `conj g` and `Rd.conv_reflectNeg_conj`).

Rd.integral_conv_mul.name: Rd.integral_conv_mul
Rd.integral_conv_mul.docstring:
**The adjoint identity for convolutions**: for integrable `K`, `f ∈ L_p` and `g ∈ L_q` with
`1/p + 1/q = 1`, `p < ∞`, and the reflection `K^∨(x) = K(-x)`,
`∫ (K ⋆ f)(x) g(x) dx = ∫ f(y) (K^∨ ⋆ g)(y) dy`. Both sides are the integral of
`K(x - y) f(y) g(x)` over `V × V` (`Rd.integrable_kernel_mul_mul`, Fubini's theorem in the form
of Mathlib's `integral_integral_swap`).

Rd.integral_conv_lineDerivOp_mul.name: Rd.integral_conv_lineDerivOp_mul
Rd.integral_conv_lineDerivOp_mul.docstring:
**A derivative moves from the kernel `η` to the Schwartz function `u`**: for Schwartz
functions `η`, `u`, `f ∈ L_p` with `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `v ∈ V`,
`∫ ((∂_v η) ⋆ f) u = -∫ (η ⋆ f) ∂_v u`. Both sides are pairings of `f` with reflected
convolutions (`Rd.integral_conv_mul`, with the conjugate exponent of `p` and Schwartz functions
in every `L_q`), and these agree up to the sign (`Rd.conv_reflectNeg_lineDerivOp`).

Rd.integral_conv_iteratedLineDerivOp_mul.name: Rd.integral_conv_iteratedLineDerivOp_mul
Rd.integral_conv_iteratedLineDerivOp_mul.docstring:
**Iterated derivatives move from the kernel `η` to the Schwartz function `u`**: for Schwartz
functions `η`, `u`, `f ∈ L_p` with `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `w ∈ V^k`,
`∫ ((∂^w η) ⋆ f) u = (-1)^k ∫ (η ⋆ f) ∂^w u`, by induction on `k` from
`Rd.integral_conv_lineDerivOp_mul`.

Rd.integral_comp_diagMap.name: Rd.integral_comp_diagMap
Rd.integral_comp_diagMap.docstring:
**Diagonal changes of variables**: for `a_i > 0`,
`∫ F((a_i z_i)_i) dz = (∏_i a_i)⁻¹ ∫ F` (Mathlib's
`Real.map_linearMap_volume_pi_eq_smul_volume_pi`).

Rd.integral_bumpMollifier.name: Rd.integral_bumpMollifier
Rd.integral_bumpMollifier.docstring: The mollifier of a bump function has integral `1` (Mathlib's `ContDiffBump.integral_normed`).

Rd.integral_besselSchwartz_mul_conv.name: Rd.integral_besselSchwartz_mul_conv
Rd.integral_besselSchwartz_mul_conv.docstring:
**`J_t` moves through a convolution, tested**: for `F ∈ L_p(V)`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, and Schwartz
functions `η`, `u`, `∫ J_t u · (η ⋆ F) = ∫ u · ((J_t η) ⋆ F)`. Both sides are pairings of `F`
with reflected convolutions (`Rd.integral_conv_mul`), and
`∫ η(z - y) J_t u(z) dz = ∫ (J_t η)(z - y) u(z) dz` by the symmetry of `J_t` and its commuting
with translations (`Rd.integral_besselSchwartz_mul`, `Rd.besselSchwartz_compSubConstCLM`).

Rd.integral_besselSchwartz_mul.name: Rd.integral_besselSchwartz_mul
Rd.integral_besselSchwartz_mul.docstring:
**`J_t` is symmetric on Schwartz functions**: `∫ J_t φ · u = ∫ φ · J_t u` for Schwartz
functions `φ`, `u`. Both sides are `(J_t φ)(u)` for the tempered distribution of `φ`
(`Rd.besselPotential_apply_apply`, `Rd.besselPotential_schwartz`).

Rd.integrable_translate_mul_of_locallyIn.name: Rd.integrable_translate_mul_of_locallyIntegrable
Rd.integrable_translate_mul_of_locallyIn.docstring:
The convolution integrals of a continuous kernel with compact support and a locally integrable
function converge absolutely.

Rd.integrable_tensorKernel.name: Rd.integrable_tensorKernel
Rd.integrable_tensorKernel.docstring: Tensor products of integrable kernels are integrable (Mathlib's `Integrable.fintype_prod`).

Rd.integrable_smul_of_forall_notMem.name: Rd.integrable_smul_of_forall_notMem
Rd.integrable_smul_of_forall_notMem.docstring:
**Multipliers supported in a set**: if moreover `c` vanishes outside the measurable set `s`,
then `c b` is integrable on `V` (`Rd.integrableOn_smul_of_hasCompactSupport`).

Rd.integrable_smul_indicator_comp_halfSp.name: Rd.integrable_smul_indicator_comp_halfSpaceReflection
Rd.integrable_smul_indicator_comp_halfSp.docstring:
Compactly supported multipliers of `1_s b ∘ σ` are integrable when `b` is integrable on every
bounded part of the measurable set `s`: compose with the measure-preserving `σ`.

Rd.integrable_smul_indicator.name: Rd.integrable_smul_indicator
Rd.integrable_smul_indicator.docstring:
Compactly supported multipliers of `1_s b` are integrable when `b` is integrable on every
bounded part of the measurable set `s` (`Rd.integrableOn_smul_of_hasCompactSupport`).

Rd.integrable_of_norm_le_of_forall_norm_.name: Rd.integrable_of_norm_le_of_forall_norm_gt_eq_zero
Rd.integrable_of_norm_le_of_forall_norm_.docstring:
**Bounded functions vanishing outside a ball are integrable**: on a proper normed group with
a measure that is finite on compact sets, an a.e. strongly measurable `f` with `‖f x‖ ≤ C` for
every `x` and `f x = 0` for `‖x‖ > R` is integrable.

Rd.integrable_mul_sub_of_enorm_le.name: Rd.integrable_mul_sub_of_enorm_le
Rd.integrable_mul_sub_of_enorm_le.docstring:
**The convolution integrand of an integrable bounded kernel and an `L_p` function is
integrable**: for `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, an integrable `K` with `|K| ≤ B < ∞`, `f ∈ L_p(V)` and every `x`,
`y ↦ K(y) f(x - y)` is integrable, by Hölder's inequality (Mathlib's `MemLp.integrable_mul`) with
`K ∈ L_{p'}`, since `K ∈ L_1 ∩ L_∞` (`MeasureTheory.MemLp.mono_exponent_of_enorm_le`).

Rd.integrable_momentKernel.name: Rd.integrable_momentKernel
Rd.integrable_momentKernel.docstring: Moment kernels of integrable functions are integrable.

Rd.integrable_mixedLpBlockKernel.name: Rd.integrable_mixedLpBlockKernel
Rd.integrable_mixedLpBlockKernel.docstring: The tensor Littlewood–Paley kernels are integrable.

Rd.integrable_mixedDilatedBandKernel.name: Rd.integrable_mixedDilatedBandKernel
Rd.integrable_mixedDilatedBandKernel.docstring: The tensor band-limiting kernels are integrable.

Rd.integrable_mixedDiff.name: Rd.integrable_mixedDiff
Rd.integrable_mixedDiff.docstring: Mixed differences of integrable functions are integrable.

Rd.integrable_lpMomentScaled.name: Rd.integrable_lpMomentScaled
Rd.integrable_lpMomentScaled.docstring: The dilated moment kernels of `Φ` are integrable.

Rd.integrable_lineDeriv.name: Rd.integrable_lineDeriv
Rd.integrable_lineDeriv.docstring:
**The line derivative of a compactly supported Lipschitz function is integrable**: it is
measurable (Mathlib's `aestronglyMeasurable_lineDeriv`), bounded by `C ‖v‖`
(`norm_lineDeriv_le_of_lipschitz`) and zero outside the closed support of `f`.

Rd.integrable_kernel_mul_mul.name: Rd.integrable_kernel_mul_mul
Rd.integrable_kernel_mul_mul.docstring:
**The double integrand of the adjoint identity is integrable**: for integrable `K`,
`f ∈ L_p` and `g ∈ L_q` with `1/p + 1/q = 1`, `p < ∞`, the function
`(x, y) ↦ K(x - y) f(y) g(x)` is integrable on `V × V`. For almost every `x` the inner integral
converges (Young's inequality, `MeasureTheory.ae_convolutionExistsAt`), and
`x ↦ ∫ |K(x - y)| |f(y)| dy |g(x)|` is the product of the convolution `|K| ⋆ |f| ∈ L_p` with
`|g| ∈ L_q`, integrable by Hölder's inequality (Mathlib's `MemLp.integrable_mul`).

Rd.integrable_inner_mul_dilate_exp.name: Rd.integrable_inner_mul_dilate_exp
Rd.integrable_inner_mul_dilate_exp.docstring:
The integrand `(x, s) ↦ ⟪w, x⟫ m_{e^s}(x)` of the dilation average is integrable on
`V × (0, c]` if `m` is continuous and vanishes outside a ball: it is continuous and vanishes
outside the compact set `B̄(0, R) × [0, c]`.

Rd.integrable_indicator_closedBall.name: Rd.integrable_indicator_closedBall
Rd.integrable_indicator_closedBall.docstring: A function `h ∈ L_2(V)` cut off to a ball is integrable.

Rd.integrable_higherDiff.name: Rd.integrable_higherDiff
Rd.integrable_higherDiff.docstring: Differences of integrable functions are integrable.

Rd.integrable_fourier_lpKernel.name: Rd.integrable_fourier_lpKernel
Rd.integrable_fourier_lpKernel.docstring: The Fourier transform of the Littlewood–Paley kernel is integrable.

Rd.integrable_fourier_lpBlockKernel.name: Rd.integrable_fourier_lpBlockKernel
Rd.integrable_fourier_lpBlockKernel.docstring: The Fourier transforms of the blocks are integrable.

Rd.integrable_fourier_dilatedLpKernel.name: Rd.integrable_fourier_dilatedLpKernel
Rd.integrable_fourier_dilatedLpKernel.docstring: The Fourier transforms of the dilated kernels are integrable.

Rd.integrable_fourier_dilatedBandKernel.name: Rd.integrable_fourier_dilatedBandKernel
Rd.integrable_fourier_dilatedBandKernel.docstring: The Fourier transforms of the dilated kernels are integrable.

Rd.integrable_fourier_dilate.name: Rd.integrable_fourier_dilate
Rd.integrable_fourier_dilate.docstring: The Fourier transform of a dilation is integrable if that of the function is.

Rd.integrable_fourier_bandKernel.name: Rd.integrable_fourier_bandKernel
Rd.integrable_fourier_bandKernel.docstring: The Fourier transform of the band-limiting kernel is integrable.

Rd.integrable_dilate.name: Rd.integrable_dilate
Rd.integrable_dilate.docstring: Dilations of integrable functions are integrable.

Rd.integrable_czGoodC.name: Rd.integrable_czGoodC
Rd.integrable_czGoodC.docstring: The signed good part of an integrable function is integrable.

Rd.integrable_czBadPart.name: Rd.integrable_czBadPart
Rd.integrable_czBadPart.docstring: A bad piece of a function that is integrable on its cube is integrable.

Rd.integrable_czBadC.name: Rd.integrable_czBadC
Rd.integrable_czBadC.docstring: The bad part of an integrable function is integrable.

Rd.integrable_conv.name: Rd.integrable_conv
Rd.integrable_conv.docstring:
Convolutions of integrable functions are integrable (Mathlib's
`Integrable.integrable_convolution`).

Rd.integrable_comp_diag.name: Rd.integrable_comp_diag
Rd.integrable_comp_diag.docstring: Diagonal changes of variables keep integrability.

Rd.integrable_comp_add_smul.name: Rd.integrable_comp_add_smul
Rd.integrable_comp_add_smul.docstring:
A continuous compactly supported function restricted to a line in the direction of a unit
vector is integrable on `ℝ`.

Rd.integrableOn_smul_of_hasCompactSuppor.name: Rd.integrableOn_smul_of_hasCompactSupport
Rd.integrableOn_smul_of_hasCompactSuppor.docstring:
**Compactly supported multipliers**: for a measurable set `s`, if `b` is integrable on every
bounded part `s ∩ B(0, R)` of `s` and `c` is continuous with compact support, then `c b` is
integrable on `s`: `c` is bounded (Mathlib's `Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support`) and
vanishes outside some ball.

Rd.integrableOn_inter_ball_of_memLp.name: Rd.integrableOn_inter_ball_of_memLp
Rd.integrableOn_inter_ball_of_memLp.docstring:
**`L_p` functions on a set are integrable on its bounded parts**: for `1 ≤ p` and every set
`s`, every `u ∈ L_p(s)` is integrable on `s ∩ B(0, R)`, a set of finite measure (Mathlib's
`MemLp.integrable`).

Rd.inner_toLp_besselSchwartz.name: Rd.inner_toLp_besselSchwartz
Rd.inner_toLp_besselSchwartz.docstring:
**`J_t` of a real Schwartz function against `L_2`**: for a Schwartz function `u` with real
values and `g ∈ L_2(V)`, `⟪J_t u, g⟫_{L_2} = (J_t g)(u)`: the inner product is
`∫ conj (J_t u) · g`, and `J_t u` is real (`Rd.conj_besselSchwartz_apply`,
`Rd.besselPotential_toLp_apply`).

Rd.inner_ofTest_toLp.name: Rd.inner_ofTest_toLp
Rd.inner_ofTest_toLp.docstring:
**Test functions against `L_2`**: for a test function `φ` of `Ω`, as an element of `H^t(V)`,
and `g ∈ L_2(V)`, `⟪J_t φ, g⟫_{L_2} = (J_t g)(φ)` (`Rd.inner_toLp_besselSchwartz`).

Rd.inner_ofTest_left.name: Rd.inner_ofTest_left
Rd.inner_ofTest_left.docstring:
**Inner products with a test function in the left slot**: for a test function `φ` of `Ω` and
`U ∈ H^t(V)`, `⟪φ, U⟫_{H^t} = (J_t (J_t U))(φ)`, the distribution `J_t` of the `L_2` function
`J_t U` at `φ` (`Rd.inner_ofTest_toLp`).

Rd.inner_halfSpaceReflection.name: Rd.inner_halfSpaceReflection
Rd.inner_halfSpaceReflection.docstring: **The reflection reverses the height**: `⟪σ y, e⟫ = -⟪y, e⟫` for a unit vector `e`.

Rd.inner_foldHalfSpace.name: Rd.inner_foldHalfSpace
Rd.inner_foldHalfSpace.docstring: `⟪F x, e⟫ = |⟪x, e⟫|` for the folding `F`.

Rd.indicator_diffStepSet_neg.name: Rd.indicator_diffStepSet_neg
Rd.indicator_diffStepSet_neg.docstring:
**Restricted differences with a negative step**:
`Δ_{-h}^r(f, x, U) = (-1)^r Δ_h^r(f, x - r h, U)`, from `Rd.higherDiff_neg`.

Rd.indicator_diffStepSet_higherDiff_indi.name: Rd.indicator_diffStepSet_higherDiff_indicator
Rd.indicator_diffStepSet_higherDiff_indi.docstring:
**Restricted differences use only the values on `U`**:
`1_{U_{rh}} Δ_h^r (1_U f) = 1_{U_{rh}} Δ_h^r f`.

Rd.indicator_ball_add_smul_le.name: Rd.indicator_ball_add_smul_le
Rd.indicator_ball_add_smul_le.docstring:
**A point of a moving ball**: for `l ≥ 0`, a step `v ∈ B(0,a)` and points `x, w`,
`1_{B(x + l v, ρ)}(w) G(w) ≤ 1_{B(x, ρ + l a)}(w) G(w) 1_T(v)` with
`T = {v' : dist(w, x + l v') < ρ}`: a point `w` of the ball `B(x + l v, ρ)` lies in
`B(x, ρ + l a)` by the triangle inequality, and `v ∈ T` by definition.

Rd.indicatorLp_sum_eq_of_partition.name: Rd.indicatorLp_sum_eq_of_partition
Rd.indicatorLp_sum_eq_of_partition.docstring:
**Pasting with a resolution of unity agrees with `f` on `O`**: if `∑_i ψ_i = 1` on `O`,
`ψ_i` vanishes outside `U_i`, `G_i = ψ_i F_i` almost everywhere and `F_i = f` almost everywhere
on `O ∩ U_i`, then `∑_i G_i = f` almost everywhere on `O`.

Rd.indicatorLp_eq_iff_ae_eq_restrict.name: Rd.indicatorLp_eq_iff_ae_eq_restrict
Rd.indicatorLp_eq_iff_ae_eq_restrict.docstring:
Two elements of `L_p` have the same restriction `1_s F = 1_s f` to a measurable set `s` iff
they agree almost everywhere on `s`: Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.ae_eq_restrict_iff_indicator_ae_eq`
for the classes in `L_p`.

Rd.indicatorLp_convLp_indicatorLp.name: Rd.indicatorLp_convLp_indicatorLp
Rd.indicatorLp_convLp_indicatorLp.docstring:
**The support principle for two sets on `L_p`**: `1_U (k ⋆ (1_W h)) = 1_U (k ⋆ h)` if
`x - y ∈ W` for `x ∈ U` and `k(y) ≠ 0`.

Rd.indicatorLp_congr_set.name: Rd.indicatorLp_congr_set
Rd.indicatorLp_congr_set.docstring: The cut-offs to almost equal sets agree.

Rd.indicatorLp_apply_ae.name: Rd.indicatorLp_apply_ae
Rd.indicatorLp_apply_ae.docstring: Multiplication by an indicator is multiplication by the indicator, almost everywhere.

Rd.indicatorLp.name: Rd.indicatorLp
Rd.indicatorLp.docstring:
**Multiplication by the indicator of a measurable set** as an operator on `L_p` of norm at
most `1`.

Rd.indicatorExtendLp_apply_ae.name: Rd.indicatorExtendLp_apply_ae
Rd.indicatorExtendLp_apply_ae.docstring: The extension by zero is `1_T g` almost everywhere.

Rd.indicatorExtendLp.name: Rd.indicatorExtendLp
Rd.indicatorExtendLp.docstring:
**Extension by zero** from `L_p(μ|_O)` to `L_p(μ)` on a measurable `T ⊆ O`: the operator
`g ↦ 1_T g` of norm at most `1`.

Rd.iUnion_zcell.name: Rd.iUnion_zcell
Rd.iUnion_zcell.docstring: The cubes of one level cover the space.

Rd.iUnion_dyadicShell.name: Rd.iUnion_dyadicShell
Rd.iUnion_dyadicShell.docstring:
The shells **cover** `V`: a point with `‖y‖ ≥ ρ` lies in the shell `i` with
`2^i ≤ ‖y‖/ρ < 2^(i+1)`.

Rd.iUnion_dyadicCell.name: Rd.iUnion_dyadicCell
Rd.iUnion_dyadicCell.docstring: The cells of one level cover the space.

Rd.iSup_enorm_lt_top_of_bddAbove.name: Rd.iSup_enorm_lt_top_of_bddAbove
Rd.iSup_enorm_lt_top_of_bddAbove.docstring:
**A bounded function has a finite supremum in `[0, ∞]`**: if the norms `‖K y‖` are bounded
above, then `sup_y ‖K y‖ₑ < ∞` (Mathlib's `ENNReal.iSup_coe_lt_top`). This is the constant `B` of
the pointwise bound of convolutions with a bounded kernel.

Rd.iSup_enorm_bandKernel_lt_top.name: Rd.iSup_enorm_bandKernel_lt_top
Rd.iSup_enorm_bandKernel_lt_top.docstring: The supremum `sup |Θ|` of the band-limiting kernel is finite (`Rd.bddAbove_bandKernel`).

Rd.hyperbolicSum.name: Rd.hyperbolicSum
Rd.hyperbolicSum.docstring:
The **hyperbolic cross partial sum** `S_N f = ∑_{|k|_1 ≤ N} δ_k ⋆ f`, band-limited to the union
of the dyadic rectangles of the blocks with `|k|_1 ≤ N`.

Rd.hyperbolicCrossConst_ne_top.name: Rd.hyperbolicCrossConst_ne_top
Rd.hyperbolicCrossConst_ne_top.docstring:
The constant of hyperbolic cross approximation is finite for `s > 0` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`
(`Rd.tsum_dyadicWeight_mul_rpow_ne_top` with `a = (d-1)(1-1/q) ≥ 0`).

Rd.hyperbolicCrossConst.name: Rd.hyperbolicCrossConst
Rd.hyperbolicCrossConst.docstring:
The **constant of hyperbolic cross approximation**,
`C(d, s, q) = ∑_l 2^(-sl) (l + 1)^((d-1)(1-1/q)) ∈ [0, ∞]`.

Rd.hormanderConst_le_familyHormanderCons.name: Rd.hormanderConst_le_familyHormanderConst
Rd.hormanderConst_le_familyHormanderCons.docstring: Every member of a uniform family has Hörmander constant at most that of the family.

Rd.hormanderConst.name: Rd.hormanderConst
Rd.hormanderConst.docstring:
The **Hörmander constant** `M_G + 2 T_G` of a Schwartz function `G`, with the gradient mass
`M_G = Rd.gradMassConst G` and the tail constant `T_G = Rd.tailConst G 0 1`.

Rd.higherDiff_tsum_apply.name: Rd.higherDiff_tsum_apply
Rd.higherDiff_tsum_apply.docstring:
Differences of a pointwise convergent sum are the sums of the differences, if the sums
converge at all the points of the difference.

Rd.higherDiff_single_tensorKernel.name: Rd.higherDiff_single_tensorKernel
Rd.higherDiff_single_tensorKernel.docstring:
**Differences of order `L` in coordinate `i` of a tensor product** act on the `i`-th
factor.

Rd.higherDiff_neg.name: Rd.higherDiff_neg
Rd.higherDiff_neg.docstring:
**Negative steps**: `Δ_{-h}^r f(x) = (-1)^r Δ_h^r f(x - r h)`, by reflecting the sum
`∑_{l ≤ r} (-1)^(r-l) C(r, l) f(x + l h)` at `l ↦ r - l`.

Rd.higherDiff_mul.name: Rd.higherDiff_mul
Rd.higherDiff_mul.docstring:
**Leibniz's rule for differences**:
`Δ_h^r(u v)(x) = ∑_{l ≤ r} C(r, l) Δ_h^l u(x) Δ_h^(r-l) v(x + l h)`, by induction from
`Δ_h(u v)(x) = Δ_h u(x) v(x + h) + u(x) Δ_h v(x)` and Pascal's rule.

Rd.higherDiff_def.name: Rd.higherDiff_def
Rd.higherDiff_def.docstring: The difference of order `r` is the `r`-th iterate of `fwdDiff h`.

Rd.higherDiff_conv_apply.name: Rd.higherDiff_conv_apply
Rd.higherDiff_conv_apply.docstring:
**Differences of convolutions**: `Δ_h^r (K ⋆ g) = (Δ_h^r K) ⋆ g` where the convolutions with
the translates of `K` converge absolutely.

Rd.higherDiff_conv_ae.name: Rd.higherDiff_conv_ae
Rd.higherDiff_conv_ae.docstring:
**Differences of convolutions**: `Δ_h^r (K ⋆ f) = (Δ_h^r K) ⋆ f` almost everywhere, for an
integrable `K` and `f ∈ L_p`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`.

Rd.higherDiff_congr_ae.name: Rd.higherDiff_congr_ae
Rd.higherDiff_congr_ae.docstring: Differences of functions that agree almost everywhere agree almost everywhere.

Rd.higherDiff_comp_add.name: Rd.higherDiff_comp_add
Rd.higherDiff_comp_add.docstring: **Differences commute with translations**: `Δ_h^r (f(· + c)) = (Δ_h^r f)(· + c)`.

Rd.higherDiff_apply.name: Rd.higherDiff_apply
Rd.higherDiff_apply.docstring:
`Δ_h^r f(x) = ∑_{l ≤ r} (-1)^(r-l) C(r, l) f(x + l h)` (Mathlib's
`fwdDiff_iter_eq_sum_shift`).

Rd.higherDiff.name: Rd.higherDiff
Rd.higherDiff.docstring:
The **difference of order `r`** with step `h`: `Δ_h^r f = (Δ_h)^r f`, the `r`-th iterate of
Mathlib's forward difference `fwdDiff h`.

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_zero.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_zero
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_zero.docstring: The weak derivative of the zero function is zero.

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_weakDerivL2Linear.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_weakDerivL2Linear
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_weakDerivL2Linear.docstring: `weakDerivL2Linear v U` is the weak derivative `∂_v` of the `L_2` function of `U`.

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_weakDerivL2.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_weakDerivL2
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_weakDerivL2.docstring: `weakDerivL2 v U` is the weak derivative `∂_v` on `V` of the `L_2` function of `U`.

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_top_iff.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_top_iff
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_top_iff.docstring:
**Weak derivatives on `V` are derivatives of tempered distributions**: for `f ∈ L_p(V)` and
`g ∈ L_r(V)`, `1 ≤ p, r`, `g` is the weak derivative `∂^v f` on `V` iff `∂^v f = g` in
`𝓢'(V, ℂ)`. One direction tests with the Schwartz functions `Rd.testSchwartz φ`; the other uses
that tempered distributions are determined by test functions (`Rd.eq_zero_of_testSchwartz`).

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_sum_conv_dualLpBlock.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_sum_conv_dualLpBlockKernel
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_sum_conv_dualLpBlock.docstring:
**The partial sums are weak derivatives**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `w ∈ V^k` and `f ∈ L_p(V)`,
`Rd.derivSynthesisSum w f J` is the weak derivative `∂^w` of the reproducing sum
`∑_{j < J} ψ̃_j ⋆ (ψ_j ⋆ f)` on `V` (`Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_conv` for each term,
`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.sum`).

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_schwartz.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_schwartz
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_schwartz.docstring:
**Schwartz functions**: on every open set `Ω`, the classical iterated derivative `∂^v η` of a
Schwartz function `η` is its weak derivative.

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_lipschitzWith.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_lipschitzWith
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_lipschitzWith.docstring:
**Lipschitz functions are weakly differentiable**: for a Lipschitz `f : V → ℂ`, the almost
everywhere line derivative `∂_v f` (Mathlib's `lineDeriv`) is the weak derivative of `f` on every
open set, for every direction `v`. The real and imaginary parts are almost everywhere the line
derivatives of `Re f` and `Im f` (`Rd.ae_re_lineDeriv_eq`, `Rd.ae_im_lineDeriv_eq`), and
`Rd.integral_testFunction_mul_lineDeriv` integrates by parts.

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_gridBasis_words.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_gridBasis_words
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_gridBasis_words.docstring:
**Weak derivatives along all directions from the words**: if `g_w = ∂^{e_w} f` weakly on `Ω`
for every word `w` of length `k`, then for all directions `v ∈ V^k`,
`∑_w ∏_l ⟪v_l, e_{w_l}⟫ g_w = ∂^v f` weakly on `Ω`
(`Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_eq_sum_prod_smul` with `v_l = ∑_j ⟪v_l, e_j⟫ e_j`, Mathlib's
`OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr'`).

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_forall_isCompact.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_forall_isCompact
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_forall_isCompact.docstring:
**Local-to-global for weak derivatives**: if every compact `K ⊆ U` lies in an open `U'` on
which `G = ∂^v F` weakly, then `G = ∂^v F` weakly on `U`. A test function on `U` is a test
function on such a `U'` containing its closed support; local integrability is checked near the
points of `U`.

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_forall_gridBasis.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_forall_gridBasis
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_forall_gridBasis.docstring:
**All directions from the basis**: if `g_i = ∂_{e_i} f` weakly on `Ω` for the basis vectors
`e_i` of `Rd.gridBasis`, then `∑_i ⟪v, e_i⟫ g_i = ∂_v f` weakly on `Ω` for every `v ∈ V`
(`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.sum_smul_dir` with `v = ∑_i ⟪v, e_i⟫ e_i`, Mathlib's
`OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr'`).

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_mulLp.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_mulLp
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_mulLp.docstring:
**The product rule in `L_p(V)`**: if `G = ∂_w F` weakly on `V` and `χ` is a smooth real
function, bounded with its derivative `∂_w χ` (bounds `C`, `C'`), then `χ G + (∂_w χ) F` is the weak
derivative `∂_w (χ F)` on `V`, with the products `Rd.mulLp` in `L_p(V)`
(`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.mul_contDiff`).

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_iff_integral.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_iff_integral
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_iff_integral.docstring:
**Weak derivatives by integration by parts**: for locally integrable `f`, `g` on `Ω`, `g` is
the weak derivative `∂^v f` on `Ω` iff `∫ φ g = (-1)^k ∫ (∂^v φ) f` for every test function `φ`
on `Ω`.

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_fin_zero.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_fin_zero
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_fin_zero.docstring:
The derivative of order zero: a locally integrable `f` is its own weak derivative along the
empty family of directions.

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_evenReflection_of_fo.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_evenReflection_of_forall
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_evenReflection_of_fo.docstring:
**The even reflection is weakly differentiable** (Brezis 2011, Chapter 9; Evans–Gariepy,
Section 4.4): let `e` be a unit vector, `u` and its weak derivatives `g_w = ∂_w u` on `H₊`
integrable on every bounded part `H₊ ∩ B(0, R)` of `H₊`. Then for every `v ∈ V` the function
`y ↦ 1_{H₊} g_v (y) + 1_{H₊} g_{σ v} (σ y)` is the weak derivative `∂_v` of the even reflection
`E u` on `V`. Tested against `φ`, both sides are integrals over `H₊` after the change of
variables `y ↦ σ y` (`Rd.integral_smul_indicator_comp_halfSpaceReflection`), and they agree by
the integration by parts of `Rd.setIntegral_openHalfSpace_smul_add_eq` with `χ_1 = φ` and
`χ_2 = φ ∘ σ`, whose boundary term vanishes by
`Rd.abs_inner_mul_add_inner_halfSpaceReflection_mul_le`.

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_conv.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_conv
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_conv.docstring:
**The weak derivative of a convolution**: for `f ∈ L_p(V)`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, a Schwartz function
`η` and `v ∈ V^k`, `(∂^v η) ⋆ f` is the weak derivative `∂^v (η ⋆ f)` on `V`. Tested with `φ`,
this is `∫ ((∂^v η) ⋆ f) φ = (-1)^k ∫ (η ⋆ f) ∂^v φ`
(`Rd.integral_conv_iteratedLineDerivOp_mul`); both convolutions lie in `L_p` by Young's
inequality and are locally integrable.

Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_comp_of_contDiff.name: Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_comp_of_contDiff
Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_comp_of_contDiff.docstring:
**Smooth functions after a Lipschitz map**: for a smooth `u` with compact support and a
Lipschitz `Φ`, the weak derivative of `u ∘ Φ` on every open set along `v` is
`x ↦ ∑_i ⟪DΦ(x) v, e_i⟫ Du(Φ x) e_i`: `u ∘ Φ` is Lipschitz
(`Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_lipschitzWith`), and `Rd.lineDeriv_comp_eq_sum` holds where `Φ` is
differentiable, almost everywhere by Rademacher's theorem.

Rd.hasTemperateGrowth_scaledSymbol.name: Rd.hasTemperateGrowth_scaledSymbol
Rd.hasTemperateGrowth_scaledSymbol.docstring:
With `m`, every rescaled symbol has temperate growth: it is a constant times `m` composed
with the linear map `ζ ↦ 2^j ζ`.

Rd.hasTemperateGrowth_besselWeight.name: Rd.hasTemperateGrowth_besselWeight
Rd.hasTemperateGrowth_besselWeight.docstring:
The Bessel weight is smooth with polynomially bounded derivatives, so it multiplies tempered
distributions.

Rd.hasTemperateGrowth_besselSymbol.name: Rd.hasTemperateGrowth_besselSymbol
Rd.hasTemperateGrowth_besselSymbol.docstring:
For `ε > 0` the shifted Bessel symbol has temperate growth: it is a constant times
Mathlib's Bessel symbol composed with a dilation (`Rd.besselSymbol_eq_mul`,
Mathlib's `Function.hasTemperateGrowth_one_add_norm_sq_rpow`).

Rd.hasSymbolGrowth_one_add_norm_sq_rpow.name: Rd.hasSymbolGrowth_one_add_norm_sq_rpow
Rd.hasSymbolGrowth_one_add_norm_sq_rpow.docstring:
**Powers of the Japanese bracket are symbols**: `ξ ↦ (1 + ‖ξ‖²)^r` is a symbol of order
`2r` (`Rd.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_one_add_norm_sq_rpow_le`).

Rd.hasSymbolGrowth_inner.name: Rd.hasSymbolGrowth_inner
Rd.hasSymbolGrowth_inner.docstring:
**Linear symbols**: `ξ ↦ ⟪ξ, v⟫`, as a complex function, is a symbol of order `1`; it is the
symbol of the derivative in the direction `v` up to the factor `2πi` (Mathlib's
`TemperedDistribution.lineDeriv_eq_fourierMultiplierCLM`).

Rd.hasSymbolGrowth_continuousLinearMap.name: Rd.hasSymbolGrowth_continuousLinearMap
Rd.hasSymbolGrowth_continuousLinearMap.docstring:
**Continuous linear maps are symbols of order `1`**
(`ContinuousLinearMap.norm_iteratedFDeriv_le_one_add_norm_sq_rpow`).

Rd.hasSymbolGrowth_besselWeight.name: Rd.hasSymbolGrowth_besselWeight
Rd.hasSymbolGrowth_besselWeight.docstring:
**The Bessel weight is a symbol**: `⟨ξ⟩^s = (1 + ‖ξ‖²)^{s/2}` (`Rd.besselWeight`), as a
complex function, is a symbol of order `s` for every real `s`
(`Rd.hasSymbolGrowth_one_add_norm_sq_rpow`).

Rd.hasSum_lpBlock.name: Rd.hasSum_lpBlock
Rd.hasSum_lpBlock.docstring:
**A finite Littlewood–Paley quasi-norm gives an absolutely convergent decomposition**: for
`s > 0`, `‖Δ_j f‖_p ≤ 2^(-js) ‖f‖_{LP}`, so `f = ∑_j Δ_j f` converges absolutely in `L_p`.

Rd.hasSum_czBadPart.name: Rd.hasSum_czBadPart
Rd.hasSum_czBadPart.docstring:
**The bad part is the sum of the bad pieces** on the maximal big cubes, at every point; at
most one piece is nonzero there.

Rd.hasSum_czAverageC.name: Rd.hasSum_czAverageC
Rd.hasSum_czAverageC.docstring:
At every point the series defining the signed averages converges, since at most one of its
terms is nonzero.

Rd.hasSum_conv_czBadPart.name: Rd.hasSum_conv_czBadPart
Rd.hasSum_conv_czBadPart.docstring:
**Convolution of the bad part, piece by piece**: for a continuous bounded kernel `K`, an
integrable `f` and the maximal big cubes of any `G` at any height `t`,
`(K ⋆ czBadC f)(x) = ∑_Q (K ⋆ czBadPart_Q f)(x)` at every point `x`. The proof bounds
`∑_Q ∫ |K(x - y)| |czBadPart_Q f(y)| dy` by `sup |K| · 2 ∫ |f|`
(`Rd.tsum_lintegral_enorm_czBadPart_le`), so sum and integral can be exchanged (Mathlib's
`hasSum_integral_of_summable_integral_norm`).

Rd.hasFDerivAt_rayIntegral.name: Rd.hasFDerivAt_rayIntegral
Rd.hasFDerivAt_rayIntegral.docstring:
**Differentiation under the ray integral**: for `g ∈ C^1` with compact support and a unit
vector `w`, the ray integral is differentiable with `DΨ(y) = ∫_0^∞ Dg(y + t w) dt` (Mathlib's
`hasFDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_of_fderiv_le`, with the bound `sup ‖Dg‖` on an interval of `t`
that contains the parameters of the line meeting the support of `g`).

Rd.hasFDerivAt_one_add_norm_sq_rpow.name: Rd.hasFDerivAt_one_add_norm_sq_rpow
Rd.hasFDerivAt_one_add_norm_sq_rpow.docstring:
The derivative of `x ↦ (1 + ‖x‖²)^r` is `(1 + ‖x‖²)^{r-1}` times the linear map `2r ⟪x, ·⟫`.
Mirrored from TauCeti (`TauCeti.hasFDerivAt_one_add_norm_sq_rpow`,
`Analysis/SpecialFunctions/JapaneseBracket/Deriv.lean`, commit `b61a90d`, Apache-2.0).

Rd.hasDerivAt_dilate_exp.name: Rd.hasDerivAt_dilate_exp
Rd.hasDerivAt_dilate_exp.docstring:
**Euler's identity for dilations**: `d/ds m_{e^s}(x) = n m_{e^s}(x) + D(m_{e^s})(x) x`, the
derivative of the dilation parameter is the radial derivative.

Rd.hasDerivAt_comp_add_smul.name: Rd.hasDerivAt_comp_add_smul
Rd.hasDerivAt_comp_add_smul.docstring: The chain rule along a line: `t ↦ g(y + t w)` has the derivative `Dg(y + t w) w`.

Rd.hasCompactSupport_shiftReflect.name: Rd.hasCompactSupport_shiftReflect
Rd.hasCompactSupport_shiftReflect.docstring: The reflected translate of a compactly supported Schwartz function has compact support.

Rd.hasCompactSupport_divergenceKernel.name: Rd.hasCompactSupport_divergenceKernel
Rd.hasCompactSupport_divergenceKernel.docstring: The divergence kernels have compact support if `m` vanishes outside a ball.

Rd.hasCompactSupport_dilate.name: Rd.hasCompactSupport_dilate
Rd.hasCompactSupport_dilate.docstring: Dilates of compactly supported functions have compact support.

Rd.hasCompactSupport_derivSymbol_mul_fou.name: Rd.hasCompactSupport_derivSymbol_mul_fourier_lpBlockKernel_one
Rd.hasCompactSupport_derivSymbol_mul_fou.docstring:
The function `ξ ↦ σ_i(ξ) 𝓕ψ_1(ξ)` has compact support: it vanishes outside the closed ball
of radius `4`.

Rd.hasCompactSupport_cutoff_smul_mul.name: Rd.hasCompactSupport_cutoff_smul_mul
Rd.hasCompactSupport_cutoff_smul_mul.docstring:
The product of the rescaled cut-off `x ↦ χ(x/(n+1))`, `χ = Rd.cutoff 1 2`, with any function
has compact support. This function-level form enters the definition of `Rd.cutoffMul`.

Rd.hasCompactSupport_cutoffMul.name: Rd.hasCompactSupport_cutoffMul
Rd.hasCompactSupport_cutoffMul.docstring: The cut-off of a Schwartz function has compact support.

Rd.hasCompactSupport_comp_add_smul.name: Rd.hasCompactSupport_comp_add_smul
Rd.hasCompactSupport_comp_add_smul.docstring:
A compactly supported function restricted to a line in the direction of a unit vector is
compactly supported.

Rd.hasCompactSupport_bumpMollifier.name: Rd.hasCompactSupport_bumpMollifier
Rd.hasCompactSupport_bumpMollifier.docstring:
The mollifier of a bump function has compact support, since the normalised bump has
(Mathlib's `ContDiffBump.hasCompactSupport_normed`).

Rd.halfSpaceReflection_notMem.name: Rd.halfSpaceReflection_notMem
Rd.halfSpaceReflection_notMem.docstring: The reflection of a point of `H₊` lies outside `H₊`.

Rd.halfSpaceReflection_halfSpaceReflecti.name: Rd.halfSpaceReflection_halfSpaceReflection
Rd.halfSpaceReflection_halfSpaceReflecti.docstring:
The reflection is an involution: `σ (σ y) = y` (Mathlib's
`Submodule.reflection_reflection`).

Rd.halfSpaceReflection_apply.name: Rd.halfSpaceReflection_apply
Rd.halfSpaceReflection_apply.docstring:
**The reflection formula**: for a unit vector `e`, `σ y = y - 2⟪y, e⟫ e` (Mathlib's
`Submodule.reflection_orthogonal_apply` and `Submodule.reflection_singleton_apply`).

Rd.halfSpaceReflection.name: Rd.halfSpaceReflection
Rd.halfSpaceReflection.docstring:
The **reflection** `σ` across the hyperplane `e^⊥` (Mathlib's `Submodule.reflection` in
`(ℝ e)^⊥`), a linear isometry of `V`; for `‖e‖ = 1`, `σ y = y - 2⟪y, e⟫ e`
(`Rd.halfSpaceReflection_apply`).

Rd.halfSpaceCutoff.name: Rd.halfSpaceCutoff
Rd.halfSpaceCutoff.docstring:
The **cutoffs near the hyperplane** `η_n(y) = s((n + 1)⟪y, e⟫ - 1)` with Mathlib's smooth
step `s = Real.smoothTransition`: `η_n = 0` where `⟪y, e⟫ ≤ 1/(n + 1)`, `η_n = 1` where
`⟪y, e⟫ ≥ 2/(n + 1)`, and `0 ≤ η_n ≤ 1`.

Rd.gridLevelSet.name: Rd.gridLevelSet
Rd.gridLevelSet.docstring:
The indices of level `n`, `{k ∈ ℕ^d : |k|_1 = n}`: Mathlib's
`Finset.Nat.antidiagonalTuple d n`.

Rd.gridCoord.name: Rd.gridCoord
Rd.gridCoord.docstring:
**The coordinates of the dyadic grid**: `x ↦ (⟪b_i, x⟫)_i` for the orthonormal basis
`b = Rd.gridBasis V`, a continuous linear equivalence of `V` with `ℝ^n = Fin n → ℝ`,
`n = dim V`, where `ℝ^n` carries the sup norm. It is the coordinate map `(Rd.gridBasis V).repr`
into `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` followed by Mathlib's identification `EuclideanSpace.equiv` of
the Euclidean space with `Fin n → ℝ`.

Rd.gridBasis_snoc.name: Rd.gridBasis_snoc
Rd.gridBasis_snoc.docstring:
The basis directions of a word `(u, j)` are those of `u` followed by `e_j` (Mathlib's
`Fin.comp_snoc`).

Rd.gridBasis.name: Rd.gridBasis
Rd.gridBasis.docstring: The orthonormal basis of the dyadic grid.

Rd.graphTrace_ae_eq_of_continuousOn.name: Rd.graphTrace_ae_eq_of_continuousOn
Rd.graphTrace_ae_eq_of_continuousOn.docstring:
**Traces of functions continuous on the closed half-space**: let `f ∈ L_p(V)` have a finite
intrinsic quasi-norm of smoothness `s + 1/p`, `s > 0`, on the open half-space, and let `G` be
continuous on the closed half-space, vanish there outside a compact set, and agree with `f` almost
everywhere on the open half-space. Then `Tr f = G` almost everywhere on `e^⊥`. The folded `G ∘ F`
is continuous with compact support and agrees with `f` on the half-space, and traces of continuous
functions are restrictions (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_comp_graphMap`).

Rd.gradMassConst_ne_top.name: Rd.gradMassConst_ne_top
Rd.gradMassConst_ne_top.docstring: The gradient mass of a Schwartz function is finite.

Rd.gradMassConst_le_familyGradMass.name: Rd.gradMassConst_le_familyGradMass
Rd.gradMassConst_le_familyGradMass.docstring: Every member of a uniform family has gradient mass at most that of the family.

Rd.gradMassConst.name: Rd.gradMassConst
Rd.gradMassConst.docstring:
The **gradient mass** `C_{G,1,n+1} I_{n+1}` of a Schwartz function `G`, a bound for
`∫ ‖DG‖`.

Rd.gagliardoMeasure.name: Rd.gagliardoMeasure
Rd.gagliardoMeasure.docstring:
**The Gagliardo measure** `μ_s = |y - x|^(-(n + 2s)) dx dy` on `V × V`, `n = dim V`: the
Lebesgue measure of `V × V` with this density. For `p = 2` the Gagliardo form `E_{s,2}(f)` is the
square of the `L_2(μ_s)` norm of `(x, y) ↦ f(y) - f(x)` (`Rd.eLpNorm_sub_sq_gagliardoMeasure`), so
that `f ↦ (f, (x, y) ↦ f(y) - f(x))` maps `W^{s,2}(V)` with the norm
`(‖f‖_2² + E_{s,2}(f))^(1/2)` isometrically into `L_2(V) × L_2(μ_s)` with the `L_2` norm on the
product.

Rd.fwdDiff_single_tensorKernel.name: Rd.fwdDiff_single_tensorKernel
Rd.fwdDiff_single_tensorKernel.docstring:
**A difference in coordinate `i` of a tensor product** acts on the `i`-th factor:
`Δ_{t e_i} (⊗K) = ⊗K'` with `K'_i = Δ_t K_i` and `K'_j = K_j` otherwise.

Rd.fwdDiff_schwartz_eq_integral.name: Rd.fwdDiff_schwartz_eq_integral
Rd.fwdDiff_schwartz_eq_integral.docstring:
**The fundamental theorem of calculus along a segment**: for a Schwartz function `G`,
`G(x + v) - G(x) = ∫_0^1 ∂_v G(x + t v) dt` (Mathlib's
`intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt`).

Rd.fwdDiff_nsmul.name: Rd.fwdDiff_nsmul
Rd.fwdDiff_nsmul.docstring: **Differences with a multiple step telescope**: `Δ_{mh} f = ∑_{i<m} (Δ_h f)(· + i h)`.

Rd.fwdDiff_iter_taylorWithinEval_eq_zero.name: Rd.fwdDiff_iter_taylorWithinEval_eq_zero
Rd.fwdDiff_iter_taylorWithinEval_eq_zero.docstring: **The differences of order `n + 1` of a Taylor polynomial of degree `n` vanish**.

Rd.fwdDiff_iter_comp_ofReal.name: Rd.fwdDiff_iter_comp_ofReal
Rd.fwdDiff_iter_comp_ofReal.docstring:
Forward differences commute with the inclusion `ℝ → ℂ`:
`Δ_1^m (F ∘ ofReal) = (Δ_1^m F) ∘ ofReal`.

Rd.fwdDiff_congr_ae.name: Rd.fwdDiff_congr_ae
Rd.fwdDiff_congr_ae.docstring: First differences of functions that agree almost everywhere agree almost everywhere.

Rd.fwdDiffSchwartz.name: Rd.fwdDiffSchwartz
Rd.fwdDiffSchwartz.docstring: The forward difference `G ↦ G(· + v) - G` as an operator on Schwartz functions.

Rd.fwdDiffL2.name: Rd.fwdDiffL2
Rd.fwdDiffL2.docstring:
**The difference operator on `L_2(V)`**: `Δ_v f = f(· + v) - f`, a bounded linear operator,
the translation by `v` (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗᵢ`) minus the
identity.

Rd.frontier_subset_frontierCenters.name: Rd.frontier_subset_frontierCenters
Rd.frontier_subset_frontierCenters.docstring: The balls `B(z, r(z))` of the chosen centres cover the frontier.

Rd.frontierCenters.name: Rd.frontierCenters
Rd.frontierCenters.docstring:
A chosen finite set of frontier points whose balls `B(z, r(z))` cover the frontier
(`Rd.exists_finset_cover_frontier`).

Rd.frontierCenterAt.name: Rd.frontierCenterAt
Rd.frontierCenterAt.docstring:
The `j`-th chosen centre, for the numbering `Fin N` of the chosen centres
(`Finset.equivFin`).

Rd.fourier_toLp_sobolevInclusion_ae.name: Rd.fourier_toLp_sobolevInclusion_ae
Rd.fourier_toLp_sobolevInclusion_ae.docstring: The Fourier transform of `J_t (ι_{t,s} U)` is `⟨ξ⟩^{t-s} 𝓕(J_s U)` almost everywhere.

Rd.fourier_toLp_sobolevConv_ae.name: Rd.fourier_toLp_sobolevConv_ae
Rd.fourier_toLp_sobolevConv_ae.docstring:
The Fourier transform of `J_s (K ⋆ U)` is `𝓕K · 𝓕(J_s U)` almost everywhere, by the
convolution theorem on `L_2` (`Rd.fourier_convLp`).

Rd.fourier_toL2_ae_eq.name: Rd.fourier_toL2_ae_eq
Rd.fourier_toL2_ae_eq.docstring: The Fourier transform of `toL2 F` is `⟨ξ⟩⁻¹ 𝓕(J_1 F)` almost everywhere.

Rd.fourier_toL2.name: Rd.fourier_toL2
Rd.fourier_toL2.docstring: The Fourier transform of `toL2 F` is `⟨ξ⟩⁻¹ 𝓕(J_1 F)`.

Rd.fourier_symbolKernelFamily.name: Rd.fourier_symbolKernelFamily
Rd.fourier_symbolKernelFamily.docstring: `𝓕K_j(ζ) = 2^{-jσ} m(2^j ζ) ω̂(ζ)` for the symbol kernels.

Rd.fourier_sum_convLp.name: Rd.fourier_sum_convLp
Rd.fourier_sum_convLp.docstring:
**The Fourier transform of a finite sum of convolutions**: for integrable kernels `θ_j`,
functions `g_j ∈ L_2(V)` and a finite set `s`,
`𝓕(∑_{j ∈ s} θ_j ⋆ g_j) = ∑_{j ∈ s} 𝓕θ_j 𝓕g_j` almost everywhere (Mathlib's
`FourierTransform.fourier_sum` and `Rd.fourier_convLp`).

Rd.fourier_sub_apply.name: Rd.fourier_sub_apply
Rd.fourier_sub_apply.docstring:
The Fourier transform of a difference of integrable functions is the difference of the
transforms.

Rd.fourier_reflectNeg.name: Rd.fourier_reflectNeg
Rd.fourier_reflectNeg.docstring:
**Fourier transform of the reflection**: `𝓕(K^∨)(ξ) = 𝓕K(-ξ)` for every function `K`, from
Mathlib's `Real.fourierInv_eq_fourier_comp_neg` and `Real.fourierInv_eq_fourier_neg`.

Rd.fourier_lpMomentScaled_eq_zero.name: Rd.fourier_lpMomentScaled_eq_zero
Rd.fourier_lpMomentScaled_eq_zero.docstring:
`𝓕μ_{2^j}` vanishes outside the ball of radius `2^(j+1)`: every term has
`‖((l + 1)/2^j) ξ‖ ≥ 2`, where `𝓕Φ = χ_{1,2}` vanishes.

Rd.fourier_lpBlockKernel_succ_eq_zero.name: Rd.fourier_lpBlockKernel_succ_eq_zero
Rd.fourier_lpBlockKernel_succ_eq_zero.docstring: `𝓕ψ_{i+1}` vanishes on the closed ball of radius `2^i`.

Rd.fourier_lpBlockKernelS_apply.name: Rd.fourier_lpBlockKernelS_apply
Rd.fourier_lpBlockKernelS_apply.docstring: `𝓕(lpBlockKernelS j)` is the Fourier transform `𝓕ψ_j` of the block.

Rd.fourier_lpBlockKernelOneS_apply.name: Rd.fourier_lpBlockKernelOneS_apply
Rd.fourier_lpBlockKernelOneS_apply.docstring: The Fourier transform of the Schwartz function `Rd.lpBlockKernelOneS` is `𝓕ψ_1`.

Rd.fourier_fourierMultiplierCLM_apply.name: Rd.fourier_fourierMultiplierCLM_apply
Rd.fourier_fourierMultiplierCLM_apply.docstring:
**Fourier multipliers multiply the Fourier transform**: `𝓕(m(D) u)(ξ) = m(ξ) 𝓕u(ξ)` for a
symbol `m` of temperate growth and a Schwartz function `u` (Fourier inversion on Schwartz
functions).

Rd.fourier_eq_fourier_dilate.name: Rd.fourier_eq_fourier_dilate
Rd.fourier_eq_fourier_dilate.docstring: The dilation formula read backwards: `𝓕Φ(ζ) = 𝓕(Φ_c)(c ζ)` for `c > 0`.

Rd.fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_mul_lpBlock.name: Rd.fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_mul_lpBlockKernel
Rd.fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_mul_lpBlock.docstring:
`𝓕ψ̃_j · 𝓕ψ_j = 𝓕ψ_j`: wherever `𝓕ψ_j(ξ) ≠ 0`, `‖ξ‖ < 2^(j+1)`, so
`𝓕Φ_{j+1}(ξ) = 1`, and for `j ≥ 2` also `‖ξ‖ > 2^(j-1)`, so `𝓕Φ_{j-2}(ξ) = 0`; hence
`𝓕ψ̃_j(ξ) = 1` there.

Rd.fourier_dilatedLpKernel_eq_one.name: Rd.fourier_dilatedLpKernel_eq_one
Rd.fourier_dilatedLpKernel_eq_one.docstring: `𝓕Φ_k = 1` on the closed ball of radius `2^k`.

Rd.fourier_dilatedBandKernel_eq_one.name: Rd.fourier_dilatedBandKernel_eq_one
Rd.fourier_dilatedBandKernel_eq_one.docstring: `𝓕Θ_k = 1` on the closed ball of radius `2^(k+1)`.

Rd.fourier_dilate_momentKernel.name: Rd.fourier_dilate_momentKernel
Rd.fourier_dilate_momentKernel.docstring:
**The Fourier transform of a dilated moment kernel**: for an integrable `g` and `c > 0`,
