uniformly Schwartz with bounds `A`, `N > n` and `K = 2^{jσ} (G_j)_{2^j}`. Then for every real `s`,
function `g` and point `x`,
`2^{j(s-σ)} |(K ⋆ g)(x)| ≤ C_{n,N} C_{A,0,N} M(2^{js} |g|)(x)`
(`Rd.IsUniformSchwartz.enorm_conv_dilate_le_maximalFunction`, `Rd.enorm_two_pow_rpow`,
`Rd.dyadicWeight_mul_maximalFunction`).

Rd.dyadicWeight_mul_enorm_blockFun_eq.name: Rd.dyadicWeight_mul_enorm_blockFun_eq
Rd.dyadicWeight_mul_enorm_blockFun_eq.docstring:
**The blocks of a Bessel potential**: if `g ∈ L_q(V)` and `h ∈ L_r(V)` satisfy
`g = J_{-s} h` as tempered distributions, then for every `j` and `x`,
`2^{js} |(ψ_j ⋆ g)(x)| = |((K^{-s}_j)_{2^j} ⋆ h)(x)|` with the Bessel kernels `K^{-s}_j` of
`lpBlockKernelBase` (`Rd.conv_eq_conv_besselSchwartz`, `Rd.conv_besselSchwartz_schwartzDilate`).

Rd.dyadicShell.name: Rd.dyadicShell
Rd.dyadicShell.docstring:
The dyadic **shell** `{y : ‖y‖ < 2^(i+1) ρ}` for `i = 0` and
`{y : 2^i ρ ≤ ‖y‖ < 2^(i+1) ρ}` for `i ≥ 1`.

Rd.dyadicCell_disjoint.name: Rd.dyadicCell_disjoint
Rd.dyadicCell_disjoint.docstring:
Cells of the same level with different indices are disjoint: they are the fibres of
`Rd.cellIndex j` (Mathlib's `pairwise_disjoint_fiber`).

Rd.dyadicCell.name: Rd.dyadicCell
Rd.dyadicCell.docstring: The **dyadic cell** `P_{j,m}` of level `j ∈ ℕ` and index `m`: the dyadic cube `Q_{j,m}`.

Rd.dualityConst_ne_zero.name: Rd.dualityConst_ne_zero
Rd.dualityConst_ne_zero.docstring: `dualityConst n p q` is positive for `0 < q < p`.

Rd.dualityConst_ne_top.name: Rd.dualityConst_ne_top
Rd.dualityConst_ne_top.docstring: `dualityConst n p q` is finite for `1 < q < p`.

Rd.dualityConst.name: Rd.dualityConst
Rd.dualityConst.docstring:
The constant of the duality argument for `q < p`:
`(C_{n,q} C_{n,u'}^{1/u'})^(p/q)` with the exponent `u' = p/(p - q)` conjugate to `u = p/q`.

Rd.dualLpBlockKernelS.name: Rd.dualLpBlockKernelS
Rd.dualLpBlockKernelS.docstring:
The synthesis kernel `ψ̃_j = (G̃_j)_{2^j}`, `G̃_j = Rd.dualLpBlockKernelBase j`, as a Schwartz
function.

Rd.dualLpBlockKernelBase.name: Rd.dualLpBlockKernelBase
Rd.dualLpBlockKernelBase.docstring:
The Schwartz functions behind the synthesis kernels:
`dualLpBlockKernelBase 0 = dualLpBlockKernelBase 1 = δ_2 Φ` and
`dualLpBlockKernelBase (j+2) = δ_2 Φ - δ_{1/4} Φ`, with the dilation `δ_c F(x) = c^n F(c x)`, so
that `ψ̃_j = δ_{2^j} (dualLpBlockKernelBase j)` (`Rd.dilate_dualLpBlockKernelBase`).

Rd.dualLpBlockKernel.name: Rd.dualLpBlockKernel
Rd.dualLpBlockKernel.docstring:
The **synthesis kernels** `ψ̃_0 = Φ_1`, `ψ̃_1 = Φ_2`, `ψ̃_{j+2} = Φ_{j+3} - Φ_j`, with
`ψ̃_j ⋆ ψ_j = ψ_j` (`Rd.conv_dualLpBlockKernel_lpBlockKernel`).

Rd.divergenceSchwartz.name: Rd.divergenceSchwartz
Rd.divergenceSchwartz.docstring:
The divergence kernel `K_w` of a smooth `m` that vanishes outside a ball, as a Schwartz
function (it is smooth with compact support).

Rd.divergenceKernel_eq_zero_of_lt.name: Rd.divergenceKernel_eq_zero_of_lt
Rd.divergenceKernel_eq_zero_of_lt.docstring: The divergence kernels vanish outside the ball of radius `R` if `m` does.

Rd.divergenceKernel_eq_zero.name: Rd.divergenceKernel_eq_zero
Rd.divergenceKernel_eq_zero.docstring: The divergence kernels vanish at `x` if `m(t x) = 0` for every `t ∈ [1, 2]`.

Rd.divergenceKernel.name: Rd.divergenceKernel
Rd.divergenceKernel.docstring:
The **divergence kernel** `K_w(x) = ⟪w, x⟫ A_m(x)` in the direction `w`. For an orthonormal
basis `(b_i)`, `∑_i ∂_{b_i} K_{b_i} = m_2 - m` (`Rd.sum_fderiv_divergenceKernel`).

Rd.distribBlock_fourierMultiplierCLM_eq_.name: Rd.distribBlock_fourierMultiplierCLM_eq_convLp
Rd.distribBlock_fourierMultiplierCLM_eq_.docstring:
**The blocks of a Fourier multiplier as convolutions**: if `m` has temperate growth,
`1 ≤ p < ∞` and the block `Δ_j u` of a tempered distribution is an `L_p` function `g`, then
`Δ_j(m(D) u)` is the `L_p` function `(m(D) ψ̃_j) ⋆ g` (`Rd.distribBlock_fourierMultiplierCLM`,
`Rd.fourierMultiplierCLM_fourier_toLp_eq_conv`).

Rd.distribBlock_fourierMultiplierCLM.name: Rd.distribBlock_fourierMultiplierCLM
Rd.distribBlock_fourierMultiplierCLM.docstring:
**The blocks of a Fourier multiplier**: for `m` of temperate growth and every tempered
distribution `u`, `Δ_j(m(D) u) = 𝓕(m(D) ψ̃_j)(D) Δ_j u`. Both sides are Fourier multipliers of
`u` (Mathlib's `TemperedDistribution.fourierMultiplierCLM_fourierMultiplierCLM_apply`), with the
symbols `m 𝓕ψ_j` and `𝓕ψ_j m 𝓕ψ̃_j`, equal since `𝓕ψ̃_j 𝓕ψ_j = 𝓕ψ_j`
(`Rd.fourier_dualLpBlockKernel_mul_lpBlockKernel`).

Rd.distribBlock_besselPotential.name: Rd.distribBlock_besselPotential
Rd.distribBlock_besselPotential.docstring:
**The blocks of a Bessel potential**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, real `s` and a tempered distribution
`u` whose block `Δ_j u` is an `L_p` function `g`, the block `Δ_j(J_s u)` is the `L_p` function
`(J_s ψ̃_j) ⋆ g` (`Rd.distribBlock_fourierMultiplierCLM_eq_convLp` for the Bessel weight).

Rd.distribBlock.name: Rd.distribBlock
Rd.distribBlock.docstring:
The **Littlewood–Paley block of a tempered distribution**, `Δ_j u = (𝓕ψ_j)(D) u`, Mathlib's
Fourier multiplier with the Fourier transform of the block `ψ_j`.

Rd.dilationAverage_eq_zero.name: Rd.dilationAverage_eq_zero
Rd.dilationAverage_eq_zero.docstring: The dilation average vanishes at `x` if `m(t x) = 0` for every `t ∈ [1, 2]`.

Rd.dilationAverage.name: Rd.dilationAverage
Rd.dilationAverage.docstring:
The **dilation average** `A_m(x) = ∫_0^{log 2} m_{e^s}(x) ds`, which is
`∫_1^2 t⁻¹ m_t(x) dt` after the substitution `t = e^s`.

Rd.dilate_two_sub_eq.name: Rd.dilate_two_sub_eq
Rd.dilate_two_sub_eq.docstring:
**The dilation identity**: `m_2(x) - m(x) = n A_m(x) + D A_m(x) x`, by the fundamental theorem
of calculus for `s ↦ m_{e^s}(x)` on `[0, log 2]` and Euler's identity
(`Rd.hasDerivAt_dilate_exp`).

Rd.dilate_sub.name: Rd.dilate_sub
Rd.dilate_sub.docstring: Dilations are linear: `(F - G)_c = F_c - G_c`.

Rd.dilate_momentKernel.name: Rd.dilate_momentKernel
Rd.dilate_momentKernel.docstring: The dilations of the moment kernel: `m_c = ∑_{l=1}^L (-1)^(l+1) C(L, l) g_{c/l}`.

Rd.dilate.name: Rd.dilate
Rd.dilate.docstring: The **dilation** `Φ_c(x) = c^n Φ(c x)`, `n = dim V`, which keeps the integral of `Φ`.

Rd.differentiable_dilationAverage.name: Rd.differentiable_dilationAverage
Rd.differentiable_dilationAverage.docstring:
The dilation average of a `C^1` function is differentiable
(`intervalIntegral.hasFDerivAt_integral_of_contDiff`).

Rd.diffStepSet_ae_eq.name: Rd.diffStepSet_ae_eq
Rd.diffStepSet_ae_eq.docstring:
**Step sets of almost equal sets are almost equal**: the translates by `l h` of almost equal
sets are almost equal, by the translation invariance of the Lebesgue measure.

Rd.diffStepSet.name: Rd.diffStepSet
Rd.diffStepSet.docstring: The set `U_{rh}` of the points `x` with `x, x + h, …, x + r h ∈ U`.

Rd.diffAct_prod_sum_pow_apply.name: Rd.diffAct_prod_sum_pow_apply
Rd.diffAct_prod_sum_pow_apply.docstring:
**Expansion**: `(∏_i ∑_t q_i(t) Y_i^{ν(t)}) f(x) = ∑_n (∏_i q_i(n_i)) f(x + (ν(n_i) w_i)_i)` for
the translations `Y_i = δ_{w_i e_i}`.

Rd.diffAct_coordElem_pow_eq_higherDiff.name: Rd.diffAct_coordElem_pow_eq_higherDiff
Rd.diffAct_coordElem_pow_eq_higherDiff.docstring: `(δ_{h_i e_i} - 1)^L` acts by the difference `Δ^L_{h_i e_i}`.

Rd.diagEquiv.name: Rd.diagEquiv
Rd.diagEquiv.docstring: For nonzero `a_i` the diagonal map is a measurable equivalence.

Rd.det_diagMap.name: Rd.det_diagMap
Rd.det_diagMap.docstring: The determinant of the diagonal map is `∏_i a_i`.

Rd.deriv_smoothTransition_mul_eq_zero.name: Rd.deriv_smoothTransition_mul_eq_zero
Rd.deriv_smoothTransition_mul_eq_zero.docstring:
The derivative terms of the cutoffs vanish outside the bounded part `H₊ ∩ B(0, R)` of `H₊`
for every multiplier `c` vanishing outside `B(0, R)`, since `s' = 0` on `(-∞, 0)`.

Rd.derivSynthesisSum.name: Rd.derivSynthesisSum
Rd.derivSynthesisSum.docstring:
The **partial sums of the derivative** `∂^w f`: `∑_{j < J} (∂^w ψ̃_j) ⋆ (ψ_j ⋆ f)`, the
derivatives of the reproducing sums `∑_{j < J} ψ̃_j ⋆ (ψ_j ⋆ f)`.

Rd.derivSymbol.name: Rd.derivSymbol
Rd.derivSymbol.docstring:
The **derivative symbol** of the multi-index `i : Fin m → Fin n`:
`σ_i(ξ) = ∏_k ⟪ξ, e_{i_k}⟫ / ((2πi)^m ‖ξ‖^{2m})`, with the orthonormal basis `e` of
`Rd.gridBasis`; at `ξ = 0` its value is `0` for `m ≥ 1` (Lean's convention `x / 0 = 0`).

Rd.derivKernelHat.name: Rd.derivKernelHat
Rd.derivKernelHat.docstring:
The Fourier transform `ξ ↦ σ_i(ξ) 𝓕ψ_1(ξ)` of the derivative kernel `η_i`, a Schwartz
function.

Rd.derivKernelBound.name: Rd.derivKernelBound
Rd.derivKernelBound.docstring:
The seminorm bounds `A^{η_i}_{k,l} = sup_x ‖x‖^k ‖D^l η_i(x)‖` of the derivative kernel
`η_i`.

Rd.derivKernel.name: Rd.derivKernel
Rd.derivKernel.docstring: The **derivative kernel** `η_i = 𝓕⁻¹(σ_i 𝓕ψ_1)` of the multi-index `i : Fin m → Fin n`.

Rd.derivDualOverlap_ne_top.name: Rd.derivDualOverlap_ne_top
Rd.derivDualOverlap_ne_top.docstring: The overlap of a dual derivative family is finite.

Rd.derivDualOverlap.name: Rd.derivDualOverlap
Rd.derivDualOverlap.docstring: The **overlap of a dual derivative family**, `4 ((8π)^k ∏_l ‖w_l‖)²`.

Rd.derivDualBound.name: Rd.derivDualBound
Rd.derivDualBound.docstring:
The seminorm bounds of the dual derivative bases `j ↦ ∂^w G̃_j`: the larger of the
seminorms of `∂^w δ_2 Φ` (`j = 0, 1`) and `∂^w (δ_2 Φ - δ_{1/4} Φ)` (`j ≥ 2`).

Rd.derivDualBase.name: Rd.derivDualBase
Rd.derivDualBase.docstring:
The **dual derivative bases** `∂^w G̃_j = ∂_{w_0} ⋯ ∂_{w_{k-1}} G̃_j` of
the directions `w ∈ V^k`.

Rd.dense_ofSchwartz_hasCompactSupport.name: Rd.dense_ofSchwartz_hasCompactSupport
Rd.dense_ofSchwartz_hasCompactSupport.docstring:
**Compactly supported Schwartz functions are dense in `H^s(V)`**, for every real `s`: the
cut-offs `χ_n w` of a Schwartz function converge to `w` in the Schwartz space
(`Rd.tendsto_cutoffMul`), hence in `H^s(V)`, and the Schwartz functions are dense
(`Rd.denseRange_ofSchwartz`).

Rd.denseRange_sobolevInclusion.name: Rd.denseRange_sobolevInclusion
Rd.denseRange_sobolevInclusion.docstring:
**The inclusion `H^s(V) ⊆ H^t(V)` has dense range**: its range contains the Schwartz
functions (`Rd.sobolevInclusion_ofSchwartz`), which are dense in `H^t(V)`
(`Rd.denseRange_ofSchwartz`).

Rd.denseRange_ofSchwartz.name: Rd.denseRange_ofSchwartz
Rd.denseRange_ofSchwartz.docstring:
**The Schwartz functions are dense in `H^s(V)`**, for every real `s`: `J_s` is an isometry of
`H^s(V)` onto `L_2(V)` (Mathlib's `BesselPotentialSpace.toLpₗᵢ`), it maps the Schwartz functions
onto the Schwartz functions (`Rd.besselSchwartz_besselSchwartz_neg`), and these are dense in
`L_2(V)` (Mathlib's `SchwartzMap.denseRange_toLpCLM`).

Rd.decayMaximalConst_ne_top.name: Rd.decayMaximalConst_ne_top
Rd.decayMaximalConst_ne_top.docstring: `decayMaximalConst V N` is finite for `N > n`.

Rd.decayMaximalConst_mul_familyDecayCons.name: Rd.decayMaximalConst_mul_familyDecayConst_ne_top
Rd.decayMaximalConst_mul_familyDecayCons.docstring:
The constant `C_{n,N} C_{A,0,N}` of `Rd.IsUniformSchwartz.enorm_conv_dilate_le_maximalFunction`
is finite for `N > n` (`Rd.decayMaximalConst_ne_top`, `Rd.familyDecayConst_ne_top`).

Rd.decayMaximalConst.name: Rd.decayMaximalConst
Rd.decayMaximalConst.docstring:
The constant `|B(0,1)| 2^n (1 - 2^(-(N-n)))⁻¹` of the maximal function bound for kernels
with the decay `2^(jn) (1 + 2^j ‖y‖)^(-N)`.

Rd.cz_volume_zcell_le.name: Rd.cz_volume_zcell_le
Rd.cz_volume_zcell_le.docstring:
A maximal big cube `Q` has volume at most `t⁻¹ ∫_Q G`, for every height `t`, with
`0⁻¹ = ∞`: for `t = 0` the integral `∫_Q G` is positive and the bound is `∞`.

Rd.cz_volume_le.name: Rd.cz_volume_le
Rd.cz_volume_le.docstring:
**The measure of the exceptional set**: `|Ω| ≤ t⁻¹ ∫ G` for every height `t`, with
`0⁻¹ = ∞`, since every maximal cube `Q` has `|Q| ≤ t⁻¹ ∫_Q G` and the cubes are disjoint.

Rd.cz_avg_le.name: Rd.cz_avg_le
Rd.cz_avg_le.docstring:
The average of `G` over a maximal big cube is at most `2^n t`: the parent cube is not big and
has `2^n` times the volume.

Rd.cz_ae_le_of_notMem.name: Rd.cz_ae_le_of_notMem
Rd.cz_ae_le_of_notMem.docstring:
**`G ≤ t` off the exceptional set**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for an a.e.-measurable `G` with
finite integral and `0 < t`, almost every `x ∉ Ω` satisfies `G x ≤ t`. No dyadic cube containing
such an `x` is big, since it would lie in a maximal big cube, so Lebesgue differentiation along
dyadic cubes (`Rd.ae_le_of_forall_laverage_le`) applies.

Rd.czSet.name: Rd.czSet
Rd.czSet.docstring:
The **exceptional set** `Ω` of the Calderón–Zygmund decomposition: the union of the maximal
big cubes.

Rd.czMaximal_pairwiseDisjoint.name: Rd.czMaximal_pairwiseDisjoint
Rd.czMaximal_pairwiseDisjoint.docstring: The maximal big cubes are **pairwise disjoint**.

Rd.czMaximal_disjoint_of_le.name: Rd.czMaximal_disjoint_of_le
Rd.czMaximal_disjoint_of_le.docstring:
Two distinct maximal big cubes `Q_{k,m}` and `Q_{k',m'}` with `k ≤ k'` are disjoint: if the
finer cube met the coarser one, the coarser one would be its ancestor, which is not big.

Rd.czMaximal_countable.name: Rd.czMaximal_countable
Rd.czMaximal_countable.docstring: There are countably many maximal big cubes.

Rd.czMaximal.name: Rd.czMaximal
Rd.czMaximal.docstring:
The **maximal big cubes** of `G` at height `t`: the pairs `(k, m)` such that the average of
`G` over the cube `Q_{k,m}` exceeds `t` while the average over every strict ancestor
`Q_{k-l, m^{(l)}}`, `l ≥ 1`, does not.

Rd.czGoodC_add_czBadC.name: Rd.czGoodC_add_czBadC
Rd.czGoodC_add_czBadC.docstring:
The signed good and bad parts add up to the function: `czGoodC f + czBadC f = f` for every
`f : V → E`.

Rd.czGoodC.name: Rd.czGoodC
Rd.czGoodC.docstring:
The **signed good part** of `f : V → E` in the Calderón–Zygmund decomposition of `G` at
height `t`: `f` outside the exceptional set `Ω`, and its mean `⨍_Q f` on each maximal big cube
`Q`.

Rd.czGood.name: Rd.czGood
Rd.czGood.docstring:
The **good part** of `h : V → [0, ∞]` in the Calderón–Zygmund decomposition of `G` at height
`t`: `h` outside the exceptional set `Ω`, and its mean `⨍_Q h` on each maximal big cube `Q`.

Rd.czEnlarged.name: Rd.czEnlarged
Rd.czEnlarged.docstring:
The **enlarged exceptional set** `Ω*`: the union of the closed balls of radius `2n 2^(-k)`
around the centres of the maximal big cubes `Q_{k,m}`, twice the radius `n 2^(-k)` of a ball
around the centre containing the cube (`Rd.zcell_subset_closedBall`).

Rd.czConst_ne_top.name: Rd.czConst_ne_top
Rd.czConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant `Rd.czConst V p B H` is finite for `1 < p < ∞` and finite `B`, `H`.

Rd.czConstBelow_ne_top.name: Rd.czConstBelow_ne_top
Rd.czConstBelow_ne_top.docstring: The constant `Rd.czConstBelow V p B H` is finite for `1 < p < 2` and finite `B`, `H`.

Rd.czConstBelow.name: Rd.czConstBelow
Rd.czConstBelow.docstring:
The constant of the strong type `(p, p)`, `1 < p < 2`, of a Calderón–Zygmund family with
overlap `B` and Hörmander constant `H`: `C^M_p(C_V(B, H), B)^{1/p}`, with the Marcinkiewicz
constant `C^M_p(C₁, C₂) = p (2 C₁/(p - 1) + 4 C₂/(2 - p))` (`MeasureTheory.marcinkiewiczConst`)
and the weak type constant `C_V(B, H)` (`Rd.vectorWeakConst`).

Rd.czConst.name: Rd.czConst
Rd.czConst.docstring:
The constant of the strong type `(p, p)`, `1 < p < ∞`, of a Calderón–Zygmund family with
overlap `B` and Hörmander constant `H`: `B^{1/2}` for `p = 2`, `Rd.czConstBelow V p B H` for
`p < 2`, and `Rd.czConstBelow V p' B H` with the conjugate exponent `p'` for `p > 2`.

Rd.czBadPart_of_notMem.name: Rd.czBadPart_of_notMem
Rd.czBadPart_of_notMem.docstring: Outside its cube the bad piece vanishes.

Rd.czBadPart_of_mem.name: Rd.czBadPart_of_mem
Rd.czBadPart_of_mem.docstring: On its cube `Q` the bad piece is `f - ⨍_Q f`.

Rd.czBadPart.name: Rd.czBadPart
Rd.czBadPart.docstring:
The **bad piece** of `f : V → E` on the dyadic cube `Q = Q_{k,m}`: `f - ⨍_Q f` on `Q` and `0`
outside.

Rd.czBadC_eq_zero_of_notMem.name: Rd.czBadC_eq_zero_of_notMem
Rd.czBadC_eq_zero_of_notMem.docstring: Outside the exceptional set `Ω` the bad part vanishes.

Rd.czBadC_eq_tsum.name: Rd.czBadC_eq_tsum
Rd.czBadC_eq_tsum.docstring: The bad part as the series of the bad pieces, `czBadC f = ∑_Q czBadPart_Q f`.

Rd.czBadC_eq_of_mem.name: Rd.czBadC_eq_of_mem
Rd.czBadC_eq_of_mem.docstring: On a maximal big cube `Q` the bad part is `f - ⨍_Q f`.

Rd.czBadC.name: Rd.czBadC
Rd.czBadC.docstring:
The **signed bad part** `f - czGoodC f` of the Calderón–Zygmund decomposition of `G` at
height `t`.

Rd.czAverage_self_le.name: Rd.czAverage_self_le
Rd.czAverage_self_le.docstring:
The Calderón–Zygmund averages of `G` itself are at most `2^n t`
(`Rd.cz_avg_le`).

Rd.czAverage_eq_zero_of_notMem.name: Rd.czAverage_eq_zero_of_notMem
Rd.czAverage_eq_zero_of_notMem.docstring: Outside the exceptional set `Ω` the Calderón–Zygmund averages vanish.

Rd.czAverage_eq_of_mem.name: Rd.czAverage_eq_of_mem
Rd.czAverage_eq_of_mem.docstring:
On a maximal big cube `Q`, the Calderón–Zygmund average of `h` is `⨍_Q h`, since the maximal
big cubes are disjoint.

Rd.czAverageC_eq_zero_of_notMem.name: Rd.czAverageC_eq_zero_of_notMem
Rd.czAverageC_eq_zero_of_notMem.docstring: Outside the exceptional set `Ω` the signed averages vanish.

Rd.czAverageC_eq_of_mem.name: Rd.czAverageC_eq_of_mem
Rd.czAverageC_eq_of_mem.docstring: On a maximal big cube `Q`, the signed average of `f` is `⨍_Q f`.

Rd.czAverageC.name: Rd.czAverageC
Rd.czAverageC.docstring:
The **signed Calderón–Zygmund averages** of `f : V → E`: on each maximal big cube `Q` of `G`
at height `t` the mean `⨍_Q f`, and `0` outside the exceptional set `Ω`.

Rd.czAverage.name: Rd.czAverage
Rd.czAverage.docstring:
The **Calderón–Zygmund averages** of `h : V → [0, ∞]`: on each maximal big cube `Q` of `G`
at height `t` the mean `⨍_Q h`, and `0` outside the exceptional set `Ω`.

Rd.cutoff_eq_zero.name: Rd.cutoff_eq_zero
Rd.cutoff_eq_zero.docstring: The cut-off is `0` outside the ball of radius `b`.

Rd.cutoff_eq_one.name: Rd.cutoff_eq_one
Rd.cutoff_eq_one.docstring: The cut-off is `1` on the closed ball of radius `a`.

Rd.cutoffMul_eventuallyEq.name: Rd.cutoffMul_eventuallyEq
Rd.cutoffMul_eventuallyEq.docstring:
The cut-off at radius `n + 1` agrees with `u` near every point of the open ball of radius
`n + 1`.

Rd.cutoffMul_apply.name: Rd.cutoffMul_apply
Rd.cutoffMul_apply.docstring: The values of the cut-off: `cutoffMul n u x = χ(x/(n+1)) u(x)`.

Rd.cutoffMulConst_nonneg.name: Rd.cutoffMulConst_nonneg
Rd.cutoffMulConst_nonneg.docstring: The constant of the cut-off estimate is nonnegative.

Rd.cutoffMulConst.name: Rd.cutoffMulConst
Rd.cutoffMulConst.docstring:
The constant of the cut-off estimate `Rd.seminorm_sub_cutoffMul_le`:
`p_{k+1,m}(u) + ∑_{i ≤ m} C(m,i) p_{0,i}(χ) p_{k+1,m-i}(u)` in the Schwartz seminorms of `u` and
of the cut-off `χ = Rd.cutoffSchwartz 1 2`.

Rd.cutoffMulBound.name: Rd.cutoffMulBound
Rd.cutoffMulBound.docstring:
The pointwise bound for the `m`-th derivative of `u - χ_n u`:
`B(x) = ‖D^m u(x)‖ + ∑_{i ≤ m} C(m,i) p_{0,i}(χ) ‖D^(m-i) u(x)‖`, the derivative of `u` plus the
Leibniz bound of `Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_cutoffMul_le`, with `χ = Rd.cutoffSchwartz 1 2`.

Rd.cutoffMul.name: Rd.cutoffMul
Rd.cutoffMul.docstring:
The **cut-off** of a Schwartz function `u` at radius `n + 1`: `x ↦ χ(x/(n+1)) u(x)` with the
smooth cut-off `χ = Rd.cutoff 1 2` (equal to `1` on the closed unit ball and to `0` outside the
ball of radius `2`), a smooth function with compact support.

Rd.cutoff.name: Rd.cutoff
Rd.cutoff.docstring:
The **smooth cut-off** `χ_{a,b}` with `0 < a < b`: `1` on the closed ball of radius `a`, `0`
outside the ball of radius `b`, with values in `[0, 1]` (Mathlib's `ContDiffBump`).

Rd.cubeParent.name: Rd.cubeParent
Rd.cubeParent.docstring: The index of the **parent** cube: `⌊m_i / 2⌋` in every coordinate.

Rd.cubeAt_subset_closedBall.name: Rd.cubeAt_subset_closedBall
Rd.cubeAt_subset_closedBall.docstring:
The cube of level `k` containing `x` lies in the closed ball of radius `(n+1) 2^(-k)` around
its centre.

Rd.cubeAt.name: Rd.cubeAt
Rd.cubeAt.docstring: The dyadic cube of level `k` containing `x`.

Rd.cubeAncestor.name: Rd.cubeAncestor
Rd.cubeAncestor.docstring: The index of the ancestor `l` levels up: the parent map iterated `l` times.

Rd.coord_zero_eq_inner.name: Rd.coord_zero_eq_inner
Rd.coord_zero_eq_inner.docstring: The first coordinate is the inner product with `e₀`.

Rd.conv_tsum_of_finset.name: Rd.conv_tsum_of_finset
Rd.conv_tsum_of_finset.docstring:
**Convolution with a locally finite series, term by term**: for a continuous kernel `K` with
compact support and locally integrable `u_m`, if only the indices of a finite set `T` have
`u_m(x - y) ≠ 0` for some `y` with `K(y) ≠ 0`, then `K ⋆ (∑_m u_m)(x) = ∑_m (K ⋆ u_m)(x)`.

Rd.conv_tsum_atom.name: Rd.conv_tsum_atom
Rd.conv_tsum_atom.docstring:
**Convolution with a series of atoms, term by term**: for a continuous kernel `K` that
vanishes outside `B̄(0, ρ)`, `ρ ≥ 0`, and smooth atoms `a_m` of level `j` centred at the cells
with radius factor `d ≥ 0`, `K ⋆ (∑_m λ_m a_m) = ∑_m λ_m K ⋆ a_m` at every point. Near each
point only finitely many atoms meet the support of `y ↦ K(x - y)`.

Rd.conv_tensorKernel_sum_dilate_ae.name: Rd.conv_tensorKernel_sum_dilate_ae
Rd.conv_tensorKernel_sum_dilate_ae.docstring:
**Convolution with tensor products of dilated bumps averages translates**: for
`κ_i = ∑_{t ∈ T} q_i(t) g_{c_i/ν(t)}` with `ν(t) ≥ 1`, `c_i > 0` and `f ∈ L_p`,
`((⊗κ) ⋆ f)(x) = ∫ (⊗g)(z) (∏_i ∑_t q_i(t) Y_i^{ν(t)}) f(x) dz` with `Y_i = δ_{-z_i e_i / c_i}`, for
almost every `x`.

Rd.conv_sub_apply_of_enorm_le.name: Rd.conv_sub_apply_of_enorm_le
Rd.conv_sub_apply_of_enorm_le.docstring:
**Convolution with an integrable bounded kernel respects differences at every point** on
`L_p`: `(K ⋆ f)(x) - (K ⋆ g)(x) = (K ⋆ (f - g))(x)` for `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, an integrable `K` with
`|K| ≤ B < ∞` and `f, g ∈ L_p(V)`.

Rd.conv_sub_ae.name: Rd.conv_sub_ae
Rd.conv_sub_ae.docstring:
**Convolution is subtractive in `f`** almost everywhere: `K ⋆ (f - g) = K ⋆ f - K ⋆ g` a.e.
for `K ∈ L_1` and `f, g ∈ L_p`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`.

Rd.conv_reflectNeg_lineDerivOp.name: Rd.conv_reflectNeg_lineDerivOp
Rd.conv_reflectNeg_lineDerivOp.docstring:
**Integration by parts against a reflected kernel**: for Schwartz functions `η`, `u`,
`(∂_v η)^∨ ⋆ u = -(η^∨ ⋆ ∂_v u)` pointwise, by integration by parts on the Schwartz space
(Mathlib's `SchwartzMap.integral_mul_lineDerivOp_right_eq_neg_left`) applied to `η(· - y)` and
`u`.

Rd.conv_reflectNeg_conj.name: Rd.conv_reflectNeg_conj
Rd.conv_reflectNeg_conj.docstring:
**Reflection and conjugation**: `(K^∨ ⋆ conj u)(x) = conj((K^* ⋆ u)(x))` at every point, for
the adjoint kernel `K^*(z) = conj K(-z)` and the reflection `K^∨(z) = K(-z)`; both sides are
`∫ K(y - x) conj u(y) dy`.

Rd.conv_reflectNeg_apply.name: Rd.conv_reflectNeg_apply
Rd.conv_reflectNeg_apply.docstring: **Convolution with a reflected kernel**: `(K^∨ ⋆ u)(y) = ∫ K(z - y) u(z) dz`.

Rd.conv_mixedDilatedBandKernel_mixedLpBl.name: Rd.conv_mixedDilatedBandKernel_mixedLpBlockKernel
Rd.conv_mixedDilatedBandKernel_mixedLpBl.docstring:
**The blocks are band-limited**: `(⊗Θ_{k_i}) ⋆ δ_k = δ_k`
(`Rd.conv_dilatedBandKernel_lpBlockKernel` in every coordinate).

Rd.conv_lpBlockKernel_lpMomentScaled.name: Rd.conv_lpBlockKernel_lpMomentScaled
Rd.conv_lpBlockKernel_lpMomentScaled.docstring:
**High blocks annihilate the moment kernels of `Φ`**: `ψ_{j+2} ⋆ μ_{2^j} = 0`, since
`𝓕ψ_{j+2}` vanishes on the ball of radius `2^(j+1)` and `𝓕μ_{2^j}` outside it.

Rd.conv_lpBlockKernel_dilatedBandKernel.name: Rd.conv_lpBlockKernel_dilatedBandKernel
Rd.conv_lpBlockKernel_dilatedBandKernel.docstring: **High blocks annihilate band-limited kernels**: `ψ_j ⋆ Θ_k = 0` for `j ≥ k + 3`.

Rd.conv_indicator_eq_of_forall.name: Rd.conv_indicator_eq_of_forall
Rd.conv_indicator_eq_of_forall.docstring:
**The support principle for two sets**: if `x - y ∈ W` whenever `k(y) ≠ 0`, then
`(k ⋆ 1_W f)(x) = (k ⋆ f)(x)`.

Rd.conv_indicator_eq_mul_sum_of_eq_sum_i.name: Rd.conv_indicator_eq_mul_sum_of_eq_sum_iteratedLineDerivOp
Rd.conv_indicator_eq_mul_sum_of_eq_sum_i.docstring:
**A convolution with a sum of derivatives of dilated kernels**: let `g_i = ∂^{u_i} f` weakly
on an open set `T` with `f ∈ L_p(T)`, let `K_i` be Schwartz functions with compact support, `t ≠ 0`,
and let `κ = c ∑_i ∂^{u_i} (K_i)_t`. If `x - y ∈ T` for every `i` and every `y` in the support of
`(K_i)_t`, then `(κ ⋆ 1_T f)(x) = c ∑_i ((K_i)_t ⋆ 1_T g_i)(x)`: each derivative moves from the
kernel to `1_T f` (`Rd.conv_eq_conv_iteratedLineDerivOp_of_hasWeakLineDeriv`).

Rd.conv_fourierMultiplierCLM_eq.name: Rd.conv_fourierMultiplierCLM_eq
Rd.conv_fourierMultiplierCLM_eq.docstring:
**Convolution with a multiplied kernel**: for an even symbol `m` of temperate growth,
`h ∈ L_r(V)`, a Schwartz function `η` and every `x`, `((m(D) η) ⋆ h)(x)` is the tempered
distribution `m(D) h` at the reflected translate `y ↦ η(x - y)`
(`Rd.fourierMultiplierCLM_apply_apply_of_even`, `Rd.fourierMultiplierCLM_shiftReflect`).

Rd.conv_finsetSum_kernel_ae.name: Rd.conv_finsetSum_kernel_ae
Rd.conv_finsetSum_kernel_ae.docstring:
**Convolution is linear in the kernel** almost everywhere:
`(∑_i a_i K_i) ⋆ f = ∑_i a_i (K_i ⋆ f)` for integrable `K_i` and `f ∈ L_p`.

Rd.conv_eq_tsum_cellAtom_of_indicator.name: Rd.conv_eq_tsum_cellAtom_of_indicator
Rd.conv_eq_tsum_cellAtom_of_indicator.docstring:
**Cell decomposition of a convolution, cellwise hypothesis**: `K ⋆ g = ∑_m λ_{j,m} a_{j,m}` at
every point, with finitely many nonzero terms, for a continuous `K` that vanishes outside
`B̄(0, ρ)`, as soon as `1_{P_{j,m}} g ∈ L_p` for every cell.

Rd.conv_eq_tsum_cellAtom.name: Rd.conv_eq_tsum_cellAtom
Rd.conv_eq_tsum_cellAtom.docstring:
**Cell decomposition of a convolution**: `K ⋆ g = ∑_m λ_{j,m} a_{j,m}` at every point, with
finitely many nonzero terms, for a continuous `K` that vanishes outside `B̄(0, ρ)`.

Rd.conv_eq_toTemperedDistribution_shiftR.name: Rd.conv_eq_toTemperedDistribution_shiftReflect
Rd.conv_eq_toTemperedDistribution_shiftR.docstring:
**Convolution as a tempered distribution**: for `g ∈ L_r(V)` and a Schwartz function `η`,
`(η ⋆ g)(x)` is the tempered distribution of `g` at the reflected translate `y ↦ η(x - y)`.

Rd.conv_eq_of_fourier.name: Rd.conv_eq_of_fourier
Rd.conv_eq_of_fourier.docstring:
**Kernel identities from Fourier transforms**: if `K`, `L`, `M` are integrable, `L` is bounded
and continuous, `M` is continuous with integrable Fourier transform, and `𝓕K · 𝓕L = 𝓕M`, then
`K ⋆ L = M`. Both sides have the same transform (`Rd.fourier_conv`), and the inversion theorem
applies to continuous integrable functions with integrable transform
(`Continuous.fourierInv_fourier_eq`).

Rd.conv_eq_integral_shiftReflect.name: Rd.conv_eq_integral_shiftReflect
Rd.conv_eq_integral_shiftReflect.docstring:
**Convolution as a pairing**: `(η ⋆ f)(x) = ∫ η(x - y) f(y) dy` is the integral of `f`
against the reflected translate of `η`.

Rd.conv_eq_convolution_mul_real.name: Rd.conv_eq_convolution_mul_real
Rd.conv_eq_convolution_mul_real.docstring: The convolution of complex functions, with the multiplication of `ℂ` as a real bilinear map.

Rd.conv_eq_conv_iteratedLineDerivOp_of_h.name: Rd.conv_eq_conv_iteratedLineDerivOp_of_hasWeakLineDeriv
Rd.conv_eq_conv_iteratedLineDerivOp_of_h.docstring:
**Weak derivatives commute with convolution, locally**: if `g = ∂^v f` weakly on an open set
`Ω` and `η` is a compactly supported Schwartz function with `x - y ∈ Ω` for every `y` in the
support of `η`, then `(η ⋆ g)(x) = ((∂^v η) ⋆ f)(x)`: the reflected translate `y ↦ η(x - y)` is a
complex test function on `Ω` (`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.integral_mul_eq`,
`Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_shiftReflect`).

Rd.conv_eq_conv_iteratedLineDerivOp.name: Rd.conv_eq_conv_iteratedLineDerivOp
Rd.conv_eq_conv_iteratedLineDerivOp.docstring:
**Weak derivatives commute with convolution**: if `g ∈ L_r(V)` is the weak derivative
`∂^v f` of `f ∈ L_p(V)` on `V`, `1 ≤ p, r ≤ ∞`, then `η ⋆ g = (∂^v η) ⋆ f` at every point, for
every Schwartz function `η`. The value `(η ⋆ g)(x)` is `g` tested with `y ↦ η(x - y)`; the
tempered derivative moves to this Schwartz function with the sign `(-1)^k`
(`TemperedDistribution.iteratedLineDerivOp_apply_apply`), which cancels against the sign of
`Rd.iteratedLineDerivOp_shiftReflect`.

Rd.conv_eq_conv_fourierMultiplierCLM.name: Rd.conv_eq_conv_fourierMultiplierCLM
Rd.conv_eq_conv_fourierMultiplierCLM.docstring:
**Blocks of a multiplied function**: for an even symbol `m` of temperate growth, if
`g ∈ L_q(V)` and `h ∈ L_r(V)` satisfy `g = m(D) h` as tempered distributions, then
`η ⋆ g = (m(D) η) ⋆ h` at every point, for every Schwartz function `η`
(`Rd.conv_eq_toTemperedDistribution_shiftReflect`, `Rd.conv_fourierMultiplierCLM_eq`).

Rd.conv_eq_conv_besselSchwartz.name: Rd.conv_eq_conv_besselSchwartz
Rd.conv_eq_conv_besselSchwartz.docstring:
**Blocks of a Bessel potential**: if `g ∈ L_q(V)` and `h ∈ L_r(V)` satisfy `g = J_t h` as
tempered distributions, then `η ⋆ g = (J_t η) ⋆ h` at every point, for every Schwartz function
`η` (`Rd.conv_eq_conv_fourierMultiplierCLM`, `Rd.besselWeight_neg`).

Rd.conv_dualLpBlockKernel_lpBlockKernel.name: Rd.conv_dualLpBlockKernel_lpBlockKernel
Rd.conv_dualLpBlockKernel_lpBlockKernel.docstring:
**The synthesis kernels reproduce the blocks**: `ψ̃_j ⋆ ψ_j = ψ_j`, by comparing
Fourier transforms (`Rd.conv_eq_of_fourier`).

Rd.conv_dualLpBlockKernel_blockFun_ae.name: Rd.conv_dualLpBlockKernel_blockFun_ae
Rd.conv_dualLpBlockKernel_blockFun_ae.docstring:
**The synthesis kernels reproduce the blocks**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `f ∈ L_p(V)`,
`ψ̃_j ⋆ (ψ_j ⋆ f) = ψ_j ⋆ f` almost everywhere, by associativity of convolution and
`ψ̃_j ⋆ ψ_j = ψ_j` (`Rd.conv_dualLpBlockKernel_lpBlockKernel`).

Rd.conv_dilatedBandKernel_dilate_lpKerne.name: Rd.conv_dilatedBandKernel_dilate_lpKernel
Rd.conv_dilatedBandKernel_dilate_lpKerne.docstring:
**Band-limited dilations of the Littlewood–Paley kernel**: `Θ_k ⋆ Φ_c = Φ_c` for
`0 < c ≤ 2^k`, since `𝓕Φ_c = χ_{1,2}(c^(-1) ·)` lives in the ball of radius `2c ≤ 2^(k+1)`.

Rd.conv_dilatedBandKernel_blockFun.name: Rd.conv_dilatedBandKernel_blockFun
Rd.conv_dilatedBandKernel_blockFun.docstring:
**The blocks are band-limited at every point**: `Θ_j ⋆ (ψ_j ⋆ f) = ψ_j ⋆ f` for
`1 ≤ p < ∞` and `f ∈ L_p(V)`. Almost everywhere this is associativity and `Θ_j ⋆ ψ_j = ψ_j`
(`Rd.conv_conv_ae`, `Rd.conv_dilatedBandKernel_lpBlockKernel`); both sides are continuous
(`Rd.continuous_conv_schwartz`), so they agree everywhere (Mathlib's
`Continuous.ae_eq_iff_eq`).

Rd.conv_dilate_near.name: Rd.conv_dilate_near
Rd.conv_dilate_near.docstring:
**Approximate identities at points of continuity**: if `Φ` is integrable with `∫ Φ = 1` and
vanishes outside `B̄(0, R)`, and `F_J(z) → z₀` as `J → ∞` and `z → y`, then
`(Φ_{2^J} ⋆ F_J)(z) → z₀` as `J → ∞` and `z → y`: for every `ε > 0` there are `J₀` and `δ > 0`
with `|(Φ_{2^J} ⋆ F_J)(z) - z₀| < ε` for `J ≥ J₀` and `‖z - y‖ < δ`. Since `∫ Φ_{2^J} = 1`,
`(Φ_{2^J} ⋆ F_J)(z) - z₀ = ∫ Φ_{2^J}(w) (F_J(z - w) - z₀) dw`, and only `‖w‖ ≤ R 2^(-J)` enters.

Rd.conv_dilate_dilate.name: Rd.conv_dilate_dilate
Rd.conv_dilate_dilate.docstring: **Dilations commute with convolution**: `A_c ⋆ B_c = (A ⋆ B)_c` for `c > 0`.

Rd.conv_dilate_apply.name: Rd.conv_dilate_apply
Rd.conv_dilate_apply.docstring:
**Convolution with a dilation**: `(Φ_c ⋆ f)(x) = ∫ Φ(z) f(x - c^(-1) z) dz` for `c > 0`
(substitute `y = c^(-1) z`, Mathlib's `Measure.integral_comp_smul`).

Rd.conv_conv_ae.name: Rd.conv_conv_ae
Rd.conv_conv_ae.docstring:
**Convolution is associative**: `(K ⋆ L) ⋆ f = K ⋆ (L ⋆ f)` almost everywhere for integrable
`K`, `L` and `f ∈ L_p`, `1 ≤ p < ∞` (Mathlib's `convolution_assoc'`, with the absolute convergence
of `Rd.ae_integrable_conv_conv`).

Rd.conv_congr_ae.name: Rd.conv_congr_ae
Rd.conv_congr_ae.docstring:
Convolutions of functions that agree almost everywhere agree everywhere (Mathlib's
`convolution_congr`).

Rd.conv_comp_add.name: Rd.conv_comp_add
Rd.conv_comp_add.docstring:
**Translates of convolutions**: `(K ⋆ f)(x + c) = (K(· + c) ⋆ f)(x)`, by the substitution
`y ↦ y + c`.

Rd.conv_besselSchwartz_schwartzDilate.name: Rd.conv_besselSchwartz_schwartzDilate
Rd.conv_besselSchwartz_schwartzDilate.docstring:
**Convolution with the Bessel potential of a dilate**: for a family `(ω_j)` of Schwartz
functions, `(J_σ (ω_j)_{2^j}) ⋆ F = (K^σ_j)_{2^j} ⋆ ((2^j)^σ F)` at every point
(`Rd.besselSchwartz_schwartzDilate`).

Rd.conv_apply_eq_integral_sub.name: Rd.conv_apply_eq_integral_sub
Rd.conv_apply_eq_integral_sub.docstring:
**Convolution with the variable in the kernel**: `(K ⋆ f)(x) = ∫ K(x - y) f(y) dy`, the
symmetric form of the convolution integral (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.convolution_mul_swap`).

Rd.conv_add_conv_sub.name: Rd.conv_add_conv_sub
Rd.conv_add_conv_sub.docstring: `(A + B) ⋆ (A - B) = A ⋆ A - B ⋆ B` for continuous kernels with compact support.

Rd.conv_add_apply.name: Rd.conv_add_apply
Rd.conv_add_apply.docstring: `(K ⋆ g)(x + v) = ∫ K(y + v) g(x - y) dy`, by translation invariance.

Rd.conv_add_ae_of_memLp.name: Rd.conv_add_ae_of_memLp
Rd.conv_add_ae_of_memLp.docstring:
**Convolution is additive** almost everywhere, in the two-exponent form: for `f ∈ L_p` and
`g ∈ L_r` with `1 ≤ p, r < ∞`, `K ⋆ (f + g) = K ⋆ f + K ⋆ g` almost everywhere, since both
convolution integrals converge absolutely at almost every point
(`MeasureTheory.ae_convolutionExistsAt`).

Rd.conv_add_ae.name: Rd.conv_add_ae
Rd.conv_add_ae.docstring:
**Convolution is additive** in `f ∈ L_p` almost everywhere: the case of equal exponents of
`Rd.conv_add_ae_of_memLp`.

Rd.convLp_sub_kernel.name: Rd.convLp_sub_kernel
Rd.convLp_sub_kernel.docstring:
**Convolution operators are subtractive in the kernel**: `(K - K') ⋆ f = K ⋆ f - K' ⋆ f`
in `L_p`.

Rd.convLp_of_eq_zero.name: Rd.convLp_of_eq_zero
Rd.convLp_of_eq_zero.docstring: Convolution with the zero kernel is zero.

Rd.convLp_finsetSum_kernel.name: Rd.convLp_finsetSum_kernel
Rd.convLp_finsetSum_kernel.docstring: **Convolution is linear in the kernel**: `∑_i K_i ⋆ f = (∑_i K_i) ⋆ f` on `L_p`.

Rd.convLp_convLp_of_eq.name: Rd.convLp_convLp_of_eq
Rd.convLp_convLp_of_eq.docstring: If `K ⋆ L = M`, then `K ⋆ (L ⋆ f) = M ⋆ f` in `L_p`.

Rd.convLp_convLp.name: Rd.convLp_convLp
Rd.convLp_convLp.docstring:
**Convolution operators compose like their kernels**: `K ⋆ (L ⋆ f) = (K ⋆ L) ⋆ f` in `L_p`
(`Rd.conv_conv_ae`).

Rd.convLp_congr.name: Rd.convLp_congr
Rd.convLp_congr.docstring: Convolution operators with equal kernels are equal.

Rd.convLp_comm.name: Rd.convLp_comm
Rd.convLp_comm.docstring: **Convolution operators commute**: `K ⋆ (L ⋆ f) = L ⋆ (K ⋆ f)` in `L_p`.

Rd.convLp_apply_ae.name: Rd.convLp_apply_ae
Rd.convLp_apply_ae.docstring: The operator `convLp` is convolution, almost everywhere.

Rd.convLp_add_kernel.name: Rd.convLp_add_kernel
Rd.convLp_add_kernel.docstring:
**Convolution operators are additive in the kernel**: `(K + K') ⋆ f = K ⋆ f + K' ⋆ f` in
`L_p`.

Rd.convLp.name: Rd.convLp
Rd.convLp.docstring:
**Convolution with an integrable kernel as a bounded operator on `L_p`**, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, of
norm at most `‖K‖_1` (Young's inequality).

Rd.conv.name: Rd.conv
Rd.conv.docstring:
The **convolution** of complex functions, `(K ⋆ f)(x) = ∫ K(y) f(x - y) dy` (Mathlib's
`MeasureTheory.convolution` with the multiplication of `ℂ`).

Rd.continuous_setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_.name: Rd.continuous_setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_of_measurableSet
Rd.continuous_setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_.docstring:
The left side of Green's formula on a measurable set `s`,
`(U, W) ↦ ∫_s (∂_v U) W + U ∂_v W`, is continuous on `H^1(V) × H^1(V)`: a sum of bounded
bilinear pairings (`Rd.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_eq`).

Rd.continuous_ofReal_besselWeight.name: Rd.continuous_ofReal_besselWeight
Rd.continuous_ofReal_besselWeight.docstring: The Bessel weight `⟨ξ⟩^t`, as a complex function, is continuous.

Rd.continuous_momentKernel.name: Rd.continuous_momentKernel
Rd.continuous_momentKernel.docstring: Moment kernels of continuous functions are continuous.

Rd.continuous_lpMomentScaled.name: Rd.continuous_lpMomentScaled
Rd.continuous_lpMomentScaled.docstring: The dilated moment kernels of `Φ` are continuous.

Rd.continuous_integral_weakDeriv_mul_add.name: Rd.continuous_integral_weakDeriv_mul_add
Rd.continuous_integral_weakDeriv_mul_add.docstring:
The left side of Green's formula on `V`, `(U, W) ↦ ∫ (∂_v U) W + U ∂_v W`, is continuous on
`H^1(V) × H^1(V)` (`Rd.continuous_setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_of_measurableSet` on `s = V`).

Rd.continuous_fourier_of_integrable.name: Rd.continuous_fourier_of_integrable
Rd.continuous_fourier_of_integrable.docstring:
**The Fourier transform of an integrable function is continuous** (Mathlib's
`VectorFourier.fourierIntegral_continuous`).

Rd.continuous_fourierInv_of_integrable.name: Rd.continuous_fourierInv_of_integrable
Rd.continuous_fourierInv_of_integrable.docstring:
The inverse Fourier transform `𝓕⁻g(x) = ∫ e^(2πi⟪ξ, x⟫) g(ξ) dξ` of an integrable function is
continuous, since `𝓕⁻g(x) = 𝓕g(-x)` (Mathlib's `Real.fourierInv_eq_fourier_neg`).

Rd.continuous_fderiv_dilate_exp_apply.name: Rd.continuous_fderiv_dilate_exp_apply
Rd.continuous_fderiv_dilate_exp_apply.docstring:
The radial derivative `s ↦ D(m_{e^s})(x) x` of the dilates of a `C^1` function is
continuous in `s`.

Rd.continuous_eLpNorm_comp_sub_sub.name: Rd.continuous_eLpNorm_comp_sub_sub
Rd.continuous_eLpNorm_comp_sub_sub.docstring:
**Continuity of translation in `L_p`**, `1 ≤ p < ∞`: `w ↦ ‖f(· - w) - f‖_p` is continuous,
from Mathlib's continuity of the action of `V` on `L_p` by translation of the domain
(`Lp.instContinuousVAddDomAddAct`).

Rd.continuous_dilate_exp.name: Rd.continuous_dilate_exp
Rd.continuous_dilate_exp.docstring: The dilations `m_{e^s}(x)` depend continuously on `(x, s)` if `m` is continuous.

Rd.continuous_dilate.name: Rd.continuous_dilate
Rd.continuous_dilate.docstring: Dilations of continuous functions are continuous.

Rd.continuous_conv_schwartz.name: Rd.continuous_conv_schwartz
Rd.continuous_conv_schwartz.docstring:
**Convolutions of Schwartz functions with `L_p` functions are continuous**, for
`1 ≤ p < ∞`: a Schwartz function `G` is integrable and bounded by its decay constant
`Rd.schwartzDecayConst G 0 0` (`Rd.enorm_schwartz_le`), so `Rd.continuous_conv_of_enorm_le`
applies.

Rd.continuous_conv_of_enorm_le.name: Rd.continuous_conv_of_enorm_le
Rd.continuous_conv_of_enorm_le.docstring:
**Convolutions of integrable bounded kernels with `L_p` functions are continuous**, for
`1 ≤ p < ∞`, an integrable `K` with `|K| ≤ B < ∞` and `f ∈ L_p(V)`. Continuous functions of
compact support `g_k` approximate `f` in `L_p` (Mathlib's
`MemLp.exists_hasCompactSupport_eLpNorm_sub_le`), each `K ⋆ g_k` is continuous (Mathlib's
`HasCompactSupport.continuous_convolution_right`), and the pointwise bound
`|(K ⋆ (f - g_k))(x)| ≤ ‖K‖_1^(1-1/p) B^(1/p) ‖f - g_k‖_p` (`Rd.enorm_conv_le_of_enorm_le`) makes
the convergence `K ⋆ g_k → K ⋆ f` uniform.

Rd.continuous_cellAtom.name: Rd.continuous_cellAtom
Rd.continuous_cellAtom.docstring: Cell atoms are continuous for a continuous kernel with compact support.

Rd.continuous_blockFun.name: Rd.continuous_blockFun
Rd.continuous_blockFun.docstring:
**The blocks are continuous**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `f ∈ L_p(V)`, `ψ_j ⋆ f` is continuous,
since `ψ_j` is a Schwartz function (`Rd.continuous_conv_schwartz`).

Rd.contDiff_divergenceKernel.name: Rd.contDiff_divergenceKernel
Rd.contDiff_divergenceKernel.docstring: The divergence kernels of a smooth function are smooth.

Rd.contDiff_dilationAverage.name: Rd.contDiff_dilationAverage
Rd.contDiff_dilationAverage.docstring:
The dilation average of a smooth function is smooth
(`intervalIntegral.contDiff_parametric_intervalIntegral_of_contDiff`).

Rd.contDiff_dilate_exp.name: Rd.contDiff_dilate_exp
Rd.contDiff_dilate_exp.docstring: The dilations `m_{e^s}(x) = e^{sn} m(e^s x)` depend smoothly on `(x, s)` if `m` is smooth.

Rd.contDiff_dilate.name: Rd.contDiff_dilate
Rd.contDiff_dilate.docstring: Dilations of smooth functions are smooth.

Rd.contDiff_derivSymbol_mul_fourier_lpBl.name: Rd.contDiff_derivSymbol_mul_fourier_lpBlockKernel_one
Rd.contDiff_derivSymbol_mul_fourier_lpBl.docstring:
The function `ξ ↦ σ_i(ξ) 𝓕ψ_1(ξ)` is smooth: `𝓕ψ_1` is smooth and vanishes on the unit ball,
and `σ_i` is smooth away from `0` (`Rd.contDiffOn_derivSymbol`).

Rd.contDiff_conv.name: Rd.contDiff_conv
Rd.contDiff_conv.docstring: The convolution with a smooth kernel of compact support is smooth.

Rd.contDiff_bumpMollifier.name: Rd.contDiff_bumpMollifier
Rd.contDiff_bumpMollifier.docstring: The mollifier of a bump function is smooth.

Rd.contDiff_besselSymbol.name: Rd.contDiff_besselSymbol
Rd.contDiff_besselSymbol.docstring: For `ε > 0` the shifted Bessel symbol is smooth, since `ε + ‖ζ‖² > 0` everywhere.

Rd.contDiffOn_derivSymbol.name: Rd.contDiffOn_derivSymbol
Rd.contDiffOn_derivSymbol.docstring:
The derivative symbols are smooth away from the origin: `ξ ↦ ∏_k ⟪ξ, e_{i_k}⟫` and
`ξ ↦ ‖ξ‖^{2m} = (‖ξ‖²)^m` are smooth, and the second vanishes only at `0`.

Rd.conj_testSchwartz.name: Rd.conj_testSchwartz
Rd.conj_testSchwartz.docstring:
**A test function is real**: `conj (φ(x)) = φ(x)` for the Schwartz function of a real test
function `φ`.

Rd.conj_fourier_apply.name: Rd.conj_fourier_apply
Rd.conj_fourier_apply.docstring:
**Conjugation and the Fourier transform**: for `f : V → ℂ` and `ξ ∈ V`,
`conj (𝓕 f(ξ)) = 𝓕⁻(conj ∘ f)(ξ)`, since `conj e^{-2πi⟨x, ξ⟩} = e^{2πi⟨x, ξ⟩}`.

Rd.conj_fourierInv_apply.name: Rd.conj_fourierInv_apply
Rd.conj_fourierInv_apply.docstring:
**Conjugation and the inverse Fourier transform**: for `f : V → ℂ` and `x ∈ V`,
`conj (𝓕⁻ f(x)) = 𝓕(conj ∘ f)(x)`.

Rd.conj_besselSchwartz_apply.name: Rd.conj_besselSchwartz_apply
Rd.conj_besselSchwartz_apply.docstring:
**`J_t` keeps real functions real**: for a Schwartz function `u` with real values,
`conj (J_t u(x)) = J_t u(x)` (`Rd.conj_fourierInv_apply`, `Rd.conj_fourier_apply`,
`Rd.besselSchwartz_apply_eq_fourier`).

Rd.completeSpace_vanishOn.name: Rd.completeSpace_vanishOn
Rd.completeSpace_vanishOn.docstring:
The subspace `Rd.vanishOn s Ω` is complete, as a closed subspace of the complete space
`H^s(V)`; hence it has an orthogonal projection.

Rd.completeSpace_tildeSpace.name: Rd.completeSpace_tildeSpace
Rd.completeSpace_tildeSpace.docstring: `H̃^s(Ω)` is complete, as a closed subspace of `H^s(V)`.

Rd.complBallRpowConst_ne_top.name: Rd.complBallRpowConst_ne_top
Rd.complBallRpowConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of `∫_{|z| ≥ R} |z|^(-a) dz` is finite for `a > n`.

Rd.complBallRpowConst.name: Rd.complBallRpowConst
Rd.complBallRpowConst.docstring:
The constant `2^n |B_1| (1 - 2^(-(a-n)))⁻¹` of the radial integral
`∫_{|z| ≥ R} |z|^(-a) dz` for `a > n = dim V`.

Rd.coeffNorm_cellCoef.name: Rd.coeffNorm_cellCoef
Rd.coeffNorm_cellCoef.docstring:
**The coefficient quasi-norm of cell coefficients**:
`‖λ‖_{b^s_{p,q}} = ‖(2^(js) ‖g_j‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}` for the cell coefficients of `g_j ∈ L_p`.

Rd.coe_symbolFamily.name: Rd.coe_symbolFamily
Rd.coe_symbolFamily.docstring: The symbol family is `ζ ↦ 2^{-jσ} m(2^j ζ) ω̂(ζ)`.

Rd.coe_shiftReflect_eq_comp.name: Rd.coe_shiftReflect_eq_comp
Rd.coe_shiftReflect_eq_comp.docstring: The reflected translate `y ↦ η(x - y)` is `η` composed with the homeomorphism `y ↦ x - y`.

Rd.coe_schwartzDilate_lpBlockKernelBase.name: Rd.coe_schwartzDilate_lpBlockKernelBase
Rd.coe_schwartzDilate_lpBlockKernelBase.docstring:
The Littlewood–Paley kernel `ψ_j` is the Schwartz function `(lpBlockKernelBase j)_{2^j}`
(`Rd.dilate_lpBlockKernelBase`).

Rd.coe_schwartzDilate_bandKernelS.name: Rd.coe_schwartzDilate_bandKernelS
Rd.coe_schwartzDilate_bandKernelS.docstring: The band-limiting kernel `Θ_j` is the Schwartz function `Θ_{2^j}`.

Rd.coe_schwartzDilate.name: Rd.coe_schwartzDilate
Rd.coe_schwartzDilate.docstring: The Schwartz dilation is the dilation `Rd.dilate`.

Rd.coe_orthogonalProjectionOnto_orthogon.name: Rd.coe_orthogonalProjectionOnto_orthogonalComplement_singleton
Rd.coe_orthogonalProjectionOnto_orthogon.docstring:
The orthogonal projection onto the hyperplane `ν^⊥` of a unit vector `ν` is
`P w = w - ⟪ν, w⟫ ν`: the identity minus Mathlib's projection onto the line `ℝ ν`
(`Submodule.starProjection_unit_singleton`).

Rd.coe_lpBlockKernelS.name: Rd.coe_lpBlockKernelS
Rd.coe_lpBlockKernelS.docstring:
The Schwartz function `Rd.lpBlockKernelS j` is the block `ψ_j`
(`Rd.dilate_lpBlockKernelBase`).

Rd.coe_lpBlockKernelOneS.name: Rd.coe_lpBlockKernelOneS
Rd.coe_lpBlockKernelOneS.docstring: The Schwartz function `Rd.lpBlockKernelOneS` is the block `ψ_1`.

Rd.coe_lineDerivOp_toSchwartzMap.name: Rd.coe_lineDerivOp_toSchwartzMap
Rd.coe_lineDerivOp_toSchwartzMap.docstring:
The directional derivative of a smooth compactly supported `K`, as a Schwartz function
(Mathlib's `HasCompactSupport.toSchwartzMap`), is `y ↦ DK(y) v`.

Rd.coe_iteratedLineDerivOp_eq.name: Rd.coe_iteratedLineDerivOp_eq
Rd.coe_iteratedLineDerivOp_eq.docstring:
Two test functions (possibly on different open sets) with the same values have iterated
directional derivatives with the same values.

Rd.coe_fwdDiffSchwartz.name: Rd.coe_fwdDiffSchwartz
Rd.coe_fwdDiffSchwartz.docstring: The Schwartz forward difference is the forward difference.

Rd.coe_dualLpBlockKernelS.name: Rd.coe_dualLpBlockKernelS
Rd.coe_dualLpBlockKernelS.docstring: The Schwartz function `Rd.dualLpBlockKernelS j` is the synthesis kernel `ψ̃_j`.

Rd.coe_cutoffSchwartz.name: Rd.coe_cutoffSchwartz
Rd.coe_cutoffSchwartz.docstring: The Schwartz cut-off is the cut-off.

Rd.coe_besselSymbolFamily.name: Rd.coe_besselSymbolFamily
Rd.coe_besselSymbolFamily.docstring: The Bessel symbol family is `ζ ↦ (2^{-2j} + ‖ζ‖²)^{σ/2} ω̂(ζ)`.

Rd.coeFn_sum_convLp_ae.name: Rd.coeFn_sum_convLp_ae
Rd.coeFn_sum_convLp_ae.docstring:
The **partial sums of convolutions in `L_p`**: for Schwartz kernels `K_j`, `g_j ∈ L_p(V)`,
`1 ≤ p < ∞` and a finite set `t`, the sum `∑_{j ∈ t} K_j ⋆ g_j` of the classes in `L_p(V)` is
almost everywhere the pointwise sum of the convolutions (`Rd.convLp_apply_ae`).

Rd.closure_range_tildeToRestrictionL.name: Rd.closure_range_tildeToRestrictionL
Rd.closure_range_tildeToRestrictionL.docstring: `H^s_0(Ω)` is the closure of the image of `H̃^s(Ω)` under the restriction.

Rd.closureToLp.name: Rd.closureToLp
Rd.closureToLp.docstring: **Bounded continuous functions on `closure Ω` as elements of `L_2(Ω)`**, for bounded `Ω`.

Rd.closedHalfSpace_ae_eq.name: Rd.closedHalfSpace_ae_eq
Rd.closedHalfSpace_ae_eq.docstring:
**The closed half-space is the open one up to a null set**: they differ by the hyperplane
`e^⊥`, a proper subspace.

Rd.closedBall_subset_union_iUnion_dyadic.name: Rd.closedBall_subset_union_iUnion_dyadicAnnulus
Rd.closedBall_subset_union_iUnion_dyadic.docstring:
**The annuli cover the punctured ball**: every `z ≠ 0` with `|z| ≤ ρ 2^(-k)` lies in an
annulus `ρ 2^(-(k+i+1)) < |z| ≤ ρ 2^(-(k+i))`, with `2^i ≤ ρ 2^(-k)/|z| < 2^(i+1)`.

Rd.centeredBumpBase.name: Rd.centeredBumpBase
Rd.centeredBumpBase.docstring: The smooth bump around `0` with outer radius `R`.

Rd.cellIndex.name: Rd.cellIndex
Rd.cellIndex.docstring:
The index `(⌊2^j x_i⌋)_i` of the dyadic cell of level `j ∈ ℕ` containing `x`: the cube index
`Rd.zcellIndex` of level `j`.

Rd.cellCoef_mul_cellAtom_of_indicator.name: Rd.cellCoef_mul_cellAtom_of_indicator
Rd.cellCoef_mul_cellAtom_of_indicator.docstring: `λ_{j,m} a_{j,m} = K ⋆ (1_{P_{j,m}} g)` as soon as `1_{P_{j,m}} g ∈ L_p`.

Rd.cellCoef_indicator.name: Rd.cellCoef_indicator
Rd.cellCoef_indicator.docstring:
The coefficient of a cell depends only on `g` on that cell:
`λ_{j,m}(1_{P_{j,m}} g) = λ_{j,m}(g)`.

Rd.cellCoefFun_of_mem.name: Rd.cellCoefFun_of_mem
Rd.cellCoefFun_of_mem.docstring: On the cell `P_{j,m}` the step function of the coefficients is `|λ_{j,m}|`.

Rd.cellCoefFun_le_maximalFunction.name: Rd.cellCoefFun_le_maximalFunction
Rd.cellCoefFun_le_maximalFunction.docstring:
**Coefficients below the maximal function**: if `|λ_{j,m}| ≤ 2^(jn) ∫_{P_{j,m}} g` for every
cell of level `j`, then at every point `x` the coefficient of the cell containing `x` is at most
`(2n + 1)^n |B_1| M g(x)`, since that cell lies in `B(x, (2n + 1) 2^(-j))`.

Rd.cellCoefFun.name: Rd.cellCoefFun
Rd.cellCoefFun.docstring:
The **step function of the coefficients** of level `j`: at `x` the modulus `|λ_{j,m}|` of
the coefficient of the cell `P_{j,m}` of level `j` that contains `x`.

Rd.cellCenter.name: Rd.cellCenter
Rd.cellCenter.docstring: The **centre** of the dyadic cell `P_{j,m}`, with the coordinates `(m_i + 1/2) 2^(-j)`.

Rd.cellAtom_indicator.name: Rd.cellAtom_indicator
Rd.cellAtom_indicator.docstring:
The atom of a cell depends only on `g` on that cell:
`a_{j,m}(1_{P_{j,m}} g) = a_{j,m}(g)`.

Rd.cellAtom_eq_zero.name: Rd.cellAtom_eq_zero
Rd.cellAtom_eq_zero.docstring:
Cell atoms vanish outside `B̄(c_{j,m}, (ρ + n) 2^(-j))` if `K` vanishes outside
`B̄(0, ρ 2^(-j))`.

Rd.cellAtomConst_ne_top.name: Rd.cellAtomConst_ne_top
Rd.cellAtomConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of the cell atoms is finite.

Rd.cellAtomConst.name: Rd.cellAtomConst
Rd.cellAtomConst.docstring:
The constant of the cell atoms as regular atoms:
`2^r A ((ρ + r)^n |B_1|)^(1-1/p) ((r + 1) (ρ + n)^n |B_1|)^(1/p)`.

Rd.cellAtom.name: Rd.cellAtom
Rd.cellAtom.docstring: The **cell atom** `a_{j,m} = λ_{j,m}⁻¹ K ⋆ (1_{P_{j,m}} g)` (zero if `λ_{j,m} = 0`).

Rd.cauchySeq_toLp_sum_conv_blockFun.name: Rd.cauchySeq_toLp_sum_conv_blockFun
Rd.cauchySeq_toLp_sum_conv_blockFun.docstring:
**Cauchy synthesis sums**: let `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `σ` real, `f ∈ F^σ_{p,2}(V)` and `K_j` Schwartz
kernels with
`‖∑_{j ∈ t} K_j ⋆ (ψ_j ⋆ f)‖_p ≤ C ‖ x ↦ ‖(1_t(j) 2^{jσ} (ψ_j ⋆ f)(x))_j‖_{ℓ_2} ‖_p` for every
finite `t` and some finite `C`. Then the classes of the partial sums
`∑_{j < J} K_j ⋆ (ψ_j ⋆ f)` form a Cauchy sequence in `L_p(V)`: their differences are bounded by
the tails of the weighted blocks (`Rd.eLpNorm_sum_conv_blockFun_sub_le`), which tend to zero
(`MeasureTheory.cauchySeq_of_edist_le_lqNorm_ite`).

Rd.card_le_of_norm_sub_cellCenter_le.name: Rd.card_le_of_norm_sub_cellCenter_le
Rd.card_le_of_norm_sub_cellCenter_le.docstring:
**Bounded overlap of the centres**: at most `⌈(2ρ + 2)^n⌉` centres of level `j` lie in a
ball of radius `ρ 2^(-j)`.

Rd.card_le_of_norm_cellCenter_sub_le.name: Rd.card_le_of_norm_cellCenter_sub_le
Rd.card_le_of_norm_cellCenter_sub_le.docstring:
**Counting centres**: at most `(2ρ + 2)^n` centres of level `j` lie in the ball of radius
`ρ 2^(-j)` around `x`.

Rd.card_le_of_lipschitz_centres.name: Rd.card_le_of_lipschitz_centres
Rd.card_le_of_lipschitz_centres.docstring:
**Bounded overlap of transported centres**: let `Φ` be `L`-Lipschitz on `B`, and let the
points `z_m ∈ B` satisfy `‖Φ z_m - c_{j,m}‖ ≤ d 2^(-j)` for the centres `c_{j,m}` of the cells of
level `j`. Then at most `⌈(2 (2 L ρ + d) + 2)^n⌉` of the `z_m` lie in a ball of radius
`ρ 2^(-j)`.

Rd.card_le_of_higherDiff_ne_zero.name: Rd.card_le_of_higherDiff_ne_zero
Rd.card_le_of_higherDiff_ne_zero.docstring:
**Bounded overlap of the differences of atoms**: if the atoms `a_m` vanish outside the balls
`B(c_m, d 2^(-j))` and at most `N` centres with `λ_m ≠ 0` lie in a ball of radius
`(d + r) 2^(-j)`, then for `‖h‖ ≤ 2^(-j)` at most `N` of the functions `λ_m Δ_h^r a_m` are nonzero
at any point, since `Δ_h^r a_m(x) ≠ 0` needs some `x + l h`, `l ≤ r`, in the ball of `a_m`.

Rd.card_gridLevelSet_le.name: Rd.card_gridLevelSet_le
Rd.card_gridLevelSet_le.docstring:
**Counting**: `#{k ∈ ℕ^d : |k|_1 = n} ≤ (n + 1)^(d-1)`, since an index of level `n` is
determined by its first `d - 1` coordinates.

Rd.bumpMollifier.name: Rd.bumpMollifier
Rd.bumpMollifier.docstring:
**The mollifier of a bump function**: the normalised smooth bump `f` around `c` (Mathlib's
`ContDiffBump.normed`), with complex values; it is smooth with compact support in the closed ball
`B̄(c, r_out)` and has integral `1`.

Rd.blockFun_smul.name: Rd.blockFun_smul
Rd.blockFun_smul.docstring: The block of a complex multiple is the multiple of the block, at every point.

Rd.blockFun_add_ae.name: Rd.blockFun_add_ae
Rd.blockFun_add_ae.docstring: The block of a sum is the sum of the blocks, almost everywhere and for all levels at once.

Rd.blockFun.name: Rd.blockFun
Rd.blockFun.docstring:
The **Littlewood–Paley block at every point**, `x ↦ (ψ_j ⋆ f)(x)`, the convolution integral
of the kernel `ψ_j` with a representative of `f ∈ L_p`. Its class in `L_p` is the block
`Rd.lpBlock` (`Rd.lpBlock_ae_eq_blockFun`).

Rd.bigBallSet_mono.name: Rd.bigBallSet_mono
Rd.bigBallSet_mono.docstring: The sets `bigBallSet g t R` increase with `R`.

Rd.bigBallSet.name: Rd.bigBallSet
Rd.bigBallSet.docstring:
The points `x` for which the integral of `g` over some ball `B(x,r)` with `0 < r ≤ R` exceeds
`t |B(0,r)|`. These sets exhaust `{M g > t}` as `R → ∞`.

Rd.besselWeight_neg_one_eq_inv.name: Rd.besselWeight_neg_one_eq_inv
Rd.besselWeight_neg_one_eq_inv.docstring:
`⟨ξ⟩^{-1} = (⟨ξ⟩^1)⁻¹`: the Bessel weight of order `-1` is the reciprocal of the one of
order `1`.

Rd.besselWeight_eq_mul_besselSymbol.name: Rd.besselWeight_eq_mul_besselSymbol
Rd.besselWeight_eq_mul_besselSymbol.docstring:
**The scaling identity of the symbols**: for `c > 0`,
`⟨ξ⟩^σ = (1 + ‖ξ‖²)^{σ/2} = c^σ (c^{-2} + ‖c^{-1} ξ‖²)^{σ/2}`, since
`c^{-2} + ‖c^{-1} ξ‖² = c^{-2} (1 + ‖ξ‖²)`.

Rd.besselWeightMul_apply_ae.name: Rd.besselWeightMul_apply_ae
Rd.besselWeightMul_apply_ae.docstring: Multiplication by `⟨ξ⟩^t` is pointwise multiplication, almost everywhere.

Rd.besselWeightMul.name: Rd.besselWeightMul
Rd.besselWeightMul.docstring:
**Multiplication by `⟨ξ⟩^t`, `t ≤ 0`, on `L_2(V)`**: the operator `g ↦ ⟨·⟩^t g` of
multiplication by a continuous function bounded by `1` (`Rd.mulLpL`). At `t = -1` it is
`Rd.besselInvMul` (`Rd.besselWeightMul_neg_one`).

Rd.besselWeight.name: Rd.besselWeight
Rd.besselWeight.docstring:
The **Bessel weight** `⟨ξ⟩^s = (1 + ‖ξ‖²)^(s/2)`, the symbol of Mathlib's Bessel potential
`J_s = TemperedDistribution.besselPotential V ℂ s`.

Rd.besselSymbol_one.name: Rd.besselSymbol_one
Rd.besselSymbol_one.docstring:
For `ε = 1` the shifted Bessel symbol is the Bessel weight `⟨ξ⟩^σ = (1 + ‖ξ‖²)^{σ/2}`
(`Rd.besselWeight`), the symbol of Mathlib's Bessel potential.

Rd.besselSymbol_eq_mul.name: Rd.besselSymbol_eq_mul
Rd.besselSymbol_eq_mul.docstring:
**Rescaling the shift**: `(ε + ‖ζ‖²)^{σ/2} = ε^{σ/2} ⟨ε^{-1/2} ζ⟩^σ` for `ε > 0`, the scaling
identity `Rd.besselWeight_eq_mul_besselSymbol` with `c = ε^{-1/2}`.

Rd.besselSymbol_eq_comp.name: Rd.besselSymbol_eq_comp
Rd.besselSymbol_eq_comp.docstring: The shifted Bessel symbol is `t ↦ t^{σ/2}` composed with `ζ ↦ ε + ‖ζ‖²`.

Rd.besselSymbolFamily.name: Rd.besselSymbolFamily
Rd.besselSymbolFamily.docstring:
The **Bessel symbol family** of a Schwartz function `ω̂`:
`j ↦ (ζ ↦ (2^{-2j} + ‖ζ‖²)^{σ/2} ω̂(ζ))`, a Schwartz function since the symbol has temperate
growth (Mathlib's `SchwartzMap.smulLeftCLM`).

Rd.besselSymbolBound.name: Rd.besselSymbolBound
Rd.besselSymbolBound.docstring:
The bound `max((a²)^{σ/2}, (1 + b²)^{σ/2})` of the shifted Bessel symbols on the annulus
`{a ≤ ‖ζ‖ ≤ b}` for `ε ∈ [0, 1]` (`Rd.norm_besselSymbol_le`).

Rd.besselSymbol.name: Rd.besselSymbol
Rd.besselSymbol.docstring:
The **shifted Bessel symbol** `ζ ↦ (ε + ‖ζ‖²)^{σ/2}`, as a complex-valued function. For
`ε = 1` it is the symbol of Mathlib's Bessel potential `TemperedDistribution.besselPotential`.

Rd.besselShift.name: Rd.besselShift
Rd.besselShift.docstring:
**`J_{2s}` as an isometry of `H^s(V)` onto `H^{-s}(V)`**: both spaces are isometric to
`L_2(V)` (Mathlib's `BesselPotentialSpace.toLpₗᵢ`), and `besselShift s U` is the element of
`H^{-s}(V)` with the same `L_2` function `J_s U` as `U`; on distributions it is `J_{2s}`
(`Rd.toDistr_besselShift`).

Rd.besselSchwartz_schwartzDilate.name: Rd.besselSchwartz_schwartzDilate
Rd.besselSchwartz_schwartzDilate.docstring:
**The Bessel potential of a dilate**: for every Schwartz function `ω`,
`J_σ ω_{2^j} = 2^{jσ} (K_j)_{2^j}` with the Bessel kernels `K_j` of `ω̂ = 𝓕ω`, where `J_σ` is the
Bessel potential on Schwartz functions (`Rd.besselSchwartz`). Both sides have the Fourier
transform `⟨ξ⟩^σ ω̂(2^{-j} ξ)` (`Rd.besselWeight_eq_mul_besselSymbol`).

Rd.besselSchwartz_compSubConstCLM.name: Rd.besselSchwartz_compSubConstCLM
Rd.besselSchwartz_compSubConstCLM.docstring:
**`J_t` commutes with translations**: `J_t (φ(· - y)) = (J_t φ)(· - y)`
(`Rd.fourierMultiplierCLM_compSubConstCLM`).

Rd.besselSchwartz_besselSchwartz_neg.name: Rd.besselSchwartz_besselSchwartz_neg
Rd.besselSchwartz_besselSchwartz_neg.docstring:
**`J_{-t}` inverts `J_t` on Schwartz functions**: `J_t (J_{-t} u) = u`, since the product of
the Bessel weights is `⟨ξ⟩^t ⟨ξ⟩^{-t} = 1` (Mathlib's
`SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM_fourierMultiplierCLM_apply` and
`SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM_const`).

Rd.besselSchwartz_apply_eq_fourier.name: Rd.besselSchwartz_apply_eq_fourier
Rd.besselSchwartz_apply_eq_fourier.docstring:
**The transpose form of `J_t`**: `J_t u(x) = 𝓕(⟨ξ⟩^t 𝓕⁻u)(x)`, since the Bessel weight is
even (`Rd.besselWeight_neg`, `Rd.fourierMultiplierCLM_apply_eq_fourier`).

Rd.besselSchwartz_apply.name: Rd.besselSchwartz_apply
Rd.besselSchwartz_apply.docstring: `J_t u(x) = 𝓕⁻(⟨ξ⟩^t 𝓕u)(x)`, with the Fourier integrals of functions.

Rd.besselSchwartz.name: Rd.besselSchwartz
Rd.besselSchwartz.docstring:
**The Bessel potential on Schwartz functions**: `J_t u = 𝓕⁻(⟨ξ⟩^t 𝓕u)` with the weight
`⟨ξ⟩^t = (1 + ‖ξ‖²)^{t/2}` (`Rd.besselWeight`), a continuous linear map of the Schwartz space
(Mathlib's `SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM`).

Rd.besselPotential_toLp_conv.name: Rd.besselPotential_toLp_conv
Rd.besselPotential_toLp_conv.docstring:
**`J_t` of a convolution**: for `F ∈ L_p(V)`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, and a Schwartz function `η`,
Mathlib's Bessel potential maps the tempered distribution of `η ⋆ F` to that of `(J_t η) ⋆ F`
(`Rd.besselPotential_apply_apply`, `Rd.integral_besselSchwartz_mul_conv`).

Rd.besselPotential_toLp_apply.name: Rd.besselPotential_toLp_apply
Rd.besselPotential_toLp_apply.docstring:
**The Bessel potential of an `L_2` function at a Schwartz function**: for `g ∈ L_2(V)` and a
Schwartz function `u`, `(J_t g)(u) = ∫ J_t u · g`, since Mathlib's `J_t` acts by the transpose
(`Rd.besselPotential_apply_apply`).

Rd.besselPotential_sobolevToL2.name: Rd.besselPotential_sobolevToL2
Rd.besselPotential_sobolevToL2.docstring:
`J_s (ι_s U) = J_s U`: the Bessel potential of the `L_2` function `ι_s U` is the `L_2`
function of `U`.

Rd.besselPotential_schwartz.name: Rd.besselPotential_schwartz
Rd.besselPotential_schwartz.docstring:
The Bessel potential `J_t` of Mathlib's tempered distributions restricts to `J_t` on Schwartz
functions (Mathlib's `TemperedDistribution.fourierMultiplierCLM_toTemperedDistributionCLM_eq`).

Rd.besselPotential_of_subsingleton.name: Rd.besselPotential_of_subsingleton
Rd.besselPotential_of_subsingleton.docstring:
**The Bessel potential in dimension `0`**: on a space with one point, `⟨ξ⟩^s = 1`, so `J_s`
is the identity (Mathlib's `TemperedDistribution.fourierMultiplierCLM_const`).

Rd.besselPotential_inner_toLp_toLp.name: Rd.besselPotential_inner_toLp_toLp
Rd.besselPotential_inner_toLp_toLp.docstring:
**The inner product of `H^t(V)` is that of the `L_2` functions**:
`⟪U, W⟫_{H^t} = ⟪J_t U, J_t W⟫_{L_2}`, which is how Mathlib defines the inner product of
`BesselPotentialSpace`.

Rd.besselPotential_eq_of_tendsto.name: Rd.besselPotential_eq_of_tendsto
Rd.besselPotential_eq_of_tendsto.docstring:
**Limits of synthesis sums**: let `1 ≤ p < ∞`, let `η_j` be Schwartz functions and
`F_j ∈ L_p(V)`. If `∑_{j < J} η_j ⋆ F_j → f` and `∑_{j < J} (J_t η_j) ⋆ F_j → g` in `L_p(V)`,
then `J_t f = g` as tempered distributions. The partial sums satisfy this identity
(`Rd.besselPotential_toLp_conv`), `J_t` and the embedding of `L_p` into tempered distributions
are continuous, and limits in the tempered distributions are unique.

Rd.besselPotential_apply_apply.name: Rd.besselPotential_apply_apply
Rd.besselPotential_apply_apply.docstring:
**Mathlib's Bessel potential acts by the transpose**: for every tempered distribution `T`
and every Schwartz function `u`, `(J_t T)(u) = T(J_t u)`, since the Bessel weight is even
(`Rd.besselWeight_neg`, `Rd.fourierMultiplierCLM_apply_apply_of_even`).

Rd.besselOverlap_ne_top.name: Rd.besselOverlap_ne_top
Rd.besselOverlap_ne_top.docstring: The overlap of the dilated Bessel kernels is finite.

Rd.besselOverlap.name: Rd.besselOverlap
Rd.besselOverlap.docstring:
The **overlap of the dilated Bessel kernels**
`(N + 1) (max((a²)^{σ/2}, (1 + (2^N a)²)^{σ/2}) sup |ω̂|)²` for `ω̂` vanishing outside the annulus
`{a ≤ ‖ζ‖ ≤ 2^N a}`: at most `N + 1` kernels see a frequency
(`Rd.tsum_fourier_dilate_besselKernelFamily_sq_le`).

Rd.besselKernelFamily.name: Rd.besselKernelFamily
Rd.besselKernelFamily.docstring:
The **Bessel kernel family** `K_j = 𝓕⁻¹[(2^{-2j} + ‖ζ‖²)^{σ/2} ω̂]` of a Schwartz function
`ω̂`.

Rd.besselInvMul_apply_ae.name: Rd.besselInvMul_apply_ae
Rd.besselInvMul_apply_ae.docstring: Multiplication by `⟨ξ⟩⁻¹` is pointwise multiplication, almost everywhere.

Rd.besselInvMul.name: Rd.besselInvMul
Rd.besselInvMul.docstring:
**Multiplication by `⟨ξ⟩⁻¹` on `L_2(V)`**, as a bounded operator (Mathlib's Hölder
multiplication `L_∞ × L_2 → L_2`); its norm is at most `1` (`Rd.norm_besselInvMul_le_one`).

Rd.besselEvalCLM_apply.name: Rd.besselEvalCLM_apply
Rd.besselEvalCLM_apply.docstring:
`besselEvalCLM s φ U = U(φ)`, the tempered distribution of `U` evaluated at `φ`, since
`J_{-s}(J_s U) = U` (Mathlib's `BesselPotentialSpace.besselPotential_neg_toLp_eq`).

Rd.besselEvalCLM.name: Rd.besselEvalCLM
Rd.besselEvalCLM.docstring:
**Evaluation at a Schwartz function is a bounded functional on `H^s(V)`**: for a Schwartz
function `φ`, the map `U ↦ U(φ)`, which evaluates the tempered distribution of `U ∈ H^s(V)` at
`φ`, as a continuous linear functional. It is the composition `U ↦ J_s U ∈ L_2(V)`,
`g ↦ J_{-s} g ∈ 𝓢'(V, ℂ)`, and evaluation at `φ`, all continuous
(Mathlib's `PointwiseConvergenceCLM.evalCLM`).

Rd.besselBase.name: Rd.besselBase
Rd.besselBase.docstring:
The **Bessel kernels of a family** `(ω_j)` of Schwartz functions:
`K^σ_j = 𝓕⁻¹[(2^{-2j} + ‖ζ‖²)^{σ/2} 𝓕ω_j]`, the Bessel kernels of `𝓕ω_j` at the scale `j`
(`Rd.besselKernelFamily`), so that `J_σ (ω_j)_{2^j} = 2^{jσ} (K^σ_j)_{2^j}`
(`Rd.besselSchwartz_schwartzDilate`).

Rd.besovEmbeddingConst_ne_top.name: Rd.besovEmbeddingConst_ne_top
Rd.besovEmbeddingConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of the Besov embedding is finite for `p ≤ r` and `s > n(1/p - 1/r)`.

Rd.besovEmbeddingConst.name: Rd.besovEmbeddingConst
Rd.besovEmbeddingConst.docstring:
The **constant of the Besov embedding** into `L_r`,
`K_{V,p,r,s} = N_p^(1-p/r) (1 - 2^(-(s - α)))⁻¹` with `α = n(1/p - 1/r)`.

Rd.bddAbove_momentKernel.name: Rd.bddAbove_momentKernel
Rd.bddAbove_momentKernel.docstring: Moment kernels of bounded functions are bounded.

Rd.bddAbove_lpMomentScaled.name: Rd.bddAbove_lpMomentScaled
Rd.bddAbove_lpMomentScaled.docstring: The dilated moment kernels of `Φ` are bounded.

Rd.bddAbove_dilate.name: Rd.bddAbove_dilate
Rd.bddAbove_dilate.docstring: Dilations of bounded functions are bounded.

Rd.bandSpace_mono.name: Rd.bandSpace_mono
Rd.bandSpace_mono.docstring: **The band-limited classes increase**: `E_k ⊆ E_{k+1}`, since `Θ_{k+1} ⋆ Θ_k = Θ_k`.

Rd.bandSpace.name: Rd.bandSpace
Rd.bandSpace.docstring: The **band-limited class** `E_k = {g ∈ L_p : Θ_k ⋆ g = g}`, a real subspace of `L_p(V)`.

Rd.bandScheme.name: Rd.bandScheme
Rd.bandScheme.docstring:
The **band-limited scheme**: `E_k` at complexity `2^k`, that is, `E_⌊log₂ n⌋` at complexity
`n ≥ 1`, and `{0}` at complexity `0` (`ApproximationScheme.ofMonotoneSubmodules`).

Rd.bandModulusData.name: Rd.bandModulusData
Rd.bandModulusData.docstring:
**The modulus of smoothness is compatible with the band-limited scheme**, with inverse order
`r`: Jackson's inequality from level `0` on, and the inverse inequality for band-limited
functions.

Rd.bandKernelS.name: Rd.bandKernelS
Rd.bandKernelS.docstring: The **band-limiting kernel** `Θ = 𝓕⁻¹ χ_{2,4}`, a Schwartz function.

Rd.bandKernel.name: Rd.bandKernel
Rd.bandKernel.docstring: The band-limiting kernel as a function.

Rd.bandJacksonConst_ne_top.name: Rd.bandJacksonConst_ne_top
Rd.bandJacksonConst_ne_top.docstring:
**The constant of Jackson's inequality is finite**: `Φ` decays faster than every power,
`|Φ(z)| (1 + |z|)^(rp) ≤ 2^N (|Φ(z)| + |z|^N |Φ(z)|)` with `N = ⌈rp⌉`.

Rd.bandInverseConst_ne_top.name: Rd.bandInverseConst_ne_top
Rd.bandInverseConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of the inverse inequality is finite.

Rd.bandInverseConst.name: Rd.bandInverseConst
Rd.bandInverseConst.docstring: The constant of the inverse inequality, `2^r + ‖D^r Θ‖_1`.

Rd.ballVolumeSqrt.name: Rd.ballVolumeSqrt
Rd.ballVolumeSqrt.docstring:
The constant `|B_K|^{1/2}`, the square root of the volume of the closed ball
`B_K = {|ξ| ≤ K}` in `V`: by Cauchy–Schwarz, `∫_{B_K} |h| ≤ |B_K|^{1/2} ‖h‖_2`.

Rd.ballRpowConst_ne_top.name: Rd.ballRpowConst_ne_top
Rd.ballRpowConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of `∫_{|z| < R} |z|^(-a) dz` is finite for `a < n`.

Rd.ballRpowConst.name: Rd.ballRpowConst
Rd.ballRpowConst.docstring:
The constant `(1 + 2^a) |B_1| (1 - 2^(-(n-a)))⁻¹` of the radial integral
`∫_{|z| < R} |z|^(-a) dz` for `a < n = dim V`.

Rd.ballMeanDiff_zero.name: Rd.ballMeanDiff_zero
Rd.ballMeanDiff_zero.docstring: The ball means of the zero function vanish.

Rd.ballMeanDiff_rpow_le.name: Rd.ballMeanDiff_rpow_le
Rd.ballMeanDiff_rpow_le.docstring:
**The power of a ball mean** (weighted Jensen inequality): for `1 ≤ P` and measurable `f`,
`(d_j f(x))^P ≤ |B|⁻¹ ∫_B |Δ^L_h f(x)|^P dh` with `B = B(0, 2^(-j))`.

Rd.ballMeanDiff_le_of_forall.name: Rd.ballMeanDiff_le_of_forall
Rd.ballMeanDiff_le_of_forall.docstring:
A bound of the differences `|Δ^L_h f(x)| ≤ c` for all steps `‖h‖ < 2^(-j)` bounds the ball
mean: `d_j f(x) ≤ c`.

Rd.ballMeanDiff_finsetSum_le.name: Rd.ballMeanDiff_finsetSum_le
Rd.ballMeanDiff_finsetSum_le.docstring:
**Subadditivity for finite sums**: `d_j (∑_{i ∈ s} f_i)(x) ≤ ∑_{i ∈ s} d_j f_i(x)` for
measurable `f_i` (Mathlib's `Finset.le_sum_of_subadditive_on_pred`, with measurability as the
predicate closed under sums).

Rd.ballMeanDiff_congr_ae.name: Rd.ballMeanDiff_congr_ae
Rd.ballMeanDiff_congr_ae.docstring:
**Ball means of almost everywhere equal functions** agree almost everywhere: at a point `x`
with `f(x) = g(x)` the values `f(x + l h)`, `1 ≤ l ≤ L`, agree for almost every step `h`, since
`h ↦ x + l h` maps null sets to null sets.

Rd.ballMeanDiff_add_le.name: Rd.ballMeanDiff_add_le
Rd.ballMeanDiff_add_le.docstring:
**Subadditivity**: `d_j (f + g)(x) ≤ d_j f(x) + d_j g(x)` for measurable `f` and every `g`.
One summand has to be measurable, since the lower Lebesgue integral of a sum of two
non-measurable functions can exceed the sum of their integrals.

Rd.ballMeanDiff.name: Rd.ballMeanDiff
Rd.ballMeanDiff.docstring:
The **ball mean of differences** of order `L` at level `j`:
`d_j f(x) = |B(0, 2^(-j))|⁻¹ ∫_{B(0, 2^(-j))} |Δ^L_h f(x)| dh`, the mean of the differences of
`f` at `x` over all steps of length less than `2^(-j)`.

Rd.atomSynthConst_ne_top.name: Rd.atomSynthConst_ne_top
Rd.atomSynthConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of the atomic synthesis is finite for `C < ∞` and `0 < s < σ`.

Rd.atomSynthConst.name: Rd.atomSynthConst
Rd.atomSynthConst.docstring:
The constant `N^(1-1/p) C ((1 - 2^(-s))⁻¹ + 2^r ((1 - 2^(-(σ-s)))⁻¹ + (1 - 2^(-s))⁻¹))` of the
atomic synthesis.

Rd.areaFactor.name: Rd.areaFactor
Rd.areaFactor.docstring:
The **area factor** `(1 + 2ε)^m (1 + ε)` of the area formula for the accuracy `ε`, with
`m = n - 1`: comparing a graph with a linear graph costs the factor `(1 + 2ε)^m`, and comparing
the Gram density with a constant costs `1 + ε`.

Rd.approxNormDyadic_le_triebelLizorkinNo.name: Rd.approxNormDyadic_le_triebelLizorkinNorm
Rd.approxNormDyadic_le_triebelLizorkinNo.docstring:
**`F^s_{p,q} ⊆ B^s_{p,max(p,q)}` with a constant**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `s > 0` and
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, the approximation norm of `f` in `A^s_{max(p,q)}` of the band-limited scheme is at
most `2 (1 - 2^(-s))⁻¹ ‖f‖_{F^s_{p,q}}`.

Rd.approxNormDyadic_bandScheme_le.name: Rd.approxNormDyadic_bandScheme_le
Rd.approxNormDyadic_bandScheme_le.docstring:
**The approximation norm is controlled by the Littlewood–Paley quasi-norm**: for `s > 0`,
`‖f‖^dyadic ≤ 2 (1 - 2^(-s))⁻¹ ‖(2^(js) ‖Δ_j f‖_p)_j‖_q`, with the band-limited scheme. The
blocks form a block decomposition (`ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_of_hasSum`).

Rd.approxError_bandScheme_le.name: Rd.approxError_bandScheme_le
Rd.approxError_bandScheme_le.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality for the band-limited scheme**:
`E(f, E_k)_p ≤ C ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p`.

Rd.apply_mem_testSpan_of_forall.name: Rd.apply_mem_testSpan_of_forall
Rd.apply_mem_testSpan_of_forall.docstring:
**Linear maps that keep the test functions keep their span**: for all real `s` and `t`, if a
linear map `f : H^s(V) → H^t(V)` maps every test function of `Ω` into the span `T^t(Ω)` of the
test functions, then it maps `T^s(Ω)` into `T^t(Ω)` (Mathlib's `Submodule.map_span_le`).

Rd.apply_add_smul_eq_zero_of_notMem_Icc.name: Rd.apply_add_smul_eq_zero_of_notMem_Icc
Rd.apply_add_smul_eq_zero_of_notMem_Icc.docstring:
**A function supported in a ball, along a line**: if `tsupport h ⊆ B̄(0, R)` and `w` is a unit
vector, then `h(y + t w) = 0` for every `t` outside `[-⟪y, w⟫ - R, -⟪y, w⟫ + R]`.

Rd.almostDiagProfile.name: Rd.almostDiagProfile
Rd.almostDiagProfile.docstring: The profile `u(l) = 2^(-(L-s) l)` for `l ≥ 0` and `2^(s l)` for `l < 0` on `ℤ`.

Rd.almostDiagCoeff.name: Rd.almostDiagCoeff
Rd.almostDiagCoeff.docstring:
The coefficient `c(i, j) = 2^(-(i-j)L)` for `j ≤ i` and `1` for `j > i` of the almost diagonal
lemma.

Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_tensorKernel.name: Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_tensorKernel
Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_tensorKernel.docstring:
Tensor products of almost everywhere strongly measurable kernels are almost everywhere strongly
measurable: each factor `x ↦ K_i(x_i)` is, since the coordinate projections are
quasi-measure-preserving (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_eval`).

Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_mixedDiff.name: Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_mixedDiff
Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_mixedDiff.docstring: Mixed differences of a.e. strongly measurable functions are a.e. strongly measurable.

Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_higherDiff.name: Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_higherDiff
Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_higherDiff.docstring: Differences of a.e. strongly measurable functions are a.e. strongly measurable.

Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_czGoodC.name: Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_czGoodC
Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_czGoodC.docstring:
The signed good part of an almost everywhere strongly measurable function is almost
everywhere strongly measurable.

Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_conv.name: Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_conv
Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_conv.docstring:
Convolutions of a.e. strongly measurable functions are a.e. strongly measurable (Mathlib's
`AEStronglyMeasurable.convolution_integrand` and `AEStronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right'`).

Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_comp_add.name: Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_comp_add
Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_comp_add.docstring: Translates of a.e. strongly measurable functions are a.e. strongly measurable.

Rd.aemeasurable_lqNorm_dyadicWeight_Lp.name: Rd.aemeasurable_lqNorm_dyadicWeight_Lp
Rd.aemeasurable_lqNorm_dyadicWeight_Lp.docstring:
The weighted `L_p` blocks of a family `g` are almost everywhere measurable, and so is their
pointwise `ℓ_q` norm `x ↦ ‖(2^{js} |g_j(x)|)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`.

Rd.aemeasurable_lqNorm_cellCoefFun.name: Rd.aemeasurable_lqNorm_cellCoefFun
Rd.aemeasurable_lqNorm_cellCoefFun.docstring:
The pointwise `ℓ_q` norm of the weighted step functions of the coefficients is
measurable.

Rd.aemeasurable_lqNorm_blockFun.name: Rd.aemeasurable_lqNorm_blockFun
Rd.aemeasurable_lqNorm_blockFun.docstring: The pointwise `ℓ_q` norm of the weighted blocks is measurable.

Rd.aemeasurable_czGood.name: Rd.aemeasurable_czGood
Rd.aemeasurable_czGood.docstring: The good part of an almost everywhere measurable function is almost everywhere measurable.

Rd.ae_weakDeriv_mul_add_eq_zero_of_mulLp.name: Rd.ae_weakDeriv_mul_add_eq_zero_of_mulLp
Rd.ae_weakDeriv_mul_add_eq_zero_of_mulLp.docstring:
**Green's integrand of a product vanishes outside the multiplier**: if the `L_2` function of
`W' ∈ H^1(V)` is `χ ι W` for a continuous bounded `χ`, then `(∂_v U) W' + U ∂_v W' = 0` almost
everywhere outside the closed support of `χ` (`Rd.weakDerivL2_ae_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_zero`).

Rd.ae_tendsto_average_cubeAt.name: Rd.ae_tendsto_average_cubeAt
Rd.ae_tendsto_average_cubeAt.docstring:
**Lebesgue differentiation along dyadic cubes**: for a locally integrable `F`, almost every
`x` satisfies `⨍_{Q_k(x)} F → F x` as `k → ∞`, where `Q_k(x)` is the cube of level `k`
containing `x`.

Rd.ae_sum_mul_eq.name: Rd.ae_sum_mul_eq
Rd.ae_sum_mul_eq.docstring:
**The pasted functions agree with `f`**: if `∑_i ψ_i = 1` on `O`, `tsupport ψ_i ⊆ U_i` and
`F_i = f` almost everywhere on `O ∩ U_i`, then `∑_i ψ_i F_i = f` almost everywhere on `O`.

Rd.ae_sub_sum_conv_dilate_eq.name: Rd.ae_sub_sum_conv_dilate_eq
Rd.ae_sub_sum_conv_dilate_eq.docstring:
**Averaged differences** (the identity behind the moment kernels and the Jackson
approximant): for an integrable `g` with `∫ g = 1`, `f ∈ L_p`, `c > 0` and almost every `x`,
`f(x) - ∑_{l=1}^L (-1)^(l+1) C(L, l) (g_{c/l} ⋆ f)(x) = (-1)^L ∫ g(z) Δ^L_{-c^(-1) z} f(x) dz`.

Rd.ae_sub_jacksonApprox_eq.name: Rd.ae_sub_jacksonApprox_eq
Rd.ae_sub_jacksonApprox_eq.docstring:
**The Jackson approximant as an averaged difference**: for almost every `x`,
`f(x) - J_k f(x) = ∫ Φ(z) (-1)^r Δ^r_{-2^(-k) z} f(x) dz`.

Rd.ae_sub_conv_dilate_momentKernel_eq.name: Rd.ae_sub_conv_dilate_momentKernel_eq
Rd.ae_sub_conv_dilate_momentKernel_eq.docstring:
**Convolution with a moment kernel averages differences**: for an integrable `g` with
`∫ g = 1`, `f ∈ L_p`, `c > 0` and almost every `x`,
`f(x) - (m_c ⋆ f)(x) = (-1)^L ∫ g(z) Δ^L_{-c^(-1) z} f(x) dz`.

Rd.ae_re_lineDeriv_eq.name: Rd.ae_re_lineDeriv_eq
Rd.ae_re_lineDeriv_eq.docstring:
**Real parts of line derivatives**: for a Lipschitz `f : F → ℂ`, almost everywhere the real
part of `∂_v f` is the line derivative of `Re f`, since `f` is differentiable almost everywhere
(Rademacher's theorem, Mathlib's `LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt`).

Rd.ae_lqNorm_czGood_le.name: Rd.ae_lqNorm_czGood_le
Rd.ae_lqNorm_czGood_le.docstring:
**The good parts are bounded**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, almost everywhere
measurable `g_j` with `F = ‖(g_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q}` integrable, and `0 < t`, the decomposition of `F` at
height `t` has `‖(czGood g_j (x))_j‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ 2^n t` for almost every `x`.

Rd.ae_lqNorm_czGoodC_le.name: Rd.ae_lqNorm_czGoodC_le
Rd.ae_lqNorm_czGoodC_le.docstring:
**The good parts of a family are bounded**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, almost
everywhere strongly measurable `g_j` with `G = ‖(‖g_j‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q}` integrable, and `0 < t`, the
good parts of the `g_j` for the cubes of `G` at height `t` satisfy
`‖(‖czGoodC g_j (x)‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ 2^n t` for almost every `x`.

Rd.ae_le_of_forall_laverage_le.name: Rd.ae_le_of_forall_laverage_le
Rd.ae_le_of_forall_laverage_le.docstring:
**Pointwise bounds from cube averages**: if `G : V → ℝ≥0∞` is a.e.-measurable with finite
integral, then for every `t` and almost every `x`, `⨍_{Q_k(x)} G ≤ t` for all levels `k ∈ ℕ`
implies `G x ≤ t`.

Rd.ae_integrable_dilate_mul.name: Rd.ae_integrable_dilate_mul
Rd.ae_integrable_dilate_mul.docstring:
**The averaged translates are integrable**: for integrable `Φ`, `f ∈ L_p`, `c > 0` and almost
every `x`, `z ↦ Φ(z) f(x - c^(-1) z)` is integrable; its integral is `(Φ_c ⋆ f)(x)`.

Rd.ae_integrable_conv_conv.name: Rd.ae_integrable_conv_conv
Rd.ae_integrable_conv_conv.docstring:
**The double convolution integral converges absolutely almost everywhere**: for integrable
`K`, `L` and `f ∈ L_p`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, for almost every `x₀`,
`∫∫ |K(y)| |L(x - y)| |f(x₀ - x)| dx dy < ∞`. The double integral is
`∫ |K(y)| F(x₀ - y) dy` with `F(z) = ∫ |L(w)| |f(z - w)| dw`, and the integral form of Young's
inequality, applied twice, bounds the integral of its `p`-th power.

Rd.ae_im_lineDeriv_eq.name: Rd.ae_im_lineDeriv_eq
Rd.ae_im_lineDeriv_eq.docstring:
**Imaginary parts of line derivatives**: for a Lipschitz `f : F → ℂ`, almost everywhere the
imaginary part of `∂_v f` is the line derivative of `Im f` (Rademacher's theorem).

Rd.ae_hasSum_blockFun.name: Rd.ae_hasSum_blockFun
Rd.ae_hasSum_blockFun.docstring:
**The series of the blocks converges almost everywhere**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `s > 0`,
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and `f ∈ L_p(V)` with a finite Littlewood–Paley quasi-norm, `∑_j (ψ_j ⋆ f)(x) = f(x)`
for almost every `x`. The norms `‖Δ_j f‖_p` are summable (`ENNReal.tsum_le_lqNorm_dyadicWeight`),
`f = ∑_j Δ_j f` in `L_p` (`Rd.hasSum_lpBlock`), and an absolutely convergent series in `L_p`
converges almost everywhere (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Lp.hasSum_coeFn_tsum`).

Rd.ae_eq_of_smulLeftCLM_eq.name: Rd.ae_eq_of_smulLeftCLM_eq
Rd.ae_eq_of_smulLeftCLM_eq.docstring:
**Identities between weighted `L_p` functions hold almost everywhere**: if `w` has temperate
growth, `G ∈ L_p(V)`, `H ∈ L_q(V)`, `1 ≤ p, q ≤ ∞`, and `w G = H` as tempered distributions,
then `w G = H` almost everywhere. Both sides are locally integrable and have the same integrals
against smooth compactly supported functions (Mathlib's `ae_eq_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq`).

Rd.ae_eq_of_indicatorLp_eq.name: Rd.ae_eq_of_indicatorLp_eq
Rd.ae_eq_of_indicatorLp_eq.docstring:
Elements of `L_p` with equal restrictions to `O` agree almost everywhere on `O`
(`Rd.indicatorLp_eq_iff_ae_eq_restrict` and Mathlib's `ae_restrict_iff'`).

Rd.ae_enorm_sub_conv_dilate_momentKernel.name: Rd.ae_enorm_sub_conv_dilate_momentKernel_le
Rd.ae_enorm_sub_conv_dilate_momentKernel.docstring:
**The averaged differences, in absolute value**: for an integrable `g` with `∫ g = 1`,
`f ∈ L_p` with `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `c > 0` and almost every `x`,
`|f(x) - (m_c ⋆ f)(x)| ≤ ∫ |g(z)| |Δ^L_{-c^(-1) z} f(x)| dz`, where `m` is the moment kernel of
order `L` of `g`.

Rd.ae_enorm_czGoodC_le.name: Rd.ae_enorm_czGoodC_le
Rd.ae_enorm_czGoodC_le.docstring:
**The good part is bounded**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for integrable `f` and `0 < t`, the good
part of `f` in the decomposition of `‖f‖` at height `t` satisfies `‖czGoodC f (x)‖ ≤ 2^n t` for
almost every `x`.

Rd.ae_enorm_conv_dilate_sub_le.name: Rd.ae_enorm_conv_dilate_sub_le
Rd.ae_enorm_conv_dilate_sub_le.docstring:
**The local bound of an approximate identity**: for `∫ Φ = 1`, `c > 0` and almost every
`x`, `|(Φ_c ⋆ f)(x) - f(x)| ≤ ∫ |Φ(z)| |f(x - c^(-1) z) - f(x)| dz`.

Rd.ae_czGood_self_le.name: Rd.ae_czGood_self_le
Rd.ae_czGood_self_le.docstring:
**The good part of `G` itself is bounded**: in dimension `n ≥ 1`, for an almost everywhere
measurable `G` with finite integral and `0 < t`, the good part of `G` in its own decomposition
at height `t` is at most `2^n t` almost everywhere: off `Ω` it is `G ≤ t`
(`Rd.cz_ae_le_of_notMem`), on a maximal big cube it is the mean `G_Q ≤ 2^n t`.

Rd.ae_comp_add_right.name: Rd.ae_comp_add_right
Rd.ae_comp_add_right.docstring: Translates of functions that agree almost everywhere agree almost everywhere.

Rd.add_sum_le_of_le_two_mul.name: Rd.add_sum_le_of_le_two_mul
Rd.add_sum_le_of_le_two_mul.docstring:
**The arithmetic of the reflection bound**: if `a ≤ 2X` and `b_k ≤ K (Y + dX)` for all `k`,
then `a + ∑_k b_k ≤ (2 + N K (1 + d)) (X + Y)` with `N` the number of indices.

Rd.add_smul_mem_of_mem_diffStepSet.name: Rd.add_smul_mem_of_mem_diffStepSet
Rd.add_smul_mem_of_mem_diffStepSet.docstring:
**Steps in a convex set**: if `x` and `x + r h` lie in the convex set `Ω`, so does `x + t h`
for `0 ≤ t ≤ r`.

Rd.add_conv_ae.name: Rd.add_conv_ae
Rd.add_conv_ae.docstring:
**Convolution is additive in the kernel** almost everywhere, for integrable kernels and
`f ∈ L_p`.
