The constant of the cross kernel `ψ_j ⋆ η_i`: the sum of the constants of the three cases,
`(1 + 2^(n+L')) C_s + C P I` with `C_s = Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossDualSupportConst L N`,
`C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.dualTailConst L L' N`, `P = Rd.lpBlockKernelDecayConst V (2N)` and
`I = Rd.peetreIntegral V N`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandSupportConst_.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandSupportConst_ne_top
Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandSupportConst_.docstring: The constant of the support case of `k_j ⋆ Θ_i` is finite.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandSupportConst.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandSupportConst
Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandSupportConst.docstring:
The constant `C (‖Θ‖_1 (1 + 4LR)^N + 2^N T)` of the support case of `k_j ⋆ Θ_i`, with
`C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.kernelSupConst L` and `T = Rd.tailConst bandKernelS 0 N`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandMomentConst_n.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandMomentConst_ne_top
Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandMomentConst_n.docstring: The constant of the moment case of `k_j ⋆ Θ_i` is finite.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandMomentConst.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandMomentConst
Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandMomentConst.docstring:
The constant `2 ‖g‖_1 (2R)^L (1 + 2LR)^N C` of the moment case of `k_j ⋆ Θ_i`, with
`C = Rd.schwartzDecayConst bandKernelS L N`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandConst_ne_top.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandConst_ne_top
Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of the cross kernel `k_j ⋆ Θ_i` is finite.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandConst.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandConst
Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandConst.docstring:
The constant of the cross kernel `k_j ⋆ Θ_i`: the sum of the constants of the moment case
and of the support case.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.conv_meansKernel_two_s.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.conv_meansKernel_two_succ_eq
Rd.LocalMeansBump.conv_meansKernel_two_s.docstring:
**Local means of order two by the gradient, at one point**: let `g_i = ∂_{e_i} f` weakly on an
open set `T`, `f ∈ L_p(T)`, and let `x - y ∈ T` for every `y` in the support of every
`(K_i)_{2^j}`. Then `(k_{j+1} ⋆ 1_T f)(x) = 2^(-j) ∑_i ((K_i)_{2^j} ⋆ 1_T g_i)(x)`: the kernel is
`2^(-j) ∑_i ∂_{e_i} (K_i)_{2^j}` (`Rd.LocalMeansBump.meansKernel_two_succ_apply`), and each
derivative moves to `f` (`Rd.conv_indicator_eq_mul_sum_of_eq_sum_iteratedLineDerivOp`).

Rd.LocalMeansBump.conv_lpBlockKernel_dua.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.conv_lpBlockKernel_dualKernel_ae_eq
Rd.LocalMeansBump.conv_lpBlockKernel_dua.docstring:
**The moment identity of `Φ` in the blocks**:
`ψ_{j'+2} ⋆ η_i = ψ_{j'+2} ⋆ (η_i - μ_{2^j'} ⋆ η_i)` almost everywhere, since
`ψ_{j'+2} ⋆ μ_{2^j'} = 0`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.continuous_scaledMomen.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.continuous_scaledMoment
Rd.LocalMeansBump.continuous_scaledMomen.docstring: The dilated moment kernels are continuous.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.continuous_partialSum_.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.continuous_partialSum_rep
Rd.LocalMeansBump.continuous_partialSum_.docstring: The representatives of the partial sums are continuous.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.continuous_meansKernel.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.continuous_meansKernel
Rd.LocalMeansBump.continuous_meansKernel.docstring: The local means kernels are continuous.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.continuous_conv_meansK.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.continuous_conv_meansKernel
Rd.LocalMeansBump.continuous_conv_meansK.docstring:
The pointwise local means `k_j ⋆ f` are continuous, since `k_j` is continuous with compact
support and `f` is locally integrable.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.contDiff_scaledMoment.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.contDiff_scaledMoment
Rd.LocalMeansBump.contDiff_scaledMoment.docstring: The dilated moment kernels are smooth.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.contDiff_momentKernel.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.contDiff_momentKernel
Rd.LocalMeansBump.contDiff_momentKernel.docstring: The moment kernel of a bump is smooth.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.centered.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.centered
Rd.LocalMeansBump.centered.docstring: The **centred bump** of radius `R > 0`: the normalised smooth bump function around `0`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpSynthConst_ne_top.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpSynthConst_ne_top
Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpSynthConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of the synthesis estimate is finite for `0 < s < L`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpSynthConst.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpSynthConst
Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpSynthConst.docstring:
The constant of the synthesis estimate,
`2 ‖m‖_1 (1 - 2^(-s))⁻¹ + C_η ((1 - 2^(-(L-s)))⁻¹ + (1 - 2^(-s))⁻¹)`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpRescale_radius.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpRescale_radius
Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpRescale_radius.docstring: The rescaled bump has radius `R / c`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpRescale.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpRescale
Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpRescale.docstring: The **rescaled bump** `c^n b(c ·)`, of radius `R / c`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpExtensionConst_ne_.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpExtensionConst_ne_top
Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpExtensionConst_ne_.docstring: The constant of the extension from one patch is finite for `1 < p < ∞`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpExtensionConst.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpExtensionConst
Rd.LocalMeansBump.bumpExtensionConst.docstring:
The constant `(2 ‖m‖_1 (1 - 2^(-1))⁻¹ + (∑_i C_i) A) C_b` of the extension from one patch, with
the constants `C_i = Rd.tlToSobolevConst p e_i` of the weak derivatives of `F^1_{p,2}` functions,
`A = Rd.LocalMeansBump.tlUpperConst b 2 p 2 1` and `C_b = Rd.LocalMeansBump.patchConst b p`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.blockByLocalMeansConst.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.blockByLocalMeansConst_ne_top
Rd.LocalMeansBump.blockByLocalMeansConst.docstring: The constant of the bound of the blocks by local means is finite.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.blockByLocalMeansConst.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.blockByLocalMeansConst
Rd.LocalMeansBump.blockByLocalMeansConst.docstring:
The constant `C_{L,L',n+1} C_{n,n+1}` of the bound of the blocks by local means: the constant
of the cross kernels `ψ_j ⋆ η_i` (`Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossDualConst`) at the decay order `n + 1`
times the constant of the maximal function bound (`Rd.decayMaximalConst`).

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_partialSu.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_partialSum_le
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_partialSu.docstring:
**Ball means of the partial sums of the reproducing formula**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`,
`f ∈ L_p`, all `J, j` and every `x`,
`d_j(m_{2^J} ⋆ m_{2^J} ⋆ f)(x) ≤ C ∑_{i ≤ J} c_{ji} M(k_i ⋆ f)(x)` with
`C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.diffByLocalMeansConst L`, since
`m_{2^J} ⋆ m_{2^J} ⋆ f = ∑_{i ≤ J} η_i ⋆ k_i ⋆ f` at every point
(`Rd.LocalMeansBump.sum_conv_dualKernel_localMean_apply`).

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_le_tsum_m.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_le_tsum_maximalFunction
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_le_tsum_m.docstring:
**Ball means by local means, pointwise**: for `L ≥ 1`, `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `f ∈ L_p`, almost
everywhere and for all levels `j`, `d_j f(x) ≤ C ∑_i c_{ji} M(k_i ⋆ f)(x)` with
`c_{ji} = 2^(-(j-i)L)` for `i ≤ j`, `c_{ji} = 1` for `i > j`, and
`C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.diffByLocalMeansConst L`. The bound holds for the partial sums of the
reproducing formula at every point, and passes to `f` by
`MeasureTheory.ae_le_of_le_add_of_tendsto_eLpNorm`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_le_tsum_a.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_le_tsum_add
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_le_tsum_a.docstring:
The bound of the ball means of `f` through the partial sums: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `f ∈ L_p`,
all `J, j` and every `x`,
`d_j f(x) ≤ C ∑_i c_{ji} M(k_i ⋆ f)(x) + d_j(f - m_{2^J} ⋆ m_{2^J} ⋆ f)(x)`, with
`C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.diffByLocalMeansConst L` (subadditivity, `Rd.ballMeanDiff_add_le`, with
the continuous partial sum as the measurable summand).

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_conv_dual.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_conv_dualKernel_le_of_lt
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_conv_dual.docstring:
**Ball means of `η_i ⋆ g`, coarse levels**: for `j < i`, a locally integrable `g` and every
`x`, `d_j(η_i ⋆ g)(x) ≤ C M|g|(x)` with `C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.diffByLocalMeansConst L`. The
difference is a sum of `L + 1` shifts `η_i ⋆ g(x + l h)` with binomial weights of sum `2^L`, and
the average of each shift over the ball is bounded by the maximal function
(`Rd.LocalMeansBump.laverage_enorm_conv_dualKernel_add_smul_le`).

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_conv_dual.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_conv_dualKernel_le_of_le
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_conv_dual.docstring:
**Ball means of `η_i ⋆ g`, fine levels**: for `i ≤ j`, a locally integrable `g` and every
`x`, `d_j(η_i ⋆ g)(x) ≤ C 2^(-(j-i)L) M|g|(x)` with
`C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.diffByLocalMeansConst L`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_conv_dual.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_conv_dualKernel_le
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanDiff_conv_dual.docstring:
**Ball means of `η_i ⋆ g`**: for all levels `i, j`, a locally integrable `g` and every `x`,
`d_j(η_i ⋆ g)(x) ≤ C c_{ji} M|g|(x)` with `c_{ji} = 2^(-(j-i)L)` for `i ≤ j`, `c_{ji} = 1` for
`i > j`, and `C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.diffByLocalMeansConst L`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanConst_ne_top.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanConst_ne_top
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of the bound of the local means by ball means is finite.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanConst.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanConst
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ballMeanConst.docstring:
The constant `sup |b| |B(0,1)| 2^(rn) (1 + 2^n)` of the bound of the local means by ball
means, with `r = ⌈R⌉₊`, the least natural number at least the radius `R` of the bump `b`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.atomic_decomposition_s.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.atomic_decomposition_smooth
Rd.LocalMeansBump.atomic_decomposition_s.docstring:
**Atomic decomposition into smooth atoms**: for every order `K` there is `A` such that for
every `F ∈ L_p` the terms of the reproducing formula are `η_j ⋆ (k_j ⋆ F) = ∑_m λ_{j,m} a_{j,m}`
with cell atoms that are smooth atoms on `V` of order `K`, radius factor `2LR + n` and
constant `A`, and `‖λ‖_{b^s_{p,q}}` is the local means quasi-norm.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.atomic_decomposition.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.atomic_decomposition
Rd.LocalMeansBump.atomic_decomposition.docstring:
**Atomic decomposition** (Schneider–Vybíral, Theorem 2.6, direction ⇒): for every order `r`
there is `C < ∞` such that for every `F ∈ L_p` the terms of the reproducing formula
`F = ∑_j η_j ⋆ (k_j ⋆ F)` (`Rd.LocalMeansBump.tendsto_sum_dual_localMean`) are
`η_j ⋆ (k_j ⋆ F) = ∑_m λ_{j,m} a_{j,m}` with the cell atoms, regular atoms of order and exponent
`r` with radius factor `2LR + n` and constant `C`; the coefficients have
`‖λ‖_{b^s_{p,q}} = ‖(2^(js) ‖k_j ⋆ F‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`, the local means quasi-norm.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.aemeasurable_lqNorm_co.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.aemeasurable_lqNorm_conv_meansKernel
Rd.LocalMeansBump.aemeasurable_lqNorm_co.docstring: The pointwise `ℓ_q` norm of the weighted local means is measurable.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_lqNorm_le_of_pointw.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_lqNorm_le_of_pointwise
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_lqNorm_le_of_pointw.docstring:
**The local means from a pointwise bound, almost everywhere**: let `F = φ` almost
everywhere, and let `2^{(j+1)s} |(k_{j+1} ⋆ φ)(x)| ≤ c ∑_i |((K_i)_{2^j} ⋆ h_i)(x)|` for the local
means kernels `k_j` of order `L`, every `x ∈ W` and every level `j`, with Schwartz kernels `K_i`
and functions `h_i`. Then almost everywhere
`‖(2^{js} |1_W (k_j ⋆ F)(x)|)_j‖_{ℓ_2} ≤ |1_W (k_0 ⋆ F)(x)| +
c ∑_i ‖(((K_i)_{2^j} ⋆ h_i)(x))_j‖_{ℓ_2}`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_localExtension_eq_o.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_localExtension_eq_of_ae_eq_indicator
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_localExtension_eq_o.docstring:
**The local extension agrees with `f` on `U`**: if `F = 1_T f` almost everywhere, `U ⊆ T`, the
dual kernels of order `L ≥ 1` at points of `U` only see `W` and the series of the local extension
converges, then `∑_j η_j ⋆ 1_W (k_j ⋆ F) = f` almost everywhere on `U`
(`Rd.LocalMeansBump.indicatorLp_localExtension_of_summable`).

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_localExtensionJet_e.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_localExtensionJet_eq
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_localExtensionJet_e.docstring:
**The local extension of a jet agrees with its value on `U`** if `U ⊆ T` and the dual kernels
at points of `U` only see `W` (`Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_localExtension_eq_of_ae_eq_indicator`).

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_lpBlock_sum_d.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_lpBlock_sum_dualKernel_le_tsum_maximalFunction
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_lpBlock_sum_d.docstring:
The bound of the blocks of a partial synthesis sum: for `L' ≥ 1`, every `J` and every family
`h_i ∈ L_p`, almost everywhere, `|Δ_j (∑_{i ≤ J} η_i ⋆ h_i)| ≤ C ∑_i c_{ji} M|h_i|` with
`c_{ji} = 2^(-(j-i)L')` for `i ≤ j`, `c_{ji} = 1` for `i > j`, and
`C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.blockByLocalMeansConst L L'`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_localMean_sum.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_localMean_sum_lpBlock_le
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_localMean_sum.docstring:
The bound of the local means by blocks for the partial sums of the block decomposition: for
every `J`, almost everywhere, `|k_j ⋆ (∑_{i < J} Δ_i f)| ≤ C ∑_i c_{ji} M(ψ_i ⋆ f)` with
`c_{ji} = 2^(-(j-i)L)` for `i ≤ j`, `c_{ji} = 1` for `i > j`, and
`C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.localMeansByBlockConst L`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_dualKernel_su.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_dualKernel_sub_conv_lpMomentScaled_le
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_dualKernel_su.docstring:
**The averaged differences of the dual kernels**: for `L' ≥ 1`, `i ≤ j' + 2` and almost
every `w`, `|η_i(w) - (μ_{2^j'} ⋆ η_i)(w)| ≤ C 2^(-(j'+2-i)L') 2^(in) (1 + 2^i ‖w‖)^(-N)` with
`C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.dualTailConst L L' N`, where `μ` is the moment kernel of order `L'` of
`Φ`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_dilatedBandKe.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_dilatedBandKernel_sub_conv_scaledMoment_le
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_dilatedBandKe.docstring:
**One scale of the moment case**: for `i ≤ k` and almost every `y`,
`|Θ_i(y) - (m_{2^k} ⋆ Θ_i)(y)| ≤ ‖g‖_1 C R^L 2^(-(k-i)L) (1 + L R)^N 2^(in)
(1 + 2^i ‖y‖)^(-N)` with `C = Rd.schwartzDecayConst bandKernelS L N`, by the averaged
differences of the moment kernel.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKer.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKernel_level_le_of_lt
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKer.docstring:
**A fine local mean of the atoms of one level**: for levels `j < i`, smooth atoms `a_{j,m}`
on `V` of level `j` and order `L ≥ 1` centred at the cells, with radius factor `d ≥ 0` and
constant `A`, and `f = ∑_m λ_{j,m} a_{j,m}` almost everywhere, almost everywhere
`|k_i ⋆ f(x)| ≤ C 2^(-(i-j)L) M(x)`, with `M` the maximal function of the step function of the
coefficients of level `j` and `C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.tlAtomFineConst L d A`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKer.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKernel_level_le
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKer.docstring:
**A local mean of the atoms of one level**: for smooth atoms `a_{j,m}` on `V` of level `j`
and order `L ≥ 1` centred at the cells, with radius factor `d ≥ 0` and constant `A`, and
`f = ∑_m λ_{j,m} a_{j,m}` almost everywhere, for every `i` almost everywhere
`|k_i ⋆ f(x)| ≤ C c_{ij} M(x)` with `c_{ij} = 2^(-(i-j)L)` for `j ≤ i`, `c_{ij} = 1` for `j > i`,
`M` the maximal function of the step function of the coefficients of level `j` and
`C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.tlAtomSynthesisConst L d A`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKer.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKernel_le_of_scaledMoment
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKer.docstring:
**Local means kernels from one scale**: for levels `j < i`, `f ∈ L_1` and a bound
`|f(x) - (m_{2^k} ⋆ f)(x)| ≤ C 2^(-(k-j)L) u(x)` almost everywhere at every scale `k ≥ j`,
almost everywhere `|k_i ⋆ f(x)| ≤ 2 · 2^L C 2^(-(i-j)L) u(x)`. The kernel
`k_i = m_{2^i} - m_{2^(i-1)}` is a difference of two moment kernels, so
`k_i ⋆ f = (f - m_{2^(i-1)} ⋆ f) - (f - m_{2^i} ⋆ f)`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKer.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKernel_dilatedBandKernel_le_of_lt
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKer.docstring:
**The moment case**: for `i < j` and almost every `y`,
`|(k_j ⋆ Θ_i)(y)| ≤ C 2^(-(j-i)L) 2^(in) (1 + 2^i ‖y‖)^(-N)` with
`C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.crossBandMomentConst L N`. The kernel `k_j = m_{2^j} - m_{2^(j-1)}` is
a difference of two moment kernels
(`Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKernel_le_of_scaledMoment`), and `Θ_i - m_{2^k} ⋆ Θ_i`
averages differences of order `L` of `Θ_i` with steps of length at most `2^(-k) R`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKer.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKernel_atom_le_of_lt
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKer.docstring:
**A fine local mean of an atom**: for a smooth atom `a` on `V` of level `j < i` and order
`L ≥ 1` with centre `c`, radius factor `d` and constant `A`, almost everywhere
`|k_i ⋆ a(x)| ≤ C 2^(-(i-j)L) 1_{|x - c| ≤ (d + LR) 2^(-j)}` with
`C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.momentAtomConst L A`. The kernel `k_i = m_{2^i} - m_{2^(i-1)}` is a
difference of two moment kernels (`Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_meansKernel_le_of_scaledMoment`),
each of which reproduces `a` up to averaged differences of order `L` with steps of length at most
`2^(1-i) R`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_lpBlockK.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_lpBlockKernel_dualKernel_le_of_two_le
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_conv_lpBlockK.docstring:
**The case `i ≤ j`, `j ≥ 2`**: for `L' ≥ 1` and almost every `y`,
`|(ψ_j ⋆ η_i)(y)| ≤ C P I 2^(-(j-i)L') 2^(in) (1 + 2^i ‖y‖)^(-N)` with
`C = Rd.LocalMeansBump.dualTailConst L L' N`, `P = Rd.lpBlockKernelDecayConst V (2N)` and
`I = Rd.peetreIntegral V N`: by the moment identity of `Φ`, the averaged differences of `η_i`
and the convolution of two Peetre bumps.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_atom_sub_conv.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_atom_sub_conv_scaledMoment_le
Rd.LocalMeansBump.ae_enorm_atom_sub_conv.docstring:
**One scale of the moment identity for an atom**: for a smooth atom `a` on `V` of level `j`
and order `L ≥ 1` with centre `c`, radius factor `d` and constant `A`, and `k ≥ j`, almost
everywhere
`|a(x) - (m_{2^k} ⋆ a)(x)| ≤ ‖g‖_1 2^L L^(L+1) A R^L 2^(-(k-j)L) 1_{|x - c| ≤ (d + LR) 2^(-j)}`,
by the averaged differences of the moment kernel `m` of the bump `g`.

Rd.LocalMeansBump.actsBounded_lmRemainde.name: Rd.LocalMeansBump.actsBounded_lmRemainder
Rd.LocalMeansBump.actsBounded_lmRemainde.docstring:
**The remaining polynomial acts boundedly**: it acts on `L_p` with norm at most `(2^L + 1)^d`
(`Rd.actsBounded_momentPoly`, `Rd.actsBounded_addPoly`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.volume_abs_graphHeight.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.volume_abs_graphHeight_le_inter_closedBall
Rd.LipschitzGraph.volume_abs_graphHeight.docstring:
**The slab `{|η| ≤ δ}` inside a ball**: `|{|η| ≤ δ} ∩ B̄(c, ρ)| ≤ 2 δ ρ^(n-1) |B^H_1|` for
`ρ ≥ 0` and every real `δ`, with `B^H_1` the unit ball of the hyperplane `H = e^⊥` of dimension
`n - 1`; for `δ < 0` the set is empty and the bound reads `0`. In graph
coordinates `(x', t)` the set lies in `B̄^H(Pc, ρ) × [-δ, δ]`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphHeight_graphEquiv`,
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphProj_graphEquiv`, `‖P‖ ≤ 1`), and the graph coordinates preserve the
Lebesgue measure (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_graphEquiv`; Mathlib's
`MeasurePreserving.measure_preimage_equiv`, for every set).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.vertCutoff_halfSpaceGr.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.vertCutoff_halfSpaceGraph
Rd.LipschitzGraph.vertCutoff_halfSpaceGr.docstring: The vertical cut-off of the flat graph is `v_j(x) = χ(2^j ⟪x, e⟫)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.vertCutoff_graphMap.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.vertCutoff_graphMap
Rd.LipschitzGraph.vertCutoff_graphMap.docstring:
**The vertical cut-off is `1` on the boundary**: `v_j(γ x') = 1`, since
`|ψ_j(γ x')| = 2^j |φ(x') - φ_j(x')| ≤ 2 M ‖ρ‖_1 < c`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.vertCutoff_eq_zero.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.vertCutoff_eq_zero
Rd.LipschitzGraph.vertCutoff_eq_zero.docstring:
**The vertical cut-off vanishes far from the smoothed graph**: `v_j(x) = 0` if
`|⟪x, e⟫ - φ_j(Px)| ≥ (c + 1) 2^(-j)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.vertCutoffConst.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.vertCutoffConst
Rd.LipschitzGraph.vertCutoffConst.docstring: The constant `B` of the differences of the vertical cut-off.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.unflatten_eq.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.unflatten_eq
Rd.LipschitzGraph.unflatten_eq.docstring:
**The inverse flattening in coordinates**: `y ↦ y + φ(y) e` is the graph coordinates
`(x', t) ↦ γ(x') + t e` after the inverse of the product coordinates `(x', t) ↦ x' + t e`, since
`φ` is constant along `e`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.unflatten.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.unflatten
Rd.LipschitzGraph.unflatten.docstring: The inverse of the flattening, `y ↦ y + φ(y) e`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.tsupport_dilate_divKer.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.tsupport_dilate_divKernel_subset
Rd.LipschitzGraph.tsupport_dilate_divKer.docstring:
**The divergence kernels of a cone-supported bump lie in the reflected closed cone**: for a bump
of radius `R` supported in `-K`, every dilate `(K_i)_{2^j}` of its divergence kernels is supported
in `{y : -y ∈ K̄, ‖y‖ ≤ 2R}`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.tsupport_coneMollifier.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.tsupport_coneMollifier_subset
Rd.LipschitzGraph.tsupport_coneMollifier.docstring:
The cone mollifier is supported in the open cone and in `B̄(0, 1/2)`: its closed support is
`B̄(e/4, ρ/2) ⊆ B(e/4, ρ) ⊆ K` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.ball_subset_graphCone`), and
`‖e/4‖ + ρ/2 ≤ 1/2`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceTerm_sub.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceTerm_sub
Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceTerm_sub.docstring: The traces of the terms are linear in `h`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceTerm_smul.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceTerm_smul
Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceTerm_smul.docstring:
The traces of the terms commute with complex scalars, since convolution does
(`Rd.conv_smul`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceTerm_ae.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceTerm_ae
Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceTerm_ae.docstring: The trace of a term agrees with `(η_j ⋆ h) ∘ γ` almost everywhere.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceTerm.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceTerm
Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceTerm.docstring: The trace of the `j`-th term `η_j ⋆ h` in `L_p(H)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceSeries.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceSeries
Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceSeries.docstring: The **trace of a series** `∑_j η_j ⋆ h_j`: `∑_j (η_j ⋆ h_j) ∘ γ` in `L_p(H)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceH1_ofSchwartz_ae.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceH1_ofSchwartz_ae
Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceH1_ofSchwartz_ae.docstring:
**The trace of a Schwartz function** is its restriction to the graph: `Tr w = w ∘ γ` almost
everywhere on `H` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_comp_graphMap`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceH1Linear.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceH1Linear
Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceH1Linear.docstring:
The trace of `H^1(V)` on the graph as a linear map, `U ↦ Tr(ι U)` for the `L_2` function
`ι U` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_sub`, `Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_smul`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceH1.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceH1
Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceH1.docstring:
**The trace of `H^1(V)` on a Lipschitz graph** as a bounded operator `H^1(V) → L_2(H)`,
`U ↦ Tr(ι U)` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.exists_enorm_graphTrace_toL2_le`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceFun_eq_tsum.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceFun_eq_tsum
Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceFun_eq_tsum.docstring:
**The trace of a term is the sum of the traces of its cell atoms**:
`(η_j ⋆ h)(γ x') = ∑_m λ'_{j,m} a_{j,m}(γ x')` with the coefficients of the cells meeting the
graph.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceFun.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceFun
Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceFun.docstring: The **trace of a term**: `x' ↦ (η_j ⋆ h)(γ x')`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceExtTerm_ae.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceExtTerm_ae
Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceExtTerm_ae.docstring: The level in `L_p` agrees with `F_j` almost everywhere.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceExtTerm.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceExtTerm
Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceExtTerm.docstring: The level `F_j` of the extension in `L_p(V)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceCoef.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceCoef
Rd.LipschitzGraph.traceCoef.docstring:
The **coefficients of the trace atoms**: `λ_{j,m}` for the cells whose atoms meet the graph,
`0` for the others.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.toOpens.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.toOpens
Rd.LipschitzGraph.toOpens.docstring:
The graph domain `Ω = {x : φ(x) < ⟪x, e⟫}` as an element of Mathlib's `Opens V`, the form in
which open sets carry weak derivatives.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.tendsto_sum_traceTerm.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.tendsto_sum_traceTerm
Rd.LipschitzGraph.tendsto_sum_traceTerm.docstring: The partial sums of the trace series converge to it.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.tendsto_graphTrace_rep.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.tendsto_graphTrace_reproducingSum
Rd.LipschitzGraph.tendsto_graphTrace_rep.docstring:
**The traces of the partial sums converge**: for `F` with a finite `B^{s+1/p}_{p,q}`-norm of
order `L > s + 1/p` on `V`, `Tr G_J → Tr F` in `L_p(H)`, by the approximation in `B^{1/p}_{p,1}`
and the continuity of the trace there.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.tendsto_graphTrace_of_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.tendsto_graphTrace_of_modNorm_sub_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.tendsto_graphTrace_of_.docstring:
**The trace along a convergent sequence**: if `F` and the `F_J` have finite intrinsic norms of
smoothness `s + 1/p`, `s > 0`, and `‖F - F_J‖_p + ‖(2^(k/p) ω_L(F - F_J, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_1} ≤ b_J`
with `b_J < ∞` and `b_J → 0`, then `Tr F_J → Tr F`: the trace is linear
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_sub`) and bounded by the norm of `B^{1/p}_{p,1}`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.enorm_graphTrace_le`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.summable_traceTerm.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.summable_traceTerm
Rd.LipschitzGraph.summable_traceTerm.docstring:
**The trace series converges absolutely** for `s > 0` and
`X = ‖(2^(j(s+1/p)) ‖h_j‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`: `‖(η_j ⋆ h_j) ∘ γ‖_{L_p(H)} ≤ K 2^(j/p) ‖h_j‖_p ≤
K X 2^(-js)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.summable_traceExtTerm.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.summable_traceExtTerm
Rd.LipschitzGraph.summable_traceExtTerm.docstring:
**The extension converges absolutely** for `s > 0` and a finite local means quasi-norm
`X = ‖(2^(js) ‖k_j ⋆ g‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`: `‖F_j‖_p ≤ K X 2^(-js)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.sum_traceFun_eq_conv.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.sum_traceFun_eq_conv
Rd.LipschitzGraph.sum_traceFun_eq_conv.docstring:
**The partial sums of the trace at a boundary point**:
`∑_{j ≤ J} (η_j ⋆ 1_Ω (k_j ⋆ f))(γ x') = (m_{2^J} ⋆ (m_{2^J} ⋆ f))(γ x')`: at boundary points the
cut-off does not matter (the kernels are supported in `-K` and `γ x' + K ⊆ Ω`), and the partial
sums of the reproducing formula are `m_{2^J} ⋆ m_{2^J} ⋆ f` at every point.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.sum_inner_mul_indicato.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.sum_inner_mul_indicator_flatDeriv
Rd.LipschitzGraph.sum_inner_mul_indicato.docstring:
**The chain rule collapses the basis sum**: for every `a` and `y`,
`∑_k ⟪a, e_k⟫ (1_{H₊}(D_{e_k})(y) + 1_{H₊}(D_{σ e_k})(σ y)) = 1_{H₊}(D_a)(y) + 1_{H₊}(D_{σ a})(σ y)`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.sum_inner_mul_flatDeriv` for the identity and for `σ`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.sum_inner_mul_flatDeri.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.sum_inner_mul_flatDeriv
Rd.LipschitzGraph.sum_inner_mul_flatDeri.docstring:
**The derivative in flat coordinates through the basis**: for a linear map `T`,
`∑_k ⟪a, e_k⟫ D_{T e_k} = D_{T a}`, since `a = ∑_k ⟪a, e_k⟫ e_k` (Mathlib's
`OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr'`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.subset_diffStepSet_of_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.subset_diffStepSet_of_coneSupported
Rd.LipschitzGraph.subset_diffStepSet_of_.docstring:
The steps of the averaged differences of a kernel supported in `-K` lie in the cone:
`Ω ⊆ Ω_{r h}` for `h = -c^(-1) z`, `c > 0` and `g(z) ≠ 0`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.subset_diffStepSet.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.subset_diffStepSet
Rd.LipschitzGraph.subset_diffStepSet.docstring: **Steps in the cone stay in `Ω`**: `Ω ⊆ Ω_{rh}` for `h ∈ K`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.sub_mem_patch_of_mem_c.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.sub_mem_patch_of_mem_closedCone
Rd.LipschitzGraph.sub_mem_patch_of_mem_c.docstring:
**Short steps into the reflected closed cone stay in a patch**: if `x ∈ Ω ∩ B(c, ρ - ε)`,
`-y ∈ K̄` and `‖y‖ ≤ ε`, then `x - y ∈ Ω ∩ B(c, ρ)` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.add_mem_of_mem_closedCone`
and the triangle inequality).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.smul_mem_graphCone.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.smul_mem_graphCone
Rd.LipschitzGraph.smul_mem_graphCone.docstring: The cone is closed under positive scaling.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.smul_mem_closedCone.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.smul_mem_closedCone
Rd.LipschitzGraph.smul_mem_closedCone.docstring: The closed cone is closed under nonnegative scaling.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.smoothGraph_halfSpaceG.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.smoothGraph_halfSpaceGraph
Rd.LipschitzGraph.smoothGraph_halfSpaceG.docstring: The mollified graph of the flat graph vanishes.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_lineDeriv_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_lineDeriv_eq_normal
Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_lineDeriv_.docstring:
**Gauss–Green with the unit normal**: `∫_Ω ∂_v g = ∫_H g(γ x') ⟪v, ν(x')⟫ √(1 + ‖∇φ(x')‖²) dx'`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_normalAt_mul_gramDensity`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_lineDeriv_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_lineDeriv_eq
Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_lineDeriv_.docstring:
**Gauss–Green on a Lipschitz graph domain, in chart form**: for `g ∈ C^1` with compact support
and every direction `v`, `∫_Ω ∂_v g = ∫_H g(γ x') n_v(x') dx'` with the normal weight
`n_v = ⟪∇φ, v⟫ - ⟪v, e⟫` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.normalWeight`). By Fubini in graph coordinates the
left side is `∫_H DΨ(γ x') v dx'` for the ray integral `Ψ` of `g`
(`Rd.fderiv_rayIntegral_apply`); write `v = Pv + ⟪v, e⟫ e`, use `DΨ e = -g` and the horizontal
identity (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.integral_fderiv_rayIntegral_graphMap`). With the surface measure it
reads `∫_Ω ∂_v g = ∫_Γ g ⟪v, ν⟫ dσ` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_lineDeriv_eq_surface`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_green_ofSc.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_green_ofSchwartz
Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_green_ofSc.docstring:
**Green's formula for Schwartz functions**: for Schwartz functions `w₁`, `w₂`, the first with
compact support, `∫_Ω (∂_v w₁) w₂ + w₁ ∂_v w₂ = ∫_H Tr w₁ · Tr w₂ · n_v`, Gauss–Green for the
product `w₁ w₂` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_lineDeriv_eq`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_green_bess.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_green_besselPotentialSpace
Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_green_bess.docstring:
**Green's formula for `H^1(V)` on a Lipschitz graph domain**: for `U, W ∈ H^1(V)` and every
direction `v`, `∫_Ω (∂_v U) W + U ∂_v W = ∫_H Tr U · Tr W · n_v` with the normal weight
`n_v = ⟪∇φ, v⟫ - ⟪v, e⟫`. Both sides are continuous on `H^1(V) × H^1(V)` and agree on the dense set
of pairs of compactly supported Schwartz functions (`Rd.dense_ofSchwartz_hasCompactSupport`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_domain_eq_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_domain_eq_of_measurePreserving
Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_domain_eq_.docstring:
**Integrals over `Ω` in coordinates**: if `T : H × ℝ → V` preserves the Lebesgue measures and
`T(x', t) ∈ Ω` iff `a(x') < t`, then `∫_Ω F = ∫_H ∫_{a(x')}^∞ F(T(x', t)) dt dx'` for every `F`
integrable on `Ω` (Fubini's theorem, Mathlib's `integral_prod`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_domain_eq_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_domain_eq_graphMap
Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_domain_eq_.docstring:
**Fubini in graph coordinates**: `∫_Ω F = ∫_H ∫_0^∞ F(γ(x') + t e) dt dx'` for every `F`
integrable on `Ω`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.rychkovExtension.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.rychkovExtension
Rd.LipschitzGraph.rychkovExtension.docstring:
**Rychkov's extension** `Ext f = ∑_j η_j ⋆ (1_Ω (k_j ⋆ f))`: the local extension of the cone
bump for `W = Ω`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension_sm.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension_smul
Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension_sm.docstring: The extension by reflection is homogeneous (`Rd.evenReflection_smul`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension_of.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension_of_mem
Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension_of.docstring: On the graph domain the extension by reflection of `u` is `u`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension_co.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension_congr_ae
Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension_co.docstring:
**The extension by reflection sees only the values on the graph domain**: if `u = u'` almost
everywhere on the graph domain, then their extensions by reflection agree almost everywhere on
`V`, since the inverse flattening maps `H₊` into the graph domain and the flattening, its inverse
and `σ` preserve Lebesgue measure (Mathlib's
`MeasureTheory.QuasiMeasurePreserving.ae_eq_comp`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension_ad.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension_add
Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension_ad.docstring: The extension by reflection is additive (`Rd.evenReflection_add`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtensionLin.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtensionLinearMap
Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtensionLin.docstring: **The extension by reflection as a linear map** on functions `V → ℂ`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension
Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension.docstring:
The **extension by reflection** of a function `u` on the graph domain `Ω`: the even reflection
(`Rd.evenReflection`) of `u ∘ F⁻¹` across `e^⊥` in the flat coordinates `F(x) = x - φ(x) e`, that
is `u` on `Ω` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension_of_mem`) and `u` after the graph reflection
below the graph (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension_of_lt`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionDeriv.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionDeriv
Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionDeriv.docstring:
The **derivative of the extension by reflection** along `v`: with `a = DF(x) v` for the
flattening `F`, `x ↦ 1_{H₊}(D_a)(F x) + 1_{H₊}(D_{σ a})(σ F x)`, where `D_w` is the derivative in
flat coordinates (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.flatDeriv`) and `σ` the reflection across `e^⊥`. It is the
weak derivative `∂_v` of the extension by reflection on `V`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasWeakLineDeriv_reflectionExtension`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.profileConst.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.profileConst
Rd.LipschitzGraph.profileConst.docstring: A bound `C` of the derivatives of the profile up to order `2`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.profileBump.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.profileBump
Rd.LipschitzGraph.profileBump.docstring: The smooth bump of the profile: `1` on `[-c, c]`, `0` outside `(-(c + 1), c + 1)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.phi_sub_smul.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.phi_sub_smul
Rd.LipschitzGraph.phi_sub_smul.docstring: `φ` is constant along `e`, also backwards: `φ(x - t e) = φ(x)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.phi_graphProj.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.phi_graphProj
Rd.LipschitzGraph.phi_graphProj.docstring: `φ(Py) = φ(y)`: `φ` is constant in the direction `e`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.phi_add_le.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.phi_add_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.phi_add_le.docstring:
**The graph function along a step**: `φ(x + y) ≤ φ(x) + M ‖y - ⟪y, e⟫ e‖`, since `φ` is
constant along `e` and `M`-Lipschitz.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.phiH.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.phiH
Rd.LipschitzGraph.phiH.docstring: The graph function on the hyperplane, `φ|_H`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.patch_support_divKerne.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.patch_support_divKernel
Rd.LipschitzGraph.patch_support_divKerne.docstring:
**Boundary patches, the support condition for the divergence kernels**: for a bump supported in
`-K` with `2R ≤ ε`, `x - y ∈ Ω ∩ B(c, ρ)` for `x ∈ Ω ∩ B(c, ρ - ε)` and `y` in the support of a
dilated divergence kernel (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.sub_mem_patch_of_mem_closedCone`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.patch_support.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.patch_support
Rd.LipschitzGraph.patch_support.docstring:
**Boundary patches, the support condition**: for a bump supported in `-K` with `L R ≤ ε`, the
dual kernels at points of `Ω ∩ B(c, ρ - 2ε)` only see `Ω ∩ B(c, ρ - ε)`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.sub_mem_patch_of_mem_closedCone`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.patch_step.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.patch_step
Rd.LipschitzGraph.patch_step.docstring:
**Boundary patches, the step condition**: for a bump supported in `-K` with `L R ≤ ε`, the steps
`-c'^(-1) z`, `c' ≥ 1`, `b(z) ≠ 0`, take `Ω ∩ B(c, ρ - ε)` into `Ω ∩ B(c, ρ)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.orthogonal_hyperplane.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.orthogonal_hyperplane
Rd.LipschitzGraph.orthogonal_hyperplane.docstring:
The orthogonal complement of the hyperplane is the line `ℝ e` (Mathlib's
`Submodule.orthogonal_orthogonal`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.one_le_ofReal_gramDens.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.one_le_ofReal_gramDensity
Rd.LipschitzGraph.one_le_ofReal_gramDens.docstring: The Gram density `√(1 + ‖∇φ(x')‖²)` is at least `1`, as an element of `[0, ∞]`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.one_le_gramDensity.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.one_le_gramDensity
Rd.LipschitzGraph.one_le_gramDensity.docstring: The Gram density is at least `1`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.ofLocal.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.ofLocal
Rd.LipschitzGraph.ofLocal.docstring:
**A local graph as a Lipschitz graph domain**: for a point `z`, a unit vector `ν` and an
`L`-Lipschitz `φ` on `ν^⊥`, the Lipschitz graph domain with direction `ν`, constant `L` and graph
function `x ↦ ⟪z, ν⟫ + φ(P(x - z))`. It is constant along `ν` since `P ν = 0` (Mathlib's
`Submodule.orthogonalProjectionOnto_orthogonalComplement_singleton_eq_zero`), and `L`-Lipschitz
since `‖P y‖ ≤ ‖y‖`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.normalWeight.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.normalWeight
Rd.LipschitzGraph.normalWeight.docstring:
The **normal weight** `n_v(x') = ⟪∇φ(x'), v⟫ - ⟪v, e⟫` of the direction `v` in the chart: the
boundary term of `∫_Ω ∂_v g` is `∫_H g(γ x') n_v(x') dx'`, and
`n_v = ⟪v, ν⟫ √(1 + ‖∇φ‖²)` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_normalAt_mul_gramDensity`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.normalAt.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.normalAt
Rd.LipschitzGraph.normalAt.docstring:
The **outward unit normal** at the boundary point `γ x'`:
`ν(x') = (∇φ(x') - e) / √(1 + ‖∇φ(x')‖²)`. Where `φ|_H` is differentiable, it is the
normalised gradient at `γ x'` of `x ↦ φ(Px) - ⟪x, e⟫`, a function that is negative on `Ω`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_vertCutoff_second.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_vertCutoff_second_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_vertCutoff_second.docstring:
**Second differences of the vertical cut-off**:
`|v_j(x + 2h) - 2 v_j(x + h) + v_j(x)| ≤ B min(1, (2^j ‖h‖)^2)`. For `t = ψ_1 - ψ_0` with
`ψ_l = ψ_j(x + lh)`, `Δ_h^2 v_j(x) = [χ(ψ_2) - χ(2ψ_1 - ψ_0)] + Δ_t^2 χ(ψ_0)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_vertCutoff_add_su.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_vertCutoff_add_sub_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_vertCutoff_add_su.docstring:
**First differences of the vertical cut-off**: `|v_j(x + h) - v_j(x)| ≤ B min(1, 2^j ‖h‖)`,
from the Lipschitz bounds of the profile and of the vertical coordinate.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_sub_le_norm_graph.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_sub_le_norm_graphOver_sub
Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_sub_le_norm_graph.docstring:
**Graphs over the hyperplane are antilipschitz with constant `1`**:
`‖x' - y'‖ ≤ ‖γ_h x' - γ_h y'‖`, since `x' - y'` is the projection of `γ_h x' - γ_h y'` onto
`H`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_sub_graphProj_le.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_sub_graphProj_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_sub_graphProj_le.docstring: `‖x' - Pc‖ ≤ ‖γ x' - c‖`: the projection is a contraction.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_reflectionDeriv_l.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_reflectionDeriv_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_reflectionDeriv_l.docstring:
**The pointwise bound of the reflection derivative**: with `S(y) = ∑_i |g_i(F⁻¹ y)|`,
`|∂_v E(x)| ≤ (1 + M)² ‖v‖ (1_{H₊}(S)(F x) + 1_{H₊}(S)(σ F x))`, since `‖DF(x) v‖ ≤ (1 + M) ‖v‖`,
`σ` preserves norms and `Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_flatDeriv_le`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_normalAt.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_normalAt
Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_normalAt.docstring: The normal is a unit vector.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_le_norm_graphMap_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_le_norm_graphMap_add_smul
Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_le_norm_graphMap_.docstring: `‖x'‖ ≤ ‖γ(x') + t e‖`: `x'` is the projection of `γ(x') + t e` onto `H`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_le_norm_coe_add_s.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_le_norm_coe_add_smul_e
Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_le_norm_coe_add_s.docstring: `‖x'‖ ≤ ‖x' + a e‖` for `x' ∈ H`, since `x'` is the projection of `x' + a e` onto `H`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_iteratedFDeriv_pr.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_iteratedFDeriv_profile_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_iteratedFDeriv_pr.docstring: The derivatives of the profile up to order `2` are bounded by `C`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_higherDiff_vertCu.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_higherDiff_vertCutoff_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_higherDiff_vertCu.docstring:
**Differences of the vertical cut-off**: `|Δ_h^m v_j| ≤ B min(1, (2^j ‖h‖)^m)` for
`m ≤ 2` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_vertCutoff_add_sub_le`,
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_vertCutoff_second_le`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_graphMap_sub_le.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_graphMap_sub_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_graphMap_sub_le.docstring: **The graph map is Lipschitz**: `‖γ x' - γ y'‖ ≤ (1 + M) ‖x' - y'‖`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_graphMap_sub_cell.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_graphMap_sub_cellCenter_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_graphMap_sub_cell.docstring:
**The centres of the trace atoms lie near the graph**: if the cell atom `a_{j,m}` of `K ⋆ g`,
`K = 0` outside `B(0, ρ 2^(-j))`, does not vanish on the graph and the projection of its centre lies
within `(d + t) 2^(-j)` of `x'`, `d = ρ + n`, then the centre lies within
`(d + (1 + M)(2d + t)) 2^(-j)` of `γ x'`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_graphFun_sub_le.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_graphFun_sub_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_graphFun_sub_le.docstring: The graph function is Lipschitz with constant `M` on `H`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_flatDeriv_le.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_flatDeriv_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_flatDeriv_le.docstring:
**The pointwise bound of the derivative in flat coordinates**:
`|D_w(y)| ≤ (1 + M) ‖w‖ ∑_i |g_i(F⁻¹ y)|`, since `F⁻¹` is `(1 + M)`-Lipschitz (Mathlib's
`norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz`) and `‖e_i‖ = 1`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_coe_add_smul_e_sq.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_coe_add_smul_e_sq
Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_coe_add_smul_e_sq.docstring: **Pythagoras**: `‖x' + a e‖² = ‖x'‖² + a²` for `x' ∈ H`, since `x' ⊥ e`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.normDet_linearGraph.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.normDet_linearGraph
Rd.LipschitzGraph.normDet_linearGraph.docstring:
**The norm determinant of a linear graph** is `√(1 + ‖g‖²)` (Mathlib's
`LinearMap.normDet`, the volume factor `√(det(S_g* S_g))` of a linear map between spaces of
different dimensions): `S_g* S_g` is a transvection of determinant `1 + ⟪g, g⟫`
(Mathlib's `LinearMap.normDet_sq` and `LinearMap.transvection.det`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceSeries_le.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceSeries_le_of_atoms
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceSeries_le.docstring:
**The trace of a series from trace atoms of order `r`**: let `0 < s < r`, and let the
restrictions `a_{j,m} ∘ γ` of the cell atoms of `η_j ⋆ h`, for every level `j` and `h ∈ L_p`, be
regular atoms on `H` of order and exponent `r` with radius factor `d` and constant `C < ∞`,
centred at `P c_{j,m}`, and for every `x' ∈ H` let at most `N` of the centres `P c_{j,m}` with
nonzero coefficient `λ'_{j,m}` lie within `(d + r) 2^(-j)` of `x'`. Then
there is `K < ∞` such that the trace `Tr = ∑_j (η_j ⋆ h_j) ∘ γ` has
`‖Tr‖_{L_p(H)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(Tr, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ K ‖(2^(j(s+1/p)) ‖h_j‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`,
by the atomic synthesis on `H` (`Rd.modNorm_le_coeffNorm`) and
`2^(j(s-(n-1)/p)) ‖λ'_{j,·}‖_{ℓ_p} ≤ 2^(j(s+1/p)) ‖h_j‖_p`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceSeries_le.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceSeries_le_halfSpaceGraph
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceSeries_le.docstring:
**The trace of a series, of every order**: on the flat graph, for `0 < s < r` there is
`K < ∞` with `‖Tr‖_{L_p(H)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(Tr, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤
K ‖(2^(j(s+1/p)) ‖h_j‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}` for the trace `Tr = ∑_j (η_j ⋆ h_j) ∘ γ`, from the trace
atoms of order `r` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.exists_trace_atoms_halfSpaceGraph`,
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceSeries_le_of_atoms`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceSeries_le.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceSeries_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceSeries_le.docstring:
**The trace of a series** (Schneider–Vybíral, Theorem 4.2): for `0 < s < 1`
there is `K < ∞` such that the trace `Tr = ∑_j (η_j ⋆ h_j) ∘ γ` has
`‖Tr‖_{L_p(H)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_1(Tr, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ K ‖(2^(j(s+1/p)) ‖h_j‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`,
by the atomic synthesis on `H` with the trace atoms of order `1`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.exists_trace_atoms`, `Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceSeries_le_of_atoms`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceExtTerm_l.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceExtTerm_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceExtTerm_l.docstring:
**One level of the extension**: for a package of extended atoms of order `r`, `0 < σ < r`,
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `g ∈ L_p(H)` and every level `j`,
`‖F_j‖_p + ‖(2^(kσ) ω_r(F_j, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ K_σ 2^(j(σ - 1/p)) ‖k_j ⋆ g‖_p` with
`K_σ = Rd.atomSynthConst p N C r σ r`: the level is a sum of the extended atoms
(`Rd.modNorm_level_le`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_rychkovExtensi.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_rychkovExtension_le_modNormOn
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_rychkovExtensi.docstring:
**Rychkov's extension is bounded in the moduli**: for `s > 0`,
`‖Ext f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(Ext f, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤
C (‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})`, with `C` finite for `s < r`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_rychkovExtensi.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_rychkovExtension_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_rychkovExtensi.docstring:
**The extension satisfies the Besov condition by differences**: for `0 < s < L`,
`‖Ext f‖_p + ‖(2^(is) ω_L(Ext f, 2^(-i))_p)_i‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C ‖(2^(js) ‖1_Ω (k_j ⋆ f)‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_one_traceExtTe.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_one_traceExtTerm_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_one_traceExtTe.docstring:
**One level of the extension in `B^{1/p}_{p,1}` of order `L`**: for a package of extended
atoms of order `r ≤ L`, `s > 0` with `s + 1/p < r` and every level `j`,
`‖F_j‖_p + ‖(2^(k/p) ω_L(F_j, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_1} ≤ 2^(L-r) K_{1/p} ‖k_j ⋆ g‖_p` with
`K_{1/p} = Rd.atomSynthConst p N C r (1/p) r` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceExtTerm_le`,
`Rd.modNorm_order_le_of_le`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphTrace_le_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphTrace_le_halfSpaceGraph
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphTrace_le_.docstring:
**The trace theorem of every order on the half-space**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < r` and
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` there is `K < ∞` with
`‖Tr f‖_{L_p(H)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(Tr f, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤
K (‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)} + ‖(2^(k(s+1/p)) ω_L(f, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphTrace_le.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphTrace_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphTrace_le.docstring:
**The trace theorem on Lipschitz graph domains** (Schneider–Vybíral, Theorem 4.2,
for `p ≥ 1`): for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < 1` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` there is `K < ∞` with
`‖Tr f‖_{L_p(H)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_1(Tr f, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤
K (‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)} + ‖(2^(k(s+1/p)) ω_L(f, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension_lt_top_of_atoms
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension.docstring:
**The finite norms along the extension**: for a package of extended atoms of order `r ≤ L`
with constant `C < ∞`, `s > 0` with `s + 1/p < r` and a finite local means quasi-norm of `g`, the
extension and its partial sums have finite norms with moduli of order `L` and smoothness `s + 1/p`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension_le_localMeansNorm`,
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_traceExtTerm_le`, `Rd.modNorm_order_le_of_le`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension_lt_top
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension.docstring:
**The extension has a finite norm of every order `L ≥ 2`**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < 1`,
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and `g ∈ B^s_{p,q}(H)`, the extension of moment order `1` has
`‖E g‖_p + ‖(2^(k(s+1/p)) ω_L(E g, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension_le`, `Rd.modNorm_order_le_of_le`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension_le_of_atoms
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension.docstring:
**The extension is bounded by the moduli of `g`**: for a package of extended atoms of order
`r`, `s > 0`, `s + 1/p < r` and every `g` with a finite right side,
`‖E g‖_p + ‖(2^(k(s+1/p)) ω_r(E g, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤
K (‖g‖_{L_p(H)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_{Lh}(g, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})` with
`K = Rd.atomSynthConst p N C r (s + 1/p) r · upperConst Lh s`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension_le_localMeansNorm`,
`Rd.LocalMeansBump.localMeansNorm_le`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension_le_localMeansNorm
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension.docstring:
**The extension is bounded by the local means**: for a package of extended atoms of order `r`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.HasExtensionAtoms`), `s > 0`, `s + 1/p < r` and every `g` with a finite local
means quasi-norm,
`‖E g‖_p + ‖(2^(k(s+1/p)) ω_r(E g, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ K ‖(2^(js) ‖k_j ⋆ g‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}` with
`K = Rd.atomSynthConst p N C r (s + 1/p) r`, by the atomic synthesis on `V`
(`Rd.modNorm_le_coeffNorm`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension.docstring:
**The extension is bounded** (Schneider–Vybíral, Theorem 4.10, for `p ≥ 1`): for `0 < s < 1`
there is `K < ∞` with
`‖E g‖_p + ‖(2^(k(s+1/p)) ω_2(E g, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤
K (‖g‖_{L_p(H)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_1(g, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})` for the extension of moment order `1`, by
the atomic synthesis on `V` with the extended atoms of order `2`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_flatExtension_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_flatExtension_le_localMeansNorm
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_flatExtension_.docstring:
**The extension of every order is bounded by the local means**: for the flat graph, `s > 0`
and `s + 1/p < r` there is `K < ∞` with
`‖E g‖_p + ‖(2^(k(s+1/p)) ω_r(E g, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ K ‖(2^(js) ‖k_j ⋆ g‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}` for the
extension `E g` of moment order `Lh` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphExtension`), from the extended atoms
of order `r` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension_le_localMeansNorm`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNormOn_le_modNorm.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNormOn_le_modNorm
Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNormOn_le_modNorm.docstring:
**The moduli on `Ω` are at most those of every function that agrees with `f` on `Ω`**: if
`1_Ω F = 1_Ω f`, then `‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤
‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q}`; the case `O = Ω` of
`Rd.modNormOn_le_modNorm_of_indicatorLp`, since the cut-off is `indicatorLp`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.mem_graphCone_of_mem_t.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.mem_graphCone_of_mem_tsupport_dilate
Rd.LipschitzGraph.mem_graphCone_of_mem_t.docstring:
**Dilates of a cone kernel are cone kernels**: if the closed support of `η` lies in the cone
`K` and `c > 0`, so does the closed support of `η_c`, since `c x ∈ supp η` for `x ∈ supp η_c`
(`Rd.smul_mem_tsupport_of_mem_tsupport_dilate`) and `c⁻¹ K ⊆ K`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.smul_mem_graphCone`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.mem_frontier_domain_if.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.mem_frontier_domain_iff
Rd.LipschitzGraph.mem_frontier_domain_if.docstring:
**The boundary of a graph domain is the graph**: `y ∈ ∂Ω` iff `γ(Py) = y`, since the
closure of `Ω` is `{φ ≤ ⟪·, e⟫}` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.closure_domain`) and `Ω` is open.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.mem_domain_iff_graphHe.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.mem_domain_iff_graphHeight_pos
Rd.LipschitzGraph.mem_domain_iff_graphHe.docstring: `x` lies in the graph domain iff its height is positive.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.memLp_traceFun.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.memLp_traceFun
Rd.LipschitzGraph.memLp_traceFun.docstring: The traces of the terms are in `L_p(H)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.memLp_top_normalWeight.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.memLp_top_normalWeight
Rd.LipschitzGraph.memLp_top_normalWeight.docstring:
The normal weight is a bounded function, an element of `L_∞(H)`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.abs_normalWeight_le`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.memLp_extLevel.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.memLp_extLevel
Rd.LipschitzGraph.memLp_extLevel.docstring: The levels of the extension are in `L_p`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_unfl.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_unflatten
Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_unfl.docstring:
**The inverse flattening preserves the Lebesgue measure** for every Lipschitz graph
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_graphEquiv`,
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_graphProdEquiv`): it is a shear along `e` in the product
coordinates.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_grap.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_graphShear
Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_grap.docstring:
The shear preserves the Lebesgue measure of `H × ℝ`: it translates each vertical line
(Mathlib's `MeasurePreserving.skew_product`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_grap.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_graphProdEquiv
Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_grap.docstring:
**The product coordinates preserve the Lebesgue measure**: `(x', t) ↦ x' + t e` carries the
product of the Lebesgue measures of `H` and `ℝ` to the Lebesgue measure of `V` (Mathlib's
`Submodule.measurePreserving_measurableEquivProd`,
`InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume` and
`LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_grap.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_graphFlatten
Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_grap.docstring:
**The flattening preserves the Lebesgue measure** for every Lipschitz graph, the inverse of
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_unflatten`: it is the product coordinates after the inverse of
the graph coordinates (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphFlatten_eq`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_grap.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_graphEquiv
Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurePreserving_grap.docstring: The graph coordinates preserve the Lebesgue measure.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurable_normalAt.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurable_normalAt
Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurable_normalAt.docstring: The outward unit normal is measurable.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurableSet_goodSet.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurableSet_goodSet
Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurableSet_goodSet.docstring:
The good sets are measurable: the differentiability set is measurable (Mathlib's
`measurableSet_of_differentiableAt`), the gradient is measurable, and the Taylor condition
quantifies over the countable dense sequence only.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurableEmbedding_gr.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurableEmbedding_graphMap
Rd.LipschitzGraph.measurableEmbedding_gr.docstring:
The graph map is a measurable embedding: an antilipschitz uniformly continuous map from the
complete space `H` is a closed embedding.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.mapsTo_unflatten_inter.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.mapsTo_unflatten_inter_ball
Rd.LipschitzGraph.mapsTo_unflatten_inter.docstring:
**The inverse flattening on bounded parts**: `F⁻¹` maps `H₊ ∩ B(0, R)` into
`Ω ∩ B(0, ‖F⁻¹ 0‖ + (1 + M) R)`, since it is `(1 + M)`-Lipschitz (Mathlib's
`LipschitzWith.mapsTo_ball`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.mapsTo_unflatten.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.mapsTo_unflatten
Rd.LipschitzGraph.mapsTo_unflatten.docstring:
**The inverse flattening maps the half-space into the domain**: `⟪y, e⟫ > 0` gives
`y + φ(y) e ∈ Ω`, since its flattening is `y`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.mapsTo_graphFlatten.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.mapsTo_graphFlatten
Rd.LipschitzGraph.mapsTo_graphFlatten.docstring:
**The flattening maps the domain into the half-space** `H₊ = {⟪y, e⟫ > 0}`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_graphFlatten`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.map_graphMap_withDensi.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.map_graphMap_withDensity
Rd.LipschitzGraph.map_graphMap_withDensi.docstring:
**The area formula in measure form**: the image under the graph map of the measure on `H`
with density `√(1 + ‖∇φ‖²)` is `μHE[n-1]` restricted to the graph `γ(H)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.lipschitzWith_unflatte.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.lipschitzWith_unflatten
Rd.LipschitzGraph.lipschitzWith_unflatte.docstring:
**The inverse flattening is Lipschitz**: `y ↦ y + φ(y) e` is `(1 + M)`-Lipschitz, since `φ`
is `M`-Lipschitz and `‖e‖ = 1`. On the hyperplane `e^⊥` this is
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.norm_graphMap_sub_le`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.lipschitzWith_phi.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.lipschitzWith_phi
Rd.LipschitzGraph.lipschitzWith_phi.docstring: The graph function `φ` is `M`-Lipschitz, in the form of Mathlib's `LipschitzWith`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.lipschitzWith_graphPro.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.lipschitzWith_graphProj_graphMap
Rd.LipschitzGraph.lipschitzWith_graphPro.docstring: The change of chart `P₁ ∘ γ₂` is Lipschitz with constant `1 + M₂`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.lipschitzWith_graphMap.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.lipschitzWith_graphMap
Rd.LipschitzGraph.lipschitzWith_graphMap.docstring: The graph map is Lipschitz with constant `1 + M`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.lipschitzWith_graphFla.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.lipschitzWith_graphFlatten
Rd.LipschitzGraph.lipschitzWith_graphFla.docstring:
**The flattening is Lipschitz**: `x ↦ x - φ(x) e` is `(1 + M)`-Lipschitz, since `φ` is
`M`-Lipschitz and `‖e‖ = 1`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.lintegral_graphMap.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.lintegral_graphMap
Rd.LipschitzGraph.lintegral_graphMap.docstring:
**The area formula in integral form**: for every `F : V → [0, ∞]`,
`∫_{γ(H)} F dμHE[n-1] = ∫_H F(γ x') √(1 + ‖∇φ(x')‖²) dx'`. The formula holds for every `F`,
measurable or not, since `γ` is a measurable embedding and the density is finite.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.lintegral_gramDensity_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.lintegral_gramDensity_le_mul
Rd.LipschitzGraph.lintegral_gramDensity_.docstring:
**Lower bound for a fixed accuracy**: for `ε > 0` and measurable `A ⊆ H`,
`∫_A √(1 + ‖∇φ‖²) ≤ C_ε μHE[m] (γ '' A)` with the area factor `C_ε = (1 + 2ε)^m (1 + ε)`: the
integral over the null rest of `A` vanishes, and the images `γ '' (A ∩ Q_n)` are disjoint and
measurable, since `γ` is an injective measurable embedding.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.linearGraph.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.linearGraph
Rd.LipschitzGraph.linearGraph.docstring:
The **linear graph** `S_g x' = x' + ⟪g, x'⟫ e` of `g ∈ H`, the graph of the linear function
`⟪g, ·⟫` over the hyperplane, as a linear map from `H` to `V`: the inclusion of `H` plus the
rank-one map `x' ↦ ⟪g, x'⟫ e`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.lineEquiv.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.lineEquiv
Rd.LipschitzGraph.lineEquiv.docstring:
The isometry `t ↦ t e` of `ℝ` onto the orthogonal complement `H^⊥ = ℝ e` of the hyperplane
(Mathlib's `LinearIsometryEquiv.toSpanUnitSingleton`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.lineDeriv_graphRayInte.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.lineDeriv_graphRayIntegral
Rd.LipschitzGraph.lineDeriv_graphRayInte.docstring:
**The line derivative of the ray integral from the graph**: where `φ|_H` is differentiable,
the chain rule and `DΨ e = -g` (`Rd.fderiv_rayIntegral_self`) give
`∂_{v'}(Ψ ∘ γ)(x') = DΨ(γ x') v' - ⟪∇φ(x'), v'⟫ g(γ x')` for `v' ∈ H`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.isSmoothAtom_comp_grap.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.isSmoothAtom_comp_graphMap_halfSpaceGraph
Rd.LipschitzGraph.isSmoothAtom_comp_grap.docstring:
**Restrictions of smooth atoms to the hyperplane**: for the flat graph, a smooth atom on `V`
of order `K` with centre `c` restricts to a smooth atom on `H` of order `K` with centre `P c`,
the same radius factor and the same constant.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.isRegularAtom_extendAt.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.isRegularAtom_extendAtom
Rd.LipschitzGraph.isRegularAtom_extendAt.docstring:
**Extended atoms are regular atoms** of order and exponent `2` on `V`: if `a` is continuous,
vanishes outside `B̄(c', d 2^(-j))` and `|Δ_h^l a| ≤ A_0 min(1, (2^j ‖h‖)^l)` for `l ≤ 2`, then
`A = (a ∘ P) v_j` is a regular atom of level `j` with centre `c' + φ_j(c') e`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.isRegularAtom_comp_gra.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.isRegularAtom_comp_graphMap
Rd.LipschitzGraph.isRegularAtom_comp_gra.docstring:
**Traces of atoms** (as in the proof of Schneider–Vybíral, Theorem 4.2): if `a` is continuous,
vanishes outside `B̄(c, d 2^(-j))`, `|a| ≤ A` and `|a(x + h) - a(x)| ≤ A min(1, 2^j ‖h‖)`, then
`a ∘ γ` is a regular atom of order and exponent `1` on `H` with centre `Pc`, radius factor `d` and
constant `(1 + M) A (2 d^(n-1) |B_1|)^(1/p)`, since `γ` is Lipschitz with constant `1 + M`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.isGoodPiece_goodSet_in.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.isGoodPiece_goodSet_inter_ball
Rd.LipschitzGraph.isGoodPiece_goodSet_in.docstring:
**Good sets cut into small balls are good pieces**: on `goodSet ε i k ∩ B(c, 1/(2(k+1)))`
the increments of `φ|_H` are within `2ε ‖x' - y'‖` of those of `⟪u_i, ·⟫`: the Taylor bound at
`y'` and `‖∇φ(y') - u_i‖ < ε`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_toL2_lt_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_toL2_lt_top
Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_toL2_lt_.docstring:
The `L_2` functions of `H^1(V)` satisfy the hypothesis of the trace theorem on `Ω` at
`s = 1/2`, `p = q = 2` and order `2` (`Rd.modNorm_toL2_lt_top`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_sub_le.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_sub_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_sub_le.docstring: The intrinsic quasi-norm of a difference is at most the sum of the intrinsic quasi-norms.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_lt_top_o.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_lt_top_of_modNorm
Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_lt_top_o.docstring: A finite norm of order `L` on `V` gives a finite intrinsic norm of order `L` on `Ω`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_lt_top.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_lt_top
Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_lt_top.docstring: Finite intrinsic moduli give a finite intrinsic local means quasi-norm.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_le.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_le.docstring:
**The intrinsic local means are bounded by the moduli on `Ω`**:
`‖(2^(js) ‖1_Ω (k_j ⋆ f)‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ≤
C (‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)} + ‖(2^(js) ω_L(f, 2^(-j), Ω)_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q})`
(`ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_le_of_head_of_succ_le`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_finsetSu.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_finsetSum_lt_top
Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_finsetSu.docstring:
Finite sums of functions with finite intrinsic quasi-norms have finite intrinsic
quasi-norms.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_def.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_def
Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_def.docstring:
The intrinsic quasi-norm written with the cut-off:
`‖(2^(js) ‖1_Ω (k_j ⋆ f)‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_add_le.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_add_le
Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_add_le.docstring: The intrinsic quasi-norm of a sum is at most the sum of the intrinsic quasi-norms.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm
Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm.docstring:
The **intrinsic local means quasi-norm** `‖(2^(js) ‖1_Ω (k_j ⋆ f)‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`: the local
means quasi-norm of the cone bump on `Ω`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicConst_ne_top.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicConst_ne_top
Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicConst_ne_top.docstring:
The constant of the intrinsic upper bound is finite
(`Rd.LocalMeansBump.momentConst_ne_top` for the cone bump).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicConst.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicConst
Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicConst.docstring: The constant `‖m‖_1 + 2 ‖g‖_1` of the intrinsic upper bound.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.integral_mul_mul_norma.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.integral_mul_mul_normalWeight_eq
Rd.LipschitzGraph.integral_mul_mul_norma.docstring:
`∫_H a b n_v = ⟨a, n_v b⟩` for `a, b ∈ L_2(H)`, with the pairing of `L_2` with `L_2` and the
product of `L_∞` with `L_2` (Mathlib's `ContinuousLinearMap.holderL`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.integral_graphMap.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.integral_graphMap
Rd.LipschitzGraph.integral_graphMap.docstring:
**The area formula for complex integrals**: for every `F : V → ℂ`,
`∫_{γ(H)} F dμHE[n-1] = ∫_H F(γ x') √(1 + ‖∇φ(x')‖²) dx'`. It holds for every `F`, since `γ` is a
measurable embedding and the density is finite (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.map_graphMap_withDensity`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.integral_fderiv_rayInt.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.integral_fderiv_rayIntegral_graphMap
Rd.LipschitzGraph.integral_fderiv_rayInt.docstring:
**The horizontal directions**: for `g ∈ C^1` with compact support and `v' ∈ H`,
`∫_H DΨ(γ x') v' dx' = ∫_H ⟪∇φ(x'), v'⟫ g(γ x') dx'`. The ray integral from the graph `Ψ ∘ γ` is
Lipschitz with compact support, so its line derivative integrates to zero
(`Rd.integral_lineDeriv_eq_zero_complex`), and almost everywhere it is the difference of the
two integrands (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.lineDeriv_graphRayIntegral`, Rademacher's theorem for `φ|_H`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrable_inner_gradP.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrable_inner_gradPhi_mul
Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrable_inner_gradP.docstring: `x' ↦ ⟪∇φ(x'), v'⟫ g(γ x')` is integrable on `H` for continuous compactly supported `g`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrable_graphBump_m.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrable_graphBump_mul
Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrable_graphBump_m.docstring: The convolution integrals of the mollifiers with the graph function converge absolutely.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrable_fderiv_rayI.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrable_fderiv_rayIntegral
Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrable_fderiv_rayI.docstring:
`x' ↦ DΨ(γ x') v` is integrable on `H`: it is bounded (`Rd.exists_norm_fderiv_rayIntegral_le`)
and vanishes for `‖x'‖ > R` when `tsupport g ⊆ B̄(0, R)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrable_comp_graphM.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrable_comp_graphMap
Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrable_comp_graphM.docstring: `x' ↦ h(γ x')` is integrable on `H` for continuous compactly supported `h`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrableOn_flatDeriv.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrableOn_flatDeriv_inter_ball
Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrableOn_flatDeriv.docstring:
**Derivatives in flat coordinates on bounded parts**: if every `g_i` is integrable on every
bounded part `Ω ∩ B(0, R)` of `Ω`, then every `D_w` is integrable on every bounded part
`H₊ ∩ B(0, R)` of `H₊` (`Rd.eLpNorm_sum_inner_fderiv_mul_comp_le` for `p = 1`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrableOn_comp_unfl.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrableOn_comp_unflatten_inter_ball
Rd.LipschitzGraph.integrableOn_comp_unfl.docstring:
**Functions in flat coordinates on bounded parts**: if `f` is integrable on every bounded part
`Ω ∩ B(0, R)` of `Ω`, then `f ∘ F⁻¹` is integrable on every bounded part `H₊ ∩ B(0, R)` of `H₊`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.mapsTo_unflatten_inter_ball`, `Rd.eLpNorm_comp_le_of_mapsTo`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_normalAt_mul_gra.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_normalAt_mul_gramDensity
Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_normalAt_mul_gra.docstring:
**The normal weight by the unit normal**: `⟪v, ν(x')⟫ √(1 + ‖∇φ(x')‖²) = n_v(x')`, since
`ν = (∇φ - e)/√(1 + ‖∇φ‖²)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_linearGraph.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_linearGraph
Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_linearGraph.docstring:
**Inner products of a linear graph**:
`⟪S_g x', S_g y'⟫ = ⟪x', y'⟫ + ⟪g, x'⟫ ⟪g, y'⟫`, since `x', y' ⊥ e` and `‖e‖ = 1`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_graphMap.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_graphMap
Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_graphMap.docstring: `⟪γ x', e⟫ = φ(x')`: the graph map lands on the boundary.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_graphFlatten.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_graphFlatten
Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_graphFlatten.docstring: **The flattening lowers the height by the graph**: `⟪F(x), e⟫ = ⟪x, e⟫ - φ(x)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_gradPhi.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_gradPhi
Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_gradPhi.docstring:
`⟪∇φ(x'), v⟫` is the derivative of `φ|_H` at `x'` in the direction `v` (Mathlib's
`inner_gradient_left`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_coe_e.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_coe_e
Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_coe_e.docstring: The points of `H` are orthogonal to `e`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.hyperplane.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.hyperplane
Rd.LipschitzGraph.hyperplane.docstring: The **hyperplane** `H = e^⊥` over which the boundary of `Ω` is a graph.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasWeakLineDeriv_refle.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasWeakLineDeriv_reflectionExtension_of_integrableOn
Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasWeakLineDeriv_refle.docstring:
**The extension by reflection is weakly differentiable** (Evans–Gariepy, Section 4.4): if
`g_i = ∂_{e_i} f` weakly on the graph domain `Ω` and `f` and the `g_i` are integrable on every
bounded part `Ω ∩ B(0, R)` of `Ω`, then for every `v ∈ V` the derivative
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionDeriv` is the weak derivative `∂_v` of the extension by reflection on
`V`. The chain rule for the inverse flattening
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasWeakLineDeriv_comp_unflatten`), the even reflection on the half-space
(`Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_evenReflection_of_forall`) and the chain rule for the flattening
(`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.comp_lipschitzWith`) give it as a basis sum, which collapses by
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.sum_inner_mul_indicator_flatDeriv`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasWeakLineDeriv_refle.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasWeakLineDeriv_reflectionExtension
Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasWeakLineDeriv_refle.docstring:
**The extension by reflection of `W^1_p` functions**: for `1 ≤ p`, `f ∈ L_p(Ω)` with weak
derivatives `g_i = ∂_{e_i} f ∈ L_p(Ω)` on the graph domain `Ω`, and every `v ∈ V`, the derivative
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionDeriv` is the weak derivative `∂_v` of the extension by reflection on
`V` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasWeakLineDeriv_reflectionExtension_of_integrableOn`; `L_p` functions are
integrable on the bounded parts, `Rd.integrableOn_inter_ball_of_memLp`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasWeakLineDeriv_comp_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasWeakLineDeriv_comp_unflatten
Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasWeakLineDeriv_comp_.docstring:
**Weak derivatives in flat coordinates**: if `g_i = ∂_{e_i} f` weakly on `Ω`, then the
derivative in flat coordinates `Rd.LipschitzGraph.flatDeriv` is the weak derivative
`∂_w (f ∘ F⁻¹)` on `H₊` (the chain rule `Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.comp_lipschitzWith` for the
measure-preserving Lipschitz map `F⁻¹`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasFDerivAt_graphMap.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasFDerivAt_graphMap
Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasFDerivAt_graphMap.docstring:
**The derivative of the graph map**: where `φ|_H` is differentiable,
`Dγ(x') v' = v' + Dφ(x') v' e`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasCompactSupport_grap.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasCompactSupport_graphRayIntegral
Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasCompactSupport_grap.docstring: The ray integral from the graph of a compactly supported `g` has compact support in `H`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasBesovExtension.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasBesovExtension
Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasBesovExtension.docstring:
**Lipschitz graph domains have the extension property**: Rychkov's extension agrees with `f`
on the domain (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphCutoff_rychkovExtension_of_modNormOn`) and is bounded by a
constant times the intrinsic quasi-norm (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_rychkovExtension_le_modNormOn`);
the proof takes `C = G.coneBump.bumpSynthConst r s * G.intrinsicConst r`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.halfSpaceGraph_graphMa.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.halfSpaceGraph_graphMap
Rd.LipschitzGraph.halfSpaceGraph_graphMa.docstring: The graph map of the flat graph is the inclusion of `H = e^⊥`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.halfSpaceGraph.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.halfSpaceGraph
Rd.LipschitzGraph.halfSpaceGraph.docstring:
The **flat Lipschitz graph domain**: the open half-space `{x : 0 < ⟪x, e⟫}` for a unit
vector `e`, with graph function `0`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_sum_traceEx.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_sum_traceExtTerm
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_sum_traceEx.docstring:
**The traces of the partial sums of the extension** are the partial sums of the reproducing
formula on `H`: for `L ≥ 1`, `s > 0` and partial sums with a finite norm with moduli of order `L`
and smoothness `s + 1/p`, `Tr (∑_{j ≤ J} F_j) = ∑_{j ≤ J} η_j ⋆ (k_j ⋆ g)`, since the partial sums
are continuous with the values `∑_{j ≤ J} (η_j ⋆ (k_j ⋆ g))(x')` on the graph
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_comp_graphMap`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_sub.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_sub
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_sub.docstring: **The trace is linear** on the functions with a finite intrinsic norm of smoothness `> 1/p`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_smul.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_smul
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_smul.docstring:
**The trace commutes with complex scalars**: `Tr (c f) = c Tr f` for every `f ∈ L_p(V)`, since
every term of the trace series does and `∑' j, c x_j = c ∑' j, x_j` (Mathlib's
`tsum_const_smul''`). With `Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_sub` the trace is linear on the functions
of finite intrinsic norm.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_mulLp_ae.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_mulLp_ae
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_mulLp_ae.docstring:
**Traces of products with smooth functions**: for smooth `ψ` with bounded derivatives up to
order `L` and `F` with a finite `B^{s+1/p}_{p,q}`-norm of order `L > s + 1/p`,
`Tr(ψ F) = (ψ ∘ γ) Tr F` almost everywhere: both are limits of the restrictions of the continuous
`ψ G_J` and `G_J`, and multiplication by `ψ` is bounded in `B^{1/p}_{p,1}`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_graphExtens.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_graphExtension_of_atoms
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_graphExtens.docstring:
**The trace of the extension, from a package of extended atoms**: for a package of extended
atoms of order `r ≤ L` with constant `C < ∞` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.HasExtensionAtoms`), `Lh ≥ 1`,
`s > 0` with `s + 1/p < r` and `g ∈ L_p(H)` with a finite local means quasi-norm
`‖(2^(js) ‖k_j ⋆ g‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`, `Tr (E g) = g`. The partial sums `∑_{j ≤ J} F_j` are continuous
with traces `∑_{j ≤ J} η_j ⋆ (k_j ⋆ g) → g` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_sum_traceExtTerm`), and
they converge to `E g` in `B^{1/p}_{p,1}` with order `L`, where the trace is continuous
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.tendsto_graphTrace_of_modNorm_sub_le`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_graphExtens.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_graphExtension
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_graphExtens.docstring:
**The trace of the extension** (Schneider–Vybíral, Theorem 4.11, for `p ≥ 1`): for
`0 < s < 1`, `L ≥ 2` and `g ∈ L_p(H)` with `‖g‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_1(g, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`,
the extension of moment order `1` has `Tr (E g) = g`, from the extended atoms of order `2`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.exists_extension_atoms`,
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_graphExtension_of_atoms`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_flatExtensi.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_flatExtension
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_flatExtensi.docstring:
**The trace of the extension of every order**: for the flat graph, `L ≥ 2`, `Lh ≥ 1`, `s > 0`
with `s + 1/p < L` and `g ∈ L_p(H)` with a finite local means quasi-norm
`‖(2^(js) ‖k_j ⋆ g‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`, the extension of moment order `Lh` has `Tr (E g) = g`, from the
extended atoms of order `L` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_graphExtension_of_atoms`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_finsetSum_o.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_finsetSum_of_intrinsicNorm
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_finsetSum_o.docstring:
**The trace of a finite sum** is the sum of the traces, for summands with finite intrinsic
quasi-norms of smoothness `s + 1/p`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_finsetSum.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_finsetSum
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_finsetSum.docstring:
**The trace of a finite sum** is the sum of the traces, for summands with finite
`B^{s+1/p}_{p,q}`-norms of order `L` on `V`: these have finite intrinsic quasi-norms
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.intrinsicNorm_lt_top_of_modNorm`), so
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_finsetSum_of_intrinsicNorm` applies.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_congr.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_congr
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_congr.docstring:
**The trace depends only on `f` on `Ω`**: `1_Ω F = 1_Ω f` gives `Tr F = Tr f`, since the
trace is built from the cut-offs `1_Ω (k_j ⋆ f)` and the kernels `k_j` are supported in `-K`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_zero_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_zero
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_zero_.docstring:
**Locality of the trace**: if `f = 0` almost everywhere on `Ω ∩ U` for an open set `U`, then
`Tr f = 0` almost everywhere on `γ⁻¹(U)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_of_ae.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_of_ae_eq
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_of_ae.docstring:
**Locality for two functions**: if `f₁ = f₂` almost everywhere on `Ω ∩ U` for an open set `U`,
then `Tr f₁ = Tr f₂` almost everywhere on `γ⁻¹(U)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_graph.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_graphTrace_comp
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_graph.docstring:
**Change of chart for traces**: let `Ω₁`, `Ω₂` be Lipschitz graph domains and `F ∈ L_p(V)` with
a finite `B^{s+1/p}_{p,q}`-norm of order `L > s + 1/p`. For almost every `x' ∈ H₁` whose boundary
point `γ₁(x')` lies on the boundary of `Ω₂`, `Tr₁ F(x') = Tr₂ F(P₂ γ₁ x')`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_comp_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_comp_graphMap
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_comp_.docstring:
**The trace of continuous functions**: if `f ∈ L_p(V)` has a continuous representative `G`
and a finite intrinsic `B^{s+1/p}_{p,q}`-norm on `Ω`, then `Tr f = G ∘ γ` almost everywhere on
`H`: the mollified restrictions converge at every point to `G(γ x')`
(`Rd.conv_dilate_near`, twice), and a subsequence converges almost everywhere to `Tr f`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace.docstring:
The **trace** on the boundary of the Lipschitz graph domain `Ω`, a function on `H`:
`Tr f = ∑_j (η_j ⋆ 1_Ω (k_j ⋆ f)) ∘ γ` with the kernels of the cone bump; only `f` on `Ω`
enters.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphShear.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphShear
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphShear.docstring: The **shear** `(x', t) ↦ (x', t + φ(x'))` of `H × ℝ`, as a measurable equivalence.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphReflect.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphReflect
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphReflect.docstring:
The **reflection across the graph** `x ↦ x + 2(φ(x) - ⟪x, e⟫) e`: it moves `x` along `e` to the
point at the same distance on the other side of the graph.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphRayIntegral.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphRayIntegral
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphRayIntegral.docstring:
The **ray integral from the graph** `Ψ(γ x') = ∫_{φ(x')}^∞ g(x' + t e) dt`, the ray integral
of `g` from the boundary point `γ x'` upwards.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphProj_graphEquiv.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphProj_graphEquiv
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphProj_graphEquiv.docstring:
**The projection of the graph coordinates is the first coordinate**: `P(γ(x') + t e) = x'`,
since `P e = 0` and `P γ(x') = x'`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphProj_extendCenter.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphProj_extendCenter
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphProj_extendCenter.docstring: The projection of the extended centre is the centre.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphProdEquiv.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphProdEquiv
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphProdEquiv.docstring:
The **product coordinates** `(x', t) ↦ x' + t e` of `V = H ⊕ ℝ e`, as a measurable
equivalence (Mathlib's `Submodule.measurableEquivProd`).

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphOver_sub_sub.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphOver_sub_sub
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphOver_sub_sub.docstring:
The increments of two graphs differ by a multiple of `e`:
`(γ_{h₁} x' - γ_{h₁} y') - (γ_{h₂} x' - γ_{h₂} y') = ((h₁ x' - h₁ y') - (h₂ x' - h₂ y')) e`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphOver_sub.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphOver_sub
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphOver_sub.docstring:
The increments of a graph over the hyperplane:
`γ_h x' - γ_h y' = (x' - y') + (h x' - h y') e`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphOver_injective.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphOver_injective
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphOver_injective.docstring: Graphs over the hyperplane are injective.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphOver.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphOver
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphOver.docstring:
The **graph over the hyperplane** of a function `h : H → ℝ`, the map `x' ↦ x' + h(x') e`
from `H` to `V`. The graph map of `Ω` is the graph of `φ`; the graphs of the linear functions
`⟪g, ·⟫` are linear maps.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphMap_graphProj_eq_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphMap_graphProj_eq_iff
Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphMap_graphProj_eq_.docstring: **The graph** `γ(Py) = y` consists of the points with `⟪y, e⟫ = φ(y)`.

Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphMap_add_smul_mem_.name: Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphMap_add_smul_mem_domain_iff
