`∫ φ g = (-1)^k ∫ (∂^v φ) f` for every test function `φ` on `Ω`.

Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.eq_of_top.name: Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.eq_of_top
Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.eq_of_top.docstring:
**Weak derivatives on `V` are unique classes**: two weak derivatives `G`, `G' ∈ L_r(V)` of the
same function on the whole space `V` are equal in `L_r(V)` (`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.unique`).

Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.cutoff_top.name: Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.cutoff_top
Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.cutoff_top.docstring:
**The cutoff of a weakly differentiable function**: if `g = ∂_w f` weakly on `O` and `χ` is
smooth with compact closed support in `O`, then `χ f` and `χ g + (∂_w χ) f` are integrable on `V`
and `χ g + (∂_w χ) f = ∂_w (χ f)` weakly on `V` (`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.mul_of_tsupport_subset`
with `V` for `O` and `O` for `B`, and
`MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrable.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport`).

Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.congr_ae.name: Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.congr_ae
Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.congr_ae.docstring: Weak derivatives only see `f` and `g` almost everywhere on `Ω`.

Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.comp_lipschitzWith_o.name: Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.comp_lipschitzWith_of_mapsTo_isCompact
Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.comp_lipschitzWith_o.docstring:
**The chain rule on a piece**: let `g_i = ∂_{e_i} f` weakly on `O`, `f` locally integrable on
`O`, `L ⊆ O` compact, `Φ` a `K`-Lipschitz map preserving Lebesgue measure, and `U` open with
`Φ(U) ⊆ L`. Then `∑_i ⟪DΦ(·) v, e_i⟫ g_i ∘ Φ = ∂_v (f ∘ Φ)` weakly on `U`: the smooth `u_k` of
`Rd.exists_tendsto_contDiff_of_hasWeakLineDeriv` give the chain rule for `u_k ∘ Φ`
(`Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_comp_of_contDiff`), and both sides converge in `L_1(U)` by
`Rd.eLpNorm_comp_le_of_mapsTo` and `Rd.eLpNorm_sum_inner_fderiv_mul_comp_le`
(`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.of_tendsto`).

Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.comp_lipschitzWith.name: Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.comp_lipschitzWith
Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.comp_lipschitzWith.docstring:
**The chain rule for weak derivatives under Lipschitz maps**: let `g_i = ∂_{e_i} f` weakly on
the open set `O` for the basis vectors `e_i` of `Rd.gridBasis`, let `Φ : V → V` be `K`-Lipschitz
and preserve Lebesgue measure, and let `Φ` map the open set `U` into `O`. Then for every `v ∈ V`,
`x ↦ ∑_i ⟪DΦ(x) v, e_i⟫ g_i(Φ x)` is the weak derivative `∂_v (f ∘ Φ)` on `U`; here `DΦ(x)` is
Mathlib's `fderiv`, which exists almost everywhere by Rademacher's theorem. Every compact
`K' ⊆ U` lies in the open set `Φ⁻¹(int L)` for a compact `L ⊆ O` with `Φ(K') ⊆ int L`, where
`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.comp_lipschitzWith_of_mapsTo_isCompact` applies
(`Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_of_forall_isCompact`).

Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.ae_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_.name: Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.ae_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_zero
Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.ae_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_.docstring:
**Weak derivatives vanish where the function vanishes**: if `g` is a weak derivative `∂^v f`
on `Ω`, `O ⊆ Ω` is open and `f = 0` almost everywhere on `O`, then `g = 0` almost everywhere on
`O`, by locality (`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.mono`) and uniqueness (`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.unique`).

Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.add.name: Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.add
Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.add.docstring: Weak derivatives are additive: `∂^v (f + f') = ∂^v f + ∂^v f'`.

Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.ofReal.name: Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.ofReal
Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.ofReal.docstring:
**Real symbols as complex symbols**: if `m` is a real symbol of order `σ`, then so is
`ξ ↦ (m(ξ) : ℂ)`, since the embedding `ℝ → ℂ` is a linear isometry (Mathlib's
`LinearIsometry.norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_left`).

Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.mono.name: Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.mono
Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.mono.docstring:
**The order of a symbol can be raised**: a symbol of order `σ` is a symbol of every order
`τ ≥ σ`, since `1 + ‖ξ‖² ≥ 1`.

Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.hasTemperateGrowth.name: Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.hasTemperateGrowth
Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.hasTemperateGrowth.docstring:
**Symbols have temperate growth**: a symbol of any order is smooth with polynomially bounded
derivatives, `(1 + ‖ξ‖²)^{(σ-k)/2} ≤ (1 + ‖ξ‖)^N` for `N ≥ σ - k`
(`Rd.one_add_norm_sq_rpow_le_one_add_norm_pow`). Hence symbols are Fourier multipliers of
Schwartz functions and tempered distributions.

Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_norm_iteratedF.name: Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_scaledSymbol_le
Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_norm_iteratedF.docstring:
**Rescaled symbols on an annulus**: for a symbol `m` of order `σ`, `0 < a` and `b`, every
order `k` has a constant `C ≥ 0` with `‖D^k (2^{-jσ} m(2^j ·))(ζ)‖ ≤ C` for all levels `j` and all
`ζ` with `a ≤ ‖ζ‖ ≤ b`. The weight `(2^{-2j} + ‖ζ‖²)^{(σ-k)/2}` of
`Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_scaledSymbol_le` is at most `max((a²)^{(σ-k)/2}, (1 + b²)^{(σ-k)/2})`
(`Rd.norm_besselSymbol_le`).

Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_isUniformSchwa.name: Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_isUniformSchwartz_symbolKernelFamily
Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_isUniformSchwa.docstring:
**The symbol kernels are uniformly Schwartz** when `m` is a symbol of order `σ` and `ω̂`
vanishes outside an annulus `{a ≤ ‖ζ‖ ≤ b}` with `a > 0`
(`Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_isUniformSchwartz_symbolFamily`,
`Rd.exists_isUniformSchwartz_fourierInv`); the bounds are existential.

Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_isUniformSchwa.name: Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_isUniformSchwartz_symbolFamily
Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_isUniformSchwa.docstring:
**The symbol families are uniformly Schwartz**: if `m` is a symbol of order `σ` and `ω̂`
vanishes outside the annulus `{a ≤ ‖ζ‖ ≤ b}` with `a > 0`, then
`j ↦ 2^{-jσ} m(2^j ·) ω̂` is uniformly Schwartz. On the annulus, `‖ζ‖^k ≤ |b|^k` and the Leibniz
bound (`Rd.norm_iteratedFDeriv_mul_schwartz_le`) combines the bounds of the rescaled symbols
(`Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_scaledSymbol_le`) with the seminorms of `ω̂`;
outside the support of `ω̂` all derivatives vanish. The bounds are existential.

Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_isUniformSchwa.name: Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_isUniformSchwartz_symbolBase
Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_isUniformSchwa.docstring:
**Symbol kernels of a family that is constant from `M` on**: if `m` is a symbol of order
`σ`, `ω_j = ω_M` for `j ≥ M` and `𝓕ω_M` vanishes outside the annulus `{a ≤ ‖ζ‖ ≤ b}`, `a > 0`,
then the symbol kernels `j ↦ K_j` of the family (`Rd.symbolBase`) are uniformly Schwartz: from
`M` on they are the symbol kernels of `𝓕ω_M`
(`Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_isUniformSchwartz_symbolKernelFamily`), and the first `M` are
exceptions (`Rd.IsUniformSchwartz.of_forall_ge_eq`).

Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_isUniformSchwa.name: Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_isUniformSchwartz_dualLpBlockKernelS
Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_isUniformSchwa.docstring:
**Symbols applied to the synthesis kernels**: for a symbol `m` of order `σ` there is a
uniformly Schwartz family `(G_j)` with `m(D) ψ̃_j = 2^{jσ} (G_j)_{2^j}` for every `j`, where
`ψ̃_j = (dualLpBlockKernelBase j)_{2^j}` (`Rd.dualLpBlockKernelS`). The family
`dualLpBlockKernelBase` is constant from `2` on, with Fourier transform in `{1/4 ≤ ‖ζ‖ ≤ 4}`
(`Rd.mem_annulus_of_fourier_dualLpBlockKernelBase_ne_zero`,
`Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_isUniformSchwartz_symbolBase`, `Rd.fourierMultiplierCLM_schwartzDilate`);
the bounds are existential.

Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_bound.name: Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_bound
Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.exists_bound.docstring: The constants in the bounds of a symbol can be taken nonnegative.

Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.name: Rd.HasSymbolGrowth
Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.docstring:
A function `m` has **symbol growth of order `σ`**, or is a **symbol of order `σ`**
(Hörmander's class `S^σ_{1,0}`), if it is smooth and every derivative satisfies
`‖D^k m(ξ)‖ ≤ C_k (1 + ‖ξ‖²)^{(σ - k)/2}`: each derivative gains one power of the Japanese
bracket `⟨ξ⟩ = (1 + ‖ξ‖²)^{1/2}`. It strengthens Mathlib's `Function.HasTemperateGrowth`
(`Rd.HasSymbolGrowth.hasTemperateGrowth`); for `σ = 0` it is Mihlin's condition with every
derivative and the inhomogeneous weight.

Rd.HasBesovExtension.modNormOn_order_le_.name: Rd.HasBesovExtension.modNormOn_order_le_of_hasBesovExtension
Rd.HasBesovExtension.modNormOn_order_le_.docstring:
**The order of the differences does not matter on a set with the extension property**: for
`0 < s < r` and `s < r'` there is `C < ∞` with `N_Ω(f; r') ≤ C N_Ω(f; r)` whenever
`N_Ω(f; r) < ∞`, where `N_Ω(f; r) = ‖1_Ω f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q}`. Extend
`f` to `V`, change the order there (`Rd.modNorm_le_modNorm_of_lt`), and restrict.

Rd.HasBesovExtension.congr_set.name: Rd.HasBesovExtension.congr_set
Rd.HasBesovExtension.congr_set.docstring:
**The extension property is the same for sets that agree up to a null set**: if `U` has it and
`U'` agrees with `U` up to a null set, then `U'` has it; the proof keeps the constant `C`, since
the cut-offs and the intrinsic quasi-norms on `U` and `U'` agree (`Rd.indicatorLp_congr_set`,
`Rd.modNormOn_congr_set`).

Rd.HasBesovExtension.name: Rd.HasBesovExtension
Rd.HasBesovExtension.docstring:
The **extension property** of a measurable set `Ω`: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < r` and
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` there is `C < ∞` such that every `f ∈ L_p(V)` with
`N_Ω(f) = ‖1_Ω f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞` (`Rd.modNormOn`) agrees on `Ω`
with some `F ∈ L_p(V)` with `‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C N_Ω(f)`.

Rd.ExtendsSobolev.name: Rd.ExtendsSobolev
Rd.ExtendsSobolev.docstring:
**Sobolev functions on `O` extend from `U` with constant `C`**: for every `f ∈ L_p(O)` with
weak derivatives `g_i = ∂_{e_i} f ∈ L_p(O)` along the orthonormal basis `e_i = Rd.gridBasis V i`
there are `F ∈ W^1_p(V)` with `F = f` almost everywhere on `U` and weak derivatives
`G_i = ∂_{e_i} F ∈ L_p(V)` with `‖F‖_p + ∑_i ‖G_i‖_p ≤ C (‖f‖_{L_p(O)} + ∑_i ‖g_i‖_{L_p(O)})`.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.norm_iteratedFDerivWithi.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.norm_iteratedFDerivWithin_mul_atom_le
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.norm_iteratedFDerivWithi.docstring:
**Derivatives of `χ a`**: for a smooth atom `a` on `V` with constant `A` and `‖D^k χ‖ ≤ M`
within `Ω ∩ U'`, `‖D^i (χ a)‖ ≤ 2^i M A 2^(ji)` within `Ω ∩ U'` for `i ≤ K`.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.modNormOn_applyLp_le_mod.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.modNormOn_applyLp_le_modNormOn
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.modNormOn_applyLp_le_mod.docstring:
**Invariance of the intrinsic Besov quasi-norm on a Besov domain** under a smooth change of
variables with a cut-off: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < r` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` there is `C < ∞` with
`N_Ω(T f) ≤ C N_Ω(f)` for all `f` with `N_Ω(f) < ∞`, where
`N_Ω(f) = ‖1_Ω f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q}`. Extend `f` to `V`
(`Rd.BesovDomain.exists_extension`) and apply `Rd.CutoffDiffeo.modNormOn_applyLp_le`.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.modNormOn_applyLp_le.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.modNormOn_applyLp_le
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.modNormOn_applyLp_le.docstring:
**Invariance under a smooth change of variables with a cut-off**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`,
`0 < s < r` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` there is `C < ∞` such that for all `F ∈ L_p(V)`
`‖1_Ω T F‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(T F, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤
C (‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})`. The smooth cell atoms of `F`
(`Rd.LocalMeansBump.atomic_decomposition_smooth`) are transported by `T`
(`Rd.CutoffDiffeo.exists_transported_atoms`) and synthesised on `Ω`
(`Rd.modNormOn_le_coeffNorm`).

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.lintegral_apply_eq.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.lintegral_apply_eq
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.lintegral_apply_eq.docstring:
**The change of variables** `x = Ψ(y)`: for `e > 0`,
`∫ |T g|^e = ∫_{K₀} |det DΨ(y)| |χ(y)|^e |g(y)|^e dy`.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.isSmoothAtom_apply.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.isSmoothAtom_apply
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.isSmoothAtom_apply.docstring:
**Smooth atoms stay smooth atoms** under a smooth change of variables with a cut-off: there are
`L` and `A'` such that for every smooth atom `a` on `V` of order `K`, level `j`, radius factor `d`
and constant `A`, and every `y₀ ∈ K₀` within `d 2^(-j)` of its centre, `T a` is a smooth atom on
`Ω` of order `K` with centre `Ψ y₀`, radius factor `2 L d` and constant `A' A`.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.imageCompact.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.imageCompact
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.imageCompact.docstring: The compact set `Ψ(K₀)` that carries the images.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.exists_transported_atoms.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.exists_transported_atoms
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.exists_transported_atoms.docstring:
**Transport of smooth atoms**: for smooth atoms on `V` of order `r ≥ 1`, radius factor `d` and
constant `A`, centred at the cell centres, there are `d'`, `C' < ∞` and `N` such that for all
coefficients `λ` the images `T a_{j,m}` are regular atoms on `Ω` of order and exponent `r` with
radius factor `d'`, constant `C'` and suitable centres, and coefficients `λ'` with `|λ'| ≤ |λ|`,
`λ' = λ` unless `T a_{j,m} = 0`, and at most `N` centres with `λ' ≠ 0` in each ball of radius
`(d' + r) 2^(-j)`.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.exists_iteratedFDerivWit.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.exists_iteratedFDerivWithin_chi_bound
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.exists_iteratedFDerivWithin_Phi_bound
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.exists_iteratedFDerivWit.docstring:
**The derivatives of `Φ` are bounded on `Ψ(K₀)`**: `‖D^i Φ‖ ≤ D` within `Ω ∩ U` for
`i ≤ K`, with `D ≥ 1` (`ContDiffOn.exists_norm_iteratedFDerivWithin_le`).

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.exists_det_bound.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.exists_det_bound
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.exists_det_bound.docstring: The Jacobian of `Ψ` is bounded on `K₀`.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.eLpNorm_apply_le.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.eLpNorm_apply_le
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.eLpNorm_apply_le.docstring: **`T` is bounded on `L_p`**: `‖T g‖_p ≤ C ‖g‖_p` for `0 < p < ∞`.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.continuousOn_apply.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.continuousOn_apply
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.continuousOn_apply.docstring:
**`T` keeps continuity on `Ω`**: for continuous `f`, `T f` is continuous on `Ω`. Near a point
of `Ψ(K₀)` it is `(χ f) ∘ Φ`, and off the compact set `Ψ(K₀)` it vanishes.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply_tsum.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply_tsum
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply_tsum.docstring:
**`T` commutes with series** whose terms it kills where the coefficients change: if for every
`m` either `λ'_m = λ_m` or `T a_m = 0`, then `T (∑_m λ_m a_m) = ∑_m λ'_m T a_m`.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply_eq_zero_of_notMem.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply_eq_zero_of_notMem
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply_eq_zero_of_notMem.docstring: **`T f` vanishes on `Ω` outside `Ψ(K₀)`**: if `Φ x ∉ K₀`, the cut-off vanishes.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply_eq_zero_of_forall_.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply_eq_zero_of_forall_far
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply_eq_zero_of_forall_.docstring:
**`T a` vanishes if `a` lives far from `K₀`**: if `a = 0` outside `B(c, d 2^(-j))` and no
point of `K₀` lies in that ball, then `T a = 0`.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply_eq_zero_of_far.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply_eq_zero_of_far
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply_eq_zero_of_far.docstring:
**The changed atom vanishes far from `Ψ(y₀)`**: if `a` vanishes outside `B(c, d 2^(-j))`,
`y₀ ∈ K₀` lies within `d 2^(-j)` of `c` and `Ψ` is `L`-Lipschitz on `K₀`, then `T a` vanishes
outside `B(Ψ y₀, 2 L d 2^(-j))`.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply_ae_eq.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply_ae_eq
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply_ae_eq.docstring:
**`T` respects null sets on `Ω`**: if `g₁ = g₂` almost everywhere on `Ω`, then
`T g₁ = T g₂` almost everywhere, since `Ψ` maps the null set `K₀ ∩ {g₁ ≠ g₂}` to a null set.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.applyLp_eq_of_indicatorL.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.applyLp_eq_of_indicatorLp_eq
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.applyLp_eq_of_indicatorL.docstring:
**`T` depends only on the values on `Ω`**: if `F = f` almost everywhere on `Ω`, then
`T F = T f` in `L_p`.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.applyLp_ae.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.applyLp_ae
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.applyLp_ae.docstring: The operator acts by `T`, almost everywhere.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.applyLp.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.applyLp
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.applyLp.docstring: **The change of variables with a cut-off as a bounded operator on `L_p`**.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.apply.docstring: The action on functions: `T f = 1_{Ω ∩ U} (χ f) ∘ Φ`.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.aestronglyMeasurable_app.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo.aestronglyMeasurable_apply
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.aestronglyMeasurable_app.docstring: `T g` is almost everywhere strongly measurable with `g`.

Rd.CutoffDiffeo.name: Rd.CutoffDiffeo
Rd.CutoffDiffeo.docstring:
A **smooth change of variables with a cut-off** on `Ω`: a bijection `Φ : Ω ∩ U → Ω ∩ U'`,
smooth within `Ω` with smooth inverse `Ψ`, and a function `χ` that is smooth within `Ω ∩ U'` and
vanishes on `Ω` outside a compact set `K₀ ⊆ Ω ∩ U'`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.zeroBoundarySp.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.zeroBoundarySpace_le_traceKer
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.zeroBoundarySp.docstring:
**`H^s_0(Ω) ⊆ ker γ_s`**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: the trace kernel is closed
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isClosed_traceKer`, Mathlib's
`Submodule.topologicalClosure_minimal`), so it suffices that it contains the restrictions of the
test functions of `Ω`, whose closure is `H^s_0(Ω)`. The restriction keeps the boundary trace
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_restrictProj`), and the boundary trace of a test
function vanishes (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_sobolevToL2_ofTest`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.volume_switchS.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.volume_switchSet_inter_closedBall_le_of_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.volume_switchS.docstring:
**The layer for short steps**: if the shrunk balls `B(c_i, ρ_i - 2ε)` cover the boundary,
`‖h‖ ≤ ε` and `ρ ≥ 0`, then `|S_h(Ω) ∩ B̄(c, ρ)| ≤ ∑_i 2 (1 + M_i) |B^{H_i}_1| · ‖h‖ ρ^(n-1)`, by
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.switchSet_subset_iUnion` and the slab volumes
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.volume_abs_graphHeight_le_inter_closedBall`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceL2_apply_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceL2_apply_ae
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceL2_apply_.docstring: `traceL2 s t = Tr_Γ ι_s (E_s t)` almost everywhere on `Γ`, for every resolution of unity.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceL2.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceL2
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceL2.docstring:
**The trace of the trace space in `L_2(Γ)`**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: an element `t` of the trace
space of `H^s(Ω)` goes to the boundary trace of its extension `E_s t ∈ H^s(Ω)`. It is injective
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceL2_injective`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_one_l.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_one_le_zeroBoundarySpace
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_one_l.docstring:
**`ker γ ⊆ H^1_0(Ω)`**: for `u` in the trace kernel, the zero extension `1_Ω ι u` is the `L_2`
function of some `U ∈ H^1(V)` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memSobolevW_indicatorLp_of_mem_traceKer`,
`Rd.exists_toL2_eq_of_memSobolevW`). `U` vanishes outside `Ω`, so `U ∈ H̃^1(Ω)`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace_of_ae_eq_zero`), and `u = U|_Ω`
(`Rd.restrictProj_eq_of_ae_eq`) lies in `H^1_0(Ω)` (`Rd.range_tildeToRestriction`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_one_e.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_one_eq_zeroBoundarySpace
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_one_e.docstring:
**`ker γ = H^1_0(Ω)`** on a bounded Lipschitz domain (McLean, Theorem 3.40; Hiptmair, Pauly
and Schulz cite it for `ker γ = H^1_0(Ω)`), for the trace kernel `Ω.traceKer 1` of `H^1(Ω)`: the
elements of `H^1(Ω)` whose chart traces all vanish, equivalently whose boundary trace vanishes
almost everywhere on `Γ` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_traceKer_one_iff`), are exactly the
limits in `H^1(Ω)` of test functions of `Ω`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.zeroBoundarySpace_le_traceKer`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_one_le_zeroBoundarySpace`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_le_ze.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_le_zeroBoundarySpace_of_one_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_le_ze.docstring:
**`ker γ_s ⊆ H^s_0(Ω)` for `1 ≤ s < 3/2`** (McLean, Theorem 3.40): the zero extension of
`u ∈ ker γ_s` lies in `H^s(V)`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevToL2_eq_indicatorLp_of_mem_traceKer`), so `u` lies in
`H^s_0(Ω)` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_zeroBoundarySpace_of_sobolevToL2_eq_indicatorLp`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_le_ze.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_le_zeroBoundarySpace_of_le_one
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_le_ze.docstring:
**`ker γ_s ⊆ H^s_0(Ω)`** for `1/2 < s ≤ 1` (McLean, Theorem 3.40): every `u ∈ ker γ_s` lies in
the closure of `H^s_0(Ω)`, which is closed. For `ε > 0` the inclusion `H^1(V) ⊆ H^s(V)` has
dense range (`Rd.denseRange_sobolevInclusion`), so some `W' ∈ H^1(V)` has
`K ‖ι_{s,1} W' - u‖ < ε`, and
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_mem_zeroBoundarySpace_enorm_sub_le` gives `y ∈ H^s_0(Ω)`
within `ε` of `u`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_eq_ze.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_eq_zeroBoundarySpace_of_le_one
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_eq_ze.docstring:
**`ker γ_s = H^s_0(Ω)`** for `1/2 < s ≤ 1` on a bounded Lipschitz domain (McLean,
Theorem 3.40, applied in this range by Hewett–Moiola, Remark 2.6): the elements of `H^s(Ω)`
whose boundary trace vanishes almost everywhere on `Γ`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_traceKer_iff`) are exactly the limits in `H^s(Ω)` of restricted
test functions of `Ω` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.zeroBoundarySpace_le_traceKer`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_le_zeroBoundarySpace_of_le_one`). At `s = 1` this is
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_one_eq_zeroBoundarySpace`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer.docstring:
**The trace kernel** `ker γ_s ⊆ H^s(Ω)`, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: the `u` whose chart traces
`Tr_j(ψ_j u)` all vanish, for the canonical resolution of unity; equivalently, the `u` whose
boundary trace vanishes almost everywhere on `Γ`, for every resolution of unity
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_traceKer_iff`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.toOpens.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.toOpens
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.toOpens.docstring:
The open set of a bounded Lipschitz domain, as an element of Mathlib's `Opens V`, the form
in which open sets carry distributions and weak derivatives.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.toL2_ae_eq_sum.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.toL2_ae_eq_sum_add
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.toL2_ae_eq_sum.docstring:
**The decomposition on `Ω`**: if `χ + ∑_j ψ_j = 1` on `Ω`, the `L_2` functions of `W_j` are
`ψ_j ι W` and that of `W_0` is `χ ι W`, then `ι W = ι (∑_j W_j + W_0)` almost everywhere on
`Ω`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.switchSet_subs.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.switchSet_subset_iUnion
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.switchSet_subs.docstring:
**Short steps switch only near a chart graph**: if the shrunk balls `B(c_i, ρ_i - 2ε)` cover
the boundary and `‖h‖ ≤ ε`, every switch point `x` of `Ω` has `|η_i(x)| ≤ (1 + M_i) ‖h‖` for some
chart `i`. The step `[x, x + h]` contains a boundary point
(`Rd.exists_mem_frontier_of_mem_switchSet`), which lies in some `B(c_i, ρ_i - 2ε)`; so `x` and
`x + h` lie in `B_i`, where `Ω` is the graph domain `Ω_i`, and
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.abs_graphHeight_le_of_mem_switchSet` applies.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.surfaceMeasure.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.surfaceMeasure_restrict_ball
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.surfaceMeasure.docstring:
**The surface measure in a boundary ball**: on `B_j` the surface measure is `μHE[n-1]` on the
graph `γ_j(H_j)` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.frontier_inter_ball_eq`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.sum_boundaryPa.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.sum_boundaryPartition_le_one
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.sum_boundaryPa.docstring: The functions of the canonical resolution of unity sum to at most `1` everywhere.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.stronglyMeasur.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.stronglyMeasurable_chartPiece
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.stronglyMeasur.docstring:
**Chart pieces are measurable**: for a strongly measurable `g` on `V`, the chart piece
`(ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j` is strongly measurable on `H_j`, since `ψ_j` and `γ_j` are continuous.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.stronglyMeasur.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.stronglyMeasurable_boundaryTrace
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.stronglyMeasur.docstring:
**The boundary trace is measurable**: `Tr_Γ F = ∑_k ψ_k (Tr_k F ∘ P_k)` is a finite sum of
products of continuous functions with measurable representatives composed with the continuous
projections `P_k`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.sobolevExtensi.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.sobolevExtensionL
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.sobolevExtensi.docstring:
**The extension operator for `W^1_p`, `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`** (Evans–Gariepy, Section 4.4, by
reflection): for a bounded Lipschitz domain `Ω` in dimension `n ≥ 1`, a bounded linear operator
`E` from the jets of `W^1_p(Ω)` to the jets of `W^1_p(V)` with `E u = u` on `Ω`, chosen among the
extension operators of `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevExtensionOp_reflection`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.slobodeckijFor.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.slobodeckijForm_chartPiece_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.slobodeckijFor.docstring:
**The Gagliardo form of a chart piece, split into its parts**: if `ψ_j` vanishes outside
`B(c_j, r)` with `r ≤ r_j` and `g` is measurable, then for `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `s ≥ 0` the Gagliardo
form on `H_j` of `G = (ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j` is at most `2^(p-1) (∫∫ A + ∫∫ B) + 2 ∫∫ |G(x')|^p k(y' - x')`
for the parts of `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPiece_integrand_le_add`; the last part appears
twice by Tonelli's theorem.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_we.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_mulLp_eq_zero
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_we.docstring:
**The interior piece of Green's formula vanishes**: if the `L_2` function of `W' ∈ H^1(V)` is
`χ ι W` for a continuous bounded `χ` with closed support in `Ω`, then
`∫_Ω (∂_v U) W' + U ∂_v W' = ∫_V (∂_v U) W' + U ∂_v W' = 0`
(`Rd.integral_weakDeriv_mul_add_eq_zero`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_we.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_localizeL2
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_we.docstring:
**The chart pieces of Green's formula**: if the `L_2` function of `W' ∈ H^1(V)` is `ψ_j ι W`,
then `∫_Ω (∂_v U) W' + U ∂_v W' = ∫_{H_j} ψ_j(γ_j x') Tr_j U Tr_j W n^j_v dx'`. The integrand
vanishes outside `B_j`, where `Ω` agrees with the graph domain `Ω_j`, so this is Green's formula
on `Ω_j` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_green_besselPotentialSpace`) with
`Tr_j (ψ_j W) = (ψ_j ∘ γ_j) Tr_j W` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_mulLp_ae`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_li.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_lineDeriv_eq_chart
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_li.docstring:
**Gauss–Green on `Ω` in one chart**: for a `C^1` function `g` with compact support in the
boundary ball `B_j` and every direction `v`, `∫_Ω ∂_v g = ∫_Γ g ⟪v, ν_j ∘ P_j⟫ dσ`. Inside `B_j`
the domain is the graph domain `Ω_j`, so this is Gauss–Green on `Ω_j`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.setIntegral_lineDeriv_eq_normal`) with the surface measure in the chart
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_surfaceMeasure_of_support`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_gr.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_green_surfaceMeasure
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_gr.docstring:
**Green's formula on a bounded Lipschitz domain** (Grisvard, Theorem 1.5.3.1): for all
`U, W ∈ H^1(V)` and every direction `v`,
`∫_Ω (∂_v U) W + U ∂_v W = ∫_Γ T_Γ U · T_Γ W ⟪v, ν⟫ dσ` with the traces
`T_Γ U, T_Γ W ∈ L_2(Γ)` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2`), the outward unit normal `ν`
and the surface measure `σ`. The chart form for a resolution of unity equal to one near `Γ`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_green_of_nhds`) is the boundary integral in the charts
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_ambientTraceL2_mul_inner_outwardNormal_eq`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_gr.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_green_of_nhds
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_gr.docstring:
**Green's formula on a bounded Lipschitz domain, chart form, for a resolution of unity equal
to one near the boundary**: if `∑_j ψ_j = 1` on a neighbourhood of `Γ`, then for all
`U, W ∈ H^1(V)` and every direction `v`,
`∫_Ω (∂_v U) W + U ∂_v W = ∑_j ∫_{H_j} ψ_j(γ_j x') Tr_j U Tr_j W n^j_v dx'`. Split
`W = ∑_j ψ_j W + χ W` on `Ω` with the interior cut-off `χ`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_interior_cutoff`): the chart pieces are Green's formula on the
graph domains (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_localizeL2`), and the
interior piece vanishes
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_weakDeriv_mul_add_mulLp_eq_zero`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_gr.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_green_of_mem_traceKer
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_gr.docstring:
**Functions with vanishing trace have no boundary term**: for `u` in the trace kernel,
`W ∈ H^1(V)` and every direction `v`, `∫_Ω (∂_v u) W + u ∂_v W = 0`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_green_surfaceMeasure`, `γ_{L_2} u = 0` by
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ker_boundaryTraceL2`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.restrictionInc.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.restrictionInclusion_mem_traceKer
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.restrictionInc.docstring:
**The inclusions keep the trace kernel**, `1/2 < t ≤ s < 3/2`: if `u ∈ ker γ_s`, then
`ι^Ω_{t,s} u = (ι_{t,s} u)|_Ω ∈ ker γ_t`. The restriction keeps the boundary trace
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_restrictProj`), and `ι_t(ι_{t,s} u) = ι_s u`
(`Rd.sobolevToL2_sobolevInclusion`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.restrictProj_s.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.restrictProj_sub_mem_traceKer
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.restrictProj_s.docstring:
**A function minus the extension of its trace has zero trace**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: for
`U ∈ H^s(V)` and every `W ∈ H^s(V)` with `ι_s W = E_Γ(T^s_Γ U)`, `(U - W)|_Ω ∈ ker γ_s`. Almost
everywhere on `Γ`, `Tr_Γ ι_s(U - W) = Tr_Γ ι_s U - Tr_Γ E_Γ(T^s_Γ U) = T^s_Γ U - T^s_Γ U = 0`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_sobolevToL2_sub`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_besovExtendLp`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBesov_ambientTraceL2`), and the restriction keeps the
boundary trace (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_restrictProj`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.restrictProj_e.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.restrictProj_eq_of_sobolevToL2_eq_indicatorLp
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.restrictProj_e.docstring:
**Zero extensions have the same restriction**: for `s ≥ 0` and `U, U' ∈ H^s(V)` with
`ι_s U' = 1_Ω ι_s U`, `U'|_Ω = U|_Ω`, since `ι_s U' = ι_s U` almost everywhere on `Ω`
(`Rd.restrictProj_eq_restrictProj_of_ae_eq`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.restrictL_comp.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.restrictL_comp_sobolevExtensionL
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.restrictL_comp.docstring:
**Restriction after extension is the identity**: `(E u)|_Ω = u` for every jet `u` of
`W^1_p(Ω)` (`Rd.SobolevExtensionOp.restrictL_comp_toContinuousLinearMap`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.reflectionExte.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.reflectionExtension_mul_eq_of_mem
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.reflectionExte.docstring:
**The extension by reflection of a cutoff agrees with the function near the patch**: if
`χ = 1` near `B̄(c_j, ρ_j - 2ε)` with `ε ≥ 0`, then the extension by reflection of `χ f` in the
graph domain `Ω_j` is `f` on `Ω ∩ B(c_j, ρ_j - 2ε)`, a subset of `Ω_j`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.inter_ball_eq`, `Rd.LipschitzGraph.reflectionExtension_of_mem`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.quotientEquivT.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.quotientEquivTraceSpace
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.quotientEquivT.docstring:
**The trace space as a quotient**: `H^s(Ω) ⧸ ker γ_s` is isometrically isomorphic to the trace
space, by the definition of the trace space as an orthogonal complement (Mathlib's
`Submodule.quotientEquivOrthogonal`); the class of `u` corresponds to `γ_s u`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.quotientEquivTraceSpace_mk`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.patch.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.patch
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.patch.docstring:
The **patches** of `Ω` for `ε, δ`: the inner patch `{infDist(·, Ωᶜ) > 2δ}` (index `none`) and
the shrunk boundary balls `B(c_j, ρ_j - 2ε)` (index `some j`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.outwardNormal_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.outwardNormal_graphMap_ae
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.outwardNormal_.docstring:
**The unit normal in a chart**: `ν(γ_j x') = ν_j(x')` for almost every `x' ∈ H_j` with
`γ_j(x') ∈ B_j` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.outwardNormal_ae_eq_normalAt`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.outwardNormal_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.outwardNormal_ae_eq_normalAt
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.outwardNormal_.docstring:
**The unit normal is the chart normal**: for every chart `j` and `σ`-almost every `y ∈ B_j`,
`ν(y) = ν_j(P_j y)`. On `Γ`, `ν(y) = ∑_k ψ_k(y) ν_k(P_k y)` is a combination with weights
summing to `1` of chart normals that all agree with `ν_j(P_j y)`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.normalAt_graphProj_ae_eq`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.outwardNormal.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.outwardNormal
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.outwardNormal.docstring:
**The outward unit normal field** `ν(y) = ∑_j ψ_j(y) ν_j(P_j y)` of `Ω`, pasted from the
outward unit normals `ν_j` of the charts (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.normalAt`) with the canonical
resolution of unity `ψ = Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryPartition`, which is nonnegative. It
is defined on all of `V`, measurable and of norm at most `1`; for `y ∈ Γ` it is a convex
combination of the chart normals `ν_j(P_j y)` with `ψ_j(y) > 0`. On each boundary ball `B_j` it
is the chart normal `ν_j(P_j y)` for `σ`-almost every `y`, by the Gauss–Green theorem in two
charts (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.outwardNormal_ae_eq_normalAt`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ofCharts.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ofCharts
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ofCharts.docstring:
**The bounded Lipschitz domain of a family of charts**: let `Ω` be open and bounded, and let
each frontier point `z` carry a radius `r(z) > 0` and a Lipschitz graph domain `G(z)` that agrees
with `Ω` on `B(z, r(z))`. The charts at the finitely many chosen centres
(`Rd.frontierCenters`) form a `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain` with carrier `Ω`, and each of its graph
domains is one of the `G(z)` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_graph_ofCharts_eq`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.normalAt_graph.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.normalAt_graphProj_ae_eq
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.normalAt_graph.docstring:
**The chart normals agree on the overlaps**: for `σ`-almost every `y ∈ B_j ∩ B_k`,
`ν_j(P_j y) = ν_k(P_k y)` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.normalAt_graphMap_ae_eq` and the null sets
of `σ` in the chart, `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_surfaceMeasure_ball_iff`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.normalAt_graph.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.normalAt_graphMap_ae_eq
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.normalAt_graph.docstring:
**The chart normals agree on the overlaps, in the chart**: for almost every `x' ∈ H_j` with
`γ_j(x') ∈ B_j ∩ B_k`, `ν_j(x') = ν_k(P_k γ_j x')`. The density
`⟪v, ν_j - ν_k ∘ P_k ∘ γ_j⟫ √(1 + ‖∇φ_j‖²)` integrates to zero against every test function `φ` on
the open set `γ_j⁻¹(B_j ∩ B_k)`, which is `g ∘ γ_j` for a test function `g` with support in
`B_j ∩ B_k` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.exists_contDiff_comp_graphMap_eq`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_graphMap_mul_inner_normalAt_sub_eq_zero`); so it vanishes
almost everywhere there (Mathlib's `IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero`), for each
vector `v` of an orthonormal basis.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.norm_outwardNo.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.norm_outwardNormal_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.norm_outwardNo.docstring: The unit normal field has norm at most `1`: `‖ν(y)‖ ≤ ∑_j ψ_j(y) ≤ 1`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.norm_domainTra.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.norm_domainTrace_apply_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.norm_domainTra.docstring: The trace has norm at most `1`: `‖γ_s u‖ ≤ ‖u‖`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.nonempty_compl.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.nonempty_compl
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.nonempty_compl.docstring:
In dimension `n ≥ 1` the complement of a bounded Lipschitz domain is nonempty, since `V` is
unbounded (Mathlib's `NormedSpace.unbounded_univ`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.modNorm_extens.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.modNorm_extensionSum_lt_top
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.modNorm_extens.docstring:
**The localised extensions have a finite norm**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < 1`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`,
`L ≥ 2`, smooth `ζ_j` with derivatives bounded up to order `L` and `G_j ∈ B^s_{p,q}(H_j)`, the sum
`F = ∑_j ζ_j E_j G_j` of the localised extensions has
`‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(k(s+1/p)) ω_L(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphExtension_lt_top`, `Rd.modNorm_mulLp_lt_top`,
`Rd.modNorm_finsetSum_lt_top`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.modNorm_eq_mod.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.modNorm_eq_modNormOn_of_carrier_eq_univ
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.modNorm_eq_mod.docstring:
**On the whole space the intrinsic quasi-norm is the quasi-norm on `V`**: if `Ω = V`
(possible only for `V = {0}`, since `Ω` is bounded), then
`‖f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q}`
`= ‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q}` (`Rd.modNormOn_univ`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.modNorm_besovE.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.modNorm_besovExtendLp_lt_top
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.modNorm_besovE.docstring:
**The extension from the boundary has a finite quasi-norm**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < t < 1`,
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and `g ∈ B^t_{p,q}(Γ)`,
`‖E_Γ g‖_p + ‖(2^(k(t+1/p)) ω_2(E_Γ g, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.modNorm_extensionSum_lt_top`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.modNormOn_mono.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.modNormOn_mono_set
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.modNormOn_mono.docstring:
The intrinsic quasi-norm of `f` on a measurable `T ⊆ Ω` is at most that on `Ω`
(`Rd.modNormOn_mono_of_subset`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_zeroBounda.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_zeroBoundarySpace_of_sobolevToL2_eq_indicatorLp
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_zeroBounda.docstring:
**A function whose zero extension lies in `H^s(V)` lies in `H^s_0(Ω)`**: for `s ≥ 0`,
`u ∈ H^s(Ω)` and
`U' ∈ H^s(V)` with `ι_s U' = 1_Ω ι_s u`, `U'` lies in `H̃^s(Ω)`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace_of_sobolevToL2_eq_indicatorLp`) and restricts to `u`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.restrictProj_eq_of_sobolevToL2_eq_indicatorLp`), and restrictions of
`H̃^s(Ω)` lie in `H^s_0(Ω)` (`Rd.range_tildeToRestrictionL_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_traceKer_i.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_traceKer_iff
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_traceKer_i.docstring:
**The trace kernel by the boundary trace**: for every resolution of unity `ψ`, `u ∈ H^s(Ω)`
lies in the trace kernel iff its boundary trace `Tr_Γ ι_s u` vanishes almost everywhere on `Γ`. In
particular the trace kernel does not depend on the resolution of unity in its definition. The
chart traces are the localised boundary traces (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartTrace_ae_eq`),
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eventuallyEq_zero_iff_forall_chart` collects them, and the boundary
traces of two resolutions agree almost everywhere on `Γ`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_eventuallyEq`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace_of_sobolevToL2_eq_indicatorLp
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace.docstring:
**Zero extensions lie in `H̃^s(Ω)`**: for `s ≥ 0` and `U, U' ∈ H^s(V)` with
`ι_s U' = 1_Ω ι_s U`, `ι_s U'` vanishes outside `Ω`, so `U' ∈ H̃^s(Ω)`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace_iff_of_nonneg`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace_of_mulLp_chart_of_nonneg
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace.docstring:
**The local lemma: chart pieces of functions vanishing outside `Ω` lie in `H̃^s(Ω)`**, for
`s ≥ 0`: let `U ∈ H^s(V)` with `ι_s U = 0` almost everywhere outside `Ω`, and let `ζ` be a
continuous bounded real function with closed support in the boundary ball `B_j`. Every
`W ∈ H^s(V)` with `ι_s W = ζ ι_s U` lies in `H̃^s(Ω)`. `ι_s W` vanishes outside the compact set
`S = Ω̄_j ∩ supp ζ`, since `Ω ∩ B_j` is the graph domain `Ω_j` inside `B_j`; the cone mollifier of
the chart moves `S` into `Ω_j` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.add_mem_of_mem_closure`,
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.mem_graphCone_of_mem_tsupport_dilate`), and its small dilates keep it inside
`B_j` (`Rd.eventually_tsupport_dilate_add_subset_thickening`,
`Rd.mem_tildeSpace_of_dilate_of_nonneg`). At `s = 1` this is
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace_of_mulLp_chart`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace_of_ae_eq_zero_of_nonneg
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace.docstring:
**Functions vanishing outside `Ω` lie in `H̃^s(Ω)`, `s ≥ 0`**: on a bounded Lipschitz
domain, every `U ∈ H^s(V)` with `ι_s U = 0` almost everywhere outside `Ω` lies in the closure of
the test functions of `Ω`. With a resolution of unity `ψ` equal to one near `Γ`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundaryPartition_nhds`) and the interior cut-off `χ`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_interior_cutoff`), `U = ∑_j ψ_j U + χ U`
(`Rd.exists_sobolevToL2_eq_mulLp`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eq_sum_add_of_ae_eq_zero_of_nonneg`); the chart pieces lie in
`H̃^s(Ω)` by the cone mollifiers
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace_of_mulLp_chart_of_nonneg`), the interior piece since
it vanishes outside a compact subset of `Ω` (`Rd.mem_tildeSpace_of_isCompact_of_nonneg`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace_of_ae_eq_zero
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace.docstring:
**Functions vanishing outside `Ω` lie in `H̃^1(Ω)`**: on a bounded Lipschitz domain, every
`U ∈ H^1(V)` whose `L_2` function vanishes almost everywhere outside `Ω` lies in the closure of the
test functions of `Ω`, the case `s = 1` of
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace_of_ae_eq_zero_of_nonneg` (`Rd.sobolevToL2_one`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace_iff_of_nonneg
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace.docstring:
**`H̃^s(Ω)` is the space of `H^s(V)` functions vanishing outside `Ω`, `s ≥ 0`**: on a bounded
Lipschitz domain, `U ∈ H^s(V)` lies in `H̃^s(Ω)` iff `ι_s U = 0` almost everywhere outside `Ω`
(`Rd.sobolevToL2_ae_eq_zero_of_mem_tildeSpace`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace_of_ae_eq_zero_of_nonneg`). In the notation of
Chandler-Wilde, Hewett and Moiola this is `H̃^s(Ω) = Ĥ^s(Ω)` (Lemma 3.15). Since `Γ` is a null
set (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.volume_frontier`), it is McLean's `H̃^s(Ω) = H^s_{Ω̄}`
(Theorem 3.29) for `s ≥ 0`. At `s = 1` it is `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_tildeSpace_iff`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_frontier_i.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_frontier_iff
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_frontier_i.docstring:
**In a boundary ball the boundary is the graph**: for `y ∈ B_j`, `y ∈ Γ` iff `γ_j(P_j y) = y`,
since `Ω` and `Ω_j` agree on the open ball `B_j` (Mathlib's `frontier_inter_open_inter`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_carrier_if.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_carrier_iff_of_mem_ball
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_carrier_if.docstring:
In a boundary ball `B_i`, membership in `Ω` is membership in the graph domain `Ω_i`, since
`B_i ∩ Ω = B_i ∩ Ω_i`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memSobolevW_so.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memSobolevW_sobolevExtensionL
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memSobolevW_so.docstring: The values of the extension operator lie in `W^1_p(V)`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memSobolevW_in.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memSobolevW_indicatorLp_of_mem_traceKer
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memSobolevW_in.docstring:
**The zero extension of a function with vanishing trace lies in `W^1_2(V)`**: for `u` in the
trace kernel, `1_Ω u ∈ W^1_2(V)`, with the weak derivatives `1_Ω ∂_v u`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.hasWeakLineDeriv_indicatorLp_of_mem_traceKer`,
`Rd.memSobolevW_one_of_forall_hasWeakLineDeriv`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memSobolevOn_i.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memSobolevOn_iff_exists_memApprox
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memSobolevOn_i.docstring:
**`H^1(Ω)` by restrictions of `B^1_{2,2}(V)`**: `f ∈ H^1(Ω)` iff `f` agrees on `Ω` with some
`F` in the approximation space `A^1_2` of the band-limited functions on `V`
(`Rd.memSobolevW_one_iff_memApprox`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memLp_chartPie.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memLp_chartPiece
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memLp_chartPie.docstring:
The chart piece `(ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j` of `g ∈ L_p(Γ)` lies in `L_p(H_j)`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eLpNorm_chartPiece_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memLp_boundary.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memLp_boundaryTrace_sobolevToL2
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memLp_boundary.docstring:
**The boundary trace of `H^s(V)` lies in `L_2(Γ)`**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: for every resolution
of unity `ψ` and `U ∈ H^s(V)`, `Tr_Γ ι_s U ∈ L_2(σ)`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memLp_boundaryTrace` at smoothness `s - 1/2`, `p = q = 2`,
`L = 2`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memLp_boundary.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memLp_boundaryTrace
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memLp_boundary.docstring:
**The boundary trace lies in `L_p(Γ)`**: under the hypotheses of the trace theorem,
`Tr_Γ F ∈ L_p(σ)` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_enorm_boundaryTrace_le`, and
`Tr_j F ∈ L_p(H_j)`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBes.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBesov_sobolevToL2
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBes.docstring:
**The boundary trace of `H^s(V)` functions lies in `B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)`**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`:
for every resolution of unity `ψ` and `U ∈ H^s(V)`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBesov_boundaryTrace` at smoothness `s - 1/2`, `p = q = 2`,
`L = 2`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBes.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBesov_iff_chartPieceLp
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBes.docstring:
**`B^s_{p,q}(Γ)` by the chart pieces in `L_p`**: `g ∈ L_p(Γ)` lies in `B^s_{p,q}(Γ)` iff
every chart piece `G_j` has `‖G_j‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_1(G_j, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBes.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBesov_iff_boundaryBesovNorm_lt_top
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBes.docstring:
**The quasi-norm is finite exactly on `B^s_{p,q}(Γ)`**: `g ∈ B^s_{p,q}(Γ)` iff
`‖g‖_{B^s_{p,q}(Γ)} < ∞`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBes.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBesov_domainExtend
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBes.docstring:
**The boundary traces of the trace space lie in `B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)`**: for every resolution
of unity `ψ` and `t ∈ Ω.TraceSpace s`, `Tr_Γ ι_s (E_s t) ∈ B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBes.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBesov_boundaryTrace
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBes.docstring:
**The boundary trace lies in `B^s_{p,q}(Γ)`** (Schneider–Vybíral, Theorem 4.11, for `p ≥ 1`,
the bound): for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < 1`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `s + 1/p < L` and `F` with
`‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(k(s+1/p)) ω_L(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`. The chart pieces are the traces of `ψ_j F`
on the graph domains (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphTrace_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBes.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBesov_ambientTraceL2
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBes.docstring:
**The trace of `H^s(V)` in `L_2(Γ)` lies in `B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)`**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: for every
resolution of unity `ψ` and `U ∈ H^s(V)`, `T^s_Γ U` is the boundary trace `Tr_Γ ι_s U` almost
everywhere on `Γ` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2_apply_ae`), which lies in
`B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBesov_sobolevToL2`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.measurable_out.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.measurable_outwardNormal
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.measurable_out.docstring: The unit normal field is measurable.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.measurableSet.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.measurableSet
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.measurableSet.docstring: A bounded Lipschitz domain is measurable.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.locallyIntegra.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.locallyIntegrable_inner_normalAt_sub_mul_gramDensity
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.locallyIntegra.docstring:
The density `x' ↦ ⟪v, ν_j(x') - ν_k(P_k γ_j x')⟫ √(1 + ‖∇φ_j(x')‖²)` is locally integrable on
`H_j`: it is measurable and bounded by `2 ‖v‖ √(1 + M_j²)`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_surf.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_surfaceMeasure_of_support
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_surf.docstring:
**Integrals over a boundary ball in the chart**: for every `F : V → [0, ∞]` vanishing outside
`B_j`, `∫_Γ F dσ = ∫_{H_j} F(γ_j x') √(1 + ‖∇φ_j(x')‖²) dx'`, by the area formula for the graph
of `φ_j` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.lintegral_graphMap`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_surf.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_surfaceMeasure_le_sum
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_surf.docstring:
**Integrals over the boundary are at most the sum of the chart integrals**: for every
`F : V → [0, ∞]`, `∫_Γ F dσ ≤ ∑_j ∫_{H_j} (1_{B_j} F)(γ_j x') √(1 + ‖∇φ_j(x')‖²) dx'`, since the
balls `B_j` cover `Γ`. It holds for every `F`, measurable or not.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lint.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lintegral_surfaceMeasure_of_support
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lint.docstring:
**Double integrals over a boundary ball in the chart**: for every `F : V → V → [0, ∞]` that
vanishes unless both points lie in `B_j`,
`∫_Γ ∫_Γ F(x, y) dσ(y) dσ(x) = ∫_{H_j} ∫_{H_j} F(γ_j x', γ_j y') w(y') w(x') dy' dx'` with the
density `w = √(1 + ‖∇φ_j‖²)`, by the chart formula
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_surfaceMeasure_of_support` twice. It holds for every `F`,
measurable or not.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lint.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lintegral_lipschitz_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lint.docstring:
**The Lipschitz part of a chart piece**: for `0 < p < ∞` and `0 < s < 1`,
`∫_{H_j} ∫_{H_j} 1_{B_j}(γ x') |g(γ x')|^p |ψ_j(γ y') - ψ_j(γ x')|^p / |y' - x'|^(n-1+sp) dy' dx'`
is at most `K ∫_Γ |g|^p dσ` with `K = Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartLipschitzConst p ψ j s`: the
inner integral is at most `K` (`Rd.lintegral_rpow_div_norm_rpow_le`, with
`|ψ_j(γ y') - ψ_j(γ x')| ≤ min(D_j (1 + M_j) |y' - x'|, 2 D_j)`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lint.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lintegral_inside_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lint.docstring:
**The inside part of a chart piece**: for every `g`,
`∫_{H_j} ∫_{H_j} 1_{B_j²}(γ x', γ y') |g(γ y') - g(γ x')|^p / |γ y' - γ x'|^(n-1+sp) dy' dx'` is at
most the Gagliardo form of `g` on `Γ` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lintegral_chart_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lint.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lintegral_indicator_le_slobodeckijForm
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lint.docstring:
**The part of the Gagliardo form inside one boundary ball**: for every `f : V → ℂ` and
`s ≥ 0`, `∫_Γ ∫_Γ 1_{B_j²}(x, y) |f(y) - f(x)|^p / |y - x|^(n-1+sp) dσ(y) dσ(x)` is at most
`(1 + M_j²)` times the Gagliardo form on `H_j` of `f ∘ γ_j`: the chart formula
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lintegral_surfaceMeasure_of_support`), the bound
`√(1 + M_j²)` of the density, and `|y' - x'| ≤ |γ_j y' - γ_j x'|`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lint.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lintegral_chart_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lint.docstring:
**Double integrals in the chart are at most those over `Γ`**: for every `F : V → V → [0, ∞]`
that vanishes unless both points lie in `B_j`,
`∫_{H_j} ∫_{H_j} F(γ_j x', γ_j y') dy' dx' ≤ ∫_Γ ∫_Γ F dσ dσ`, since the density
`√(1 + ‖∇φ_j‖²)` is at least `1` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.one_le_ofReal_gramDensity`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_le_c.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_le_chart
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_le_c.docstring:
**Integrals over `Γ` by the chart**: for every `F : V → [0, ∞]` vanishing outside `B_j`,
`∫_Γ F dσ ≤ √(1 + M_j²) ∫_{H_j} F(γ_j x') dx'` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.gramDensity_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_enor.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_enorm_boundaryTrace_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_enor.docstring:
**The `L_p(Γ)` bound of the boundary trace**: under the hypotheses of the trace theorem,
`∫_Γ |Tr_Γ F|^p dσ ≤ ∑_j √(1 + M_j²) ‖Tr_j F‖_{L_p(H_j)}^p`, with the Lipschitz constants `M_j`
of the charts. In the chart `j`, `Tr_Γ F ∘ γ_j = Tr_j F` almost everywhere on `γ_j⁻¹(B_j)`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_graphMap`) and the Gram density is at most
`√(1 + M_j²)` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.gramDensity_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_char.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_chart_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_char.docstring:
**Integrals in the chart are at most those over `Γ`**: for every `F : V → [0, ∞]` vanishing
outside `B_j`, `∫_{H_j} F(γ_j x') dx' ≤ ∫_Γ F dσ`, since the density `√(1 + ‖∇φ_j‖²)` is at least
`1` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.one_le_ofReal_gramDensity`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_char.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_chartPiece_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_char.docstring:
**The `L_p` norm of a chart piece**: for `P > 0`,
`∫_{H_j} |ψ_j(γ_j x') g(γ_j x')|^P dx' ≤ D_j^P ∫_Γ |g|^P dσ` with `D_j = ψ.derivBound j`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_chart_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lineDerivOp_in.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lineDerivOp_indicatorLp_of_mem_traceKer
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lineDerivOp_in.docstring:
**The derivatives of the zero extension of `u ∈ ker γ_s`**, `1 ≤ s < 3/2`: for every direction
`v`, `∂_v(1_Ω ι_s u) = 1_Ω ∂_v(ι_{1,s} u)` as tempered distributions, with `u` read in `H^s(V)`.
`u₁ = ι^Ω_{1,s} u = (ι_{1,s} u)|_Ω` lies in `ker γ_1`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.restrictionInclusion_mem_traceKer`), so `1_Ω ∂_v u₁` is the weak
derivative of `1_Ω ι_1 u₁` on `V`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.hasWeakLineDeriv_indicatorLp_of_mem_traceKer`); on `Ω`, `u₁` and
`ι_{1,s} u` have the same `L_2` function and weak derivatives
(`Rd.sobolevToL2_restrictProj_ae_eq`, `Rd.weakDerivL2_restrictProj_ae_eq`), and weak
derivatives on `V` are derivatives of tempered distributions (`Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_top_iff`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ker_boundaryTr.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ker_boundaryTraceL2
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ker_boundaryTr.docstring:
**The kernel of `γ^s_{L_2} : H^s(Ω) → L_2(Γ)` is the trace kernel**: `γ^s_{L_2} u = 0` in
`L_2(Γ)` iff the boundary trace of `u` vanishes almost everywhere on `Γ`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_traceKer_iff`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isSobolevExten.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isSobolevExtensionMap_interior_cutoff
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isSobolevExten.docstring:
**The inner patch by a cutoff is linear**: for `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞` and a smooth `χ` with values in
`[0, 1]`, compact closed support in `Ω`, `|∂_{e_i} χ| ≤ d_i` and `χ = 1` near
`{infDist(·, Ωᶜ) ≥ 2δ}`, the map `f ↦ χ f` is a linear extension of Sobolev functions on `Ω` from
`{x ∈ Ω : infDist(x, Ωᶜ) > 2δ}` with the constant `1 + ∑_i d_i`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_hasWeakLineDeriv_mul_interior`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isSobolevExten.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isSobolevExtensionMap_boundary_reflection
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isSobolevExten.docstring:
**The boundary patches by reflection are linear**: for `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, `ε ≥ 0` and a smooth `χ`
with values in `[0, 1]`, closed support in `B(c_j, ρ_j)`, `|∂_{e_i} χ| ≤ d_i` and `χ = 1` near
`B̄(c_j, ρ_j - 2ε)`, the map `f ↦ E_j(χ f)` (the extension by reflection in the graph domain `Ω_j`)
is a linear extension of Sobolev functions on `Ω` from `Ω ∩ B(c_j, ρ_j - 2ε)` with the constant
`Rd.reflectionConst` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_hasWeakLineDeriv_reflectionExtension_mul`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.reflectionExtension_mul_eq_of_mem`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isFiniteMeasur.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isFiniteMeasure_surfaceMeasure
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isFiniteMeasur.docstring:
**The surface measure is finite**: `σ(Γ) ≤ ∑_j √(1 + M_j²) |γ_j⁻¹(B_j)|`, and the sets
`γ_j⁻¹(B_j) ⊆ H_j` are bounded since the graph maps are antilipschitz.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isCompact_fron.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isCompact_frontier
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isCompact_fron.docstring: The boundary of a bounded Lipschitz domain is compact.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isCompact_clos.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isCompact_closure
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isCompact_clos.docstring: The closure of a bounded Lipschitz domain is compact.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isClosed_trace.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isClosed_traceKer
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isClosed_trace.docstring: The trace kernel is closed, an intersection of kernels of bounded operators.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isBounded_patc.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isBounded_patch
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isBounded_patc.docstring:
The patches are bounded for `δ ≥ 0`: the inner patch lies in `Ω`
(`Rd.setOf_lt_infDist_compl_subset`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.inter_ball_eq.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.inter_ball_eq
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.inter_ball_eq.docstring: On a concentric ball of smaller radius the domain is the graph domain.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_surfa.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_surfaceMeasure_of_support
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_surfa.docstring:
**Complex integrals over a boundary ball in the chart**: for every `F : V → ℂ` vanishing outside
`B_j`, `∫_Γ F dσ = ∫_{H_j} F(γ_j x') √(1 + ‖∇φ_j(x')‖²) dx'`, by the area formula for the graph of
`φ_j` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.integral_graphMap`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_surfa.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_surfaceMeasure
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_surfa.docstring:
**The surface measure in the charts, for complex integrals**: for every resolution of unity `ψ`
on the boundary, of any sign, and every `σ`-integrable `f : V → ℂ`,
`∫_Γ f dσ = ∑_j ∫_{H_j} ψ_j(γ_j x') f(γ_j x') √(1 + ‖∇φ_j(x')‖²) dx'`. On `Γ`, `f = ∑_j ψ_j f`;
each `ψ_j f` is integrable since `ψ_j` is bounded, and vanishes outside `B_j`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_surfaceMeasure_of_support`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_mul_i.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_mul_inner_normalAt_sub_eq_zero
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_mul_i.docstring:
**The chart normals give the same boundary integrals**: for a `C^1` function `g` with compact
support in `B_j ∩ B_k` and every `v`, `∫_Γ g ⟪v, ν_j ∘ P_j - ν_k ∘ P_k⟫ dσ = 0`, since both
chart integrals are `∫_Ω ∂_v g` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_lineDeriv_eq_chart`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_graph.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_graphMap_mul_inner_normalAt_sub_eq_zero
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_graph.docstring:
**The chart identity in the chart**: for a `C^1` function `g` with compact support in
`B_j ∩ B_k` and every `v`,
`∫_{H_j} g(γ_j x') ⟪v, ν_j(x') - ν_k(P_k γ_j x')⟫ √(1 + ‖∇φ_j(x')‖²) dx' = 0`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_mul_inner_normalAt_sub_eq_zero` and the surface measure in the
chart).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_ambie.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_ambientTraceL2_mul_inner_outwardNormal_eq
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_ambie.docstring:
**The boundary integral of Green's formula in the charts**: for every resolution of unity `ψ`,
`U, W ∈ H^1(V)` and every direction `v`,
`∫_Γ T_Γ U · T_Γ W ⟪v, ν⟫ dσ = ∑_j ∫_{H_j} ψ_j(γ_j x') Tr_j U Tr_j W n^j_v dx'`, by the
surface measure in the charts (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integral_surfaceMeasure`), the traces and
the normal in the charts, and `⟪v, ν_j⟫ √(1 + ‖∇φ_j‖²) = n^j_v`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.inner_normalAt_mul_gramDensity`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integrable_mul.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integrable_mul_inner_normalAt
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integrable_mul.docstring:
For a continuous `g` with compact support, `y ↦ g(y) ⟪v, ν_j(P_j y)⟫` is integrable with
respect to the finite surface measure: it is bounded and measurable.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integrable_amb.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integrable_ambientTraceL2_mul_inner_outwardNormal
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.integrable_amb.docstring:
The boundary integrand `T_Γ U · T_Γ W ⟪v, ν⟫` of Green's formula, with the trace
`T_Γ = Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2 1` of `H^1(V)`, is integrable with respect to the
surface measure: a product of two `L_2(Γ)` functions and a bounded one.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.indicator_one_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.indicator_one_sub_sum_eventuallyEq_zero
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.indicator_one_.docstring:
**The interior remainder vanishes near the complement**: if `∑_j ψ_j = 1` on a neighbourhood
of `Γ`, the function `1_Ω (1 - ∑_j ψ_j)` vanishes on a neighbourhood of every point outside `Ω`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.hasWeakLineDer.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.hasWeakLineDeriv_mul_graph
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.hasWeakLineDer.docstring:
**Cutoffs carry weak derivatives from `Ω` to a graph domain**: if `g = ∂_w f` weakly on `Ω`
and the smooth `χ` has closed support in the boundary ball `B(c_j, ρ_j)`, then
`χ g + (∂_w χ) f = ∂_w (χ f)` weakly on the graph domain `Ω_j`
(`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.mul_of_tsupport_subset`, `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.inter_ball_eq`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.hasWeakLineDer.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.hasWeakLineDeriv_indicatorLp_of_mem_traceKer
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.hasWeakLineDer.docstring:
**The weak derivatives of the zero extension**: for `u` in the trace kernel and every
direction `v`, the zero extension `1_Ω ∂_v u` of the weak derivative is the weak derivative of the
zero extension `1_Ω u` on `V`. Tested against `φ`, this is
`∫_Ω (∂_v u) φ = -∫_Ω u ∂_v φ`, Green's formula without boundary term
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.setIntegral_green_of_mem_traceKer`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.graph_toOpens_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.graph_toOpens_inf_ball_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.graph_toOpens_.docstring:
**The graph domain near a boundary ball lies in `Ω`**: `Ω_j ∩ B(c_j, ρ_j) ⊆ Ω` as open sets
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.inter_ball_eq`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.graphTrace_mul.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.graphTrace_mulLp_ae_boundaryTrace
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.graphTrace_mul.docstring:
**The chart pieces of the boundary trace are traces**: `(ψ_j Tr_Γ F) ∘ γ_j = Tr_j(ψ_j F)` almost
everywhere on `H_j` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_mulLp_ae`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.graphMap_mem_f.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.graphMap_mem_frontier
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.graphMap_mem_f.docstring: The boundary meets `B_j` in the graph of `Ω_j`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.graphMap_graph.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.graphMap_graphProj_graphMap
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.graphMap_graph.docstring:
**Boundary points in two balls lie on both graphs**: if `γ_j(x') ∈ B_j ∩ B_k`, then
`γ_k(P_k γ_j x') = γ_j x'`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.frontier_inter.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.frontier_inter_ball_eq
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.frontier_inter.docstring:
**In a boundary ball the boundary is the graph**: `Γ ∩ B_j = γ_j(H_j) ∩ B_j`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_frontier_iff`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_volume_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_volume_switchSet_inter_closedBall_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_volume_.docstring:
**The boundary layer of a bounded Lipschitz domain**: there is `C < ∞` with
`|S_h(Ω) ∩ B̄(c, ρ)| ≤ C ‖h‖ ρ^(n-1)` for all `c, h ∈ V` and `ρ ≥ ‖h‖`. For short steps
`‖h‖ ≤ ε`, with `ε` from `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_shrink`, this is
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.volume_switchSet_inter_closedBall_le_of_le`; for long steps
`|S_h(Ω)| ≤ 2 |Ω|` (`Rd.volume_switchSet_le`) and `‖h‖ ρ^(n-1) ≥ ε^n`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_volume_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_volume_switchSet_inter_closedBall_div_two_pow_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_volume_.docstring:
**The boundary layer at the scale of an atom**: there is `C < ∞` with
`|S_h(Ω) ∩ B̄(c, d 2^(-j))| ≤ C d^n 2^(-jn) min(1, 2^j ‖h‖)` for all `c, h ∈ V`, `d ≥ 1` and
`j ∈ ℕ`. For `‖h‖ ≤ d 2^(-j)` this follows from
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_volume_switchSet_inter_closedBall_le` and
`Rd.mul_div_two_pow_pow_sub_one_le` (for `h ≠ 0`, so `n ≥ 1`; for `h = 0` the switch set is
empty, `Rd.switchSet_zero`); for longer steps the ball has volume `d^n |B_1| 2^(-jn)`
(`Rd.volume_closedBall_div_two_pow`) and `min(1, 2^j ‖h‖) = 1`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_traceSp.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_traceSpace_of_memBoundaryBesov_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_traceSp.docstring:
**Bounded preimages under the trace**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: for every resolution of unity `ψ`
there is `C < ∞` such that every `g ∈ B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)` is `Tr_Γ ι_s(E_s t)` almost everywhere
on `Γ` for some `t ∈ Ω.TraceSpace s` with `‖t‖ ≤ C ‖g‖_{B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)}`; `t = γ_s(U|_Ω)` for
the `U` of `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevToL2_boundaryTrace_eq_le`. By uniqueness
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_domainExtend_eventuallyEq_iff`) `t` is determined by `g`;
the linear right inverse is `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceRightInverse`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevToL2_eq_indicatorLp_of_mem_traceKer
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.docstring:
**The zero extension of `u ∈ ker γ_s` lies in `H^s(V)`**, `1 ≤ s < 3/2`: there is
`U' ∈ H^s(V)` with `ι_s U' = 1_Ω ι_s u`. As `0 ≤ s - 1 < 1/2`, multiplication by `1_Ω` keeps
`H^{s-1}(V)` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevToL2_eq_indicatorLp`), so `1_Ω ι_s u` lies
in `H^{s-1}(V)`, and so do its derivatives `1_Ω ∂_v(ι_{1,s} u)`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lineDerivOp_indicatorLp_of_mem_traceKer`,
`Rd.memSobolev_bessel_weakDerivL2_sobolevInclusion`); a tempered distribution in `H^{s-1}(V)` with
all first derivatives in `H^{s-1}(V)` lies in `H^s(V)`
(`TemperedDistribution.memSobolev_add_one_iff`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevToL2_eq_indicatorLp
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.docstring:
**Zero extensions in `H^s(V)` for `0 ≤ s < 1/2`**: for every `U ∈ H^s(V)` there is
`U' ∈ H^s(V)` with `ι_s U' = 1_Ω ι_s U`. At `s = 0` every `L_2` function is `ι_0 U'`
(`Rd.sobolevToL2_zero_surjective`); for `0 < s < 1/2` the multiplier theorem
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_modNorm_indicatorLp_le`) and `Rd.modNorm_sobolevToL2_le` give
`1_Ω ι_s U` a finite `B^s_{2,2}` quantity, so it is `ι_s U'`
(`Rd.exists_sobolevToL2_eq_of_modNorm_lt_top`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevToL2_eq_besovExtendLp
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.docstring:
**The extension from the boundary maps `B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)` into `H^s(V)`**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`:
for every `g ∈ L_2(Γ)` in `B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)`, the extension `E_Γ g`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.besovExtendLp`) is `ι_s W` for some `W ∈ H^s(V)`. Its quasi-norm with
differences of order `2` and weight `(s - 1/2) + 1/2 = s` is finite
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.modNorm_besovExtendLp_lt_top`), and such functions come from
`H^s(V)` (`Rd.exists_sobolevToL2_eq_of_modNorm_lt_top`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevToL2_boundaryTrace_eq_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.docstring:
**A bounded extension from `B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)` into `H^s(V)`**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: for every
resolution of unity `ψ` there is `C < ∞` such that every `g ∈ B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)` is
`Tr_Γ ι_s U` almost everywhere on `Γ` for some `U ∈ H^s(V)` with
`‖U‖ ≤ C ‖g‖_{B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)}`: the bounded extension
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundaryTrace_eq_le` at `p = q = L = 2` and smoothness
`s - 1/2`) gives `F ∈ B^s_{2,2}(V)`, which is `ι_s U` for some `U ∈ H^s(V)`
(`Rd.exists_sobolevToL2_eq_of_modNorm_lt_top`) with
`‖U‖ ≤ Rd.sobolevBesovInvConst V s 2 ‖F‖_{B^s_{2,2}}` (`Rd.enorm_le_modNorm_sobolevToL2`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevExtensionOp_reflection
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.docstring:
**The extension operator by reflection with a finite constant**: for a bounded Lipschitz
domain `Ω` in dimension `n ≥ 1` and `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞` there is an extension operator from `Ω` with a
finite constant (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevExtensionOp_of_patches` with the patch
operators `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevExtensionOp_boundary_reflection` and
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevExtensionOp_interior_cutoff`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevExtensionOp_of_patches
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.docstring:
**Pasting the patch operators**: for a bounded Lipschitz domain `Ω` in dimension `n ≥ 1` and
`1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, if for every `ε > 0` and every `j` there is an extension operator from the boundary
patch `Ω ∩ B(c_j, ρ_j - 2ε)` with a finite constant, and for every `δ > 0` one from the inner patch
`{x ∈ Ω : infDist(x, Ωᶜ) > 2δ}`, then there is an extension operator from `Ω` with a finite
constant (the patches of `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.patch`, pasted by
`Rd.sobolevExtensionOp_of_cover`, `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_of_patches`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevExtensionOp_interior_cutoff
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.docstring:
**The inner patch carries an extension operator**: for `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞` and `δ > 0` there is an
extension operator from `{x ∈ Ω : infDist(x, Ωᶜ) > 2δ}` with a finite constant
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isSobolevExtensionMap_interior_cutoff` with the cutoff of
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_cutoff_interior`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevExtensionOp_interior
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.docstring:
**The inner patch**: there is an extension operator from `{infDist(·, Ωᶜ) > 2δ}` with a finite
constant (`Rd.LocalMeansBump.sobolevExtensionOp` on `T = Ω` with a centred bump of radius
`≤ δ / 2`, `Rd.sub_mem_of_lt_infDist_of_norm_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevExtensionOp_boundary_reflection
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.docstring:
**The boundary patches by reflection carry extension operators**: for `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞` and
`ε > 0` there is an extension operator from `Ω ∩ B(c_j, ρ_j - 2ε)` with a finite constant
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.isSobolevExtensionMap_boundary_reflection` with the cutoff of
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_cutoff_boundary`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevExtensionOp_boundary
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.docstring:
**The boundary patches**: there are extension operators from `Ω ∩ B(c_j, ρ_j - 2ε)` with finite
constants (`Rd.LocalMeansBump.sobolevExtensionOp` on `T = Ω_j ∩ B(c_j, ρ_j) ⊆ Ω` with the cone
bump of `Ω_j` rescaled to radius `≤ ε / 2`, `Rd.LipschitzGraph.exists_coneBump_radius_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevExtensionOp
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolev.docstring:
**Rychkov's extension operator with a finite constant**: for a bounded Lipschitz domain
`Ω` in dimension `n ≥ 1` and `1 < p < ∞` there is an extension operator from `Ω` with a finite
constant (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevExtensionOp_of_patches` with the patch operators
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevExtensionOp_boundary` and
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevExtensionOp_interior`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_slobode.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_slobodeckijForm_chartPiece_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_slobode.docstring:
**The Gagliardo form of a chart piece by the form on `Γ`**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < 1`, a
resolution of unity `ψ` and a chart `j` there is `K < ∞` such that for every measurable `g` the
Gagliardo form on `H_j` of `G = (ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j` is at most
`K (∫_Γ |g|^p dσ + ∫_Γ ∫_Γ |g(y) - g(x)|^p / |y - x|^(n-1+sp) dσ dσ)`. The parts of
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.slobodeckijForm_chartPiece_le` are bounded by
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lintegral_inside_le`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lintegral_lipschitz_le`,
`Rd.lintegral_lintegral_mul_indicator_le` and
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_chartPiece_le`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_shrink.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_shrink
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_shrink.docstring:
**Shrinking the boundary balls**: `Γ ⊆ ⋃_j B(c_j, ρ_j - 2ε)` for some `ε > 0`, by
compactness of `Γ`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_of_patc.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_of_patches
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_of_patc.docstring:
**Pasting over the patches**: let `P U C` be a property of a set `U ⊆ V` and a constant
`C ∈ [0, ∞]` that passes from the sets `Ω ∩ U_i` of every cover `(U_i)_{i ∈ {0, …, N}}` of `Ω̄` by
`N + 1` bounded open sets, one for each boundary ball and one inner set (indexed by
`Option (Fin Ω.N)`), with finite constants, to `Ω`, with a finite constant. If `P` holds with a
finite constant for every boundary patch `Ω ∩ B(c_j, ρ_j - 2ε)`, `ε > 0`, and for every inner
patch `Ω ∩ {infDist(·, Ωᶜ) > 2δ}`, `δ > 0`, then it holds for `Ω` with a finite constant: for
suitable `ε` and `δ` the patches `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.patch` cover `Ω̄`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_shrink`, `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_interior_margin`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.closure_subset_iUnion_patch`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_modNorm.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_modNorm_indicatorLp_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_modNorm.docstring:
**The indicator of a bounded Lipschitz domain is a pointwise multiplier of `B^s_{p,q}(V)` for
`0 < s < 1/p`** (Triebel 2002, Proposition 5.3 and Remark 5.4; Schneider–Vybíral, Theorem 5.4(i)
and Remark 5.10): for `1 ≤ p < ∞` there is `C < ∞` with
`‖1_Ω F‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_1(1_Ω F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q}`
`≤ C (‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_1(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})` for every `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and every
`F ∈ L_p(V)`. The smooth cell atoms of `F`
(`Rd.LocalMeansBump.atomic_decomposition_smooth` with the standard bump, radius factor `2 + n`)
become regular atoms of exponent `1/p` after multiplication by `1_Ω`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_isRegularAtom_indicator`), with the same coefficients; the
reproducing formula (`Rd.LocalMeansBump.tendsto_sum_dual_localMean`) passes through the bounded
operator `1_Ω`; the atomic synthesis (`Rd.modNorm_le_coeffNorm`) and the bound of the local means
by differences (`Rd.LocalMeansBump.localMeansNorm_le`) finish the proof.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_modNorm.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_modNorm_besovExtendLp_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_modNorm.docstring:
**The extension from the boundary is bounded** (following Schneider–Vybíral, Theorem 4.11,
for `p ≥ 1`): for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < t < 1` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` there is `C < ∞` with
`‖E_Γ g‖_p + ‖(2^(k(t+1/p)) ω_2(E_Γ g, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C ‖g‖_{B^t_{p,q}(Γ)}` for every
`g ∈ B^t_{p,q}(Γ)`: the triangle inequality `Rd.modNorm_finsetSum_le` and the chart bounds
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.exists_modNorm_mulLp_graphExtension_le`, `C = ∑_j K_j`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_mem_zer.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_mem_zeroBoundarySpace_enorm_sub_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_mem_zer.docstring:
**Approximation of `ker γ_s` by `H^s_0(Ω)` with a bound**, `1/2 < s ≤ 1`: there is `K < ∞`
such that for every `u ∈ ker γ_s` and every `W' ∈ H^1(V)` some `y ∈ H^s_0(Ω)` has
`‖y - u‖ ≤ K ‖ι_{s,1} W' - u‖`. Let `g = T^1_Γ W'` and `W ∈ H^1(V)` with `ι_1 W = E_Γ g`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevToL2_eq_besovExtendLp` at `s = 1`). The correction
`(W' - W)|_Ω` lies in `ker γ_1 = H^1_0(Ω)`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.restrictProj_sub_mem_traceKer`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.traceKer_one_eq_zeroBoundarySpace`), so `y = ι^Ω_{s,1}((W' - W)|_Ω)`
lies in `H^s_0(Ω)` (`Rd.restrictionInclusion_mem_zeroBoundarySpace`), and
`y - u = (ι_{s,1} W' - u - ι_{s,1} W)|_Ω`. Since `T^s_Γ u = 0`, `g = T^s_Γ(ι_{s,1} W' - u)`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2_sobolevInclusion`), so
`‖g‖_{B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)} ≤ C_tr ‖ι_{s,1} W' - u‖`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundaryBesovNorm_sobolevToL2_le`); `ι_{s,1} W` has the
`L_2` function `E_Γ g` as well, so `‖ι_{s,1} W‖ ≤ C_E ‖g‖_{B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)}`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_enorm_le_of_sobolevToL2_eq_besovExtendLp`). The one function
`E_Γ g` serves the levels `1` and `s`; `K = 1 + C_E C_tr`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_memSobo.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_memSobolevW_of_memWeakSobolev
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_memSobo.docstring:
**The extension theorem for `W^1_p`, `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`** (Evans–Gariepy, Section 4.4; Brezis 2011,
Chapter 9): for a bounded Lipschitz domain `Ω` and `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, every `f ∈ W^1_p(Ω)` agrees almost
everywhere on `Ω` with some `F ∈ W^1_p(V)`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_extendsSobolev_reflection` in dimension `n ≥ 1`,
`Rd.exists_memSobolevW_of_memWeakSobolev_of_subsingleton` in dimension `0`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_memAppr.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_memApprox_extension_iff_indicator
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_memAppr.docstring:
**Restrictions of band-limited approximation spaces to bounded Lipschitz domains**: for
`1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < r` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `f` agrees on `Ω` with some `F` in the approximation
space `A^s_q(L_p(V))` of band-limited functions iff
`‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_local_e.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_local_extension_interior_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_local_e.docstring:
**The inner patch with a bound**: there is `C < ∞` such that on `{infDist(·, Ωᶜ) > 2δ}` every
`f` with `N_Ω(f) = ‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞` agrees with a
function `F` with `‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C N_Ω(f)`, by the local extension
with a centred bump of radius `≤ δ / r` (`Rd.LocalMeansBump.exists_local_extension_le`); the bump
and `C` depend only on `δ`, `r` and `s`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_local_e.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_local_extension_boundary_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_local_e.docstring:
**The boundary patches with a bound**: there is `C < ∞` such that on `Ω ∩ B(c_j, ρ_j - 2ε)`
every `f` with `N_Ω(f) = ‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞` agrees with a
function `F` with `‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C N_Ω(f)`, by the local extension
with the cone bump of `Ω_j` rescaled to radius `≤ ε / r`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.exists_coneBump_radius_le`, `Rd.LocalMeansBump.exists_local_extension_le`);
the bump and `C` depend only on `ε`, `r`, `s` and `j`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_isRegul.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_isRegularAtom_indicator
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_isRegul.docstring:
**Indicators of smooth atoms are regular atoms** (the mechanism of Schneider–Vybíral,
Theorem 5.4(i)): for `1 ≤ p` (`p = ∞` included, with exponent `1/∞ = 0`) there is `K < ∞` such
that for every smooth atom `a` on `V` of order `1`, level `j`, centre `c`, radius factor `d ≥ 1`
and constant `A`, the function `1_Ω a` is a regular atom of exponent `1/p` and order `1` with the
constant `K A d^n` (`Rd.IsSmoothAtom.eLpNorm_indicator_le_dyadicWeight`,
`Rd.IsSmoothAtom.eLpNorm_fwdDiff_indicator_le_of_volume_le`, with the boundary layer
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_volume_switchSet_inter_closedBall_div_two_pow_le`). The
exponent `1/p` is the volume of the layer, `≈ ‖h‖ ρ^(n-1)`, raised to `1/p`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_interio.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_interior_margin
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_interio.docstring:
**The interior margin**: if `Ωᶜ` is nonempty and `Γ ⊆ ⋃_j B(c_j, ρ_j - 2ε)`, the points of
`Ω` outside these balls have distance `> 2δ` from `Ωᶜ` for some `δ > 0`, by compactness.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_interio.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_interior_cutoff
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_interio.docstring:
**The interior cut-off**: if `∑_j ψ_j = 1` on a neighbourhood of `Γ`, there is a smooth real
