`χ` with compact support in `Ω` and `χ + ∑_j ψ_j = 1` on `Ω`, namely `χ = 1_Ω (1 - ∑_j ψ_j)`,
smooth because it vanishes near every point outside `Ω`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.indicator_one_sub_sum_eventuallyEq_zero`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_hasWeak.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_hasWeakLineDeriv_reflectionExtension_mul
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_hasWeak.docstring:
**The extension by reflection of a cutoff on a boundary patch, with its bound**: for `1 ≤ p`, a
smooth `χ` with values in `[0, 1]`, closed support in the boundary ball `B(c_j, ρ_j)` and
`|∂_{e_i} χ| ≤ d_i`, and `f ∈ L_p(Ω)` with weak derivatives `g_i = ∂_{e_i} f ∈ L_p(Ω)` on `Ω`, the
extension by reflection `F` of `χ f` in the graph domain `Ω_j` has weak derivatives
`G_k = ∂_{e_k} F` on `V` with
`‖F‖_p + ∑_k ‖G_k‖_p ≤ C (‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)} + ∑_i ‖g_i‖_{L_p(Ω)})`,
`C = 2 + 2 n (1 + M_j)² (1 + ∑_i d_i)` (`Rd.reflectionConst`) with the Lipschitz constant `M_j` of
the graph of `Ω_j`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.hasWeakLineDeriv_mul_graph`,
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasWeakLineDeriv_reflectionExtension`, `Rd.add_sum_le_of_le_two_mul`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_hasWeak.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_hasWeakLineDeriv_mul_interior
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_hasWeak.docstring:
**The cutoff of a function on the inner patch, with its bound**: for `1 ≤ p`, a smooth `χ` with
values in `[0, 1]`, compact closed support in `Ω`, `|∂_{e_i} χ| ≤ d_i` and `χ = 1` near
`{infDist(·, Ωᶜ) ≥ 2δ}`, and `f` with weak derivatives `g_i = ∂_{e_i} f` on `Ω`, the function
`χ f` has weak derivatives `G_i = ∂_{e_i} (χ f)` on `V`, equals `f` on
`{x ∈ Ω : infDist(x, Ωᶜ) > 2δ}`, and
`‖χ f‖_p + ∑_i ‖G_i‖_p ≤ (1 + ∑_i d_i) (‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)} + ∑_i ‖g_i‖_{L_p(Ω)})`
(`Rd.HasWeakLineDeriv.cutoff_top`, `Rd.eLpNorm_mul_add_sum_le_of_tsupport_subset`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_extends.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_extendsSobolev_reflection
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_extends.docstring:
**The extension theorem for `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞` with a bound**: for a bounded Lipschitz domain `Ω` in
dimension `n ≥ 1` and `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞` there is a finite constant `C` such that every `f ∈ L_p(Ω)` with
weak derivatives `g_i = ∂_{e_i} f ∈ L_p(Ω)` agrees on `Ω` with some `F ∈ W^1_p(V)` whose weak
derivatives `G_i = ∂_{e_i} F` satisfy
`‖F‖_p + ∑_i ‖G_i‖_p ≤ C (‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)} + ∑_i ‖g_i‖_{L_p(Ω)})`: the extension operator by
reflection (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_sobolevExtensionOp_reflection`) applied to `f`
(`Rd.SobolevExtensionOp.extendsSobolev`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_enorm_l.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_enorm_le_of_sobolevToL2_eq_besovExtendLp
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_enorm_l.docstring:
**The extension from the boundary is bounded into `H^s(V)`**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: there is
`C < ∞` with `‖W‖ ≤ C ‖g‖_{B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)}` for every `g ∈ L_2(Γ)` in `B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)`
and every `W ∈ H^s(V)` with `ι_s W = E_Γ g`: the bound of the extension
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_modNorm_besovExtendLp_le`) and the bound of `H^s(V)` by
differences of order `2` (`Rd.enorm_le_modNorm_sobolevToL2`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_enorm_l.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_enorm_le_boundaryBesovNorm_domainExtend
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_enorm_l.docstring:
**The norm of the trace space of `H^s(Ω)` is bounded by the norm of the boundary trace**: for
every resolution of unity `ψ` there is `C < ∞` with
`‖t‖ ≤ C ‖Tr_Γ ι_s(E_s t)‖_{B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)}` for every `t ∈ Ω.TraceSpace s`: the bounded
preimage (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_traceSpace_of_memBoundaryBesov_le`) is `t`, since
elements of the trace space are determined by their boundary traces
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_domainExtend_eventuallyEq_iff`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_enorm_g.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_enorm_graphTrace_localizeL2_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_enorm_g.docstring:
**The chart traces are bounded**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: `‖Tr_j(ψ_j ι_s U)‖_{L_2(H_j)} ≤ C ‖U‖` for
every `U ∈ H^s(V)`, for every resolution of unity `ψ`, with
`C = K M c Rd.sobolevBesovConst V s 2`. The trace is at most `K` times the `B^{1/2}_{2,1}`
quantity of `ψ_j ι_s U` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.enorm_graphTrace_le`), which is at most `M` times that
of `ι_s U` (`Rd.modNorm_mulLp_le`, with the multiplier constant `M = Rd.multiplierTotal` of `ψ_j`
for differences of order `2` and smoothness `1/2`), which is at most
`c Rd.sobolevBesovConst V s 2 ‖U‖` with `c = ‖(2^{-k(s-1/2)})_k‖_{ℓ_2}`
(`Rd.modNorm_half_one_le_norm_of_lt`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_eLpNorm.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_eLpNorm_boundaryTrace_sobolevToL2_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_eLpNorm.docstring:
**The `L_2(Γ)` bound of the trace of `H^s(V)`**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`:
`‖Tr_Γ ι_s U‖_{L_2(Γ)} ≤ C ‖U‖` for every resolution of unity and every `U ∈ H^s(V)`, with
`C = (∑_j √(1 + M_j²) K_j²)^(1/2)` for the constants `K_j` of the traces of the graph domains
`Ω_j` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.exists_enorm_graphTrace_sobolevToL2_le`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_enorm_boundaryTrace_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_cutoff_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_cutoff_interior
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_cutoff_.docstring:
**The cutoff of the inner patch**: for `δ > 0` there is a smooth `χ` with values in `[0, 1]`,
compact closed support in `Ω` and `χ = 1` near the compact set `{infDist(·, Ωᶜ) ≥ 2δ} ⊆ Ω`
(`Rd.exists_contDiff_eventuallyEq_one`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_cutoff_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_cutoff_boundary
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_cutoff_.docstring:
**The cutoff of a boundary patch**: for `ε > 0` and every `j` there is a smooth `χ` with values
in `[0, 1]`, compact closed support in the boundary ball `B(c_j, ρ_j)` and `χ = 1` near
`B̄(c_j, ρ_j - 2ε)` (`Rd.exists_contDiff_eventuallyEq_one`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundaryTrace_eq_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.docstring:
**A bounded extension from the boundary** (following Schneider–Vybíral, Theorem 4.11, for
`p ≥ 1`): for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < 1`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and `L ≥ 2`, there is `C < ∞` such that every
`g ∈ B^s_{p,q}(Γ)` is `Tr_Γ F` almost everywhere on `Γ` for some `F` with
`‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(k(s+1/p)) ω_L(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C ‖g‖_{B^s_{p,q}(Γ)}`. The function is
`F = ∑_j ζ_j E_j G_j` for the chart pieces `G_j` and the cut-offs `ζ_j`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_extensionSum_eventuallyEq`), with the triangle inequality
`Rd.modNorm_finsetSum_le` and the chart bounds
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.exists_modNorm_mulLp_graphExtension_le`; `C = ∑_j K_j`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundaryTrace_eq
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.docstring:
**Every function of `B^s_{p,q}(Γ)` is a boundary trace** (Schneider–Vybíral, Theorem 4.11, for
`p ≥ 1`, the extension): for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < 1`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and `L ≥ 2`, every
`g ∈ B^s_{p,q}(Γ)` is `Tr_Γ F` almost everywhere on `Γ` for some `F` with
`‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(k(s+1/p)) ω_L(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`. With the chart pieces `G_j` of `g`,
`F = ∑_j ζ_j E_j G_j` with the extensions `E_j` of the graph domains
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphExtension`) and the cut-offs `ζ_j`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartition.exists_cutoff`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_extensionSum_eventuallyEq`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundarySlobodeckijForm_mul_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.docstring:
**The Gagliardo form of one localised piece, by its chart piece**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `s > 0`,
a resolution of unity `ψ` and a chart `j` there is `C < ∞` such that for every measurable `g` and
every `G ∈ L_p(H_j)` with `G = (ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j` almost everywhere,
`[ψ_j g]_{W^{s,p}(Γ)}^p ≤ C (‖G‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_1(G, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_p})^p`, by
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundarySlobodeckijForm_le_of_support` and the bound of the Gagliardo
form on `H_j` (`Rd.slobodeckijForm_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundarySlobodeckijForm_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.docstring:
**The Gagliardo form by the chart-wise Besov norm** (the upper half of Gagliardo's description
of `B^s_{p,p}(Γ)`): for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `s > 0` and a resolution of unity `ψ` there is `C < ∞` with
`∫_Γ ∫_Γ |g(y) - g(x)|^p / |y - x|^(n-1+sp) dσ dσ ≤ C ‖g‖_{B^s_{p,p}(Γ)}^p` for every `g`. For
`g ∈ B^s_{p,p}(Γ)`, `g` is measurable on `Γ`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.aestronglyMeasurable_of_memBoundaryBesov`), `g = ∑_j ψ_j g` on `Γ`,
the form of the sum is at most `N^(p-1)` times the sum of the forms
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundarySlobodeckijForm_finsetSum_le`), and each piece is bounded by
its chart piece (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundarySlobodeckijForm_mul_le`); otherwise the
right side is `∞`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundaryPartition_nonneg
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.docstring:
**Nonnegative resolutions of unity on the boundary exist**: smooth `ψ_j ≥ 0` with
`tsupport ψ_j ⊆ B_j`, `∑_j ψ_j = 1` on `Γ` and `∑_j ψ_j ≤ 1` everywhere, a smooth resolution of
unity subordinate to the boundary balls (`Rd.exists_smooth_partition`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundaryPartition_nhds
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.docstring:
**Resolutions of unity equal to one near the boundary**: there is a resolution of unity `ψ`
on the boundary with `ψ_j ≥ 0`, `∑_j ψ_j ≤ 1` everywhere and `∑_j ψ_j = 1` on a neighbourhood of
`Γ` (`Rd.exists_smooth_partition_nhds` for the compact `Γ`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundaryBesovNorm_sobolevToL2_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.docstring:
**The boundary trace of `H^s(V)` is bounded into `B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)`**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: for
every resolution of unity `ψ` there is `C < ∞` with
`‖Tr_Γ ι_s U‖_{B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)} ≤ C ‖U‖` for every `U ∈ H^s(V)`: the trace bound
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundaryBesovNorm_boundaryTrace_le` at `p = q = L = 2` and
smoothness `s - 1/2`) and `H^s(V) ⊆ B^s_{2,2}(V)` with differences of order `2`
(`Rd.modNorm_sobolevToL2_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundaryBesovNorm_rpow_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.docstring:
**The chart-wise Besov norm by the Gagliardo form** (the lower half of Gagliardo's description
of `B^s_{p,p}(Γ)`): for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < 1` and a resolution of unity `ψ` there is `C < ∞`
with `‖g‖_{B^s_{p,p}(Γ)}^p ≤ C (‖g‖_{L_p(Γ)}^p + ∫_Γ ∫_Γ |g(y) - g(x)|^p / |y - x|^(n-1+sp) dσ dσ)`
for every `g` measurable on `Γ`. If `g ∈ L_p(Γ)`, every chart piece `G_j = (ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j` lies in
`L_p(H_j)` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_chartPiece_le`), its first-difference norm is
bounded by its Gagliardo form on `H_j` (`Rd.lqNorm_modulus_rpow_le_slobodeckijForm`), and that by
the form on `Γ` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_slobodeckijForm_chartPiece_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundaryBesovNorm_domainExtend_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.docstring:
**The trace of the trace space of `H^s(Ω)` is bounded into `B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)`**: for every
resolution of unity `ψ` there is `C < ∞` with `‖Tr_Γ ι_s(E_s t)‖_{B^{s-1/2}_{2,2}(Γ)} ≤ C ‖t‖`
for every `t ∈ Ω.TraceSpace s`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundaryBesovNorm_sobolevToL2_le`, `‖E_s t‖ = ‖t‖`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundaryBesovNorm_boundaryTrace_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundar.docstring:
**The boundary trace is bounded** (following Schneider–Vybíral, Theorem 4.11, for `p ≥ 1`): for
`1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < 1`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and `s + 1/p < L` (so `L ≥ 1`), there is `C < ∞` with
`‖Tr_Γ F‖_{B^s_{p,q}(Γ)} ≤ C (‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(k(s+1/p)) ω_L(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})` for every `F`
with a finite right side. The chart pieces of `Tr_Γ F` are the traces `Tr_j(ψ_j F)`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.graphTrace_mulLp_ae_boundaryTrace`), bounded chart by chart
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.exists_modNorm_graphTrace_mulLp_le`); `C = ∑_j K_j`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_besov_e.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_besov_extension_of_modulusOn
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_besov_e.docstring:
**The extension for bounded Lipschitz domains**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < r` and
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, if `‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`, then `f` agrees on
`Ω` with a function with a finite Besov quasi-norm by differences on `V`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_besov_extension_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_besov_e.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_besov_extension_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_besov_e.docstring:
**The extension for bounded Lipschitz domains with a bound** (Rychkov): for `1 ≤ p < ∞`,
`0 < s < r` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` there is `C < ∞` such that every `f` with
`N_Ω(f) = ‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞` agrees on
`Ω` with some `F` with `‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C N_Ω(f)`. The patches, the
bumps of the local extensions and the resolution of unity depend only on `Ω` and `r`, so `C`
is fixed before `f`: it is the pasting constant times the sum of the local constants
(`Rd.exists_pasting_le`, `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_local_extension_boundary_le`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_local_extension_interior_le`; for `V = {0}`, where `Ω = V`,
`C = 1`). Every step is linear in `f`, so for fixed `r` the construction is a bounded linear
operator, as in Rychkov; this theorem records its bound for each `f`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eventually_aeB.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eventually_aeBoundary_of_chart
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eventually_aeB.docstring:
**Chart statements hold almost everywhere on the boundary**: if `P(γ_k x')` holds for almost
every `x' ∈ H_k` with `γ_k(x') ∈ B_k`, then `P` holds almost everywhere on `Γ ∩ B_k`, by the change
of chart (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.ae_graphProj_graphMap`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eventually_aeB.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eventually_aeBoundary_iff
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eventually_aeB.docstring: The statements that hold almost everywhere on the boundary.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eventuallyEq_z.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eventuallyEq_zero_iff_forall_chart
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eventuallyEq_z.docstring:
**Vanishing on the boundary, chart by chart**: for every resolution of unity `ψ`, a function
`T` vanishes almost everywhere on `Γ` iff `(ψ_j T) ∘ γ_j = 0` almost everywhere on `H_j` for every
`j`. `⇐`: the localised statements hold almost everywhere on `Γ ∩ B_j`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eventually_aeBoundary_of_chart`), and `T = ∑_j ψ_j T` on `Γ`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eq_sum_localiz.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eq_sum_localizeL2_add_mulLp
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eq_sum_localiz.docstring:
**The decomposition in `L_2(V)` of a function vanishing outside `Ω`**: if
`χ + ∑_j ψ_j = 1` on `Ω` for a resolution of unity `ψ` and a continuous bounded real `χ`, then
`F = ∑_j ψ_j F + χ F` for every `F ∈ L_2(V)` vanishing almost everywhere outside `Ω`: on `Ω` the
factors add up to `1`, outside `Ω` both sides vanish.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eq_sum_add_of_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eq_sum_add_of_ae_eq_zero_of_nonneg
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eq_sum_add_of_.docstring:
**The decomposition of a function vanishing outside `Ω`**, for `s ≥ 0`: if `χ + ∑_j ψ_j = 1`
on `Ω`, `U ∈ H^s(V)` has `ι_s U = 0` almost everywhere outside `Ω`, `ι_s W_j = ψ_j ι_s U` and
`ι_s W_0 = χ ι_s U`, then `U = ∑_j W_j + W_0` in `H^s(V)`: the `L_2` functions agree
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eq_sum_localizeL2_add_mulLp`), and `ι_s` is injective
(`Rd.sobolevToL2_injective`). At `s = 1` this is
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eq_sum_add_of_ae_eq_zero`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.enorm_domainTr.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.enorm_domainTrace_restrictProj_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.enorm_domainTr.docstring:
The trace of the restriction to `Ω` has norm at most that of `U ∈ H^s(V)`, `1/2 < s < 3/2`:
`‖γ_s(U|_Ω)‖ ≤ ‖U|_Ω‖ ≤ ‖U‖` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.norm_domainTrace_apply_le`,
`Rd.norm_restrictProj_apply_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eLpNorm_mul_gr.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eLpNorm_mul_graph_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eLpNorm_mul_gr.docstring:
**The `L_p` norm of a cutoff on a graph domain**: if `χ` is continuous with closed support in
the boundary ball `B(c_j, ρ_j)` and `|χ| ≤ C`, then `‖χ f‖_{L_p(Ω_j)} ≤ C ‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)}` for every
`f` and every `0 ≤ p ≤ ∞` (`Rd.eLpNorm_mul_le_of_tsupport_subset`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eLpNorm_mul_ad.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eLpNorm_mul_add_fderiv_mul_graph_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eLpNorm_mul_ad.docstring:
**The `L_p` norm of a cutoff derivative on a graph domain**: for `1 ≤ p`, a smooth `χ` with
closed support in the boundary ball `B(c_j, ρ_j)`, `|χ| ≤ C` and `|∂_w χ| ≤ C'`,
`‖χ g + (∂_w χ) f‖_{L_p(Ω_j)} ≤ C ‖g‖_{L_p(Ω)} + C' ‖f‖_{L_p(Ω)}` for all `f`, `g`
(`Rd.eLpNorm_mul_add_fderiv_mul_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eLpNorm_chartP.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eLpNorm_chartPiece_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eLpNorm_chartP.docstring:
**The `L_p` norm of a chart piece, for every `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`**: for a strongly measurable `g`,
`‖(ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j‖_{L_p(H_j)} ≤ D_j ‖g‖_{L_p(Γ)}` with `D_j = ψ.derivBound j`; for `p < ∞` by
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_chartPiece_le`, for `p = ∞` since `σ`-null sets are null in
the charts (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_graphMap_of_ae_surfaceMeasure`) and `ψ_j = 0` outside
`B_j`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainTrace_eq.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainTrace_eq_zero_iff
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainTrace_eq.docstring:
`γ_s u = 0` iff `u` lies in the trace kernel (Mathlib's
`Submodule.orthogonalProjectionOnto_eq_zero_iff`, `Submodule.orthogonal_orthogonal`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainTrace_eq.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainTrace_eq_iff
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainTrace_eq.docstring:
**Equal traces are equal boundary traces**: for every resolution of unity `ψ`,
`γ_s u = γ_s u'` iff `Tr_Γ ι_s u = Tr_Γ ι_s u'` almost everywhere on `Γ`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_traceKer_iff` for `u - u'`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_sobolevToL2_sub`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainTrace_do.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainTrace_domainExtend
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainTrace_do.docstring: **The extension is a right inverse of the trace**: `γ_s (E_s t) = t`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainTrace.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainTrace
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainTrace.docstring:
**The trace** `γ_s : H^s(Ω) → Ω.TraceSpace s`, `1/2 < s < 3/2`, the orthogonal projection onto
the trace space. Two elements of `H^s(Ω)` have the same trace iff their boundary traces agree
almost everywhere on `Γ` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainTrace_eq_iff`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainExtend.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainExtend
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainExtend.docstring:
**The extension** `Ω.TraceSpace s → H^s(Ω)`, `1/2 < s < 3/2`, the inclusion of the trace space:
a right inverse of the trace (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.domainTrace_domainExtend`) and an isometry
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.norm_domainExtend_apply`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.completeSpace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.completeSpace_traceKer
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.completeSpace_.docstring:
The trace kernel is complete, as a closed subspace of the Hilbert space `H^s(Ω)`; hence it
has an orthogonal projection.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.coe_toOpens.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.coe_toOpens
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.coe_toOpens.docstring: The points of `Ω.toOpens` are the points of `Ω`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.closure_subset.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.closure_subset_iUnion_patch
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.closure_subset.docstring:
**The patches cover `Ω̄`** if the shrunk balls cover `Γ` and the points of `Ω` outside them
have distance `> 2δ` from `Ωᶜ` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_shrink`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_interior_margin`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chart_ae_eq_of.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chart_ae_eq_of_eventuallyEq
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chart_ae_eq_of.docstring:
**Chart pieces see `g` only almost everywhere on `Γ`**: if `g = h` almost everywhere on `Γ`,
then `(ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j = (ψ_j h) ∘ γ_j` almost everywhere on `H_j`, since `ψ_j ≠ 0` only in `B_j`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartTrace_ae_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartTrace_ae_eq
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartTrace_ae_.docstring:
**The chart trace is the localised boundary trace**:
`Tr_j(ψ_j ι_s u) = (ψ_j Tr_Γ ι_s u) ∘ γ_j` almost everywhere on `H_j`, with the canonical
resolution of unity
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.graphTrace_mulLp_ae_boundaryTrace`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartTraceLine.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartTraceLinear
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartTraceLine.docstring:
**The chart trace as a linear map**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: `u ↦ Tr_j(ψ_j ι_s u)` from `H^s(Ω)` to
`L_2(H_j)`, with the trace of the graph domain of the chart `j`, the canonical resolution of unity
and the `L_2` function `ι_s u` (`Rd.sobolevToL2`). It is additive by
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_sub` on the localised `H^s(V)` functions and homogeneous by
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_smul` and `Rd.mulLp_smul`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartTrace.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartTrace
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartTrace.docstring:
**The chart traces are bounded operators**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: `u ↦ Tr_j(ψ_j ι_s u)` from
`H^s(Ω)` to `L_2(H_j)`, with the canonical resolution of unity
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_enorm_graphTrace_localizeL2_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPiece_int.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPiece_integrand_le_of_notMem
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPiece_int.docstring:
**The integrand of a chart piece, with one point outside the chart ball**: if `ψ_j` vanishes
outside `B(c_j, r)`, `r ≤ r_j`, and `γ_j x' ∉ B_j`, then for the chart piece
`G = (ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j`, `|G(y') - G(x')|^P / |y' - x'|^a ≤ |G(y')|^P 1_{|x' - y'| ≥ η} |x' - y'|^(-a)`
with `η = (r_j - r) / (1 + M_j)`: `G(x') = 0`, and `G(y') ≠ 0` puts `γ_j y'` in `B(c_j, r)`, at
distance at least `r_j - r` from `γ_j x'`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPiece_int.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPiece_integrand_le_add
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPiece_int.docstring:
**The integrand of a chart piece, bounded by four parts**: if `ψ_j` vanishes outside
`B(c_j, r)` with `r ≤ r_j`, then for `P ≥ 1`, `a ≥ 0`, the chart piece `G = (ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j` and all
`x', y' ∈ H_j`, `|G(y') - G(x')|^P / |y' - x'|^a` is at most
`2^(P-1) (A(x', y') + B(x', y')) + |G(x')|^P k(y' - x') + |G(y')|^P k(x' - y')` with the kernel
`k(z) = 1_{|z| ≥ η} |z|^(-a)`, `η = (r_j - r) / (1 + M_j)`, the part
`A = D_j^P (1 + M_j)^a 1_{B_j²}(γ x', γ y') |g(γ y') - g(γ x')|^P / |γ y' - γ x'|^a` and the part
`B = 1_{B_j}(γ x') |g(γ x')|^P |ψ_j(γ y') - ψ_j(γ x')|^P / |y' - x'|^a`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPiece_integrand_le`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPiece_integrand_le_of_notMem`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPiece_int.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPiece_integrand_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPiece_int.docstring:
**The integrand of a chart piece, by the product rule for differences**: for `P ≥ 1`,
`a ≥ 0`, the chart piece `G = (ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j` and all `x', y' ∈ H_j`,
`|G(y') - G(x')|^P / |y' - x'|^a ≤ 2^(P-1) (D_j^P (1 + M_j)^a |g(γ y') - g(γ x')|^P /
|γ y' - γ x'|^a + |g(γ x')|^P |ψ_j(γ y') - ψ_j(γ x')|^P / |y' - x'|^a)`, from
`G(y') - G(x') = ψ_j(γ y') (g(γ y') - g(γ x')) + (ψ_j(γ y') - ψ_j(γ x')) g(γ x')` and
`|γ y' - γ x'| ≤ (1 + M_j) |y' - x'|`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPieceLp_a.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPieceLp_ae
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPieceLp_a.docstring: The chart piece in `L_p(H_j)` is `(ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j` almost everywhere on `H_j`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPieceLp.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPieceLp
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPieceLp.docstring:
**The chart piece as a bounded operator** `L_p(Γ) → L_p(H_j)`, `g ↦ (ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j`, for every
`1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, of norm at most `D_j = ψ.derivBound j`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eLpNorm_chartPiece_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPieceLine.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPieceLinear
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPieceLine.docstring:
**The chart piece as a linear map** `L_p(Γ) → L_p(H_j)`, `g ↦ (ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j`: additive and
homogeneous, since `σ`-almost everywhere identities hold almost everywhere in the chart where
`ψ_j ≠ 0` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chart_ae_eq_of_eventuallyEq`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartLipschitz.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartLipschitzConst_ne_top
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartLipschitz.docstring:
The constant `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartLipschitzConst` is finite for `0 < p < ∞` and
`0 < s < 1`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartLipschitz.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartLipschitzConst
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartLipschitz.docstring:
The constant `(D_j (1 + M_j))^p c_1 + (2 D_j)^p c_2` of the Lipschitz part of a chart piece,
with `c_1 = Rd.ballRpowConst H_j (n - 1 + sp - p)`, `c_2 = Rd.complBallRpowConst H_j (n - 1 + sp)`
and the derivative bound `D_j = ψ.derivBound j`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_sobolevToL2_sub
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.docstring:
**The boundary trace of `H^s(V)` functions is linear**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: for every resolution
of unity `ψ` and `U, W ∈ H^s(V)`, `Tr_Γ ι_s(U - W) = Tr_Γ ι_s U - Tr_Γ ι_s W` almost everywhere on
`Γ`, since `ι_s(U - W) + ι_s W = ι_s U` and the boundary trace is additive
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_add`, `Rd.modNorm_sobolevToL2_lt_top`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_sobolevToL2_smul
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.docstring:
`Tr_Γ ι_s (c U) = c Tr_Γ ι_s U` almost everywhere on `Γ`, for every resolution of unity and
`1/2 < s < 3/2`, since `ι_s (c U) = c ι_s U` and the boundary trace is homogeneous
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_smul`, `Rd.modNorm_sobolevToL2_lt_top`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_sobolevToL2_ofTest
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.docstring:
**Test functions have zero boundary trace**: on a bounded Lipschitz domain, for every
`s ≥ 0` and every test function `φ` of `Ω`, the boundary trace of `ι_s φ` vanishes almost
everywhere on `Γ`. For every `s ≥ 0`, `ι_s φ` is the continuous function `φ`
(`Rd.ofTest_eq_ofSchwartz`, `Rd.sobolevToL2_ofSchwartz`), the same `L_2` function as at the level
`1`, where its differences of order `2` have a finite quasi-norm with weight `1`
(`Rd.modNorm_sobolevToL2_lt_top`). So its boundary trace is its restriction to `Γ`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_eventuallyEq_of_continuous`), which vanishes: `φ` has
closed support in the open set `Ω`, and `Γ` does not meet `Ω`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_sobolevToL2_add
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.docstring:
`Tr_Γ ι_s (U + W) = Tr_Γ ι_s U + Tr_Γ ι_s W` almost everywhere on `Γ`, for every resolution of
unity and `1/2 < s < 3/2` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_sobolevToL2_sub`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_smul
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.docstring:
**The boundary trace is homogeneous**: under the hypotheses of
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_add`, `Tr_Γ(c F) = c Tr_Γ F` almost everywhere on `Γ`
for every `c ∈ ℂ` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_smul`, `Rd.modNorm_const_smul`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_restrictProj
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.docstring:
**The restriction to `Ω` keeps the boundary trace**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: for every resolution of
unity `ψ` and `U ∈ H^s(V)`, `Tr_Γ ι_s(U|_Ω) = Tr_Γ ι_s U` almost everywhere on `Γ`, since
`U - U|_Ω` vanishes on `Ω` (`Rd.sub_restrictProj_mem`, `Rd.mem_vanishOn_iff_sobolevToL2`) and the
boundary trace depends only on the function on `Ω`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_congr`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_graphMap
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.docstring:
**The boundary trace in a chart**: for `F` with a finite `B^{s+1/p}_{p,q}`-norm of order
`L > s + 1/p` on `V`, `Tr_Γ F(γ_j x') = Tr_j F(x')` for almost every `x' ∈ H_j` with
`γ_j(x') ∈ B_j`. If `ψ_k(γ_j x') ≠ 0`, then `γ_j x' ∈ B_k` lies on the graph of `Ω_k` and
`Tr_k F(P_k γ_j x') = Tr_j F(x')` by the change of chart; and `∑_k ψ_k = 1` on `Γ`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_extensionSum_eventuallyEq
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.docstring:
**The boundary trace of the sum of the localised extensions**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < 1`,
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `L ≥ 2`, smooth `ζ_j` with derivatives bounded up to order `L`, `ζ_j ≠ 0` only in
`B_j` and `ζ_j = 1` where `ψ_j ≠ 0`, and chart pieces `G_j ∈ B^s_{p,q}(H_j)` of `g`,
`G_j = (ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j` almost everywhere on `H_j`, the function `F = ∑_j ζ_j E_j G_j` has
`Tr_Γ F = g` almost everywhere on `Γ`. In the chart of `Ω_k`,
`Tr_k(ζ_j E_j G_j) = ζ_j ψ_j g = ψ_j g` by the change of chart
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_mulLp_ae`, `Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_graphTrace_comp`,
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_graphExtension`), and `∑_j ψ_j = 1` on `Γ`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_eventuallyEq_of_continuous
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.docstring:
**The boundary trace of continuous functions is the restriction**: if `F` has a continuous
representative `G`, then `Tr_Γ F = G` almost everywhere on `Γ`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_comp_graphMap`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_eventuallyEq
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.docstring:
**The boundary trace does not depend on the resolution of unity**: in every chart both are the
trace of the graph domain.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_domainExtend_eventuallyEq_iff
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.docstring:
**Elements of the trace space are determined by their boundary traces**: `Tr_Γ ι_s (E_s t)`
and `Tr_Γ ι_s (E_s t')` agree almost everywhere on `Γ` iff `t = t'`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_domainExtend_domainTrace
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.docstring:
**The extension of the trace has the same boundary trace**: `Tr_Γ ι_s (E_s γ_s u) = Tr_Γ ι_s u`
almost everywhere on `Γ`, for every resolution of unity.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_congr
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.docstring:
**The boundary trace depends only on `F` on `Ω`**: if `F₁ = F₂` almost everywhere on `Ω`, then
`Tr_Γ F₁ = Tr_Γ F₂` almost everywhere on `Γ`, since `Ω` agrees with `Ω_j` on `B_j`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_ae_eq_of_ae_eq`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_besovExtendLp
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.docstring:
**The extension from the boundary is a right inverse of the boundary trace**: for
`1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < t < 1`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and `g ∈ B^t_{p,q}(Γ)`, `Tr_Γ E_Γ g = g` almost everywhere
on `Γ` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_extensionSum_eventuallyEq`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_add
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_.docstring:
**The boundary trace is additive**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `s > 0`, `s + 1/p < L`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and
`F₁, F₂` with finite `‖F_i‖_p + ‖(2^(k(s+1/p)) ω_L(F_i, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q}`,
`Tr_Γ(F₁ + F₂) = Tr_Γ F₁ + Tr_Γ F₂` almost everywhere on `Γ`: in each chart the boundary traces
are traces of the graph domain (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_graphMap`), which are
linear (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_sub`). The order is `L ≥ 1`, since `0 < s + 1/p < L`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTraceL.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTraceL2_eq_ambientTraceL2
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTraceL.docstring:
**`γ^s_{L_2} u` is the trace of `u` read in `H^s(V)`**: `γ^s_{L_2} u = T^s_Γ u`, that is
`boundaryTraceL2 s u = ambientTraceL2 s u`, for every `u ∈ H^s(Ω)`; both are the boundary trace
`Tr_Γ ι_s u` almost everywhere on `Γ` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTraceL2_apply_ae`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2_apply_ae`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTraceL.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTraceL2_apply_ae
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTraceL.docstring:
**`γ^s_{L_2} u` is the boundary trace of `u`**: `γ^s_{L_2} u = Tr_Γ ι_s u` almost everywhere
on `Γ`, for every resolution of unity
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_domainExtend_domainTrace`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace.docstring:
**The boundary trace** `Tr_Γ F(y) = ∑_k ψ_k(y) Tr_k F(P_k y)`, with the traces `Tr_k` of the
graph domains `Ω_k` (cone bumps, differences of order `L`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundarySlobod.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundarySlobodeckijForm_le_of_support
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundarySlobod.docstring:
**The Gagliardo form of a function supported in a boundary ball**: let `f : V → ℂ` be
measurable and vanish outside `B(c_j, r)` with `r < r_j`, the radius of `B_j`. For `0 < p < ∞`
and `s ≥ 0`, `∫_Γ ∫_Γ |f(y) - f(x)|^p / |y - x|^(n-1+sp) dσ dσ` is at most
`(1 + M_j²) [f ∘ γ_j]_{W^{s,p}(H_j)}^p + 2 σ(Γ) (r_j - r)^(-(n-1+sp)) ∫_Γ |f|^p dσ`: the pairs in
`B_j²` go to the chart
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.lintegral_lintegral_indicator_le_slobodeckijForm`), the other pairs
are at distance at least `r_j - r` (`Rd.slobodeckijIntegrand_le_of_support`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundarySlobod.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundarySlobodeckijForm_finsetSum_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundarySlobod.docstring:
**The Gagliardo form of a finite sum**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞` and measurable `f_i`, the Gagliardo
form on `Γ` of `∑_{i ∈ t} f_i` is at most `(#t)^(p-1)` times the sum of the forms of the `f_i`, by
the triangle inequality and Hölder's inequality for finite sums (Mathlib's
`ENNReal.rpow_sum_le_const_mul_sum_rpow`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundarySlobod.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundarySlobodeckijForm_congr_ae
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundarySlobod.docstring:
The Gagliardo form on the boundary depends only on the class of `g` modulo null sets of the
surface measure.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundarySlobod.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundarySlobodeckijForm
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundarySlobod.docstring:
**The Gagliardo form on the boundary** `Γ` of a bounded Lipschitz domain in `V`, `dim V = n`:
`∫_Γ ∫_Γ |g(y) - g(x)|^p / |y - x|^(n - 1 + sp) dσ(y) dσ(x)` with the surface measure `σ`, for
`0 < p < ∞` the `p`-th power of the Gagliardo seminorm of the Sobolev–Slobodeckij space
`W^{s,p}(Γ)` of the `(n-1)`-dimensional surface `Γ` (Gagliardo 1957). For `p = 2`, `s = 1/2` the
exponent is `n`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryPartit.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryPartition_nonneg
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryPartit.docstring: The functions of the canonical resolution of unity are nonnegative.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryPartit.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryPartition
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryPartit.docstring:
**The canonical resolution of unity** on the boundary of `Ω`, a fixed choice among the
nonnegative resolutions of `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_boundaryPartition_nonneg`: `ψ_j ≥ 0`
and `∑_j ψ_j ≤ 1` everywhere. The trace kernel uses it and does not depend on it
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.mem_traceKer_iff`); the surface measure and the unit normal use its
nonnegativity.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryCutoff.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryCutoffBound_spec
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryCutoff.docstring: The derivatives of `ζ_j` of order at most `2` are bounded by `Ω.boundaryCutoffBound j`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryCutoff.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryCutoffBound
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryCutoff.docstring:
**A bound of the derivatives of `ζ_j`** up to order `2`, a choice among the bounds of
`Rd.exists_iteratedFDeriv_bound`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryCutoff.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryCutoff
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryCutoff.docstring:
**The cut-offs of the canonical resolution of unity**: smooth `ζ_j` with compact support,
`ζ_j ≠ 0` only in `B_j` and `ζ_j = 1` where `ψ_j ≠ 0`, for
`ψ = Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryPartition`; a choice among the cut-offs of
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartition.exists_cutoff`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovN.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovNorm_le_sum
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovN.docstring:
**The quasi-norm is at most the sum for chart pieces**: for `G_j = (ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j` almost
everywhere on `H_j`,
`‖g‖_{B^s_{p,q}(Γ)} ≤ ∑_j (‖G_j‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_1(G_j, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovN.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovNorm_eq_top_of_not_mem
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovN.docstring:
**The quasi-norm is infinite outside `B^s_{p,q}(Γ)`**: if `g ∉ B^s_{p,q}(Γ)`, then
`‖g‖_{B^s_{p,q}(Γ)} = ∞`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memBoundaryBesov_iff_boundaryBesovNorm_lt_top`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovN.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovNorm_eq_sum_chartPieceLp
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovN.docstring:
**The quasi-norm on the boundary by the chart pieces in `L_p`**: for `g ∈ L_p(Γ)`,
`‖g‖_{B^s_{p,q}(Γ)} = ∑_j (‖G_j‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_1(G_j, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})` for the chart pieces
`G_j` of `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPieceLp`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovNorm_eq_sum`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovN.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovNorm_eq_sum
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovN.docstring:
**The quasi-norm is the sum for chart pieces**: for `G_j = (ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j` almost everywhere on
`H_j`, `‖g‖_{B^s_{p,q}(Γ)} = ∑_j (‖G_j‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_1(G_j, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})`, since two
elements of `L_p(H_j)` that agree almost everywhere are equal.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovN.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovNorm_congr
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovN.docstring:
**The quasi-norm sees `g` only almost everywhere on `Γ`**: if `g = h` almost everywhere on
`Γ`, then `‖g‖_{B^s_{p,q}(Γ)} = ‖h‖_{B^s_{p,q}(Γ)}`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovN.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovNorm
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovN.docstring:
**The Besov quasi-norm on the boundary** (Schneider–Vybíral, Definition 3.3; Triebel 2002, with
Lebesgue measure on the hyperplanes): for a resolution of unity `ψ`,
`‖g‖_{B^s_{p,q}(Γ)} = ∑_j (‖G_j‖_{L_p(H_j)} + ‖(2^(ks) ω_1(G_j, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q})` for the
chart pieces `G_j ∈ L_p(H_j)` with `G_j = (ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j` almost everywhere on `H_j`. Each infimum
runs over at most one element of `L_p(H_j)`, the class of the chart piece, and is `∞` if the chart
piece is not in `L_p(H_j)` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryBesovNorm_eq_sum`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.besovExtendLp.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.besovExtendLp
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.besovExtendLp.docstring:
**The extension from the boundary** `E_Γ g = ∑_j ζ_j E_j G_j` for `g ∈ L_p(Γ)`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`,
with the chart pieces `G_j = (ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j` (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.chartPieceLp`) of the
canonical resolution of unity, the extensions `E_j` of the graph domains
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphExtension`, moment order `1`) and the cut-offs `ζ_j`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryCutoff`). The same operator serves every smoothness index.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceLi.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceLinear
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceLi.docstring:
**The trace of `H^s(V)` in `L_2(Γ)` as a linear map**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: `U ↦ Tr_Γ ι_s U`,
with the canonical resolution of unity.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2_sobolevInclusion
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2.docstring:
**The trace of `H^s(V)` in `L_2(Γ)` commutes with the inclusions**, `1/2 < t ≤ s < 3/2`:
`T^t_Γ(ι_{t,s} U) = T^s_Γ U` for every `U ∈ H^s(V)`, since `ι_t(ι_{t,s} U) = ι_s U`
(`Rd.sobolevToL2_sobolevInclusion`) and both traces are the boundary trace of this `L_2` function
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2_apply_ae`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2_one_apply_ae
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2.docstring:
The trace of `U ∈ H^1(V)` in `L_2(Γ)` is the boundary trace `Tr_Γ ι U` of its `L_2` function
`Rd.toL2 U`, the case `s = 1` of `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2_apply_ae`
(`Rd.sobolevToL2_one`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2_graphMap_ae
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2.docstring:
**The trace in `L_2(Γ)` in a chart**: for `U ∈ H^1(V)` and its trace
`T_Γ U = Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2 1 U`, `(T_Γ U)(γ_j x') = Tr_j U(x')` for
almost every `x' ∈ H_j` with `γ_j(x') ∈ B_j`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2_one_apply_ae`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_graphMap`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2_eq_zero_of_mem_traceKer
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2.docstring:
**Elements of the trace kernel have zero trace in `L_2(Γ)`**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: for
`u ∈ ker γ_s`, read in `H^s(V)`, `T^s_Γ u = 0`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTraceL2_eq_ambientTraceL2`,
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ker_boundaryTraceL2`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2_apply_ae
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2.docstring:
The trace of `U ∈ H^s(V)` in `L_2(Γ)` is the boundary trace `Tr_Γ ι_s U` almost everywhere on
`Γ`, for every resolution of unity (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_eventuallyEq`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ambientTraceL2.docstring:
**The trace `T^s_Γ` of `H^s(V)` on `Γ`**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`, as a bounded operator
`H^s(V) → L_2(Γ)`, `U ↦ Tr_Γ ι_s U`; `T_Γ = T^1_Γ`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_eLpNorm_boundaryTrace_sobolevToL2_le`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.aestronglyMeas.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.aestronglyMeasurable_of_memBoundaryBesov
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.aestronglyMeas.docstring:
**The functions of `B^s_{p,q}(Γ)` are measurable on `Γ`**: every `g ∈ B^s_{p,q}(Γ)` is
almost everywhere strongly measurable for the surface measure. On `B_j`, `ψ_j g` is
`σ`-almost everywhere the chart piece `G_j ∈ L_p(H_j)` composed with the projection `P_j`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_surfaceMeasure_ball_iff`), it vanishes outside `B_j`, and
`g = ∑_j ψ_j g` on `Γ`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_surfaceMeas.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_surfaceMeasure_iff_aeBoundary
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_surfaceMeas.docstring:
**The null sets of the surface measure are those of the charts**: a property holds
`σ`-almost everywhere iff it holds almost everywhere on the boundary in the sense of the charts
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.aeBoundary`), since the balls `B_j` cover `Γ`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_surfaceMeas.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_surfaceMeasure_ball_iff
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_surfaceMeas.docstring:
**Almost everywhere on a boundary ball, in the chart**: a property holds for `σ`-almost every
`y ∈ B_j` iff it holds at `γ_j(x')` for almost every `x' ∈ H_j` with `γ_j(x') ∈ B_j`. The image of
the measure with the density `√(1 + ‖∇φ_j‖²) ≥ 1` under `γ_j` is `μHE[n-1]` on the graph
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.map_graphMap_withDensity`), and this density has the null sets of the volume.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_mem_frontie.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_mem_frontier
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_mem_frontie.docstring: The surface measure is carried by the boundary: almost every point lies on `Γ`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_graphMap_of.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_graphMap_of_ae_surfaceMeasure
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_graphMap_of.docstring:
**`σ`-almost everywhere statements in a chart**: if `P` holds `σ`-almost everywhere, then
`P(γ_j x')` holds for almost every `x' ∈ H_j` with `γ_j(x') ∈ B_j`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_surfaceMeasure_ball_iff`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_eq_sum_mul.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_eq_sum_mul
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.ae_eq_sum_mul.docstring:
On `Γ`, `g = ∑_j ψ_j g` almost everywhere for the surface measure, since `∑_j ψ_j = 1` on `Γ`
and `σ` is carried by `Γ`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.aeBoundary.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.aeBoundary
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.aeBoundary.docstring:
**Almost everywhere on the boundary**: `∀ᶠ y in Ω.aeBoundary, P y` iff for every `j`,
`P(γ_j x')` holds for almost every `x' ∈ H_j` with `γ_j(x') ∈ B_j`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.eventually_aeBoundary_iff`). The exceptional sets are the null sets of
the surface measure on `Γ`, described in the charts.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.SobolevOne.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.SobolevOne
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.SobolevOne.docstring:
**The Sobolev space `H^1(Ω)`** of a bounded Lipschitz domain, as a Hilbert space: the
restriction space `Rd.RestrictionSpace 1 Ω` of the open set `Ω`. `Rd.restrictL2` identifies its
elements with the restrictions to `Ω` of the functions of `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.MemSobolevOn`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memSobolevOn_iff_exists_restrictL2`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.MemSobolevOn.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.MemSobolevOn
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.MemSobolevOn.docstring:
**The Sobolev space `H^1(Ω)`** of a bounded Lipschitz domain, as the space of restrictions:
`f ∈ L_2(V)` lies in `H^1(Ω)` if `f = F` almost everywhere on `Ω` for some `F ∈ W^1_2(V)`, which is
Mathlib's `H^1(V)` (`Rd.memSobolevW_one_iff`). Only the values of `f` on `Ω` matter
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.MemSobolevOn.congr_ae`). By this definition every such `f` lies in
the Sobolev space `W^1_2(Ω)` of weak derivatives on `Ω`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.MemSobolevOn.memWeakSobolev`); the converse is the extension theorem
of Calderón and Stein (Stein 1970, Chapter VI;
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.memSobolevOn_iff_memWeakSobolev`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.MemBoundaryBes.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.MemBoundaryBesov
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.MemBoundaryBes.docstring:
**Besov spaces on the boundary** (Schneider–Vybíral, Definition 3.3, with Lebesgue measure on
the hyperplanes): `g ∈ B^s_{p,q}(Γ)` if every chart piece `(ψ_j g) ∘ γ_j` agrees almost everywhere
on `H_j` with some `G_j ∈ L_p(H_j)` with `‖G_j‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_1(G_j, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`.
First differences suffice for `0 < s < 1`, the range of the trace theorem.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.IsBoundaryTrac.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.IsBoundaryTrace
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.IsBoundaryTrac.docstring:
`g` is **the boundary trace of `f`**: `Tr_Γ F = g` almost everywhere on `Γ` for every `F` with
`F = f` on `Ω` and `‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(kσ) ω_L(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`. For `f` with a finite
intrinsic norm on `Ω`, `0 < σ < L` and `1 ≤ q` such `F` exist
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.exists_besov_extension_of_modulusOn`), and they all have the same
boundary trace (`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.boundaryTrace_congr`). The predicate makes a statement
only when an admissible `F` exists; `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.HasBoundaryTrace` adds the finite
intrinsic norm.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartition.localizeL2
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.docstring: **Localisation to the chart `j`**: `F ↦ ψ_j F` on `L_2(V)` (`Rd.mulLp`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartition.intrinsicNorm_localizeL2_lt_top
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.docstring:
**Localisations of `H^s(V)` functions satisfy the trace hypothesis**, `1/2 < s < 3/2`: for
every resolution of unity `ψ` and `U ∈ H^s(V)` with `L_2` function `ι_s U`, the intrinsic norm of
`ψ_j ι_s U` of smoothness `(s - 1/2) + 1/2` on the graph domain of every chart `k` is finite
(`Rd.modNorm_mulLp_lt_top`, `Rd.modNorm_sobolevToL2_lt_top`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartition.hasCompactSupport
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.docstring:
The functions of a resolution of unity on the boundary have compact support: closed supports
inside the bounded balls `B_j`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartition.exists_toL2_eq_localizeL2
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.docstring:
**Localised `H^1(V)` functions**: for every resolution of unity `ψ`, every chart `j` and
`W ∈ H^1(V)` there is `W' ∈ H^1(V)` whose `L_2` function is `ψ_j ι W`
(`Rd.exists_toL2_eq_mulLp`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartition.exists_sobolevToL2_eq_localizeL2
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.docstring:
**Localised `H^s(V)` functions, `s ≥ 0`**: for every resolution of unity `ψ` of a bounded
Lipschitz domain, every chart `j` and `U ∈ H^s(V)` there is `W ∈ H^s(V)` with `ι_s W = ψ_j ι_s U`,
since `ψ_j` is smooth with closed support in the bounded ball `B_j`
(`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartition.hasCompactSupport`,
`Rd.exists_sobolevToL2_eq_mulLp`). At `s = 1` this is
`Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartition.exists_toL2_eq_localizeL2`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartition.exists_cutoff
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.docstring:
**Cut-offs for the resolution of unity**: smooth `ζ_j` with compact support, `ζ_j ≠ 0` only in
`B_j` and `ζ_j = 1` where `ψ_j ≠ 0`; a bump function equal to `1` on a ball around `tsupport ψ_j`
inside `B_j` (Mathlib's `exists_lt_subset_ball` and `ContDiffBump`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartition.enorm_toComplex_sub_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.docstring:
`ψ_j` is Lipschitz: `|ψ_j(x) - ψ_j(y)| ≤ D_j |x - y|` for the derivative bound
`D_j = ψ.derivBound j` (`Rd.norm_higherDiff_le_of_iteratedFDeriv` with differences of order
`1`).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartition.enorm_toComplex_le
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.docstring: `|ψ_j| ≤ D_j` for the derivative bound `D_j = ψ.derivBound j`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartition.derivBound_spec
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.docstring: The derivatives of `ψ_j` of order at most `2` are bounded by `ψ.derivBound j`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartition.derivBound
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.docstring:
**A bound of the derivatives of `ψ_j`** up to order `2`, a choice among the bounds of
`Rd.exists_iteratedFDeriv_bound` (smooth functions with compact support).

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartition
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryPartit.docstring:
A **resolution of unity on the boundary** subordinate to the boundary balls: smooth `ψ_j` with
`tsupport ψ_j ⊆ B_j` and `∑_j ψ_j = 1` on `Γ`.

Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryL2.name: Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryL2
Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.BoundaryL2.docstring:
**The space `L_2(Γ)`** of square integrable functions on the boundary with respect to the
surface measure.

Rd.BesovDomain.range_euclideanHalfSpace.name: Rd.BesovDomain.range_euclideanHalfSpace
Rd.BesovDomain.range_euclideanHalfSpace.docstring:
**The Euclidean half-space model is a Besov domain**: the range of the model with corners
`𝓡∂ n` is the closed half-space `{y : 0 ≤ ⟪y, e₀⟫}` (`Manifold.range_eq_closedHalfSpace`).

Rd.BesovDomain.of_hasBesovExtension.name: Rd.BesovDomain.of_hasBesovExtension
Rd.BesovDomain.of_hasBesovExtension.docstring:
**A closed convex set with nonempty interior and the extension property is a Besov
domain.**

Rd.BesovDomain.of_ae_eq.name: Rd.BesovDomain.of_ae_eq
Rd.BesovDomain.of_ae_eq.docstring:
**Besov domains up to null sets**: a closed convex set `Ω` with nonempty interior is a Besov
domain if it agrees up to a null set with a set `U` with the extension property
(`Rd.HasBesovExtension.congr_set`).

Rd.BesovDomain.modNormOn_order_le_of_bes.name: Rd.BesovDomain.modNormOn_order_le_of_besovDomain
Rd.BesovDomain.modNormOn_order_le_of_bes.docstring:
**The order of the differences on a Besov domain does not matter**: for `0 < s < r` and
`s < r'` there is `C < ∞` with `N_Ω(f; r') ≤ C N_Ω(f; r)` whenever `N_Ω(f; r) < ∞`, where
`N_Ω(f; r) = ‖1_Ω f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(f, 2^(-k), Ω)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q}`
(`Rd.HasBesovExtension.modNormOn_order_le_of_hasBesovExtension`).

Rd.BesovDomain.hasBesovExtension.name: Rd.BesovDomain.hasBesovExtension
Rd.BesovDomain.hasBesovExtension.docstring: **A Besov domain has the extension property.**

Rd.BesovDomain.closedHalfSpace.name: Rd.BesovDomain.closedHalfSpace
Rd.BesovDomain.closedHalfSpace.docstring:
**The closed half-space is a Besov domain**: it agrees up to a null set with the flat Lipschitz
graph domain (`Rd.closedHalfSpace_ae_eq`), which has the extension property
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasBesovExtension`).

Rd.BesovDomain.name: Rd.BesovDomain
Rd.BesovDomain.docstring:
A **Besov domain**: a closed convex set with nonempty interior with the extension property
(`Rd.HasBesovExtension`): every function of finite intrinsic Besov quasi-norm agrees with a
function on `V` whose Besov quasi-norm is bounded by a constant times the intrinsic one, for
`1 ≤ p < ∞`, `0 < s < r` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`. The extension is a field of the class, so the class is a
hypothesis; its instances are `univ`, the closed half-space, the models of manifolds with and
without boundary and the quadrant model of manifolds with corners (`Rd.BesovDomain.univ`,
`Rd.BesovDomain.closedHalfSpace`, `Rd.BesovDomain.range_euclideanHalfSpace`,
`Rd.BesovDomain.range_of_boundaryless`, `Rd.BesovDomain.range_euclideanQuadrant`) and the closed
unit cube (`Rd.BesovDomain.closedUnitCube`). The closure of a Lipschitz graph domain with convex
graph function, of a nonempty convex bounded Lipschitz domain and of a nonempty bounded open
convex set is a Besov domain (`Rd.BesovDomain.closure_lipschitzGraph`,
`Rd.BesovDomain.closure_boundedLipschitzDomain`, `Rd.BesovDomain.closure_of_convex`), and so is
every closed ball of positive radius (`Rd.BesovDomain.closedBall`).
The class consists of closed convex sets; every Lipschitz graph domain and every bounded Lipschitz
domain, convex or not, has the extension property (`Rd.HasBesovExtension`,
`Rd.LipschitzGraph.hasBesovExtension`, `Rd.BoundedLipschitzDomain.hasBesovExtension`).

Rd.ActsBounded.sub.name: Rd.ActsBounded.sub
Rd.ActsBounded.sub.docstring: Differences act with the sum of the bounds.

Rd.ActsBounded.smul.name: Rd.ActsBounded.smul
Rd.ActsBounded.smul.docstring: Scalar multiples act with the scaled bound.

Rd.ActsBounded.single.name: Rd.ActsBounded.single
Rd.ActsBounded.single.docstring: `c δ_v` acts with norm `|c|`: translations preserve `L_p` norms.

Rd.ActsBounded.prod.name: Rd.ActsBounded.prod
Rd.ActsBounded.prod.docstring: Finite products act with the product of the bounds.

Rd.ActsBounded.pow.name: Rd.ActsBounded.pow
Rd.ActsBounded.pow.docstring: Powers act with the power of the bound.

Rd.ActsBounded.neg.name: Rd.ActsBounded.neg
Rd.ActsBounded.neg.docstring: Negatives act with the same bound.

Rd.ActsBounded.mul.name: Rd.ActsBounded.mul
Rd.ActsBounded.mul.docstring: Products act with the product of the bounds.

Rd.ActsBounded.add.name: Rd.ActsBounded.add
Rd.ActsBounded.add.docstring: Sums act with the sum of the bounds.

Rd.ActsBounded.name: Rd.ActsBounded
Rd.ActsBounded.docstring:
An element `a` of the algebra of translations **acts boundedly on `L_p`** with constant `C`:
`a` keeps a.e. strong measurability and `‖a G‖_p ≤ C ‖G‖_p`.

Nat.le_add_of_dyadic_annulus.name: Nat.le_add_of_dyadic_annulus
Nat.le_add_of_dyadic_annulus.docstring:
**Dyadic scales of an annulus**: for `a > 0`, if `a ≤ t / 2^j` and `t / 2^i ≤ 2^N a`, then
`j ≤ i + N`, since `2^j a ≤ t ≤ 2^{i+N} a`.

Metric.subset_ball_three_mul_of_inter_no.name: Metric.subset_ball_three_mul_of_inter_nonempty
Metric.subset_ball_three_mul_of_inter_no.docstring:
If a set `Q ⊆ B̄(c, ρ)` meets the ball `B(x, r)` around a point `x ∉ B̄(c, 2ρ)`, then
`Q ⊆ B(x, 3r)`: a point of `Q` in the ball forces `r > ρ`, so every point of `Q` lies within
`r + 2ρ < 3r` of `x`.

MeasureTheory.wnorm_ne_top.name: MeasureTheory.wnorm_ne_top
MeasureTheory.wnorm_ne_top.docstring: For a finite exponent the weak `L_p` norm is the supremum of `t μ{‖f‖ > t}^{1/p}`.

MeasureTheory.wnorm'.name: MeasureTheory.wnorm'
MeasureTheory.wnorm'.docstring: The **weak `L_p` norm** for a real exponent: `sup_{t ≥ 0} t μ{‖f‖ > t}^{1/p}`.

MeasureTheory.wnorm.name: MeasureTheory.wnorm
MeasureTheory.wnorm.docstring:
The **weak `L_p` norm**: `sup_{t ≥ 0} t μ{‖f‖ > t}^{1/p}` for `p < ∞`, and the essential
supremum of `‖f‖` for `p = ∞`.

MeasureTheory.tsum_setLIntegral_le_mul_l.name: MeasureTheory.tsum_setLIntegral_le_mul_lintegral
MeasureTheory.tsum_setLIntegral_le_mul_l.docstring:
**The window inequality**: let `I_i`, `i ∈ ι`, be countably many measurable sets such that
every point lies in at most `M` of them (every finite set `S` of indices with `x ∈ I_i` for all
`i ∈ S` has at most `M` elements). Then `∑_i ∫_{I_i} F ≤ M ∫ F` for every a.e. measurable
`F : α → [0, ∞]`. Indeed `∑_i 1_{I_i}(x) F(x) ≤ M F(x)` at every point, and the sum and the
integral may be exchanged (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.lintegral_tsum`).

MeasureTheory.toReal_eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul.name: MeasureTheory.toReal_eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul
MeasureTheory.toReal_eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul.docstring:
The interpolation inequality in real numbers, for a bounded function on a finite measure
space: `‖f‖_r ≤ M^(1 - p/r) ‖f‖_p^(p/r)` for `0 < p ≤ r < ∞`.

MeasureTheory.tendsto_lintegral_lqNorm_i.name: MeasureTheory.tendsto_lintegral_lqNorm_ite_le_rpow
MeasureTheory.tendsto_lintegral_lqNorm_i.docstring:
**Dominated convergence for tails in `L_p(ℓ_q)`**: for `0 < p, q < ∞` and measurable
`g_j : α → [0, ∞]` with `‖x ↦ ‖(g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p < ∞`,
`∫ ‖(0, …, 0, g_N(x), g_{N+1}(x), …)‖_{ℓ_q}^p dμ(x) → 0` as `N → ∞`: the integrands are at most
`‖(g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}^p`, which is integrable and hence finite almost everywhere, and tend to zero
wherever it is finite (`ENNReal.tendsto_lqNorm_ite_le`; Mathlib's
`tendsto_lintegral_of_dominated_convergence'`).

MeasureTheory.tendsto_eLpNorm_lqNorm_ite.name: MeasureTheory.tendsto_eLpNorm_lqNorm_ite_le
MeasureTheory.tendsto_eLpNorm_lqNorm_ite.docstring:
**Tails in `L_p(ℓ_q)` tend to zero**: for `0 < p, q < ∞` and measurable `g_j : α → [0, ∞]`
with `‖x ↦ ‖(g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p < ∞`,
`‖x ↦ ‖(0, …, 0, g_N(x), g_{N+1}(x), …)‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p → 0` as `N → ∞`
(`MeasureTheory.tendsto_lintegral_lqNorm_ite_le_rpow`).

MeasureTheory.tendstoInMeasure_of_eLpNor.name: MeasureTheory.tendstoInMeasure_of_eLpNorm_sub_le
MeasureTheory.tendstoInMeasure_of_eLpNor.docstring:
**Near-best sequences converge in measure, `0 < p ≤ ∞`**: if `e_k → 0` along a filter and
`‖f - b_k‖_p ≤ e_k` eventually along it, then `b_k → f` in measure along it (Mathlib's
`tendstoInMeasure_of_tendsto_eLpNorm`, valid for every exponent `p ≠ 0`).

MeasureTheory.sum_rpow_lintegral_le_mul.name: MeasureTheory.sum_rpow_lintegral_le_mul
MeasureTheory.sum_rpow_lintegral_le_mul.docstring:
The **duality step** of Minkowski's integral inequality on a finite set `S`, for `r > 1`
with conjugate exponent `r'`: `∑_{i ∈ S} (∫ g_i)^r ≤ (∫ (∑_{i ∈ S} g_i^r)^(1/r)) ·
(∑_{i ∈ S} (∫ g_i)^r)^(1/r')`. Write `(∫ g_i)^r = ∫ g_i · (∫ g_i)^(r-1)`, exchange the finite
sum with the integral and apply Hölder's inequality at every point.

MeasureTheory.sum_mul_conj_normingFamily.name: MeasureTheory.sum_mul_conj_normingFamily
MeasureTheory.sum_mul_conj_normingFamily.docstring:
**The pairing of a family with its norming family**: if `u_j(x) = 0` for every `j` outside a
finite set `s`, then `∑_{j ∈ s} u_j(x) conj N_j(x) = ‖(u_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_2}^p` for every `p > 0`,
since `u_j conj u_j = |u_j|²` and `∑_{j ∈ s} |u_j(x)|² = ‖(u_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_2}²`.

MeasureTheory.setLIntegral_lqNorm_sub_se.name: MeasureTheory.setLIntegral_lqNorm_sub_setAverage_le
MeasureTheory.setLIntegral_lqNorm_sub_se.docstring:
**The mass of a family minus its means**: for `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, every set `s` of finite measure
and every countable family of functions `g_i` with values in a real normed space that are almost
everywhere strongly measurable on `s`,
`∫_s ‖(‖g_i - ⨍_s g_i‖)_i‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ 2 ∫_s ‖(‖g_i‖)_i‖_{ℓ_q}`, by Minkowski's inequality in `ℓ_q`
and `MeasureTheory.measure_mul_lqNorm_setAverage_le`.

MeasureTheory.setLIntegral_enorm_sub_set.name: MeasureTheory.setLIntegral_enorm_sub_setAverage_le
MeasureTheory.setLIntegral_enorm_sub_set.docstring:
**The mass of `f` minus its mean**: `∫_s ‖f - ⨍_s f‖ ≤ 2 ∫_s ‖f‖` for every set `s` of finite
measure and every function `f` with values in a real normed space, since
`‖f - ⨍_s f‖ ≤ ‖f‖ + ‖⨍_s f‖` and `μ(s) ‖⨍_s f‖ ≤ ∫_s ‖f‖`.

MeasureTheory.rpow_sum_rpow_lintegral_le.name: MeasureTheory.rpow_sum_rpow_lintegral_le
MeasureTheory.rpow_sum_rpow_lintegral_le.docstring:
**Minkowski's integral inequality on a finite set**: for `r > 1` and measurable
`g_i : α → [0, ∞]`, `(∑_{i ∈ S} (∫ g_i)^r)^(1/r) ≤ ∫ (∑_{i ∈ S} g_i^r)^(1/r)`. If the left side is
finite and nonzero, cancel the factor `(∑_{i ∈ S} (∫ g_i)^r)^(1/r')` in
`MeasureTheory.sum_rpow_lintegral_le_mul`; if it is infinite, some `∫ g_i` is infinite and so is
the right side.

MeasureTheory.normingFamily.name: MeasureTheory.normingFamily
MeasureTheory.normingFamily.docstring:
The **norming family** of a family `u = (u_j)_{j ∈ ℕ}` of functions `α → ℂ` for the real
exponent `p`: `N_j(x) = u_j(x) ‖(u_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_2}^{p-2}`. For `u` in `L_p(ℓ_2)` vanishing
outside a finite set it lies in `L_{p'}(ℓ_2)`, `p'` the conjugate exponent, and its pairing
with `u` is `∫ ‖(u_i)_i‖_{ℓ_2}^p`, so it realises the `L_p(ℓ_2)` norm by duality.

MeasureTheory.mul_distribution_le_wnorm_.name: MeasureTheory.mul_distribution_le_wnorm_one
MeasureTheory.mul_distribution_le_wnorm_.docstring:
**The weak `L_1` norm bounds every level**: `t μ{‖f‖ > t} ≤ ‖f‖_{1,∞}` for every
`t ∈ [0, ∞]`.

MeasureTheory.memLp_two_of_lintegral_eno.name: MeasureTheory.memLp_two_of_lintegral_enorm_sq_ne_top
MeasureTheory.memLp_two_of_lintegral_eno.docstring:
A function with `∫ ‖f‖² < ∞` that is almost everywhere strongly measurable lies in `L_2`
(Mathlib's `eLpNorm_lt_top_iff_lintegral_rpow_eNorm_lt_top`).

MeasureTheory.memLp_two_indicator_compl.name: MeasureTheory.memLp_two_indicator_compl
MeasureTheory.memLp_two_indicator_compl.docstring:
**The part below a level lies in `L_2`**: for almost everywhere strongly measurable `f` with
`‖f‖ = G` almost everywhere, where `G` is measurable with `∫ G^p < ∞` for some `0 ≤ p ≤ 2`,
`1_{G ≤ τ} f ∈ L_2` for every real `τ`, since `∫_{G ≤ τ} G² ≤ τ^(2-p) ∫ G^p`.

MeasureTheory.memLp_one_indicator_lt.name: MeasureTheory.memLp_one_indicator_lt
MeasureTheory.memLp_one_indicator_lt.docstring:
**The part above a level lies in `L_1`**: for almost everywhere strongly measurable `f` with
`‖f‖ = G` almost everywhere, where `G` is measurable with `∫ G^p < ∞` for some `p ≥ 1`,
`1_{G > τ} f ∈ L_1` for every `τ > 0`, since `∫_{G > τ} G ≤ τ^(1-p) ∫ G^p`.

MeasureTheory.memLp_of_lintegral_lqNorm_.name: MeasureTheory.memLp_of_lintegral_lqNorm_rpow_ne_top
MeasureTheory.memLp_of_lintegral_lqNorm_.docstring:
A member of a family lies in `L_p` if the pointwise `ℓ_2` norm of the family has finite
`p`-th power integral, `0 < p < ∞`, since `|g_j| ≤ ‖(g_i)_i‖_{ℓ_2}`; the member is assumed
almost everywhere strongly measurable.

MeasureTheory.memLp_normingFamily.name: MeasureTheory.memLp_normingFamily
MeasureTheory.memLp_normingFamily.docstring:
**The norming family lies in `L_q`**: let `1 < p < ∞` with conjugate exponent `q`, and let
`u_j ∈ L_p(μ)` for every `j` with `u_j = 0` for `j` outside a finite set `s`. Then every member
`N_j` of the norming family lies in `L_q(μ)`, since `|N_j| ≤ ‖(N_i)_i‖_{ℓ_2}`.

MeasureTheory.measure_mul_lqNorm_setAver.name: MeasureTheory.measure_mul_lqNorm_setAverage_le
MeasureTheory.measure_mul_lqNorm_setAver.docstring:
`μ(s) ‖(‖⨍_s g_i‖)_i‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ∫_s ‖(‖g_i‖)_i‖_{ℓ_q}` for `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, every set `s` of finite
measure and every countable family of functions `g_i` with values in a real normed space that
are almost everywhere strongly measurable on `s`, by `MeasureTheory.enorm_average_le` and
Minkowski's inequality for means (`MeasureTheory.lqNorm_laverage_le`).

MeasureTheory.measure_mul_enorm_setAvera.name: MeasureTheory.measure_mul_enorm_setAverage_le
MeasureTheory.measure_mul_enorm_setAvera.docstring:
`μ(s) ‖⨍_s f‖ ≤ ∫_s ‖f‖` for every set `s` of finite measure and every function `f` with
values in a real normed space, by `MeasureTheory.enorm_average_le` and Mathlib's
`measure_mul_setLAverage`.

MeasureTheory.measure_lt_mul_rpow_le_of_.name: MeasureTheory.measure_lt_mul_rpow_le_of_le_add
MeasureTheory.measure_lt_mul_rpow_le_of_.docstring:
**The level estimate**: let `τ > 0` and `F ≤ F₁ + F₂` almost everywhere, with `F₂` almost
everywhere measurable. If `ν{F₁ > τ/2} ≤ C₁ (τ/2)⁻¹ I₁` and `∫ F₂² dν ≤ C₂ I₂`, then
`ν{F > τ} τ^(p-1) ≤ 2 C₁ τ^(p-2) I₁ + 4 C₂ τ^(p-3) I₂` for every real `p`: `{F > τ}` lies in
`{F₁ > τ/2} ∪ {F₂ > τ/2}` almost everywhere (`MeasureTheory.distribution_add_le_of_enorm`), and
Chebyshev's inequality bounds the second set.

MeasureTheory.measure_lt_mul_enorm_le_wn.name: MeasureTheory.measure_lt_mul_enorm_le_wnorm_one
MeasureTheory.measure_lt_mul_enorm_le_wn.docstring:
**Level sets of a multiple from the weak `L_1` norm**: for `g : α' → ε`, `A ≥ 0` and
`0 < t < ∞`, `ν{A ‖g‖ > t} ≤ A t⁻¹ ‖g‖_{1,∞}`.

MeasureTheory.measure_lt_le_of_ae_le_add.name: MeasureTheory.measure_lt_le_of_ae_le_add
MeasureTheory.measure_lt_le_of_ae_le_add.docstring:
**The level sets of a split function**: let `u ≤ a + b` almost everywhere, with almost
everywhere measurable `a, b : α → [0, ∞]`, let `S` be measurable and `0 < t < ∞`. If
`∫ a² ≤ A t I`, `μ(S) ≤ D t⁻¹ I` and `∫_{Sᶜ} b ≤ K I`, then `μ {u > t} ≤ (4A + D + 2K) t⁻¹ I`.
This is the bookkeeping of the Calderón–Zygmund argument: `a` is the good part, controlled in
`L_2`, and `b` the bad part, controlled in `L_1` off the exceptional set `S`.

MeasureTheory.measure_lt_le_inv_rpow_mul.name: MeasureTheory.measure_lt_le_inv_rpow_mul_lintegral
MeasureTheory.measure_lt_le_inv_rpow_mul.docstring:
**Chebyshev's inequality with a power**: for an almost everywhere measurable
`F : α → [0, ∞]`, `r > 0` and `0 < t < ∞`, `μ {F > t} ≤ t^(-r) ∫ F^r`, from Mathlib's
`mul_meas_ge_le_lintegral₀` for `F^r`. This is the lintegral form of
`MeasureTheory.distribution_le_inv_rpow_mul_eLpNorm_rpow`. The bound holds for `t ∈ {0, ∞}` as
well (at `t = ∞` the level set is empty, at `t = 0` the right side is `∞` unless `F = 0` almost
everywhere); the callers use `0 < t < ∞`.

MeasureTheory.measure_half_lt_le_lintegr.name: MeasureTheory.measure_half_lt_le_lintegral_sq
MeasureTheory.measure_half_lt_le_lintegr.docstring:
**Chebyshev's inequality with squares at half height**: for an almost everywhere measurable
`a : α → [0, ∞]` and `0 < t < ∞`, `μ {a > t/2} ≤ 4 t⁻² ∫ a²`
(`MeasureTheory.measure_lt_le_inv_rpow_mul_lintegral` with `r = 2`).

MeasureTheory.measure_half_lt_le_add_set.name: MeasureTheory.measure_half_lt_le_add_setLIntegral_compl
MeasureTheory.measure_half_lt_le_add_set.docstring:
**Chebyshev's inequality off a set, at half height**: for an almost everywhere measurable
`b : α → [0, ∞]`, a measurable set `S` and `0 < t < ∞`,
`μ {b > t/2} ≤ μ(S) + 2 t⁻¹ ∫_{Sᶜ} b`.

MeasureTheory.measurable_lqNorm_comp.name: MeasureTheory.measurable_lqNorm_comp
MeasureTheory.measurable_lqNorm_comp.docstring:
The pointwise `ℓ_q` norm `x ↦ ‖(g_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_q}` of a countable family of measurable
functions is measurable, as in `MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_lqNorm_comp`.

MeasureTheory.measurable_indicator_secti.name: MeasureTheory.measurable_indicator_section
MeasureTheory.measurable_indicator_secti.docstring:
For a measurable set `S ⊆ ℝ × α` and measurable `F : α → [0, ∞]`, the function
`(τ, x) ↦ 1_{S_τ}(x) F(x)` with the sections `S_τ = {y : (τ, y) ∈ S}` is measurable.

MeasureTheory.measurableSet_ofReal_lt.name: MeasureTheory.measurableSet_ofReal_lt
MeasureTheory.measurableSet_ofReal_lt.docstring: The set `{(τ, y) : ofReal τ < F(y)}` is measurable for measurable `F : α → [0, ∞]`.

MeasureTheory.marcinkiewiczNormConst.name: MeasureTheory.marcinkiewiczNormConst
MeasureTheory.marcinkiewiczNormConst.docstring:
The constant of Marcinkiewicz interpolation in `L_p` norms, for an operator of weak type
`(1,1)` with constant `C₁`, of strong type `(2,2)` with constant `C₂` and subadditive with
constant `A`: `(marcinkiewiczConst p (A C₁) (A² C₂²))^(1/p)` for `1 < p < 2`, the range where it
is used.

MeasureTheory.marcinkiewiczConst_ne_top.name: MeasureTheory.marcinkiewiczConst_ne_top
MeasureTheory.marcinkiewiczConst_ne_top.docstring: `marcinkiewiczConst p C₁ C₂` is finite for `1 < p < 2` and finite `C₁`, `C₂`.

MeasureTheory.marcinkiewiczConst.name: MeasureTheory.marcinkiewiczConst
MeasureTheory.marcinkiewiczConst.docstring:
The constant of Marcinkiewicz interpolation between weak type `(1,1)` with constant `C₁`
and the bound `∫ (T f)² ≤ C₂ ∫ f²`, for the integrals of `p`-th powers:
`p (2 C₁/(p - 1) + 4 C₂/(2 - p))` for `1 < p < 2`, the range where it is used.

MeasureTheory.lqNorm_normingFamily.name: MeasureTheory.lqNorm_normingFamily
MeasureTheory.lqNorm_normingFamily.docstring:
**The size of the norming family**: for `p > 1` and every point `x` with
`‖(u_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_2} < ∞`, `‖(N_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_2} = ‖(u_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_2}^{p-1}`, since every member
is multiplied by `‖(u_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_2}^{p-2}`.

MeasureTheory.lqNorm_max_weighted_le.name: MeasureTheory.lqNorm_max_weighted_le
MeasureTheory.lqNorm_max_weighted_le.docstring:
**The lower half of the sandwich for weighted families**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`,
weights `w_j ∈ [0, ∞]` and measurable `u_j : α → E` with values in a normed group, indexed by a
countable set, `‖(w_j ‖u_j‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_{max(p,q)}} ≤ ‖ x ↦ ‖(w_j ‖u_j(x)‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p`.

MeasureTheory.lqNorm_max_le_eLpNorm_lqNo.name: MeasureTheory.lqNorm_max_le_eLpNorm_lqNorm
MeasureTheory.lqNorm_max_le_eLpNorm_lqNo.docstring:
**The lower half of the sandwich**:
`‖(‖g_i‖_p)_i‖_{ℓ_{max(p,q)}} ≤ ‖ x ↦ ‖(g_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p` for `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`.
For `p ≤ q` the inequality `ℓ_q(L_p) ≤ L_p(ℓ_q)`; for `q ≤ p` the identity
`ℓ_p(L_p) = L_p(ℓ_p)` and the pointwise bound `‖·‖_{ℓ_p} ≤ ‖·‖_{ℓ_q}`.

MeasureTheory.lqNorm_max_dyadicWeight_le.name: MeasureTheory.lqNorm_max_dyadicWeight_le
MeasureTheory.lqNorm_max_dyadicWeight_le.docstring:
**The lower half of the sandwich for dyadic weights**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`,
`s ∈ ℝ` and measurable `u_j : α → E`,
`‖(2^(js) ‖u_j‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_{max(p,q)}} ≤ ‖ x ↦ ‖(2^(js) ‖u_j(x)‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p`.

MeasureTheory.lqNorm_lintegral_le.name: MeasureTheory.lqNorm_lintegral_le
MeasureTheory.lqNorm_lintegral_le.docstring:
**Minkowski's integral inequality for `ℓ_u`-valued functions**, `1 ≤ u ≤ ∞`: for measurable
`g_i : α → [0, ∞]` indexed by a countable set, `‖(∫ g_i)_i‖_{ℓ_u} ≤ ∫ ‖(g_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_u} dx`. For
`u = 1` both sides are equal (Tonelli), for `u = ∞` the supremum of integrals is at most the
integral of the supremum, and for `1 < u < ∞` the finite sums are bounded by
`MeasureTheory.rpow_sum_rpow_lintegral_le`.

MeasureTheory.lqNorm_le_mul_eLpNorm_of_o.name: MeasureTheory.lqNorm_le_mul_eLpNorm_of_overlap
MeasureTheory.lqNorm_le_mul_eLpNorm_of_o.docstring:
**Summing local bounds over sets of bounded overlap**: let `W_i`, `i ∈ κ`, be countably many
measurable sets such that every point lies in at most `M` of them, let `0 < p < ∞`, let `f` be
a.e. strongly measurable, and let `w : κ → [0, ∞]` satisfy `w_i ≤ ‖1_{W_i} f‖_p B` for every `i`.
Then `‖w‖_{ℓ_p} ≤ M^(1/p) B ‖f‖_p`: the `p`-th powers satisfy
`∑_i w_i^p ≤ B^p ∑_i ∫_{W_i} |f|^p ≤ M B^p ‖f‖_p^p` by the window inequality
(`MeasureTheory.tsum_setLIntegral_le_mul_lintegral`).

MeasureTheory.lqNorm_laverage_le.name: MeasureTheory.lqNorm_laverage_le
MeasureTheory.lqNorm_laverage_le.docstring:
**Minkowski's integral inequality for means**: for `1 ≤ u ≤ ∞` and almost everywhere
measurable `g_i : α → [0, ∞]` indexed by a countable set,
`‖(⨍ g_i dμ)_i‖_{ℓ_u} ≤ ⨍ ‖(g_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_u} dμ(x)`. The mean is the integral for the normalised
measure `μ(α)⁻¹ μ`, so this is `MeasureTheory.lqNorm_lintegral_le`.

MeasureTheory.lqNorm_enorm_ne_top_of_fin.name: MeasureTheory.lqNorm_enorm_ne_top_of_finite
MeasureTheory.lqNorm_enorm_ne_top_of_fin.docstring:
A family of complex functions that vanishes outside a finite set `s` has finite pointwise
`ℓ_2` norm: `‖(u_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_2} ≤ ∑_{j ∈ s} |u_j(x)| < ∞` (`ENNReal.lqNorm_le_sum_of_eq_zero`).

MeasureTheory.lqNorm_eLpNorm_sub_le_of_n.name: MeasureTheory.lqNorm_eLpNorm_sub_le_of_nearBest
MeasureTheory.lqNorm_eLpNorm_sub_le_of_n.docstring:
**Near-best sequences in weighted `ℓ_q`, `0 < p, r ≤ ∞`**: let `ρ_p = min(1, p)`,
`ρ_r = min(1, r)`, and let `b_k` be almost everywhere strongly measurable functions with
`‖f - b_k‖_p ≤ e_k`, where `e` decreases to `0`, and blocks with
`‖b_{k+1} - b_k‖_r ≤ C 2^(kβ) ‖b_{k+1} - b_k‖_p`. Then for every `s ∈ ℝ` and every `q`,
`‖(2^(k(s-β)) ‖f - b_k‖_r)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C 2^(1/ρ_p) H^(1/ρ_r) ‖(2^(ks) e_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q}` with Hardy's
constant `H = hardyConst ((s - β) ρ_r) (q/ρ_r)`, finite for `s > β`. The transfer of near-best
sequences (`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_tsum_of_nearBest`) bounds
`‖f - b_k‖_r^(ρ_r)` by a tail of `(2^(jβ) e_j)^(ρ_r)`, the tail inequality in `ρ_r`-th powers
(`ENNReal.lqNorm_rpow_le_of_rpow_le_tsum`) turns this into a bound of the `ρ_r`-th power of the
left side, and `2^(k(s-β)) 2^(kβ) = 2^(ks)`.

MeasureTheory.lqNorm_eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_.name: MeasureTheory.lqNorm_eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_lqNorm
MeasureTheory.lqNorm_eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_.docstring:
**`ℓ_q(L_p) ≤ L_p(ℓ_q)` for `0 < p ≤ q ≤ ∞`**:
`‖(‖g_i‖_p)_i‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ‖ x ↦ ‖(g_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p`. For `q = ∞` every `g_i` is at most the
pointwise supremum. For `q < ∞`, with `U = q/p ≥ 1`, the `p`-th power of the left side is
`‖(∫ g_i^p)_i‖_{ℓ_U}`, and Minkowski's integral inequality for `ℓ_U`-valued functions
(`MeasureTheory.lqNorm_lintegral_le`) bounds it by `∫ ‖(g_i^p)_i‖_{ℓ_U}`, the `p`-th power of the
right side.

MeasureTheory.locallyIntegrable_of_foral.name: MeasureTheory.locallyIntegrable_of_forall_integrableOn_ball
MeasureTheory.locallyIntegrable_of_foral.docstring:
**Local integrability from the balls**: a function integrable on every ball `B(x₀, R)` around
a fixed point `x₀` is locally integrable, since every point has the neighbourhood
`B(x₀, d(x, x₀) + 1)`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_sq_le_mul_linteg.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_sq_le_mul_lintegral_of_ae_le
MeasureTheory.lintegral_sq_le_mul_linteg.docstring:
If `u ≤ c` almost everywhere, then `∫ u² ≤ c ∫ u`, for every almost everywhere measurable
`u : α → [0, ∞]`: the case `r = 2` of
`MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_mul_lintegral_of_ae_le`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_lintegral_m.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_lintegral_mul_le
MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_lintegral_m.docstring:
**The integral form of Young's inequality** for nonnegative functions: for `1 ≤ q`,
`∫ (∫ a(y) b(x - y) dy)^q dx ≤ (∫ a)^q ∫ b^q`. This is the kernel form
`MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_lintegral_kernel_le` for `K(x, y) = b(x - y)`, since
`∫ b(x - y)^q dx = ∫ b^q` by the invariance of `μ`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_lintegral_l.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_lintegral_le
MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_lintegral_l.docstring:
**The integral form of Young's inequality**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`,
`∫ (∫ |K(y)| |f(x - y)| dy)^p dx ≤ (‖K‖_1 ‖f‖_p)^p`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_lintegral_k.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_lintegral_kernel_le
MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_lintegral_k.docstring:
**Young's inequality for kernels**, for nonnegative functions: for `1 ≤ q`, s-finite measures
`μ` on `X` and `ν` on `Y`, an almost everywhere measurable `a : Y → [0, ∞]` and a jointly almost
everywhere measurable `K : X × Y → [0, ∞]` with `∫ K(x, y)^q dμ(x) ≤ C` for every `y`,
`∫ (∫ a(y) K(x, y) dν(y))^q dμ(x) ≤ (∫ a dν)^q C`. By the weighted Jensen inequality the inner
power is at most `(∫ a)^(q-1) ∫ a(y) K(x, y)^q dν(y)`, and Tonelli's theorem gives
`(∫ a)^(q-1) ∫ a(y) C dν(y)`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_of_weak_.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_of_weak_one_strong_two
MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_of_weak_.docstring:
**Marcinkiewicz interpolation for operators on an abstract input type**: let `μ` be
s-finite and `1 < p < 2`. Every input `x : X` has a measurable size `G x : α → [0, ∞]` and an
almost everywhere measurable output `T x : α' → [0, ∞]`, and `res x S` restricts `x` to a
measurable set `S`, with size `1_S G x`. Suppose that `T x ≤ T (res x S) + T (res x Sᶜ)` almost
everywhere when `∫ (G x)^p < ∞`, that `ν{T x > t} ≤ C₁ t⁻¹ ∫ G x` for `0 < t < ∞` when
`∫ G x < ∞` (weak type `(1,1)`), and that `∫ (T x)² ≤ C₂ ∫ (G x)²` when `∫ (G x)² < ∞`
(strong type `(2,2)`). Then `∫ (T x)^p ≤ marcinkiewiczConst p C₁ C₂ ∫ (G x)^p` for every `x`
with `∫ (G x)^p < ∞`. At the level `τ` the input is split along `{G x > τ}`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_of_measu.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_of_measure_lt_mul_rpow_le
MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_of_measu.docstring:
**Integrals of powers from bounds at every level**: let `μ` be s-finite, `F : α' → [0, ∞]`
almost everywhere measurable, `G : α → [0, ∞]` measurable, `1 < p < r` and `K₁, K₂ ∈ [0, ∞]`. If
for every `τ > 0`
`ν{F > τ} τ^(p-1) ≤ K₁ τ^(p-2) ∫_{G > τ} G dμ + K₂ τ^(p-1-r) ∫_{G ≤ τ} G^r dμ`, then
`∫ F^p dν ≤ p (K₁/(p - 1) + K₂/(r - p)) ∫ G^p dμ`: the layer cake formula and the two Tonelli
steps.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_of_foral.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_of_forall_le_add
MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_of_foral.docstring:
**The layer cake argument of Marcinkiewicz interpolation**: let `μ` be s-finite,
`F : α' → [0, ∞]` almost everywhere measurable, `G : α → [0, ∞]` measurable and `1 < p < 2`.
Suppose that for every `τ > 0` there are `F₁ τ`, `F₂ τ` with `F ≤ F₁ τ + F₂ τ` almost
everywhere, `F₂ τ` almost everywhere measurable,
`ν{F₁ τ > τ/2} ≤ C₁ (τ/2)⁻¹ ∫_{G > τ} G dμ` and `∫ (F₂ τ)² dν ≤ C₂ ∫_{G ≤ τ} G² dμ`. Then
`∫ F^p dν ≤ marcinkiewiczConst p C₁ C₂ ∫ G^p dμ`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_mul_lint.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_mul_lintegral_of_ae_le
MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_mul_lint.docstring:
**Powers of a bounded function**: if `u ≤ c` almost everywhere, then
`∫ u^r ≤ c^(r-1) ∫ u` for every `r ≥ 1` and every almost everywhere measurable `u : α → [0, ∞]`,
since `u^r = u · u^(r-1) ≤ u · c^(r-1)`.
