MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegra.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul_ennreal
MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegra.docstring:
The **layer cake formula** for `[0, ∞]`-valued functions:
`∫ F^p dν = p ∫_0^∞ ν{F > t} t^(p-1) dt` for every measure `ν`, every almost everywhere
measurable `F : α → [0, ∞]` and `p > 0`. The truncations `min(F, N)` reduce it to Mathlib's
real-valued `lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul`, and both sides pass to the limit
`N → ∞` by monotone convergence.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_rpow_le.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_rpow_le
MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_rpow_le.docstring:
**Weighted Jensen inequality**: for `1 ≤ p` and nonnegative `a`, `g`,
`(∫ a g)^p ≤ (∫ a)^(p-1) ∫ a g^p`. This is Hölder's inequality for the measure `a dμ`: split
`a g = a^(1/q) (a^(1/p) g)` with the conjugate exponent `q` (Mathlib's
`ENNReal.lintegral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq`).

MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_le_eLpNorm_m.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_le_eLpNorm_mul_eLpNorm
MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_le_eLpNorm_m.docstring:
**Hölder's inequality for functions with values in `[0, ∞]`, in `L_p` norms**: for
conjugate exponents `1 < p, q < ∞` and almost everywhere measurable `F, G`,
`∫ F G ≤ ‖F‖_p ‖G‖_q`. This is Mathlib's `ENNReal.lintegral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq`, which writes the
right side with the integrals `(∫ F^p)^(1/p) (∫ G^q)^(1/q)` and real exponents.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_enorm_sq_le_.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_enorm_sq_le_of_hasStrongType
MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_enorm_sq_le_.docstring:
**Squares of a multiple from the strong type `(2,2)`**: if `T` has strong type `(2,2)` with
constant `C₂`, then `∫ (A ‖T g‖)² dν ≤ A² C₂² ∫ ‖g‖² dμ` for every `g ∈ L_2(μ)` and `A ≥ 0`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_min_natCast_rpow.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_min_natCast_rpow_eq
MeasureTheory.lintegral_min_natCast_rpow.docstring:
The **layer cake formula for the truncation** `min F N`:
`∫ min(F, N)^p dν = p ∫_0^N ν{F > t} t^(p-1) dt`, from Mathlib's real-valued
`lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_lqNorm_rpow_ne_t.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_lqNorm_rpow_ne_top_of_finite
MeasureTheory.lintegral_lqNorm_rpow_ne_t.docstring:
A family in `L_p`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, that vanishes outside a finite set `s` has
`∫ ‖(u_j)_j‖_{ℓ_2}^p dμ < ∞` (`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_ne_top_of_finite`).

MeasureTheory.lintegral_le_of_le_on_piec.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_le_of_le_on_pieces
MeasureTheory.lintegral_le_of_le_on_piec.docstring:
**Integral of a function bounded on pieces**: if almost every point lies in one of the
disjoint measurable sets `S n`, each of measure `c`, and `G ≤ a n` on `S n`, then
`∫ G dμ ≤ c ∑_n a n`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_lt_ne_.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_lt_ne_top
MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_lt_ne_.docstring:
**The part above a level has finite integral**: if `∫ F^p < ∞` for some `p ≥ 1`, then
`∫_{F > s} F < ∞` for every `0 < s < ∞` (`MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_lt_le`).

MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_lt_le.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_lt_le
MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_lt_le.docstring:
**The part above a level**: `∫_{F > s} F ≤ s^(1-p) ∫ F^p` for `p ≥ 1`, `0 < s < ∞` and every
`F : α → [0, ∞]`, since `s^(p-1) F ≤ F^p` where `F > s`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_compl_.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_compl_rpow_ne_top
MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_compl_.docstring:
**The part below a level has finite integral**: if `∫ F^p < ∞` for some `0 ≤ p ≤ r` with
`0 < r`, then `∫_{F ≤ s} F^r < ∞` for every `s < ∞`
(`MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_compl_rpow_le`).

MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_compl_.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_compl_rpow_le
MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_compl_.docstring:
**The part below a level**: `∫_{F ≤ s} F^r ≤ s^(r-p) ∫ F^p` for `0 ≤ p ≤ r`, `0 < r`,
`s < ∞` and every `F : α → [0, ∞]`, since `F^r = F^p F^(r-p) ≤ F^p s^(r-p)` where `F ≤ s`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_enorm_sq_eq_eLpN.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_enorm_sq_eq_eLpNorm_sq
MeasureTheory.lintegral_enorm_sq_eq_eLpN.docstring:
`L_2` norms through integrals of squares: `∫ ‖g‖² = ‖g‖_2²` for every almost everywhere
strongly measurable `g` with values in a space with an extended norm. This is Mathlib's
`eLpNorm_nnreal_pow_eq_lintegral` for `p = 2`, with natural-number powers in place of real
powers.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_enorm_rpow_le_of.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_enorm_rpow_le_of_hasWeakType_of_hasStrongType
MeasureTheory.lintegral_enorm_rpow_le_of.docstring:
**Marcinkiewicz interpolation in integral form, in the terms of the Carleson project**: let
`μ` be s-finite, `1 < p < 2`, and let `T` be almost everywhere subadditive with constant `A` on
`L_1(μ) ∪ L_2(μ)`, of weak type `(1,1)` with constant `C₁` and of strong type `(2,2)` with
constant `C₂`. Then `∫ ‖T f‖^p dν ≤ marcinkiewiczConst p (A C₁) (A² C₂²) ∫ ‖f‖^p dμ` for every
almost everywhere strongly measurable `f` with `∫ ‖f‖^p < ∞` and almost everywhere strongly
measurable `T f`. At the level `τ`, `f` splits into `1_{‖f‖ > τ} f ∈ L_1` and
`1_{‖f‖ ≤ τ} f ∈ L_2`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_enorm_indicator_.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_enorm_indicator_rpow_eq
MeasureTheory.lintegral_enorm_indicator_.docstring:
Integrals of powers of a restricted function: if `‖f‖ = G` almost everywhere, then
`∫ ‖1_S f‖^r = ∫ (1_S G)^r` for every set `S` and every real `r`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_rpow_eq_top.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_rpow_eq_top
MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_rpow_eq_top.docstring:
`∫_{(0,∞)} t^r dt = ∞` for every exponent `r`, since `t^r` is not integrable on `(0, ∞)`
(Mathlib's `not_integrableOn_Ioi_rpow`).

MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_lintegral_in.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_lintegral_indicator_lt_mul_rpow
MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_lintegral_in.docstring:
**The first Tonelli step**: for every s-finite measure `μ`, measurable `F : α → [0, ∞]` and
`p > 1`, `∫_0^∞ (∫_{F > τ} F dμ) τ^(p-2) dτ = (p - 1)⁻¹ ∫ F^p dμ`, since
`∫_0^F τ^(p-2) dτ = F^(p-1)/(p-1)`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_lintegral_in.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_lintegral_indicator_compl_mul_rpow_le
MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_lintegral_in.docstring:
**The second Tonelli step**: for every s-finite measure `μ`, measurable `F : α → [0, ∞]`,
`0 < r` and `p < r`, `∫_0^∞ (∫_{F ≤ τ} F^r dμ) τ^(p-1-r) dτ ≤ (r - p)⁻¹ ∫ F^p dμ`, since
`∫_F^∞ τ^(p-1-r) dτ = F^(p-r)/(r-p)` and `F^r F^(p-r) ≤ F^p`.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_indicator_ha.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_indicator_half_lt_mul_rpow
MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_indicator_ha.docstring:
**A power integral below half a level**: for `a, b ∈ [0, ∞]` and `p > 1`,
`∫_0^∞ 1_{t/2 < a} a b t^(p-2) dt = 2^(p-1)/(p-1) a^p b`, by
`MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_rpow_indicator_lt` at the level `2a`. It is the integral in `t` of
the Tonelli step of the weighted strong type of the maximal function.

MeasureTheory.le_rpow_mul_eLpNorm_of_ae_.name: MeasureTheory.le_rpow_mul_eLpNorm_of_ae_enorm_le
MeasureTheory.le_rpow_mul_eLpNorm_of_ae_.docstring:
**A bound of the supremum by one `L_{p₀}` quasi-norm gives it by every smaller one**
(Ditzian–Prymak 2016, Theorem 2.1, (2.2)): let `N < ∞` bound `|f|` almost everywhere, for example
the essential supremum of `f` or the supremum norm of a bounded continuous `f`. If
`N ≤ M ‖f‖_{p₀}` with `p₀ < ∞`, then `N ≤ M^(p₀/p) ‖f‖_p` for every `0 < p ≤ p₀`. By
interpolation, `‖f‖_{p₀} ≤ N^(1-θ) ‖f‖_p^θ` with `θ = p/p₀`
(`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_eLpNorm_rpow`); cancelling `N^(1-θ)` leaves
`N^θ ≤ M ‖f‖_p^θ`, and the `1/θ`-th power gives the claim. A function that is not almost
everywhere strongly measurable has `‖f‖_q = ∞` for every `q`, so the claim holds for it too.

MeasureTheory.le_lintegral_of_le_on_piec.name: MeasureTheory.le_lintegral_of_le_on_pieces
MeasureTheory.le_lintegral_of_le_on_piec.docstring:
**Integral of a function bounded below on pieces**: if the measurable sets `S n` are
disjoint, each of measure `c`, and `a n ≤ G` on `S n`, then `c ∑_n a n ≤ ∫ G dμ`.

MeasureTheory.le_eLpNorm_of_le_on_pieces.name: MeasureTheory.le_eLpNorm_of_le_on_pieces
MeasureTheory.le_eLpNorm_of_le_on_pieces.docstring:
**`L_q` norm of a function bounded below on pieces**: if the measurable sets `S n` are
disjoint, each of measure `c ≠ 0`, and `a n ≤ G` on `S n`, then
`c^(1/q) ‖a‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ‖G‖_{L_q(μ)}` for every `q` (with `c^(1/q) = 1` for `q = ∞`).

MeasureTheory.inhmgELpNorm_eq_eLpNorm_rp.name: MeasureTheory.inhmgELpNorm_eq_eLpNorm_rpow_min
MeasureTheory.inhmgELpNorm_eq_eLpNorm_rp.docstring:
**Mathlib's inhomogeneous `L_p` quasi-norm is the `ρ`-th power of the `L_p` quasi-norm**:
`inhmgELpNorm f p μ = ‖f‖_p^ρ` with `ρ = min(1, p)`, for every `p ≠ 0` and every function with
values in an additive monoid with an extended seminorm. For `p ≤ 1` this is Mathlib's
`inhmgELpNorm_eq_eLpNorm_pow`, for `p ≥ 1` Mathlib's `inhmgELpNorm_eq_eLpNorm`; at `p = 0`
Mathlib's value is the measure of the support of an almost everywhere strongly measurable `f`.

MeasureTheory.hasStrongType_of_hasWeakTy.name: MeasureTheory.hasStrongType_of_hasWeakType_one_of_hasStrongType_two
MeasureTheory.hasStrongType_of_hasWeakTy.docstring:
**Marcinkiewicz interpolation between weak type `(1,1)` and strong type `(2,2)`, in the terms
of the Carleson project**: let `μ` be s-finite, `1 < p < 2`, and let `T` map functions in
`L_p(μ)` to almost everywhere strongly measurable functions, be almost everywhere subadditive
with constant `A` on `L_1(μ) ∪ L_2(μ)`, of weak type `(1,1)` with constant `C₁` and of strong
type `(2,2)` with constant `C₂`. Then `T` has strong type `(p, p)` with constant
`marcinkiewiczNormConst p A C₁ C₂ = (p (2 A C₁/(p - 1) + 4 A² C₂²/(2 - p)))^(1/p)`. Since strong
type `(2,2)` implies weak type `(2,2)` (`MeasureTheory.HasStrongType.hasWeakType`), the Carleson
project's `exists_hasStrongType_real_interpolation` with `(p₀, q₀) = (1, 1)`,
`(p₁, q₁) = (2, 2)` gives strong type `(p,p)` for `A ≥ 1` and positive finite constants; here
the layer cake argument gives it on s-finite measure spaces for every `A ≥ 0` and
`C₁, C₂ ∈ [0, ∞]`, with this constant.

MeasureTheory.enorm_sum_integral_mul_con.name: MeasureTheory.enorm_sum_integral_mul_conj_normingFamily
MeasureTheory.enorm_sum_integral_mul_con.docstring:
**The pairing with the norming family**: let `1 < p < ∞` with conjugate exponent `q`, and
let `u_j ∈ L_p(μ)` for every `j` with `u_j = 0` for `j` outside a finite set `s`. Then
`|∑_{j ∈ s} ∫ u_j conj N_j dμ| = ∫ ‖(u_j)_j‖_{ℓ_2}^p dμ`, the integral of the pointwise
identity `MeasureTheory.sum_mul_conj_normingFamily`, a nonnegative real function.

MeasureTheory.enorm_le_dyadicWeight_neg_.name: MeasureTheory.enorm_le_dyadicWeight_neg_mul_eLpNorm_lqNorm
MeasureTheory.enorm_le_dyadicWeight_neg_.docstring:
**One term of a family is bounded by the mixed norm**: for `q ≠ 0`, a family `h_i ∈ L_p(μ)`
and every `j`, `‖h_j‖_p ≤ 2^(-js) ‖ x ↦ ‖(2^(is) |h_i(x)|)_i‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p`
(`MeasureTheory.dyadicWeight_mul_enorm_le_eLpNorm_lqNorm`).

MeasureTheory.enorm_convolution_le_linte.name: MeasureTheory.enorm_convolution_le_lintegral
MeasureTheory.enorm_convolution_le_linte.docstring: The pointwise bound `|(K ⋆ f)(x)| ≤ ∫ |K(y)| |f(x - y)| dy`.

MeasureTheory.enorm_average_le.name: MeasureTheory.enorm_average_le
MeasureTheory.enorm_average_le.docstring:
The norm of a mean is at most the mean of the norm: `‖⨍ f dμ‖ ≤ ⨍ ‖f‖ dμ` in `[0, ∞]`, for
every function `f` with values in a real normed space. Both means are integrals for the
normalised measure `μ(α)⁻¹ μ`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_tsum_le.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_tsum_le
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_tsum_le.docstring:
**Minkowski's inequality for series** in `L_p`, `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, on any measure space: for
`g_i : α → [0, ∞]` indexed by a countable set, `‖∑_i g_i‖_p ≤ ∑_i ‖g_i‖_p`. If some `g_i` is not
measurable, then `‖g_i‖_p = ∞` and so is the right side. Otherwise the series is the supremum of
its finite partial sums, and this follows from Mathlib's finite version `eLpNorm_sum_le` by
monotone convergence (`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_iSup_of_directed`).

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_tw.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_two_mul
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_tw.docstring:
**Two approximants of one function are close, in the `ρ`-th power**: with `ρ = min(1, p)`,
if `‖f - g‖_p ≤ e` and `‖f - h‖_p ≤ e`, then `‖g - h‖_p^ρ ≤ 2 e^ρ`, for functions with values in
a normed group. Indeed `g - h = (f - h) - (f - g)`, and the `ρ`-triangle inequality
(`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_add_rpow_min_le`) applies. At `p = 0` the exponent is `ρ = 0` and the
inequality reads `1 ≤ 2`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_ts.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_tsum_of_nearBest
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_ts.docstring:
**Transfer of near-best sequences from `L_p` to `L_r`, `0 < p, r ≤ ∞`**: let
`ρ_p = min(1, p)`, `ρ_r = min(1, r)`, and let `b_k` be almost everywhere strongly measurable
functions with `‖f - b_k‖_p ≤ e_k`, where `e` decreases to `0`. If the blocks satisfy the
Nikolskii-type inequality `‖b_{k+1} - b_k‖_r ≤ C 2^(kβ) ‖b_{k+1} - b_k‖_p`, with the dyadic
weight `2^(kβ) = ENNReal.dyadicWeight β k`, then for every `k`
`‖f - b_k‖_r^(ρ_r) ≤ (C 2^(1/ρ_p))^(ρ_r) ∑_{i ≥ 0} (2^((k+i)β) e_{k+i})^(ρ_r)`.
The blocks satisfy `‖b_{k+1} - b_k‖_p ≤ 2^(1/ρ_p) e_k`
(`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_le_two_rpow_mul`), the `b_k` converge to `f` in measure
(`MeasureTheory.tendstoInMeasure_of_eLpNorm_sub_le`), and Fatou's lemma for telescoping sums in
`L_r` (`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_tsum`) bounds `‖f - b_k‖_r`. Here `‖f‖_r` may be
infinite, and so may the measure.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_ts.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_tsum
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_ts.docstring:
**Fatou's lemma for telescoping sums in `L_r`, `0 < r ≤ ∞`**: if `u_n → g` in measure, with
almost everywhere strongly measurable `u_n`, then, with `ρ = min(1, r)`,
`‖g - u_k‖_r^ρ ≤ ∑_{i ≥ 0} ‖u_{k+i+1} - u_{k+i}‖_r^ρ`. The finite telescoping sums bound
`‖u_{k+n} - u_k‖_r^ρ` (`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_sum`), and Mathlib's
`eLpNorm_le_of_tendstoInMeasure`, valid for every exponent, passes the bound to the limit. Its
case `r ≤ 1` is `MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_le_tsum`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_su.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_sum
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_su.docstring:
**Telescoping in `L_r`, `0 < r ≤ ∞`**: with `ρ = min(1, r)`,
`‖u_{k+n} - u_k‖_r^ρ ≤ ∑_{i<n} ‖u_{k+i+1} - u_{k+i}‖_r^ρ` for functions with values in a
seminormed group, by the `ρ`-triangle inequality (`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_add_rpow_min_le`).

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_le_two_rpow_mu.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_le_two_rpow_mul
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_le_two_rpow_mu.docstring:
**Two approximants of one function are close, `0 < p ≤ ∞`**: with `ρ = min(1, p)`, if
`‖f - g‖_p ≤ e` and `‖f - h‖_p ≤ e`, then `‖g - h‖_p ≤ 2^(1/ρ) e`, the `ρ`-th root of
`‖g - h‖_p^ρ ≤ 2 e^ρ` (`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_rpow_min_le_two_mul`). For `p ≥ 1` the factor
is `2`, for `p ≤ 1` it is `2^(1/p)`. For elements of `L_p(μ)` with `p ≤ 1` the same bound, in
the `p`-th power, is `MeasureTheory.Lp.enorm_sub_rpow_le_two_mul`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_rpow_eq_lintegral.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_rpow_eq_lintegral
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_rpow_eq_lintegral.docstring:
`‖g‖_p^p = ∫ g^p` for `0 < p < ∞` and `g : α → [0, ∞]` measurable: the case `[0, ∞]` of
`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_rpow_eq`, with `‖g(x)‖ₑ = g(x)`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_rpow_eq.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_rpow_eq
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_rpow_eq.docstring:
`L_p` norms through `L_p` integrals: `‖g‖_p^p = ∫ ‖g‖^p` for `0 < p < ∞` and every
almost everywhere strongly measurable `g` with values in a space with an extended norm, such as
`ℂ` or `[0, ∞]`. This is Mathlib's `eLpNorm_nnreal_pow_eq_lintegral`, with the exponent given in
`[0, ∞]` instead of `[0, ∞)`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_mul_le_of_forall_n.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_mul_le_of_forall_norm_le
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_mul_le_of_forall_n.docstring:
**Bounded multipliers on `L_p`**: if `c` is almost everywhere strongly measurable with
`‖c x‖ ≤ C` for every `x`, then `‖c u‖_{L_p(μ)} ≤ C ‖u‖_{L_p(μ)}` for every `u` and every
`0 ≤ p ≤ ∞`. For almost everywhere strongly measurable `u` this is Mathlib's
`eLpNorm_le_mul_eLpNorm_of_ae_le_mul'`; for the other `u`, `‖u‖_{L_p(μ)} = ∞`
(`eLpNorm_of_not_aestronglyMeasurable`), and for `C = 0` the product is `0`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_mul_conj_le_of_for.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_mul_conj_le_of_forall_notMem
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_mul_conj_le_of_for.docstring:
**Hölder's inequality on a set outside which one factor vanishes**: let `W` be measurable,
let `g` be a.e. strongly measurable with `g = 0` outside `W`, let `1 ≤ p`, and let `f` be a.e.
strongly measurable. Then `‖f conj g‖_1 ≤ ‖1_W f‖_p ‖g‖_{p'}` with the conjugate exponent `p'`.
Outside `W` the factor `g` vanishes, so `f` may be replaced by `1_W f`; then Hölder's inequality
(Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_mul_eLpNorm`) applies.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_weighted_le.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_weighted_le_min
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_weighted_le.docstring:
**The upper half of the sandwich for weighted families**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`,
weights `w_j ∈ [0, ∞]` and measurable `u_j : α → E` with values in a normed group, indexed by a
countable set, `‖ x ↦ ‖(w_j ‖u_j(x)‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p ≤ ‖(w_j ‖u_j‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_{min(p,q)}}`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_weighted_eq.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_weighted_eq
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_weighted_eq.docstring:
**`L_p(ℓ_p) = ℓ_p(L_p)` for weighted families**: for `0 < p < ∞`, weights `w_j ∈ [0, ∞]` and
measurable `u_j : α → E` with values in a normed group, indexed by a countable set,
`‖ x ↦ ‖(w_j ‖u_j(x)‖)_j‖_{ℓ_p} ‖_p = ‖(w_j ‖u_j‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_p}`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_normingFami.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_normingFamily
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_normingFami.docstring:
**The `L_q(ℓ_2)` norm of the norming family**: let `1 < p < ∞` with conjugate exponent `q`,
and let the `u_j` be almost everywhere strongly measurable with `‖(u_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_2} < ∞` at
every point. Then `‖ ‖(N_j)_j‖_{ℓ_2} ‖_q = (∫ ‖(u_j)_j‖_{ℓ_2}^p)^{1/q}`, by
`MeasureTheory.lqNorm_normingFamily` and `(p - 1) q = p`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_ne_top_of_f.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_ne_top_of_finite
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_ne_top_of_f.docstring:
**A family in `L_p` that vanishes outside a finite set lies in `L_p(ℓ_2)`**: if
`u_j ∈ L_p(μ)` for every `j`, `p ≥ 1`, and `u_j = 0` for `j` outside a finite set `s`, then
`‖ ‖(u_j)_j‖_{ℓ_2} ‖_p < ∞`, since `‖(u_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_2} ≤ ∑_{j ∈ s} |u_j(x)|` and Minkowski's
inequality bounds the right side by `∑_{j ∈ s} ‖u_j‖_p`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_le_of_foral.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_le_of_forall_enorm_sum_integral_le
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_le_of_foral.docstring:
**The `L_p(ℓ_2)` norm by duality**: let `1 < p < ∞` with conjugate exponent `q`, let
`u_j ∈ L_p(μ)` for every `j` with `u_j = 0` for `j` outside a finite set `s`, and let
`A ∈ [0, ∞]`. If `|∑_{j ∈ s} ∫ u_j conj g_j dμ| ≤ A ‖ ‖(g_j)_j‖_{ℓ_2} ‖_q` for every family of
`g_j ∈ L_q(μ)`, then `‖ ‖(u_j)_j‖_{ℓ_2} ‖_p ≤ A`. The norming family gives `X ≤ A X^{1/q}` for
`X = ∫ ‖(u_j)_j‖_{ℓ_2}^p < ∞`, so `X^{1/p} ≤ A` (`ENNReal.le_rpow_mul_of_le_mul_rpow`).

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_le_lqNorm_m.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_le_lqNorm_min
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_le_lqNorm_m.docstring:
**The upper half of the sandwich**:
`‖ x ↦ ‖(g_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p ≤ ‖(‖g_i‖_p)_i‖_{ℓ_{min(p,q)}}` for `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`.
For `p ≤ q` the pointwise bound `‖·‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ‖·‖_{ℓ_p}` and `L_p(ℓ_p) = ℓ_p(L_p)`; for `q ≤ p` the
inequality `L_p(ℓ_q) ≤ ℓ_q(L_p)`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_le_lqNorm_e.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_le_lqNorm_eLpNorm
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_le_lqNorm_e.docstring:
**`L_p(ℓ_q) ≤ ℓ_q(L_p)` for `0 < q ≤ p < ∞`**:
`‖ x ↦ ‖(g_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p ≤ ‖(‖g_i‖_p)_i‖_{ℓ_q}`. If some `g_i` is not measurable, then
`‖g_i‖_p = ∞` and so is the right side. Otherwise, with `U = p/q ≥ 1`, the `q`-th power of the
left side is `‖∑_i g_i^q‖_U`, and Minkowski's inequality for series in `L_U`
(`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_tsum_le`) bounds it by `∑_i ‖g_i^q‖_U = ∑_i ‖g_i‖_p^q`, the `q`-th power of
the right side.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_le_add.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_le_add
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_le_add.docstring:
**The triangle inequality for mixed norms**: for `1 ≤ p`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and families
`u_j, v_j, w_j : α → [0, ∞]` with `w` measurable and, almost everywhere, `w_j ≤ u_j + v_j` for
every `j`, `‖x ↦ ‖(w_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p` is at most the sum of the same norms of `u` and `v`, by
the triangle inequalities in `ℓ_q` at every point and in `L_p`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_ite_mono.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_ite_mono
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_ite_mono.docstring:
**Setting more terms to zero decreases the mixed norm**: for measurable `g_j : α → [0, ∞]` and
predicates `P`, `Q` on `ℕ` with `P j → Q j` for every `j`,
`‖x ↦ ‖(1_P(j) g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p ≤ ‖x ↦ ‖(1_Q(j) g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p`;
`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_ite_le` is the case where `Q` always holds.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_ite_le.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_ite_le
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_ite_le.docstring:
**Setting terms to zero decreases the mixed norm**: for measurable `g_j : α → [0, ∞]` and every
predicate `P` on `ℕ`,
`‖x ↦ ‖(1_P(j) g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p ≤ ‖x ↦ ‖(g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p`, by the monotonicity of the
`ℓ_q` norm and of the `L_p` norm.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_eq_lqNorm_e.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_eq_lqNorm_eLpNorm
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_eq_lqNorm_e.docstring:
**`L_p(ℓ_p) = ℓ_p(L_p)`** for `0 < p < ∞`:
`‖ x ↦ ‖(g_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_p} ‖_p = ‖(‖g_i‖_p)_i‖_{ℓ_p}`. Both sides to the power `p` equal
`∑_i ∫ g_i^p`, by Tonelli's theorem for series (`lintegral_tsum`).

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_eq_const_mu.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_eq_const_mul
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_eq_const_mu.docstring:
**Homogeneity of mixed norms**: for `c ∈ [0, ∞]` and families `u_j, w_j : α → [0, ∞]` with
`u` measurable and, almost everywhere, `w_j = c u_j` for every `j`,
`‖x ↦ ‖(w_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p = c ‖x ↦ ‖(u_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeigh.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeight_zero_left
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeigh.docstring:
**Smoothness `0` for dyadic families**: for every family `u_j : α → [0, ∞]`,
`‖x ↦ ‖(2^(j·0) u_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p = ‖x ↦ ‖(u_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p`, since the weights are `1`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeigh.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeight_mono_smoothness
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeigh.docstring:
**Monotonicity in `s` for dyadic families**: for `s ≤ t` and measurable `u_j : α → [0, ∞]`,
`‖x ↦ ‖(2^(js) u_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p ≤ ‖x ↦ ‖(2^(jt) u_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p`, since
`2^(js) ≤ 2^(jt)`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeigh.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeight_le_zero_add_succ
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeigh.docstring:
**The first term of a weighted family splits off**: for `1 ≤ p`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `s ∈ ℝ` and
measurable `b_j : α → [0, ∞]`,
`‖x ↦ ‖(2^(js) b_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p ≤ ‖b_0‖_p + ‖x ↦ ‖(2^((n+1)s) b_{n+1}(x))_n‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p`,
by the bound of the `ℓ_q` norm by its first term and its shifted tail
(`ENNReal.lqNorm_le_sum_range_add_shift`) and the triangle inequality in `L_p`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeigh.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeight_le_min
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeigh.docstring:
**The upper half of the sandwich for dyadic weights**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`,
`s ∈ ℝ` and measurable `u_j : α → E`,
`‖ x ↦ ‖(2^(js) ‖u_j(x)‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p ≤ ‖(2^(js) ‖u_j‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_{min(p,q)}}`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeigh.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeight_eq
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_dyadicWeigh.docstring:
**`L_p(ℓ_p) = ℓ_p(L_p)` for dyadic weights**: for `0 < p < ∞`, `s ∈ ℝ` and measurable
`u_j : α → E`, `‖ x ↦ ‖(2^(js) ‖u_j(x)‖)_j‖_{ℓ_p} ‖_p = ‖(2^(js) ‖u_j‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_p}`. With `u_j` the
Littlewood–Paley blocks of `f`, this says that the Triebel–Lizorkin and the Besov quasi-norm agree
for `q = p`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_of_lin.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_of_lintegral_le
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_of_lin.docstring:
**From integrals of powers to `L_p` norms**: if `∫ F^p ≤ C ∫ G^p` for `0 < p < ∞` and
almost everywhere measurable `F, G : α → [0, ∞]`, then `‖F‖_p ≤ C^(1/p) ‖G‖_p`: the case
`[0, ∞]` of `MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_of_lintegral_enorm_le`, with `‖F(x)‖ₑ = F(x)`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_of_lin.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_of_lintegral_enorm_le
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_of_lin.docstring:
**From integrals of powers to `L_p` norms, for two measure spaces**: if
`∫ ‖F‖^p dν ≤ C ∫ ‖G‖^p dμ` for `0 < p < ∞` and almost everywhere strongly measurable `F`, `G`,
then `‖F‖_{L_p(ν)} ≤ C^(1/p) ‖G‖_{L_p(μ)}`: take `p`-th roots in `MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_rpow_eq`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_eLpNor.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_eLpNorm_rpow
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_eLpNor.docstring:
**Interpolation between `L_p` and `L_∞`**: for `‖f‖ ≤ M` a.e. and `0 < p ≤ r < ∞`,
`‖f‖_r ≤ M^(1 - p/r) ‖f‖_p^(p/r)`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_weak_one_str.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_weak_one_strong_two
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_weak_one_str.docstring:
**Marcinkiewicz interpolation for operators on an abstract input type, in `L_p` norms**:
under the hypotheses of `MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_of_weak_one_strong_two` with
`p ∈ (1, 2)` in `[0, ∞]`, `‖T x‖_p ≤ (marcinkiewiczConst p C₁ C₂)^(1/p) ‖G x‖_p` for every `x`
with `‖G x‖_p < ∞`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_lintegral_le.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_lintegral_le
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_lintegral_le.docstring:
**The `L_p` norm through the integral of the `p`-th power, as an inequality**: for
`0 < p < ∞`, every `B ∈ [0, ∞]` and every almost everywhere strongly measurable `g` with values
in a space with an extended norm, `∫ ‖g‖^p ≤ B^p` gives `‖g‖_p ≤ B`. This is
`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_rpow_eq` combined with the monotonicity of `t ↦ t^p`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_le_on_pieces.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_le_on_pieces
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_le_on_pieces.docstring:
**`L_q` norm of a function bounded on pieces**: if almost every point lies in one of the
disjoint measurable sets `S n`, each of measure `c`, and `G ≤ a n` on `S n`, then
`‖G‖_{L_q(μ)} ≤ c^(1/q) ‖a‖_{ℓ_q}` for every `q` (with `c^(1/q) = 1` for `q = ∞`).  `G` is
measurable, since `eLpNorm` is `∞` otherwise.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_forall_enorm.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_forall_enorm_integral_mul_conj_le
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_forall_enorm.docstring:
**The `L_p` norm by duality**: let `1 < p < ∞` with conjugate exponent `q`, `v ∈ L_p(μ)`
and `A ∈ [0, ∞]`. If `|∫ v conj g dμ| ≤ A ‖g‖_q` for every `g ∈ L_q(μ)`, then `‖v‖_p ≤ A`: the
case of one function in `MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_le_of_forall_enorm_sum_integral_le`,
where the norming function is `v |v|^{p-2}`; the `ℓ_2` norm of `(v(x), 0, 0, …)` is `|v(x)|`
(`ENNReal.lqNorm_ite_eq`).

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_forall_eLpNo.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_forall_eLpNorm_restrict_le
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_forall_eLpNo.docstring:
**Summing local bounds over a cover**: let `I_i`, `i ∈ ι`, be countably many sets covering
`α`, let `W_i` be sets, and let `0 < p < ∞`. Let `F : α → ℂ` be a.e. strongly measurable and
`G : α → ℂ` a function whose local norms satisfy the window inequality
`∑_i ‖G‖_{L_p(W_i)}^p ≤ M ‖G‖_p^p`. If `‖F‖_{L_p(I_i)} ≤ B ‖G‖_{L_p(W_i)}` for every `i`, then
`‖F‖_p ≤ M^(1/p) B ‖G‖_p`. Indeed
`‖F‖_p^p = ∫ |F|^p ≤ ∑_i ∫_{I_i} |F|^p ≤ B^p ∑_i ‖G‖_{L_p(W_i)}^p ≤ M B^p ‖G‖_p^p` by the
countable subadditivity of the integral (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.lintegral_iUnion_le`), which
holds for arbitrary sets `I_i`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_eLpNorm_top_.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_eLpNorm_top_le
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_eLpNorm_top_.docstring:
**A bound of `‖f‖_∞` by `‖f‖_p` gives a bound of every `‖f‖_r`, `p ≤ r ≤ ∞`, by `‖f‖_p`**
(Ditzian–Prymak 2016, Theorem 2.1, (2.3) with `q = p`): if `‖f‖_∞ ≤ M ‖f‖_p` with `p ≠ 0`, then
`‖f‖_r ≤ M^(1 - p/r) ‖f‖_p` for every `p ≤ r ≤ ∞`. For `r = ∞` this is the hypothesis; for
`r < ∞` interpolation gives `‖f‖_r ≤ ‖f‖_∞^(1-θ) ‖f‖_p^θ` with `θ = p/r`
(`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_eLpNorm_rpow`), and
`(M ‖f‖_p)^(1-θ) ‖f‖_p^θ = M^(1-θ) ‖f‖_p`. A function that is not almost everywhere strongly
measurable has `‖f‖_q = ∞` for every `q`, so the hypothesis forces `M ≠ 0` and the right side is
`∞`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_const_mul_sum_o.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_const_mul_sum_of_ae_le
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_const_mul_sum_o.docstring:
**Minkowski's inequality for a pointwise bound**: for `1 ≤ p`, a measurable `B : α → [0, ∞]`
and measurable `F_i : α → [0, ∞]`, `i ∈ s` finite, the bound `B ≤ c ∑_i F_i` almost everywhere
gives `‖B‖_p ≤ c ∑_i ‖F_i‖_p` (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_const_mul_ennreal` and
`eLpNorm_sum_le`).

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_integral_kernel_le.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_integral_kernel_le_of_bound
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_integral_kernel_le.docstring:
**Weighted averages of uniformly bounded functions**: if `‖G(·, z)‖_p ≤ M` for every `z` with
`Φ(z) ≠ 0` and `0 < ‖Φ‖_1 < ∞`, then `‖∫ Φ(z) G(·, z) dν(z)‖_p ≤ ‖Φ‖_1 M`
(`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_integral_kernel_le`).

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_integral_kernel_le.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_integral_kernel_le
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_integral_kernel_le.docstring:
**Weighted averages in `L_p`** (Minkowski's integral inequality, in the form of the weighted
Jensen inequality): for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, a weight `Φ` on `β` and a jointly measurable `G`,
`‖∫ Φ(z) G(·, z) dν(z)‖_p^p ≤ ‖Φ‖_1^(p-1) ∫ |Φ(z)| ‖G(·, z)‖_p^p dν(z)`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_iSup_of_directed.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_iSup_of_directed
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_iSup_of_directed.docstring:
**Monotone convergence for `L_p` norms**: for a directed countable family of measurable
functions `F_b : α → [0, ∞]`, `‖sup_b F_b‖_p = sup_b ‖F_b‖_p`. For `p < ∞` this is the monotone
convergence theorem for `∫ F_b^p`; for `p = ∞` it holds for every countable family.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_fun_rpow.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_fun_rpow
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_fun_rpow.docstring:
**Powers inside an `L_p` norm**: `‖g^r‖_p = ‖g‖_{p r}^r` for `r > 0` and `g : α → [0, ∞]`
measurable (Mathlib's `eLpNorm_eNorm_rpow`).

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_convolution_le.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_convolution_le
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_convolution_le.docstring:
**Young's inequality** for an integrable kernel on a measurable group:
`‖K ⋆ f‖_p ≤ ‖K‖_1 ‖f‖_p`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_const_mul_enorm.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_const_mul_enorm
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_const_mul_enorm.docstring:
**Homogeneity of the pointwise norm**: `‖c ‖v(·)‖‖_p = c ‖v‖_p` for every constant
`c ∈ [0, ∞]`, every measurable `v : α → E` with values in a normed group and every `p`.

MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_add_rpow_min_le.name: MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_add_rpow_min_le
MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_add_rpow_min_le.docstring:
**The `ρ`-triangle inequality of `L_p` for every `0 < p ≤ ∞`**: with `ρ = min(1, p)`,
`‖f + g‖_p^ρ ≤ ‖f‖_p^ρ + ‖g‖_p^ρ` on any measure space, for all functions with values in an
additive monoid with an extended seminorm and continuous addition, such as a normed group or
`[0, ∞]`. For `p ≤ 1` this is `MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_add_rpow_le_of_le_one`, for `p ≥ 1` the
triangle inequality `eLpNorm_add_le`. Both are Mathlib's triangle inequality
`inhmgELpNorm_add_le`, since `inhmgELpNorm f p μ = ‖f‖_p^ρ` for `p ≠ 0`
(`MeasureTheory.inhmgELpNorm_eq_eLpNorm_rpow_min`).

MeasureTheory.dyadicWeight_mul_enorm_le_.name: MeasureTheory.dyadicWeight_mul_enorm_le_eLpNorm_lqNorm
MeasureTheory.dyadicWeight_mul_enorm_le_.docstring:
**One weighted term of a family is bounded by the mixed norm**: for `q ≠ 0`, a family
`h_i ∈ L_p(μ)` and every `j`, `2^(js) ‖h_j‖_p ≤ ‖ x ↦ ‖(2^(is) |h_i(x)|)_i‖_{ℓ_q} ‖_p`, since
pointwise `2^(js) |h_j(x)|` is at most the `ℓ_q` norm (`ENNReal.le_lqNorm`).

MeasureTheory.distribution_top.name: MeasureTheory.distribution_top
MeasureTheory.distribution_top.docstring: No extended norm exceeds `∞`, so the distribution function vanishes at the level `∞`.

MeasureTheory.distribution_add_le_of_eno.name: MeasureTheory.distribution_add_le_of_enorm
MeasureTheory.distribution_add_le_of_eno.docstring:
**The distribution of a sum**: if `‖f‖ ≤ c (‖g₁‖ + ‖g₂‖)` almost everywhere, then
`μ{‖f‖ > c (t + s)} ≤ μ{‖g₁‖ > t} + μ{‖g₂‖ > s}`, since `‖g₁‖ ≤ t` and `‖g₂‖ ≤ s` force
`‖f‖ ≤ c (t + s)`.

MeasureTheory.distribution.name: MeasureTheory.distribution
MeasureTheory.distribution.docstring:
The **distribution function** of `f`: the measure `μ {x | ‖f x‖ > t}` of the set where the
extended norm of `f` exceeds the level `t ∈ [0, ∞]`.

MeasureTheory.condExp_comap_ae_eq.name: MeasureTheory.condExp_comap_ae_eq
MeasureTheory.condExp_comap_ae_eq.docstring:
**Conditional expectation onto a countable partition**: for a finite measure and an
integrable `f`, `E[f | φ](x)` is the average of `f` over the fibre of `φ` through `x`, for
almost every `x`.  The fibres of measure `0` form a null set, which is why the formula holds
only almost everywhere.

MeasureTheory.comap_top_le.name: MeasureTheory.comap_top_le
MeasureTheory.comap_top_le.docstring:
The σ-algebra of the fibres of `φ` lies below the ambient σ-algebra when the fibres are
measurable and `φ` takes countably many values.

MeasureTheory.cauchySeq_of_edist_le_lqNo.name: MeasureTheory.cauchySeq_of_edist_le_lqNorm_ite
MeasureTheory.cauchySeq_of_edist_le_lqNo.docstring:
**Cauchy sequences from tails in `L_p(ℓ_q)`**: let `0 < p, q < ∞`, let `g_j : α → [0, ∞]` be
measurable with `‖x ↦ ‖(g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p < ∞`, and let `C < ∞`. A sequence `S` in a
pseudo-extended metric space with `edist(S_{N'}, S_N) ≤ C ‖x ↦ ‖(g_j(x))_{j ≥ N}‖_{ℓ_q}‖_p` for
all `N ≤ N'` (the terms `j < N` set to `0`) is a Cauchy sequence: two members beyond `N` are
within `2 C` times the `N`-th tail, and the tails tend to zero
(`MeasureTheory.tendsto_eLpNorm_lqNorm_ite_le`; Mathlib's `EMetric.cauchySeq_iff_le_tendsto_0`).

MeasureTheory.aestronglyMeasurable_normi.name: MeasureTheory.aestronglyMeasurable_normingFamily
MeasureTheory.aestronglyMeasurable_normi.docstring:
The members of the norming family are almost everywhere strongly measurable if the members
of `u` are.

MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_lqNorm_ite.name: MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_lqNorm_ite
MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_lqNorm_ite.docstring:
**Measurability with terms set to zero**: if every `g_j : α → [0, ∞]` is measurable, then for
every predicate `P` on `ℕ` the function `x ↦ ‖(1_P(j) g_j(x))_j‖_{ℓ_q}` is measurable, where
`1_P(j) g_j(x)` is `g_j(x)` if `P j` holds and `0` otherwise.

MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_lqNorm_comp.name: MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_lqNorm_comp
MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_lqNorm_comp.docstring:
The pointwise `ℓ_q` norm `x ↦ ‖(g_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_q}` of a countable family of measurable
functions is measurable: it is a constant for `q = 0`, a countable supremum for `q = ∞` and a
power of a series otherwise.

MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_lintegral_ker.name: MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_lintegral_kernel
MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_lintegral_ker.docstring: The function `x ↦ ∫ |K(y)| |f(x - y)| dy` is measurable.

MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_kernel_rpow.name: MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_kernel_rpow
MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_kernel_rpow.docstring: The integrand of `x ↦ ∫ |K(y)| |f(x - y)|^q dy` is measurable on the product.

MeasureTheory.ae_le_of_le_add_of_tendsto.name: MeasureTheory.ae_le_of_le_add_of_tendsto_eLpNorm
MeasureTheory.ae_le_of_le_add_of_tendsto.docstring:
**Limits of pointwise bounds**: if `u` and `v` are measurable, `u ≤ v + w_J` almost everywhere
for every `J` and `‖w_J‖_p → 0` for some `p > 0`, then `u ≤ v` almost everywhere. The truncated
difference `(u - v)_+` has `‖(u - v)_+‖_p ≤ ‖w_J‖_p` for every `J`, hence norm `0`. This passes
pointwise bounds to limits in `L_p` for functions with values in `[0, ∞]` directly; Mathlib
derives convergence in measure from `L_p` convergence for functions with values in a normed group
(`tendstoInMeasure_of_tendsto_eLpNorm`).

MeasureTheory.ae_enorm_le_of_tendsto_Lp.name: MeasureTheory.ae_enorm_le_of_tendsto_Lp
MeasureTheory.ae_enorm_le_of_tendsto_Lp.docstring:
**Pointwise bounds pass to limits in `L_p`**: for `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, if `G_J → F` in `L_p` and
`|G_J| ≤ v` almost everywhere for every `J`, then `|F| ≤ v` almost everywhere, for every
`v : α → [0, ∞]`. A subsequence of `G_J` converges to `F` almost everywhere (Mathlib's
`tendstoInMeasure_of_tendsto_Lp` and `MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure.exists_seq_tendsto_ae`).

MeasureTheory.ae_enorm_le_eLpNorm_top.name: MeasureTheory.ae_enorm_le_eLpNorm_top
MeasureTheory.ae_enorm_le_eLpNorm_top.docstring:
**A function is bounded almost everywhere by its `L_∞` quasi-norm**: `‖f(x)‖ ≤ ‖f‖_∞` for
almost every `x`, for every function, measurable or not (Mathlib's
`eNorm_ae_le_eLpNormEssSup` with `eLpNormEssSup_le_eLpNorm_top`).

MeasureTheory.ae_enorm_indicator_eq.name: MeasureTheory.ae_enorm_indicator_eq
MeasureTheory.ae_enorm_indicator_eq.docstring:
Restricting a function and its extended norm to a set: if `‖f‖ = G` almost everywhere,
then `‖1_S f‖ = 1_S G` almost everywhere, for every set `S`.

MeasureTheory.ae_convolutionExistsAt.name: MeasureTheory.ae_convolutionExistsAt
MeasureTheory.ae_convolutionExistsAt.docstring:
**The convolution integral converges absolutely almost everywhere** for an integrable
kernel and `f ∈ L_p`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`: the integral form of Young's inequality is finite.

MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure.sub_right.name: MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure.sub_right
MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure.sub_right.docstring:
Convergence in measure is unaffected by subtracting one function from every term and from
the limit.

MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.eq_of_c.name: MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.eq_of_comap_top
MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.eq_of_c.docstring: A function measurable for the σ-algebra of the fibres of `φ` is constant on every fibre.

MeasureTheory.MemLp.mono_exponent_of_eno.name: MeasureTheory.MemLp.mono_exponent_of_enorm_le
MeasureTheory.MemLp.mono_exponent_of_eno.docstring:
**Bounded functions in `L_p` lie in `L_r` for every `r ≥ p`**: if `f ∈ L_p` with `p > 0` and
`‖f‖ ≤ M < ∞` almost everywhere, then `f ∈ L_r` for every `p ≤ r ≤ ∞`, by
`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_eLpNorm_rpow` for `r < ∞` and the essential supremum for
`r = ∞`.

MeasureTheory.Lp.topInclusion.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.topInclusion
MeasureTheory.Lp.topInclusion.docstring:
The inclusion `L_∞ → L_p` of the essentially bounded functions, for every exponent `p` and a
finite measure `μ`, as a linear map: `ι_{∞,p}`.

MeasureTheory.Lp.norm_condExpLp_le.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.norm_condExpLp_le
MeasureTheory.Lp.norm_condExpLp_le.docstring: **The conditional expectation is a contraction** on `L_p`.

MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionOfExponentLe_a.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionOfExponentLe_apply
MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionOfExponentLe_a.docstring:
The bounded inclusion and the linear inclusion agree: both send `f ∈ L_r` to its class in
`L_p`.

MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionOfExponentLeLi.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionOfExponentLeLinear_self
MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionOfExponentLeLi.docstring: The identity case `p = r` of the inclusion, for every exponent `p`.

MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionOfExponentLeLi.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionOfExponentLeLinear
MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionOfExponentLeLi.docstring: The inclusion `L_r → L_p` for `p ≤ r` and a finite measure, as a linear map.

MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionOfExponentLe.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionOfExponentLe
MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionOfExponentLe.docstring:
The **inclusion `L_r ↪ L_p`** for `p ≤ r` and a finite measure `μ`, as a bounded linear
map with `‖f‖_p ≤ μ(Ω)^(1/p - 1/r) ‖f‖_r`.

MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionConst.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionConst
MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionConst.docstring: The constant `μ(Ω)^(1/p - 1/r)` of Hölder's inequality between `L_r` and `L_p`.

MeasureTheory.Lp.eLpNorm_sub_topInclusio.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.eLpNorm_sub_topInclusion
MeasureTheory.Lp.eLpNorm_sub_topInclusio.docstring:
**The quasi-norms of a difference with an essentially bounded function**: for `f ∈ L_p` and
`a ∈ L_∞` on a finite measure space, `‖f - ι_{∞,p} a‖_t = ‖f - a‖_t` for every exponent `t`,
since `ι_{∞,p} a = a` almost everywhere.

MeasureTheory.Lp.condExpLp_of_mem.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.condExpLp_of_mem
MeasureTheory.Lp.condExpLp_of_mem.docstring: The conditional expectation fixes the `m`-measurable functions.

MeasureTheory.Lp.condExpLpLinear.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.condExpLpLinear
MeasureTheory.Lp.condExpLpLinear.docstring: The **conditional expectation** `E[· | m]` on `L_p(μ)`, as a real-linear map.

MeasureTheory.Lp.condExpLp.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.condExpLp
MeasureTheory.Lp.condExpLp.docstring: The **conditional expectation** `E[· | m]` on `L_p(μ)`, a contraction.

MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_topInclusion.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_topInclusion
MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_topInclusion.docstring: The inclusion `L_∞ → L_p` agrees with the function almost everywhere.

MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_inclusionOfExpone.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_inclusionOfExponentLeLinear
MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_inclusionOfExpone.docstring: The inclusion agrees with the function almost everywhere.

MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_inclusionOfExpone.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_inclusionOfExponentLe
MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_inclusionOfExpone.docstring:
The inclusion agrees with the function almost everywhere:
`inclusionOfExponentLe μ hpr f = f` a.e.

MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_condExpLpLinear.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_condExpLpLinear
MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_condExpLpLinear.docstring: The linear conditional expectation agrees a.e. with Mathlib's `μ[f | m]`.

MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_condExpLp.name: MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_condExpLp
MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_condExpLp.docstring: `E[f | m]` on `L_p` agrees a.e. with Mathlib's `μ[f | m]`.

MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrable.integrab.name: MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrable.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport
MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrable.integrab.docstring:
**Locally integrable functions with compact support are integrable**: such a function is
integrable on its compact closed support (Mathlib's `LocallyIntegrable.integrableOn_isCompact`) and
zero outside it, as for continuous functions in `Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport`.

MeasureTheory.HasWeakType.name: MeasureTheory.HasWeakType
MeasureTheory.HasWeakType.docstring:
An operator has **weak type `(p, q)`** if it is bounded as a map from `L^p` to weak `L^q`.
`HasWeakType T p p' μ ν c` means that `T` has weak type `(p, p')` w.r.t. measures `μ`, `ν`
and constant `c`.

MeasureTheory.HasStrongType.name: MeasureTheory.HasStrongType
MeasureTheory.HasStrongType.docstring:
An operator has **strong type `(p, q)`** if it is bounded as an operator on `L^p → L^q`.
`HasStrongType T p p' μ ν c` means that `T` has strong type (p, p') w.r.t. measures `μ`, `ν`
and constant `c`.

MeasureTheory.Filtration.mem_filtrationS.name: MeasureTheory.Filtration.mem_filtrationScheme
MeasureTheory.Filtration.mem_filtrationS.docstring:
The approximants of complexity `n ≥ 1` of the filtration scheme are the
`ℱ_⌊log₂ n⌋`-measurable functions in `L_p`.

MeasureTheory.Filtration.memApprox_iff_m.name: MeasureTheory.Filtration.memApprox_iff_martingale
MeasureTheory.Filtration.memApprox_iff_m.docstring:
**The martingale-difference characterisation**: for `s > 0`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and approximants
dense in `L_p`, `f ∈ A^s_q(L_p, ℱ)` iff
`‖E[f | ℱ_0]‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ‖E[f | ℱ_{k+1}] - E[f | ℱ_k]‖_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`.

MeasureTheory.Filtration.filtrationSchem.name: MeasureTheory.Filtration.filtrationScheme
MeasureTheory.Filtration.filtrationSchem.docstring:
The **filtration scheme** in `L_p(μ)`: the dyadic scheme
(`ApproximationScheme.ofMonotoneSubmodules`) of the increasing subspaces `L_p(ℱ_k)` of
`ℱ_k`-measurable functions, so `{0}` at complexity `0` and `L_p(ℱ_⌊log₂ n⌋)` at complexity
`n ≥ 1`.

MeasureTheory.Filtration.filtrationProje.name: MeasureTheory.Filtration.filtrationProjectionScheme
MeasureTheory.Filtration.filtrationProje.docstring:
**The filtration scheme is a projection scheme** with bound `1`: the conditional
expectations are contractive projections onto the approximants, `P_0 = 0` and
`P_n = E[· | ℱ_⌊log₂ n⌋]` for `n ≥ 1`, so `P_{2^k} = E[· | ℱ_k]`
(`ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.ofMonotone_two_pow`).

MeasureTheory.AESubadditiveOn.name: MeasureTheory.AESubadditiveOn
MeasureTheory.AESubadditiveOn.docstring:
The operator is **almost everywhere subadditive** on the functions satisfying `P` with
constant `A`: `‖T(f + g)‖ ≤ A (‖T f‖ + ‖T g‖)` almost everywhere for all `f, g` satisfying `P`
(this is almost vacuous if `A = ⊤`).

Manifold.stronglyMeasurable_chartLift.name: Manifold.stronglyMeasurable_chartLift
Manifold.stronglyMeasurable_chartLift.docstring:
The lift from a chart is strongly measurable for continuous `θ` and strongly measurable `F`,
since `κ`, set to `0` off the open source, is measurable
(`Manifold.measurable_piecewise_extend`).

Manifold.range_inter_coordChange_target.name: Manifold.range_inter_coordChange_target
Manifold.range_inter_coordChange_target.docstring: The target of the change of charts is the relatively open set `range I ∩ U'`.

Manifold.range_inter_coordChange_source.name: Manifold.range_inter_coordChange_source
Manifold.range_inter_coordChange_source.docstring: The source of the change of charts is the relatively open set `range I ∩ U`.

Manifold.range_eq_closedHalfSpace.name: Manifold.range_eq_closedHalfSpace
Manifold.range_eq_closedHalfSpace.docstring: The range of the half-space model is the closed half-space `{y : 0 ≤ ⟪y, e₀⟫}`.

Manifold.range_ae_eq_domain.name: Manifold.range_ae_eq_domain
Manifold.range_ae_eq_domain.docstring: The range of the half-space model is the flat domain up to the null set `H₀`.

Manifold.modNormOn_range_eq.name: Manifold.modNormOn_range_eq
Manifold.modNormOn_range_eq.docstring:
**The intrinsic quasi-norms of the closed and of the open half-space agree**: the two sets
differ by the null set `H₀`.

Manifold.mem_interior_extend_target_iff.name: Manifold.mem_interior_extend_target_iff
Manifold.mem_interior_extend_target_iff.docstring:
**Interior points of a chart target**: a point of the target of an extended chart lies in its
interior iff its first coordinate is positive.

Manifold.mem_coordChange_target_iff_of_b.name: Manifold.mem_coordChange_target_iff_of_bdry
Manifold.mem_coordChange_target_iff_of_b.docstring: A point of `H₀` lies in `range I ∩ U'` iff it lies in the target of the change of charts.

Manifold.mem_coordChange_source_iff_of_b.name: Manifold.mem_coordChange_source_iff_of_bdry
Manifold.mem_coordChange_source_iff_of_b.docstring: A point of `H₀` lies in `range I ∩ U` iff it lies in the source of the change of charts.

Manifold.mem_coordChange_source.name: Manifold.mem_coordChange_source
Manifold.mem_coordChange_source.docstring:
`y` lies in the source of the change of charts iff it lies in the target of `e.extend I`
and its preimage lies in the source of `e'`.

Manifold.memLp_chartLift.name: Manifold.memLp_chartLift
Manifold.memLp_chartLift.docstring:
**The lift from a chart is in `L_p(μ)`** for `F ∈ L_p(E)`, a continuous cut-off `θ` with
`tsupport θ ⊆ e.source` and a smooth measure `μ`, by the `L_p` bound
(`Manifold.exists_eLpNorm_chartLift_le`).

Manifold.measurable_piecewise_extend.name: Manifold.measurable_piecewise_extend
Manifold.measurable_piecewise_extend.docstring:
**The extended chart, set to `0` off the source, is measurable**: `κ = e.extend I` is
continuous on the open source (Mathlib's `ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise`).

Manifold.measurableSet_extend_target.name: Manifold.measurableSet_extend_target
Manifold.measurableSet_extend_target.docstring:
The target of an extended chart is measurable: it is the intersection of an open set with the
closed range of `I`.

Manifold.graphTrace_chartChange_applyLp_.name: Manifold.graphTrace_chartChange_applyLp_of_modNorm
Manifold.graphTrace_chartChange_applyLp_.docstring:
**The trace commutes with a change of charts**: for `F ∈ L_p(ℝ^n)` with a finite
`B^{s+1/p}_{p,q}`-norm of order `L > s + 1/p`, `Tr (T F) = T^∂ (Tr F)` on `H₀`. The partial sums
`G_J` of the reproducing formula are continuous, so the identity holds for them
(`Manifold.graphTrace_chartChange_applyLp_of_continuous`); they converge to `F` in `B^{1/p}_{p,1}`,
where `T` and the trace are bounded, and `Tr G_J → Tr F` in `L_p(H₀)`, where `T^∂` is bounded.

Manifold.graphTrace_chartChange_applyLp_.name: Manifold.graphTrace_chartChange_applyLp_of_continuous
Manifold.graphTrace_chartChange_applyLp_.docstring:
**The trace commutes with a change of charts, for continuous functions**: if `G` has a finite
`B^{s+1/p}_{p,q}`-norm of order `L > s + 1/p` and a continuous representative `g`, then
`Tr (T G) = T^∂ (Tr G)`: both are the restriction of `T g` to `H₀`.

Manifold.graphTrace_chartChange_applyLp.name: Manifold.graphTrace_chartChange_applyLp
Manifold.graphTrace_chartChange_applyLp.docstring:
**The trace commutes with a change of charts** for `G` with a finite intrinsic
`B^{s+1/p}_{p,q}`-norm of order `L > s + 1/p` on the closed half-space: extend `G` to `ℝ^n`
(the half-space is a Besov domain); neither side sees the extension.

Manifold.graphCutoff_eq_indicatorLp.name: Manifold.graphCutoff_eq_indicatorLp
Manifold.graphCutoff_eq_indicatorLp.docstring: The cut-off to the open half-space is the cut-off to the closed half-space.

Manifold.flatDomain.name: Manifold.flatDomain
Manifold.flatDomain.docstring: The flat graph domain `{y : y_0 > 0}` of `ℝ^n`.

Manifold.extendCoordChange_apply.name: Manifold.extendCoordChange_apply
Manifold.extendCoordChange_apply.docstring: The change of charts is `e'.extend I ∘ (e.extend I).symm`.

Manifold.exists_flatGraphExtension.name: Manifold.exists_flatGraphExtension
Manifold.exists_flatGraphExtension.docstring:
**Extensions from the boundary hyperplane**: for `G ∈ L_p(H₀)` with
`‖G‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_r(G, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`, `r = ⌊s⌋ + 1`, the extension `E G` of moment
order `r` (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphExtension` of the flat graph) has a finite
`B^{s+1/p}_{p,q}`-norm of order `L` and the trace `Tr (E G) = G`
(`Rd.LipschitzGraph.graphTrace_flatExtension`).

Manifold.exists_eLpNorm_chartLift_le.name: Manifold.exists_eLpNorm_chartLift_le
Manifold.exists_eLpNorm_chartLift_le.docstring:
**The lift from a chart is bounded in `L_p`**: for a chart `e` of the atlas, a continuous
cut-off `θ` with `tsupport θ ⊆ e.source`, a smooth measure `μ` and `0 < p < ∞` there is `C < ∞`
with `‖θ · F ∘ κ‖_{L_p(μ)} ≤ C ‖F‖_{L_p(E)}` for every strongly measurable `F`. The `L_p` norms on
`M` and in the chart are comparable on `tsupport θ`
(`Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.exists_eLpNorm_chart_le`), and `|θ| ≤ B` on the compact `M`.

Manifold.exists_contMDiff_eq_one_tsuppor.name: Manifold.exists_contMDiff_eq_one_tsupport_subset
Manifold.exists_contMDiff_eq_one_tsuppor.docstring:
**Smooth cut-offs**: for a compact set `K` inside an open set `U` of a σ-compact Hausdorff
manifold there is a smooth `θ : M → ℝ` with `θ = 1` on `K` and `tsupport θ ⊆ U`: Mathlib's
smooth function with support an open `V` and equal to `1` exactly on `K`
(`exists_contMDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff`), for `K ⊆ V` and `closure V ⊆ U`
(`exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure`).

Manifold.coordChange_target_eq_image.name: Manifold.coordChange_target_eq_image
Manifold.coordChange_target_eq_image.docstring:
The target of the change of charts is the image of `e.source ∩ e'.source` under
`e'.extend I`.

Manifold.coordChange_mem_bdry.name: Manifold.coordChange_mem_bdry
Manifold.coordChange_mem_bdry.docstring:
**Changes of charts preserve the boundary hyperplane**: if `y_0 = 0` in the source of the
change of charts from `e` to `e'`, the image has first coordinate `0`.

Manifold.contDiffOn_comp_extend_symm.name: Manifold.contDiffOn_comp_extend_symm
Manifold.contDiffOn_comp_extend_symm.docstring:
**Smooth functions in a chart**: for a chart `e` of the atlas and a smooth `g : M → ℝ`,
`g ∘ κ⁻¹` is smooth within the target of the extended chart `κ = e.extend I`.

Manifold.coe_graphProj_of_mem_bdry.name: Manifold.coe_graphProj_of_mem_bdry
Manifold.coe_graphProj_of_mem_bdry.docstring: The projection onto `H₀` is the identity on `H₀`.

Manifold.coe_graphProj_coordChange_symm.name: Manifold.coe_graphProj_coordChange_symm
Manifold.coe_graphProj_coordChange_symm.docstring: The inverse change of charts maps the boundary part of its target into `H₀`.

Manifold.coe_graphProj_coordChange.name: Manifold.coe_graphProj_coordChange
Manifold.coe_graphProj_coordChange.docstring: The change of charts maps the boundary part of its source into `H₀`.

Manifold.chartLift.name: Manifold.chartLift
Manifold.chartLift.docstring:
The **lift from a chart**: `θ · F ∘ κ` on the source of the chart `e`, `0` outside, for a
cut-off `θ` on `M` and `F : E → ℂ`.

Manifold.chartChange_apply_coe.name: Manifold.chartChange_apply_coe
Manifold.chartChange_apply_coe.docstring:
**The change of charts on the boundary**: on `H₀`, the change of charts with a cut-off acts as
its restriction to `H₀`.

Manifold.boundaryChartChange.name: Manifold.boundaryChartChange
Manifold.boundaryChartChange.docstring:
The **boundary change of charts with a cut-off**: the restriction of the change of charts with
a cut-off to the boundary hyperplane `H₀`, a smooth change of variables with a cut-off on all of
`H₀`.

Manifold.bdry_subset_range.name: Manifold.bdry_subset_range
Manifold.bdry_subset_range.docstring: The boundary hyperplane lies in the half-space.

Manifold.bdry.name: Manifold.bdry
Manifold.bdry.docstring: The **boundary hyperplane** `H₀ = e₀^⊥ = {y : y_0 = 0}` of the half-space.

Manifold.aemeasurable_extend_restrict.name: Manifold.aemeasurable_extend_restrict
Manifold.aemeasurable_extend_restrict.docstring:
**The extended chart is almost everywhere measurable on its source**: for every measure `μ` on
`M`, `κ = e.extend I` is almost everywhere measurable for `μ` restricted to the open source, on
which `κ` is continuous.

Manifold.MemManifoldBesov.name: Manifold.MemManifoldBesov
Manifold.MemManifoldBesov.docstring:
The **Besov space** `B^s_{p,q}(M)` of a compact manifold with a smooth measure: `f ∈ L_p(μ)`
with a finite Besov quasi-norm for a chosen Besov atlas. For `s > 0` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` every Besov
atlas gives the same space (`Manifold.memManifoldBesov_iff`).

Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.lintegral_sourc.name: Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.lintegral_source_eq
Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.lintegral_sourc.docstring:
**Integrals in a chart**: for a chart `e` of the atlas with density `ρ` and a measurable
`F ≥ 0`, `∫_{e.source} F dμ = ∫_{κ(e.source)} ρ(y) F(κ⁻¹ y) dy`.

Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.exists_lintegra.name: Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.exists_lintegral_chart_le
Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.exists_lintegra.docstring:
**Integrals on `M` and in a chart are comparable** for functions that vanish outside a compact
subset `K` of the source of a chart `e` of the atlas: there are `c > 0` and `C < ∞` with
`∫_{κ(e.source)} F ∘ κ⁻¹ ≤ c⁻¹ ∫_M F dμ` and `∫_M F dμ ≤ C ∫_{κ(e.source)} F ∘ κ⁻¹`.

Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.exists_eLpNorm_.name: Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.exists_eLpNorm_chart_le
Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.exists_eLpNorm_.docstring:
**`L_p` norms on `M` and in a chart are comparable** for strongly measurable functions that
vanish outside a compact subset `K` of the source of a chart `e` of the atlas: for `0 < p < ∞`
there are `c, C < ∞` with `‖1_{κ(e.source)} (G ∘ κ⁻¹)‖_p ≤ c ‖G‖_{L_p(μ)}` and
`‖G‖_{L_p(μ)} ≤ C ‖1_{κ(e.source)} (G ∘ κ⁻¹)‖_p`
(`Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.exists_lintegral_chart_le` for `‖G‖^p`, with Mathlib's
`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_indicator_eq_eLpNorm_restrict` for the indicator).

Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.exists_density_.name: Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.exists_density_bounds
Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.exists_density_.docstring:
**The density is bounded above and below on compact sets**: on a compact `K'` inside the
target, `c ≤ ρ ≤ C` with `0 < c` and `C < ∞`, since `ρ` is continuous with values in `(0, ∞)`.

Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.name: Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure
Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.docstring:
A **smooth measure** on `M`, here a measure with a continuous positive density in every chart:
in every chart `e` of the atlas, the image of `μ` on the source of `e` under the extended chart is
a measure with a continuous density `ρ_e` with `0 < ρ_e < ∞` on the target, with respect to the
Lebesgue measure on the target.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.tsupport_psi_mul_the.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.tsupport_psi_mul_theta_subset
Manifold.BesovAtlas.tsupport_psi_mul_the.docstring: The cut-off `ψ_i θ'_j` of two atlases has its support in both sources.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.transition_apply_of_.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.transition_apply_of_notMem
Manifold.BesovAtlas.transition_apply_of_.docstring:
**The change of charts off the common sources**: `T_{ij} G (y) = 0` unless `y = κ_i x` with `x`
in the source of `κ'_j`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.transition_apply_of_.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.transition_apply_of_mem
Manifold.BesovAtlas.transition_apply_of_.docstring:
**The change of charts at a point of both sources**: for `y = κ_i x` with `x` in the source
of `κ'_j`, `T_{ij} G (y) = ψ_i(x) θ'_j(x) G(κ'_j x)`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.transition_apply.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.transition_apply
Manifold.BesovAtlas.transition_apply.docstring:
The change of charts acts on the source of the change of charts:
`T_{ij} G = 1_{κ_i(s_i ∩ s'_j)} (χ G) ∘ Φ`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.transition.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.transition
Manifold.BesovAtlas.transition.docstring:
The **change of charts** from the `i`-th chart of `A` to the `j`-th chart of `A'`, with the
cut-off `(ψ_i θ'_j) ∘ κ'_j⁻¹`, as a smooth change of variables with a cut-off on `range I`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.piece_eq_sum_apply.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.piece_eq_sum_apply
Manifold.BesovAtlas.piece_eq_sum_apply.docstring:
**The pieces of two atlases** (pointwise): `piece_i g = ∑_j T_{ij}(piece'_j g)`, since
`ψ_i g = ∑_j ψ_i ψ'_j g` and `θ'_j ψ'_j = ψ'_j` (`Manifold.BesovAtlas.transition_apply_of_mem`).

Manifold.BesovAtlas.piece_chartLift.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.piece_chartLift
Manifold.BesovAtlas.piece_chartLift.docstring:
**The pieces of a lift from a chart**: `piece_i (θ_k · F ∘ κ_k) = T_{ik} F` pointwise, for the
change of charts `T_{ik}` with the cut-off `ψ_i θ_k` (`Manifold.BesovAtlas.transition_apply_of_mem`,
`Manifold.BesovAtlas.transition_apply_of_notMem`).

Manifold.BesovAtlas.piece_ae_eq.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.piece_ae_eq
Manifold.BesovAtlas.piece_ae_eq.docstring:
**The pieces see only classes**: if `g₁ = g₂` `μ`-almost everywhere, their pieces agree
almost everywhere, by the `L_1` bound of the pieces of `g₁ - g₂`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.pieceLp_finsetSum.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.pieceLp_finsetSum
Manifold.BesovAtlas.pieceLp_finsetSum.docstring: The pieces in `L_p` of a finite sum are the sums of the pieces.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.pieceLp_eq_sum.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.pieceLp_eq_sum
Manifold.BesovAtlas.pieceLp_eq_sum.docstring:
**The pieces of two atlases in `L_p`**: `piece_i f = ∑_j T_{ij}(piece'_j f)`, with the changes
of charts acting on `L_p(E)`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.pieceLp_chartLiftLp.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.pieceLp_chartLiftLp
Manifold.BesovAtlas.pieceLp_chartLiftLp.docstring: **The pieces of a lift from a chart in `L_p`**: `piece_i (θ_k · F ∘ κ_k) = T_{ik} F`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.pieceLp_ae.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.pieceLp_ae
Manifold.BesovAtlas.pieceLp_ae.docstring: The chart piece in `L_p(E)` agrees with `(ψ_i f) ∘ κ_i⁻¹` almost everywhere.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.pieceLp.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.pieceLp
Manifold.BesovAtlas.pieceLp.docstring: The **chart piece** of `f ∈ L_p(μ)` as an element of `L_p(E)`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.piece.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.piece
Manifold.BesovAtlas.piece.docstring: The **chart piece** `(ψ_i g) ∘ κ_i⁻¹` on the target of `κ_i`, `0` outside.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.nonempty.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.nonempty
Manifold.BesovAtlas.nonempty.docstring:
**Every compact manifold has a Besov atlas**: finitely many chart sources cover `M`, a smooth
partition of unity is subordinate to them, and the cut-off `θ_i` is a smooth function equal to
`1` on `tsupport ψ_i` with `tsupport θ_i ⊆ e_i.source`
(`Manifold.exists_contMDiff_eq_one_tsupport_subset`).

Manifold.BesovAtlas.modNormOn_pieceLp_le.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.modNormOn_pieceLp_le_atlasBesovNorm
Manifold.BesovAtlas.modNormOn_pieceLp_le.docstring:
**One piece is at most the whole**: the intrinsic quasi-norm of the `i`-th chart piece is at
most the Besov quasi-norm of the atlas, one term of its sum (Mathlib's `Finset.single_le_sum`).

Manifold.BesovAtlas.memLp_piece.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.memLp_piece
Manifold.BesovAtlas.memLp_piece.docstring: The pieces of `f ∈ L_p(μ)` are in `L_p(E)`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.memAtlasBoundaryBeso.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.memAtlasBoundaryBesov_atlasBoundaryTrace
Manifold.BesovAtlas.memAtlasBoundaryBeso.docstring:
**The trace maps into the boundary space**: for `s > 0`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `L > s + 1/p` and
`f ∈ B^{s+1/p}_{p,q}(M)`, the trace `Tr_A f` lies in `B^s_{p,q}(∂M)`: the quasi-norm bound
`Manifold.BesovAtlas.exists_atlasBoundaryTrace_norm_le`, with `‖f‖_{A, L, s+1/p, q} < ∞`
(`Manifold.BesovAtlas.memAtlasBesov_iff_atlasBesovNorm_lt_top`).

Manifold.BesovAtlas.memAtlasBesov_iff_me.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.memAtlasBesov_iff_memAtlasBesov
Manifold.BesovAtlas.memAtlasBesov_iff_me.docstring: **The Besov space does not depend on the atlas**: `f ∈ B^s_{p,q}` for `A` iff for `A'`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.memAtlasBesov_iff_at.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.memAtlasBesov_iff_atlasBesovNorm_lt_top
Manifold.BesovAtlas.memAtlasBesov_iff_at.docstring:
**The order does not matter**: for `0 < s < r`, `f ∈ B^s_{p,q}` iff its Besov quasi-norm of
order `r` is finite (`Rd.BesovDomain.modNormOn_order_le_of_besovDomain` piece by piece).

Manifold.BesovAtlas.memAtlasBesov_chartL.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.memAtlasBesov_chartLiftLp
Manifold.BesovAtlas.memAtlasBesov_chartL.docstring:
**Lifts from a chart are in `B^σ_{p,q}(M)`**: for `F ∈ L_p(E)` with
`‖F‖_p + ‖(2^(kσ) ω_r(F, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`, `0 < σ < r`, the lift `θ_k · F ∘ κ_k` lies in
`B^σ_{p,q}(M)`: its pieces are `T_{ik} F`, bounded on `range I`
(`Rd.CutoffDiffeo.modNormOn_applyLp_le`).

Manifold.BesovAtlas.interior_univ_bdry_n.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.interior_univ_bdry_nonempty
Manifold.BesovAtlas.interior_univ_bdry_n.docstring: The whole hyperplane has nonempty interior in itself.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.graphTrace_pieceLp_e.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.graphTrace_pieceLp_eq_sum
Manifold.BesovAtlas.graphTrace_pieceLp_e.docstring:
**The traces of the pieces of two atlases**: for `s > 0`, `L > s + 1/p` and
`f ∈ B^{s+1/p}_{p,q}(M)`, `Tr (piece_i f) = ∑_j T^∂_{ij} (Tr (piece'_j f))`. The pieces satisfy
`piece_i f = ∑_j T_{ij} (piece'_j f)`, and the trace commutes with the changes of charts
(`Manifold.graphTrace_chartChange_applyLp`).

Manifold.BesovAtlas.exists_eLpNorm_piece.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.exists_eLpNorm_piece_le
Manifold.BesovAtlas.exists_eLpNorm_piece.docstring:
**The pieces are bounded in `L_p`**: `‖piece_i g‖_{L_p(E)} ≤ C ‖g‖_{L_p(μ)}`, since
`0 ≤ ψ_i ≤ 1` and the `L_p` norms on `M` and in the chart are comparable on `tsupport ψ_i`
(`Manifold.IsSmoothMeasure.exists_eLpNorm_chart_le`).

Manifold.BesovAtlas.exists_atlasBoundary.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.exists_atlasBoundaryTrace_norm_le
Manifold.BesovAtlas.exists_atlasBoundary.docstring:
**The trace is bounded**: for `s > 0`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and `L > s + 1/p` there is `C < ∞` such
that for every `f ∈ B^{s+1/p}_{p,q}(M)` each boundary piece of `Tr_A f` agrees almost everywhere
with some `G ∈ L_p(H₀)` of Besov quasi-norm
`‖G‖_p + ‖(2^(js) ω_{⌊s⌋+1}(G, 2^(-j))_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C ‖f‖_{A, L, s+1/p, q}`, with the Besov
quasi-norm of the atlas with differences of order `L` (`Manifold.BesovAtlas.atlasBesovNorm`). `G` is
the trace of the piece of `f` (`Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryPiece_atlasBoundaryTrace`), bounded by
the trace theorem of the half-space (`Rd.LipschitzGraph.modNorm_graphTrace_le_halfSpaceGraph`); the
piece is one term of the sum `‖f‖_{A, L, s+1/p, q}`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.exists_atlasBoundary.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.exists_atlasBoundaryTrace_eq
Manifold.BesovAtlas.exists_atlasBoundary.docstring:
**The trace is onto**: for `s > 0` and `L ≥ 2` with `L > s + 1/p`, every
`g ∈ B^s_{p,q}(∂M)` is the trace of some `f ∈ B^{s+1/p}_{p,q}(M)`, in the sense that the boundary
pieces of `Tr_A f` and of `g` agree almost everywhere. The function is
`f = ∑_k θ_k · (E G_k) ∘ κ_k` with the extensions `E G_k` of the boundary pieces of `g`
(`Manifold.exists_flatGraphExtension`); its pieces are `piece_i f = ∑_k T_{ik} (E G_k)`, whose
traces are `∑_k T^∂_{ik} G_k`, the `i`-th boundary piece of `g`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.chartLiftLp_ae.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.chartLiftLp_ae
Manifold.BesovAtlas.chartLiftLp_ae.docstring: The lift from the `k`-th chart in `L_p(μ)` is `θ_k · F ∘ κ_k` almost everywhere.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.chartLiftLp.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.chartLiftLp
Manifold.BesovAtlas.chartLiftLp.docstring:
The **lift from the `k`-th chart** of `F ∈ L_p(E)` to `L_p(μ)`: `θ_k · F ∘ κ_k`
(`Manifold.chartLift`).

Manifold.BesovAtlas.chartChange_apply.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.chartChange_apply
Manifold.BesovAtlas.chartChange_apply.docstring:
The change of charts with a cut-off acts on the source of the change of charts:
`T G = 1_{κ(s ∩ s')} (χ G) ∘ Φ`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.chartChange.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.chartChange
Manifold.BesovAtlas.chartChange.docstring:
**The change of charts with a cut-off** from a chart `e` to a chart `e'` of the atlas, with a
smooth cut-off `c` on `M` whose support lies in both sources: `Φ = κ' ∘ κ⁻¹` with
`χ = c ∘ κ'⁻¹`, as a smooth change of variables with a cut-off on `range I`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryTransition.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryTransition
Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryTransition.docstring: The **boundary change of charts** from the `i`-th chart of `A` to the `j`-th chart of `A'`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryPiece_eq_sum.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryPiece_eq_sum
Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryPiece_eq_sum.docstring: **The boundary pieces of two atlases**: `∂piece_i g = ∑_j T^∂_{ij}(∂piece'_j g)`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryPiece_atlasB.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryPiece_atlasBoundaryTrace_eq_sum
Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryPiece_atlasB.docstring:
**The boundary pieces of the trace**, pointwise on `H₀`: the `k`-th boundary piece of
`Tr_A f` is `∑_i T^∂_{ki} (Tr (piece_i f))`, since `ψ_k θ_i` is the cut-off of `T^∂_{ki}`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryPiece_atlasB.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryPiece_atlasBoundaryTrace
Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryPiece_atlasB.docstring:
**The boundary pieces of the trace are the traces of the pieces**: for `s > 0`, `L > s + 1/p`
and `f ∈ B^{s+1/p}_{p,q}(M)`, the `k`-th boundary piece of `Tr_A f` is `Tr (piece_k f)` almost
everywhere on `H₀`: both are `∑_i T^∂_{ki} (Tr (piece_i f))`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryPiece.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryPiece
Manifold.BesovAtlas.boundaryPiece.docstring: The **boundary pieces** of `g : M → ℂ`: the restrictions of the chart pieces to `H₀`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.atlasBoundaryTrace.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.atlasBoundaryTrace
Manifold.BesovAtlas.atlasBoundaryTrace.docstring:
The **trace on the boundary** of `f ∈ L_p(μ)` in the atlas `A`:
`Tr_A f = ∑_i θ_i · Tr(piece_i f) ∘ P ∘ κ_i` on the chart sources, with the trace `Tr` of order
`L` of the half-space and the projection `P` onto `H₀`. On `∂M` the points `κ_i x` lie in `H₀`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.atlasBesovNorm_le_at.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.atlasBesovNorm_le_atlasBesovNorm
Manifold.BesovAtlas.atlasBesovNorm_le_at.docstring:
**Independence of the atlas**: for two Besov atlases `A, A'`, `0 < s < r` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`
there is `C < ∞` with `‖f‖_{A, r, s, q} ≤ C ‖f‖_{A', r, s, q}` for all `f ∈ L_p(μ)`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.atlasBesovNorm.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.atlasBesovNorm
Manifold.BesovAtlas.atlasBesovNorm.docstring:
The **Besov quasi-norm of a Besov atlas**: the sum over the charts of the intrinsic
quasi-norms on `range I` of the chart pieces `(ψ_i f) ∘ κ_i⁻¹`, with differences of order `r`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.MemAtlasBoundaryBeso.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.MemAtlasBoundaryBesov
Manifold.BesovAtlas.MemAtlasBoundaryBeso.docstring:
The **Besov space of the boundary** for a Besov atlas: `g : M → ℂ` whose boundary pieces agree
almost everywhere with functions on `H₀` of finite Besov quasi-norm of order `⌊s⌋ + 1`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.MemAtlasBesov.modNor.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.MemAtlasBesov.modNormOn_pieceLp_lt_top_of_memAtlasBesov
Manifold.BesovAtlas.MemAtlasBesov.modNor.docstring:
**The pieces of `f ∈ B^s_{p,q}` have finite intrinsic quasi-norms** of every order `r > s` on
`range I`.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.MemAtlasBesov.finset.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.MemAtlasBesov.finsetSum
Manifold.BesovAtlas.MemAtlasBesov.finset.docstring: `B^s_{p,q}` of an atlas is closed under finite sums.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.MemAtlasBesov.add.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.MemAtlasBesov.add
Manifold.BesovAtlas.MemAtlasBesov.add.docstring: `B^s_{p,q}` of an atlas is closed under addition.

Manifold.BesovAtlas.MemAtlasBesov.name: Manifold.BesovAtlas.MemAtlasBesov
Manifold.BesovAtlas.MemAtlasBesov.docstring:
The **Besov space of a Besov atlas**: `f ∈ L_p(μ)` with a finite Besov quasi-norm of order
`⌊s⌋ + 1`.

LipschitzOnWith.euclideanHausdorffMeasur.name: LipschitzOnWith.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_pow_mul
LipschitzOnWith.euclideanHausdorffMeasur.docstring:
**Lipschitz maps and the Euclidean Hausdorff measure**: a map that is `K`-Lipschitz on `s`
increases `μHE[d]` by at most the factor `K^d`, `μHE[d] (f '' s) ≤ K^d μHE[d] s`. This is
Mathlib's `LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le` for the normalised measure `μHE[d]`, a
fixed multiple of `μH[d]`.

LineDeriv.lineDerivOp_iteratedLineDerivO.name: LineDeriv.lineDerivOp_iteratedLineDerivOp_comm_of
LineDeriv.lineDerivOp_iteratedLineDerivO.docstring:
If directional derivatives commute pairwise, `∂_a ∂_b x = ∂_b ∂_a x`, then a directional
derivative commutes with every iterated one: `∂_a ∂^v x = ∂^v ∂_a x`.

Interval.zero_add_two_pow_mul_eq_one.name: Interval.zero_add_two_pow_mul_eq_one
Interval.zero_add_two_pow_mul_eq_one.docstring: `[0, 1]` is the union of the `2^k` intervals of length `2^(-k)` starting at `0`.

Interval.two_pow_mul_inv_div_sq_pow_mul_.name: Interval.two_pow_mul_inv_div_sq_pow_mul_le
Interval.two_pow_mul_inv_div_sq_pow_mul_.docstring:
**The constant of the derivative at the step `δ = L / r²`**: for `r ≥ 1`, `L > 0` and
`a ≤ b`, `2^r δ^(-r) a ≤ L^(-r) 2^r r^(2r) b`, since `δ^(-1) = r² L^(-1)`.

Interval.two_pow_le_two_pow_mul_one_add.name: Interval.two_pow_le_two_pow_mul_one_add
Interval.two_pow_le_two_pow_mul_one_add.docstring: The constant of the inverse inequality is at least `2^r`.

Interval.tsum_localMass_ppFun_le.name: Interval.tsum_localMass_ppFun_le
Interval.tsum_localMass_ppFun_le.docstring: The local masses of a piecewise polynomial add up to at most `‖u‖_p^p`.

Interval.top_le_span_shiftedPow.name: Interval.top_le_span_shiftedPow
Interval.top_le_span_shiftedPow.docstring: The shifted powers span the polynomials of degree `< r`.

Interval.top_le_span_bsplineVec.name: Interval.top_le_span_bsplineVec
Interval.top_le_span_bsplineVec.docstring:
**The B-splines on `[0, 1)` span the polynomials of degree `< r`**: every shifted power is a
combination of them, by induction along the triangular form.

Interval.sum_sum_localMass_le.name: Interval.sum_sum_localMass_le
Interval.sum_sum_localMass_le.docstring:
**Bounded overlap**: summing the local masses of `r + 1` consecutive pieces over all starting
pieces counts each piece at most `r + 1` times,
`∑_{n < 2^j} ∑_{l ≤ r} ∫_{I_{j,n+l}} |u|^p ≤ (r + 1) ‖u‖_p^p`.

Interval.sum_range_eq_first_add.name: Interval.sum_range_eq_first_add
Interval.sum_range_eq_first_add.docstring: Splitting off the first term of a sum over `range r`, `r ≥ 1`.

Interval.sum_range_eq_add_last.name: Interval.sum_range_eq_add_last
Interval.sum_range_eq_add_last.docstring: Splitting off the last term of a sum over `range r`, `r ≥ 1`.

Interval.sum_range_choose_succ_le.name: Interval.sum_range_choose_succ_le
Interval.sum_range_choose_succ_le.docstring:
`∑_{k=1}^r C(r, k) ≤ 2^r`, written with the index `k + 1` for `k < r`: the full sum
`∑_{k=0}^r C(r, k)` is `2^r` (Mathlib's `Nat.sum_range_choose`).

Interval.sum_polyPairing_smul_dualPoly.name: Interval.sum_polyPairing_smul_dualPoly
Interval.sum_polyPairing_smul_dualPoly.docstring: **Expansion in the dual basis**: `P = ∑_i ⟨P, b_i⟩ d_i` for every `P` of degree `< r`.

Interval.sum_localMass_ppFun_le.name: Interval.sum_localMass_ppFun_le
Interval.sum_localMass_ppFun_le.docstring:
The local masses of a piecewise polynomial of level `j`, summed over `n < 2^j`, are at most
`‖u‖_p^p`.

Interval.sum_lintegral_window_le.name: Interval.sum_lintegral_window_le
Interval.sum_lintegral_window_le.docstring:
**Bounded overlap of the windows**: the windows `[(i + 1 - r) 2^(-k), (i + 1) 2^(-k)]`,
`i < N`, cover every point at most `r` times: `∑_i ∫_{W_i} G ≤ r ∫ G`.

Interval.sum_le_lintegral_Icc.name: Interval.sum_le_lintegral_Icc
Interval.sum_le_lintegral_Icc.docstring:
**Integrals over a union of intervals, reverse inequality**: for measurable `G` and `L ≥ 0`,
`∑_{n < m} ∫_{[u + nL, u + (n+1)L]} G ≤ ∫_{[u, u + mL]} G`, the intervals meeting in single
points.

Interval.sum_eLpNorm_sub_qiPieces_le.name: Interval.sum_eLpNorm_sub_qiPieces_le
Interval.sum_eLpNorm_sub_qiPieces_le.docstring:
**Summing the local errors of the quasi-interpolant**: let `F` be measurable and integrable on
the intervals `I_{k,m}`, `m < N`, and let `s ⊆ {0, …, N - 1}`. If on the window `W_i` of every
`i ∈ s` some polynomial `T` of degree `< r` has `‖F - T‖_{L_p(W_i)}^p ≤ ∫_{W_i} H`, then
`∑_{i ∈ s} ‖F - Q_k F‖_{L_p(I_{k,i})}^p ≤ C_q^p r ∫ H` with `C_q = 1 + r M_N C_b r M²`, since the
windows overlap at most `r` times (`Interval.sum_lintegral_window_le`).

Interval.sum_bcoord.name: Interval.sum_bcoord
Interval.sum_bcoord.docstring: **Expansion in the B-spline basis**: `P = ∑_{j < r} a_j β_j`.

Interval.sub_steklovSmooth_eq.name: Interval.sub_steklovSmooth_eq
Interval.sub_steklovSmooth_eq.docstring:
**`f - S_δ f` is an averaged difference**:
`f - S_δ f = (-1)^r avg^r_{h} Δ_h^r f` at step `0`.

Interval.sub_eq_jumpCoeff.name: Interval.sub_eq_jumpCoeff
Interval.sub_eq_jumpCoeff.docstring:
The jump at a knot: `P_m - P_{m-1} = c_m (X - ξ_m)^(r-1)`, since `(X - ξ)^(r-1)` is monic of
degree `r - 1`.

Interval.stripBound.name: Interval.stripBound
Interval.stripBound.docstring:
The **strip function** of the inverse estimate: `c M_n` at the points `x` of the strip
`[(n + 1) 2^(-j) - rh, (n + 1) 2^(-j))` left of the right end of the dyadic interval
`I_{j,n}` containing `x`, and `0` elsewhere.

Interval.step_div_sq_bounds.name: Interval.step_div_sq_bounds
Interval.step_div_sq_bounds.docstring:
**The step `δ = L / r²` of the smoothing**: for `r ≥ 1` and `L > 0`, `δ > 0`, `rδ ≤ L` and
`r (rδ) = L`.

Interval.stepRegion_eq_diffStepSet.name: Interval.stepRegion_eq_diffStepSet
Interval.stepRegion_eq_diffStepSet.docstring:
**The step region is a step set**: `J(m, t) = [0, 1]_{mt}` (`Rd.diffStepSet`), since `x + lt`,
`l ≤ m`, lies between `x` and `x + mt`.

Interval.stepRegion.name: Interval.stepRegion
Interval.stepRegion.docstring:
The **step region** of a difference of order `m` and step `t`: the points `x ∈ [0, 1]` with
`x + mt ∈ [0, 1]`, for `t` of either sign.

Interval.steklov_sub.name: Interval.steklov_sub
Interval.steklov_sub.docstring: Steklov averages are additive on continuous functions.

Interval.steklov_fwdDiff.name: Interval.steklov_fwdDiff
Interval.steklov_fwdDiff.docstring: Steklov averages commute with forward differences.

Interval.steklovSmooth.name: Interval.steklovSmooth
Interval.steklovSmooth.docstring: The **Steklov smoothing** `S_δ f = ∑_{k=1}^r (-1)^(k+1) C(r,k) M_{kδ}^r f`.

Interval.steklovIter_fwdDiff.name: Interval.steklovIter_fwdDiff
Interval.steklovIter_fwdDiff.docstring: Iterated Steklov averages commute with forward differences.

Interval.steklov.name: Interval.steklov
Interval.steklov.docstring: The **Steklov average** `M_η g(x) = η^(-1) ∫_0^η g(x + τ) dτ`.

Interval.splineStripConst_mul_le.name: Interval.splineStripConst_mul_le
Interval.splineStripConst_mul_le.docstring:
The local estimate for splines in dyadic form: for `j ≤ k` and `0 ≤ h ≤ 2^(-k)`,
`G (rh (r + 1))^(1/p) B ≤ C 2^(-(k-j)(r - 1 + 1/p)) B`.

Interval.splineStripConst_mul_eq.name: Interval.splineStripConst_mul_eq
Interval.splineStripConst_mul_eq.docstring:
The bound of the local estimate in terms of `2^j h`:
`G (rh (r + 1))^(1/p) = C (2^j h)^(r - 1 + 1/p)`.

Interval.splineStripConst.name: Interval.splineStripConst
Interval.splineStripConst.docstring:
The constant of the pointwise bound,
`G = 2 r 2^r K (r 2^j h)^(r-1) 2^(j/p)`.

Interval.splineSpace_zero.name: Interval.splineSpace_zero
Interval.splineSpace_zero.docstring:
**At level `0` the splines are the polynomials of degree `< r`**: there are no interior
knots.

Interval.splineSpace_mono.name: Interval.splineSpace_mono
Interval.splineSpace_mono.docstring: The spline spaces increase with the level.

Interval.splineSpace.name: Interval.splineSpace
Interval.splineSpace.docstring:
The space `S_k` of **splines of order `r`** on the dyadic grid of level `k` in `L_p[0, 1]`:
the classes of piecewise polynomials of level `k` and degree `< r` with spline joins.

Interval.splineScheme.name: Interval.splineScheme
Interval.splineScheme.docstring:
The **scheme of dyadic splines** of order `r` in `L_p[0, 1]`: `{0}` at complexity `0` and
`S_{⌊log₂ n⌋}` at complexity `n ≥ 1`.

Interval.splineModulusData.name: Interval.splineModulusData
Interval.splineModulusData.docstring:
The modulus `ω_r(f, 2^(-k), [0, 1])_p` is compatible with the scheme of dyadic splines of
order `r`, with inverse order `θ = r - 1 + 1/p` and Jackson's inequality at every level.

Interval.splineJoins_zero.name: Interval.splineJoins_zero
Interval.splineJoins_zero.docstring: The zero pieces have spline joins.

Interval.splineJoins_bsplinePieces.name: Interval.splineJoins_bsplinePieces
Interval.splineJoins_bsplinePieces.docstring: **The B-splines have spline joins** at the interior knots of `[0, 1]`.

Interval.splineInverseConst_ne_top.name: Interval.splineInverseConst_ne_top
Interval.splineInverseConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of the inverse inequality for splines is finite.

Interval.splineInverseConst.name: Interval.splineInverseConst
Interval.splineInverseConst.docstring:
The constant of the inverse inequality for splines,
`2 r 2^r K r^(r-1) (r (r + 1))^(1/p)`.

Interval.shiftedPow.name: Interval.shiftedPow
Interval.shiftedPow.docstring: The shifted powers as elements of the polynomials of degree `< r`.

Interval.rpow_strip_mul_eq.name: Interval.rpow_strip_mul_eq
Interval.rpow_strip_mul_eq.docstring: **The strip constant**: `(A 2^(j/p))^p (r h) = A^p r (2^j h)`.

Interval.rpow_piece_mul_le.name: Interval.rpow_piece_mul_le
Interval.rpow_piece_mul_le.docstring:
**The gain inside the pieces**: for `σ = 2^j h ≤ 1` and `m ≥ 1`,
`(K σ^m 2^(j/p))^p 2^(-j) ≤ K^p σ`, since `σ^(mp) ≤ σ^p ≤ σ`.

Interval.qiWindow_subset.name: Interval.qiWindow_subset
