Interval.qiWindow_subset.docstring: The window lies in `[(i + 1 - r) 2^(-k), (i + 1) 2^(-k)]`, with real subtraction.

Interval.qiWindow.name: Interval.qiWindow
Interval.qiWindow.docstring:
The window `W_i = [(i + 1 - r) 2^(-k), (i + 1) 2^(-k)]` (truncated at `0`) of the
quasi-interpolant on `I_{k,i}`.

Interval.qiPieces_mem.name: Interval.qiPieces_mem
Interval.qiPieces_mem.docstring: The quasi-interpolant has pieces of degree `< r`.

Interval.qiPieces_join.name: Interval.qiPieces_join
Interval.qiPieces_join.docstring: **The quasi-interpolant has spline joins at every knot** `m 2^(-k)`, `m ≥ 1`.

Interval.qiPieces.name: Interval.qiPieces
Interval.qiPieces.docstring: The pieces of the **quasi-interpolant** `Q_k g = ∑_n λ_n(g) N_r(2^k x - n)`.

Interval.qiIdx.name: Interval.qiIdx
Interval.qiIdx.docstring: The indices `-r < n < N` of the B-splines of level `k` that meet `[0, N 2^(-k))`.

Interval.qiCoeff_eq_sum.name: Interval.qiCoeff_eq_sum
Interval.qiCoeff_eq_sum.docstring:
**The quasi-interpolant coefficients are combinations of the local coefficients**:
`λ_n(g) = ∑_i c_i(g) β_{n,i}` with the coefficients `c_i(g)` of the local projection on `J(n)` and
the B-spline coefficients `β_{n,i}` of the rescaled dual polynomials.

Interval.qiCoeff_eq_bcoord.name: Interval.qiCoeff_eq_bcoord
Interval.qiCoeff_eq_bcoord.docstring:
The quasi-interpolant coefficient as a coordinate on the unit interval of `J(n)`:
`λ_n(g) = a_{max(n,0) - n}(Π g((· + max(n, 0)) 2^(-k)))`.

Interval.qiCoeff_add_const_mul.name: Interval.qiCoeff_add_const_mul
Interval.qiCoeff_add_const_mul.docstring: **The quasi-interpolant coefficients are linear** on functions integrable on `J(n)`.

Interval.qiCoeff.name: Interval.qiCoeff
Interval.qiCoeff.docstring:
The **quasi-interpolant coefficients** `λ_n(g) = c_n(Π_{k, J(n)} g(· 2^(-k)))`, with
`J(n) = I_{k, max(n, 0)}`.

Interval.qiBasisPoly.name: Interval.qiBasisPoly
Interval.qiBasisPoly.docstring:
The dual polynomial `d_i` of the interval `I_{k,m}` in the coordinate `y = 2^k x`, so that
the rescaled local projection is `∑_i c_i(g) d_i(y - m)` (`Interval.locProjScaled_eq_sum`).

Interval.ppSpace_mono.name: Interval.ppSpace_mono
Interval.ppSpace_mono.docstring: The spaces of piecewise polynomials increase with the level.

Interval.ppSpace.name: Interval.ppSpace
Interval.ppSpace.docstring: The space `V_k` of **piecewise polynomials of level `k` and degree `< r`** in `L_p[0, 1]`.

Interval.ppScheme.name: Interval.ppScheme
Interval.ppScheme.docstring:
The **scheme of dyadic piecewise polynomials** of degree `< r` in `L_p[0, 1]`: `{0}` at
complexity `0` and `V_{⌊log₂ n⌋}` at complexity `n ≥ 1`.

Interval.ppProjConst_ne_top.name: Interval.ppProjConst_ne_top
Interval.ppProjConst_ne_top.docstring: The bound of the projections is finite.

Interval.ppProjConst.name: Interval.ppProjConst
Interval.ppProjConst.docstring: The bound of the projections onto piecewise polynomials, `r M²`.

Interval.ppFun_zero.name: Interval.ppFun_zero
Interval.ppFun_zero.docstring: The piecewise polynomials of level `k` with zero pieces vanish.

Interval.ppFun_sum.name: Interval.ppFun_sum
Interval.ppFun_sum.docstring: Piecewise polynomials are additive in the pieces, for finite sums.

Interval.ppFun_refine_eq.name: Interval.ppFun_refine_eq
Interval.ppFun_refine_eq.docstring:
**Refinement of piecewise polynomials, everywhere**: the pieces `Q_{⌊n/2⌋}` of level `k + 1`
give the same function as the pieces `Q_n` of level `k`, on all of `ℝ`.

Interval.ppFun_refine.name: Interval.ppFun_refine
Interval.ppFun_refine.docstring:
**Refinement**: a piecewise polynomial of level `k` is one of level `k + 1` with the pieces
`Q_{⌊n/2⌋}`, almost everywhere on `[0, 1]` (`Interval.ppFun_refine_eq` holds everywhere).

Interval.ppFun_locProj_ppFun.name: Interval.ppFun_locProj_ppFun
Interval.ppFun_locProj_ppFun.docstring:
**The local projections reproduce piecewise polynomials exactly**:
`P_j (ppFun j Q) = ppFun j Q` as functions, for pieces of degree `< r`.

Interval.ppFun_eq_polyFun.name: Interval.ppFun_eq_polyFun
Interval.ppFun_eq_polyFun.docstring:
On `I_{k,m}` a piecewise polynomial of level `k` is a polynomial: `Q_m` for `m < 2^k`, and
`0` for the intervals beyond `[0, 1)`.

Interval.ppFun_const_mul.name: Interval.ppFun_const_mul
Interval.ppFun_const_mul.docstring: Piecewise polynomials are homogeneous in the pieces.

Interval.ppFun_congr.name: Interval.ppFun_congr
Interval.ppFun_congr.docstring: Piecewise polynomials only depend on the pieces in `[0, 1)`.

Interval.ppFun_add.name: Interval.ppFun_add
Interval.ppFun_add.docstring: Piecewise polynomials are additive in the pieces.

Interval.pow_mem_degreeLT.name: Interval.pow_mem_degreeLT
Interval.pow_mem_degreeLT.docstring:
The power of a polynomial of degree `≤ 1` to the `r - 1` has degree `< r` (Mathlib's
`Polynomial.natDegree_pow_le_of_le`).

Interval.polyPairing_separatingLeft.name: Interval.polyPairing_separatingLeft
Interval.polyPairing_separatingLeft.docstring:
**The pairing separates points**: if `∫_0^1 P Q = 0` for all `Q`, then `P = 0`; take
`Q = P̄`, so that `∫_0^1 |P|² = 0`.

Interval.polyPairing.name: Interval.polyPairing
Interval.polyPairing.docstring: The **pairing** `⟨P, Q⟩ = ∫_0^1 P Q` of polynomials of degree `< r`, a bilinear form.

Interval.polyFun_qiPieces_sub.name: Interval.polyFun_qiPieces_sub
Interval.polyFun_qiPieces_sub.docstring:
**The error of the quasi-interpolant through a polynomial**: on `I_{k,i}`,
`g - Q_k g = (g - T) - Q_k(g - T)` for every polynomial `T` of degree `< r`.

Interval.polyFun_qiPieces_of_eq.name: Interval.polyFun_qiPieces_of_eq
Interval.polyFun_qiPieces_of_eq.docstring:
**Local reproduction of polynomials**: if `g = T` on the intervals `J(n)`, `i - r < n ≤ i`,
for a polynomial `T` of degree `< r`, then `Q_k g = T` on `I_{k,i}`: the local projections
reproduce `T`, so the coefficients are those of `T`.

Interval.polyFun_qiPieces_of_coeff.name: Interval.polyFun_qiPieces_of_coeff
Interval.polyFun_qiPieces_of_coeff.docstring:
**The quasi-interpolant from its coefficients**: if the coefficients `λ_n(g)`,
`i - r < n ≤ i`, are the B-spline coefficients `c_n` of `T(· 2^(-k))` for a polynomial `T` of
degree `< r`, then `Q_k g = T` on `I_{k,i}`, by Marsden's identity for `T(· 2^(-k))` on
`[i, i + 1)`.

Interval.polyFun_qiPieces_eq_sum_Ioc.name: Interval.polyFun_qiPieces_eq_sum_Ioc
Interval.polyFun_qiPieces_eq_sum_Ioc.docstring: On `I_{k,i}` the quasi-interpolant is the sum over the B-splines `i - r < n ≤ i`.

Interval.polyFun_qiPieces.name: Interval.polyFun_qiPieces
Interval.polyFun_qiPieces.docstring: The values of the quasi-interpolant on `I_{k,m}`: `Q_k g(x) = ∑_n λ_n(g) N_r(2^k x - n)`.

Interval.polyFun_map_conj.name: Interval.polyFun_map_conj
Interval.polyFun_map_conj.docstring:
The polynomial `P̄` with conjugate coefficients takes the values `P̄(x) = conj P(x)` at real
points.

Interval.polyFun_locProj_of_eqOn.name: Interval.polyFun_locProj_of_eqOn
Interval.polyFun_locProj_of_eqOn.docstring:
**Polynomials are reproduced**: if `g = Q` on `I_{j,m}` with `Q` of degree `< r`, then the
local projection of `g` on `I_{j,m}` is `Q`.

Interval.polyFun_locProj.name: Interval.polyFun_locProj
Interval.polyFun_locProj.docstring: The values of the local projection, `Π g(x) = ∑_i c_i d_i(2^j x - m)`.

Interval.polyFun_eq_sum_dualPoly.name: Interval.polyFun_eq_sum_dualPoly
Interval.polyFun_eq_sum_dualPoly.docstring: The expansion at a point: `P(x) = ∑_i (∫_0^1 P b_i) d_i(x)`.

Interval.polyFun_eq_sum_bsplineCoef.name: Interval.polyFun_eq_sum_bsplineCoef
Interval.polyFun_eq_sum_bsplineCoef.docstring:
**Polynomials are combinations of B-splines** (Marsden's identity): for `P` of degree `< r`
and `x ∈ [i, i + 1)`, `P(x) = ∑_{j < r} c_{i-j}(P) N_r(x - (i - j))`, with the coefficients
`c_n(P)` independent of the interval.

Interval.polyFun_eq_add_sum_jumps.name: Interval.polyFun_eq_add_sum_jumps
Interval.polyFun_eq_add_sum_jumps.docstring:
**A spline across the knots**: let `u` be the polynomial `P_m` on `I_{j,m}` for `m < N`, with
spline joins below `N`. For `0 ≤ x ≤ y < N 2^(-j)` with `⌊2^j y⌋ ≤ ⌊2^j x⌋ + r`,
`u(y) = P_{n₀}(y) + ∑_{n₀ < m ≤ n₀ + r} c_m (y - ξ_m)_+^(r-1)`, `n₀ = ⌊2^j x⌋`.

Interval.polyFun_degreeLTEquiv_symm.name: Interval.polyFun_degreeLTEquiv_symm
Interval.polyFun_degreeLTEquiv_symm.docstring:
The value of the polynomial with coefficients `c`: `∑_i c_i x^i` (Mathlib's
`Polynomial.eval_eq_sum_degreeLTEquiv`).

Interval.polyFun_bsplinePieces.name: Interval.polyFun_bsplinePieces
Interval.polyFun_bsplinePieces.docstring: On `I_{k,m}` the pieces are the B-spline: `Q_m(x) = N_r(2^k x - n)`.

Interval.polyFun.name: Interval.polyFun
Interval.polyFun.docstring: The function `x ↦ P(x)` on `ℝ` of a complex polynomial `P`.

Interval.pairwise_disjoint_dyadicIco.name: Interval.pairwise_disjoint_dyadicIco
Interval.pairwise_disjoint_dyadicIco.docstring: The dyadic intervals of one level are pairwise disjoint.

Interval.norm_polyFun_degreeLTEquiv_symm.name: Interval.norm_polyFun_degreeLTEquiv_symm_le
Interval.norm_polyFun_degreeLTEquiv_symm.docstring: The value of a polynomial with coefficients `c` at `x ∈ [0, 1]` is at most `r ‖c‖`.

Interval.norm_higherDiff_polyFun_le.name: Interval.norm_higherDiff_polyFun_le
Interval.norm_higherDiff_polyFun_le.docstring:
**Differences of polynomials by derivatives**: if `|P^(m)| ≤ M` on `[y, y + mσ]` with
`σ ≥ 0`, then `|Δ_σ^m P(y)| ≤ σ^m M`. Induction on `m`: `Δ_σ^(m+1) P(y) = Δ_σ^m P(y + σ) -
Δ_σ^m P(y)`, and the mean value theorem (Mathlib's
`norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment'`) applies to `Δ_σ^m P` with derivative
`Δ_σ^m P'`.

Interval.natDegree_comp_affine_le.name: Interval.natDegree_comp_affine_le
Interval.natDegree_comp_affine_le.docstring:
**Affine changes of variable do not raise the degree**:
`deg P(u + v X) ≤ deg P`, since `deg (P ∘ Q) ≤ deg P · deg Q` (Mathlib's `natDegree_comp_le`).

Interval.natCast_div_two_pow_le.name: Interval.natCast_div_two_pow_le
Interval.natCast_div_two_pow_le.docstring:
`r 2^(-k) ≤ 1/4` for `k ≥ r + 2`: the windows of the quasi-interpolant have length at most
`1/4`.

Interval.natCast_add_one_sub_le.name: Interval.natCast_add_one_sub_le
Interval.natCast_add_one_sub_le.docstring: `i + 1 - r ≤ (i + 1 - r : ℕ)` in `ℝ`, the natural subtraction truncating at `0`.

Interval.monoBasis.name: Interval.monoBasis
Interval.monoBasis.docstring: The **monomial basis** `b_i = X^i` of the polynomials of degree `< r`.

Interval.mem_stepRegion.name: Interval.mem_stepRegion
Interval.mem_stepRegion.docstring: `x` lies in the step region iff `x` and `x + mt` lie in `[0, 1]`.

Interval.mem_splineScheme_two_pow.name: Interval.mem_splineScheme_two_pow
Interval.mem_splineScheme_two_pow.docstring: The approximants of complexity `2^k` are the splines of level `k`.

Interval.mem_splineScheme.name: Interval.mem_splineScheme
Interval.mem_splineScheme.docstring: The approximants of complexity `n ≥ 1` are the splines of level `⌊log₂ n⌋`.

Interval.mem_ppScheme.name: Interval.mem_ppScheme
Interval.mem_ppScheme.docstring: The approximants of complexity `n ≥ 1` are the piecewise polynomials of level `⌊log₂ n⌋`.

Interval.mem_dyadicIco_floor.name: Interval.mem_dyadicIco_floor
Interval.mem_dyadicIco_floor.docstring: A point of `[0, 1)` lies in the dyadic interval `I_{k, ⌊2^k x⌋}`, of index `< 2^k`.

Interval.memLp_polyFun.name: Interval.memLp_polyFun
Interval.memLp_polyFun.docstring: Polynomials lie in `L_p` of a bounded interval.

Interval.localMass_le_sum_range.name: Interval.localMass_le_sum_range
Interval.localMass_le_sum_range.docstring: One piece is counted in the local mass of `r + 1` consecutive pieces.

Interval.localMass.name: Interval.localMass
Interval.localMass.docstring: The **local mass** `∫_{I_{k,m}} |u|^p` of `u` on the dyadic interval `I_{k,m}`.

Interval.locProj_mem.name: Interval.locProj_mem
Interval.locProj_mem.docstring: The local projection has degree `< r`.

Interval.locProjScaled_mem.name: Interval.locProjScaled_mem
Interval.locProjScaled_mem.docstring: The rescaled local projections have degree `< r`.

Interval.locProjScaled_eq_sum.name: Interval.locProjScaled_eq_sum
Interval.locProjScaled_eq_sum.docstring: The rescaled local projection in terms of the local coefficients.

Interval.locProjScaled.name: Interval.locProjScaled
Interval.locProjScaled.docstring: The local projection on `I_{k,m}` in the coordinate `y = 2^k x`.

Interval.locProj.name: Interval.locProj
Interval.locProj.docstring: The **local projection** of `g` on `I_{j,m}`, the polynomial `∑_i c_i d_i(2^j x - m)`.

Interval.locCoeff.name: Interval.locCoeff
Interval.locCoeff.docstring:
The coefficients of the local projection of `g` on `I_{j,m}`,
`c_i = 2^j ∫_{I_{j,m}} g(y) b_i(2^j y - m) dy`.

Interval.lintegral_sub_ppFun_le_sum.name: Interval.lintegral_sub_ppFun_le_sum
Interval.lintegral_sub_ppFun_le_sum.docstring: The `p`-th power of the error over `[0, 1]` is the sum over the dyadic intervals.

Interval.lintegral_stripBound_le.name: Interval.lintegral_stripBound_le
Interval.lintegral_stripBound_le.docstring:
**Integral of the strip function**: the strips have width `rh`, so
`∫_{[0,1]} (strip function) ≤ c rh ∑_{n < 2^j} M_n`.

Interval.lintegral_localBound_le.name: Interval.lintegral_localBound_le
Interval.lintegral_localBound_le.docstring: **Integral of a local bound**: `∫_{[0,1]} c M_{⌊2^j x⌋} dx ≤ c 2^(-j) ∑_{n < 2^j} M_n`.

Interval.lintegral_Icc_le_sum_dyadicIco.name: Interval.lintegral_Icc_le_sum_dyadicIco
Interval.lintegral_Icc_le_sum_dyadicIco.docstring: **`[0, 1]` against the dyadic intervals**: `∫_{[0,1]} G ≤ ∑_{n < 2^k} ∫_{I_{k,n}} G`.

Interval.lintegral_Icc_le_sum.name: Interval.lintegral_Icc_le_sum
Interval.lintegral_Icc_le_sum.docstring:
**Integrals over a union of intervals**: `∫_{[u, u + mL]} G ≤ ∑_{n < m} ∫_{[u + nL, u + (n+1)L]} G`
for `L ≥ 0`.

Interval.lintegral_Icc_eq_dyadicIco.name: Interval.lintegral_Icc_eq_dyadicIco
Interval.lintegral_Icc_eq_dyadicIco.docstring:
The closed intervals `[0 + n 2^(-k), 0 + (n + 1) 2^(-k)]` of `Interval.lintegral_Icc_le_sum`
agree with the dyadic intervals up to a null set.

Interval.linearIndependent_X_add_C_pow.name: Interval.linearIndependent_X_add_C_pow
Interval.linearIndependent_X_add_C_pow.docstring:
**The shifted powers `(X + m)^(r-1)`, `m < r`, are linearly independent**: their
coefficients give the system `∑_m g_m m^e = 0`, `e < r`, with a Vandermonde matrix.

Interval.le_two_pow_mul_one_add.name: Interval.le_two_pow_mul_one_add
Interval.le_two_pow_mul_one_add.docstring: The constant of the inverse inequality dominates the local constant.

Interval.jumpCoeff.name: Interval.jumpCoeff
Interval.jumpCoeff.docstring:
The **jump coefficients** of pieces `P`: the coefficient of `X^(r-1)` in `P_m - P_{m-1}` at
the knots `0 < m < N`, and `0` elsewhere. With spline joins below `N`,
`P_m - P_{m-1} = c_m (X - ξ_m)^(r-1)` (`Interval.sub_eq_jumpCoeff`).

Interval.iteratedDeriv_steklovSmooth_eq_.name: Interval.iteratedDeriv_steklovSmooth_eq_sum_smul
Interval.iteratedDeriv_steklovSmooth_eq_.docstring:
**The derivative of the smoothing as a sum of functions**: for continuous `f : ℝ → ℂ`,
`(S_δ f)^(r) = ∑_{k=1}^r (-1)^(k+1) C(r, k) (kδ)^(-r) Δ_{kδ}^r f`
as an identity of functions `ℝ → ℂ` (`Interval.iteratedDeriv_steklovSmooth` at every point), written
with the index `k + 1` for `k < r` and as a sum `∑_k c_k • g_k`, the form to which the triangle
inequality in `L_p` applies.

Interval.iteratedDeriv_steklovSmooth.name: Interval.iteratedDeriv_steklovSmooth
Interval.iteratedDeriv_steklovSmooth.docstring:
**The derivative of order `r` of the smoothing is a combination of differences**:
`(S_δ f)^(r) = ∑_{k=1}^r (-1)^(k+1) C(r,k) (kδ)^(-r) Δ_{kδ}^r f`.

Interval.iteratedDeriv_steklovIter_add.name: Interval.iteratedDeriv_steklovIter_add
Interval.iteratedDeriv_steklovIter_add.docstring:
**The derivative of order `k` of an iterated Steklov average**:
`(M_η^(m+k) g)^(k) = η^(-k) M_η^m (Δ_η^k g)` for continuous `g`.

Interval.iteratedDeriv_steklovIter.name: Interval.iteratedDeriv_steklovIter
Interval.iteratedDeriv_steklovIter.docstring: **`(M_η^r g)^(r) = η^(-r) Δ_η^r g`** for continuous `g`.

Interval.iterate_derivative_mem_degreeLT.name: Interval.iterate_derivative_mem_degreeLT
Interval.iterate_derivative_mem_degreeLT.docstring: The derivatives of polynomials of degree `< r` have degree `< r`.

Interval.ite_mem_degreeLT.name: Interval.ite_mem_degreeLT
Interval.ite_mem_degreeLT.docstring: The piece `Q_m` (or `0` beyond `[0, 1)`) has degree `< r`.

Interval.isProbabilityMeasure_unitVol.name: Interval.isProbabilityMeasure_unitVol
Interval.isProbabilityMeasure_unitVol.docstring: Lebesgue measure on `[0, 1]` is a probability measure.

Interval.isPiecewisePoly_ppFun.name: Interval.isPiecewisePoly_ppFun
Interval.isPiecewisePoly_ppFun.docstring:
A piecewise polynomial on `[0, 1)`, extended by `0`, is a piecewise polynomial on
`[0, ∞)`.

Interval.interval_eLpNorm_comp_affine.name: Interval.interval_eLpNorm_comp_affine
Interval.interval_eLpNorm_comp_affine.docstring:
**Affine change of variables in `L_p`**: for `L > 0` and `p ≠ ∞`,
`‖g(u + L ·)‖_{L_p[α, β]} = L^(-1/p) ‖g‖_{L_p[u + Lα, u + Lβ]}`.

Interval.interval_approxError_le_of_cont.name: Interval.interval_approxError_le_of_continuous
Interval.interval_approxError_le_of_cont.docstring:
**From continuous functions to `L_p` by density**: a bound `E_n(g) ≤ C ω_r(g, 2^(-k))_p`
for every bounded continuous `g`, given by an approximant `u ∈ A_n` of `g`, holds for every
`f ∈ L_p[0, 1]`, `p < ∞`. The bounded continuous functions are dense in `L_p` (Mathlib's
`BoundedContinuousFunction.toLp_denseRange`), so `ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_of_dense`
applies.

Interval.intervalModulus_reflect.name: Interval.intervalModulus_reflect
Interval.intervalModulus_reflect.docstring: **Reflection**: `ω_r(f(a + b - ·), t, [a, b]) = ω_r(f, t, [a, b])`.

Interval.intervalModulus_eq_iSup_nonneg.name: Interval.intervalModulus_eq_iSup_nonneg
Interval.intervalModulus_eq_iSup_nonneg.docstring:
**The modulus on an interval through steps `h ≥ 0`**:
`ω_r(f, t, [a, b])_p = sup_{0 ≤ h ≤ t} ‖Δ_h^r f‖_{L_p[a, b - rh]}`, since the step `-h` gives the
norm of the step `h` (`Rd.eLpNorm_indicator_diffStepSet_neg`).

Interval.intervalModulus_congr_ae.name: Interval.intervalModulus_congr_ae
Interval.intervalModulus_congr_ae.docstring:
**The modulus depends only on the class in `L_p[a, b]`**: functions that agree almost
everywhere on `[a, b]` have the same modulus.

Interval.intervalModulus.name: Interval.intervalModulus
Interval.intervalModulus.docstring:
The **modulus of smoothness of order `r`** on `[a, b]` in `L_p`, the modulus on the set
`[a, b]` (`Rd.modulusOn`): `ω_r(f, t, [a, b])_p = sup_{|h| ≤ t} ‖Δ_h^r(f, ·, [a, b])‖_p`, with the
differences taken at the points `x` with `x, x + h, …, x + r h ∈ [a, b]`.

Interval.intervalLpModulus_anti.name: Interval.intervalLpModulus_anti
Interval.intervalLpModulus_anti.docstring: The modulus at the dyadic scales decreases with the level.

Interval.intervalLpModulus_add_le.name: Interval.intervalLpModulus_add_le
Interval.intervalLpModulus_add_le.docstring: The modulus of elements of `L_p[0, 1]` is subadditive.

Interval.intervalLpModulus.name: Interval.intervalLpModulus
Interval.intervalLpModulus.docstring:
The modulus of an element of `L_p[0, 1]` at the dyadic scale `2^(-k)`,
`ω_r(f, 2^(-k), [0, 1])_p`.

Interval.intervalJacksonConst_ne_top.name: Interval.intervalJacksonConst_ne_top
Interval.intervalJacksonConst_ne_top.docstring: The local Jackson constant is finite.

Interval.intervalJacksonConst.name: Interval.intervalJacksonConst
Interval.intervalJacksonConst.docstring: The constant of the local Jackson estimate, `1 + 2^r r^(2r)`.

Interval.integral_dyadicIco_eq.name: Interval.integral_dyadicIco_eq
Interval.integral_dyadicIco_eq.docstring:
**Change of variables** on a dyadic interval:
`2^j ∫_{I_{j,m}} φ = ∫_0^1 φ(t 2^(-j) + m 2^(-j))`.

Interval.integrableOn_polyFun_mul.name: Interval.integrableOn_polyFun_mul
Interval.integrableOn_polyFun_mul.docstring: The product of two polynomials is integrable on `[0, 1]`.

Interval.integrableOn_mul_monoBasis.name: Interval.integrableOn_mul_monoBasis
Interval.integrableOn_mul_monoBasis.docstring: The local integrands `g(y) b_i(2^j y - m)` are integrable on `I_{j,m}`.

Interval.integrableOn_dyadicIco_of_conti.name: Interval.integrableOn_dyadicIco_of_continuous
Interval.integrableOn_dyadicIco_of_conti.docstring: Continuous functions are integrable on the dyadic intervals.

Interval.higherDiff_succ.name: Interval.higherDiff_succ
Interval.higherDiff_succ.docstring: `Δ_h^(r+1) f(x) = Δ_h^r f(x + h) - Δ_h^r f(x)`.

Interval.higherDiff_reflect.name: Interval.higherDiff_reflect
Interval.higherDiff_reflect.docstring: **Reflection**: for `g(x) = f(c - x)`, `Δ_h^r g(x) = (-1)^r Δ_h^r f(c - x - r h)`.

Interval.higherDiff_polynomial.name: Interval.higherDiff_polynomial
Interval.higherDiff_polynomial.docstring:
**Differences of order `r` annihilate polynomials of degree `< r`**:
`Δ_h^r P = 0` for `P ∈ degreeLT ℂ r`.

Interval.higherDiff_eq_zero_of_isPiecewi.name: Interval.higherDiff_eq_zero_of_isPiecewisePoly
Interval.higherDiff_eq_zero_of_isPiecewi.docstring:
**Differences vanish inside a piece**: if `x, x + h, …, x + rh` lie in the dyadic interval of
`x`, then `Δ_h^r u(x) = 0`, since there `u` is a polynomial of degree `< r`.

Interval.higherDiff_eq_sum_smul.name: Interval.higherDiff_eq_sum_smul
Interval.higherDiff_eq_sum_smul.docstring:
`Δ_h^r f = ∑_{k=0}^r (-1)^(r-k) C(r,k) f(· + k h)`, as an identity of functions: a sum of
multiples of translates of `f`.

Interval.higherDiff_eq_sum_jumps.name: Interval.higherDiff_eq_sum_jumps
Interval.higherDiff_eq_sum_jumps.docstring:
**Differences of a spline are differences of its jumps**: on `[x, x + rh]` with
`x + rh < N 2^(-j)` and `h ≤ 2^(-j)`,
`Δ_h^r u(x) = ∑_{n₀ < m ≤ n₀ + r} c_m Δ_h^r (· - ξ_m)_+^(r-1)(x)`, since the piece has
`Δ_h^r P_{n₀} = 0` (`Interval.higherDiff_eq_add_sum_jumps` with `m = r`).

Interval.higherDiff_eq_of_mem_piece.name: Interval.higherDiff_eq_of_mem_piece
Interval.higherDiff_eq_of_mem_piece.docstring:
**Inside a piece a difference sees only the piece**: for `h ≥ 0` and `x ≥ 0`: if `u` agrees
with `P` on the dyadic interval `I_{k,n}` of `x`, `n = ⌊2^k x⌋`, and `x + mh` lies left of its
right end, then
`Δ_h^m u(x) = Δ_h^m P(x)`, since `x, x + h, …, x + mh` lie in `I_{k,n}`.

Interval.higherDiff_eq_add_sum_jumps.name: Interval.higherDiff_eq_add_sum_jumps
Interval.higherDiff_eq_add_sum_jumps.docstring:
**Differences of a spline: the piece plus the jumps**: for `m ≤ r`, `0 ≤ h ≤ 2^(-j)`,
`x ≥ 0` and `x + mh < N 2^(-j)`,
`Δ_h^m u(x) = Δ_h^m P_{n₀}(x) + ∑_{n₀ < l ≤ n₀ + r} c_l Δ_h^m (· - ξ_l)_+^(r-1)(x)`, with
`n₀ = ⌊2^j x⌋` (`Interval.polyFun_eq_add_sum_jumps` at every point `x + ih`).

Interval.hasDerivAt_steklov.name: Interval.hasDerivAt_steklov
Interval.hasDerivAt_steklov.docstring:
**Steklov averages gain a derivative**: `(M_η g)' = η^(-1) (g(· + η) - g)` for continuous
`g`.

Interval.hasDerivAt_polyFun.name: Interval.hasDerivAt_polyFun
Interval.hasDerivAt_polyFun.docstring: The derivative of a polynomial along the real line.

Interval.hasDerivAt_higherDiff_polyFun.name: Interval.hasDerivAt_higherDiff_polyFun
Interval.hasDerivAt_higherDiff_polyFun.docstring:
The derivative of a difference of a polynomial is the difference of its derivative:
`(Δ_σ^m P)' = Δ_σ^m P'`.

Interval.floor_two_pow_succ_div.name: Interval.floor_two_pow_succ_div
Interval.floor_two_pow_succ_div.docstring: The parent dyadic interval: `⌊2^k x⌋ = ⌊2^(k+1) x⌋ / 2`.

Interval.floor_eq_of_mem_dyadicIco.name: Interval.floor_eq_of_mem_dyadicIco
Interval.floor_eq_of_mem_dyadicIco.docstring: Floor of `2^k x` on a dyadic interval: `x ∈ I_{k,n}` gives `⌊2^k x⌋ = n`.

Interval.floor_add_mul_le.name: Interval.floor_add_mul_le
Interval.floor_add_mul_le.docstring:
**The points `x + i h` meet at most `r + 1` pieces**: for `x ≥ 0`, `h ≥ 0`, `2^j h ≤ 1` and
`i ≤ r`, `⌊2^j (x + i h)⌋ ≤ ⌊2^j x⌋ + r`.

Interval.finrank_degreeLT.name: Interval.finrank_degreeLT
Interval.finrank_degreeLT.docstring:
The polynomials of degree `< r` form a space of dimension `r` (with Mathlib's monomial basis
`Polynomial.degreeLT.basis`).

Interval.exists_window_poly.name: Interval.exists_window_poly
Interval.exists_window_poly.docstring:
**Approximation on a window**: if `‖g - T₀‖_{L_p[a,b]} ≤ (b - a)^r ‖D‖_{L_p[a,b]}` for some
polynomial `T₀` and `(b - a)^r ≤ c`, then
`‖F - T₀‖^p ≤ 2^(p-1) ∫_{[a,b]} (|F - g|^p + c^p |D|^p)`.

Interval.exists_taylor_pieces.name: Interval.exists_taylor_pieces
Interval.exists_taylor_pieces.docstring:
**Taylor polynomials on consecutive intervals**: let `g` have on every interval `[u, v]` a
polynomial `T` of degree `< r` with `‖g - T‖_{L_p[u, v]} ≤ (v - u)^r ‖D‖_{L_p[u, v]}`. For the
intervals `[a + nL, a + (n + 1)L]`, `n < N`, there are such polynomials `Q_n`, and every
measurable `S` equal to `Q_n` on the open intervals satisfies
`‖g - S‖_{L_p[a, a + NL]} ≤ L^r ‖D‖_{L_p[a, a + NL]}`: the `p`-th powers of the local errors add
up.

Interval.exists_sum_eLpNorm_sub_qiPieces.name: Interval.exists_sum_eLpNorm_sub_qiPieces_le_of_taylor
Interval.exists_sum_eLpNorm_sub_qiPieces.docstring:
**Jackson's estimate for splines from one smoothing**: there is `A < ∞` such that for every
level `k`, every `N`, every set `s ⊆ {0, …, N - 1}` of cells whose windows lie in `[a, b]`, every
measurable `u` integrable on the dyadic intervals `I_{k,m}`, `m < N`, and all measurable `g, D`
such that `g` has the Taylor polynomials `‖g - T‖_{L_p[v,w]} ≤ (w - v)^r ‖D‖_{L_p[v,w]}`,
`∑_{i ∈ s} ‖u - Q_k u‖_{L_p(I_{k,i})}^p ≤ (A (‖u - g‖_{L_p[a,b]} + c ‖D‖_{L_p[a,b]}))^p` with
`c = (r 2^(-k))^r`. On every window a Taylor polynomial of `g` approximates `u`
(`Interval.exists_qiWindow_poly`), the windows overlap at most `r` times
(`Interval.sum_eLpNorm_sub_qiPieces_le`), and `a^p + b^p ≤ (a + b)^p`.

Interval.exists_right_smoothing.name: Interval.exists_right_smoothing
Interval.exists_right_smoothing.docstring:
**Smoothing on a right part**: the same on `[b - w, b]`, by the reflection `x ↦ b - x`, which
preserves the modulus on `[0, b]` (`Interval.intervalModulus_reflect`).

Interval.exists_qiWindow_poly.name: Interval.exists_qiWindow_poly
Interval.exists_qiWindow_poly.docstring:
**A polynomial on a window from a smoothing**: if `g` has the Taylor polynomials
`‖g - T‖_{L_p[u,v]} ≤ (v - u)^r ‖D‖_{L_p[u,v]}` on all intervals, then on the window `W_i` some
polynomial `T` of degree `< r` satisfies
`‖F - T‖_{L_p(W_i)}^p ≤ 2^(p-1) ∫_{W_i} (|F - g|^p + c^p |D|^p)` with `c = (r 2^(-k))^r`, since
`W_i` has length at most `r 2^(-k)`.

Interval.exists_ppFun_approx_of_taylor.name: Interval.exists_ppFun_approx_of_taylor
Interval.exists_ppFun_approx_of_taylor.docstring:
**Piecewise Taylor approximation on the two halves of `[0, 1]`**: let `g_L` and `g_R` have
Taylor polynomials of degree `< r` on every interval, with remainders controlled by `D_L` and
`D_R` as in `Interval.exists_taylor_pieces`. For every measurable `u` and every `k` there is a
piecewise polynomial `S` of level `k + 1` and degree `< r`, made of Taylor polynomials of `g_L`
on `[0, 1/2]` and of `g_R` on `[1/2, 1]`, with
`‖u - S‖_{L_p[0, 1]} ≤ (‖u - g_L‖_{L_p[0, 1/2]} + L^r ‖D_L‖_{L_p[0, 1/2]}) + (‖u - g_R‖_{L_p[1/2, 1]} + L^r ‖D_R‖_{L_p[1/2, 1]})`,
`L = 2^(-(k+1))`. The point `1/2` is a knot of level `k + 1`.

Interval.exists_norm_ppFun_le.name: Interval.exists_norm_ppFun_le
Interval.exists_norm_ppFun_le.docstring:
**Piecewise polynomials are bounded**: for every level `k` and pieces `Q` there is `M` with
`‖ppFun k Q x‖ ≤ M` for all `x ∈ ℝ`, since each piece is a polynomial on a subinterval of the
compact interval `[0, 1]`.

Interval.exists_left_smoothing.name: Interval.exists_left_smoothing
Interval.exists_left_smoothing.docstring:
**Smoothing on a left part**: for continuous `F`, `r ≥ 1`, a scale `L > 0` and `w + L ≤ b`,
the Steklov smoothing `g = S_δ F`, `δ = L/r²`, and its derivative `D = g^(r)` satisfy
`‖F - g‖_{L_p[0,w]} ≤ ω_r(F, L, [0, b])_p` and
`‖D‖_{L_p[0,w]} ≤ L^(-r) 2^r r^(2r) ω_r(F, L, [0, b])_p`, and for every `u ≤ v` there is `T` of
degree `< r` with `‖g - T‖_{L_p[u,v]} ≤ (v - u)^r ‖D‖_{L_p[u,v]}` (Taylor).

Interval.exists_inverse_splineScheme.name: Interval.exists_inverse_splineScheme
Interval.exists_inverse_splineScheme.docstring:
**The inverse inequality for dyadic splines**, of order `θ = r - 1 + 1/p`: there is
`C_B < ∞` with `ω_r(a, 2^(-k), [0, 1])_p ≤ C_B 2^(-(k-j)θ) ‖a‖_p` for every spline `a` of order `r`
and level `j` (and `k - j` truncated at `0`).

Interval.exists_enorm_polyFun_le_of_fint.name: Interval.exists_enorm_polyFun_le_of_fintype
Interval.exists_enorm_polyFun_le_of_fint.docstring: A finite family of polynomials is bounded on `[0, 1]`.

Interval.exists_enorm_linearMap_le_eLpNo.name: Interval.exists_enorm_linearMap_le_eLpNorm
Interval.exists_enorm_linearMap_le_eLpNo.docstring:
**Linear maps of polynomials are bounded by the norm**: let `Φ` be a linear map of the
polynomials that preserves the degree bound `< r`, and `[α, β]` an interval of positive length.
There is `K` with `|Φ P(x)| ≤ K ‖P‖_{L_p[α, β]}` for all `x ∈ [0, 1]` and `P` of degree `< r`. In
coordinates `Φ` is a linear map of `ℂ^r`, hence bounded, and the coordinates are bounded by the
`L_p` norm, since `coeffToLp` is injective on a space of finite dimension.

Interval.exists_enorm_le_eLpNorm.name: Interval.exists_enorm_le_eLpNorm
Interval.exists_enorm_le_eLpNorm.docstring:
**Equivalence of norms on polynomials**: for an interval `[α, β]` of positive length there
is `K` with `|P(x)| ≤ K ‖P‖_{L_p[α, β]}` for all `x ∈ [0, 1]` and `P` of degree `< r`, the
case `Φ = id` of `Interval.exists_enorm_linearMap_le_eLpNorm`.

Interval.exists_enorm_bcoord_le.name: Interval.exists_enorm_bcoord_le
Interval.exists_enorm_bcoord_le.docstring:
**The B-spline coordinates are bounded functionals**: there is `C` with
`|a_j(R)| ≤ C ‖R‖_{L_p[0,1]}` for every polynomial `R` of degree `< r` (finite dimension).

Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_qi_le_of_tay.name: Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_qi_le_of_taylor
Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_qi_le_of_tay.docstring:
**Jackson's estimate for splines from two smoothings**: there is `A < ∞` such that for
`k ≥ r + 2`, every measurable `u` integrable on the dyadic intervals of level `k`, and measurable
`g₁, D₁` and `g₂, D₂` such that `g_ν` has Taylor polynomials
`‖g_ν - T‖_{L_p[a,b]} ≤ (b - a)^r ‖D_ν‖_{L_p[a,b]}` on all intervals,
`‖u - Q_k u‖_{L_p[0,1]} ≤ A ((‖u - g₁‖_{L_p[0,3/4]} + c ‖D₁‖_{L_p[0,3/4]}) + (‖u - g₂‖_{L_p[1/4,1]} + c ‖D₂‖_{L_p[1/4,1]}))`
with `c = (r 2^(-k))^r`. Every window of the quasi-interpolant has length at most `1/4`, so it
lies in `[0, 3/4]` or in `[1/4, 1]`, and `Interval.exists_sum_eLpNorm_sub_qiPieces_le_of_taylor`
applies to the two sets of cells.

Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_qi_le.name: Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_qi_le
Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_qi_le.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality for splines, continuous functions**: there is `C` with
`‖F - Q_k F‖_{L_p[0,1]} ≤ C ω_r(F, 2^(-k), [0, 1])_p` for every continuous `F` and `k ≥ r + 2`:
the smoothings of `F` from the left on `[0, 3/4]` and from the right on `[1/4, 1]` enter
`Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_qi_le_of_taylor`.

Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_refl.name: Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_reflect_le
Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_refl.docstring:
**Taylor polynomials of a reflected function**: if `g` has a polynomial `T` of degree `< r`
with `‖g - T‖_{L_p[c - v, c - u]} ≤ (v - u)^r ‖D‖_{L_p[c - v, c - u]}`, then `T(c - ·)` does the
same for `g(c - ·)` on `[u, v]`, with `D(c - ·)` in place of `D`.

Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le_i.name: Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le_intervalModulus
Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le_i.docstring:
**Whitney's inequality for continuous functions**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `r ≥ 1` and
`0 < t ≤ 1/3` there is `W < ∞` such that every continuous `F` has a polynomial `P` of degree
`< r` with `‖F - P‖_{L_p[0, 1]} ≤ W ω_r(F, t, [0, 1])_p`.

Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le_g.name: Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le_glue
Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le_g.docstring:
**Gluing two polynomial approximations**: there is `K < ∞` such that for measurable `u` and
polynomials `T₁`, `T₂` of degree `< r`,
`‖u - T₁‖_{L_p[0, 1]} ≤ (1 + K) (‖u - T₁‖_{L_p[0, 2/3]} + ‖u - T₂‖_{L_p[1/3, 1]})`. On the
middle third `T₁` and `T₂` are close, hence on all of `[0, 1]`
(`Interval.exists_eLpNorm_le_middle`).

Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le.name: Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le
Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le.docstring:
**Taylor's theorem in `L_p`**: for `g ∈ C^r` and `u ≤ v` there is `Q` of degree `< r` with
`‖g - Q‖_{L_p[u, v]} ≤ (v - u)^r ‖g^(r)‖_{L_p[u, v]}`.

Interval.exists_eLpNorm_qi_le.name: Interval.exists_eLpNorm_qi_le
Interval.exists_eLpNorm_qi_le.docstring:
**The quasi-interpolant is bounded on `L_p[0, 1]`**: there is `C < ∞` with
`‖Q_k u‖_{L_p[0,1]} ≤ C ‖u‖_{L_p[0,1]}` for every level `k` and every measurable `u` integrable
on the dyadic intervals, from `Interval.exists_sum_eLpNorm_sub_qiPieces_le_of_taylor` with the
smoothing `0`.

Interval.exists_eLpNorm_le_middle.name: Interval.exists_eLpNorm_le_middle
Interval.exists_eLpNorm_le_middle.docstring:
**Polynomials are controlled by their middle third**: there is `K'` with
`‖P‖_{L_p[0, 1]} ≤ K' ‖P‖_{L_p[1/3, 2/3]}` for every polynomial `P` of degree `< r`, by the
equivalence of norms on the polynomials of degree `< r`.

Interval.exists_eLpNorm_higherDiff_splin.name: Interval.exists_eLpNorm_higherDiff_spline_le_of_lt
Interval.exists_eLpNorm_higherDiff_splin.docstring:
**Differences of lower order of splines**: for `1 ≤ m < r` there is `C` such that for every
level `j`, every spline `u` of order `r` and level `j` and `0 ≤ h ≤ 2^(-j)`,
`‖Δ_h^m u‖_{L_p[0, 1 - mh]} ≤ C (2^j h)^m ‖u‖_p`. For `mh ≤ 2^(-j)` the pointwise bound
(`Interval.enorm_higherDiff_spline_le_of_lt`) holds at almost every point, and the local masses
of `r + 1` consecutive pieces add up to at most `(r + 1) ‖u‖_p^p`; for `mh > 2^(-j)` the trivial
bound `2^m ‖u‖_p ≤ 2^m (m 2^j h)^m ‖u‖_p` suffices.

Interval.exists_eLpNorm_higherDiff_ppFun.name: Interval.exists_eLpNorm_higherDiff_ppFun_le
Interval.exists_eLpNorm_higherDiff_ppFun.docstring:
**Differences of every positive order of piecewise polynomials**: for `1 ≤ m ≤ r` there is
`C` such that for every level `j`, every piecewise polynomial `u` of level `j` and degree `< r` and
`0 ≤ h ≤ 2^(-j)`, `‖Δ_h^m u‖_{L_p[0, 1 - mh]} ≤ C (2^j h)^(1/p) ‖u‖_p`. On the strips of width
`rh` left of the knots the difference is bounded by the neighbouring pieces
(`Interval.enorm_higherDiff_le_of_isPiecewisePoly_of_le`), inside a piece by `(2^j h)^m` times the
piece (`Interval.enorm_higherDiff_le_of_mem_piece`), and `(2^j h)^(mp) ≤ 2^j h`.

Interval.exists_diffBound.name: Interval.exists_diffBound
Interval.exists_diffBound.docstring:
**Differences of polynomials are small**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞` and every order `m` there is a
difference bound for the polynomials of degree `< r`. On `[0, 1]` the derivative `P^(m)` is
bounded by `K ‖P‖_{L_p[0, 1/2]}` (`Interval.exists_enorm_linearMap_le_eLpNorm`), so
`|Δ_σ^m P(y)| ≤ σ^m K ‖P‖_{L_p[0, 1/2]}` (`Interval.norm_higherDiff_polyFun_le`); the substitution
`x = u + 2L y` rescales.

Interval.exists_derivative_eq.name: Interval.exists_derivative_eq
Interval.exists_derivative_eq.docstring:
**Antiderivatives of polynomials**: every polynomial of degree `< r` is the derivative of a
polynomial of degree `< r + 1`.

Interval.exists_approxError_splineScheme.name: Interval.exists_approxError_splineScheme_le
Interval.exists_approxError_splineScheme.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality for dyadic splines**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `r ≥ 1` there is `C_J` with
`E_{2^k}(f)_p ≤ C_J ω_r(f, 2^(-k), [0, 1])_p` for all `f ∈ L_p[0, 1]` and all `k ≥ 0`: the
quasi-interpolant for `k ≥ r + 2`, Whitney's inequality for `k ≤ r + 1`.

Interval.exists_approxError_ppScheme_one.name: Interval.exists_approxError_ppScheme_one_le
Interval.exists_approxError_ppScheme_one.docstring:
**Whitney's inequality in `L_p[0, 1]`**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `r ≥ 1` and `m ≥ 2` there is
`W < ∞` with `E_1(f)_p ≤ W ω_r(f, 2^(-m), [0, 1])_p` for every `f ∈ L_p[0, 1]`, where `E_1` is the
error of best approximation by the polynomials of degree `< r` (the approximants of
complexity `1`).

Interval.eq_zero_of_ae_eq_zero.name: Interval.eq_zero_of_ae_eq_zero
Interval.eq_zero_of_ae_eq_zero.docstring: A polynomial vanishing almost everywhere on an interval of positive length is zero.

Interval.eq_of_polyFun_eq.name: Interval.eq_of_polyFun_eq
Interval.eq_of_polyFun_eq.docstring: Two polynomials with the same values at all real points are equal.

Interval.eq_of_mem_dyadicIco.name: Interval.eq_of_mem_dyadicIco
Interval.eq_of_mem_dyadicIco.docstring: Dyadic intervals of one level are disjoint.

Interval.eq_add_sum_Ioc_sub.name: Interval.eq_add_sum_Ioc_sub
Interval.eq_add_sum_Ioc_sub.docstring: **Telescoping**: `f b = f a + ∑_{a < m ≤ b} (f m - f (m - 1))` for `a ≤ b`.

Interval.enorm_qiCoeff_le.name: Interval.enorm_qiCoeff_le
Interval.enorm_qiCoeff_le.docstring:
**The quasi-interpolant coefficients are bounded by the local `L_p` norm**:
`|λ_n(g)| ≤ C_b r M² 2^(k/p) ‖g‖_{L_p(J(n))}`.

Interval.enorm_polyFun_locProj_le.name: Interval.enorm_polyFun_locProj_le
Interval.enorm_polyFun_locProj_le.docstring:
**Pointwise bound for the local projection**: on `I_{j,m}`,
`|Π g(x)| ≤ r M² 2^(j/p) ‖g‖_{L_p(I_{j,m})}` when the monomials and the dual basis are bounded by
`M` on `[0, 1]`.

Interval.enorm_polyFun_le.name: Interval.enorm_polyFun_le
Interval.enorm_polyFun_le.docstring:
**Nikolskii inequality for polynomials on intervals**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞` there is `K` with
`|P(x)| ≤ K L^(-1/p) ‖P‖_{L_p[u, u + L]}` for `x ∈ [u, u + 2L]` and `P` of degree `< r`. The values
on `[0, 1]` are bounded by the norm on `[0, 1/2]`, and `x ↦ u + 2L x` rescales.

Interval.enorm_monoBasis_le.name: Interval.enorm_monoBasis_le
Interval.enorm_monoBasis_le.docstring: The monomials are bounded by `basisBound r` on `[0, 1]`.

Interval.enorm_locCoeff_le.name: Interval.enorm_locCoeff_le
Interval.enorm_locCoeff_le.docstring:
**Bound for the local coefficients**: `|c_i| ≤ M 2^(j/p) ‖g‖_{L_p(I_{j,m})}` when the
monomials are bounded by `M` on `[0, 1]`.

Interval.enorm_le_localMass.name: Interval.enorm_le_localMass
Interval.enorm_le_localMass.docstring:
**Pointwise bound** for a piecewise polynomial by its local mass (Nikolskii's inequality on
`I_{k,m}`): `|u(y)| ≤ K 2^(k/p) (∫_{I_{k,m}} |u|^p)^(1/p)` for `y ∈ I_{k,m}`.

Interval.enorm_jumpCoeff_mul_higherDiff_.name: Interval.enorm_jumpCoeff_mul_higherDiff_truncPow_le_any_order
Interval.enorm_jumpCoeff_mul_higherDiff_.docstring:
**A jump term of a spline, for every order**: for `h ≥ 0` and a knot `l 2^(-j)` with
`n₀ < l ≤ n₀ + r`, `n₀ = ⌊2^j x⌋`, the term `c_l Δ_h^m (· - l 2^(-j))_+^(r-1)(x)` is at most
`2 · 2^m m^(r-1) K (2^j h)^(r-1) 2^(j/p) (∑_{l' ≤ r} M_{n₀+l'})^(1/p)`: the jump coefficient is
bounded by `Interval.enorm_jumpCoeff_le` and the difference of the truncated power by
`2^m (mh)^(r-1)`.

Interval.enorm_jumpCoeff_mul_higherDiff_.name: Interval.enorm_jumpCoeff_mul_higherDiff_truncPow_le
Interval.enorm_jumpCoeff_mul_higherDiff_.docstring:
**A jump term of a spline**: for `1 ≤ m < r`, `h ≥ 0` with `mh ≤ 2^(-j)`, `x ≥ 0` and a knot
`l 2^(-j)` with `n₀ < l ≤ n₀ + r`, `n₀ = ⌊2^j x⌋`, the term `c_l Δ_h^m (· - l 2^(-j))_+^(r-1)(x)`
is at most `2 · 2^m m^(r-1) K (2^j h)^m 2^(j/p) (∑_{l' ≤ r} M_{n₀+l'})^(1/p)`: the bound of every
order (`Interval.enorm_jumpCoeff_mul_higherDiff_truncPow_le_any_order`) with
`(2^j h)^(r-1) ≤ (2^j h)^m`, since `2^j h ≤ 1`.

Interval.enorm_jumpCoeff_le.name: Interval.enorm_jumpCoeff_le
Interval.enorm_jumpCoeff_le.docstring:
**The jumps are bounded by the neighbouring pieces**: for `0 < m < N` and `L = 2^(-j)`,
`|c_m| L^(r-1) ≤ K 2^(j/p) (m_m^(1/p) + m_{m-1}^(1/p))`, from
`c_m L^(r-1) = P_m(ξ_m + L) - P_{m-1}(ξ_m + L)` and Nikolskii's inequality, for `P_{m-1}` on the
doubled interval.

Interval.enorm_higherDiff_truncPow_le_of.name: Interval.enorm_higherDiff_truncPow_le_of_lt
Interval.enorm_higherDiff_truncPow_le_of.docstring:
**Differences of any order of a truncated power left of its knot**: for `x < ξ` and
`h ≥ 0`, `|Δ_h^m (· - ξ)_+^(r-1)(x)| ≤ 2^m (mh)^(r-1)`, since `0 ≤ (x + ih - ξ)_+ ≤ mh`.

Interval.enorm_higherDiff_spline_le_of_l.name: Interval.enorm_higherDiff_spline_le_of_lt
Interval.enorm_higherDiff_spline_le_of_l.docstring:
**Pointwise bound for differences of lower order of splines**: for `1 ≤ m < r`, `h ≥ 0` with
`mh ≤ 2^(-j)`, `x ≥ 0` and `x + mh < N 2^(-j)`,
`|Δ_h^m u(x)| ≤ (K_m + 2 r 2^m m^(r-1) K) (2^j h)^m 2^(j/p) (∑_{l ≤ r} M_{n₀+l})^(1/p)`. The
piece contributes by the difference bound `K_m` of the polynomials, a jump
`c_l (· - ξ_l)_+^(r-1)` by `|c_l| 2^m (mh)^(r-1)` with
`|c_l| 2^(-j(r-1)) ≤ 2 K 2^(j/p) (…)^(1/p)`, and `(2^j h)^(r-1) ≤ (2^j h)^m`.

Interval.enorm_higherDiff_spline_le.name: Interval.enorm_higherDiff_spline_le
Interval.enorm_higherDiff_spline_le.docstring:
**Pointwise bound for differences of splines**: on the strips left of the knots,
`|Δ_h^r u(x)| ≤ G (∑_{l ≤ r} m_{n₀+l})^(1/p)` for `x + rh < N 2^(-j)`.

Interval.enorm_higherDiff_rpow_le_strip_.name: Interval.enorm_higherDiff_rpow_le_strip_add_piece
Interval.enorm_higherDiff_rpow_le_strip_.docstring:
**The pointwise bound for differences of piecewise polynomials**: for `m ≤ r`,
`0 ≤ h ≤ 2^(-j)` and `x ∈ [0, 1 - mh]`, `|Δ_h^m u(x)|^p` is at most the strip bound of the
neighbouring masses `∑_{l ≤ r} M_{n+l}` (`Interval.enorm_higherDiff_le_of_isPiecewisePoly_of_le`)
plus `(K_m (2^j h)^m 2^(j/p))^p M_n` for the piece of `x`
(`Interval.enorm_higherDiff_le_of_mem_piece`), where `n = ⌊2^j x⌋`.

Interval.enorm_higherDiff_le_of_mem_piec.name: Interval.enorm_higherDiff_le_of_mem_piece
Interval.enorm_higherDiff_le_of_mem_piec.docstring:
**Differences inside a piece**: if `x, …, x + mh` lie in the dyadic interval `I_{k,n}` of `x`,
`n = ⌊2^k x⌋`, then `|Δ_h^m u(x)| ≤ K (2^k h)^m 2^(k/p) M_n^(1/p)`, by the difference bound of
the polynomial piece (`Interval.DiffBound`).

Interval.enorm_higherDiff_le_of_isPiecew.name: Interval.enorm_higherDiff_le_of_isPiecewisePoly_of_le
Interval.enorm_higherDiff_le_of_isPiecew.docstring:
**Pointwise bound for differences of order `m ≤ r`**: for `0 ≤ h ≤ 2^(-k)` and `x ≥ 0`,
`|Δ_h^m u(x)| ≤ 2^m K 2^(k/p) (∑_{l ≤ r} M_{n+l})^(1/p)` with `n = ⌊2^k x⌋`, since
`x, …, x + mh` meet only the intervals `I_{k,n}, …, I_{k,n+r}`.

Interval.enorm_higherDiff_le_of_forall.name: Interval.enorm_higherDiff_le_of_forall
Interval.enorm_higherDiff_le_of_forall.docstring:
**Pointwise bound for differences**: if `|f(x + k h)| ≤ B` for `k ≤ r`, then
`|Δ_h^r f(x)| ≤ 2^r B`, since the coefficients `C(r, k)` add up to `2^r`.

Interval.enorm_higherDiff_coeff.name: Interval.enorm_higherDiff_coeff
Interval.enorm_higherDiff_coeff.docstring: **The coefficients of a difference**: `‖(-1)^(r-k) C(r, k)‖ = C(r, k)`.

Interval.enorm_dualPoly_le.name: Interval.enorm_dualPoly_le
Interval.enorm_dualPoly_le.docstring: The dual basis is bounded by `basisBound r` on `[0, 1]`.

Interval.enorm_coeffToLp.name: Interval.enorm_coeffToLp
Interval.enorm_coeffToLp.docstring: The norm of `coeffToLp` is the `L_p` norm of the polynomial.

Interval.eLpNorm_sum_smoothCoeff_smul_le.name: Interval.eLpNorm_sum_smoothCoeff_smul_le
Interval.eLpNorm_sum_smoothCoeff_smul_le.docstring:
**The derivative bound of the smoothing, for any measure and any family**: for `δ > 0`,
`1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, a measure `μ` and functions `D_h` with `‖D_h‖_{L_p(μ)} ≤ B` for `0 ≤ h ≤ rδ`,
`‖∑_{k=1}^r (-1)^(k+1) C(r, k) (kδ)^(-r) D_{kδ}‖_{L_p(μ)} ≤ 2^r δ^(-r) B`, by the triangle
inequality and `∑_{k=1}^r C(r, k) ≤ 2^r`. With `D_h = Δ_h^r f` this bounds `(S_δ f)^(r)`
(`Interval.iteratedDeriv_steklovSmooth_eq_sum_smul`) on an interval, on a region of the cube and on
the whole line.

Interval.eLpNorm_sub_steklovSmooth_le.name: Interval.eLpNorm_sub_steklovSmooth_le
Interval.eLpNorm_sub_steklovSmooth_le.docstring:
**The smoothing is close to `f`**: for `[u, w]` with `a ≤ u` and `w + r² δ ≤ b`,
`‖f - S_δ f‖_{L_p[u, w]} ≤ ω_r(f, rδ, [a, b])_p`.

Interval.eLpNorm_sub_qiPieces_le.name: Interval.eLpNorm_sub_qiPieces_le
Interval.eLpNorm_sub_qiPieces_le.docstring:
**The local error of the quasi-interpolant**: for every polynomial `T` of degree `< r`,
`‖g - Q_k g‖_{L_p(I_{k,i})} ≤ (1 + r M_N C_b r M²) ‖g - T‖_{L_p(W_i)}`.

Interval.eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le_of_smoot.name: Interval.eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le_of_smoothing
Interval.eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le_of_smoot.docstring:
**Smoothing and Taylor on one part**: if `‖F - g‖_{L_p[a,b]} ≤ ω`, `‖D‖_{L_p[a,b]} ≤ c ω`,
`‖g - T‖_{L_p[a,b]} ≤ (b - a)^r ‖D‖_{L_p[a,b]}` and `b - a ≤ 1`, then
`‖F - T‖_{L_p[a,b]} ≤ (1 + c) ω`.

Interval.eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le_add.name: Interval.eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le_add
Interval.eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le_add.docstring:
**Taylor approximation on one part**: if `‖g - T‖_{L_p[a,b]} ≤ (b - a)^r ‖D‖_{L_p[a,b]}` and
`b - a ≤ 1`, then `‖F - T‖_{L_p[a,b]} ≤ ‖F - g‖_{L_p[a,b]} + ‖D‖_{L_p[a,b]}`.

Interval.eLpNorm_smoothCoeff_smul_le.name: Interval.eLpNorm_smoothCoeff_smul_le
Interval.eLpNorm_smoothCoeff_smul_le.docstring:
**One term of the derivative of the smoothing**: for `k ≥ 1` (written `k + 1`), `δ > 0`, a
measure `μ` and `g` with `‖g‖_{L_p(μ)} ≤ B`,
`‖(-1)^(k+1) C(r, k) (kδ)^(-r) g‖_{L_p(μ)} ≤ C(r, k) δ^(-r) B`, since `(kδ)^(-r) ≤ δ^(-r)`.

Interval.eLpNorm_qiPieces_le.name: Interval.eLpNorm_qiPieces_le
Interval.eLpNorm_qiPieces_le.docstring:
**The quasi-interpolant is locally bounded**: on `I_{k,i}`,
`‖Q_k g‖_{L_p(I_{k,i})} ≤ M_N C_b r M² ∑_{i - r < n ≤ i} ‖g‖_{L_p(J(n))}`, with `M_N` a bound of
the B-spline.

Interval.eLpNorm_ppFun_locProj_le.name: Interval.eLpNorm_ppFun_locProj_le
Interval.eLpNorm_ppFun_locProj_le.docstring:
**The projections onto piecewise polynomials are uniformly bounded**:
`‖P_j g‖_{L_p[0,1]} ≤ r M² ‖g‖_{L_p[0,1]}` for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, with `P_j g` the local projections
of `g` on the dyadic intervals of level `j`.

Interval.eLpNorm_piece_eq_localMass.name: Interval.eLpNorm_piece_eq_localMass
Interval.eLpNorm_piece_eq_localMass.docstring:
**The norm of a piece is a local mass**: if `u = P` on `I_{k,m}`, then
`‖P‖_{L_p[m 2^(-k), (m + 1) 2^(-k)]} = (∫_{I_{k,m}} |u|^p)^(1/p)`.

Interval.eLpNorm_locProj_le.name: Interval.eLpNorm_locProj_le
Interval.eLpNorm_locProj_le.docstring:
**The local projection is bounded in `L_p(I_{j,m})`**:
`‖Π g‖_{L_p(I_{j,m})} ≤ r M² ‖g‖_{L_p(I_{j,m})}`, with a constant independent of `j` and `m`.

Interval.eLpNorm_le_of_strip.name: Interval.eLpNorm_le_of_strip
Interval.eLpNorm_le_of_strip.docstring:
**The strip integral**: for `0 < p < ∞`, if `|F|^p` is bounded by `G^p M_n` on the strip of
width `rh` left of the right end of every dyadic interval `I_{j,n}` and vanishes elsewhere on
`S ⊆ [0, 1]`, and `∑_{n < 2^j} M_n ≤ (r + 1) B^p`, then `‖F‖_{L_p(S)} ≤ G (rh (r + 1))^(1/p) B`.

Interval.eLpNorm_le_of_lintegral_le_mul.name: Interval.eLpNorm_le_of_lintegral_le_mul
Interval.eLpNorm_le_of_lintegral_le_mul.docstring:
**From an integral bound to an `L_p` bound**: `∫ |F|^p ≤ A^p σ B^p` gives
`‖F‖_p ≤ A σ^(1/p) B`.

Interval.eLpNorm_iteratedDeriv_steklovSm.name: Interval.eLpNorm_iteratedDeriv_steklovSmooth_le
Interval.eLpNorm_iteratedDeriv_steklovSm.docstring:
**The derivative of order `r` of the smoothing**: for `[u, w]` with `a ≤ u` and
`w + r² δ ≤ b`, `‖(S_δ f)^(r)‖_{L_p[u, w]} ≤ 2^r δ^(-r) ω_r(f, rδ, [a, b])_p`.

Interval.eLpNorm_indicator_diffStepSet_I.name: Interval.eLpNorm_indicator_diffStepSet_Icc
Interval.eLpNorm_indicator_diffStepSet_I.docstring:
For `h ≥ 0`, the restricted difference on `[a, b]` has the norm of `Δ_h^r f` on
`[a, b - rh]`.

Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_stepRegion_e.name: Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_stepRegion_eq
Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_stepRegion_e.docstring:
**The norm of a difference depends only on the size of the step**:
`‖Δ_t^m u‖_{L_p(step region)} = ‖Δ_{|t|}^m u‖_{L_p[0, 1 - m|t|]}`
(`Rd.eLpNorm_indicator_diffStepSet_neg`).

Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_spline_le.name: Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_spline_le
Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_spline_le.docstring:
**The local inverse estimate for splines**: let `u` be a spline of level `j` below `N`, a
piecewise polynomial on `[0, ∞)`, and `0 ≤ h ≤ 2^(-j)`. On a measurable `S ⊆ [0, 1]` with
`x + rh < N 2^(-j)` for almost every `x ∈ S`, and if the local masses of `r + 1` consecutive
pieces add up to at most `(r + 1) B^p`, then `‖Δ_h^r u‖_{L_p(S)} ≤ G (rh (r + 1))^(1/p) B`.

Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_reflect.name: Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_reflect
Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_reflect.docstring:
**Reflection of a difference**:
`‖Δ_h^r f(a + b - ·)‖_{L_p[a, b - rh]} = ‖Δ_h^r f‖_{L_p[a, b - rh]}`, since
`Δ_h^r f(a + b - ·)(x) = (-1)^r Δ_h^r f(a + b - rh - x)`.

Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_ppFun_spline.name: Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_ppFun_spline_le
Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_ppFun_spline.docstring:
**The local inverse estimate for splines on `[0, 1]`**: for the pieces `Q` of a spline of
level `j` and `0 ≤ h ≤ 2^(-j)`,
`‖Δ_h^r (ppFun j Q)‖_{L_p[0, 1 - rh]} ≤ S_j(h) (r h (r + 1))^(1/p) ‖ppFun j Q‖_{L_p[0,1]}` with the
strip constant `S_j(h)` of `Interval.splineStripConst`.

Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_of_pointw.name: Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_of_pointwise
Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_of_pointw.docstring:
**The local inverse estimate from a pointwise bound**: let `u` be a piecewise polynomial of
level `j` on `[0, ∞)`, `S ⊆ [0, 1]` measurable and `h ≥ 0`. If on the strips of width `rh` left
of the knots `|Δ_h^r u(x)| ≤ G (∑_{l ≤ r} ∫_{I_{j,n+l}} |u|^p)^(1/p)`, `n = ⌊2^j x⌋`, for almost
every `x ∈ S`, and these local masses add up to at most `(r + 1) B^p` over `n < 2^j`, then
`‖Δ_h^r u‖_{L_p(S)} ≤ G (rh (r + 1))^(1/p) B`. Off the strips the difference vanishes
(`Interval.higherDiff_eq_zero_of_isPiecewisePoly`).

Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_of_lt_mul.name: Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_of_lt_mul
Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_of_lt_mul.docstring:
**Long steps**: for `mh > 2^(-j)`, `‖Δ_h^m u‖_{L_p[0, 1 - mh]} ≤ 2^m m^m (2^j h)^m ‖u‖_p`,
from `‖Δ_h^m u‖_p ≤ 2^m ‖u‖_p` and `1 < m 2^j h`.

Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_of_forall.name: Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_of_forall
Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_of_forall.docstring:
**Differences in `L_p`**: if `‖f(· + k h)‖_{L_p(μ)} ≤ B` for `k ≤ r`, then
`‖Δ_h^r f‖_{L_p(μ)} ≤ 2^r B`, by the triangle inequality and `∑_k C(r, k) = 2^r`.

Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_intervalM.name: Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_intervalModulus
Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_intervalM.docstring: `‖Δ_h^r f‖_{L_p[a, b - rh]} ≤ ω_r(f, t)` for `0 ≤ h ≤ t`.

Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_congr_ae.name: Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_congr_ae
Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_congr_ae.docstring:
**Differences depend only on the class in `L_p[a, b]`**: for `h ≥ 0`, functions that agree
almost everywhere on `[a, b]` have differences of step `h` with the same `L_p` norm on
`[a, b - rh]`: the norm is that of `Δ_h^r (1_{[a,b]} f)` on the step set
(`Interval.eLpNorm_indicator_diffStepSet_Icc`, `Rd.indicator_diffStepSet_higherDiff_indicator`), and
the differences of `1_{[a,b]} f = 1_{[a,b]} g` agree almost everywhere
(`Rd.higherDiff_congr_ae`).

Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_Icc_le_inter.name: Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_Icc_le_intervalModulus
Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_Icc_le_inter.docstring:
**Differences on a subinterval are bounded by the modulus**: for `a ≤ u`, `w + r (rδ) ≤ b` and
`0 ≤ h ≤ rδ`, `‖Δ_h^r f‖_{L_p[u, w]} ≤ ω_r(f, rδ, [a, b])_p`, since `[u, w]` lies in
`[a, b - rh]`.

Interval.eLpNorm_comp_add_mul_le.name: Interval.eLpNorm_comp_add_mul_le
Interval.eLpNorm_comp_add_mul_le.docstring:
**Translates on a shorter interval**: for `h ≥ 0` and `k ≤ r`,
`‖f(· + k h)‖_{L_p[a, b - rh]} ≤ ‖f‖_{L_p[a, b]}`, since `[a, b - rh] + kh ⊆ [a, b]`.

Interval.eLpNorm_avg_le.name: Interval.eLpNorm_avg_le
Interval.eLpNorm_avg_le.docstring:
**Minkowski's inequality for averages**: for jointly continuous `K`, `δ > 0`,
`1 ≤ p < ∞` and an s-finite measure `μ` on the point space,
`‖δ^(-1) ∫_0^δ K(t, ·) dt‖_{L_p(μ)} ≤ sup_{0 ≤ t ≤ δ} ‖K(t, ·)‖_{L_p(μ)}`: the weighted average
with the weight `Φ = δ^(-1) 1_{(0, δ]}` of total mass `1`
(`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_integral_kernel_le_of_bound`).

Interval.eLpNorm_avgStepIter_le.name: Interval.eLpNorm_avgStepIter_le
Interval.eLpNorm_avgStepIter_le.docstring:
**Iterated averages are bounded by the sup over the steps**:
`‖avg^m G(σ, ·)‖_{L_p(μ)} ≤ sup_{σ ≤ h ≤ σ + mδ} ‖G(h, ·)‖_{L_p(μ)}`.

Interval.dyadicIco_subset_qiWindow.name: Interval.dyadicIco_subset_qiWindow
Interval.dyadicIco_subset_qiWindow.docstring: The intervals `J(n)`, `i - r < n ≤ i`, lie in the window of `I_{k,i}`.

Interval.dualPoly.name: Interval.dualPoly
Interval.dualPoly.docstring: The **dual basis** `d_i` of the monomials for the pairing `∫_0^1 P Q`.

Interval.differentiable_steklov.name: Interval.differentiable_steklov
Interval.differentiable_steklov.docstring: Steklov averages of continuous functions are differentiable.

Interval.diffStepSet_Icc_of_nonneg.name: Interval.diffStepSet_Icc_of_nonneg
Interval.diffStepSet_Icc_of_nonneg.docstring: For `h ≥ 0`, the points `x` with `x, x + h, …, x + rh ∈ [a, b]` form `[a, b - rh]`.

Interval.deriv_steklov.name: Interval.deriv_steklov
Interval.deriv_steklov.docstring: The derivative of a Steklov average.

Interval.continuous_steklovIter.name: Interval.continuous_steklovIter
Interval.continuous_steklovIter.docstring: Iterated Steklov averages of continuous functions are continuous.

Interval.continuous_higherDiff_uncurry.name: Interval.continuous_higherDiff_uncurry
Interval.continuous_higherDiff_uncurry.docstring: Differences of a continuous function are jointly continuous in the step and the point.

Interval.continuous_fwdDiff.name: Interval.continuous_fwdDiff
Interval.continuous_fwdDiff.docstring: Forward differences of continuous functions are continuous.

Interval.continuous_avgStepIter.name: Interval.continuous_avgStepIter
Interval.continuous_avgStepIter.docstring: Iterated averages of jointly continuous functions are jointly continuous.

Interval.continuous_avgStep.name: Interval.continuous_avgStep
Interval.continuous_avgStep.docstring: Averages of jointly continuous functions are jointly continuous.

Interval.contDiff_steklovSmooth.name: Interval.contDiff_steklovSmooth
Interval.contDiff_steklovSmooth.docstring: The Steklov smoothing of a continuous function lies in `C^r`.

Interval.contDiff_steklovIter.name: Interval.contDiff_steklovIter
Interval.contDiff_steklovIter.docstring: **The `m`-fold Steklov average of a continuous function lies in `C^m`**.

Interval.contDiff_steklov.name: Interval.contDiff_steklov
Interval.contDiff_steklov.docstring: **Averaging gains one derivative**: `g ∈ C^k` implies `M_η g ∈ C^(k+1)`.

Interval.comp_affine_mem_degreeLT.name: Interval.comp_affine_mem_degreeLT
Interval.comp_affine_mem_degreeLT.docstring: **Affine changes of variable** keep the degree `< r`.

Interval.comp_X_add_C_mem.name: Interval.comp_X_add_C_mem
Interval.comp_X_add_C_mem.docstring:
Translates of polynomials of degree `< r` have degree `< r`: Mathlib's
`Polynomial.taylor_mem_degreeLT`, since `taylor a P = P.comp (X + C a)` (`Polynomial.taylor_apply`),
stated in the `comp` form that the rewrites below need.

Interval.coeffToLp_injective.name: Interval.coeffToLp_injective
Interval.coeffToLp_injective.docstring: `coeffToLp` is injective on an interval of positive length.

Interval.coeffToLp.name: Interval.coeffToLp
Interval.coeffToLp.docstring:
The map from the coefficients of a polynomial of degree `< r` to its class in
`L_p[α, β]`.

Interval.bspline_sub_eq.name: Interval.bspline_sub_eq
Interval.bspline_sub_eq.docstring: `N_r(x - (i - j)) = β_j(x - i)` for `x ∈ [i, i + 1)` and `j < r`.

Interval.bspline_eq_zero_of_not_mem.name: Interval.bspline_eq_zero_of_not_mem
Interval.bspline_eq_zero_of_not_mem.docstring: On `I_{k,i}` only the B-splines `i - r < n ≤ i` are nonzero.

Interval.bspline_eq_piece.name: Interval.bspline_eq_piece
Interval.bspline_eq_piece.docstring: On `[j, j + 1)`, `j < r`, the B-spline is its piece `B_j`.

Interval.bsplineVec_eq.name: Interval.bsplineVec_eq
Interval.bsplineVec_eq.docstring:
`β_j = (1/(r-1)!) (X + j)^(r-1) + ∑_{1 ≤ l ≤ j} (…) (X + (j - l))^(r-1)`, the triangular
form in the shifted powers.

Interval.bsplineVec.name: Interval.bsplineVec
Interval.bsplineVec.docstring: The B-splines on `[0, 1)` as elements of the polynomials of degree `< r`.

Interval.bsplinePieces_mem.name: Interval.bsplinePieces_mem
Interval.bsplinePieces_mem.docstring: The B-spline pieces have degree `< r`.

Interval.bsplinePieces_join.name: Interval.bsplinePieces_join
Interval.bsplinePieces_join.docstring:
**The B-splines have spline joins at every knot**: at the knot `m 2^(-k)`, `m ≥ 1`, the pieces
of `N_r(2^k x - n)` jump by `(-1)^d C(r, d)/(r-1)! 2^(k(r-1)) (x - m 2^(-k))^(r-1)`, `d = m - n`.

Interval.bsplinePieces.name: Interval.bsplinePieces
Interval.bsplinePieces.docstring:
The pieces of the B-spline `N_r(2^k x - n)` on the dyadic intervals `I_{k,m}`:
`B_{m-n}(2^k x - n)` for `0 ≤ m - n ≤ r`, and `0` otherwise.

Interval.bsplinePiece_top.name: Interval.bsplinePiece_top
Interval.bsplinePiece_top.docstring:
**The last piece vanishes**, `B_r = 0`: `∑_{l ≤ r} (-1)^l C(r, l) (z - l)^(r-1) = 0` is the
`r`-th difference of the polynomial `(z - X)^(r-1)` of degree `< r` at `0` (Mathlib's
`Polynomial.fwdDiff_iter_eq_zero_of_degree_lt` and `fwdDiff_iter_eq_sum_shift`).

Interval.bsplinePiece_succ.name: Interval.bsplinePiece_succ
Interval.bsplinePiece_succ.docstring: Consecutive pieces differ by a multiple of `(X - (j + 1))^(r-1)`.

Interval.bsplinePiece.name: Interval.bsplinePiece
Interval.bsplinePiece.docstring:
The `j`-th piece of the cardinal B-spline of order `r`,
`B_j(X) = ∑_{l ≤ j} (-1)^l C(r, l) (X - l)^(r-1) / (r-1)!`, the B-spline on `[j, j + 1)`.

Interval.bsplineLocal_mem.name: Interval.bsplineLocal_mem
Interval.bsplineLocal_mem.docstring: The B-splines on `[0, 1)` have degree `< r`.

Interval.bsplineLocal.name: Interval.bsplineLocal
Interval.bsplineLocal.docstring: The **B-splines on `[0, 1)`**: `β_j(X) = B_j(X + j)` is `N_r(· + j)` on `[0, 1)`.

Interval.bsplineCoeff.name: Interval.bsplineCoeff
Interval.bsplineCoeff.docstring: The coefficients `(-1)^l C(r, l) / (r-1)!` of the pieces of the B-spline of order `r`.

Interval.bsplineCoef_sum.name: Interval.bsplineCoef_sum
Interval.bsplineCoef_sum.docstring: The B-spline coefficients of finite combinations of polynomials of degree `< r`.

Interval.bsplineCoef.name: Interval.bsplineCoef
Interval.bsplineCoef.docstring:
The **B-spline coefficient** `c_n(P)` of a polynomial `P`: the coordinate of `N_r(· - n)` in
the expansion of `P` on `[n, n + 1)`.

Interval.bsplineBasis_apply.name: Interval.bsplineBasis_apply
Interval.bsplineBasis_apply.docstring: The elements of the B-spline basis.

Interval.bsplineBasis.name: Interval.bsplineBasis
Interval.bsplineBasis.docstring: **The B-spline basis** of the polynomials of degree `< r` on `[0, 1)`.

Interval.bspline.name: Interval.bspline
Interval.bspline.docstring:
The **cardinal B-spline** `N_r` of order `r`: the piece `B_j` on `[j, j + 1)`, `0 ≤ j < r`,
and `0` outside `[0, r)`.

Interval.bcoord_eq_of_sum.name: Interval.bcoord_eq_of_sum
Interval.bcoord_eq_of_sum.docstring:
**The coordinates are unique**: if `P = ∑_{j < r} c_j β_j`, then the `c_j` are the
coordinates.

Interval.bcoord_comp_eq_bsplineCoef.name: Interval.bcoord_comp_eq_bsplineCoef
Interval.bcoord_comp_eq_bsplineCoef.docstring:
**Consistency of the coefficients**: on `[i, i + 1)` the coordinate `j` of `P(X + i)` is the
coefficient `c_{i-j}(P)` of the B-spline `N_r(· - (i - j))`, whatever the interval.

Interval.bcoord_comp_add_one.name: Interval.bcoord_comp_add_one
Interval.bcoord_comp_add_one.docstring:
**The coordinates move by one under a shift by `1`**: the coordinate `j + 1` of `P(X + 1)` is
the coordinate `j` of `P`.

Interval.bcoord.name: Interval.bcoord
Interval.bcoord.docstring:
The **coordinates** of a polynomial `P` of degree `< r` in the B-spline basis on `[0, 1)`:
`P = ∑_{j < r} a_j β_j` (`0` for `j ≥ r` or `P` of higher degree).

Interval.basisBound.name: Interval.basisBound
Interval.basisBound.docstring: A common bound for the monomials and the dual basis on `[0, 1]`.

Interval.avgStepIter_shift.name: Interval.avgStepIter_shift
Interval.avgStepIter_shift.docstring:
**Averaged translates are Steklov averages**: averaging `g(x + k h)` `m` times in the step
gives `M_{kδ}^m g(x + kσ)`, for `k ≥ 1`.

Interval.avgStepIter_const.name: Interval.avgStepIter_const
Interval.avgStepIter_const.docstring: Averaging a function of `x` alone changes nothing.

Interval.avgStepIter_congr_point.name: Interval.avgStepIter_congr_point
Interval.avgStepIter_congr_point.docstring:
The iterated average at a point only sees the values at that point: if `G(h, x) = G'(h, x')`
for all steps `h`, the averages at `x` and at `x'` agree.

Interval.avgStep.name: Interval.avgStep
Interval.avgStep.docstring:
Averaging a function of `(h, x)` in the step: `δ^(-1) ∫_0^δ G(σ + t, x) dt`. The point `x`
lies in any space `α`: the real line for the interval, the cube for slices in one coordinate.

Interval.approxError_splineScheme_one.name: Interval.approxError_splineScheme_one
Interval.approxError_splineScheme_one.docstring:
At complexity `1` the spline scheme and the piecewise polynomial scheme have the same error:
both approximate by the polynomials of degree `< r` (`Interval.splineSpace_zero`).

Interval.ae_mem_Ico_unitVol.name: Interval.ae_mem_Ico_unitVol
Interval.ae_mem_Ico_unitVol.docstring: Almost every point of `[0, 1]` lies in `[0, 1)`.

Interval.add_ofReal_pow_mul_le_intervalJ.name: Interval.add_ofReal_pow_mul_le_intervalJacksonConst
Interval.add_ofReal_pow_mul_le_intervalJ.docstring:
The bound of a smoothing and of its Taylor remainders at scale `L` combine to the local
Jackson constant: `a ≤ ω` and `b ≤ L^(-r) 2^r r^(2r) ω` give `a + L^r b ≤ (1 + 2^r r^(2r)) ω`.

Interval.add_ofReal_div_pow_mul_le.name: Interval.add_ofReal_div_pow_mul_le
Interval.add_ofReal_div_pow_mul_le.docstring:
At the scale `L = 2^(-k)` the factor `c = (r 2^(-k))^r` of the Taylor remainders on the
windows and the bound `L^(-r) 2^r r^(2r)` of the derivative combine to `r^r 2^r r^(2r)`:
`a ≤ ω` and `b ≤ L^(-r) 2^r r^(2r) ω` give `a + c b ≤ (1 + r^r 2^r r^(2r)) ω`.

Interval.X_sub_C_pow_comp_affine.name: Interval.X_sub_C_pow_comp_affine
Interval.X_sub_C_pow_comp_affine.docstring:
The affine change of variables of the powers:
`(2^k x - n - d)^(r-1) = 2^(k(r-1)) (x - (n + d) 2^(-k))^(r-1)`.

Interval.SplineJoinsBelow.name: Interval.SplineJoinsBelow
Interval.SplineJoinsBelow.docstring:
The pieces `P` have **spline joins of order `r` below `N`** at the knots of level `k`: at
`ξ = n 2^(-k)`, `0 < n < N`, consecutive pieces differ by a multiple of `(x - ξ)^(r-1)`. With
`N = 2^k` these are the interior knots of `[0, 1]`; larger `N` describe splines on
`[0, N 2^(-k))`, such as periodic extensions.

Interval.SplineJoins.sum.name: Interval.SplineJoins.sum
Interval.SplineJoins.sum.docstring: Spline joins are preserved by finite sums.

Interval.SplineJoins.refine.name: Interval.SplineJoins.refine
Interval.SplineJoins.refine.docstring:
Spline joins of level `k` are spline joins of level `k + 1`: the new knots lie inside the
pieces, where the jump is `0`.

Interval.SplineJoins.const_mul.name: Interval.SplineJoins.const_mul
Interval.SplineJoins.const_mul.docstring: Spline joins are preserved by constant multiples.

Interval.SplineJoins.below.name: Interval.SplineJoins.below
Interval.SplineJoins.below.docstring: Spline joins at the interior knots of `[0, 1]` are spline joins below `2^k`.

Interval.SplineJoins.add.name: Interval.SplineJoins.add
Interval.SplineJoins.add.docstring: Spline joins are preserved by sums.

Interval.SplineJoins.name: Interval.SplineJoins
Interval.SplineJoins.docstring:
The pieces `Q` have **spline joins of order `r`** at the interior knots of level `k`: at
`ξ = n 2^(-k)`, `0 < n < 2^k`, consecutive pieces differ by a multiple of `(x - ξ)^(r-1)`.

Interval.NikolskiiBound.enorm_le.name: Interval.NikolskiiBound.enorm_le
Interval.NikolskiiBound.enorm_le.docstring: Nikolskii's bound on the interval `[u, u + L]` itself.

Interval.NikolskiiBound.name: Interval.NikolskiiBound
Interval.NikolskiiBound.docstring:
**Nikolskii's bound** with constant `K` for the polynomials of degree `< r`:
`|P(x)| ≤ K L^(-1/p) ‖P‖_{L_p[u, u + L]}` for `x ∈ [u, u + 2L]`.

Interval.IsPiecewisePoly.name: Interval.IsPiecewisePoly
Interval.IsPiecewisePoly.docstring:
`u` is a **piecewise polynomial of level `k` and degree `< r` on `[0, ∞)`**: on every dyadic
interval `I_{k,m}`, `m ∈ ℕ`, it agrees with a polynomial of degree `< r`. The local estimates
below need only this, so they serve the piecewise polynomials on `[0, 1)` and their periodic
extensions alike.

Interval.DiffBound.name: Interval.DiffBound
Interval.DiffBound.docstring:
The **difference bound** of order `m` with constant `K` for the polynomials of degree `< r`:
`|Δ_t^m P(x)| ≤ K (t/L)^m L^(-1/p) ‖P‖_{L_p[u, u + L]}` for `t ≥ 0` and `u ≤ x`,
`x + mt ≤ u + 2L`. For `m = 0` this is Nikolskii's bound `Interval.NikolskiiBound`.

InterpCouple.two_rpow_mul_kSumBelow.name: InterpCouple.two_rpow_mul_kSumBelow
InterpCouple.two_rpow_mul_kSumBelow.docstring:
The weighted sum below `m` as a geometric convolution: for `θ = θ₀ + ηρ`,
`2^(-mρη) S₀(m) = ∑_{j ≥ 0} 2^(-(j+1)ηρ) c_{m-(j+1)}` with `c_n = 2^(-nθ) K(2^n, u)`.

InterpCouple.two_rpow_mul_kSumAbove.name: InterpCouple.two_rpow_mul_kSumAbove
InterpCouple.two_rpow_mul_kSumAbove.docstring:
The weighted sum from `m` on as a geometric convolution: for `θ₁ = θ + (1 - η) ρ`,
`2^(-mρη) 2^(mρ) S₁(m) = ∑_{j ≥ 0} 2^(-j(1-η)ρ) c_{m+j}` with `c_n = 2^(-nθ) K(2^n, u)`.

InterpCouple.two_rpow_mul_kFunctional_le.name: InterpCouple.two_rpow_mul_kFunctional_le_kSumAbove
InterpCouple.two_rpow_mul_kFunctional_le.docstring: The term `2^(-mθ) K(2^m, u)` is at most `S₁(m)`, being its first term.

InterpCouple.reiterationConst_ne_top.name: InterpCouple.reiterationConst_ne_top
InterpCouple.reiterationConst_ne_top.docstring:
The constant `reiterationConst C θ₀ θ₁ η` is finite for `C < ∞`, `0 < θ₀ < θ₁ < 1` and
`0 < η < 1`.

InterpCouple.reiterationConst.name: InterpCouple.reiterationConst
InterpCouple.reiterationConst.docstring:
The constant
`holmstedtConst C θ₀ θ₁ · ((1 - 2^(-η(θ₁-θ₀)))⁻¹ + (1 - 2^(-(1-η)(θ₁-θ₀)))⁻¹)` of the
reiteration theorem.

InterpCouple.ofMap.name: InterpCouple.ofMap
InterpCouple.ofMap.docstring:
The **couple of a bounded linear map** `ι : Y → X`: `N₀(f) = ‖f‖` and
`N₁(f) = inf {‖y‖ : ι y = f}` (`∞` off the range of `ι`), so that the spaces are `X` and
`ι(Y)` with the quotient norm; `ι` need not be injective.

InterpCouple.norm1_ofMap_neg_le.name: InterpCouple.norm1_ofMap_neg_le
InterpCouple.norm1_ofMap_neg_le.docstring: The quotient norm of `-f` is at most that of `f`.

InterpCouple.norm1_ofMap_le.name: InterpCouple.norm1_ofMap_le
InterpCouple.norm1_ofMap_le.docstring: Every preimage bounds the quotient norm: `N₁(f) ≤ ‖y‖` if `ι y = f`.

InterpCouple.norm0_le_mul_kFunctional_on.name: InterpCouple.norm0_le_mul_kFunctional_one
InterpCouple.norm0_le_mul_kFunctional_on.docstring:
**The first norm of an ordered couple by the K-functional at `t = 1`**: if the couple is
quasi-normed with constant `C` and `N₀ ≤ c N₁` with `c < ∞`, then
`N₀(u) ≤ C max(1, c) K(1, u)`, since `N₀(u) ≤ C (N₀(u - b) + c N₁(b))` for every `b`.

InterpCouple.norm0_le_leftECouple_norm1.name: InterpCouple.norm0_le_leftECouple_norm1
InterpCouple.norm0_le_leftECouple_norm1.docstring:
**`(N₀, E_{r,q₁})` is ordered**: `N₀(u) ≤ 1 · ‖u‖^dy_{r,q₁}` for every `u`, since `N₀(u)` is the
first term of the dyadic norm.

InterpCouple.norm0_le_eFunctional_of_lt_.name: InterpCouple.norm0_le_eFunctional_of_lt_one
InterpCouple.norm0_le_eFunctional_of_lt_.docstring:
**If every `b` with `N₁(b) < 1` is `0`, then `E(t, u) ≥ N₀(u)` for `t < 1`**: every
admissible element is `b = 0`.

InterpCouple.monotone_kFunctional.name: InterpCouple.monotone_kFunctional
InterpCouple.monotone_kFunctional.docstring: The K-functional `t ↦ K(t, u)` is monotone (Bonn's `monotone_kNorm`).

InterpCouple.mem_of_complexity_norm1_le.name: InterpCouple.mem_of_complexity_norm1_le
InterpCouple.mem_of_complexity_norm1_le.docstring:
For increasing sets, an element of complexity at most `n` lies in `S n`: every `m` with
`b ∈ S m` exceeds `n` otherwise, and then the complexity is at least `n + 1`.

InterpCouple.memKMethod_ofMap_iff.name: InterpCouple.memKMethod_ofMap_iff
InterpCouple.memKMethod_ofMap_iff.docstring:
The real interpolation space of `ofMap ι` is that of
`ApproximationSpaces.Interpolation.KMethod`.

InterpCouple.memKMethod_leftKCouple_iff.name: InterpCouple.memKMethod_leftKCouple_iff
InterpCouple.memKMethod_leftKCouple_iff.docstring:
**The reiteration theorem for the left endpoint** (Bergh–Löfström, Theorem 3.5.3): for a
couple quasi-normed with constant `C`, `0 < θ₁ < 1`, `0 ≤ η < 1` and `q₁, q ≥ 1`,
`(X₀, (X₀, X₁)_{θ₁,q₁})_{η,q} = (X₀, X₁)_{ηθ₁,q}`.

InterpCouple.memKMethod_leftECouple_iff.name: InterpCouple.memKMethod_leftECouple_iff
InterpCouple.memKMethod_leftECouple_iff.docstring:
**E-spaces are interpolation spaces** (Pietsch, J. Approx. Theory 32 (1981); DeVore–Popov,
LNM 1302 (1988); DeVore, Acta Numer. 7 (1998), §4.3, Theorem 2): if `A` is quasi-normed with
constant `C` and its complexity is subadditive, then for `r > 0`, `0 < η < 1` and
`0 < q, q₁ ≤ ∞`, `u` lies in the real interpolation space `(N₀, E_{r,q₁})_{η,q}` iff
`‖u‖^dy_{ηr,q} < ∞`. The two halves are `InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_interpNorm_of_jackson`
(with Jackson's inequality `InterpCouple.eFunctional_two_pow_le_dyadicWeight_mul`) and
`InterpCouple.interpNorm_leftECouple_le_eNormDyadic`, on the grid `t = 2^(-kr)` of the ordered
quasi-normed couple `(N₀, E_{r,q₁})` (`InterpCouple.memKMethod_iff_interpNorm_lt_top`).

InterpCouple.memKMethod_kMethodCouple_if.name: InterpCouple.memKMethod_kMethodCouple_iff
InterpCouple.memKMethod_kMethodCouple_if.docstring:
**The reiteration theorem for the continuous K-norms**: under the hypotheses of
`memKMethod_kCouple_iff`, `((X₀, X₁)_{θ₀,q₀}, (X₀, X₁)_{θ₁,q₁})_{η,q} = (X₀, X₁)_{θ,q}` with
`θ = (1 - η) θ₀ + η θ₁`, for the continuous K-norms `‖·‖_{K,θ_i,q_i}` of the two K-spaces.

InterpCouple.memKMethod_iff_of_discreteK.name: InterpCouple.memKMethod_iff_of_discreteKMethodNorm_le
InterpCouple.memKMethod_iff_of_discreteK.docstring:
**Equal spaces from comparable discrete K-norms**: for couples `A`, `B`, finite constants
`c, c'`, `η ≥ 0`, `ρ > 0` and `θ ≥ 0`, if `‖u‖^B_{η,ρ,q} ≤ c ‖u‖^A_{θ,1,q}` and
`‖u‖^A_{θ,1,q} ≤ c' ‖u‖^B_{η,ρ,q}`, then `u ∈ (Y₀, Y₁)_{η,q}` if and only if
`u ∈ (X₀, X₁)_{θ,q}` (`memKMethod_iff_discreteKMethodNorm_lt_top`).

InterpCouple.memKMethod_iff_interpNorm_l.name: InterpCouple.memKMethod_iff_interpNorm_lt_top
InterpCouple.memKMethod_iff_interpNorm_l.docstring:
**The continuous K-method and the grid on `ℕ`**, for an ordered couple: if the couple is
quasi-normed with constant `C` and `N₀ ≤ c N₁` with `c < ∞`, then for `θ > 0`, `ρ > 0` and
`q ≠ 0`, `‖u‖_{K,θ,q} < ∞` if and only if `N₀(u) + ‖(2^(kρθ) K(2^(-kρ), u))_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`.

InterpCouple.memKMethod_iff_discreteKMet.name: InterpCouple.memKMethod_iff_discreteKMethodNorm_lt_top
InterpCouple.memKMethod_iff_discreteKMet.docstring:
**The discrete and the continuous K-method agree** (Bergh–Löfström, Lemma 3.1.3; Bonn's
`discreteKMethod_equiv_kmethod`): for `θ ≥ 0`, `ρ > 0` and every `q`, `‖u‖_{K,θ,q} < ∞` if and
only if `‖(2^(-nρθ) K(2^(nρ), u))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`.

InterpCouple.memKMethod_eCouple_iff.name: InterpCouple.memKMethod_eCouple_iff
InterpCouple.memKMethod_eCouple_iff.docstring:
**The reiteration theorem for E-spaces** (for approximation spaces: Pietsch, J. Approx.
Theory 32 (1981); DeVore–Lorentz, Chapter 7): if `A` is quasi-normed with constant `C`
and its complexity is subadditive, then for `0 < s₀ < s₁`, `0 < η < 1` and
`1 ≤ q₀, q₁, q ≤ ∞`, `(E_{s₀,q₀}, E_{s₁,q₁})_{η,q} = E_{(1-η)s₀+ηs₁,q}`: `u` lies in the real
interpolation space of the couple `(E_{s₀,q₀}, E_{s₁,q₁})` iff
`‖u‖^dy_{(1-η)s₀+ηs₁,q} < ∞`. Both spaces are represented in the couple `(N₀, E_{r,∞})` with
`r = s₁ + 1`, whose discrete K-norms are comparable with the dyadic norms
(`InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_discreteKMethodNorm_leftECouple`,
`InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_leftECouple_le_eNormDyadic`), and the reiteration theorem
`InterpCouple.memKMethod_kCouple_iff` with `InterpCouple.memKMethod_leftECouple_iff` gives the
result. The fine indices `≥ 1` are those of the reiteration theorem.

InterpCouple.memKMethod_congr.name: InterpCouple.memKMethod_congr
InterpCouple.memKMethod_congr.docstring:
**Equivalent couples give the same interpolation spaces**: if `N₀' ≤ c₀ N₀`, `N₁' ≤ c₁ N₁`,
`N₀ ≤ c₀' N₀'` and `N₁ ≤ c₁' N₁'` with finite constants, then
`(X₀, X₁)_{θ,q} = (X₀', X₁')_{θ,q}`.

InterpCouple.lqNorm_kFunctional_leftECou.name: InterpCouple.lqNorm_kFunctional_leftECouple_le_of_nearBest
InterpCouple.lqNorm_kFunctional_leftECou.docstring:
**Bernstein's half in `ℓ_q`**: under the hypotheses of
`InterpCouple.kFunctional_leftECouple_le_of_nearBest`, for `s ≤ r` and every `q`, with
`ρ₁ = min(1, q₁)` and `L = ‖(2^(ks) e_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q}`,
`‖(2^(ks) K(2^(-kr), u))_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤
C_q (C_q ((1 + C) L + C N₀(u) γ_{r-s,q}) + ((2C)^ρ₁ H)^(1/ρ₁) L)` for the K-functional of
`(N₀, E_{r,q₁})`, with `H = hardyConst ((r - s)ρ₁) (q/ρ₁)`
(`InterpCouple.lqNorm_kFunctional_le_of_le`). The last term of the bound at one level satisfies
`x_k^ρ₁ = (2C)^ρ₁ ∑_{j<k} 2^(-(k-j)rρ₁) e_j^ρ₁`, so Hardy's inequality for partial sums in
`ρ₁`-th powers (`ENNReal.lqNorm_le_of_rpow_le_sum`) bounds `‖(2^(ks) x_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q}`.

InterpCouple.lqNorm_kFunctional_le_of_le.name: InterpCouple.lqNorm_kFunctional_le_of_le
InterpCouple.lqNorm_kFunctional_le_of_le.docstring:
**The `ℓ_q` bookkeeping of Bernstein's halves**: for a couple `B`, `s ≤ r` and sequences
`e`, `x` and numbers `a, b ∈ [0, ∞]`, if `K(2^(-kr), u) ≤ a e_k + b 2^(-kr) + x_k` for every `k`,
then `‖(2^(ks) K(2^(-kr), u))_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C_q (C_q (a ‖(2^(ks) e_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q} + b γ_{r-s,q}) +
‖(2^(ks) x_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q})`, with Mathlib's constant `C_q = LpAddConst q` of the quasi-triangle
inequality (`ENNReal.lqNorm_add_le'`, used twice) and `γ_{r-s,q} = dyadicGeomConst (r - s) q`,
which bounds `‖(2^(-k(r-s)))_k‖_{ℓ_q}`.

InterpCouple.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_mul_eFu.name: InterpCouple.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_mul_eFunctional_add_le
InterpCouple.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_mul_eFu.docstring:
**The dyadic errors with tolerances**: for every couple, `s` and `q`, the sequence
`2^(ks) (E(2^k, f) + N₀(f) 2^(-k(s+1)))` has `ℓ_q` norm at most
`C_q (1 + γ_{1,q}) (N₀(f) + ‖(2^(ks) E(2^k, f))_k‖_{ℓ_q})`, with Mathlib's constant
`C_q = LpAddConst q` and `γ_{1,q} = dyadicGeomConst 1 q`, since
`2^(ks) N₀(f) 2^(-k(s+1)) = N₀(f) 2^(-k)`.

InterpCouple.leftKCouple_discreteKMethod.name: InterpCouple.leftKCouple_discreteKMethodNorm_le
InterpCouple.leftKCouple_discreteKMethod.docstring:
**The reiteration bound for the left endpoint couple**: for a couple quasi-normed with
constant `C`, `q₁, q ≥ 1` and `0 < θ₁ < 1`, the discrete K-norm of `(N₀, ‖·‖_{θ₁,q₁})` on the
grid `t = 2^(nθ₁)` satisfies `‖u‖_{η,q} ≤ endpointReiterationConst C θ₁ η · ‖u‖_{ηθ₁,q}`.

InterpCouple.leftKCouple.name: InterpCouple.leftKCouple
InterpCouple.leftKCouple.docstring:
The **left endpoint couple** `(X₀, (X₀, X₁)_{θ₁,q₁})`: the norm `N₀` and the discrete K-norm
`‖·‖_{θ₁,q₁}` on the grid `t = 2^n`.

InterpCouple.leftECouple.name: InterpCouple.leftECouple
InterpCouple.leftECouple.docstring:
The **couple `(N₀, E_{r,q₁})`** of a couple `A = (N₀, N₁)`: the first norm `N₀` of `A` and the
dyadic norm `‖u‖^dy_{r,q₁} = N₀(u) + ‖(2^(kr) E(2^k, u))_k‖_{ℓ_{q₁}}` of its approximation space
`E_{r,q₁}`. It is the couple of the representation of `E_{s,q}`, `0 < s < r`, as an
interpolation space, the analogue of `ApproximationScheme.leftApproxCouple` (whose case `q₁ = ∞`
is `ApproximationScheme.reprCouple`).

InterpCouple.le_eFunctional.name: InterpCouple.le_eFunctional
InterpCouple.le_eFunctional.docstring: A lower bound of `N₀(u - b)` for every admissible `b` is a lower bound of `E(t, u)`.

InterpCouple.le_eAddConst.name: InterpCouple.le_eAddConst
InterpCouple.le_eAddConst.docstring:
The constant `eAddConst C s q = C C_q (2 + 2^s C_q)` is at least `C`, for every `C`, `s` and
`q`, since `C_q ≥ 1` (`ENNReal.one_le_LpAddConst`) and `2 + 2^s C_q ≥ 1`.

InterpCouple.le_add_mul_kFunctional.name: InterpCouple.le_add_mul_kFunctional
InterpCouple.le_add_mul_kFunctional.docstring:
**An upper bound by decompositions passes to the K-functional**: if
`F ≤ X + c (N₀(u - b) + t N₁(b))` for every `b` and `c < ∞`, then `F ≤ X + c K(t, u)`, since
`b ↦ X + c (N₀(u - b) + t N₁(b))` has the infimum `X + c K(t, u)`.

InterpCouple.kSumBelow_le.name: InterpCouple.kSumBelow_le
InterpCouple.kSumBelow_le.docstring:
**The sum below `m` under a pointwise bound**: if `K(2^n, v) ≤ a K(2^n, u) + 2^(n-m) X` for
every `n < m`, then `S₀(m; v) ≤ a S₀(m; u) + 2^(-mθ) (1 - 2^(-(1-θ)))⁻¹ X`.

InterpCouple.kSumBelow.name: InterpCouple.kSumBelow
InterpCouple.kSumBelow.docstring:
The sum `S₀(m) = ∑_{n < m} 2^(-nθ) K(2^n, u)` of the terms below `m` of the discrete
K-method on the grid `t = 2^n`, indexed by `n = m - (j + 1)`, `j ∈ ℕ`.

InterpCouple.kSumAbove_le.name: InterpCouple.kSumAbove_le
InterpCouple.kSumAbove_le.docstring:
**The sum from `m` on under a pointwise bound**: if `K(2^n, v) ≤ a K(2^n, u) + X` for every
`n ≥ m`, then `S₁(m; v) ≤ a S₁(m; u) + 2^(-mθ) (1 - 2^(-θ))⁻¹ X`.

InterpCouple.kSumAbove.name: InterpCouple.kSumAbove
InterpCouple.kSumAbove.docstring:
The sum `S₁(m) = ∑_{n ≥ m} 2^(-nθ) K(2^n, u)` of the terms from `m` on of the discrete
K-method on the grid `t = 2^n`, indexed by `n = m + j`, `j ∈ ℕ`.

InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_ofMap.name: InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_ofMap
InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_ofMap.docstring: The continuous K-norm of `ofMap ι` is `ApproximationScheme.inclKMethodNorm ι`.

InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_map_le.name: InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_map_le
InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_map_le.docstring:
**The interpolation property of the K-method** (Bergh–Löfström, Theorems 3.1.2 and 3.11.2):
the K-method is exact of exponent `θ`.  If `T : U → V` is additive with `N₀'(T a) ≤ M₀ N₀(a)`
and `N₁'(T a) ≤ M₁ N₁(a)` for every `a`, and `0 < M₀, M₁ < ∞`, then
`‖T u‖_{K,θ,q} ≤ M₀^(1-θ) M₁^θ ‖u‖_{K,θ,q}` for every `θ`, `q` and `u`.  Bounds with `M_i = 0`
can be enlarged.

InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_le_of_kFunction.name: InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_le_of_kFunctional_le
InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_le_of_kFunction.docstring:
**The K-norm under a rescaled bound of the K-functional**: if `0 < M₀, M₁ < ∞` and
`K'(t, v) ≤ M₀ K((M₁/M₀) t, u)` for every `0 < t < ∞`, then
`‖v‖_{K,θ,q} ≤ M₀^(1-θ) M₁^θ ‖u‖_{K,θ,q}`, by the dilation formula for `Φ_{θ,q}`.

InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_le_mul_discrete.name: InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_le_mul_discreteKMethodNorm
InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_le_mul_discrete.docstring:
The continuous K-norm by the discrete K-norm on the grid `t = 2^n`: for `θ ≥ 0`,
`‖u‖_{K,θ,q} ≤ (log 2)^(1/q) 2^θ ‖u‖_{θ,1,q}` (`kMethodNorm_le_discreteKMethodNorm` with
`ρ = 1`).

InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_le_interpNorm.name: InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_le_interpNorm
InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_le_interpNorm.docstring:
**The continuous K-norm by the norm on the grid `ℕ`**: if `N₁(0) = 0`, `θ ≥ 0` and `ρ > 0`,
then `‖u‖_{K,θ,q} ≤ c (N₀(u) + ‖(2^(kρθ) K(2^(-kρ), u))_k‖_{ℓ_q})` with the constant
`c = ApproximationScheme.kMethodUpperConst θ ρ q` of the couples of bounded linear maps.

InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_le_discreteKMet.name: InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_le_discreteKMethodNorm
InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_le_discreteKMet.docstring:
**The continuous K-norm by the discrete one**: for `θ ≥ 0` and `ρ > 0`,
