`‖u‖_{K,θ,q} ≤ (ρ log 2)^(1/q) 2^(ρθ) ‖(2^(-nρθ) K(2^(nρ), u))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q}`.

InterpCouple.kMethodNorm.name: InterpCouple.kMethodNorm
InterpCouple.kMethodNorm.docstring:
The norm of the **continuous K-method** of the couple, `‖u‖_{K,θ,q} = Φ_{θ,q}(K(·, u))`,
that is `(∫_0^∞ (t^(-θ) K(t, u))^q dt/t)^(1/q)` for `0 < q < ∞`, the essential supremum of
`t^(-θ) K(t, u)` for `q = ∞`, and `0` for `q = 0` (Bergh–Löfström, Sections 3.1 and 3.11; the
norm of Bonn's `kMethod`).

InterpCouple.kMethodCouple.name: InterpCouple.kMethodCouple
InterpCouple.kMethodCouple.docstring:
The couple of two K-spaces with the **continuous K-norms** `‖·‖_{K,θ₀,q₀}` and
`‖·‖_{K,θ₁,q₁}`.

InterpCouple.kFunctional_two_rpow_le_dis.name: InterpCouple.kFunctional_two_rpow_le_discreteKMethodNorm
InterpCouple.kFunctional_two_rpow_le_dis.docstring:
The class `C_K` on the grid `t = 2^n`: `K(2^n, u) ≤ 2^(nθ) ‖u‖_{θ,1,q}` for every `n ∈ ℤ`
and `q ≠ 0` (`kFunctional_le_discreteKMethodNorm` with `ρ = 1`).

InterpCouple.kFunctional_ofMap.name: InterpCouple.kFunctional_ofMap
InterpCouple.kFunctional_ofMap.docstring:
**The K-functional of `ofMap ι`** is the K-functional `inf_y (‖f - ι y‖ + t ‖y‖)` of
`ApproximationSpaces.Interpolation.KFunctional`, for `0 < t < ∞`.

InterpCouple.kFunctional_neg.name: InterpCouple.kFunctional_neg
InterpCouple.kFunctional_neg.docstring:
The K-functional of a couple of even functions is even: `K(t, -u) = K(t, u)` if
`N₀(-a) = N₀(a)` and `N₁(-a) = N₁(a)` for every `a`, by the substitution `b ↦ -b`.  For a
quasi-normed couple `hA` the hypotheses are `hA.norm0_neg` and `hA.norm1_neg`.

InterpCouple.kFunctional_map_le_of_decom.name: InterpCouple.kFunctional_map_le_of_decomp
InterpCouple.kFunctional_map_le_of_decom.docstring:
**One decomposition under a map**: if `T u = T (u - b) + T b`,
`N₀'(T (u - b)) ≤ M₀ N₀(u - b)` and `N₁'(T b) ≤ M₁ N₁(b)`, then
`K'(t, T u) ≤ M₀ N₀(u - b) + t M₁ N₁(b)`.

InterpCouple.kFunctional_map_le.name: InterpCouple.kFunctional_map_le
InterpCouple.kFunctional_map_le.docstring:
**The K-functional under an additive map** (Bergh–Löfström (3.1.8)): if `T : U → V` is
additive with `N₀'(T a) ≤ M₀ N₀(a)` and `N₁'(T a) ≤ M₁ N₁(a)` for every `a`, and `0 < M₀ < ∞`,
then `K'(t, T u) ≤ M₀ K((M₁/M₀) t, u)` for every `t` and `u`.

InterpCouple.kFunctional_leftKCouple_le.name: InterpCouple.kFunctional_leftKCouple_le
InterpCouple.kFunctional_leftKCouple_le.docstring:
**Holmstedt's formula for the left endpoint couple**, the upper bound in `ℓ₁` form (with an
`ℓ₁` sum in place of the `ℓ_{q₁}` norm of Bergh–Löfström, Theorem 3.6.1, which is enough for
the reiteration theorem): for a couple quasi-normed with constant `C`, `q₁ ≥ 1`, `0 < θ₁ < 1`,
`m ∈ ℤ` and `s = 2^(mθ₁)`, the K-functional of `(N₀, ‖·‖_{θ₁,q₁})` satisfies
`K̄(s, u) ≤ endpointHolmstedtConst C θ₁ · s S₁(m)`, with
`S₁(m) = ∑_{n ≥ m} 2^(-nθ₁) K(2^n, u)`.

InterpCouple.kFunctional_leftECouple_le_.name: InterpCouple.kFunctional_leftECouple_le_of_nearBest
InterpCouple.kFunctional_leftECouple_le_.docstring:
**Bernstein's half at one level**: under the hypotheses of
`InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_of_nearBest` and `r ≥ 0`, with `ρ₁ = min(1, q₁)`, the K-functional of
`(N₀, E_{r,q₁})` satisfies
`K(2^(-kr), u) ≤ (1 + C) e_k + C N₀(u) 2^(-kr) + 2^(-kr) · 2C (∑_{j<k} (2^(jr) e_j)^ρ₁)^(1/ρ₁)`,
from `K(2^(-kr), u) ≤ N₀(u - b_k) + 2^(-kr) ‖b_k‖^dy_{r,q₁}` and `2^(-kr) ≤ 1`.

InterpCouple.kFunctional_le_mul_norm1.name: InterpCouple.kFunctional_le_mul_norm1
InterpCouple.kFunctional_le_mul_norm1.docstring: `K(t, u) ≤ t N₁(u)` if `N₀(0) = 0`, from `b = u`.

InterpCouple.kFunctional_le_discreteKMet.name: InterpCouple.kFunctional_le_discreteKMethodNorm
InterpCouple.kFunctional_le_discreteKMet.docstring:
**The K-functional by the discrete K-norm** (the class `C_K(θ)` of Bergh–Löfström,
Definition 3.5.1, in discrete form): for `q ≠ 0` and every `n ∈ ℤ`,
`K(2^(nρ), u) ≤ 2^(nρθ) ‖(2^(-mρθ) K(2^(mρ), u))_{m ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q}`.

InterpCouple.kFunctional_le.name: InterpCouple.kFunctional_le
InterpCouple.kFunctional_le.docstring:
Every decomposition bounds the K-functional: `K(t, u) ≤ N₀(u - b) + t N₁(b)` (Bonn's
`kNorm_le_of_decomp`).

InterpCouple.kFunctional_kCouple_le.name: InterpCouple.kFunctional_kCouple_le
InterpCouple.kFunctional_kCouple_le.docstring:
**Holmstedt's formula, the upper bound in `ℓ₁` form** (Holmstedt 1970; Bergh–Löfström,
Theorem 3.6.1, in discrete form, with `ℓ₁` sums in place of the `ℓ_{q_i}` norms of
Theorem 3.6.1, which is enough for the reiteration theorem): for a couple quasi-normed with
constant `C`, `q₀, q₁ ≥ 1`, `0 < θ₀, θ₁ < 1`, `m ∈ ℤ` and `s = 2^(m(θ₁-θ₀))`, the K-functional
of the couple of K-spaces satisfies `K̄(s, u) ≤ holmstedtConst C θ₀ θ₁ · (S₀(m) + s S₁(m))`,
with `S₀(m) = ∑_{n < m} 2^(-nθ₀) K(2^n, u)` and `S₁(m) = ∑_{n ≥ m} 2^(-nθ₁) K(2^n, u)`.

InterpCouple.kFunctional_add_le_of_decom.name: InterpCouple.kFunctional_add_le_of_decomp
InterpCouple.kFunctional_add_le_of_decom.docstring:
The pointwise bound behind the quasi-triangle inequality of the K-functional: for all
`b, b'`, `K(t, u + v) ≤ C ((N₀(u - b) + t N₁(b)) + (N₀(v - b') + t N₁(b')))`.

InterpCouple.kFunctional_add_le.name: InterpCouple.kFunctional_add_le
InterpCouple.kFunctional_add_le.docstring:
**The quasi-triangle inequality of the K-functional** (Bergh–Löfström, Lemma 3.11.1; Bonn's
`kNorm_add_le_mul`): `K(t, u + v) ≤ C (K(t, u) + K(t, v))` for a couple quasi-normed with
constant `C`.

InterpCouple.kFunctional.name: InterpCouple.kFunctional
InterpCouple.kFunctional.docstring:
The **K-functional** of the couple, `K(t, u) = inf_b (N₀(u - b) + t N₁(b))` for
`t ∈ [0, ∞]` (Bergh–Löfström, Section 3.1).  It is `kNorm` of the project
*MultilinearInterpolation*, there an infimum over the pairs `u = a + b`.

InterpCouple.kCouple_discreteKMethodNorm.name: InterpCouple.kCouple_discreteKMethodNorm_le
InterpCouple.kCouple_discreteKMethodNorm.docstring:
**The reiteration bound** (the hard inclusion of Bergh–Löfström, Theorems 3.5.3 and
3.11.5): for a couple quasi-normed with constant `C`, `q₀, q₁, q ≥ 1`, `0 < θ₀, θ₁ < 1` and
`θ = (1 - η) θ₀ + η θ₁`, the discrete K-norm of the couple of K-spaces on the grid
`t = 2^(n(θ₁-θ₀))` satisfies `‖u‖_{η,q} ≤ reiterationConst C θ₀ θ₁ η · ‖u‖_{θ,q}`.

InterpCouple.kCouple.name: InterpCouple.kCouple
InterpCouple.kCouple.docstring:
The **couple of two K-spaces** `((X₀, X₁)_{θ₀,q₀}, (X₀, X₁)_{θ₁,q₁})`, with the discrete
K-norms `‖u‖_{θ_i,q_i} = ‖(2^(-nθ_i) K(2^n, u))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_{q_i}}` on the grid `t = 2^n`.

InterpCouple.isQuasiNormed_ofMap.name: InterpCouple.isQuasiNormed_ofMap
InterpCouple.isQuasiNormed_ofMap.docstring: The couple of a bounded linear map is quasi-normed with constant `1`.

InterpCouple.isQuasiNormed_leftECouple.name: InterpCouple.isQuasiNormed_leftECouple
InterpCouple.isQuasiNormed_leftECouple.docstring:
**`(N₀, E_{r,q₁})` is quasi-normed**: if `A` is quasi-normed with constant `C` and its
complexity is subadditive, then for every `r` and every `q₁` the couple `(N₀, E_{r,q₁})` is
quasi-normed with constant `eAddConst C r q₁`: the dyadic norm vanishes at `0`, is even and
satisfies the quasi-triangle inequality with this constant (`InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_zero`,
`InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_neg`, `InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_add_le`), and `N₀` satisfies it since
`C ≤ eAddConst C r q₁` (`InterpCouple.le_eAddConst`).

InterpCouple.interpNorm_zero.name: InterpCouple.interpNorm_zero
InterpCouple.interpNorm_zero.docstring: The norm on the grid `ℕ` vanishes at `0` if both norms do.

InterpCouple.interpNorm_leftECouple_le_e.name: InterpCouple.interpNorm_leftECouple_le_eNormDyadic
InterpCouple.interpNorm_leftECouple_le_e.docstring:
**Bernstein's half of `E_{s,q} = (N₀, E_{r,q₁})_{s/r,q}`**: if `A` is quasi-normed with
constant `C`, `0 ≤ s < r` and `q₁ ≠ 0`, then for every `q` and every `u`,
`‖u‖_{s/r,r,q} ≤ eReprConst C r s q₁ q · ‖u‖^dy_{s,q}`, where
`‖u‖_{s/r,r,q} = N₀(u) + ‖(2^(ks) K(2^(-kr), u))_k‖_{ℓ_q}` is the norm of `(N₀, E_{r,q₁})` on the
grid `t = 2^(-kr)` (`InterpCouple.interpNorm`). The near-best approximants of `u` with their
tolerances (`InterpCouple.exists_nearBest_tolerances`) lie in `E_{r,q₁}` and take the place of
the lifts (`InterpCouple.lqNorm_kFunctional_leftECouple_le_of_nearBest`). Only the quasi-triangle
inequality of `N₀` is used.

InterpCouple.interpNorm_le_kMethodNorm.name: InterpCouple.interpNorm_le_kMethodNorm
InterpCouple.interpNorm_le_kMethodNorm.docstring:
**The norm on the grid `ℕ` by the continuous K-norm**, for an ordered couple: if the couple
is quasi-normed with constant `C`, `N₀ ≤ c N₁` with `c < ∞`, `θ ≥ 0`, `ρ > 0` and `q ≠ 0`, then
`N₀(u) + ‖(2^(kρθ) K(2^(-kρ), u))_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ (1 + C max(1, c)) 2^(ρθ) (ρ log 2)^(-1/q)
‖u‖_{K,θ,q}`.

InterpCouple.interpNorm_le_discreteKMeth.name: InterpCouple.interpNorm_le_discreteKMethodNorm
InterpCouple.interpNorm_le_discreteKMeth.docstring:
**The norm on the grid `ℕ` by the discrete K-norm on `ℤ`**, for an ordered couple: if the
couple is quasi-normed with constant `C`, `N₀ ≤ c N₁` with `c < ∞`, and `q ≠ 0`, then
`N₀(u) + ‖(2^(kρθ) K(2^(-kρ), u))_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ (1 + C max(1, c)) ‖(2^(-nρθ) K(2^(nρ), u))_n‖_{ℓ_q}`.

InterpCouple.interpNorm.name: InterpCouple.interpNorm
InterpCouple.interpNorm.docstring:
The norm `N₀(u) + ‖(2^(kρθ) K(2^(-kρ), u))_{k ∈ ℕ}‖_{ℓ_q}` of the discrete K-method on the
grid `t = 2^(-kρ)`, `k ∈ ℕ`, as in `ApproximationScheme.inclInterpNorm`.

InterpCouple.holmstedtSideConst_ne_top.name: InterpCouple.holmstedtSideConst_ne_top
InterpCouple.holmstedtSideConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant `holmstedtSideConst C α` is finite for `C < ∞` and `0 < α < 1`.

InterpCouple.holmstedtSideConst.name: InterpCouple.holmstedtSideConst
InterpCouple.holmstedtSideConst.docstring: The constant `(1 - 2^(-α))⁻¹ + C (1 - 2^(-(1-α)))⁻¹` of one half of Holmstedt's formula.

InterpCouple.holmstedtConst_ne_top.name: InterpCouple.holmstedtConst_ne_top
InterpCouple.holmstedtConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant `holmstedtConst C θ₀ θ₁` is finite for `C < ∞` and `0 < θ₀, θ₁ < 1`.

InterpCouple.holmstedtConst.name: InterpCouple.holmstedtConst
InterpCouple.holmstedtConst.docstring:
The constant `C + holmstedtSideConst C θ₀ + holmstedtSideConst C (1 - θ₁)` of Holmstedt's
formula for the couple of K-spaces.

InterpCouple.exists_norm0_sub_le_eFuncti.name: InterpCouple.exists_norm0_sub_le_eFunctional_add
InterpCouple.exists_norm0_sub_le_eFuncti.docstring:
**Near-best elements**: if `E(t, u) < ∞` and `ε > 0`, some `b` with `N₁(b) ≤ t` has
`N₀(u - b) ≤ E(t, u) + ε`.

InterpCouple.exists_nearBest_tolerances.name: InterpCouple.exists_nearBest_tolerances
InterpCouple.exists_nearBest_tolerances.docstring:
**Near-best sequences with their tolerances**: if `N₁(0) = 0` and `s ≥ -1`, every `u` has
`b_k` with `N₁(b_k) ≤ 2^k` and a decreasing sequence `e` with `N₀(u - b_k) ≤ e_k`,
`N₀(u) ≤ e_0` and `‖(2^(ks) e_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C_q (1 + γ_{1,q}) ‖u‖^dy_{s,q}` for every `q`, with
Mathlib's constant `C_q = LpAddConst q` and `γ_{1,q} = dyadicGeomConst 1 q`: the near-best
sequence of `InterpCouple.exists_nearBest_eFunctional` with the tolerances
`e_k = E(2^k, u) + N₀(u) 2^(-k(s+1))` (`InterpCouple.antitone_eFunctional_add_dyadicWeight`,
`InterpCouple.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_mul_eFunctional_add_le`).

InterpCouple.exists_nearBest_eFunctional.name: InterpCouple.exists_nearBest_eFunctional
InterpCouple.exists_nearBest_eFunctional.docstring:
**Near-best sequences**: if `N₁(0) = 0`, then for every `u` and `s` there are `b_k` with
`N₁(b_k) ≤ 2^k` and `N₀(u - b_k) ≤ E(2^k, u) + N₀(u) 2^(-k(s+1))`. For `N₀(u) ∈ (0, ∞)` the
tolerance is positive and `E(2^k, u) ≤ N₀(u)` is finite
(`InterpCouple.exists_norm0_sub_le_eFunctional_add`); for `N₀(u) = 0` and for `N₀(u) = ∞` the
element `b_k = 0` is admissible and near-best. Near-best sequences take the role of bounded
linear projections onto the approximants.

InterpCouple.eq_zero_of_complexity_norm1.name: InterpCouple.eq_zero_of_complexity_norm1_lt_one
InterpCouple.eq_zero_of_complexity_norm1.docstring: If `S 0 = {0}`, every `b` with complexity below `1` is `0`.

InterpCouple.endpointReiterationConst_ne.name: InterpCouple.endpointReiterationConst_ne_top
InterpCouple.endpointReiterationConst_ne.docstring:
The constant `endpointReiterationConst C θ₁ η` is finite for `C < ∞`, `0 < θ₁ < 1` and
`η < 1`.

InterpCouple.endpointReiterationConst.name: InterpCouple.endpointReiterationConst
InterpCouple.endpointReiterationConst.docstring:
The constant `endpointHolmstedtConst C θ₁ · (1 - 2^(-(1-η)θ₁))⁻¹` of the reiteration theorem
for the endpoint couples.

InterpCouple.endpointHolmstedtConst_ne_t.name: InterpCouple.endpointHolmstedtConst_ne_top
InterpCouple.endpointHolmstedtConst_ne_t.docstring: The constant `endpointHolmstedtConst C θ₁` is finite for `C < ∞` and `0 < θ₁ < 1`.

InterpCouple.endpointHolmstedtConst.name: InterpCouple.endpointHolmstedtConst
InterpCouple.endpointHolmstedtConst.docstring:
The constant `C + (1 + holmstedtSideConst C (1 - θ₁))` of Holmstedt's formula for the left
endpoint couple.

InterpCouple.eReprUpperConst_ne_top.name: InterpCouple.eReprUpperConst_ne_top
InterpCouple.eReprUpperConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant `eReprUpperConst C r s q` is finite for `C < ∞` and `0 < s < r`.

InterpCouple.eReprUpperConst.name: InterpCouple.eReprUpperConst
InterpCouple.eReprUpperConst.docstring:
The constant of the bound of the discrete K-norm of `(N₀, E_{r,∞})` on the grid `t = 2^n` by
`‖·‖^dy_{s,q}`: `((log 2)^(1/q) 2^(-s/r))⁻¹ · kMethodUpperConst (s/r) r q · eReprConst C r s ∞ q`.

InterpCouple.eReprLowerConst_ne_top.name: InterpCouple.eReprLowerConst_ne_top
InterpCouple.eReprLowerConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant `eReprLowerConst C r s q` is finite for `C < ∞` and `r > 0`.

InterpCouple.eReprLowerConst.name: InterpCouple.eReprLowerConst
InterpCouple.eReprLowerConst.docstring:
The constant of the bound of `‖·‖^dy_{s,q}` by the discrete K-norm of `(N₀, E_{r,∞})` on the
grid `t = 2^n`: `eJacksonConst C 1 s q · (1 + K_r) 2^s (r log 2)^(-1/q) · (log 2)^(1/q) 2^(s/r)`
with `K_r = eAddConst C r ∞`.

InterpCouple.eReprConst_ne_top.name: InterpCouple.eReprConst_ne_top
InterpCouple.eReprConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant `eReprConst C r s q₁ q` is finite for `C < ∞`, `s < r` and `q₁ ≠ 0`.

InterpCouple.eReprConst.name: InterpCouple.eReprConst
InterpCouple.eReprConst.docstring:
The constant of Bernstein's half of the representation `E_{s,q} = (N₀, E_{r,q₁})_{s/r,q}`:
with Mathlib's constant `C_q = LpAddConst q`, `M = C_q (1 + γ_{1,q})`, `ρ₁ = min(1, q₁)` and
`H = hardyConst ((r - s)ρ₁) (q/ρ₁)`, it is
`1 + C_q (C_q ((1 + C) M + C γ_{r-s,q}) + ((2C)^ρ₁ H)^(1/ρ₁) M)`.

InterpCouple.eNormPietsch_lt_top_iff.name: InterpCouple.eNormPietsch_lt_top_iff
InterpCouple.eNormPietsch_lt_top_iff.docstring:
**Pietsch's form and the dyadic norm are finite together**: if `N₁(0) = 0` and only `0` has
complexity below `1`, then for `s ≥ 0` and `q ∈ (0, ∞]`, `‖u‖^P_{s,q} < ∞` iff
`‖u‖^dy_{s,q} < ∞`.

InterpCouple.eNormPietsch_le_eNormDyadic.name: InterpCouple.eNormPietsch_le_eNormDyadic
InterpCouple.eNormPietsch_le_eNormDyadic.docstring:
**Pietsch's form by the dyadic norm**: if `N₁(0) = 0`, then for `s ≥ 0` and every `q`,
`‖u‖^P_{s,q} ≤ C_q 2^s ‖u‖^dy_{s,q}` with `C_q = LpAddConst q`, by Cauchy condensation for the
decreasing sequence `E(n, u)` (`ENNReal.lqNorm_pow_mul_le_dyadic`), whose first term is
`E(0, u) ≤ N₀(u)`.

InterpCouple.eNormPietsch.name: InterpCouple.eNormPietsch
InterpCouple.eNormPietsch.docstring:
**Pietsch's form** of the norm of the approximation space of a couple:
`‖((n + 1)^(s - 1/q) E(n, u))_{n ∈ ℕ}‖_{ℓ_q}`, the weights of Pietsch's quasi-norm of `A^s_q`
(`ApproximationScheme.approxNorm`) with the E-functional at the integers in place of the errors
`E_n(f)`.

InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_zero.name: InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_zero
InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_zero.docstring: **The dyadic norm of `0`** is `0` if both norms vanish at `0`, since then `E(t, 0) = 0`.

InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_neg.name: InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_neg
InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_neg.docstring:
**The dyadic norm of a couple of even functions is even**: if `N₀` and `N₁` are even, then
`‖-u‖^dy_{s,q} = ‖u‖^dy_{s,q}` for all `s` and `q`, termwise by `InterpCouple.eFunctional_neg`.

InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_mono_exponent.name: InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_mono_exponent
InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_mono_exponent.docstring:
**The dyadic norm decreases in the fine index**: `‖u‖^dy_{s,r} ≤ ‖u‖^dy_{s,q}` for
`0 < q ≤ r ≤ ∞`, also below `1`, by the monotonicity of the `ℓ_q` norms
(`ENNReal.lqNorm_le_lqNorm_of_le`).

InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_of_nearBest.name: InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_of_nearBest
InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_of_nearBest.docstring:
**The dyadic norm of a near-best approximant**: under the hypotheses of
`InterpCouple.eFunctional_two_pow_le_of_nearBest`, for every `r`, every `q₁ ≠ 0` and every `k`,
with `ρ₁ = min(1, q₁)`,
`‖b_k‖^dy_{r,q₁} ≤ C (e_k + N₀(u)) + 2C (∑_{j<k} (2^(jr) e_j)^ρ₁)^(1/ρ₁)`. The first term bounds
`N₀(b_k) ≤ C (N₀(u - b_k) + N₀(u))`. The sequence `(2^(jr) E(2^j, b_k))_j` vanishes from `j = k`
on, so its `ℓ_{q₁}` norm is at most its `ℓ_{ρ₁}` norm (`ENNReal.lqNorm_le_lqNorm_of_le`), a finite
sum.

InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_of_lt.name: InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_of_lt
InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_of_lt.docstring:
**Lower smoothness with any fine index**: for `t < s`, `q ≠ 0` and every `r`,
`‖u‖^dy_{t,r} ≤ γ_{s-t,r} ‖u‖^dy_{s,q}` with `γ_{s-t,r} = dyadicGeomConst (s - t) r`, finite
since `s - t > 0`. Every term satisfies `2^(kt) E(2^k, u) ≤ 2^(-k(s-t)) L` with `L` the `ℓ_q`
part of `‖u‖^dy_{s,q}`, the geometric sequence has `ℓ_r` norm at most `γ_{s-t,r}`, and
`N₀(u) ≤ γ_{s-t,r} N₀(u)` since `γ_{s-t,r} ≥ 1` (`ENNReal.one_le_dyadicGeomConst`).

InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_interpNorm_o.name: InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_interpNorm_of_jackson
InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_interpNorm_o.docstring:
**Jackson's half of the representation of `E_{s,q}`**: under the hypotheses of
`InterpCouple.eFunctional_succ_le_kFunctional` and `r ≠ 0`, for every `s`, every `q` and every
`u`, `‖u‖^dy_{s,q} ≤ eJacksonConst C C_J s q · ‖u‖_{s/r,r,q}`, where
`‖u‖_{s/r,r,q} = N₀(u) + ‖(2^(ks) K(2^(-kr), u))_k‖_{ℓ_q}` is the norm of the couple `(N₀, N)` on
the grid `t = 2^(-kr)` (`InterpCouple.interpNorm`). The first term `E(1, u) ≤ N₀(u)` of the `ℓ_q`
norm is split off at the cost `C_q = LpAddConst q` (`ENNReal.lqNorm_le_head_add_shift'`), and
every other term is bounded one level down.

InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_eNormPietsch.name: InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_eNormPietsch
InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_eNormPietsch.docstring:
**The dyadic norm by Pietsch's form**: if only `0` has complexity below `1`, then for `s ≥ 0`
and `q ∈ (0, ∞]`, `‖u‖^dy_{s,q} ≤ 4 C_q² 2^s ‖u‖^P_{s,q}` with `C_q = LpAddConst q`
(`ENNReal.dyadic_le_lqNorm_pow_mul`), since the first term of the decreasing sequence `E(n, u)`
is `E(0, u) ≥ N₀(u)`.

InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_discreteKMet.name: InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_discreteKMethodNorm_leftECouple
InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_discreteKMet.docstring:
**The dyadic norm by the discrete K-norm of `(N₀, E_{r,∞})`**: if `A` is quasi-normed with
constant `C` and its complexity is subadditive, `s ≥ 0`, `r > 0` and `q ≠ 0`, then
`‖u‖^dy_{s,q} ≤ eReprLowerConst C r s q · ‖(2^(-ns/r) K(2^n, u))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q}` for the
K-functional of `(N₀, E_{r,∞})`: Jackson's half
(`InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_interpNorm_of_jackson`), then the comparisons of the norm on the
grid `ℕ` with the continuous and the discrete K-norm (`InterpCouple.interpNorm_le_kMethodNorm`,
`InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_le_mul_discreteKMethodNorm`).

InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_add_le.name: InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_add_le
InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_add_le.docstring:
**The quasi-triangle inequality of the dyadic norm** (Bergh–Löfström, Lemma 7.1.6, in dyadic
form): for a couple quasi-normed with constant `C` whose complexity is subadditive,
`‖u + v‖ ≤ C C_q (2 + 2^s C_q) (‖u‖ + ‖v‖)` for the norm `N₀(u) + ‖(2^(ks) E(2^k, u))_k‖_{ℓ_q}`,
by `E(2^(k+1), u + v) ≤ C (E(2^k, u) + E(2^k, v))` and the shift by one level.

InterpCouple.eNormDyadic.name: InterpCouple.eNormDyadic
InterpCouple.eNormDyadic.docstring:
The **dyadic norm** of `E_{s,q}`: `N₀(u) + ‖(2^(ks) E(2^k, u))_{k ∈ ℕ}‖_{ℓ_q}`. For the
complexity couple of an approximation scheme it is the dyadic quasi-norm of `A^s_q`.

InterpCouple.eJacksonConst_ne_top.name: InterpCouple.eJacksonConst_ne_top
InterpCouple.eJacksonConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant `eJacksonConst C C_J s q` is finite for `C, C_J < ∞`.

InterpCouple.eJacksonConst.name: InterpCouple.eJacksonConst
InterpCouple.eJacksonConst.docstring:
The constant `1 + C_q (1 + 2^s C max(1, C_J))` of Jackson's half of the representation of
`E_{s,q}`, with Mathlib's constant `C_q = LpAddConst q`, for a couple quasi-normed with constant
`C` and Jackson's inequality with constant `C_J`.

InterpCouple.eFunctional_two_pow_le_of_n.name: InterpCouple.eFunctional_two_pow_le_of_nearBest
InterpCouple.eFunctional_two_pow_le_of_n.docstring:
**The E-functionals of near-best approximants**: let `A` be quasi-normed with constant `C`,
and let `N₁(b_k) ≤ 2^k` and `N₀(u - b_k) ≤ e_k` for every `k`, with `e` decreasing. Then
`E(2^j, b_k) = 0` for `j ≥ k`, since `b_k` itself is admissible, and
`E(2^j, b_k) ≤ N₀(b_k - b_j) ≤ C (e_j + e_k) ≤ 2C e_j` for `j < k`, from
`b_k - b_j = (u - b_j) - (u - b_k)`.

InterpCouple.eFunctional_two_pow_le_dyad.name: InterpCouple.eFunctional_two_pow_le_dyadicWeight_mul
InterpCouple.eFunctional_two_pow_le_dyad.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality for `E_{r,q₁}`**: for `q₁ ≠ 0`, every `b` and every `k`,
`E(2^k, b) ≤ 1 · 2^(-kr) ‖b‖^dy_{r,q₁}`, since `2^(kr) E(2^k, b)` is one term of the `ℓ_{q₁}` part
of the dyadic norm (`ENNReal.le_dyadicWeight_neg_mul_lqNorm`).

InterpCouple.eFunctional_succ_le_kFuncti.name: InterpCouple.eFunctional_succ_le_kFunctional
InterpCouple.eFunctional_succ_le_kFuncti.docstring:
**Jackson's half at one level**: let `A` be quasi-normed with constant `C` and subadditive
complexity, and let `N : U → [0, ∞]` satisfy Jackson's inequality
`E(2^k, g) ≤ C_J 2^(-kr) N(g)` for all `k` and `g`, with `C_J < ∞`. Then
`E(2^(k+1), u) ≤ C max(1, C_J) K(2^(-kr), u)` for the K-functional of the couple `(N₀, N)`:
for every `g`, `E(2^(k+1), u) ≤ C (E(2^k, u - g) + E(2^k, g)) ≤ C (N₀(u - g) + C_J 2^(-kr) N(g))`
(`InterpCouple.eFunctional_add_le`), and the infimum over `g` passes to the K-functional
(`InterpCouple.le_add_mul_kFunctional`). The hypothesis `C_J < ∞` is needed: on `U = ℝ²` with
`N₀(x, y) = |x| + |y|`, only `0` as approximant, `N(x, 0) = |x|` and `N(x, y) = |y|` for `y ≠ 0`,
Jackson's inequality holds with `C_J = ∞` and `K(t, (1, 0)) = 0` along `g = (1, 1/n)`, while
`E(2^(k+1), (1, 0)) = 1`.

InterpCouple.eFunctional_neg.name: InterpCouple.eFunctional_neg
InterpCouple.eFunctional_neg.docstring:
The E-functional of a couple of even functions is even: `E(t, -u) = E(t, u)`, by the
substitution `b ↦ -b`.

InterpCouple.eFunctional_le.name: InterpCouple.eFunctional_le
InterpCouple.eFunctional_le.docstring: Every admissible element bounds the E-functional: `E(t, u) ≤ N₀(u - b)` if `N₁(b) ≤ t`.

InterpCouple.eFunctional_complexity_natC.name: InterpCouple.eFunctional_complexity_natCast
InterpCouple.eFunctional_complexity_natC.docstring:
**The E-functional of the complexity couple at an integer** is the error of best
approximation from `S n`: for increasing sets, `E(n, u) = inf_{b ∈ S n} N(u - b)`.

InterpCouple.eFunctional_anti.name: InterpCouple.eFunctional_anti
InterpCouple.eFunctional_anti.docstring:
**The E-functional decreases in `t`** (Bergh–Löfström, Lemma 7.1.1): more elements are
admissible for a larger `t`.

InterpCouple.eFunctional_add_le_of_le.name: InterpCouple.eFunctional_add_le_of_le
InterpCouple.eFunctional_add_le_of_le.docstring:
The decomposition bound behind the subadditivity of the E-functional: if `N₀` satisfies the
quasi-triangle inequality with constant `C`, `N₁` is subadditive, `N₁(b) ≤ t` and `N₁(b') ≤ s`,
then `E(t + s, u + v) ≤ C (N₀(u - b) + N₀(v - b'))`.

InterpCouple.eFunctional_add_le.name: InterpCouple.eFunctional_add_le
InterpCouple.eFunctional_add_le.docstring:
**Subadditivity of the E-functional** (Bergh–Löfström, Lemma 7.1.1, with `c₀ = 1`): if `N₀`
satisfies the quasi-triangle inequality with a finite constant `C`, `N₁(0) = 0` and `N₁` is
subadditive, then `E(t + s, u + v) ≤ C (E(t, u) + E(s, v))`. The hypothesis `N₁(0) = 0` serves
the case `C = 0`, in which `N₀` vanishes and the left side is `0` once `b = 0` is admissible.

InterpCouple.eFunctional.name: InterpCouple.eFunctional
InterpCouple.eFunctional.docstring:
The **E-functional** of a couple `A = (N₀, N₁)`: the error of best approximation of `u` in
`N₀` by elements of complexity `N₁(b) ≤ t`, `E(t, u) = inf {N₀(u - b) : N₁(b) ≤ t}`, with the
value `∞` if no `b` has `N₁(b) ≤ t` (Bergh–Löfström, Section 7.1). Bergh–Löfström put the
complexity first: their `E(t, a; A₀, A₁)` is `eFunctional` of the swapped couple
`(‖·‖_{A₁}, ‖·‖_{A₀})`.

InterpCouple.eDyadicUpperConst.name: InterpCouple.eDyadicUpperConst
InterpCouple.eDyadicUpperConst.docstring:
The constant `(log 2)^(1/q) C_q (2^α + γ_{α,q})` of the bound of `‖·‖_{α,q;E}` by the dyadic
norm, with `C_q = LpAddConst q` and `γ_{α,q} = dyadicGeomConst α q`.

InterpCouple.eCouple.name: InterpCouple.eCouple
InterpCouple.eCouple.docstring:
The **couple `(E_{s₀,q₀}, E_{s₁,q₁})`** of a couple `A`: the dyadic norms `‖·‖^dy_{s₀,q₀}` and
`‖·‖^dy_{s₁,q₁}` of two of its approximation spaces, the analogue of
`ApproximationScheme.approxCouple`.

InterpCouple.eAddConst_ne_top.name: InterpCouple.eAddConst_ne_top
InterpCouple.eAddConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant `eAddConst C s q` is finite for `C < ∞`.

InterpCouple.eAddConst.name: InterpCouple.eAddConst
InterpCouple.eAddConst.docstring:
The constant `C C_q (2 + 2^s C_q)` of the quasi-triangle inequality of the dyadic norm, for a
couple quasi-normed with constant `C` and Mathlib's constant `C_q = LpAddConst q`.

InterpCouple.dyadicWeight_succ_mul_eFunc.name: InterpCouple.dyadicWeight_succ_mul_eFunctional_add_le
InterpCouple.dyadicWeight_succ_mul_eFunc.docstring:
One level up: `2^((k+1)s) E(2^(k+1), u + v) ≤ 2^s C (2^(ks) E(2^k, u) + 2^(ks) E(2^k, v))`
for a couple quasi-normed with constant `C` with subadditive complexity, since
`2^(k+1) = 2^k + 2^k` (`eFunctional_add_le`).

InterpCouple.discreteKSeq_one.name: InterpCouple.discreteKSeq_one
InterpCouple.discreteKSeq_one.docstring:
The term `n` of the discrete K-method on the grid `t = 2^n`:
`2^(-nθ) K(2^n, u)`.

InterpCouple.discreteKSeq_le_of_kFunctio.name: InterpCouple.discreteKSeq_le_of_kFunctional_le
InterpCouple.discreteKSeq_le_of_kFunctio.docstring:
The termwise bound behind `discreteKMethodNorm_le_of_kFunctional_le`: for a couple `A`
quasi-normed with constant `C` and a couple `B = (M₀, M₁)` with
`K_A(2^n, a) ≤ 2^(nθ_i) M_i(a)` for `i = 0, 1`, every `n ∈ ℤ` and every `a`, and for
`θ = (1 - η) θ₀ + η θ₁`, `2^(-nθ) K_A(2^n, u) ≤ C 2^(-n(θ₁-θ₀)η) K_B(2^(n(θ₁-θ₀)), u)`.

InterpCouple.discreteKSeq.name: InterpCouple.discreteKSeq
InterpCouple.discreteKSeq.docstring:
The sequence `(2^(-nρθ) K(2^(nρ), u))_{n ∈ ℤ}` of the discrete K-method on the grid
`t = 2^(nρ)`.

InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_sub_le_.name: InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_sub_le_kSumBelow
InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_sub_le_.docstring:
**The first half of Holmstedt's bound**: for a couple quasi-normed with constant `C`,
`q ≥ 1`, `m ∈ ℤ` and `u, b ∈ U`, with `J = N₀(u - b) + 2^m N₁(b)`,
`‖u - b‖_{θ,q} ≤ C S₀(m; u) + 2^(-mθ) holmstedtSideConst C θ · J`.

InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_leftECo.name: InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_leftECouple_le_eNormDyadic
InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_leftECo.docstring:
**The discrete K-norm of `(N₀, E_{r,∞})` by the dyadic norm**: if `A` is quasi-normed with
constant `C` and `0 < s < r`, then for every `q`,
`‖(2^(-ns/r) K(2^n, u))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ eReprUpperConst C r s q · ‖u‖^dy_{s,q}`: Bernstein's half
(`InterpCouple.interpNorm_leftECouple_le_eNormDyadic`), then the comparisons of the norm on the
grid `ℕ` with the continuous and the discrete K-norm (`InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_le_interpNorm`,
`InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_mul_kMethodNorm`).

InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_of_k.name: InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_of_kFunctional_le
InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_of_k.docstring:
**The easy inclusion of the reiteration theorem** (the class `C_K` of Bergh–Löfström,
Definition 3.5.1, and the first half of the proof of Theorem 3.5.3): let `A` be quasi-normed
with constant `C` and let `B = (M₀, M₁)` be a couple with `K_A(2^n, a) ≤ 2^(nθ_i) M_i(a)` for
`i = 0, 1`, every `n ∈ ℤ` and every `a`.  Then for `θ = (1 - η) θ₀ + η θ₁`, the discrete
K-norms of `A` on the grid `2^n` and of `B` on the grid `2^(n(θ₁-θ₀))` satisfy
`‖u‖_{θ,q} ≤ C ‖u‖^B_{η,q}`.

InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_mul_.name: InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_mul_kMethodNorm
InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_mul_.docstring:
The discrete K-norm on the grid `t = 2^n` by the continuous K-norm: for `θ ≥ 0`,
`‖u‖_{θ,1,q} ≤ ((log 2)^(1/q) 2^(-θ))⁻¹ ‖u‖_{K,θ,q}` (`discreteKMethodNorm_le_inv_mul_kMethodNorm`
with `ρ = 1`).

InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_left.name: InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_leftKCouple
InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_left.docstring:
**The easy inclusion for the left endpoint couple**: for a couple quasi-normed with
constant `C` and `q₁ ≠ 0`, `‖u‖_{ηθ₁,q} ≤ C ‖u‖_{η,q}`, where the right side is the discrete
K-norm of `leftKCouple` on the grid `t = 2^(nθ₁)`.

InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_kSum.name: InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_kSumAbove_add_kSumBelow
InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_kSum.docstring:
The discrete K-norm on the grid `2^n` is at most the sum of all its terms, split at `m`:
`‖v‖_{θ,q} ≤ S₁(m) + S₀(m)` for `q ≥ 1`.

InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_kSum.name: InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_kSumAbove
InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_kSum.docstring:
**The second half of Holmstedt's bound**: for a couple quasi-normed with constant `C`,
`q ≥ 1`, `m ∈ ℤ` and `u, b ∈ U`, with `J = N₀(u - b) + 2^m N₁(b)`,
`‖b‖_{θ,q} ≤ C S₁(m; u) + 2^(-mθ) holmstedtSideConst C (1 - θ) · J`.

InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_kMet.name: InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_kMethodNorm
InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_kMet.docstring:
**The discrete K-norm by the continuous one**: for `θ ≥ 0` and `ρ > 0`,
`(ρ log 2)^(1/q) 2^(-ρθ) ‖(2^(-nρθ) K(2^(nρ), u))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ‖u‖_{K,θ,q}`.

InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_kCou.name: InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_kCouple
InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_kCou.docstring:
**The easy inclusion for the couple of K-spaces**: for a couple quasi-normed with constant
`C`, `q₀, q₁ ≠ 0` and `θ = (1 - η) θ₀ + η θ₁`, `‖u‖_{θ,q} ≤ C ‖u‖_{η,q}`, where the right side is
the discrete K-norm of `kCouple` on the grid `t = 2^(n(θ₁-θ₀))`.

InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_inv_.name: InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_inv_mul_kMethodNorm
InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_inv_.docstring:
**The discrete K-norm by the continuous one, solved for the discrete norm**: for `θ ≥ 0` and
`ρ > 0`, `‖(2^(-nρθ) K(2^(nρ), u))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ((ρ log 2)^(1/q) 2^(-ρθ))⁻¹ ‖u‖_{K,θ,q}`
(`discreteKMethodNorm_le_kMethodNorm`).

InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_inte.name: InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_interpNorm
InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_inte.docstring:
**The discrete K-norm on `ℤ` by the norm on the grid `ℕ`**: if `N₁(0) = 0` and `ρθ ≥ 0`,
`‖(2^(-nρθ) K(2^(nρ), u))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C_q γ (N₀(u) + ‖(2^(kρθ) K(2^(-kρ), u))_k‖_{ℓ_q})`
with `γ = dyadicGeomConst (ρθ) q` and Mathlib's constant `C_q = LpAddConst q`.

InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_eq.name: InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_eq
InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_eq.docstring:
The discrete K-norm is the `ℓ_q` norm of `ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq θ ρ` for
`φ = K(·, u)`.

InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm.name: InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm
InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm.docstring:
The norm of the **discrete K-method** on the grid `t = 2^(nρ)`, `n ∈ ℤ`:
`‖(2^(-nρθ) K(2^(nρ), u))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q}`.  For `ρ = 1` it is the norm of Bonn's
`discreteKMethod`.

InterpCouple.complexity_norm1_zero.name: InterpCouple.complexity_norm1_zero
InterpCouple.complexity_norm1_zero.docstring: If `0 ∈ S 0`, the element `0` has complexity `0`.

InterpCouple.complexity_norm1_neg.name: InterpCouple.complexity_norm1_neg
InterpCouple.complexity_norm1_neg.docstring: If every `S n` is symmetric, the complexity is even.

InterpCouple.complexity_norm1_le_of_mem.name: InterpCouple.complexity_norm1_le_of_mem
InterpCouple.complexity_norm1_le_of_mem.docstring: An element of `S n` has complexity at most `n`.

InterpCouple.complexity_norm1_add_le.name: InterpCouple.complexity_norm1_add_le
InterpCouple.complexity_norm1_add_le.docstring: If `S m + S n ⊆ S (m + n)`, the complexity is subadditive.

InterpCouple.complexity.name: InterpCouple.complexity
InterpCouple.complexity.docstring:
The **complexity couple** of a function `N : U → [0, ∞]` and a sequence of sets `S n`:
`N₀ = N` and `N₁(b) = min {n : b ∈ S n}`, with `N₁(b) = ∞` if `b` lies in no `S n`.

InterpCouple.antitone_eFunctional_natCas.name: InterpCouple.antitone_eFunctional_natCast
InterpCouple.antitone_eFunctional_natCas.docstring: The E-functional at the integers decreases: `E(n, u) ≥ E(m, u)` for `n ≤ m`.

InterpCouple.antitone_eFunctional_add_dy.name: InterpCouple.antitone_eFunctional_add_dyadicWeight
InterpCouple.antitone_eFunctional_add_dy.docstring:
**The tolerances decrease**: `e_k = E(2^k, u) + N₀(u) 2^(-k(s+1))` decreases in `k` for
`s ≥ -1`, since `E(t, u)` decreases in `t` and `2^(-k(s+1))` in `k`.

InterpCouple.MemKMethod.of_le.name: InterpCouple.MemKMethod.of_le
InterpCouple.MemKMethod.of_le.docstring:
**Smaller norms give larger interpolation spaces**: if `N₀' ≤ c₀ N₀` and `N₁' ≤ c₁ N₁` with
finite `c₀, c₁`, then `(X₀, X₁)_{θ,q} ⊆ (X₀', X₁')_{θ,q}`.

InterpCouple.MemKMethod.map.name: InterpCouple.MemKMethod.map
InterpCouple.MemKMethod.map.docstring:
**Interpolation spaces are mapped into interpolation spaces**: if `T : U → V` is additive
with `N_i'(T a) ≤ M_i N_i(a)` for every `a` and finite `M₀, M₁`, then `T u ∈ (X₀', X₁')_{θ,q}`
for every `u ∈ (X₀, X₁)_{θ,q}`.  The bounds hold with the constants `max(1, M_i) ∈ (0, ∞)`
(Mathlib's `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right` and `le_max_right`), and `kMethodNorm_map_le` applies.

InterpCouple.MemKMethod.name: InterpCouple.MemKMethod
InterpCouple.MemKMethod.docstring:
`u` belongs to the **real interpolation space** `(X₀, X₁)_{θ,q}` of the couple:
`‖u‖_{K,θ,q} < ∞`.

InterpCouple.IsQuasiNormed.name: InterpCouple.IsQuasiNormed
InterpCouple.IsQuasiNormed.docstring:
The couple is **quasi-normed with constant `C`**: `C < ∞`, and both `N_i` vanish at `0`,
are even and satisfy the quasi-triangle inequality `N_i(a + b) ≤ C (N_i(a) + N_i(b))`.  These are
the axioms of a quasi-normed abelian group (Bergh–Löfström, Section 3.10) except definiteness;
the zero and quasi-triangle axioms are those of `EQuasinorm` in *MultilinearInterpolation*, which
lives on a monoid and asks `C ≥ 1`.

InterpCouple.name: InterpCouple
InterpCouple.docstring:
A **couple** on an additive commutative group `U`: two functions `N₀, N₁ : U → [0, ∞]`,
whose spaces are `X_i = {u : N_i(u) < ∞}`.  This is a couple of quasi-normed abelian groups of
Bergh–Löfström, Section 3.10, with the compatibility of Section 2.3 built in, since both spaces
lie in `U`; the axioms are the separate propositions `InterpCouple.IsQuasiNormed` and
`InterpCouple.IsHomogeneousCouple`.  `EQuasinorm.Couple` of the project *MultilinearInterpolation*
(Bonn, Apache 2.0) carries the axioms in its data.

HasSum.of_tendsto_of_lqNorm_dyadicWeight.name: HasSum.of_tendsto_of_lqNorm_dyadicWeight_lt_top
HasSum.of_tendsto_of_lqNorm_dyadicWeight.docstring:
**A weighted `ℓ_q` bound gives the sum**: for `s > 0` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, a sequence `b_j` in a
complete normed group with `‖(2^(js) ‖b_j‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞` is absolutely summable
(`ENNReal.tsum_le_lqNorm_dyadicWeight`), so its sum is the limit `f` of its partial sums.

HasSum.enorm_sub_sum_range_le.name: HasSum.enorm_sub_sum_range_le
HasSum.enorm_sub_sum_range_le.docstring:
**The tail of a convergent series**: if `∑_i a_i = f`, then
`‖f - ∑_{i<n} a_i‖ ≤ ∑_{i ≥ 0} ‖a_{i+n}‖`.

Haar.vol.name: Haar.vol
Haar.vol.docstring: Lebesgue measure on `[0, 1]`, as a measure on `ℝ` (`Interval.unitVol`).

Haar.toLp_mem_closure.name: Haar.toLp_mem_closure
Haar.toLp_mem_closure.docstring:
**Bounded continuous functions are limits of dyadic step functions** in `L_p[0, 1]`, even
uniformly on `[0, 1)`: they lie in the closure of the Haar approximants.

Haar.sum_fin_eq_of_ne.name: Haar.sum_fin_eq_of_ne
Haar.sum_fin_eq_of_ne.docstring:
A sum over the positions of level `j` whose terms vanish away from the index of a point
`x ∈ [0, 1)` is the term at that index.

Haar.stronglyMeasurable_stepFun.name: Haar.stronglyMeasurable_stepFun
Haar.stronglyMeasurable_stepFun.docstring: The step function of level `j` is `ℱ_j`-measurable.

Haar.stepFun.name: Haar.stepFun
Haar.stepFun.docstring:
The dyadic step function `x ↦ g(⌊2^j x⌋ 2^(-j))` of `g`: the value of `g` at the left end
point of the dyadic interval of level `j` containing `x`.

Haar.setIntegral_haarDyadicInterval.name: Haar.setIntegral_haarDyadicInterval
Haar.setIntegral_haarDyadicInterval.docstring: The integral over `I_{j,n}` is the sum of the integrals over its two halves.

Haar.measurable_haarFunction.name: Haar.measurable_haarFunction
Haar.measurable_haarFunction.docstring: Haar functions are measurable: they are functions of `⌊2^(j+1) x⌋`.

Haar.haarScheme.name: Haar.haarScheme
Haar.haarScheme.docstring:
The **Haar scheme** in `L_p[0, 1]`: the approximants of complexity `2^j` are the step
functions on the dyadic intervals of level `j`.

Haar.haarFunction.name: Haar.haarFunction
Haar.haarFunction.docstring:
The **Haar function** `h_{j,m} = 2^(j/2) (1_{I_{j+1,2m}} - 1_{I_{j+1,2m+1}})`, supported on
`I_{j,m}` and normalised in `L_2`.

Haar.haarDyadicInterval_subset.name: Haar.haarDyadicInterval_subset
Haar.haarDyadicInterval_subset.docstring:
For `0 ≤ n < 2^j`, the dyadic interval `I_{j,n}` lies in `[0, 1)`
(`Interval.dyadicIco_subset`).

Haar.haarDyadicInterval_natCast.name: Haar.haarDyadicInterval_natCast
Haar.haarDyadicInterval_natCast.docstring: For `n ∈ ℕ` the dyadic interval `I_{j,n}` is `Interval.dyadicIco j n`.

Haar.haarDyadicInterval.name: Haar.haarDyadicInterval
Haar.haarDyadicInterval.docstring:
The dyadic interval `I_{j,n} = [n 2^(-j), (n + 1) 2^(-j))`, the fibre of `dyadicIndex j`
over `n` (`Haar.haarDyadicInterval_eq_Ico`).

Haar.haarCoeff.name: Haar.haarCoeff
Haar.haarCoeff.docstring: The **Haar coefficient** `⟨f, h_{j,m}⟩ = ∫ h_{j,m} f` of `f` on `[0, 1]`.

Haar.exists_norm_sub_stepFun_le.name: Haar.exists_norm_sub_stepFun_le
Haar.exists_norm_sub_stepFun_le.docstring:
A uniformly continuous `g` on `[0, 1]` is uniformly close to its step functions: given
`ε > 0` there is a level `j` with `|g(x) - g(⌊2^j x⌋ 2^(-j))| ≤ ε` on `[0, 1)`.

Haar.enorm_haarFunction.name: Haar.enorm_haarFunction
Haar.enorm_haarFunction.docstring: `|h_{j,m}| = 2^(j/2)` on `I_{j,m}`, as a dyadic weight in `ℝ≥0∞`.

Haar.eLpNorm_sum_haar.name: Haar.eLpNorm_sum_haar
Haar.eLpNorm_sum_haar.docstring:
**Level-wise norm of Haar sums**: for `0 < p < ∞`,
`‖∑_{m < 2^j} c_m h_{j,m}‖_p = 2^(j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖c‖_{ℓ_p}`, since the Haar functions of one level
have disjoint supports of measure `2^(-j)` and modulus `2^(j/2)` there.

Haar.dyadicSigma.name: Haar.dyadicSigma
Haar.dyadicSigma.docstring: The dyadic σ-algebra `ℱ_j`, generated by the dyadic intervals of level `j`.

Haar.dyadicIndex_succ_div.name: Haar.dyadicIndex_succ_div
Haar.dyadicIndex_succ_div.docstring:
`⌊2^j x⌋ = ⌊2^(j+1) x⌋ / 2`: the dyadic interval of level `j` containing `x` is the parent of
the one of level `j + 1`.

Haar.dyadicIndex_nonneg.name: Haar.dyadicIndex_nonneg
Haar.dyadicIndex_nonneg.docstring: The index of a point of `[0, 1)` is nonnegative.

Haar.dyadicIndex_lt.name: Haar.dyadicIndex_lt
Haar.dyadicIndex_lt.docstring: The index of a point of `[0, 1)` is `< 2^j`.

Haar.dyadicIndex.name: Haar.dyadicIndex
Haar.dyadicIndex.docstring: The index `⌊2^j x⌋` of the dyadic interval of level `j` containing `x`.

Haar.disjoint_haarDyadicInterval.name: Haar.disjoint_haarDyadicInterval
Haar.disjoint_haarDyadicInterval.docstring: Dyadic intervals of the same level with different indices are disjoint.

Haar.condExp_zero_ae_eq.name: Haar.condExp_zero_ae_eq
Haar.condExp_zero_ae_eq.docstring: `E[f | ℱ_0] = ∫_0^1 f`, a constant, for integrable `f`.

Haar.condExp_succ_sub_ae_eq.name: Haar.condExp_succ_sub_ae_eq
Haar.condExp_succ_sub_ae_eq.docstring:
**Martingale differences are Haar sums**: for integrable `f`,
`E[f | ℱ_{k+1}] - E[f | ℱ_k] = ∑_{m < 2^k} ⟨f, h_{k,m}⟩ h_{k,m}` almost everywhere on `[0, 1]`.

Haar.condExp_dyadic_ae_eq.name: Haar.condExp_dyadic_ae_eq
Haar.condExp_dyadic_ae_eq.docstring:
**Conditional expectation onto `ℱ_j`**: `E[f | ℱ_j](x) = 2^j ∫_{I_{j,⌊2^j x⌋}} f`, the
average of `f` over the dyadic interval of level `j` containing `x`.

Haar.condExpLp_succ_sub_ae_eq.name: Haar.condExpLp_succ_sub_ae_eq
Haar.condExpLp_succ_sub_ae_eq.docstring:
**Martingale differences are Haar sums** in `L_p[0, 1]`, `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`:
`E[f | ℱ_{k+1}] - E[f | ℱ_k] = ∑_{m < 2^k} ⟨f, h_{k,m}⟩ h_{k,m}` (`Haar.condExp_succ_sub_ae_eq`).

Haar.closure_iUnion_haarScheme.name: Haar.closure_iUnion_haarScheme
Haar.closure_iUnion_haarScheme.docstring: **The Haar approximants are dense** in `L_p[0, 1]` for `1 ≤ p < ∞`.

FunctionScheme.toLp_ofContinuous.name: FunctionScheme.toLp_ofContinuous
FunctionScheme.toLp_ofContinuous.docstring:
**The scheme of `T` in `L_p`**: for `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, the approximants of `(ofContinuous T μ)^(p)`
are the `L_p` classes of the elements of `T`.

FunctionScheme.toLp.name: FunctionScheme.toLp
FunctionScheme.toLp.docstring:
The scheme `S^(p)` in `L_p(μ)`, `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`: the images `ι_{∞,p}(S n)` of the sets of `S`
under the inclusion `ι_{∞,p} : L_∞ ↪ L_p`.

FunctionScheme.ofContinuous.name: FunctionScheme.ofContinuous
FunctionScheme.ofContinuous.docstring:
The **scheme of functions of a scheme of bounded continuous functions** `T`: the classes in
`L_∞(μ)` of the elements of `T_n`.

FunctionScheme.neg_mem_lpSets.name: FunctionScheme.neg_mem_lpSets
FunctionScheme.neg_mem_lpSets.docstring: The approximants in `L_p` are symmetric: `-S^(p)_n ⊆ S^(p)_n`.

FunctionScheme.nearBestEmbeddingConst_ne.name: FunctionScheme.nearBestEmbeddingConst_ne_top
FunctionScheme.nearBestEmbeddingConst_ne.docstring:
The constant `nearBestEmbeddingConst C α s p r q` is finite for `C < ∞`, `α < s` and
`r ≠ 0`: Hardy's constant `hardyConst ((s - α) ρ_r) (q/ρ_r)` is finite since
`(s - α) ρ_r > 0` (`FunctionScheme.nearBestEmbeddingConst_hardy_ne_top`).

FunctionScheme.nearBestEmbeddingConst_ha.name: FunctionScheme.nearBestEmbeddingConst_hardy_ne_top
FunctionScheme.nearBestEmbeddingConst_ha.docstring:
**The Hardy factor of `nearBestEmbeddingConst` is finite**: with `ρ_r = min(1, r)`, the
factor `hardyConst ((s - α) ρ_r) (q/ρ_r) ^ (1/ρ_r)` is finite for `α < s` and `r ≠ 0`, since
`(s - α) ρ_r > 0` (`ENNReal.hardyConst_ne_top`).

FunctionScheme.nearBestEmbeddingConst.name: FunctionScheme.nearBestEmbeddingConst
FunctionScheme.nearBestEmbeddingConst.docstring:
The **constant of the Besov embedding along a near-best sequence**: with `ρ_p = min(1, p)`,
`ρ_r = min(1, r)`, Mathlib's constant `C_r = LpAddConst r` of the quasi-triangle inequality in
`L_r` and Hardy's constant `H = hardyConst ((s - α) ρ_r) (q/ρ_r)`, it is
`((1 + C_r) C 2^(2α) H^(1/ρ_r) + C_r C) 2^(1/ρ_p)`, where `C` is the constant of a Nikolskii
inequality `‖a‖_r ≤ C n^α ‖a‖_p`.

FunctionScheme.monotone_lpSets.name: FunctionScheme.monotone_lpSets
FunctionScheme.monotone_lpSets.docstring: The approximants in `L_p` increase with the complexity: `S^(p)_m ⊆ S^(p)_n` for `m ≤ n`.

FunctionScheme.mem_toLp_ofContinuous.name: FunctionScheme.mem_toLp_ofContinuous
FunctionScheme.mem_toLp_ofContinuous.docstring:
`g ∈ L_p(μ)` is an approximant of complexity `n` of the scheme of `T` in `L_p` iff it is the
`L_p` class of some element of `T_n`.

FunctionScheme.mem_ofContinuous.name: FunctionScheme.mem_ofContinuous
FunctionScheme.mem_ofContinuous.docstring:
`a ∈ L_∞(μ)` is an approximant of complexity `n` of the scheme of `T` iff it is the class
of some `g ∈ T_n`.

FunctionScheme.mem_lpSets_of_lpCouple_no.name: FunctionScheme.mem_lpSets_of_lpCouple_norm1_le
FunctionScheme.mem_lpSets_of_lpCouple_no.docstring: An element of complexity at most `n` lies in `S^(p)_n`, since the sets increase.

FunctionScheme.mem_lpSets.name: FunctionScheme.mem_lpSets
FunctionScheme.mem_lpSets.docstring: `f ∈ S^(p)_n` iff `f` is the class in `L_p` of some `a ∈ S_n`.

FunctionScheme.memBesov_iff_memApprox.name: FunctionScheme.memBesov_iff_memApprox
FunctionScheme.memBesov_iff_memApprox.docstring:
**For `p ≥ 1` the Besov space is the approximation space**: for `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`,
`f ∈ B^s_{p,q}(Ω, S)` iff `f ∈ A^s_q(L_p(μ), S^(p))`, where `S^(p) = S.toLp p` is the scheme `S`
sent into the normed space `L_p(μ)`.

FunctionScheme.memBesov_iff_eNormDyadic_.name: FunctionScheme.memBesov_iff_eNormDyadic_lt_top
FunctionScheme.memBesov_iff_eNormDyadic_.docstring:
**The Besov space through the dyadic norm**: for `s ≥ 0` and `0 < q ≤ ∞`, `f ∈ B^s_{p,q}` iff
`‖f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) E_{2^k}(f)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`, the dyadic norm of the couple of `S` in `L_p`.
Only `0` has complexity `0`, so Pietsch's form and the dyadic norm are finite together
(`InterpCouple.eNormPietsch_lt_top_iff`).

FunctionScheme.lpSets_zero.name: FunctionScheme.lpSets_zero
FunctionScheme.lpSets_zero.docstring: The only approximant of complexity `0` in `L_p` is `0`: `S^(p)_0 = {0}`.

FunctionScheme.lpSets_add_subset.name: FunctionScheme.lpSets_add_subset
FunctionScheme.lpSets_add_subset.docstring:
The sum of two approximants in `L_p` has at most the sum of their complexities:
`S^(p)_m + S^(p)_n ⊆ S^(p)_{m+n}`.

FunctionScheme.lpSets.name: FunctionScheme.lpSets
FunctionScheme.lpSets.docstring:
The **approximants of a scheme of functions in `L_p`**: for a scheme `S` of essentially
bounded functions and every exponent `p`, the sets `S^(p)_n = ι_{∞,p}(S_n)` of the classes in
`L_p(μ)` of the elements of `S_n`.

FunctionScheme.lpCouple_norm1_zero.name: FunctionScheme.lpCouple_norm1_zero
FunctionScheme.lpCouple_norm1_zero.docstring: The element `0` has complexity `0` in the couple in `L_p`.

FunctionScheme.lpCouple_norm1_add_le.name: FunctionScheme.lpCouple_norm1_add_le
FunctionScheme.lpCouple_norm1_add_le.docstring: The complexity is subadditive: `N₁(f + g) ≤ N₁(f) + N₁(g)`.

FunctionScheme.lpCouple_norm0.name: FunctionScheme.lpCouple_norm0
FunctionScheme.lpCouple_norm0.docstring: The first norm of the couple in `L_p` is the quasi-norm `‖f‖_p`.

FunctionScheme.lpCouple_eq_complexityCou.name: FunctionScheme.lpCouple_eq_complexityCouple
FunctionScheme.lpCouple_eq_complexityCou.docstring:
**For `p ≥ 1` the couple in `L_p` is a complexity couple of an approximation scheme**: the
couple of `S` in `L_p` is the complexity couple of the scheme `S^(p) = S.toLp p`, the image of
`S` in the normed space `L_p(μ)`. The sets agree by definition, and the first norms since
`‖f‖ₑ = ‖f‖_p` on `Lp` (`MeasureTheory.Lp.eNorm_def`).

FunctionScheme.lpCouple.name: FunctionScheme.lpCouple
FunctionScheme.lpCouple.docstring:
The **couple of a scheme of functions in `L_p`**, for every exponent `p`: the complexity
couple of the quasi-norm `N₀(f) = ‖f‖_p` and the approximants `S^(p)_n`, so
that `N₁(f) = inf {n : f ∈ S^(p)_n}`, the least such `n`, and `∞` if `f` lies in no `S^(p)_n`.
It needs only the group structure of `Lp ℂ p μ`, which exists also for `p < 1`.

FunctionScheme.lpBesovCouple.name: FunctionScheme.lpBesovCouple
FunctionScheme.lpBesovCouple.docstring:
The **couple `(L_p, B^{s₁}_{p,q₁})`** of the scheme, for every exponent `p`: the couple
`(N₀, E_{s₁,q₁})` of the couple of `S` in `L_p`, with the quasi-norm `‖f‖_p` of `L_p(μ)` and the
dyadic quasi-norm `‖f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks₁) E_{2^k}(f)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_{q₁}}` of the Besov space
`B^{s₁}_{p,q₁}`.

FunctionScheme.isQuasiNormed_lpCouple.name: FunctionScheme.isQuasiNormed_lpCouple
FunctionScheme.isQuasiNormed_lpCouple.docstring:
**The couple in `L_p` is quasi-normed** with Mathlib's constant `C_p = LpAddConst p`
(`2^(1/p - 1)` for `0 < p < 1`, `1` otherwise), for every exponent `p`: the quasi-triangle
inequality `‖f + g‖_p ≤ C_p (‖f‖_p + ‖g‖_p)` is `eLpNorm_add_le'`, and the complexity is
subadditive, so its quasi-triangle inequality holds with `C_p ≥ 1`.

FunctionScheme.hasNikolskii_ofContinuous.name: FunctionScheme.hasNikolskii_ofContinuous
FunctionScheme.hasNikolskii_ofContinuous.docstring:
**The Nikolskii property of the scheme of a scheme of bounded continuous functions**: if an
approximation scheme `T` of bounded continuous functions satisfies, for every `1 ≤ p < ∞`,
`sup |a| ≤ C n^(D/p) ‖a‖_p` for all `a ∈ T n`, `n ≥ 1`, then its scheme of functions has the
Nikolskii property of dimension `D`, since `‖a‖_∞ ≤ sup |a|`. At `p = ∞` the bound of the
Nikolskii property reads `‖a‖_∞ ≤ C ‖a‖_∞` and holds with `C = 1` for every scheme.

FunctionScheme.exists_uniform_inclusion_.name: FunctionScheme.exists_uniform_inclusion_eq_of_nikolskii
FunctionScheme.exists_uniform_inclusion_.docstring:
**The Besov embedding** in the dyadic norms of the couples, for `0 < p ≤ r ≤ ∞` and
`0 < q ≤ ∞` (the method of the proof of DeVore–Popov 1988, Theorem 7.1; Kerkyacharian–Petrushev
2015, Proposition 6.14, for Besov spaces on Dirichlet spaces): let `S` satisfy the Nikolskii
bound `‖a‖_∞ ≤ C₀ n^(D/p) ‖a‖_p` of dimension `D ≥ 0` at the source exponent `p`
(`FunctionScheme.HasNikolskiiAt`), for instance by having the Nikolskii property, and let
`α = D(1/p - 1/r) < s`. There is `K < ∞` such that every
`f ∈ L_p` whose dyadic norm `‖f‖^dy_{s,q}` in the couple of `S` in `L_p` is finite is the
inclusion of some `g ∈ L_r` with `‖g‖^dy_{s-α,q} ≤ K ‖f‖^dy_{s,q}`, the dyadic norm of `g` in
the couple of `S` in `L_r`. The Nikolskii inequality from `L_p` to `L_r` that the bound at `p`
gives (`FunctionScheme.HasNikolskiiAt.exists_eLpNorm_le_mul`) and near-best approximants
(`FunctionScheme.exists_nearBest_lpCouple`) with the tolerances
`e_k = E(2^k, f) + ‖f‖_p 2^(-k(s+1))`, which decrease
(`InterpCouple.antitone_eFunctional_add_dyadicWeight`) and satisfy
`‖(2^(ks) e_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C_q (1 + γ_{1,q}) ‖f‖^dy_{s,q}`
(`InterpCouple.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_mul_eFunctional_add_le`), give the bound along the near-best
sequence (`FunctionScheme.exists_inclusion_eq_eNormDyadic_le_of_nearBest`), so
`K = nearBestEmbeddingConst C α s p r q · C_q (1 + γ_{1,q})` with `C_q = LpAddConst q` and
`γ_{1,q} = dyadicGeomConst 1 q`. For the dyadic steps on `[0, 1)` (`D = 1`) this is
`Haar.exists_uniform_inclusion_eq_stepCouple`, and the bound of `‖f‖_r` that follows
(`FunctionScheme.exists_eLpNorm_le_eNormDyadic_of_nikolskii`) is
`Haar.exists_eLpNorm_le_eNormDyadic_stepCouple`; its case `r = 1`, `p ≤ 1` holds with an
explicit constant (`Haar.eLpNorm_one_le_eNormDyadic`).

FunctionScheme.exists_nearBest_lpCouple.name: FunctionScheme.exists_nearBest_lpCouple
FunctionScheme.exists_nearBest_lpCouple.docstring:
**Near-best approximants from the scheme**, for every exponent `p`: for every `f ∈ L_p` and
`s ∈ ℝ` there are `b_k ∈ S_{2^k}` with `‖f - b_k‖_p ≤ E(2^k, f) + ‖f‖_p 2^(-k(s+1))`, from the
near-best elements of the couple (`InterpCouple.exists_nearBest_eFunctional`) and a choice of
preimages in `S_{2^k}`. They take the role of bounded linear projections onto the
approximants.

FunctionScheme.exists_inclusion_eq_eNorm.name: FunctionScheme.exists_inclusion_eq_eNormDyadic_le_of_nearBest
FunctionScheme.exists_inclusion_eq_eNorm.docstring:
**The Besov embedding along a near-best sequence**, for `0 < p ≤ r ≤ ∞` and `q ≠ 0`: let
`‖a‖_r ≤ C n^α ‖a‖_p` for all `a ∈ S_n`, `n ≥ 1`, with `C < ∞`, `α < s` and `s > 0`. Let
`f ∈ L_p`, `b_k ∈ S_{2^k}` and a decreasing sequence `e` with `‖f - b_k‖_p ≤ e_k`,
`‖f‖_p ≤ e_0` and `Y = ‖(2^(ks) e_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`. Then `f` is the inclusion of some
`g ∈ L_r` whose dyadic norm in the couple of `S` in `L_r` satisfies
`‖g‖^dy_{s-α,q} ≤ K₀ Y` with `K₀ = nearBestEmbeddingConst C α s p r q`. The terms `e_k` tend to
`0` (`ENNReal.tendsto_zero_of_lqNorm_dyadicWeight_ne_top`, since `s > 0`), the blocks satisfy
the Nikolskii inequality (`FunctionScheme.eLpNorm_sub_succ_le_of_nikolskii`), so
`MeasureTheory.lqNorm_eLpNorm_sub_le_of_nearBest` bounds `X = ‖(2^(k(s-α)) ‖f - b_k‖_r)_k‖_{ℓ_q}`
by `C 2^(2α) 2^(1/ρ_p) H^(1/ρ_r) Y`; `FunctionScheme.exists_inclusion_eq_eNormDyadic_le` gives
`g`, and `‖b_0‖_r ≤ C ‖b_0‖_p ≤ C 2^(1/ρ_p) e_0 ≤ C 2^(1/ρ_p) Y`
(`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_sub_le_two_rpow_mul` with `‖f - 0‖_p ≤ e_0`).

FunctionScheme.exists_inclusion_eq_eNorm.name: FunctionScheme.exists_inclusion_eq_eNormDyadic_le
FunctionScheme.exists_inclusion_eq_eNorm.docstring:
**Membership in `L_r` along approximants**: let `p ≤ r`, `q ≠ 0`, `t ∈ ℝ`, let
`b_k ∈ S_{2^k}`, and let `X = ‖(2^(kt) ‖f - b_k‖_r)_k‖_{ℓ_q}` be finite for some `f ∈ L_p`. Then
`f` is the inclusion of some `g ∈ L_r`, and the dyadic norm of `g` in the couple of `S` in `L_r`
satisfies `‖g‖^dy_{t,q} ≤ C_r (X + ‖b_0‖_r) + X` with Mathlib's constant `C_r = LpAddConst r`.
The error of best approximation of `g` at `2^k` is at most `‖g - b_k‖_r = ‖f - b_k‖_r`
(`FunctionScheme.eFunctional_lpCouple_natCast`), and
`‖g‖_r ≤ C_r (‖f - b_0‖_r + ‖b_0‖_r)` with `‖f - b_0‖_r ≤ X`.

FunctionScheme.eq_zero_of_lpCouple_norm1.name: FunctionScheme.eq_zero_of_lpCouple_norm1_lt_one
FunctionScheme.eq_zero_of_lpCouple_norm1.docstring: Only `0` has complexity below `1` in the couple in `L_p`, since `S^(p)_0 = {0}`.

FunctionScheme.eLpNorm_sub_succ_le_of_ni.name: FunctionScheme.eLpNorm_sub_succ_le_of_nikolskii
FunctionScheme.eLpNorm_sub_succ_le_of_ni.docstring:
**The Nikolskii inequality on the blocks of a dyadic sequence**: if
`‖a‖_r ≤ C n^α ‖a‖_p` for all `a ∈ S_n`, `n ≥ 1`, and `b_k ∈ S_{2^k}` for every `k`, then
`‖b_{k+1} - b_k‖_r ≤ C 2^(2α) 2^(kα) ‖b_{k+1} - b_k‖_p`, since
`b_{k+1} - b_k ∈ S_{2^(k+2)}` (`ApproximationScheme.sub_mem_pow_add_two`) and
`(2^(k+2))^α = 2^(2α) 2^(kα)`.

FunctionScheme.eFunctional_lpCouple_natC.name: FunctionScheme.eFunctional_lpCouple_natCast
FunctionScheme.eFunctional_lpCouple_natC.docstring:
**The E-functional of the couple in `L_p` at a natural number** is the error of best
approximation from `S_n` in `L_p`: `E(n, f) = inf {‖f - a‖_p : a ∈ S_n}`, the quasi-norm taken of
the difference of `f` and the essentially bounded function `a`.

FunctionScheme.besovNorm_eq_approxNorm.name: FunctionScheme.besovNorm_eq_approxNorm
FunctionScheme.besovNorm_eq_approxNorm.docstring:
**For `p ≥ 1` the Besov quasi-norm is Pietsch's quasi-norm of the approximation space**:
`‖f‖_{B^s_{p,q}} = ‖f‖_{A^s_q(L_p(μ), S^(p))}` for `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, where `S^(p) = S.toLp p` is the
scheme `S` sent into the normed space `L_p(μ)`. The couple of `S` in `L_p` is the complexity
couple of `S^(p)` (`FunctionScheme.lpCouple_eq_complexityCouple`), whose Pietsch form is
Pietsch's quasi-norm (`ApproximationScheme.eNormPietsch_complexityCouple`).

FunctionScheme.besovNorm.name: FunctionScheme.besovNorm
FunctionScheme.besovNorm.docstring:
The **Besov quasi-norm** `‖f‖_{B^s_{p,q}} = ‖((n + 1)^(s - 1/q) E_n(f)_p)_n‖_{ℓ_q}` of
`f ∈ L_p(μ)`, for every exponent `p`: Pietsch's form of the couple of `S` in `L_p`, whose
E-functional at `t = n` is the error `E_n(f)_p` of best approximation from `S_n` in `L_p`. It is
meant for `0 < p ≤ ∞` and `0 < q ≤ ∞`: at `q = 0` it vanishes by the convention
`lqNorm 0 = 0`, and at `p = 0` since `eLpNorm f 0 μ = 0`.

FunctionScheme.besovCouple.name: FunctionScheme.besovCouple
FunctionScheme.besovCouple.docstring:
The **couple `(B^{s₀}_{p,q₀}, B^{s₁}_{p,q₁})`** of two Besov spaces of the scheme, on
`L_p(μ)`, for every exponent `p`: the couple `(E_{s₀,q₀}, E_{s₁,q₁})` of the couple of `S` in
`L_p`, with the dyadic quasi-norms `‖f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks_i) E_{2^k}(f)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_{q_i}}` of the two
Besov spaces.

FunctionScheme.SobolevSpace.exists_eq_in.name: FunctionScheme.SobolevSpace.exists_eq_inclusion
FunctionScheme.SobolevSpace.exists_eq_in.docstring:
**The Sobolev embedding** `W^s_p ↪ W^t_r`: for a scheme with the Nikolskii property of
dimension `D ≥ 0`, Sobolev spaces `V` of order `s` in `L_p` and `V'` of order `t` in `L_r`,
`p ≤ r`, and `t < s - D(1/p - 1/r)`, every element of `V` is, as an `L_p` function, the
inclusion of an element of `V'`.

FunctionScheme.MemBesov.of_eNormDyadic_l.name: FunctionScheme.MemBesov.of_eNormDyadic_lt_top
FunctionScheme.MemBesov.of_eNormDyadic_l.docstring:
**A finite dyadic norm gives membership in the Besov space**, for `s ≥ 0` and every fine
index `q`: if `‖f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) E_{2^k}(f)_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`, then `f ∈ B^s_{p,q}`, since
Pietsch's form is at most `C_q 2^s` times the dyadic norm
(`InterpCouple.eNormPietsch_le_eNormDyadic`). No hypothesis on `q` is needed in this direction.

FunctionScheme.MemBesov.mono.name: FunctionScheme.MemBesov.mono
FunctionScheme.MemBesov.mono.docstring:
**Embeddings in the smoothness and fine indices**: for every exponent `p` and
`0 < q ≤ ∞`, if `0 ≤ t` and `t < s`, or `t = s` and `q ≤ q'`, then `B^s_{p,q} ⊆ B^t_{p,q'}`.
The dyadic norms of the couple of `S` in `L_p` compare (`InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_le_of_lt`,
`InterpCouple.eNormDyadic_mono_exponent`), and a finite dyadic norm gives membership for every
fine index (`FunctionScheme.MemBesov.of_eNormDyadic_lt_top`).

FunctionScheme.MemBesov.exists_inclusion.name: FunctionScheme.MemBesov.exists_inclusion_eq_top
FunctionScheme.MemBesov.exists_inclusion.docstring:
**Embedding into `L_∞`**, for `0 < p ≤ ∞` and `0 < q ≤ ∞`: for a scheme with the Nikolskii
bound of dimension `D ≥ 0` at `p` (`FunctionScheme.HasNikolskiiAt`), for instance a scheme with the
Nikolskii property, and `s > D/p`, every `f ∈ B^s_{p,q}` is the inclusion of some
`g ∈ L_∞` lying in `B^{s - D/p}_{∞,q}`. This is the case `r = ∞` of
`FunctionScheme.MemBesov.exists_inclusion_eq_of_nikolskii`, where `D(1/p - 1/∞) = D/p`
(`nikolskiiExponent_top`).

FunctionScheme.MemBesov.name: FunctionScheme.MemBesov
FunctionScheme.MemBesov.docstring:
`f` belongs to the **Besov space** `B^s_{p,q}(Ω, S)`: its Besov quasi-norm is finite. Meant
for `0 < p ≤ ∞` and `0 < q ≤ ∞`; at `p = 0` or `q = 0` every `f` belongs to it
(`FunctionScheme.besovNorm`).

FunctionScheme.HasNikolskiiAt.exists_eLp.name: FunctionScheme.HasNikolskiiAt.exists_eLpNorm_le_mul
FunctionScheme.HasNikolskiiAt.exists_eLp.docstring:
**The Nikolskii inequality from the bound at the source exponent**, for
`0 < p ≤ r ≤ ∞`, in `[0, ∞]` (Ditzian–Prymak 2016, Theorem 2.1, (2.3) with `q = p`): if `S`
satisfies the Nikolskii bound `‖a‖_∞ ≤ C₀ n^(D/p) ‖a‖_p` of dimension `D` at `p`, there is
`C < ∞` with `‖a‖_r ≤ C n^(D(1/p - 1/r)) ‖a‖_p` for all `a ∈ S n`, `n ≥ 1`. Interpolation
between `L_p` and `L_∞` gives `‖a‖_r ≤ (C₀ n^(D/p))^(1 - p/r) ‖a‖_p`
(`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_eLpNorm_top_le`), and `(D/p)(1 - p/r) = D(1/p - 1/r)`
(`nikolskiiExponent_eq_mul_one_sub_div`), so `C = C₀^(1 - p/r)`.

FunctionScheme.HasNikolskiiAt.name: FunctionScheme.HasNikolskiiAt
FunctionScheme.HasNikolskiiAt.docstring:
The **Nikolskii bound of dimension `D` at the exponent `p`**: there is `C < ∞` with
`‖a‖_∞ ≤ C n^(D/p) ‖a‖_p` for all approximants `a ∈ S n`, `n ≥ 1`, as an inequality of extended
nonnegative reals, with the norm `‖a‖_∞` of the class `a` in `L_∞(μ)` and `1/∞ = 0`. A
hypothesis on the scheme at one exponent: the Nikolskii property gives it at every `0 < p ≤ ∞`
(`FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii.hasNikolskiiAt`), and the local Weyl bound of a continuous spectral
basis gives it at every `0 < p ≤ 2` (`ContinuousSpectralBasis.hasNikolskiiAt_basisScheme`). It
yields the Nikolskii inequality from `L_p` to every `L_r`, `p ≤ r ≤ ∞`
(`FunctionScheme.HasNikolskiiAt.exists_eLpNorm_le_mul`), which is all that the Besov embeddings
of `FunctionSpaces.MeasureSpaces.Besov.Embeddings` use. It is meant for `0 < p ≤ ∞`: at `p = 0`
Lean reads `1/0 = 0` and `‖a‖_0 = 0`, so the bound would say that every approximant of
complexity `n ≥ 1` vanishes almost everywhere; every theorem that uses it assumes `p ≠ 0`.

FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii.hasNikolskii.name: FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii.hasNikolskiiAt
FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii.hasNikolskii.docstring:
**The Nikolskii property gives the Nikolskii bound at every exponent `0 < p ≤ ∞`**: under
the Nikolskii property of dimension `D`, `S` satisfies the Nikolskii bound of dimension `D` at
every `p ≠ 0` (`FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii.exists_eLpNorm_top_le`).

FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii.exists_eLpNo.name: FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii.exists_eLpNorm_top_le_of_one_le
FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii.exists_eLpNo.docstring:
**The Nikolskii bound for one exponent `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, in `[0, ∞]`**: under the Nikolskii
property of dimension `D` there is `C < ∞` with `‖a‖_∞ ≤ C n^(D/p) ‖a‖_p` for all `a ∈ S n`,
`n ≥ 1`, as an inequality of extended nonnegative reals. The real bound of the property passes
to `[0, ∞]` because `‖a‖_∞ < ∞` for the class `a ∈ L_∞`.

FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii.exists_eLpNo.name: FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii.exists_eLpNorm_top_le
FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii.exists_eLpNo.docstring:
**The Nikolskii bound for every `0 < p ≤ ∞`** (Ditzian–Prymak 2016, Theorem 2.1, (2.2)):
under the Nikolskii property of dimension `D`, for every `0 < p ≤ ∞` there is `C < ∞` with
`‖a‖_∞ ≤ C n^(D/p) ‖a‖_p` for all `a ∈ S n`, `n ≥ 1`. For `p ≥ 1` this is the property itself
(`FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii.exists_eLpNorm_top_le_of_one_le`). For `p < 1` the property at
`p₀ = 1` gives `‖a‖_∞ ≤ C₁ n^D ‖a‖_1`, and the bootstrap
`MeasureTheory.le_rpow_mul_eLpNorm_of_ae_enorm_le` with the almost everywhere bound
`N = ‖a‖_∞ < ∞` of `|a|` turns it into `‖a‖_∞ ≤ (C₁ n^D)^(1/p) ‖a‖_p = C₁^(1/p) n^(D/p) ‖a‖_p`.
The conclusion is the Nikolskii bound at `p` (`FunctionScheme.HasNikolskiiAt`) written out;
`FunctionScheme.HasNikolskii.hasNikolskiiAt` states it in that form.

FunctionScheme.HasContinuousApproximants.name: FunctionScheme.HasContinuousApproximants
FunctionScheme.HasContinuousApproximants.docstring:
A scheme of functions has **continuous approximants** if every element of every `S_n` is
the class of a bounded continuous function. The range of `BoundedContinuousFunction.toLp` is
Mathlib's subgroup `MeasureTheory.Lp.boundedContinuousFunction ℂ ∞ μ`
(`BoundedContinuousFunction.range_toLp`); the range form fits the closedness of this set,
`BoundedContinuousFunction.isClosed_range_toLp_top`.

FunctionScheme.name: FunctionScheme
FunctionScheme.docstring:
A **scheme of functions** on a measure space `(Ω, μ)`: an approximation scheme of
essentially bounded complex functions, that is, of classes in `L_∞(μ)`.

ENNReal.two_rpow_one_div_le_two_mul_LpAd.name: ENNReal.two_rpow_one_div_le_two_mul_LpAddConst
ENNReal.two_rpow_one_div_le_two_mul_LpAd.docstring:
**`2^(1/q)` and the constant of the quasi-triangle inequality**: `2^(1/q) ≤ 2 C_q` for every
`q`, with Mathlib's constant `C_q = LpAddConst q` (and `1/0 = 1/∞ = 0` for the real value of
`q`). For `0 < q < 1` both sides are equal, since `C_q = 2^(1/q - 1)`; otherwise `C_q = 1` and
the left side is at most `2`.

ENNReal.two_rpow_neg_lt_one.name: ENNReal.two_rpow_neg_lt_one
ENNReal.two_rpow_neg_lt_one.docstring: For `α > 0` the ratio `2 ^ (-α)` of the decaying weights is `< 1`.

ENNReal.two_rpow_mul_two_rpow.name: ENNReal.two_rpow_mul_two_rpow
ENNReal.two_rpow_mul_two_rpow.docstring:
The product rule for powers of `2` in `[0, ∞]`: `2^x 2^y = 2^(x+y)` for all real `x, y`
(Mathlib's `ENNReal.rpow_add` with the side conditions `2 ≠ 0` and `2 ≠ ∞` discharged).

ENNReal.two_pow_rpow_eq_dyadicWeight.name: ENNReal.two_pow_rpow_eq_dyadicWeight
ENNReal.two_pow_rpow_eq_dyadicWeight.docstring: `(2^(jn))^t = 2^(j n t)`: a power of the volume factor `2^(jn)` is a dyadic weight.

ENNReal.tsum_rpow_le_lqNorm_dyadicWeight.name: ENNReal.tsum_rpow_le_lqNorm_dyadicWeight
ENNReal.tsum_rpow_le_lqNorm_dyadicWeight.docstring:
**The sum of powers by the weighted `ℓ_q` norm**: for `q ≠ 0`, every `s` and every `ρ ≥ 0`,
`∑_j a_j^ρ ≤ (1 - 2^(-sρ))⁻¹ ‖(2^(js) a_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q}^ρ`, since
`a_j ≤ 2^(-js) ‖(2^(ks) a_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q}` (`ENNReal.le_dyadicWeight_neg_mul_lqNorm`) and
`∑_j 2^(-jsρ) = (1 - 2^(-sρ))⁻¹`. The constant is finite for `sρ > 0`.

ENNReal.tsum_pow_mul_le_dyadic.name: ENNReal.tsum_pow_mul_le_dyadic
ENNReal.tsum_pow_mul_le_dyadic.docstring:
**Weighted condensation, upper bound**:
`∑ₙ (n+1)^γ b n ≤ b 0 + 2^(max γ 0) ∑ₖ 2^(k(γ+1)) b (2^k)` for decreasing `b`.

ENNReal.tsum_mul_le_of_le.name: ENNReal.tsum_mul_le_of_le
ENNReal.tsum_mul_le_of_le.docstring:
**A series against bounds supported on some indices**: if `u_m ≤ B 1_{P(m)}` for every index
`m`, then `∑_m c_m u_m ≤ B ∑_{m : P(m)} c_m`, for every family `c_m ∈ [0, ∞]`.

ENNReal.tsum_min_two_pow_le.name: ENNReal.tsum_min_two_pow_le
ENNReal.tsum_min_two_pow_le.docstring:
**The dyadic sum of `min(t, t⁻¹)`**: for every `a ∈ [0, ∞]`,
`∑_{j ∈ ℕ} min(2^j a, (2^j a)⁻¹) ≤ 4`. With `j₀` the least `j` such that `2^j a > 1`, the terms
below `j₀` add up to at most `2` (`ENNReal.sum_range_min_two_pow_le`) and the terms from `j₀` on
to at most `2` (`ENNReal.tsum_min_two_pow_add_le`).

ENNReal.tsum_min_two_pow_add_le.name: ENNReal.tsum_min_two_pow_add_le
ENNReal.tsum_min_two_pow_add_le.docstring:
The terms `min(2^{i+j₀} a, (2^{i+j₀} a)⁻¹)` with `2^{j₀} a > 1` add up to at most `2`: they
are at most `2^{-i}`.

ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum_add_sum_of_forall_g.name: ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum_add_sum_of_forall_ge_eq
ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum_add_sum_of_forall_g.docstring:
**Finitely many changed terms**: if `u_j = v_j` for every `j ≥ N`, then
`∑_j u_j ≤ ∑_j v_j + ∑_{i < N} u_i` in `[0, ∞]`.

ENNReal.tsum_le_of_mem_Icc.name: ENNReal.tsum_le_of_mem_Icc
ENNReal.tsum_le_of_mem_Icc.docstring:
**A sum with at most `N + 1` nonzero terms**: if `u_j ≤ M` for every `j` and `u_j ≠ 0` only
for `i₀ ≤ j ≤ i₀ + N`, then `∑_j u_j ≤ (N + 1) M`.

ENNReal.tsum_le_of_dyadic_annulus.name: ENNReal.tsum_le_of_dyadic_annulus
ENNReal.tsum_le_of_dyadic_annulus.docstring:
**At most `N + 1` dyadic scales see a point of an annulus**: for `a > 0`, if `u_j ≤ M` for
every `j` and `u_j ≠ 0` only when `t / 2^j` lies in the annulus `[a, 2^N a]`, then
`∑_j u_j ≤ (N + 1) M`. With `i₀` the least `j` with `u_j ≠ 0`, every such `j` satisfies
`i₀ ≤ j ≤ i₀ + N` (`Nat.le_add_of_dyadic_annulus`, `ENNReal.tsum_le_of_mem_Icc`).

ENNReal.tsum_le_lqNorm_dyadicWeight.name: ENNReal.tsum_le_lqNorm_dyadicWeight
ENNReal.tsum_le_lqNorm_dyadicWeight.docstring:
**Weighted sequences are summable**: `∑_j a_j ≤ (1 - 2^(-s))⁻¹ ‖(2^(js) a_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q}` for
`q ≥ 1`, the case `ρ = 1` of `ENNReal.tsum_rpow_le_lqNorm_dyadicWeight`.

ENNReal.tsum_int_eq_tsum_add_tsum_sub.name: ENNReal.tsum_int_eq_tsum_add_tsum_sub
ENNReal.tsum_int_eq_tsum_add_tsum_sub.docstring:
**A series over `ℤ` split at `m`**:
`∑_{n ∈ ℤ} f n = ∑_{j ≥ 0} f(m + j) + ∑_{j ≥ 0} f(m - (j+1))`, the terms with `n ≥ m` and those
with `n < m` (Mathlib's `tsum_of_nat_of_neg_add_one` after the shift `n ↦ m + n`).

ENNReal.tsum_dyadicWeight_neg_succ_le.name: ENNReal.tsum_dyadicWeight_neg_succ_le
ENNReal.tsum_dyadicWeight_neg_succ_le.docstring:
The geometric series without its first term is at most the full series:
`∑_{j ≥ 0} 2^(-(j+1)α) ≤ (1 - 2^(-α))⁻¹` for every real `α`.

ENNReal.toReal_min_one_pos.name: ENNReal.toReal_min_one_pos
ENNReal.toReal_min_one_pos.docstring: The exponent `ρ = min(1, p)` is positive for `p ≠ 0`, also at `p = ∞`, where `ρ = 1`.

ENNReal.toReal_min_one_of_one_le.name: ENNReal.toReal_min_one_of_one_le
ENNReal.toReal_min_one_of_one_le.docstring: For `p ≥ 1`, including `p = ∞`, the exponent `ρ = min(1, p)` is `1`.

ENNReal.toReal_min_one_of_le_one.name: ENNReal.toReal_min_one_of_le_one
ENNReal.toReal_min_one_of_le_one.docstring: For `p ≤ 1` the exponent `ρ = min(1, p)` is `p`.

ENNReal.toReal_mem_Ioc_of_le_one.name: ENNReal.toReal_mem_Ioc_of_le_one
ENNReal.toReal_mem_Ioc_of_le_one.docstring: An exponent `0 < q ≤ 1` in `[0, ∞]` has real value `q.toReal ∈ (0, 1]`.

ENNReal.tendsto_zero_of_lqNorm_dyadicWei.name: ENNReal.tendsto_zero_of_lqNorm_dyadicWeight_ne_top
ENNReal.tendsto_zero_of_lqNorm_dyadicWei.docstring:
**A sequence with finite weighted `ℓ_q` norm tends to `0`**: for `q ≠ 0` and `s > 0`, if
`‖(2^(ks) e_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`, then `e_j ≤ 2^(-js) ‖(2^(ks) e_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q} → 0`.

ENNReal.tendsto_lqNorm_ite_le.name: ENNReal.tendsto_lqNorm_ite_le
ENNReal.tendsto_lqNorm_ite_le.docstring:
**The tails of a sequence in `ℓ_q` tend to zero**: for `0 < q < ∞` and `‖a‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`,
`‖(0, …, 0, a_N, a_{N+1}, …)‖_{ℓ_q} → 0` as `N → ∞`, since the tails `∑_{k ≥ N} a_k^q` of a
convergent series tend to zero (Mathlib's `ENNReal.tendsto_sum_nat_add`).

ENNReal.sum_range_two_pow_eq.name: ENNReal.sum_range_two_pow_eq
ENNReal.sum_range_two_pow_eq.docstring:
The initial segment `[0, 2^K)` of `ℕ` is `{0}` together with the dyadic blocks
`[2^k, 2^(k+1))`, `k < K`.

ENNReal.sum_range_pow_le_pow_mul_inv.name: ENNReal.sum_range_pow_le_pow_mul_inv
ENNReal.sum_range_pow_le_pow_mul_inv.docstring:
**Geometric partial sums**: `∑_{j < J} r^j ≤ r^J (r - 1)⁻¹` for `1 ≤ r < ∞`, from the
geometric sum `(∑_{j < J} r^j)(r - 1) + 1 = r^J` (Mathlib's `geom_sum_mul_add` with
`x = r - 1`).

ENNReal.sum_range_min_two_pow_le.name: ENNReal.sum_range_min_two_pow_le
ENNReal.sum_range_min_two_pow_le.docstring:
The terms `min(2^j a, (2^j a)⁻¹)` with `2^j a ≤ 1`, the indices `j < j₀`, add up to at most
`2`: they are at most `2^j a`, and `∑_{j < j₀} 2^j a ≤ 2^{j₀} a ≤ 2` when `2^{j₀ - 1} a ≤ 1`.

ENNReal.sum_mul_le_sum_mul_sum.name: ENNReal.sum_mul_le_sum_mul_sum
ENNReal.sum_mul_le_sum_mul_sum.docstring:
`∑_{i ∈ s} a_i b_i ≤ (∑_{i ∈ s} a_i)(∑_{i ∈ s} b_i)` for every finite set `s` and all families
`a, b` in `[0, ∞]`: each `b_i` is at most `∑_{j ∈ s} b_j` (Mathlib's `Finset.single_le_sum`,
`Finset.sum_mul`).

ENNReal.sum_mul_le_lqNorm_two_mul.name: ENNReal.sum_mul_le_lqNorm_two_mul
ENNReal.sum_mul_le_lqNorm_two_mul.docstring:
**The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for finite sums against `ℓ_2` norms**:
`∑_{j ∈ s} a_j b_j ≤ ‖a‖_{ℓ_2} ‖b‖_{ℓ_2}` for every finite set `s` and all families `a, b` in
`[0, ∞]` indexed by a countable set: a finite sum is at most the series
(`sum_le_tsum`), which is the `ℓ_1` norm of the products (`ENNReal.lqNorm_one`), and
`ENNReal.lqNorm_one_mul_le` bounds that.

ENNReal.sum_Ico_pow_mul_le.name: ENNReal.sum_Ico_pow_mul_le
ENNReal.sum_Ico_pow_mul_le.docstring: The weighted sum over a dyadic block is at most `2^(max γ 0) 2^(k(γ+1)) b (2^k)`.

ENNReal.rpow_tsum_rpow_le.name: ENNReal.rpow_tsum_rpow_le
ENNReal.rpow_tsum_rpow_le.docstring:
**The `ℓ_p` sums of a series decrease in `p`**: `(∑_i f_i^q)^(1/q) ≤ (∑_i f_i^p)^(1/p)` for
`0 < p ≤ q` and every family `f` in `[0, ∞]` on any index set, so `‖f‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ‖f‖_{ℓ_p}`; for a
countable index set this is `ENNReal.lqNorm_le_lqNorm_of_le`, the same bound for `ENNReal.lqNorm`.
The subadditivity `ENNReal.rpow_tsum_le_tsum_rpow` with the exponent `p/q ≤ 1`, applied to the
family `f_i^q`, gives `(∑_i f_i^q)^(p/q) ≤ ∑_i f_i^p`; this is the series form of
`ENNReal.rpow_sum_rpow_le`.

ENNReal.rpow_tsum_le_tsum_rpow.name: ENNReal.rpow_tsum_le_tsum_rpow
ENNReal.rpow_tsum_le_tsum_rpow.docstring:
**Subadditivity of `x ↦ x^p` for series**, `0 < p ≤ 1`: `(∑_i f_i)^p ≤ ∑_i f_i^p` for every
family `f` in `[0, ∞]`. A series is the supremum of its finite partial sums
(`tsum_eq_iSup_sum`), the power `x ↦ x^p` commutes with suprema
(`ENNReal.orderIsoRpow`), and `ENNReal.rpow_sum_le_sum_rpow` bounds each partial sum.

ENNReal.rpow_sum_le_sum_rpow.name: ENNReal.rpow_sum_le_sum_rpow
ENNReal.rpow_sum_le_sum_rpow.docstring:
**Subadditivity of `x ↦ x^p` for `0 < p ≤ 1`**: `(∑_{i ∈ s} f_i)^p ≤ ∑_{i ∈ s} f_i^p` for every
finite set `s` and every family `f` in `[0, ∞]` (Mathlib's `Finset.le_sum_of_subadditive` for the
case of two terms, `ENNReal.rpow_add_le_add_rpow`).

ENNReal.rpow_mul_rpow_sub_le.name: ENNReal.rpow_mul_rpow_sub_le
ENNReal.rpow_mul_rpow_sub_le.docstring:
`a^r a^(p-r) ≤ a^p` in `[0, ∞]` for `0 < r` and `p < r`, with equality for `0 < a < ∞`; for
`a = ∞` the left side is `∞ · 0 = 0`.

ENNReal.rpow_mul_rpow_ne_top.name: ENNReal.rpow_mul_rpow_ne_top
ENNReal.rpow_mul_rpow_ne_top.docstring: The constant `a^(1-θ) b^θ` is finite for `0 < a, b < ∞`.

ENNReal.rpow_le_self_of_one_le.name: ENNReal.rpow_le_self_of_one_le
ENNReal.rpow_le_self_of_one_le.docstring:
**`x^z ≤ x` for `x ≥ 1` and `z ≤ 1`** in `[0, ∞]`, the companion of Mathlib's
`ENNReal.rpow_le_self_of_le_one` (`x ≤ 1`, `z ≥ 1`), from Mathlib's
`ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le` and `ENNReal.rpow_one`.

ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow_of_nonpos.name: ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow_of_nonpos
ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow_of_nonpos.docstring: For a nonpositive exponent, `x ↦ x ^ z` is decreasing on `ℝ≥0∞`.

ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow_add_rpow_of_le_of_l.name: ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow_add_rpow_of_le_of_le
ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow_add_rpow_of_le_of_l.docstring: A power of a number between `l` and `u` is at most `l^b + u^b`, whatever the sign of `b`.

ENNReal.rpow_add_rpow_le_LpAddConst_mul.name: ENNReal.rpow_add_rpow_le_LpAddConst_mul
ENNReal.rpow_add_rpow_le_LpAddConst_mul.docstring:
**The `ℓ_q` sum of two numbers**: `(x^q + y^q)^(1/q) ≤ C_q (x + y)` for `0 < q < ∞` and all
`x, y ∈ [0, ∞]`, with Mathlib's constant `C_q = LpAddConst q` (Mathlib's
`ENNReal.rpow_add_le_mul_rpow_add_rpow''` for `x^q` and `y^q`).

ENNReal.one_sub_two_rpow_neg_inv_ne_top.name: ENNReal.one_sub_two_rpow_neg_inv_ne_top
ENNReal.one_sub_two_rpow_neg_inv_ne_top.docstring: The constant `(1 - 2 ^ (-α))⁻¹` of geometric sums is finite for `α > 0`.

ENNReal.one_sub_toReal_div_nonneg.name: ENNReal.one_sub_toReal_div_nonneg
ENNReal.one_sub_toReal_div_nonneg.docstring: The interpolation exponent is nonnegative: `0 ≤ 1 - p/r` for `p ≤ r ≤ ∞`, with `1/∞ = 0`.

ENNReal.one_lt_toReal.name: ENNReal.one_lt_toReal
ENNReal.one_lt_toReal.docstring: An exponent `1 < p < ∞` in `[0, ∞]` has real value `p.toReal > 1`.

ENNReal.one_le_two_mul_two_rpow.name: ENNReal.one_le_two_mul_two_rpow
ENNReal.one_le_two_mul_two_rpow.docstring:
`1 ≤ 2 · 2^s` for `s ≥ 0`: the quasi-triangle constants `2 · 2^s` of the dyadic quasi-norms
dominate the constant `1` of the norm.

ENNReal.one_le_toReal_of_one_le.name: ENNReal.one_le_toReal_of_one_le
ENNReal.one_le_toReal_of_one_le.docstring: For `1 ≤ q < ∞` the exponent `q.toReal` is at least `1`.

ENNReal.one_le_ofReal_mul_inv_of_le.name: ENNReal.one_le_ofReal_mul_inv_of_le
ENNReal.one_le_ofReal_mul_inv_of_le.docstring:
Near the origin the Peetre weight is bounded below: if `a ≤ t` with `0 ≤ t`, then
`1 ≤ (1 + t)^N (1 + a)^(-N)`.

ENNReal.one_le_dyadicGeomConst.name: ENNReal.one_le_dyadicGeomConst
ENNReal.one_le_dyadicGeomConst.docstring: The constant `dyadicGeomConst α q` is at least `1`, for every `α` and `q`.

ENNReal.one_le_LpAddConst.name: ENNReal.one_le_LpAddConst
ENNReal.one_le_LpAddConst.docstring:
Mathlib's constant `LpAddConst q` of the quasi-triangle inequality is at least `1`: it is `1`
outside `(0, 1)` and `2^(1/q - 1)` with `1/q - 1 > 0` inside.

ENNReal.one_div_toReal_sub_one_div_toRea.name: ENNReal.one_div_toReal_sub_one_div_toReal_nonneg
ENNReal.one_div_toReal_sub_one_div_toRea.docstring:
**The exponent of Hölder's inequality between `L_r` and `L_p` is nonnegative**:
`0 ≤ 1/p - 1/r` for `0 < p ≤ r ≤ ∞`, with `1/∞ = 0`. So the constant `μ(Ω)^(1/p - 1/r)` of
Hölder's inequality `‖f‖_p ≤ μ(Ω)^(1/p - 1/r) ‖f‖_r` is finite for a finite measure `μ`.

ENNReal.ofReal_two_rpow.name: ENNReal.ofReal_two_rpow
ENNReal.ofReal_two_rpow.docstring: `ofReal (2^x) = 2^x`: the real power of two as an element of `[0, ∞]`.

ENNReal.ofReal_two_pow_mul_rpow.name: ENNReal.ofReal_two_pow_mul_rpow
ENNReal.ofReal_two_pow_mul_rpow.docstring: `(2^j ρ)^b = ρ^b 2^(jb)` in `[0, ∞]` for `ρ > 0` and every real `b`.

ENNReal.ofReal_one_div_two_pow_rpow.name: ENNReal.ofReal_one_div_two_pow_rpow
ENNReal.ofReal_one_div_two_pow_rpow.docstring:
**Dyadic scales as dyadic weights**: `(2^(-n))^θ = 2^(-nθ)` for every `n ∈ ℕ` and every real
exponent `θ`, as an identity in `[0, ∞]` (`ENNReal.dyadicWeight`); the case `ρ = 1` of
`ENNReal.ofReal_div_two_pow_rpow`.

ENNReal.ofReal_div_two_pow_rpow.name: ENNReal.ofReal_div_two_pow_rpow
ENNReal.ofReal_div_two_pow_rpow.docstring: `(ρ 2^(-j))^b = ρ^b 2^(-jb)` in `[0, ∞]` for `ρ > 0` and every real `b`.

ENNReal.natCast_two_pow_rpow.name: ENNReal.natCast_two_pow_rpow
ENNReal.natCast_two_pow_rpow.docstring: `(2 ^ k) ^ s = 2 ^ (k s)`: the dyadic weight is the power weight at the dyadic point.

ENNReal.mul_div_rpow_eq.name: ENNReal.mul_div_rpow_eq
ENNReal.mul_div_rpow_eq.docstring:
`a (b/a)^θ = a^(1-θ) b^θ` for `0 < a < ∞` and every `b ∈ [0, ∞]`.  For `b = ∞` the power
rule for products holds since both factors `∞` and `a⁻¹` are nonzero
(`ENNReal.mul_rpow_of_ne_zero`).

ENNReal.mul_add_div_mul_mul.name: ENNReal.mul_add_div_mul_mul
ENNReal.mul_add_div_mul_mul.docstring:
`a (x + (b/a) t y) = a x + t (b y)` for `0 < a < ∞`: the rescaled decomposition term of the
K-functional under a map.

ENNReal.monotone_ite_lt.name: ENNReal.monotone_ite_lt
ENNReal.monotone_ite_lt.docstring: **The truncations of a sequence increase**: `J ↦ (a_j 1_{j < J})_j` is monotone.

ENNReal.min_inv_sq_le.name: ENNReal.min_inv_sq_le
ENNReal.min_inv_sq_le.docstring: `min(x, x⁻¹)² ≤ min(x, x⁻¹)` in `ℝ≥0∞`, since `min(x, x⁻¹) ≤ 1` (Mathlib's `sq_le`).

ENNReal.lt_toReal_min_natCast_iff.name: ENNReal.lt_toReal_min_natCast_iff
ENNReal.lt_toReal_min_natCast_iff.docstring:
The level sets of the truncation `min(a, N)`: for `t > 0`, `t < min(a, N)` exactly when
`t < a` and `t < N`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_zero_left.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_zero_left
ENNReal.lqNorm_zero_left.docstring:
The exponent `0` is degenerate: `eLpNorm` assigns it the value `0`.  The statements below
that hold only for genuine exponents carry a hypothesis `q ≠ 0` or `1 ≤ q`; the others hold for
every `q`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_two_sq.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_two_sq
ENNReal.lqNorm_two_sq.docstring:
**The square of the `ℓ_2` norm** is the sum of the squares:
`‖a‖_{ℓ_2}² = ∑_i a_i²` (`ENNReal.lqNorm_rpow` with `q = 2`, natural exponent).

ENNReal.lqNorm_tsum_shift_le.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_tsum_shift_le
ENNReal.lqNorm_tsum_shift_le.docstring:
**Young's inequality for a series of shifts on `ℤ`**: for weights `w_j ≥ 0`, shifts
`s_j ∈ ℤ` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `‖(∑_j w_j c_{m + s_j})_{m ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ (∑_j w_j) ‖c‖_{ℓ_q}`, by the
countable Minkowski inequality and the invariance of the norm under shifts.

ENNReal.lqNorm_tsum_le.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_tsum_le
ENNReal.lqNorm_tsum_le.docstring:
**Minkowski's inequality for series** of families: the norm of a pointwise sum is at most the
sum of the norms (`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_tsum_le` for the counting measure).

ENNReal.lqNorm_tsum_geom_sub_le.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_tsum_geom_sub_le
ENNReal.lqNorm_tsum_geom_sub_le.docstring:
**The geometric convolution from below on `ℤ`**: for `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and every real `α`,
`‖(∑_{j ≥ 0} 2^(-(j+1)α) c_{m-(j+1)})_{m ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ (1 - 2^(-α))⁻¹ ‖c‖_{ℓ_q}`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_tsum_geom_add_le.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_tsum_geom_add_le
ENNReal.lqNorm_tsum_geom_add_le.docstring:
**The geometric convolution from above on `ℤ`**: for `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and every real `α`,
`‖(∑_{j ≥ 0} 2^(-jα) c_{m+j})_{m ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ (1 - 2^(-α))⁻¹ ‖c‖_{ℓ_q}`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_sum_le.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_sum_le
ENNReal.lqNorm_sum_le.docstring: **Minkowski's inequality for finite sums** of families.

ENNReal.lqNorm_shift_le'.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_shift_le'
ENNReal.lqNorm_shift_le'.docstring:
Dropping the first `i` terms does not increase the norm
(`ENNReal.lqNorm_comp_le_of_injective` for `n ↦ n + i`).

ENNReal.lqNorm_shift_le.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_shift_le
ENNReal.lqNorm_shift_le.docstring: Dropping the first term does not increase the norm.

ENNReal.lqNorm_shiftRight_le.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_shiftRight_le
ENNReal.lqNorm_shiftRight_le.docstring:
