Shifting a sequence to the right by `i` places, filling with zeros, does not increase the
norm: the shifted sequence is the extension by zero of `a` along `k ↦ k + i`
(`ENNReal.lqNorm_extend_zero`).

ENNReal.lqNorm_rpow_le_of_rpow_le_tsum.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_rpow_le_of_rpow_le_tsum
ENNReal.lqNorm_rpow_le_of_rpow_le_tsum.docstring:
**A tail inequality in `ℓ_q`, in `ρ`-th powers**: let `ρ > 0`, `β ∈ ℝ` and `c ∈ [0, ∞]`. If
`x_k^ρ ≤ c ∑_{i ≥ 0} 2^(iβ) y_{k+i}^ρ` for every `k`, then
`‖(2^(ks) x_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q}^ρ ≤ c H ‖(2^(ks) y_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q}^ρ` with the constant
`H = hardyConst (sρ - β) (q/ρ)` of Hardy's inequality for tails (`ENNReal.hardy_tail_le'`), which
is finite for `sρ > β`. The `ρ`-th powers pass through `ℓ_{q/ρ}` (`ENNReal.lqNorm_div_fun_rpow`).

ENNReal.lqNorm_rpow_le_of_rpow_le_sum.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_rpow_le_of_rpow_le_sum
ENNReal.lqNorm_rpow_le_of_rpow_le_sum.docstring:
**A partial-sum inequality in `ℓ_q`, in `ρ`-th powers**: let `ρ > 0`, `β ∈ ℝ` and
`c ∈ [0, ∞]`. If `x_k^ρ ≤ c ∑_{j ≤ k} 2^(-(k-j)β) y_j^ρ` for every `k`, then
`‖(2^(ks) x_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q}^ρ ≤ c H ‖(2^(ks) y_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q}^ρ` with the constant
`H = hardyConst (β - sρ) (q/ρ)` of Hardy's inequality for partial sums
(`ENNReal.hardy_sum_le'`), which is finite for `β > sρ`. With `α = β - sρ`,
`2^(ksρ) 2^(-(k-j)β) = 2^(-kα) 2^(jβ)` for `j ≤ k`
(`ENNReal.dyadicWeight_mul_dyadicWeight_neg_sub`), and the `ρ`-th powers pass through
`ℓ_{q/ρ}` (`ENNReal.lqNorm_div_fun_rpow`).

ENNReal.lqNorm_rpow.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_rpow
ENNReal.lqNorm_rpow.docstring: The `q`-th power of the norm is the sum of the `q`-th powers.

ENNReal.lqNorm_pow_mul_rpow.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_pow_mul_rpow
ENNReal.lqNorm_pow_mul_rpow.docstring:
**The `q`-th power of Pietsch's weighted `ℓ_q` norm**: for `0 < q < ∞`,
`‖((n + 1)^(s - 1/q) e_n)_n‖_{ℓ_q}^q = ∑_n (n + 1)^(sq - 1) e_n^q`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_pow_mul_le_dyadic.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_pow_mul_le_dyadic
ENNReal.lqNorm_pow_mul_le_dyadic.docstring:
**Pietsch's weighted `ℓ_q` norm by the dyadic one, for a decreasing sequence**: for
`e_0 ≥ e_1 ≥ ⋯` in `[0, ∞]`, `s ≥ 0` and `q ∈ (0, ∞]`,
`‖((n + 1)^(s - 1/q) e_n)_n‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C_q 2^s (e_0 + ‖(2^(ks) e_{2^k})_k‖_{ℓ_q})` with Mathlib's
constant `C_q = LpAddConst q` (`1` for `q ≥ 1`); for `q = 0` the left side is `lqNorm 0 = 0`.
Cauchy condensation (`ENNReal.tsum_pow_mul_le_dyadic`, `ENNReal.iSup_pow_mul_le_dyadic`)
compares the `q`-th powers, and `(x^q + y^q)^(1/q) ≤ C_q (x + y)`. For `e_n = E_n(f)` this is
`ApproximationScheme.approxNorm_le_approxNormDyadic'`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_one_mul_le.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_one_mul_le
ENNReal.lqNorm_one_mul_le.docstring:
**The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for nonnegative sequences**:
`∑_k a_k b_k ≤ ‖a‖_{ℓ_2} ‖b‖_{ℓ_2}` for families `a, b` in `[0, ∞]` indexed by a countable set
(Mathlib's `ENNReal.lintegral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq` for the counting measure).

ENNReal.lqNorm_mono.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_mono
ENNReal.lqNorm_mono.docstring: The `ℓ_q` norm is monotone in the sequence.

ENNReal.lqNorm_lt_top_iff_of_le_mul.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_lt_top_iff_of_le_mul
ENNReal.lqNorm_lt_top_iff_of_le_mul.docstring:
**Comparable sequences have finite `ℓ_q` norms together**: if `a ≤ M b` and `b ≤ K a` with
finite `K, M`, then `‖a‖_q < ∞ ↔ ‖b‖_q < ∞`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_le_sum_range_add_shift.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_le_sum_range_add_shift
ENNReal.lqNorm_le_sum_range_add_shift.docstring: **Splitting off the first `m` terms**: `‖a‖_q ≤ a 0 + ⋯ + a (m - 1) + ‖(a (n + m))ₙ‖_q`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_le_sum_of_eq_zero.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_le_sum_of_eq_zero
ENNReal.lqNorm_le_sum_of_eq_zero.docstring:
A family that vanishes outside a finite set `s` has `‖a‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ∑_{i ∈ s} a_i` for
`q ≥ 1` (`ENNReal.lqNorm_le_lqNorm_one`).

ENNReal.lqNorm_le_rpow_mul_of_tsum_rpow_.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_le_rpow_mul_of_tsum_rpow_le
ENNReal.lqNorm_le_rpow_mul_of_tsum_rpow_.docstring:
**Comparing `ℓ_q` norms through the sums of `q`-th powers**: for `q < ∞` and families
`a`, `b` in `[0, ∞]` on two countable sets, if `∑_i a_i^q ≤ C ∑_j b_j^q`, then
`‖a‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C^(1/q) ‖b‖_{ℓ_q}` (for `q = 0` the left side is the degenerate value `0`). For
`q ≤ 1` the `q`-th power of an inner series is at most the series of the `q`-th powers, so an
inequality for `ℓ_1` norms transfers to `ℓ_q` this way.

ENNReal.lqNorm_le_of_rpow_le_sum.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_le_of_rpow_le_sum
ENNReal.lqNorm_le_of_rpow_le_sum.docstring:
**The partial-sum inequality in `ℓ_q`, root form**: under the hypotheses of
`ENNReal.lqNorm_rpow_le_of_rpow_le_sum`,
`‖(2^(ks) x_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ (c H)^(1/ρ) ‖(2^(ks) y_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q}` with
`H = hardyConst (β - sρ) (q/ρ)`, by taking the `ρ`-th root
(`ENNReal.le_rpow_one_div_mul_of_rpow_le`).

ENNReal.lqNorm_le_lqNorm_of_le.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_le_lqNorm_of_le
ENNReal.lqNorm_le_lqNorm_of_le.docstring:
**Monotonicity in the exponent**: for `0 < q ≤ r`, `‖a‖_r ≤ ‖a‖_q`, also for exponents below
`1`.  For `r = ∞` every term is at most `‖a‖_q`; for `r < ∞` this is the decrease of the `ℓ_p`
sums of a series in `p` (`ENNReal.rpow_tsum_rpow_le`).

ENNReal.lqNorm_le_head_add_shift'.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_le_head_add_shift'
ENNReal.lqNorm_le_head_add_shift'.docstring:
**Splitting off the first term, for every exponent**:
`‖a‖_q ≤ C_q (a 0 + ‖(a (n + 1))ₙ‖_q)` with Mathlib's constant `C_q = LpAddConst q` of the
quasi-triangle inequality (`ENNReal.lqNorm_add_le'`) for
`a = (a 0, 0, 0, …) + (0, a 1, a 2, …)`; the second summand is the extension by zero of
`(a (n + 1))ₙ` along `n ↦ n + 1` (`ENNReal.lqNorm_extend_zero`).

ENNReal.lqNorm_le_head_add_shift.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_le_head_add_shift
ENNReal.lqNorm_le_head_add_shift.docstring:
**Splitting off the first term**: `‖a‖_q ≤ a 0 + ‖(a (n + 1))ₙ‖_q` for `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, the case
`LpAddConst q = 1` of `ENNReal.lqNorm_le_head_add_shift'`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_le_almostDiagonalConst_mu.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_le_almostDiagonalConst_mul_of_le
ENNReal.lqNorm_le_almostDiagonalConst_mu.docstring:
**The almost diagonal step at one point**: if `a_j ≤ C ∑_i c_{ji} m_i` for every `j`, with
`c_{ji} = 2^(-(j-i)L)` for `i ≤ j` and `c_{ji} = 1` for `i > j`, then for `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`,
`‖(2^(js) a_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C A_{s,L} ‖(2^(is) m_i)_i‖_{ℓ_q}` with
`A_{s,L} = ENNReal.almostDiagonalConst s L`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_ite_le_eq.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_ite_le_eq
ENNReal.lqNorm_ite_le_eq.docstring:
**The `ℓ_q` norm of a tail is the norm of the shifted sequence**: for `0 < q < ∞`,
`‖(0, …, 0, a_N, a_{N+1}, …)‖_{ℓ_q} = ‖(a_{N+k})_k‖_{ℓ_q}` (`ENNReal.tsum_ite_le_eq`).

ENNReal.lqNorm_ite_eq.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_ite_eq
ENNReal.lqNorm_ite_eq.docstring: `‖(…, 0, x, 0, …)‖_{ℓ_q} = x` for a sequence with one nonzero term and every `q ≠ 0`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_indicator.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_indicator
ENNReal.lqNorm_indicator.docstring:
Restricting every member of a family to a set `S` restricts its pointwise `ℓ_q` norm:
`‖(1_S g_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_q} = 1_S(x) ‖(g_i(x))_i‖_{ℓ_q}`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_iSup.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_iSup
ENNReal.lqNorm_iSup.docstring:
**Monotone convergence** for the `ℓ_q` norm: for an increasing sequence of families indexed
by a countable set, the norm of the pointwise supremum is the supremum of the norms
(`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_iSup_of_directed` for the counting measure).

ENNReal.lqNorm_geometric_le.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_geometric_le
ENNReal.lqNorm_geometric_le.docstring:
The norm of a geometric sequence: `‖(r ^ k)ₖ‖_q ≤ (1 - r)⁻¹`, the value of the series
for `q = 1`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_fun_rpow.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_fun_rpow
ENNReal.lqNorm_fun_rpow.docstring:
**Powers inside an `ℓ_u` norm**: `‖(a_i^r)_i‖_{ℓ_u} = ‖a‖_{ℓ_{u r}}^r` for `r > 0`
(`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_fun_rpow` for the counting measure).

ENNReal.lqNorm_extend_zero.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_extend_zero
ENNReal.lqNorm_extend_zero.docstring:
**Extension by zero along an injective map** does not change the `ℓ_q` norm: if
`g : ι → ι'` is injective, the family on `ι'` equal to `a i` at `g i` and to `0` off the range
of `g` has the norm of `a`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_eq_sum.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_eq_sum
ENNReal.lqNorm_eq_sum.docstring: For a finite index set, `‖a‖_{ℓ_q} = (∑_i a_i^q)^(1/q)` for `0 < q < ∞`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_eq_iSup_lqNorm_ite.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_eq_iSup_lqNorm_ite
ENNReal.lqNorm_eq_iSup_lqNorm_ite.docstring:
**`ℓ_q` norms of truncations increase to the norm**: for every sequence `a` in `[0, ∞]`,
`‖a‖_{ℓ_q} = sup_J ‖(a_j 1_{j < J})_j‖_{ℓ_q}`, the case of `ENNReal.lqNorm_iSup` for the
truncations of `a`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadic_succ_le_lqNorm_pow.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadic_succ_le_lqNorm_pow_mul
ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadic_succ_le_lqNorm_pow.docstring:
**The shifted dyadic sequence by Pietsch's weighted norm, for a decreasing sequence**: for
`e_0 ≥ e_1 ≥ ⋯` in `[0, ∞]`, `s ≥ 0` and `q ∈ (0, ∞]`,
`‖(2^(ks) e_{2^(k+1)})_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ 2 C_q P` with `P = ‖((n + 1)^(s - 1/q) e_n)_n‖_{ℓ_q}` Pietsch's
weighted norm; for `q = 0` the left side is `lqNorm 0 = 0`. Cauchy condensation
(`ENNReal.dyadic_le_tsum_pow_mul`) bounds the `q`-th power of the left side by
`2^(max(1 - sq, 0)) P^q`, and `2^(max(1 - sq, 0)) ≤ 2 ≤ (2 C_q)^q`. For `e_n = E_n(f)` this is
`ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_dyadic_succ_le'`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_succ_le_sum.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_succ_le_sum
ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_succ_le_sum.docstring:
**Shifted dyadic weights against a finite sum**: for `m ∈ ℕ`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, a sequence
`b : ℕ → [0, ∞]` and finitely many sequences `c_i : ℕ → [0, ∞]` with
`2^(nm) b_n ≤ ∑_i c_{i,n}` for every `n`,
`‖(2^((n+1)m) b_n)_n‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ 2^m ∑_i ‖c_i‖_{ℓ_q}`, since `2^((n+1)m) = 2^m 2^(nm)`, by the
homogeneity of the `ℓ_q` norm and Minkowski's inequality (`ENNReal.lqNorm_sum_le`).

ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_neg_le_dyadi.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_neg_le_dyadicGeomConst
ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_neg_le_dyadi.docstring:
The geometric sequence for every `q`: `‖(2^(-kα))_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ dyadicGeomConst α q` for
`α ≥ 0`; for `q = 0` the left side is `0`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_neg_eq_dyadi.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_neg_eq_dyadicGeomConst
ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_neg_eq_dyadi.docstring:
**The geometric sequence in `ℓ_q`** for every `q ≠ 0`:
`‖(2^(-kα))_k‖_{ℓ_q} = dyadicGeomConst α q` for `α ≥ 0`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_le_of_head_o.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_le_of_head_of_succ_le
ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_le_of_head_o.docstring:
**A weighted `ℓ_q` norm from its first term and a bound of the others**: if `x_0 ≤ M a` and
`x_{j+1} ≤ A w_{j+1}` for every `j`, then for `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`
`‖(2^(js) x_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ (M + A) (a + ‖(2^(js) w_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q})`. The first term splits off
(`ENNReal.lqNorm_le_head_add_shift`), and the shifted rest is at most `A ‖(2^(js) w_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_div_fun_rpow.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_div_fun_rpow
ENNReal.lqNorm_div_fun_rpow.docstring:
**Powers inside an `ℓ_q` norm, quotient form**: `‖(a_i^r)_i‖_{ℓ_{q/r}} = ‖a‖_{ℓ_q}^r` for
every `r > 0` and every exponent `q`, with `∞ / r = ∞`. For `0 < r ≤ 1` the `r`-th powers of a
sum are subadditive, so estimates in `ℓ_q` for sums of `r`-th powers pass through `ℓ_{q/r}`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_comp_le_of_injective.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_comp_le_of_injective
ENNReal.lqNorm_comp_le_of_injective.docstring:
**Restriction to the range of an injective map** does not increase the `ℓ_q` norm:
`‖a ∘ g‖_q ≤ ‖a‖_q`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_comp_equiv.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_comp_equiv
ENNReal.lqNorm_comp_equiv.docstring: **Reindexing by a bijection** does not change the `ℓ_q` norm: `‖a ∘ e‖_q = ‖a‖_q`.

ENNReal.lqNorm_comp_add_int.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_comp_add_int
ENNReal.lqNorm_comp_add_int.docstring:
**The `ℓ_q` norm on `ℤ` is shift invariant**: `‖(a(k + i))_k‖_{ℓ_q} = ‖a‖_{ℓ_q}` for every
`a : ℤ → [0, ∞]`, every `i ∈ ℤ` and every exponent `q`, since `k ↦ k + i` is a bijection of `ℤ`
(`lqNorm_comp_equiv` for Mathlib's `Equiv.addRight`).

ENNReal.lqNorm_almostDiagonal_le.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_almostDiagonal_le
ENNReal.lqNorm_almostDiagonal_le.docstring:
**An almost diagonal sum in weighted `ℓ_q`**:
`‖(2^(is) ∑_j c_{ij} a_j)_i‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ((1 - 2^(-(L-s)))⁻¹ + (1 - 2^(-s))⁻¹) ‖(2^(js) a_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`
with `c_{ij} = 2^(-(i-j)L)` for `j ≤ i` and `c_{ij} = 1` for `j > i`, by Hardy's inequalities for
the sum below and the tail above the diagonal (finite for `0 < s < L`).

ENNReal.lqNorm_add_le'.name: ENNReal.lqNorm_add_le'
ENNReal.lqNorm_add_le'.docstring:
**The quasi-triangle inequality** for `ℓ_q`, every `q ∈ [0, ∞]`:
`‖a + b‖_q ≤ C_q (‖a‖_q + ‖b‖_q)` with Mathlib's constant `C_q = LpAddConst q`, which is
`2^(1/q - 1)` for `0 < q < 1` and `1` otherwise (`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_add_le'` for the counting
measure).

ENNReal.lqNorm.name: ENNReal.lqNorm
ENNReal.lqNorm.docstring:
The **`ℓ_q` norm** of a family `a : ι → [0, ∞]`: `(∑_i a_i ^ q) ^ (1/q)` for `q < ∞` and
`sup_i a_i` for `q = ∞`, defined as the `L_q` norm for the counting measure.  The index set is `ℕ`
for sequences, `ℕ^d` for the spaces of dominating mixed smoothness and a finite set for the
coefficients of one level of atoms or wavelets; the general lemmas hold for every countable `ι`
with measurable singletons.

ENNReal.le_two_rpow_mul_of_rpow_le.name: ENNReal.le_two_rpow_mul_of_rpow_le
ENNReal.le_two_rpow_mul_of_rpow_le.docstring:
From `x^p ≤ 2 y^p` to `x ≤ 2^(1/p) y`, for `0 < p < ∞`: the case `ρ = p.toReal`, `c = 2` of
`ENNReal.le_rpow_one_div_mul_of_rpow_le`.

ENNReal.le_tsum_of_tendsto_sum.name: ENNReal.le_tsum_of_tendsto_sum
ENNReal.le_tsum_of_tendsto_sum.docstring:
**Subadditive functionals and series**: if `Q` is subadditive, `Q a ≤ C ‖a‖` with `C < ∞`, and
the partial sums of `∑ u_j` converge to `f`, then `Q f ≤ ∑_j Q(u_j)`.

ENNReal.le_tsum_of_tendsto_finsetSum.name: ENNReal.le_tsum_of_tendsto_finsetSum
ENNReal.le_tsum_of_tendsto_finsetSum.docstring:
**Subadditive functionals and multiple series**: if `Q` is subadditive, `Q a ≤ C ‖a‖` with
`C < ∞`, and the partial sums of `∑ u_k` over finite sets `S_J` converge to `F`, then
`Q F ≤ ∑_k Q(u_k)`.

ENNReal.le_sum_Ico_pow_mul.name: ENNReal.le_sum_Ico_pow_mul
ENNReal.le_sum_Ico_pow_mul.docstring: The weighted sum over a dyadic block is at least `2^(-max (-γ) 0) 2^(k(γ+1)) b (2^(k+1))`.

ENNReal.le_rpow_sum_rpow.name: ENNReal.le_rpow_sum_rpow
ENNReal.le_rpow_sum_rpow.docstring:
Every term of a finite family is bounded by its `ℓ_r` norm:
`a_i ≤ (∑_{j ∈ S} a_j^r)^(1/r)` for `i ∈ S` and `r > 0`.

ENNReal.le_rpow_one_div_mul_of_rpow_le.name: ENNReal.le_rpow_one_div_mul_of_rpow_le
ENNReal.le_rpow_one_div_mul_of_rpow_le.docstring:
**From a bound in `ρ`-th powers to the bound itself**: `x^ρ ≤ c y^ρ` implies
`x ≤ c^(1/ρ) y`, for every real `ρ > 0` and all `x, y, c ∈ [0, ∞]`, since `t ↦ t^ρ` is an order
isomorphism of `[0, ∞]` (Mathlib's `ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow_iff`).

ENNReal.le_rpow_mul_of_le_mul_rpow.name: ENNReal.le_rpow_mul_of_le_mul_rpow
ENNReal.le_rpow_mul_of_le_mul_rpow.docstring:
**Cancellation in Hölder's inequality**: for conjugate exponents `u, u'` and `X < ∞`, the
bound `X ≤ K A^{1/u} X^{1/u'}` implies `X ≤ K^u A`, since `X = X^{1/u} X^{1/u'}`.

ENNReal.le_lqNorm.name: ENNReal.le_lqNorm
ENNReal.le_lqNorm.docstring: Every term is bounded by the norm.

ENNReal.le_dyadicWeight_neg_mul_lqNorm.name: ENNReal.le_dyadicWeight_neg_mul_lqNorm
ENNReal.le_dyadicWeight_neg_mul_lqNorm.docstring:
A term of a sequence by the weighted `ℓ_q` norm: `e_j ≤ 2^(-js) ‖(2^(ks) e_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q}` for
`q ≠ 0`.

ENNReal.inv_one_add_mul_pow_le_two_pow.name: ENNReal.inv_one_add_mul_pow_le_two_pow
ENNReal.inv_one_add_mul_pow_le_two_pow.docstring: Halving the scale costs `2^N`: `(1 + a u)^(-N) ≤ 2^N (1 + 2 a u)^(-N)`.

ENNReal.inv_one_add_mul_pow_le.name: ENNReal.inv_one_add_mul_pow_le
ENNReal.inv_one_add_mul_pow_le.docstring:
**Peetre's inequality** for the weights `(1 + a ‖·‖)^(-N)` in `[0, ∞]`: if `u ≤ v + w` and
`a, w < ∞`, then `(1 + a v)^(-N) ≤ (1 + a w)^N (1 + a u)^(-N)`, from
`1 + a u ≤ (1 + a w)(1 + a v)`.

ENNReal.inv_one_add_mul_pow_anti.name: ENNReal.inv_one_add_mul_pow_anti
ENNReal.inv_one_add_mul_pow_anti.docstring: The Peetre weights decrease with the scale: `(1 + b u)^(-N) ≤ (1 + a u)^(-N)` for `a ≤ b`.

ENNReal.inv_le_mul_inv_of_le.name: ENNReal.inv_le_mul_inv_of_le
ENNReal.inv_le_mul_inv_of_le.docstring: `X⁻¹ ≤ c Y⁻¹` in `[0, ∞]` whenever `Y ≤ c X` with `0 < c < ∞`.

ENNReal.iSup_pow_mul_le_dyadic.name: ENNReal.iSup_pow_mul_le_dyadic
ENNReal.iSup_pow_mul_le_dyadic.docstring:
**Condensation for suprema**, upper bound: for decreasing `b` and `s ≥ 0`,
`supₙ (n+1)^s b n ≤ b 0 + 2^s supₖ 2^(ks) b (2^k)`.

ENNReal.hardy_tail_le_of_le_one.name: ENNReal.hardy_tail_le_of_le_one
ENNReal.hardy_tail_le_of_le_one.docstring:
**Hardy's inequality for tails, `0 < q ≤ 1`**:
`‖(2^(kα) ∑_{i ≥ 0} b (k + i))ₖ‖_q ≤ γ_{α,q} ‖(2^(kα) b k)ₖ‖_q` with
`γ_{α,q} = (1 - 2^(-αq))^(-1/q)` (`ENNReal.dyadicGeomConst`); for `q = 0` both sides are the
degenerate value `0`. The `q`-th power of a series is at most the series of the `q`-th powers
(`ENNReal.rpow_tsum_le_tsum_rpow`), and Hardy's inequality for `ℓ_1` with the exponent `αq`
(`ENNReal.hardy_tail_le`) bounds the result.

ENNReal.hardy_tail_le'.name: ENNReal.hardy_tail_le'
ENNReal.hardy_tail_le'.docstring:
**Hardy's inequality for tails, every exponent**:
`‖(2^(kα) ∑_{i ≥ 0} b (k + i))ₖ‖_q ≤ hardyConst α q · ‖(2^(kα) b k)ₖ‖_q` for every `q`, by
`ENNReal.hardy_tail_le` for `q ≥ 1` and `ENNReal.hardy_tail_le_of_le_one` for `q < 1`.

ENNReal.hardy_tail_le.name: ENNReal.hardy_tail_le
ENNReal.hardy_tail_le.docstring:
**Hardy's inequality for tails**: for `α > 0` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`,
`‖(2^(kα) ∑_{i ≥ 0} b (k + i))ₖ‖_q ≤ (1 - 2^(-α))⁻¹ ‖(2^(kα) b k)ₖ‖_q`.

ENNReal.hardy_sum_le_of_le_one.name: ENNReal.hardy_sum_le_of_le_one
ENNReal.hardy_sum_le_of_le_one.docstring:
**Hardy's inequality for partial sums, `0 < q ≤ 1`**:
`‖(2^(-kα) ∑_{j ≤ k} b j)ₖ‖_q ≤ γ_{α,q} ‖(2^(-kα) b k)ₖ‖_q` with
`γ_{α,q} = (1 - 2^(-αq))^(-1/q)` (`ENNReal.dyadicGeomConst`); for `q = 0` both sides are the
degenerate value `0`. The `q`-th power of a finite sum is at most the sum of the `q`-th powers
(`ENNReal.rpow_sum_le_sum_rpow`), and Hardy's inequality for `ℓ_1` with the exponent `αq`
(`ENNReal.hardy_sum_le`) bounds the result.

ENNReal.hardy_sum_le'.name: ENNReal.hardy_sum_le'
ENNReal.hardy_sum_le'.docstring:
**Hardy's inequality for partial sums, every exponent**:
`‖(2^(-kα) ∑_{j ≤ k} b j)ₖ‖_q ≤ hardyConst α q · ‖(2^(-kα) b k)ₖ‖_q` for every `q`, by
`ENNReal.hardy_sum_le` for `q ≥ 1` and `ENNReal.hardy_sum_le_of_le_one` for `q < 1`.

ENNReal.hardy_sum_le.name: ENNReal.hardy_sum_le
ENNReal.hardy_sum_le.docstring:
**Hardy's inequality for partial sums**: for `α > 0` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`,
`‖(2^(-kα) ∑_{j ≤ k} b j)ₖ‖_q ≤ (1 - 2^(-α))⁻¹ ‖(2^(-kα) b k)ₖ‖_q`.

ENNReal.hardyConst_ne_top.name: ENNReal.hardyConst_ne_top
ENNReal.hardyConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant `hardyConst α q` is finite for `α > 0`.

ENNReal.hardyConst.name: ENNReal.hardyConst
ENNReal.hardyConst.docstring:
The constant of Hardy's inequalities for every exponent `q`: `(1 - 2^(-α))⁻¹` for
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` (`ENNReal.hardy_tail_le`, `ENNReal.hardy_sum_le`) and
`γ_{α,q} = (1 - 2^(-αq))^(-1/q)` for `q < 1` (`ENNReal.dyadicGeomConst`).

ENNReal.half_lt_or_half_lt_of_lt_add.name: ENNReal.half_lt_or_half_lt_of_lt_add
ENNReal.half_lt_or_half_lt_of_lt_add.docstring:
If `t < a + b` in `[0, ∞]`, then `t/2 < a` or `t/2 < b`: Mathlib's `lt_or_lt_of_add_lt_add`
applied to `t/2 + t/2 = t`.

ENNReal.exists_one_lt_two_pow_mul.name: ENNReal.exists_one_lt_two_pow_mul
ENNReal.exists_one_lt_two_pow_mul.docstring:
For `a ≠ 0` in `[0, ∞]` there is `j ∈ ℕ` with `2^j a > 1`: Mathlib's
`ENNReal.exists_nat_mul_gt` gives `n a > 1`, and `n < 2^n`.

ENNReal.enorm_le_of_tendsto_sum.name: ENNReal.enorm_le_of_tendsto_sum
ENNReal.enorm_le_of_tendsto_sum.docstring:
**A series with weighted bounds**: if the partial sums of `∑ u_j` converge to `F` and
`‖u_j‖ ≤ K b_j`, then `‖F‖ ≤ K (1 - 2^(-s))⁻¹ ‖(2^(js) b_j)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`
(`ENNReal.tsum_le_lqNorm_dyadicWeight`).

ENNReal.dyadic_le_tsum_pow_mul.name: ENNReal.dyadic_le_tsum_pow_mul
ENNReal.dyadic_le_tsum_pow_mul.docstring:
**Weighted condensation, lower bound**:
`∑ₖ 2^(k(γ+1)) b (2^(k+1)) ≤ 2^(max (-γ) 0) ∑ₙ (n+1)^γ b n` for decreasing `b`.

ENNReal.dyadic_le_lqNorm_pow_mul.name: ENNReal.dyadic_le_lqNorm_pow_mul
ENNReal.dyadic_le_lqNorm_pow_mul.docstring:
**The dyadic norm by Pietsch's weighted norm, for a decreasing sequence**: for
`e_0 ≥ e_1 ≥ ⋯` in `[0, ∞]`, `s ≥ 0` and `q ∈ (0, ∞]`,
`e_0 + ‖(2^(ks) e_{2^k})_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ 4 C_q² 2^s ‖((n + 1)^(s - 1/q) e_n)_n‖_{ℓ_q}` with Mathlib's
constant `C_q = LpAddConst q`. The term `n = 0` gives `e_0`; the first dyadic term is `e_1 ≤ e_0`,
and splitting it off costs `C_q` (`ENNReal.lqNorm_le_head_add_shift'`); the others are bounded by
`ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadic_succ_le_lqNorm_pow_mul`. For `e_n = E_n(f)` this is
`ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_approxNorm'`.

ENNReal.dyadic_le_iSup_pow_mul.name: ENNReal.dyadic_le_iSup_pow_mul
ENNReal.dyadic_le_iSup_pow_mul.docstring:
**Condensation for suprema**, lower bound: for `s ≥ 0`,
`supₖ 2^(ks) b (2^k) ≤ supₙ (n+1)^s b n`.

ENNReal.dyadicWeight_natCast.name: ENNReal.dyadicWeight_natCast
ENNReal.dyadicWeight_natCast.docstring:
For a natural order `L`, the dyadic weight `dyadicWeight L k`, a real power `2^(k·L)` in
`[0, ∞]`, equals the natural power `2^(kL)`.

ENNReal.dyadicWeight_mul_dyadicWeight_ne.name: ENNReal.dyadicWeight_mul_dyadicWeight_neg_sub
ENNReal.dyadicWeight_mul_dyadicWeight_ne.docstring:
**Trading growth for decay**: `2^(ks) 2^(-(k-j)σ) = 2^(-k(σ-s)) 2^(jσ)` for `j ≤ k`, the
identity behind every almost diagonal estimate.

ENNReal.dyadicWeight_mono.name: ENNReal.dyadicWeight_mono
ENNReal.dyadicWeight_mono.docstring: For `s ≥ 0` the dyadic weights increase in `k`.

ENNReal.dyadicWeight_le_of_le.name: ENNReal.dyadicWeight_le_of_le
ENNReal.dyadicWeight_le_of_le.docstring: For a fixed `k`, the weight `2 ^ (k s)` increases with `s`.

ENNReal.dyadicWeight_eq_pow.name: ENNReal.dyadicWeight_eq_pow
ENNReal.dyadicWeight_eq_pow.docstring: The dyadic weights are a geometric sequence with ratio `2 ^ s`.

ENNReal.dyadicWeight.name: ENNReal.dyadicWeight
ENNReal.dyadicWeight.docstring:
The **dyadic weight** `2 ^ (k s)`: the factor by which the error `E_{2^k}` is multiplied
in the dyadic form of an approximation space of smoothness `s`.

ENNReal.dyadicGeomConst_ne_top.name: ENNReal.dyadicGeomConst_ne_top
ENNReal.dyadicGeomConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant `dyadicGeomConst α q` is finite for `α > 0`.

ENNReal.dyadicGeomConst.name: ENNReal.dyadicGeomConst
ENNReal.dyadicGeomConst.docstring:
The constant `(1 - 2^(-α q))^(-1/q)` of the dyadic geometric sequence `(2^(-kα))_k`, with
the value `1` for `q = ∞` (where `q.toReal = 0`).  For `α ≥ 0` and `q ≠ 0` it is the `ℓ_q` norm
of that sequence (`ENNReal.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_neg_eq_dyadicGeomConst`).

ENNReal.div_rpow_le_rpow_mul_div_rpow.name: ENNReal.div_rpow_le_rpow_mul_div_rpow
ENNReal.div_rpow_le_rpow_mul_div_rpow.docstring:
**Dividing by a smaller power**: if `w ≤ c v` with `0 < c < ∞` and `a ≥ 0`, then
`u / v^a ≤ c^a (u / w^a)` in `[0, ∞]`.

ENNReal.almostDiagonalConst_ne_top.name: ENNReal.almostDiagonalConst_ne_top
ENNReal.almostDiagonalConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of the almost diagonal estimate is finite for `0 < s < L`.

ENNReal.almostDiagonalConst.name: ENNReal.almostDiagonalConst
ENNReal.almostDiagonalConst.docstring:
The constant `(1 - 2^(-(L-s)))⁻¹ + (1 - 2^(-s))⁻¹` of the almost diagonal estimate in `ℓ_q`
(`ENNReal.lqNorm_almostDiagonal_le`).

ENNReal.aestronglyMeasurable_count.name: ENNReal.aestronglyMeasurable_count
ENNReal.aestronglyMeasurable_count.docstring:
Every sequence is measurable for the counting measure; this is the side condition of the
Mathlib lemmas on `eLpNorm`.

ENNReal.HolderConjugate.lt_two_of_two_lt.name: ENNReal.HolderConjugate.lt_two_of_two_lt
ENNReal.HolderConjugate.lt_two_of_two_lt.docstring:
**Conjugate exponents of exponents above `2`**: if `1/p + 1/q = 1` and `p > 2`, then
`q < 2`, since `1/q = 1 - 1/p > 1/2`.

Distribution.iteratedLineDerivOp_apply_a.name: Distribution.iteratedLineDerivOp_apply_apply
Distribution.iteratedLineDerivOp_apply_a.docstring:
The **transpose formula** for iterated derivatives of a distribution on `Ω`: for directions
`v = (v_0, …, v_{k-1})`, `∂^v T (φ) = (-1)^k T(∂^v φ)` for every test function `φ`. Mathlib
defines `∂_w T (φ) = T(-∂_w φ)` (`Distribution.lineDerivOp_apply_apply`); the order of the
derivatives on `φ` is irrelevant because they commute
(`TestFunction.lineDerivOp_iteratedLineDerivOp_comm`).

Daubechies.window_eq_supportWindow.name: Daubechies.window_eq_supportWindow
Daubechies.window_eq_supportWindow.docstring:
The window `[(k - (2N - 2))/2^j, (k + 2N - 1)/2^j]` is the support window
`{x : 2^j x - k ∈ [-(2N - 2), 2N - 1]}` (`Daubechies.supportWindow_eq_Icc`).

Daubechies.wavelet_eq_zero.name: Daubechies.wavelet_eq_zero
Daubechies.wavelet_eq_zero.docstring:
**Support of the wavelet**: for `N ≥ 2`, `ψ(x) = 0` for every `x` outside `[1 - N, N]`. A term
`g_k φ(2x - k)` with `2 - 2N ≤ k ≤ 1` is nonzero only if `0 ≤ 2x - k ≤ 2N - 1`
(`Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_zero`), which forces `2 - 2N ≤ 2x ≤ 2N`.

Daubechies.waveletScaled_refine.name: Daubechies.waveletScaled_refine
Daubechies.waveletScaled_refine.docstring:
**The wavelets through the scaling functions of the next level**: for every level `j`,
position `k` and point `x`, `ψ_{j,k}(x) = ∑_{i = 2 - 2N}^{1} (g_i/√2) φ_{j+1,2k+i}(x)`. This is the
definition `ψ(y) = ∑_i g_i φ(2y - i)` at `y = 2^j x - k`, with
`2(2^j x - k) - i = 2^(j+1) x - (2k + i)` and `2^(j/2) = 2^((j+1)/2)/√2`
(`Daubechies.two_rpow_succ_div_two`).

Daubechies.waveletScaled_eq_daubechiesEx.name: Daubechies.waveletScaled_eq_daubechiesExpand
Daubechies.waveletScaled_eq_daubechiesEx.docstring:
**`ψ_{j,k}` is an expansion of level `j + 1`**: for every level `j`, position `k` and point
`x`, `ψ_{j,k}(x) = ∑_{n ∈ ℤ} (g_{n-2k}/√2) φ_{j+1,n}(x)`. This is
`Daubechies.waveletScaled_refine` after the substitution `n = 2k + i`; the dual filter vanishes
outside `2 - 2N ≤ i ≤ 1` (`Daubechies.dualCoeff_eq_zero`).

Daubechies.waveletScaled.name: Daubechies.waveletScaled
Daubechies.waveletScaled.docstring:
**The wavelets of level `j`**: `ψ_{j,k}(x) = 2^(j/2) ψ(2^j x - k)` for the level `j ∈ ℕ` and
the position `k ∈ ℤ`; this is the generic `Daubechies.scaledFun` for `g = ψ`.

Daubechies.waveletRefineCoeff.name: Daubechies.waveletRefineCoeff
Daubechies.waveletRefineCoeff.docstring:
**The refined wavelet coefficients**: for coefficients `b : ℤ → ℂ` of level `j`, the
coefficients `b'_n = ∑_{k ∈ ℤ} b_k g_{n-2k}/√2` of level `j + 1`, with the dual filter `g`
(`Daubechies.dualCoeff`); only the `k` with `2 - 2N ≤ n - 2k ≤ 1` contribute. They express a
wavelet expansion of level `j` as an expansion in the scaling functions of level `j + 1`,
`∑_k b_k ψ_{j,k} = ∑_n b'_n φ_{j+1,n}`
(`Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_wavelet_eq_daubechiesExpand_succ`).

Daubechies.wavelet.name: Daubechies.wavelet
Daubechies.wavelet.docstring:
**The Daubechies wavelet** `ψ(x) = ∑_{k = 2 - 2N}^{1} g_k φ(2x - k)` of a mask of order `N`,
with the dual filter `g_k = (-1)^k c_{1-k}` (`Daubechies.dualCoeff`) and the scaling function `φ`
(`Daubechies.scalingFun`). The dual filter vanishes outside `2 - 2N ≤ k ≤ 1`
(`Daubechies.dualCoeff_eq_zero`), so this is the sum over all `k ∈ ℤ`.

Daubechies.univ_subset_Icc_union_annulus.name: Daubechies.univ_subset_Icc_union_annulus
Daubechies.univ_subset_Icc_union_annulus.docstring: **The covering of `ℝ`**: every real `ξ` lies in `[-1/4, 1/4]` or in one of the annuli.

Daubechies.two_rpow_two_mul_mul_lt.name: Daubechies.two_rpow_two_mul_mul_lt
Daubechies.two_rpow_two_mul_mul_lt.docstring:
If `λ > 0` and `s < N - log₄ λ`, then `2^(2s) λ < 4^N`: the hypothesis says
`log₄ λ < N - s`, that is `λ < 4^(N - s) = 4^N/4^s`, and `2^(2s) = 4^s`.

Daubechies.two_rpow_succ_div_two.name: Daubechies.two_rpow_succ_div_two
Daubechies.two_rpow_succ_div_two.docstring:
`2^((j+1)/2) = 2^(j/2) √2` for every `j ∈ ℕ`: the normalising factors of two consecutive
levels differ by the factor `√2`.

Daubechies.two_pow_mul_one_div_two_pow.name: Daubechies.two_pow_mul_one_div_two_pow
Daubechies.two_pow_mul_one_div_two_pow.docstring: **Dyadic scales of two levels**: `2^j 2^(-k) = 2^(-(k - j))` for `j ≤ k`.

Daubechies.two_mul_intervalIntegral_comp.name: Daubechies.two_mul_intervalIntegral_comp_two_mul_mul_normSq_symbol
Daubechies.two_mul_intervalIntegral_comp.docstring:
**Halving against the squared symbol**: for every continuous `1`-periodic `w : ℝ → ℂ`,
`2 ∫_0^1 w(2ζ) |m_0(ζ)|² dζ = ∫_0^1 w(ξ) dξ`. Split `[0, 1]` into its two halves
(`Daubechies.intervalIntegral_zero_one_eq_add_half`); since `w(2ζ + 1) = w(2ζ)`, the integrand
on `[0, 1/2]` becomes `w(2ζ) (|m_0(ζ)|² + |m_0(ζ + 1/2)|²) = w(2ζ)` by the quadrature mirror
filter identity (`Daubechies.qmf`), and `2 ∫_0^(1/2) w(2ζ) dζ = ∫_0^1 w`
(`Daubechies.two_mul_intervalIntegral_comp_two_mul`).

Daubechies.two_mul_intervalIntegral_comp.name: Daubechies.two_mul_intervalIntegral_comp_two_mul
Daubechies.two_mul_intervalIntegral_comp.docstring:
**The doubling substitution on a half period**: `2 ∫_0^(1/2) w(2ζ) dζ = ∫_0^1 w(ξ) dξ` for
every `w : ℝ → ℂ`, by the substitution `ξ = 2ζ` (Mathlib's
`intervalIntegral.smul_integral_comp_mul_left`).

Daubechies.tsum_tsum_add_tsum_tsum.name: Daubechies.tsum_tsum_add_tsum_tsum
Daubechies.tsum_tsum_add_tsum_tsum.docstring:
**Combining and exchanging two double sums**: for families `X, Y : ℤ → ℤ → ℂ` that are
summable over `ℤ × ℤ`, `∑_k ∑_n X_{k,n} + ∑_k ∑_n Y_{k,n} = ∑_n ∑_k (X_{k,n} + Y_{k,n})` (Mathlib's
`Summable.tsum_comm`, `Summable.prod`, `Summable.prod_factor`).

Daubechies.tsum_intCast_pow_mul_scalingF.name: Daubechies.tsum_intCast_pow_mul_scalingFun_sub
Daubechies.tsum_intCast_pow_mul_scalingF.docstring:
**The integer moments of the translates, as a polynomial in `x`**: for `N ≥ 2`, `l < N` and
every `x ∈ ℝ`,
`∑_{k ∈ ℤ} k^l φ(x - k) = ∑_{i=0}^{l} C(l, i) (-1)^(l-i) μ_(l-i) x^i`,
where `μ_r = ∫ y^r φ(y) dy` are the moments of `φ`. Write `k = x + (-(x - k))` and expand `k^l`
by the binomial theorem (Mathlib's `add_pow`); exchange the finite sum over `i` with the sum over
`k` (each sum over `k` has only finitely many nonzero terms,
`Daubechies.summable_mul_scalingFun_sub`), and use that the periodised moments
`∑_k (x - k)^r φ(x - k)` equal `μ_r` for `r < N` (`Daubechies.periodization_moment_eq`).

Daubechies.tsum_eq_sum_of_daubechiesScal.name: Daubechies.tsum_eq_sum_of_daubechiesScaled_eq_zero
Daubechies.tsum_eq_sum_of_daubechiesScal.docstring:
**Sums over the positions at a point are finite**: for `N ≥ 2`, a level `j`, a point `x` and
a family `F : ℤ → ℂ` with `F k = 0` whenever `φ_{j,k}(x) = 0`,
`∑_{k ∈ ℤ} F k = ∑_{k = ⌈2^j x - (2N - 1)⌉}^{⌊2^j x⌋} F k`
(`Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_eq_zero_of_notMem_Icc`).

Daubechies.tsum_eLpNorm_window_rpow_le.name: Daubechies.tsum_eLpNorm_window_rpow_le
Daubechies.tsum_eLpNorm_window_rpow_le.docstring:
**Window summation**: for `N ≥ 1`, `0 < p < ∞`, every a.e. strongly measurable `G : ℝ → ℂ`
and every level `j`, the windows `W_k = [(k - (2N - 2))/2^j, (k + 2N - 1)/2^j]` satisfy
`∑_{k ∈ ℤ} ‖G‖_{L_p(W_k)}^p ≤ (4N - 2) ‖G‖_p^p`. This is the window inequality
`∑_k ∫_{W_k} |G|^p ≤ M ∫ |G|^p` (`MeasureTheory.tsum_setLIntegral_le_mul_lintegral`) with the
overlap number `M = 4N - 2` (`Daubechies.card_le_of_forall_mem_window`).

Daubechies.tsum_daubechiesScaled_mul_int.name: Daubechies.tsum_daubechiesScaled_mul_integral_conj
Daubechies.tsum_daubechiesScaled_mul_int.docstring:
**Partition of unity at level `j`**: for `N ≥ 2`, every level `j` and point `x`,
`∑_{k ∈ ℤ} φ_{j,k}(x) ∫ conj φ_{j,k} = ∑_k φ(2^j x - k) = 1`
(`Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_mul_integral_conj`, `Daubechies.sum_scalingFun_translate`).

Daubechies.tsum_daubechiesCoeff_mul_add_.name: Daubechies.tsum_daubechiesCoeff_mul_add_dual
Daubechies.tsum_daubechiesCoeff_mul_add_.docstring:
**The filter identity with normalised filters**: for all `n, n' ∈ ℤ`,
`∑_{k ∈ ℤ} ((c_{n-2k}/√2)(c_{n'-2k}/√2) + (g_{n-2k}/√2)(g_{n'-2k}/√2))` is `1` for `n = n'` and
`0` otherwise (`Daubechies.sum_daubechiesCoeff_mul_add_dual`); only finitely many terms are
nonzero.

Daubechies.truncProduct_zero.name: Daubechies.truncProduct_zero
Daubechies.truncProduct_zero.docstring: `Φ_0 = 1_[-1/2, 1/2)`, the indicator function of `[-1/2, 1/2)`: the product is empty.

Daubechies.truncProduct_succ.name: Daubechies.truncProduct_succ
Daubechies.truncProduct_succ.docstring:
**The recursion of the truncated products**: `Φ_(n+1)(ξ) = m_0(ξ/2) Φ_n(ξ/2)` for every `n`
and every `ξ ∈ ℝ`. Split off the first factor of the product
(`Daubechies.prod_range_succ_symbol`); `ξ` lies in the cut-off interval of level `n + 1` exactly
when `ξ/2` lies in the one of level `n` (`Daubechies.mem_Ico_two_pow_succ_iff`).

Daubechies.truncProduct.name: Daubechies.truncProduct
Daubechies.truncProduct.docstring:
**The truncated symbol products**
`Φ_n(ξ) = ∏_{j<n} m_0(ξ/2^(j+1)) · 1_[-2^n/2, 2^n/2)(ξ)`: the first `n` factors of the symbol
product `Φ`, cut off outside the interval `[-2^n/2, 2^n/2)`. They satisfy
`Φ_(n+1)(ξ) = m_0(ξ/2) Φ_n(ξ/2)` (`Daubechies.truncProduct_succ`), converge to `Φ` pointwise
(`Daubechies.tendsto_truncProduct`), and `∫ w |Φ_n|² = ∫_0^1 w` for every continuous `1`-periodic
`w` (`Daubechies.integral_periodic_mul_normSq_truncProduct`).

Daubechies.transferOp_periodic.name: Daubechies.transferOp_periodic
Daubechies.transferOp_periodic.docstring:
`T` maps `1`-periodic functions to `1`-periodic functions: from `ξ` to `ξ + 1` the points
`ξ/2` and `(ξ + 1)/2` become `(ξ + 1)/2` and `(ξ + 2)/2 = ξ/2 + 1`, so the two summands swap,
since `P` and `g` have period `1`.

Daubechies.transferOp.name: Daubechies.transferOp
Daubechies.transferOp.docstring:
**The transfer operator** of order `N`: for `g : ℝ → ℝ` and `ξ ∈ ℝ`,
`(T g)(ξ) = P(ξ/2) g(ξ/2) + P((ξ + 1)/2) g((ξ + 1)/2)`, where `P = daubFun N` is the
trigonometric Daubechies polynomial `P(ξ) = P_N(sin²(πξ))`. The points `ξ/2` and `(ξ + 1)/2` are
the two preimages of `ξ` under the doubling map `η ↦ 2η` modulo `1`.

Daubechies.transferGrowth_crude.name: Daubechies.transferGrowth_crude
Daubechies.transferGrowth_crude.docstring:
**The crude growth bound**: `T^n 1 ≤ (2 C(2N - 1, N))^n` for every `N`, from
`|T g| ≤ 2 C(2N - 1, N) sup |g|` (`Daubechies.abs_iterate_transferOp_le`). By
`Daubechies.choose_lt_four_pow`, `2 C(2N - 1, N) < 4^(N - 1/2)` for `N ≥ 2`.

Daubechies.tprod_daubFun_shift_le.name: Daubechies.tprod_daubFun_shift_le
Daubechies.tprod_daubFun_shift_le.docstring:
**The tail bound**: for `|ξ| ≤ 2^n/2`,
`∏_{j ≥ 0} P(ξ/2^(n+j+1)) ≤ exp(C(2N - 1, N) π²/12)`. The tail is the full product at
`x = ξ/2^n`, and `|x| ≤ 1/2` gives `x²/3 ≤ 1/12` in `Daubechies.tprod_daubFun_le`.

Daubechies.tprod_daubFun_le.name: Daubechies.tprod_daubFun_le
Daubechies.tprod_daubFun_le.docstring:
**The bound on the product of the trigonometric Daubechies polynomial**:
`∏_{j ≥ 0} P(x/2^(j+1)) ≤ exp(C(2N - 1, N) π² x²/3)` for every `N` and every real `x`. Each
factor is at most `1 + C(2N - 1, N) π² (x/2^(j+1))² ≤ exp(C(2N - 1, N) π² (x/2^(j+1))²)`
(`Daubechies.daubFun_le`, Mathlib's `Real.prod_one_add_le_exp_sum`), and
`∑_{j ≥ 0} (x/2^(j+1))² = x²/3`.

Daubechies.tprod_daubFun_eq_prod_mul.name: Daubechies.tprod_daubFun_eq_prod_mul
Daubechies.tprod_daubFun_eq_prod_mul.docstring:
**The split into the first `n` factors and the tail**:
`∏_{j ≥ 0} P(ξ/2^(j+1)) = ∏_{j<n} P(ξ/2^(j+1)) · ∏_{j ≥ 0} P(ξ/2^(n+j+1))` for every `n`
(Mathlib's `Multipliable.prod_mul_tprod_nat_mul'`, which needs the tail to converge).

Daubechies.tendsto_truncProduct.name: Daubechies.tendsto_truncProduct
Daubechies.tendsto_truncProduct.docstring:
**The truncated products converge to the symbol product**: `Φ_n(ξ) → Φ(ξ)` as `n → ∞`, for
every `ξ ∈ ℝ`. For large `n` the cut-off factor at `ξ` is `1`
(`Daubechies.eventually_mem_Ico_two_pow`), and the partial products converge to `Φ(ξ)`
(`Daubechies.tendsto_prod_symbol`).

Daubechies.tendsto_prod_symbol.name: Daubechies.tendsto_prod_symbol
Daubechies.tendsto_prod_symbol.docstring:
**The partial products converge pointwise**: `∏_{j<n} m_0(ξ/2^(j+1)) → Φ(ξ)` as
`n → ∞`, for every `ξ`.

Daubechies.tendsto_integral_cascade_mul.name: Daubechies.tendsto_integral_cascade_mul
Daubechies.tendsto_integral_cascade_mul.docstring:
**The cascade converges to the scaling function against Schwartz functions**: for a mask of
order `N ≥ 2` and every Schwartz function `ψ`, `∫ η_n ψ → ∫ φ ψ` as `n → ∞`. The
multiplication formula gives `∫ η_n ψ = ∫ 𝓕 η_n · 𝓕⁻ ψ` (`Real.integral_mul_schwartz_eq`). These
integrands converge pointwise to `Φ · 𝓕⁻ ψ` (`Daubechies.tendsto_fourier_cascade`) and are
bounded by the integrable function `|𝓕⁻ ψ|` (`Daubechies.norm_fourier_cascade_le_one`), so
dominated convergence (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence`) gives
the limit `∫ Φ · 𝓕⁻ ψ = ∫ 𝓕⁻ Φ · ψ = ∫ φ ψ` (`Real.real_integral_fourierInv_mul`, which needs
`Φ ∈ L¹`, `Daubechies.integrable_symbolProduct`).

Daubechies.tendsto_fourier_cascade.name: Daubechies.tendsto_fourier_cascade
Daubechies.tendsto_fourier_cascade.docstring:
**The Fourier transforms of the cascade converge to the symbol product**: `𝓕 η_n(ξ) → Φ(ξ)`
as `n → ∞`, for every `ξ ∈ ℝ`. In `𝓕 η_n(ξ) = ∏_{j<n} m_0(ξ/2^(j+1)) · 𝓕 η_0(ξ/2^n)` the
partial products converge to `Φ(ξ)` (`Daubechies.tendsto_prod_symbol`), and
`𝓕 η_0(ξ/2^n) → 𝓕 η_0(0) = 1` since `𝓕 η_0` is continuous.

Daubechies.tendsto_eLpNorm_sub_projFun.name: Daubechies.tendsto_eLpNorm_sub_projFun
Daubechies.tendsto_eLpNorm_sub_projFun.docstring:
**`P_j f → f` for continuous functions with compact support**: for `N ≥ 2`, every continuous
`f` with compact support and every exponent `p`, `‖f - P_j f‖_p → 0` as `j → ∞`. The function
`f` is uniformly continuous, so `‖f(y) - f(x)‖ ≤ η` once `|y - x| ≤ (2N - 1)/2^j` and `j` is
large; `φ` is bounded; and `Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le` bounds the error by a fixed
multiple of `η`.

Daubechies.tendstoLocallyUniformly_prod_.name: Daubechies.tendstoLocallyUniformly_prod_symbol
Daubechies.tendstoLocallyUniformly_prod_.docstring:
**The partial products converge locally uniformly**:
`∏_{j<n} m_0(ξ/2^(j+1)) → Φ(ξ)` as `n → ∞`, locally uniformly in `ξ ∈ ℝ`.

Daubechies.symbol_neg.name: Daubechies.symbol_neg
Daubechies.symbol_neg.docstring:
`m_0(-ξ) = conj (m_0(ξ))`: the mask polynomial has real coefficients, and
`e^(-2πi(-ξ)) = conj (e^(-2πiξ))`.

Daubechies.symbol_ne_zero.name: Daubechies.symbol_ne_zero
Daubechies.symbol_ne_zero.docstring:
**The symbol has no zeros in `(-1/2, 1/2)`**: there `cos(πξ) > 0`, and `P(ξ) ≥ 1`
(`Daubechies.one_le_daubFun`), so `|m_0(ξ)|² = cos(πξ)^(2N) P(ξ) > 0`.

Daubechies.symbol_eq_sum_cexp.name: Daubechies.symbol_eq_sum_cexp
Daubechies.symbol_eq_sum_cexp.docstring: The symbol as a finite exponential sum: `m_0(ξ) = ∑_{k < 2N} (c_k/2) e^(-2πikξ)`.

Daubechies.symbol_eq_sum.name: Daubechies.symbol_eq_sum
Daubechies.symbol_eq_sum.docstring:
**The symbol as a trigonometric polynomial**:
`m_0(ξ) = (1/2) ∑_{k < 2N} c_k e^(-2πikξ)`, with `e^(-2πikξ) = (e^(-2πiξ))^k`.

Daubechies.symbol_eq_mul.name: Daubechies.symbol_eq_mul
Daubechies.symbol_eq_mul.docstring: The symbol factors as `m_0(ξ) = ((1 + e^(-2πiξ))/2)^N L(e^(-2πiξ))`.

Daubechies.symbol_eq_finsum.name: Daubechies.symbol_eq_finsum
Daubechies.symbol_eq_finsum.docstring: **The symbol as a sum over `ℤ`**: `m_0(ξ) = (1/2) ∑_{k ∈ ℤ} c_k e^(-2πikξ)`.

Daubechies.symbolProduct_two_mul_eq_sum.name: Daubechies.symbolProduct_two_mul_eq_sum
Daubechies.symbolProduct_two_mul_eq_sum.docstring:
**The refinement identity on the Fourier side**:
`Φ(2ξ) = m_0(ξ) Φ(ξ) = ∑_{k<2N} (c_k/2) e^(-2πikξ) Φ(ξ)` for every `ξ ∈ ℝ`
(`Daubechies.symbolProduct_two_mul` and `Daubechies.symbol_eq_sum`).

Daubechies.symbolProduct_two_mul.name: Daubechies.symbolProduct_two_mul
Daubechies.symbolProduct_two_mul.docstring:
**The refinement identity** `Φ(2ξ) = m_0(ξ) Φ(ξ)`: the case `n = 1` of
`Daubechies.symbolProduct_eq_prod_mul` at the point `2ξ`.

Daubechies.symbolProduct_neg.name: Daubechies.symbolProduct_neg
Daubechies.symbolProduct_neg.docstring:
**`Φ(-ξ) = conj Φ(ξ)`**: every factor satisfies `m_0(-η) = conj m_0(η)`
(`Daubechies.symbol_neg`), and complex conjugation is a continuous multiplicative map.

Daubechies.symbolProduct_ne_zero.name: Daubechies.symbolProduct_ne_zero
Daubechies.symbolProduct_ne_zero.docstring:
**`Φ` has no zeros on `[-1/2, 1/2]`**: for `|ξ| ≤ 1/2` every argument `ξ/2^(j+1)` has modulus
`≤ 1/4 < 1/2`, so no factor vanishes (`Daubechies.symbol_ne_zero`), and a convergent product of
nonzero factors `1 + a_j` with `∑_j |a_j| < ∞` is nonzero (Mathlib's
`tprod_one_add_ne_zero_of_summable`).

Daubechies.symbolProduct_eq_prod_mul.name: Daubechies.symbolProduct_eq_prod_mul
Daubechies.symbolProduct_eq_prod_mul.docstring:
**Splitting off the first `n` factors**:
`Φ(ξ) = ∏_{j<n} m_0(ξ/2^(j+1)) · Φ(ξ/2^n)` for every `n`, since
`ξ/2^(n+j+1) = (ξ/2^n)/2^(j+1)` (Mathlib's `Multipliable.prod_mul_tprod_nat_mul'`).

Daubechies.symbolProduct.name: Daubechies.symbolProduct
Daubechies.symbolProduct.docstring:
**The symbol product** of a mask: `Φ(ξ) = ∏_{j ≥ 0} m_0(ξ/2^(j+1))`, where `m_0` is the
symbol (`Daubechies.symbol`). The product converges for every `ξ`
(`Daubechies.multipliable_symbolProduct`).

Daubechies.symbolLip.name: Daubechies.symbolLip
Daubechies.symbolLip.docstring:
**The Lipschitz constant of the symbol at `0`**, `π ∑_{k < 2N} k |c_k|`: by
`Daubechies.norm_symbol_sub_one_le`, `|m_0(ξ) - 1| ≤ π ∑_k k |c_k| · |ξ|`.

Daubechies.symbol.name: Daubechies.symbol
Daubechies.symbol.docstring:
**The symbol** `m_0(ξ) = m(e^(-2πiξ))` of a mask, the mask polynomial evaluated on the unit
circle; it equals `(1/2) ∑_k c_k e^(-2πikξ)` (`Daubechies.symbol_eq_sum`).

Daubechies.supportWindow_subset_of_mem_I.name: Daubechies.supportWindow_subset_of_mem_Icc
Daubechies.supportWindow_subset_of_mem_I.docstring:
**The positions meeting a cell have their supports in one window**: for
`k - (2N - 2) ≤ l ≤ k`, the support window `[l/2^j, (l + 2N - 1)/2^j]` of `φ_{j,l}` lies in the
window `[(k - (2N - 2))/2^j, (k + 2N - 1)/2^j]`.

Daubechies.supportWindow_eq_Icc.name: Daubechies.supportWindow_eq_Icc
Daubechies.supportWindow_eq_Icc.docstring: The support window is the interval `[(k + a)/2^j, (k + b)/2^j]`.

Daubechies.supportWindow.name: Daubechies.supportWindow
Daubechies.supportWindow.docstring:
**The support window** `{x : 2^j x - k ∈ [a, b]}` of level `j` and position `k`: the
interval `[(k + a)/2^j, (k + b)/2^j]` (`Daubechies.supportWindow_eq_Icc`) outside which
`g_{j,k}` vanishes when `g` vanishes outside `[a, b]` (`Daubechies.scaledFun_eq_zero`).

Daubechies.summable_refine_of_filter.name: Daubechies.summable_refine_of_filter
Daubechies.summable_refine_of_filter.docstring:
**The double sum of a refinement has finitely many terms**: for `N ≥ 2`, a real filter `h`
vanishing outside `[a, b]`, a level `j`, coefficients `c : ℤ → ℂ` and a point `x`, the family
`(k, n) ↦ c_k (h_{n-2k}/√2) φ_{j+1,n}(x)` is summable over `ℤ × ℤ`. A nonzero term needs
`a ≤ n - 2k ≤ b` and `0 ≤ 2^(j+1) x - n ≤ 2N - 1`, which leaves finitely many pairs
(`Daubechies.mem_Icc_ceil_floor`).

Daubechies.summable_of_daubechiesScaled_.name: Daubechies.summable_of_daubechiesScaled_eq_zero
Daubechies.summable_of_daubechiesScaled_.docstring:
The families of `Daubechies.tsum_eq_sum_of_daubechiesScaled_eq_zero` are summable: they have
only finitely many nonzero terms.

Daubechies.summable_norm_symbol_sub_one.name: Daubechies.summable_norm_symbol_sub_one
Daubechies.summable_norm_symbol_sub_one.docstring:
The deviations `|m_0(ξ/2^(j+1)) - 1|` are summable over `j`: they are bounded by the
geometric sequence `(C|ξ|/2)/2^j`.

Daubechies.summable_mul_scalingFun_sub.name: Daubechies.summable_mul_scalingFun_sub
Daubechies.summable_mul_scalingFun_sub.docstring:
The sums `∑_{k ∈ ℤ} a(k) φ(x - k)` converge (for `N ≥ 2`): only finitely many terms are
nonzero (`Daubechies.scalingFun_sub_eq_zero`).

Daubechies.summable_filter_mul_filter.name: Daubechies.summable_filter_mul_filter
Daubechies.summable_filter_mul_filter.docstring:
**The double sum of the filter identity has finitely many terms**: let `h, h' : ℤ → ℝ` vanish
outside `[-B, B]`. Then for every `a : ℤ → ℂ` and `n' ∈ ℤ` the family
`(k, n) ↦ (h_{n-2k}/√2)(h'_{n'-2k}/√2) a_n` is summable over `ℤ × ℤ`: a nonzero term needs
`|n' - 2k| ≤ B` and `|n - 2k| ≤ B`, which leaves finitely many pairs.

Daubechies.summable_expand.name: Daubechies.summable_expand
Daubechies.summable_expand.docstring:
The series `∑_k c_k g_{j,k}(x)` converges for every point `x`, if `g` vanishes outside
`[a, b]`: only finitely many terms are nonzero.

Daubechies.sum_scalingFun_translate.name: Daubechies.sum_scalingFun_translate
Daubechies.sum_scalingFun_translate.docstring:
**Partition of unity**: `∑_{k ∈ ℤ} φ(x - k) = 1` for every `x ∈ ℝ` (for `N ≥ 2`), the case
`l = 0` of `Daubechies.periodization_moment_eq` together with `∫ φ = 1`
(`Daubechies.integral_scalingFun`).

Daubechies.sum_range_rule.name: Daubechies.sum_range_rule
Daubechies.sum_range_rule.docstring:
**The sum rules** as finite sums over `k = 0, …, 2N - 1`:
`∑_{k < 2N} (-1)^k k^l c_k = 0` for `l < N`.

Daubechies.sum_range_neg_one_pow_mul_pow.name: Daubechies.sum_range_neg_one_pow_mul_pow_mul_coeff
Daubechies.sum_range_neg_one_pow_mul_pow.docstring:
**Sum rules for polynomials divisible by `(X + 1)^j`**: if `(X + 1)^j ∣ p`, `l < j` and
`deg p < n`, then `∑_{k < n} (-1)^k k^l [X^k] p = 0`. The sum is the value at `-1` of the `l`-th
iterate of the Euler operator `p ↦ X p'`, which is still divisible by `X + 1`.

Daubechies.sum_mul_conj_filter.name: Daubechies.sum_mul_conj_filter
Daubechies.sum_mul_conj_filter.docstring:
**A sum of products of shifted filters**: let `h, h' : ℤ → ℝ`, `k, l ∈ ℤ`, and let
`h'(n - 2l) = 0` for every `n` outside a finite set `T`. Then
`∑_{n ∈ T} (h_{n-2k}/√2) conj(h'_{n-2l}/√2) = (1/2) ∑_{n ∈ ℤ} h_{n-2k} h'_{n-2l}`, since
`√2 √2 = 2` and the sequences are real.

Daubechies.sum_inner_poly_mul_scalingFun.name: Daubechies.sum_inner_poly_mul_scalingFun_two_pow
Daubechies.sum_inner_poly_mul_scalingFun.docstring:
**The projection identity at the dyadic level `j`**: for `N ≥ 2`, every polynomial `Q` of
degree `< N`, every `j ∈ ℕ` and every `x ∈ ℝ`,
`∑_{k ∈ ℤ} 2^j (∫ Q(y) conj φ(2^j y - k) dy) φ(2^j x - k) = Q(x)`.
For the normalised functions `φ_(j,k)(x) = 2^(j/2) φ(2^j x - k)` this reads
`∑_k ⟨Q, φ_(j,k)⟩ φ_(j,k)(x) = Q(x)`. Apply `Daubechies.sum_inner_poly_mul_scalingFun` to the
polynomial `R` of degree `< N` with `R(2^j y) = Q(y)` (`Daubechies.exists_poly_comp_two_pow_mul`)
at the point `2^j x`, and substitute `u = 2^j y` in the integrals
(`Daubechies.integral_eq_two_pow_mul_integral_comp`).

Daubechies.sum_inner_poly_mul_scalingFun.name: Daubechies.sum_inner_poly_mul_scalingFun
Daubechies.sum_inner_poly_mul_scalingFun.docstring:
**The projection identity: the translates of `φ` reproduce polynomials**: for `N ≥ 2`, every
polynomial `Q` of degree `< N` and every `x ∈ ℝ`,
`∑_{k ∈ ℤ} ⟨Q, φ(· - k)⟩ φ(x - k) = Q(x)`, where `⟨Q, φ(· - k)⟩ = ∫ Q(y) conj φ(y - k) dy`.
So the projection `f ↦ ∑_k ⟨f, φ(· - k)⟩ φ(· - k)` leaves every polynomial of degree `< N`
unchanged. Write `Q = ∑_j a(j) φ(· - j)` with a polynomial `a` (`Daubechies.exists_coeff_poly`);
then `⟨Q, φ(· - k)⟩ = a(k)` (`Daubechies.integral_tsum_mul_scalingFun_sub_mul_conj`), and the left
side is `∑_k a(k) φ(x - k) = Q(x)`.

Daubechies.sum_dualCoeff_mul_dualCoeff_a.name: Daubechies.sum_dualCoeff_mul_dualCoeff_add
Daubechies.sum_dualCoeff_mul_dualCoeff_a.docstring:
**Orthogonality of the even shifts of the dual filter**: `∑_k g_k g_(k+2j) = 2 δ_(j0)` for
every `j ∈ ℤ`. The substitution `k ↦ 1 - 2j - k` turns the sum into `∑_k c_k c_(k+2j)`
(`Daubechies.sum_daubechiesCoeff_mul_daubechiesCoeff_add`).

Daubechies.sum_daubechiesCoeff_mul_daube.name: Daubechies.sum_daubechiesCoeff_mul_daubechiesCoeff_add
Daubechies.sum_daubechiesCoeff_mul_daube.docstring:
**Orthogonality of the even shifts of the filter**: `∑_k c_k c_(k+2j) = 2 δ_(j0)` for every
`j ∈ ℤ`. Integrating the quadrature mirror filter identity
`|m_0(ξ)|² + |m_0(ξ + 1/2)|² = 1` (`Daubechies.qmf`) against `e^(2πi·2jξ)` over `[0, 1]` gives
`(1/4) ∑_k c_k c_(k+2j) + (1/4) ∑_k c_k c_(k+2j) = δ_(j0)`.

Daubechies.sum_daubechiesCoeff_mul_add_d.name: Daubechies.sum_daubechiesCoeff_mul_add_dual
Daubechies.sum_daubechiesCoeff_mul_add_d.docstring:
**The filter and its dual resolve the identity**: for all `a, b ∈ ℤ`,
`∑_j (c_(a-2j) c_(b-2j) + g_(a-2j) g_(b-2j)) = 2 δ_(ab)`. Both sums run over one parity class
of the products `h(k) = c_(k+(a-b)) c_k`. For `a - b` even the two classes are complementary and
the sum is `∑_k c_k c_(k+(a-b)) = 2 δ_(ab)`
(`Daubechies.sum_daubechiesCoeff_mul_daubechiesCoeff_add`); for `a - b` odd the two classes agree
and the sign `(-1)^(a+b) = -1` makes them cancel.

Daubechies.sum_daubechiesCoeff.name: Daubechies.sum_daubechiesCoeff
Daubechies.sum_daubechiesCoeff.docstring: **The filter coefficients add up to `2`**: `∑_{k < 2N} c_k = 2 m(1) = 2`.

Daubechies.sub_projFun_eq_sub_projFun_su.name: Daubechies.sub_projFun_eq_sub_projFun_sub
Daubechies.sub_projFun_eq_sub_projFun_su.docstring:
**Subtracting a reproduced polynomial**: for `N ≥ 2`, a locally integrable `S : ℝ → ℂ`, a
complex polynomial `Q` of degree `< N` and every level `j`,
`S - P_j S = (S - Q) - P_j (S - Q)` at every point, since `P_j` is linear on locally integrable
functions (`Daubechies.projFun_sub`) and reproduces `Q` (`Daubechies.projFun_poly`).

Daubechies.sub_C_coeff_mul_mem_degreeLT.name: Daubechies.sub_C_coeff_mul_mem_degreeLT
Daubechies.sub_C_coeff_mul_mem_degreeLT.docstring:
**Lowering the degree of a polynomial**: let `Q` have degree `< n + 1`, and let `P` have
degree `≤ n` and coefficient `1` at `X^n`. Then `Q - q_n P` has degree `< n`, where `q_n` is the
coefficient of `X^n` in `Q`: the coefficients at `X^n` cancel, and both polynomials have no terms
of higher degree.

Daubechies.sq_div_two_pow_succ.name: Daubechies.sq_div_two_pow_succ
Daubechies.sq_div_two_pow_succ.docstring: `(x/2^(j+1))² = (x²/4) (1/4)^j` for every real `x` and every `j ∈ ℕ`.

Daubechies.smoothnessModulus_mem_scaling.name: Daubechies.smoothnessModulus_mem_scalingSpace_le
Daubechies.smoothnessModulus_mem_scaling.docstring:
**The Bernstein inequality for the scaling spaces**: for `N ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, every order
`r`, every level `j`, every `a ∈ V_j` (`Daubechies.scalingSpace`) and every `t` with `2^j t ≤ 1`,
`ω_r(a, t)_p ≤ C ω_r(φ, 2^j t)_p ‖a‖_p` with the constant
`C = Daubechies.daubechiesBernsteinConst m p r`, which is finite
(`Daubechies.daubechiesBernsteinConst_ne_top`) and independent of `j`, `a` and `t`.

The element `a` is almost everywhere the expansion `∑_k λ_k φ_{j,k}` of its coefficients
`λ_k = ⟨a, φ_{j,k}⟩` (`Daubechies.daubechiesProj_eq_self_of_mem`), so for `|h| ≤ t`,
`Δ_h^r a = ∑_k λ_k (Δ_{2^j h}^r φ)_{j,k}` (`Daubechies.iterate_fwdDiff_daubechiesExpand`). As
`|2^j h| ≤ 1`, the generator `Δ_{2^j h}^r φ` vanishes outside `[-r, 2N - 1 + r]`
(`Daubechies.higherDiff_scalingFun_eq_zero`), and the upper estimate of expansions
(`Daubechies.eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand_le`) and the coefficient estimate
(`Daubechies.dyadicWeight_mul_lqNorm_coeffFun_le`) give
`‖Δ_h^r a‖_p ≤ (2N + 2r)^(1 - 1/p) ‖Δ_{2^j h}^r φ‖_p 2^(j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖λ‖_{ℓ_p}`
`≤ C ‖Δ_{2^j h}^r φ‖_p ‖a‖_p`, where the dyadic weights cancel.

Daubechies.smoothJacksonConst_ne_top.name: Daubechies.smoothJacksonConst_ne_top
Daubechies.smoothJacksonConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant `smoothJacksonConst m p` is finite for `N ≥ 2` (`Daubechies.cellConst_ne_top`).

Daubechies.smoothJacksonConst.name: Daubechies.smoothJacksonConst
Daubechies.smoothJacksonConst.docstring:
**The constant of Jackson's inequality for smooth functions**:
`(4N - 2)^(1/p) (1 + C) (4N - 3)^N` with the constant `C = cellConst m p` of the local bound, the
overlap number `4N - 2` of the windows and their length `(4N - 3)/2^j`
(`Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le_of_contDiff`).

Daubechies.sinc_pow_le_of_mem_annulus.name: Daubechies.sinc_pow_le_of_mem_annulus
Daubechies.sinc_pow_le_of_mem_annulus.docstring:
On the annulus `A_n`: `sinc(πξ)^(2N) ≤ (4/(π 2^n))^(2N)`, since `|sinc(πξ)| ≤ 1/(π|ξ|)` and
`π|ξ| > π 2^n/4`.

Daubechies.sinc_mul_cos.name: Daubechies.sinc_mul_cos
Daubechies.sinc_mul_cos.docstring:
**The doubling formula for `sinc`**: `sinc(y) cos(y) = sinc(2y)` for every real `y`, from
`sin(2y) = 2 sin(y) cos(y)` (Mathlib's `Real.sin_two_mul`); at `y = 0` both sides are `1`.

Daubechies.sinc_div_two_pow_mul_prod_cos.name: Daubechies.sinc_div_two_pow_mul_prod_cos
Daubechies.sinc_div_two_pow_mul_prod_cos.docstring:
**The finite cosine product**: `sinc(x/2^n) ∏_{j<n} cos(x/2^(j+1)) = sinc(x)` for every real
`x` and every `n ∈ ℕ`, by induction on `n` with `sinc(y) cos(y) = sinc(2y)` at
`y = x/2^(n+1)`.

Daubechies.scalingSpace_mono.name: Daubechies.scalingSpace_mono
Daubechies.scalingSpace_mono.docstring:
**The scaling spaces increase with the level**: `V_i ⊆ V_j` for `i ≤ j`
(`Daubechies.scalingSpace_le_succ`).

Daubechies.scalingSpace_le_succ.name: Daubechies.scalingSpace_le_succ
Daubechies.scalingSpace_le_succ.docstring:
**The scaling spaces are nested**: `V_j ⊆ V_{j+1}`, since `P_j f = P_{j+1} (P_j f)`
(`Daubechies.daubechiesProj_succ_daubechiesProj`), a consequence of the refinement equation.

Daubechies.scalingSpace.name: Daubechies.scalingSpace
Daubechies.scalingSpace.docstring:
**The scaling space of level `j`**: the range `V_j` of the projection `P_j` in `L_p`, for
`N ≥ 2` and `1 ≤ p < ∞`, a real subspace of `L_p`. It consists of the classes of the expansions
`∑_k ⟨f, φ_{j,k}⟩ φ_{j,k}`, `f ∈ L_p`, and `P_j` is the identity on it
(`Daubechies.daubechiesProj_eq_self_of_mem`).

Daubechies.scalingFun_sub_eq_zero.name: Daubechies.scalingFun_sub_eq_zero
Daubechies.scalingFun_sub_eq_zero.docstring:
**Only finitely many translates are nonzero at a point**: for `N ≥ 2`, `x ∈ ℝ` and an
integer `k` outside `[⌊x⌋ - (2N - 1), ⌊x⌋]`, `φ(x - k) = 0`. Indeed `φ(x - k) ≠ 0` forces
`x - k ∈ [0, 2N - 1]` (`Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_zero`), hence `k ≤ x`, so `k ≤ ⌊x⌋`, and
`k ≥ x - (2N - 1) ≥ ⌊x⌋ - (2N - 1)`. The index set depends only on `⌊x⌋`.

Daubechies.scalingFun_refine.name: Daubechies.scalingFun_refine
Daubechies.scalingFun_refine.docstring:
**The refinement equation** `φ(x) = ∑_{k=0}^{2N-1} c_k φ(2x - k)` for every `x ∈ ℝ` and every
mask of order `N ≥ 2`. By the dilation step (`Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_two_mul_fourierInv`) and
the Fourier-side identity `Φ(2ξ) = ∑_k (c_k/2) e^(-2πikξ) Φ(ξ)`
(`Daubechies.symbolProduct_two_mul_eq_sum`),
`φ(x) = 2 𝓕⁻[∑_k (c_k/2) e^(-2πik ·) Φ](2x) = ∑_k c_k 𝓕⁻[e^(-2πik ·) Φ](2x) = ∑_k c_k φ(2x - k)`:
the inverse transform is linear on the integrable summands (`Φ ∈ L¹` for `N ≥ 2`,
`Daubechies.integrable_symbolProduct`), and modulation by `e^(-2πikξ)` is translation by `k`
(`Daubechies.fourierInv_expFreq_mul_apply`).

Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_zero_of_notMem_.name: Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_zero_of_notMem_Ioo
Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_zero_of_notMem_.docstring:
**The scaling function vanishes at the endpoints as well**: `φ(x) = 0` for every
`x ∉ (0, 2N - 1)`, for `N ≥ 2`. The zero set of the continuous function `φ` is closed and
contains the open set `ℝ \ [0, 2N - 1]` (`Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_zero`), hence also its closure
`ℝ \ (0, 2N - 1)`.

Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_zero.name: Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_zero
Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_zero.docstring:
**The scaling function vanishes outside `[0, 2N - 1]`**: for a mask of order `N ≥ 2`,
`φ(x) = 0` for every `x ∉ [0, 2N - 1]`. For a Schwartz function `ψ` with support in the open set
`ℝ \ [0, 2N - 1]` every integral `∫ η_n ψ` vanishes (`Daubechies.integral_cascade_mul_eq_zero`),
so their limit `∫ φ ψ` (`Daubechies.tendsto_integral_cascade_mul`) is `0`. The continuous
function `φ` therefore vanishes on the open set, by the fundamental lemma
(`Real.eqOn_zero_of_integral_mul_schwartz_eq_zero`).

Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_two_mul_fourier.name: Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_two_mul_fourierInv
Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_two_mul_fourier.docstring:
**The dilation step**: `φ(x) = 2 𝓕⁻[ξ ↦ Φ(2ξ)](2x)` for every `x ∈ ℝ`, the dilation rule
`𝓕⁻[f(2 ·)](y) = 𝓕⁻ f(y/2)/2` (`Real.fourierInv_comp_mul_left_apply`) at `y = 2x`.

Daubechies.scalingFun.name: Daubechies.scalingFun
Daubechies.scalingFun.docstring:
**The scaling function** of a Daubechies mask: the inverse Fourier transform
`φ(x) = 𝓕⁻ Φ(x) = ∫ Φ(ξ) e^(2πixξ) dξ` of the symbol product `Φ` (`Daubechies.symbolProduct`).
It is defined for every mask; for order `N ≥ 2` the symbol product is integrable, and then `φ`
is continuous (`Daubechies.continuous_scalingFun`) and satisfies the refinement equation
(`Daubechies.scalingFun_refine`).

Daubechies.scaledFun_zero.name: Daubechies.scaledFun_zero
Daubechies.scaledFun_zero.docstring:
**The generators of level `0` are the integer translates**: `g_{0,k}(x) = g(x - k)` for every
`g : ℝ → ℂ`, `k ∈ ℤ` and `x ∈ ℝ`, since `2^0 = 1`.

Daubechies.scaledFun_mul_conj_eq_zero.name: Daubechies.scaledFun_mul_conj_eq_zero
Daubechies.scaledFun_mul_conj_eq_zero.docstring:
**Generators of one level overlap only for nearby positions**: if `g` vanishes outside
`[a, b]`, then `g_{j,l}(y) conj g_{j,k}(y) = 0` for every `y` unless `|l - k| ≤ ⌈b - a⌉`. If both
factors are nonzero, then `y` lies in both support windows
(`Daubechies.mem_Icc_of_mem_supportWindow`).

Daubechies.scaledFun_mul_conj.name: Daubechies.scaledFun_mul_conj
Daubechies.scaledFun_mul_conj.docstring:
**The product of two generators of one level**:
`g_{j,k}(x) conj g_{j,l}(x) = 2^j g(2^j x - k) conj g(2^j x - l)`, since the factor `2^(j/2)` is
real.

Daubechies.scaledFun_eq_zero.name: Daubechies.scaledFun_eq_zero
Daubechies.scaledFun_eq_zero.docstring:
**Support of `g_{j,k}`**: if `g` vanishes outside `[a, b]`, then `g_{j,k}(x) = 0` for every
`x` outside the support window `{x : 2^j x - k ∈ [a, b]}`.

Daubechies.scaledFun.name: Daubechies.scaledFun
Daubechies.scaledFun.docstring:
**The dilated and translated generator** `g_{j,k}(x) = 2^(j/2) g(2^j x - k)` of level
`j ∈ ℕ` and position `k ∈ ℤ`. The factor `2^(j/2)` makes the `L_2` norm independent of `j` and
`k`. For the scaling function `g = φ` these are the functions `φ_{j,k}` of the multiresolution
analysis (`Daubechies.daubechiesScaled`).

Daubechies.rpow_mul_le_rpow_add_rpow_mul.name: Daubechies.rpow_mul_le_rpow_add_rpow_mul_sq
Daubechies.rpow_mul_le_rpow_add_rpow_mul.docstring:
`x^a c ≤ x^(2(a - b)) + x^(2b) c²` for `x > 0`, `c ≥ 0` and all real `a`, `b`: with
`u = x^(a - b)` and `v = x^b c`, `x^a c = uv ≤ 2uv ≤ u² + v²`.

Daubechies.rpow_le_four_rpow_abs_mul.name: Daubechies.rpow_le_four_rpow_abs_mul
Daubechies.rpow_le_four_rpow_abs_mul.docstring:
**Comparable bases give comparable powers**: if `y > 0` and `y/4 ≤ x ≤ 4y`, then
`x^t ≤ 4^|t| y^t` for every real exponent `t` (for `t ≥ 0` from `x ≤ 4y`, for `t ≤ 0` from
`y/4 ≤ x`).

Daubechies.refineCoeff_add_waveletRefine.name: Daubechies.refineCoeff_add_waveletRefineCoeff
Daubechies.refineCoeff_add_waveletRefine.docstring:
**Perfect reconstruction**: for every `a : ℤ → ℂ` and `n' ∈ ℤ`,
`∑_k (∑_n (c_{n-2k}/√2) a_n)(c_{n'-2k}/√2) + ∑_k (∑_n (g_{n-2k}/√2) a_n)(g_{n'-2k}/√2) = a_{n'}`:
the left side is `∑_n a_n ∑_k ((c_{n-2k}/√2)(c_{n'-2k}/√2) + (g_{n-2k}/√2)(g_{n'-2k}/√2))` after
exchanging the sums (`Daubechies.summable_filter_mul_filter`,
`Daubechies.tsum_tsum_add_tsum_tsum`), and the inner sum is `δ_{nn'}`
(`Daubechies.tsum_daubechiesCoeff_mul_add_dual`). In terms of the refined coefficients
(`Daubechies.refineCoeff`, `Daubechies.waveletRefineCoeff`) this reads `H* H a + G* G a = a`.

Daubechies.refineCoeff.name: Daubechies.refineCoeff
Daubechies.refineCoeff.docstring:
**The refined coefficients**: for coefficients `a : ℤ → ℂ` of level `j`, the coefficients
`a'_n = ∑_{k ∈ ℤ} a_k c_{n-2k}/√2` of level `j + 1`, with the filter coefficients `c_i`
(`Daubechies.daubechiesCoeff`); only the `k` with `0 ≤ n - 2k ≤ 2N - 1` contribute. They express an
expansion of level `j` as one of level `j + 1`, `∑_k a_k φ_{j,k} = ∑_n a'_n φ_{j+1,n}`
(`Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_eq_daubechiesExpand_succ`).

Daubechies.qmf.name: Daubechies.qmf
Daubechies.qmf.docstring:
**The quadrature mirror filter identity** `|m_0(ξ)|² + |m_0(ξ + 1/2)|² = 1`: with
`cos(π(ξ + 1/2)) = -sin(πξ)` it is the trigonometric Bézout identity
`cos(πξ)^(2N) P(ξ) + sin(πξ)^(2N) P(ξ + 1/2) = 1` (`Daubechies.daubFun_bezout`).

Daubechies.projLinear.name: Daubechies.projLinear
Daubechies.projLinear.docstring:
**The projection of level `j` as a linear map on `L_p`**, for `N ≥ 2` and `1 ≤ p < ∞`:
the class of the pointwise projection `P_j f` (`Daubechies.projFun`) of a representative of `f`.

Daubechies.projFun_succ_projFun.name: Daubechies.projFun_succ_projFun
Daubechies.projFun_succ_projFun.docstring:
**The projections of consecutive levels**: `P_{j+1} (P_j f) = P_j f` at every point, for
`N ≥ 2` and every `f`. The function `P_j f` is an expansion of level `j + 1`
(`Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_eq_daubechiesExpand_succ`), which `P_{j+1}` reproduces
(`Daubechies.projFun_daubechiesExpand`).

Daubechies.projFun_succ_eq_add.name: Daubechies.projFun_succ_eq_add
Daubechies.projFun_succ_eq_add.docstring:
**The block identity, pointwise**: for `N ≥ 2`, locally integrable `f`, every level `j` and
point `x`, `P_{j+1} f(x) = P_j f(x) + ∑_k ⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩ ψ_{j,k}(x)`. Both terms on the right are
expansions of level `j + 1` (`Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_eq_daubechiesExpand_succ`,
`Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_wavelet_eq_daubechiesExpand_succ`) whose coefficients, written through
`a_n = ⟨f, φ_{j+1,n}⟩` (`Daubechies.coeffFun_scalingFun_eq_tsum`,
`Daubechies.coeffFun_wavelet_eq_tsum`), add up to `a` (perfect reconstruction,
`Daubechies.refineCoeff_add_waveletRefineCoeff`).

Daubechies.projFun_sub_eq_tsum.name: Daubechies.projFun_sub_eq_tsum
Daubechies.projFun_sub_eq_tsum.docstring:
**The kernel form of `P_j f - f`**: for `N ≥ 2`, locally integrable `f`, every level `j` and
point `x`, `P_j f(x) - f(x) = ∑_{k ∈ ℤ} φ_{j,k}(x) ∫ (f(y) - f(x)) conj φ_{j,k}(y) dy`. Subtract
`f(x) = ∑_k φ_{j,k}(x) f(x) ∫ conj φ_{j,k}` (`Daubechies.tsum_daubechiesScaled_mul_integral_conj`)
term by term; both sums have only finitely many nonzero terms.

Daubechies.projFun_sub.name: Daubechies.projFun_sub
Daubechies.projFun_sub.docstring:
**The projection is subtractive** on locally integrable functions: for `N ≥ 2`,
`P_j (f - g) = P_j f - P_j g` at every point (`Daubechies.projFun_add` and
`Daubechies.projFun_const_mul` with `z = -1`).

Daubechies.projFun_projFun.name: Daubechies.projFun_projFun
Daubechies.projFun_projFun.docstring:
**The pointwise projection is idempotent**: `P_j (P_j f) = P_j f` at every point, for `N ≥ 2`
and every `f`, since `P_j f` is an expansion of level `j`
(`Daubechies.projFun_daubechiesExpand`).

Daubechies.projFun_poly.name: Daubechies.projFun_poly
Daubechies.projFun_poly.docstring:
**The projection reproduces polynomials**: for `N ≥ 2`, every complex polynomial `Q` of
degree `< N` and every level `j`, `P_j Q = Q` at every point. This is the dyadic polynomial
reproduction `∑_k 2^j (∫ Q(y) conj φ(2^j y - k) dy) φ(2^j x - k) = Q(x)`
(`Daubechies.sum_inner_poly_mul_scalingFun_two_pow`), since
`⟨Q, φ_{j,k}⟩ φ_{j,k}(x) = 2^j (∫ Q(y) conj φ(2^j y - k) dy) φ(2^j x - k)`.

Daubechies.projFun_eq_sum_of_mem_cell.name: Daubechies.projFun_eq_sum_of_mem_cell
Daubechies.projFun_eq_sum_of_mem_cell.docstring:
**The projection on a dyadic cell is a finite sum**: for `N ≥ 2`, every `f` and every `x` in
the dyadic cell `[k/2^j, (k + 1)/2^j)`,
`P_j f(x) = ∑_{l = k - (2N - 2)}^{k} ⟨f, φ_{j,l}⟩ φ_{j,l}(x)`
(`Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_eq_zero_of_mem_cell`).

Daubechies.projFun_daubechiesExpand.name: Daubechies.projFun_daubechiesExpand
Daubechies.projFun_daubechiesExpand.docstring:
**The projection reproduces expansions**: for `N ≥ 2`, every level `j` and every coefficient
sequence `a : ℤ → ℂ`, `P_j (∑_k a_k φ_{j,k}) = ∑_k a_k φ_{j,k}` at every point, since the
coefficients are recovered, `⟨∑_l a_l φ_{j,l}, φ_{j,k}⟩ = a_k`
(`Daubechies.coeffFun_daubechiesExpand_scalingFun`).

Daubechies.projFun_const_mul.name: Daubechies.projFun_const_mul
Daubechies.projFun_const_mul.docstring:
**The projection is homogeneous**: `P_j (z f) = z P_j f` for every `z ∈ ℂ` and every `f`
(`Daubechies.coeffFun_const_mul`, `Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_const_mul`).

Daubechies.projFun_congr_ae.name: Daubechies.projFun_congr_ae
Daubechies.projFun_congr_ae.docstring:
**The projection depends only on the class of `f`**: if `f = f'` almost everywhere, then
`P_j f = P_j f'` at every point, since the coefficients agree
(`Daubechies.coeffFun_congr_ae`).

Daubechies.projFun_apply.name: Daubechies.projFun_apply
Daubechies.projFun_apply.docstring: `P_j f(x) = ∑_{k ∈ ℤ} ⟨f, φ_{j,k}⟩ φ_{j,k}(x)`, by definition.

Daubechies.projFun_add.name: Daubechies.projFun_add
Daubechies.projFun_add.docstring:
**The projection is additive** on locally integrable functions: for `N ≥ 2`,
`P_j (f + g) = P_j f + P_j g` at every point (`Daubechies.coeffFun_add`,
`Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_add`).

Daubechies.projFun.name: Daubechies.projFun
Daubechies.projFun.docstring:
**The projection of level `j`, pointwise**: for every function `f : ℝ → ℂ`,
`P_j f(x) = ∑_{k ∈ ℤ} ⟨f, φ_{j,k}⟩ φ_{j,k}(x)`, with the coefficients
`⟨f, φ_{j,k}⟩ = ∫ f(y) conj φ_{j,k}(y) dy` (`Daubechies.coeffFun`) and the functions
`φ_{j,k}(x) = 2^(j/2) φ(2^j x - k)` (`Daubechies.daubechiesScaled`). Only finitely many terms are
nonzero at each point, so the sum is meaningful for every `f`; for locally integrable `f` the
coefficients are genuine integrals.

Daubechies.projConst_nonneg.name: Daubechies.projConst_nonneg
Daubechies.projConst_nonneg.docstring: The bound `projConst m p` is nonnegative.

Daubechies.projConst.name: Daubechies.projConst
Daubechies.projConst.docstring:
**The bound of the projections**: the real number
`M^(1 - 1/p) ‖φ‖_p · M^(1/p) ‖φ‖_{p'} = 2N ‖φ‖_p ‖φ‖_{p'}` with the overlap number
`M = ⌈2N - 1⌉ + 1 = 2N` (for `N ≥ 1`) and the conjugate exponent `p'`, the product of the
constants of the upper estimate and of the coefficient estimate of the expansions
(`Daubechies.expandConst`, `Daubechies.coeffConst`, with the support interval `[0, 2N - 1]` of
`φ`). It is the same for every level.

Daubechies.prod_range_succ_symbol.name: Daubechies.prod_range_succ_symbol
Daubechies.prod_range_succ_symbol.docstring:
**Splitting off the first factor of a partial product**:
`∏_{j<n+1} m_0(ξ/2^(j+1)) = m_0(ξ/2) ∏_{j<n} m_0((ξ/2)/2^(j+1))`, since
`ξ/2^(j+2) = (ξ/2)/2^(j+1)`.

Daubechies.prod_daubFun_two_pow_mul_div.name: Daubechies.prod_daubFun_two_pow_mul_div
Daubechies.prod_daubFun_two_pow_mul_div.docstring:
Reindexing a dyadic product by `j = n - 1 - i`:
`∏_{j<n} P(2^n η / 2^(j+1)) = ∏_{i<n} P(2^i η)`, since `2^n / 2^(j+1) = 2^(n-1-j)` for `j < n`
(Mathlib's `Finset.prod_range_reflect`).

Daubechies.prod_daubFun_nonneg.name: Daubechies.prod_daubFun_nonneg
Daubechies.prod_daubFun_nonneg.docstring:
The finite dyadic products `∏_{j<n} P(ξ/2^(j+1))` of the trigonometric Daubechies polynomial
`P = Daubechies.daubFun N` are nonnegative, since `P ≥ 0`.

Daubechies.pow_dvd_iterate_X_mul_derivat.name: Daubechies.pow_dvd_iterate_X_mul_derivative
Daubechies.pow_dvd_iterate_X_mul_derivat.docstring:
If `(X + 1)^j` divides `p`, then `(X + 1)^(j - l)` divides the `l`-th iterate of the Euler
operator `p ↦ X p'` applied to `p`: each step differentiates once (Mathlib's
`Polynomial.pow_sub_one_dvd_derivative_of_pow_dvd`) and multiplies by `X`.

Daubechies.periodization_moment_eq.name: Daubechies.periodization_moment_eq
Daubechies.periodization_moment_eq.docstring:
**The periodised moments are constant**: for `N ≥ 2`, `l < N` and every `x ∈ ℝ`,
`∑_{k ∈ ℤ} (x - k)^l φ(x - k) = ∫ y^l φ(y) dy`. The function `f(y) = y^l φ(y)` is continuous,
vanishes outside `[0, 2N - 1]`, and `𝓕 f(n) = 0` for every integer `n ≠ 0`
(`Daubechies.fourier_pow_mul_scalingFun_int`), so Poisson summation
(`Real.tsum_comp_add_int_eq_integral`) gives `∑_n f(x + n) = ∫ f`; the substitution `k = -n`
turns this into the sum over the points `x - k`.

Daubechies.periodic_iterate_transferOp.name: Daubechies.periodic_iterate_transferOp
Daubechies.periodic_iterate_transferOp.docstring: The iterates `T^n g` of a `1`-periodic `g` are `1`-periodic.

Daubechies.periodic_expFreq_intCast_mul.name: Daubechies.periodic_expFreq_intCast_mul
Daubechies.periodic_expFreq_intCast_mul.docstring:
For every integer `k`, the function `ξ ↦ e^(-2πikξ)` has period `1`, since `e^(-2πik) = 1`
(`Daubechies.expFreq_intCast`).

Daubechies.periodic_comp_two_mul_mul_nor.name: Daubechies.periodic_comp_two_mul_mul_normSq_symbol
Daubechies.periodic_comp_two_mul_mul_nor.docstring:
For a `1`-periodic `w : ℝ → ℂ`, the function `ζ ↦ w(2ζ) |m_0(ζ)|²` is `1`-periodic again:
`w(2ζ + 2) = w(2ζ)`, and `m_0` has period `1` (`Daubechies.symbol_periodic`).

Daubechies.periodic_comp_two_mul.name: Daubechies.periodic_comp_two_mul
Daubechies.periodic_comp_two_mul.docstring:
If `h` has period `1`, then so has `η ↦ h(2η)`: `h` has period `2`, so `η ↦ h(2η)` has period
`2⁻¹ · 2 = 1` (Mathlib's `Function.Periodic.nat_mul` and `Function.Periodic.const_mul`).

Daubechies.one_sub_mul_eval_daubPoly_suc.name: Daubechies.one_sub_mul_eval_daubPoly_succ
Daubechies.one_sub_mul_eval_daubPoly_suc.docstring:
**The recurrence of the Daubechies polynomials**, evaluated: for every `N` and every real `y`,
`(1 - y) P_{N+1}(y) = P_N(y) + C(2N - 1, N) y^N - C(2N, N) y^(N+1)`.
On the left the constant term is `1`, the coefficient of `y^(k+1)` for `k < N` is
`C(N + k + 1, k + 1) - C(N + k, k) = C(N + k, k + 1)` (Pascal's rule, Mathlib's
`Nat.choose_succ_succ'`), and the top term is `-C(2N, N) y^(N+1)`; on the right
`P_N(y) + C(2N - 1, N) y^N = ∑_{k ≤ N} C(N - 1 + k, k) y^k` has the same coefficients.

Daubechies.one_le_eval_daubPoly.name: Daubechies.one_le_eval_daubPoly
Daubechies.one_le_eval_daubPoly.docstring:
`P_N(y) ≥ 1` for `y ≥ 0` and `N ≥ 1`: the constant term is `1`, and the other terms are
nonnegative.

Daubechies.one_div_toReal_conjExponent.name: Daubechies.one_div_toReal_conjExponent
Daubechies.one_div_toReal_conjExponent.docstring:
**The conjugate exponent**: for `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞` and `p' = p/(p - 1)` (Mathlib's
`ENNReal.conjExponent`), the real exponents satisfy `1/p' = 1 - 1/p`, from `1/p + 1/p' = 1`; for
`p = 1` this reads `1/∞ = 0`, the value Lean assigns.

Daubechies.one_add_expFreq_div_two.name: Daubechies.one_add_expFreq_div_two
Daubechies.one_add_expFreq_div_two.docstring:
**The factor `(1 + z)/2` on the unit circle**: `(1 + e^(-2πiξ))/2 = e^(-πiξ) cos(πξ)`, since
`2 cos(πξ) = e^(πiξ) + e^(-πiξ)` (Mathlib's `Complex.two_cos`).

Daubechies.one_add_abs_rpow_le_of_mem_an.name: Daubechies.one_add_abs_rpow_le_of_mem_annulus
Daubechies.one_add_abs_rpow_le_of_mem_an.docstring:
**The weight on the annuli**: for `ξ ∈ A_n` and every real `t`,
`(1 + |ξ|)^t ≤ 4^|t| (2^t)^n`, since `2^n/4 ≤ 1 + |ξ| ≤ 4 · 2^n`
(`Daubechies.rpow_le_four_rpow_abs_mul`).

Daubechies.ofReal_window_length_pow.name: Daubechies.ofReal_window_length_pow
Daubechies.ofReal_window_length_pow.docstring:
**The length of a window**: `|W_k|^N = (4N - 3)^N 2^(-jN)` for the window
`W_k = [(k - (2N - 2))/2^j, (k + 2N - 1)/2^j]` of length `(4N - 3)/2^j`, `N ≥ 1`.

Daubechies.ofReal_projConst.name: Daubechies.ofReal_projConst
Daubechies.ofReal_projConst.docstring:
For `N ≥ 2` the bound `projConst m p` is the product of the (finite) constants of the upper
estimate and of the coefficient estimate (`Daubechies.expandConst_ne_top`,
`Daubechies.coeffConst_ne_top`).

Daubechies.norm_truncProduct_le.name: Daubechies.norm_truncProduct_le
Daubechies.norm_truncProduct_le.docstring:
**The truncated products are dominated by the symbol product**: if `κ > 0` and
`κ ≤ |Φ(ξ)|` for all `|ξ| ≤ 1/2` (such a `κ` exists by
`Daubechies.exists_pos_le_norm_symbolProduct`), then `|Φ_n(ξ)| ≤ |Φ(ξ)|/κ` for every `n` and
every `ξ ∈ ℝ`. Outside `[-2^n/2, 2^n/2)` the left side is `0`. Inside, `|ξ/2^n| ≤ 1/2` and
`Φ(ξ) = ∏_{j<n} m_0(ξ/2^(j+1)) · Φ(ξ/2^n)` (`Daubechies.symbolProduct_eq_prod_mul`), so
`|Φ(ξ)| ≥ |Φ_n(ξ)| κ`.

Daubechies.norm_symbol_sub_one_le.name: Daubechies.norm_symbol_sub_one_le
Daubechies.norm_symbol_sub_one_le.docstring:
**The symbol is Lipschitz at `0`**: `|m_0(ξ) - 1| ≤ π ∑_k k |c_k| · |ξ|`. Since
`∑_k c_k = 2`, `m_0(ξ) - 1 = (1/2) ∑_k c_k (e^(-2πikξ) - 1)`, and
`|e^(-2πikξ) - 1| ≤ 2πk|ξ|`.

Daubechies.norm_symbol_le_one.name: Daubechies.norm_symbol_le_one
Daubechies.norm_symbol_le_one.docstring: `|m_0(ξ)| ≤ 1`, from the quadrature mirror filter identity.

Daubechies.norm_prod_symbol_le_one.name: Daubechies.norm_prod_symbol_le_one
Daubechies.norm_prod_symbol_le_one.docstring:
The partial products have modulus at most `1`:
`|∏_{j<n} m_0(ξ/2^(j+1))| ≤ 1`, since `|m_0| ≤ 1`.

Daubechies.norm_fourier_cascade_le_one.name: Daubechies.norm_fourier_cascade_le_one
Daubechies.norm_fourier_cascade_le_one.docstring:
**The Fourier transforms of the cascade are bounded by `1`**: `|𝓕 η_n(ξ)| ≤ 1` for every `n`
and every `ξ ∈ ℝ`. In `Daubechies.fourier_cascade` the partial products of the symbol have
modulus at most `1` (`Daubechies.norm_prod_symbol_le_one`), and `|𝓕 η_0| ≤ 1`.

Daubechies.norm_daubechiesProj_le.name: Daubechies.norm_daubechiesProj_le
Daubechies.norm_daubechiesProj_le.docstring: **The projections are uniformly bounded**: `‖P_j‖ ≤ projConst m p` for every level `j`.

Daubechies.norm_cos_sub_one_le.name: Daubechies.norm_cos_sub_one_le
Daubechies.norm_cos_sub_one_le.docstring:
`|cos(y) - 1| ≤ y²/2` for every real `y`, from `1 - y²/2 ≤ cos(y) ≤ 1` (Mathlib's
`Real.one_sub_sq_div_two_le_cos`).

Daubechies.normSq_truncProduct_succ.name: Daubechies.normSq_truncProduct_succ
Daubechies.normSq_truncProduct_succ.docstring:
The recursion for the squared moduli:
`|Φ_(n+1)(ξ)|² = |m_0(ξ/2)|² |Φ_n(ξ/2)|²` (`Daubechies.truncProduct_succ`).

Daubechies.normSq_symbolProduct_le_of_me.name: Daubechies.normSq_symbolProduct_le_of_mem_annulus
Daubechies.normSq_symbolProduct_le_of_me.docstring:
**The pointwise bound on the annuli**: for `ξ ∈ A_n`,
`|Φ(ξ)|² ≤ exp(C(2N - 1, N) π²/12) (4/(π 2^n))^(2N) ∏_{j<n} P(ξ/2^(j+1))`, from
`Daubechies.normSq_symbolProduct_le` (`|ξ| ≤ 2^n/2` on `A_n`) and the bound on `sinc`
(`Daubechies.sinc_pow_le_of_mem_annulus`).

Daubechies.normSq_symbolProduct_le.name: Daubechies.normSq_symbolProduct_le
Daubechies.normSq_symbolProduct_le.docstring:
**The bound on `|Φ|²` by a finite product**: for `|ξ| ≤ 2^n/2`,
`|Φ(ξ)|² ≤ exp(C(2N - 1, N) π²/12) · sinc(πξ)^(2N) ∏_{j<n} P(ξ/2^(j+1))`. The product of `P` splits
into the first `n` factors and the tail (`Daubechies.tprod_daubFun_eq_prod_mul`), and the tail is
at most `exp(C(2N - 1, N) π²/12)` (`Daubechies.tprod_daubFun_shift_le`).

Daubechies.normSq_symbolProduct.name: Daubechies.normSq_symbolProduct
Daubechies.normSq_symbolProduct.docstring:
**The squared modulus of the symbol product**:
`|Φ(ξ)|² = sinc(πξ)^(2N) ∏_{j ≥ 0} P(ξ/2^(j+1))`, where `P = Daubechies.daubFun N`. The factors
satisfy `|m_0(η)|² = cos(πη)^(2N) P(η)` (`Daubechies.normSq_symbol`), and
`∏_{j ≥ 0} cos(πξ/2^(j+1)) = sinc(πξ)` (`Daubechies.hasProd_cos_div_two_pow`); both products
converge, so the product of the squared moduli is the product of the two.

Daubechies.normSq_symbol.name: Daubechies.normSq_symbol
Daubechies.normSq_symbol.docstring:
**The squared modulus of the symbol**: `|m_0(ξ)|² = cos(πξ)^(2N) P(ξ)`, from
`|(1 + e^(-2πiξ))/2|² = cos²(πξ)` and `|L(e^(-2πiξ))|² = P(ξ)`.

Daubechies.neg_one_zpow_eq_of_even_sub.name: Daubechies.neg_one_zpow_eq_of_even_sub
Daubechies.neg_one_zpow_eq_of_even_sub.docstring: `(-1)^a = (-1)^b` for integers `a, b` of the same parity.

Daubechies.natDegree_maskPoly_le.name: Daubechies.natDegree_maskPoly_le
Daubechies.natDegree_maskPoly_le.docstring: The mask polynomial has degree `≤ 2N - 1`: `N` factors of degree `1` and `deg L ≤ N - 1`.

Daubechies.natCeil_higherDiff_support_ad.name: Daubechies.natCeil_higherDiff_support_add_one
Daubechies.natCeil_higherDiff_support_ad.docstring:
**The overlap number of the differences of `φ`**: for `N ≥ 1` and every `r ∈ ℕ`, the interval
`[-r, 2N - 1 + r]`, outside which the differences `Δ_H^r φ` with `|H| ≤ 1` vanish
(`Daubechies.higherDiff_scalingFun_eq_zero`), has the overlap number
`⌈(2N - 1 + r) - (-r)⌉ + 1 = 2N + 2r` of the upper estimate of expansions
(`Daubechies.eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand_le`).

Daubechies.multipliable_symbolProduct.name: Daubechies.multipliable_symbolProduct
Daubechies.multipliable_symbolProduct.docstring:
**The symbol product converges** for every `ξ`: the factors are `1 + a_j` with
`∑_j |a_j| < ∞` (Mathlib's `multipliable_one_add_of_summable`).

Daubechies.multipliable_daubFun_shift.name: Daubechies.multipliable_daubFun_shift
Daubechies.multipliable_daubFun_shift.docstring:
The tail `∏_{j ≥ 0} P(ξ/2^(n+j+1))` of the product of the trigonometric Daubechies
polynomial converges: it is the full product at the point `ξ/2^n`.

Daubechies.multipliable_daubFun.name: Daubechies.multipliable_daubFun
Daubechies.multipliable_daubFun.docstring:
**The product of the trigonometric Daubechies polynomial converges**:
`∏_{j ≥ 0} P(x/2^(j+1))` is multipliable for every `N` and every real `x`, where
`P = Daubechies.daubFun N`. For `N ≥ 1` the factors are `1 + a_j` with
`0 ≤ a_j ≤ C(2N - 1, N) π² (x/2^(j+1))²` (`Daubechies.one_le_daubFun`, `Daubechies.daubFun_le`),
a summable bound; for `N = 0` every factor is `0`.

Daubechies.multipliable_cos_div_two_pow.name: Daubechies.multipliable_cos_div_two_pow
Daubechies.multipliable_cos_div_two_pow.docstring:
The infinite product `∏_{j ≥ 0} cos(x/2^(j+1))` converges: its factors are `1 + a_j` with
`|a_j| ≤ (x/2^(j+1))²/2`, a summable bound (Mathlib's `Real.multipliable_one_add_of_summable`).

Daubechies.modulusData.name: Daubechies.modulusData
Daubechies.modulusData.docstring:
**The modulus of smoothness is compatible with the Daubechies scheme**: for `N ≥ 2`,
`1 ≤ p < ∞` and a Bernstein bound `ω_N(φ, t)_p ≤ K t^θ` for `0 < t ≤ 1`
(`Daubechies.BernsteinBound` with differences of order `N`), the modulus
`ω_N(f, 2^(-k))_p` (`Rd.lpModulus p N`) is compatible with the Daubechies scheme with inverse
order `θ` (`ApproximationScheme.ModulusData`). Jackson's inequality
`E_{2^k}(f)_p ≤ C_J ω_N(f, 2^(-k))_p` holds from level `0` on
(`Daubechies.approxError_daubechiesScheme_le_daubechiesJacksonConst_mul`), and the inverse
inequality `ω_N(a, 2^(-k))_p ≤ C_B 2^(-(k-j)θ) ‖a‖_p` for the approximants `a` of complexity `2^j`
is `Daubechies.inverse_daubechiesScheme`.

Daubechies.mem_supportWindow_of_scaledFu.name: Daubechies.mem_supportWindow_of_scaledFun_ne_zero
Daubechies.mem_supportWindow_of_scaledFu.docstring:
If `g` vanishes outside `[a, b]` and `g_{j,k}(x) ≠ 0`, then `x` lies in the support window
`{x : 2^j x - k ∈ [a, b]}` (`Daubechies.scaledFun_eq_zero`).

Daubechies.mem_scalingSpace.name: Daubechies.mem_scalingSpace
Daubechies.mem_scalingSpace.docstring: `a ∈ V_j` iff `a = P_j f` for some `f ∈ L_p`.

Daubechies.mem_daubechiesScheme_two_pow.name: Daubechies.mem_daubechiesScheme_two_pow
Daubechies.mem_daubechiesScheme_two_pow.docstring: The approximants of complexity `2^k` are the elements of the scaling space `V_k`.

Daubechies.mem_Ico_two_pow_succ_iff.name: Daubechies.mem_Ico_two_pow_succ_iff
Daubechies.mem_Ico_two_pow_succ_iff.docstring:
The cut-off intervals double from one level to the next:
`ξ ∈ [-2^(n+1)/2, 2^(n+1)/2)` if and only if `ξ/2 ∈ [-2^n/2, 2^n/2)`.

Daubechies.mem_Icc_of_two_mul_sub_mem_Ic.name: Daubechies.mem_Icc_of_two_mul_sub_mem_Icc
Daubechies.mem_Icc_of_two_mul_sub_mem_Ic.docstring:
If `0 ≤ k ≤ b` and `2x - k ∈ [0, b]`, then `x ∈ [0, b]`: `x ≥ k/2 ≥ 0` and
`x ≤ (b + k)/2 ≤ b`. For `b = 2N - 1` this is the step of the support argument for the cascade:
no map `x ↦ 2x - k` with `0 ≤ k ≤ 2N - 1` sends a point outside `[0, 2N - 1]` into
`[0, 2N - 1]`.

Daubechies.mem_Icc_of_mem_supportWindow.name: Daubechies.mem_Icc_of_mem_supportWindow
Daubechies.mem_Icc_of_mem_supportWindow.docstring:
