**Positions of overlapping windows are close**: if `x` lies in the support windows of level
`j` and positions `l` and `k`, then `|l - k| ≤ ⌈b - a⌉`, since `2^j x - l` and `2^j x - k` both
lie in `[a, b]`.

Daubechies.mem_Icc_of_dualCoeff_ne_zero.name: Daubechies.mem_Icc_of_dualCoeff_ne_zero
Daubechies.mem_Icc_of_dualCoeff_ne_zero.docstring:
**Support of the dual filter**: if `g_i ≠ 0`, then `2 - 2N ≤ i ≤ 1`
(`Daubechies.dualCoeff_eq_zero`).

Daubechies.mem_Icc_of_daubechiesCoeff_ne.name: Daubechies.mem_Icc_of_daubechiesCoeff_ne_zero
Daubechies.mem_Icc_of_daubechiesCoeff_ne.docstring:
**Support of the filter**: if the filter coefficient `c_i` is nonzero, then
`0 ≤ i ≤ 2N - 1` (`Daubechies.daubechiesCoeff_eq_zero`).

Daubechies.mem_Icc_ceil_floor.name: Daubechies.mem_Icc_ceil_floor
Daubechies.mem_Icc_ceil_floor.docstring:
**The integers in an interval**: if `t - k ∈ [a, b]` for an integer `k`, then
`⌈t - b⌉ ≤ k ≤ ⌊t - a⌋`.

Daubechies.memLp_wavelet.name: Daubechies.memLp_wavelet
Daubechies.memLp_wavelet.docstring:
**The wavelet lies in every `L_p`**, `p ∈ [0, ∞]`, for `N ≥ 2`: it is continuous with compact
support (Mathlib's `Continuous.memLp_of_hasCompactSupport`).

Daubechies.memLp_symbolProduct_two.name: Daubechies.memLp_symbolProduct_two
Daubechies.memLp_symbolProduct_two.docstring:
**The symbol product is square integrable** for every Daubechies mask of order `N ≥ 2`: the
case `s = 0` of `Daubechies.integrable_rpow_mul_normSq` with the crude growth bound, since
`log₄(2 C(2N - 1, N)) < N - 1/2 < N`.

Daubechies.memLp_scalingFun.name: Daubechies.memLp_scalingFun
Daubechies.memLp_scalingFun.docstring:
**The scaling function lies in every `L^p`**: `φ ∈ L^p(ℝ)` for every exponent `p ∈ [0, ∞]`,
for `N ≥ 2`, since it is continuous with compact support (Mathlib's
`Continuous.memLp_of_hasCompactSupport`).

Daubechies.memLp_projFun.name: Daubechies.memLp_projFun
Daubechies.memLp_projFun.docstring:
**The projection of an `L_p` function lies in `L_p`**: for `N ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `f ∈ L_p`
and every level `j` (`Daubechies.memLp_daubechiesExpand_coeffFun`).

Daubechies.memLp_of_continuous_of_eq_zer.name: Daubechies.memLp_of_continuous_of_eq_zero
Daubechies.memLp_of_continuous_of_eq_zer.docstring:
A continuous `g` vanishing outside `[a, b]` lies in every `L_p`: it has compact support
(Mathlib's `Continuous.memLp_of_hasCompactSupport`).

Daubechies.memLp_daubechiesExpand_coeffF.name: Daubechies.memLp_daubechiesExpand_coeffFun
Daubechies.memLp_daubechiesExpand_coeffF.docstring:
**The expansion of the coefficients of an `L_p` function lies in `L_p`**: if `g` is
continuous and vanishes outside `[a, b]`, `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `f ∈ L_p`, then
`∑_k ⟨f, g_{j,k}⟩ g_{j,k} ∈ L_p` for every level `j`
(`Daubechies.eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand_coeffFun_le`).

Daubechies.memLp_daubechiesDetailFun.name: Daubechies.memLp_daubechiesDetailFun
Daubechies.memLp_daubechiesDetailFun.docstring:
**The wavelet part of an `L_p` function lies in `L_p`**: for `N ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `f ∈ L_p`
and every level `j` (`Daubechies.memLp_daubechiesExpand_coeffFun` for `g = ψ`).

Daubechies.memApprox_daubechiesScheme_if.name: Daubechies.memApprox_daubechiesScheme_iff_modulus
Daubechies.memApprox_daubechiesScheme_if.docstring:
**Approximation by the Daubechies scaling spaces and moduli of smoothness**: for `N ≥ 2`,
`1 ≤ p < ∞`, a Bernstein bound of order `θ` for `φ` with differences of order `N`,
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and `0 ≤ s < θ`, an `f ∈ L_p(ℝ)` lies in the approximation space `A^s_q` of the
Daubechies scheme iff `‖f‖_p + ‖(2^(ks) ω_N(f, 2^(-k))_p)_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`. This is the coincidence
theorem `ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.memApprox_iff_modNorm_lt_top` for
`Daubechies.modulusData`.

Daubechies.memApprox_daubechiesScheme_if.name: Daubechies.memApprox_daubechiesScheme_iff_coeff
Daubechies.memApprox_daubechiesScheme_if.docstring:
**Approximation by the Daubechies scaling spaces through coefficients**: for `N ≥ 2`,
`1 ≤ p < ∞`, `s > 0` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, an `f ∈ L_p(ℝ)` lies in the approximation space `A^s_q`
of the Daubechies scheme iff its coefficient quasi-norm
`‖(⟨f, φ(· - k)⟩)_k‖_{ℓ_p} + ‖(2^(j(s + 1/2 - 1/p)) ‖(⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩)_k‖_{ℓ_p})_j‖_{ℓ_q}`
(`Daubechies.daubechiesCoeffNorm`) is finite.

The projections form a projection scheme with dense union, so `f ∈ A^s_q` iff
`‖P_0 f‖_p + ‖(2^(js) ‖P_{j+1} f - P_j f‖_p)_j‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`
(`ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.memApprox_iff_blockNorm_lt_top_of_dense`). The first summand
`‖P_0 f‖_p` and `‖(⟨f, φ(· - k)⟩)_k‖_{ℓ_p}` are both finite
(`Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesProj_zero_equiv`), and
`2^(js) ‖P_{j+1} f - P_j f‖_p` is comparable with
`2^(j(s + 1/2 - 1/p)) ‖(⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩)_k‖_{ℓ_p}` uniformly in `j` (`Daubechies.enorm_block_equiv`),
so the two `ℓ_q` norms are finite together (`ENNReal.lqNorm_lt_top_iff_of_le_mul`).

Daubechies.measurable_truncProduct.name: Daubechies.measurable_truncProduct
Daubechies.measurable_truncProduct.docstring:
The truncated products are measurable: a continuous function times the indicator function
of an interval.

Daubechies.measurableSet_supportWindow.name: Daubechies.measurableSet_supportWindow
Daubechies.measurableSet_supportWindow.docstring: The support windows are measurable (closed intervals).

Daubechies.maskPoly.name: Daubechies.maskPoly
Daubechies.maskPoly.docstring: **The mask polynomial** `m(z) = ((1 + z)/2)^N L(z)` of a mask of order `N`.

Daubechies.lqNorm_le_of_le_eLpNorm_indic.name: Daubechies.lqNorm_le_of_le_eLpNorm_indicator
Daubechies.lqNorm_le_of_le_eLpNorm_indic.docstring:
**Summing local bounds over the support windows**: let `0 < p < ∞`, let `f` be a.e. strongly
measurable, and let `d : ℤ → [0, ∞]` satisfy `d_k ≤ ‖1_{W_k} f‖_p B` for every `k`, where
`W_k = {x : 2^j x - k ∈ [a, b]}` are the support windows of level `j`. Then
`‖d‖_{ℓ_p} ≤ M^(1/p) B ‖f‖_p` with the overlap number `M = ⌈b - a⌉ + 1`: the windows overlap at
most `M` times (`Daubechies.card_le_of_forall_mem_supportWindow`), so the window inequality in
`ℓ_p` form (`MeasureTheory.lqNorm_le_mul_eLpNorm_of_overlap`) applies.

Daubechies.lqNorm_le_eLpNorm_daubechiesE.name: Daubechies.lqNorm_le_eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand
Daubechies.lqNorm_le_eLpNorm_daubechiesE.docstring:
**Lower stability of the expansions**: let `g` be continuous, vanish outside `[a, b]`, and
have orthonormal integer translates, and let `1 ≤ p < ∞`. Then for every level `j` and all
coefficients `c : ℤ → ℂ`, `2^(j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖c‖_{ℓ_p} ≤ C' ‖∑_k c_k g_{j,k}‖_p` with the constant
`C' = coeffConst g a b p`. The coefficients are recovered from the expansion,
`c_k = ⟨∑_l c_l g_{j,l}, g_{j,k}⟩` (`Daubechies.coeffFun_daubechiesExpand`), and the coefficient
estimate (`Daubechies.dyadicWeight_mul_lqNorm_coeffFun_le`) applies to the continuous expansion.

Daubechies.lqNorm_coeffFun_le.name: Daubechies.lqNorm_coeffFun_le
Daubechies.lqNorm_coeffFun_le.docstring:
**The coefficient estimate**: let `g` be a.e. strongly measurable and vanish outside
`[a, b]`, and let `1 ≤ p < ∞`. Then for every a.e. strongly measurable `f` and every level `j`,
`‖(⟨f, g_{j,k}⟩)_k‖_{ℓ_p} ≤ M^(1/p) ‖g‖_{p'} 2^(-j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖f‖_p` with the overlap number
`M = ⌈b - a⌉ + 1` and the conjugate exponent `p'`. The constant `M^(1/p) ‖g‖_{p'}`
(`Daubechies.coeffConst`) is the same for every `j` and `f`. Each coefficient is bounded by
Hölder's inequality on its support window, `|⟨f, g_{j,k}⟩| ≤ ‖1_{W_k} f‖_p ‖g_{j,k}‖_{p'}`
(`Daubechies.enorm_coeffFun_le`) with `‖g_{j,k}‖_{p'} = 2^(-j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖g‖_{p'}`
(`Daubechies.eLpNorm_scaledFun_conjExponent`), and the windows overlap at most `M` times
(`Daubechies.lqNorm_le_of_le_eLpNorm_indicator`).

Daubechies.lpModulus_le_of_mem_scalingSp.name: Daubechies.lpModulus_le_of_mem_scalingSpace
Daubechies.lpModulus_le_of_mem_scalingSp.docstring:
**The modulus of an element of `V_j` at the dyadic scales `2^(-k)`, `k ≥ j`**: let `N ≥ 2`,
`1 ≤ p < ∞`, and let `ω_r(φ, t)_p ≤ K t^θ` for all `0 < t ≤ 1`. Then for all levels `j ≤ k` and
every `a ∈ V_j` (`Daubechies.scalingSpace`), `ω_r(a, 2^(-k))_p ≤ C K 2^(-(k-j)θ) ‖a‖_p` with
`C = Daubechies.daubechiesBernsteinConst m p r`. This is the Bernstein inequality
`Daubechies.smoothnessModulus_mem_scalingSpace_le` at `t = 2^(-k)`, where
`2^j t = 2^(-(k-j)) ∈ (0, 1]`.

Daubechies.logb_four_two_mul_choose_lt.name: Daubechies.logb_four_two_mul_choose_lt
Daubechies.logb_four_two_mul_choose_lt.docstring:
`log₄(2 C(2N - 1, N)) < N - 1/2` for `N ≥ 2`. It follows from `C(2N - 1, N) < 4^(N - 1)`
(`Daubechies.choose_lt_four_pow`), since `2 · 4^(N - 1) = 4^(N - 1/2)`.

Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbol_half_add.name: Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbol_half_add_int
Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbol_half_add.docstring:
**The derivatives of the symbol vanish at the half-integers** up to order `N - 1`:
`m_0^(l)(1/2 + n) = 0` for `l < N` and `n ∈ ℤ`. At `ξ = 1/2 + n` one has
`e^(-2πikξ) = (-1)^k`, so `m_0^(l)(1/2 + n) = (1/2) (-2πi)^l ∑_k (-1)^k k^l c_k`, which vanishes
by the sum rules.

Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_t.name: Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_two_mul_eq_zero
Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_t.docstring:
If all derivatives `Φ^(i)`, `i ≤ l`, vanish at a point `ξ`, then `Φ^(l)(2ξ) = 0` (for
`N ≥ 2`): every term of the Leibniz sum in `Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_two_mul`
contains a factor `Φ^(l-i)(ξ) = 0`.

Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_t.name: Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_two_mul_add_one
Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_t.docstring:
**`Φ^(l)` vanishes at the odd integers** for `l < N` (and `N ≥ 2`): `Φ^(l)(2n + 1) = 0` for
every `n ∈ ℤ`. In the Leibniz sum of `Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_two_mul` at
`ξ = 1/2 + n` every derivative `m_0^(i)(1/2 + n)`, `i ≤ l < N`, vanishes
(`Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbol_half_add_int`, a consequence of the sum rules).

Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_t.name: Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_two_mul
Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_t.docstring:
**The derivatives of the refinement identity** `Φ(2ξ) = m_0(ξ) Φ(ξ)`: for `N ≥ 2`, every
`l ∈ ℕ` and every `ξ ∈ ℝ`,
`2^l Φ^(l)(2ξ) = ∑_{i=0}^{l} C(l, i) m_0^(i)(ξ) Φ^(l-i)(ξ)`.
The left side is the `l`-th derivative of `ξ ↦ Φ(2ξ)` (chain rule, Mathlib's
`iteratedDeriv_comp_const_smul`), the right side that of `m_0 · Φ` (Leibniz rule, Mathlib's
`iteratedDeriv_fun_mul`); both factors are smooth (`Daubechies.contDiff_symbol`,
`Daubechies.contDiff_symbolProduct`).

Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_i.name: Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_int
Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_i.docstring:
**The derivatives of `Φ` vanish at the nonzero integers**: for `N ≥ 2`, every integer
`j ≠ 0` and every `l < N`, `Φ^(l)(j) = 0`. By induction on `|j|`, for all `l < N` at once: an
odd `j` is covered by `Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_two_mul_add_one`; for even
`j = 2j'` the integer `j' ≠ 0` is smaller in absolute value, so `Φ^(i)(j') = 0` for every
`i ≤ l`, and `Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_two_mul_eq_zero` gives `Φ^(l)(2j') = 0`.

Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_e.name: Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_eq_fourier
Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_e.docstring:
**The derivatives of `Φ` are the Fourier transforms of the moments**: for `N ≥ 2`, every
`l ∈ ℕ` and every `ξ ∈ ℝ`, `Φ^(l)(ξ) = (-2πi)^l 𝓕[x^l φ](ξ)`. This is differentiation under the
integral sign in `Φ = 𝓕 φ` (Mathlib's `Real.iteratedDeriv_fourier`), legitimate since every
moment of `φ` is integrable.

Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_sum_mul_cexp.name: Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_sum_mul_cexp
Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_sum_mul_cexp.docstring:
**Derivatives of a finite exponential sum** in a real variable: for `a_i, b_i ∈ ℂ`,
`(d/dt)^l ∑_i a_i e^(b_i t) = ∑_i a_i b_i^l e^(b_i t)`. Mathlib's
`iteratedDeriv_cexp_const_mul` is the version for a complex variable.

Daubechies.iterate_fwdDiff_eq_zero_of_no.name: Daubechies.iterate_fwdDiff_eq_zero_of_notMem
Daubechies.iterate_fwdDiff_eq_zero_of_no.docstring:
**The support of a difference**: if `f : ℝ → ℂ` vanishes outside `[a, b]`, then `Δ_h^r f`
vanishes outside `[a - r|h|, b + r|h|]`, for every `r ∈ ℕ` and every `h ∈ ℝ`. By induction on
`r`: `Δ_h^(r+1) f(x) = Δ_h^r f(x + h) - Δ_h^r f(x)`, and for `x` outside
`[a - (r+1)|h|, b + (r+1)|h|]` both `x` and `x + h` lie outside `[a - r|h|, b + r|h|]`.

Daubechies.iterate_fwdDiff_daubechiesExp.name: Daubechies.iterate_fwdDiff_daubechiesExpand
Daubechies.iterate_fwdDiff_daubechiesExp.docstring:
**Higher differences of an expansion**: if `g` vanishes outside `[a, b]`, then for every
order `r`, level `j`, all coefficients `c : ℤ → ℂ` and every step `h`,
`Δ_h^r (∑_k c_k g_{j,k}) = ∑_k c_k (Δ_{2^j h}^r g)_{j,k}` at every point. By induction on `r`
from `Daubechies.fwdDiff_daubechiesExpand`; each generator `Δ_{2^j h}^i g` vanishes outside a
bounded interval (`Daubechies.iterate_fwdDiff_eq_zero_of_notMem`).

Daubechies.isCompact_supportWindow.name: Daubechies.isCompact_supportWindow
Daubechies.isCompact_supportWindow.docstring: The support windows are compact (closed bounded intervals).

Daubechies.inverse_daubechiesScheme.name: Daubechies.inverse_daubechiesScheme
Daubechies.inverse_daubechiesScheme.docstring:
**The inverse inequality of the Daubechies scheme** (Bernstein): let `N ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`,
and let `φ` have a Bernstein bound of order `θ` with differences of order `r`
(`Daubechies.BernsteinBound`). Then there is a finite constant `C_B` with
`ω_r(a, 2^(-k))_p ≤ C_B 2^(-(k-j)θ) ‖a‖_p` for all `j, k ∈ ℕ` and every approximant `a` of
complexity `2^j` of the Daubechies scheme (`Daubechies.daubechiesScheme`; these are the elements of
`V_j`), where `k - j` is truncated at `0`. For `k ≥ j` this is
`Daubechies.lpModulus_le_of_mem_scalingSpace`; for `k < j` the weight is `1` and
`ω_r(a, t)_p ≤ 2^r ‖a‖_p` (`Rd.lpModulus_le`). This is the inverse inequality of
`ApproximationScheme.ModulusData` for the modulus `Rd.lpModulus p r`.

Daubechies.intervalIntegral_zero_one_eq_.name: Daubechies.intervalIntegral_zero_one_eq_add_half
Daubechies.intervalIntegral_zero_one_eq_.docstring:
**Splitting a period into two halves**: `∫_0^1 g(ζ) dζ = ∫_0^(1/2) (g(ζ) + g(ζ + 1/2)) dζ`
for every continuous `g : ℝ → ℂ`. The integral over `[1/2, 1]` is the integral of `g(· + 1/2)`
over `[0, 1/2]` (Mathlib's `intervalIntegral.integral_comp_add_right`).

Daubechies.integral_wavelet_translate_mu.name: Daubechies.integral_wavelet_translate_mul_conj_translate
Daubechies.integral_wavelet_translate_mu.docstring:
**Orthonormality of the integer translates of the wavelet**: for `N ≥ 2` and all `k, l ∈ ℤ`,
`∫ ψ(x - k) conj ψ(x - l) dx` is `1` for `k = l` and `0` otherwise: the level `j = 0` of
`Daubechies.integral_waveletScaled_mul_conj` (`Daubechies.scaledFun_zero`).

Daubechies.integral_waveletScaled_mul_co.name: Daubechies.integral_waveletScaled_mul_conj
Daubechies.integral_waveletScaled_mul_co.docstring:
**Orthonormality of the wavelets at every level**: for `N ≥ 2`, every level `j` and all
positions `k, l`, `∫ ψ_{j,k}(x) conj ψ_{j,l}(x) dx` is `1` for `k = l` and `0` otherwise. Both
wavelets are expansions of level `j + 1` with the coefficients `g_{n-2k}/√2` and `g_{n-2l}/√2`
(`Daubechies.waveletScaled_eq_daubechiesExpand`), so by Parseval's identity
(`Daubechies.integral_daubechiesExpand_mul_conj_daubechiesExpand`) the integral is
`(1/2) ∑_n g_{n-2k} g_{n-2l} = (1/2) ∑_a g_a g_{a+2(k-l)} = δ_{kl}`
(`Daubechies.sum_dualCoeff_mul_dualCoeff_add`).

Daubechies.integral_tsum_mul_scalingFun_.name: Daubechies.integral_tsum_mul_scalingFun_sub_mul_conj
Daubechies.integral_tsum_mul_scalingFun_.docstring:
**Coefficient recovery**: for `N ≥ 2`, every sequence `a : ℤ → ℂ` and every `k ∈ ℤ`,
`∫ (∑_{j ∈ ℤ} a(j) φ(y - j)) conj φ(y - k) dy = a(k)`. This is coefficient recovery for the
scaling function at level `0` (`Daubechies.coeffFun_daubechiesExpand_scalingFun`,
`Daubechies.scaledFun_zero`). The sequence `a` is arbitrary: at each point the sum over `j` is
finite.

Daubechies.integral_transferOp.name: Daubechies.integral_transferOp
Daubechies.integral_transferOp.docstring:
**The adjoint identity of the transfer operator**: for continuous `1`-periodic `h` and `g`,
`∫_{-1/2}^{1/2} h(η) (T g)(η) dη = 2 ∫_{-1/2}^{1/2} h(2η) P(η) g(η) dη`. With
`f(u) = h(2u) P(u) g(u)`, which is continuous and `1`-periodic, the integrand on the left is
`f(η/2) + f((η + 1)/2)`, because `h(η) = h(η + 1)`; then
`Daubechies.integral_comp_div_two_add_comp_add_one_div_two` applies.

Daubechies.integral_sum_mul_conj_sum.name: Daubechies.integral_sum_mul_conj_sum
Daubechies.integral_sum_mul_conj_sum.docstring:
**Orthonormality of the exponentials `e^(-2πikξ)` on `[0, 1]`**, for finite sums over a
finite set `u ⊆ ℤ` with coefficients `a, b : ℤ → ℂ`:
`∫_0^1 (∑_{k ∈ u} a_k e^(-2πikξ)) conj (∑_{k ∈ u} b_k e^(-2πikξ)) dξ = ∑_{k ∈ u} a_k conj b_k`.

Daubechies.integral_scalingFun_translate.name: Daubechies.integral_scalingFun_translate_mul_conj_translate
Daubechies.integral_scalingFun_translate.docstring:
**Orthonormality of the integer translates, for two translates**: for a mask of order
`N ≥ 2` and all `k, l ∈ ℤ`, `∫ φ(x - k) conj φ(x - l) dx` is `1` for `k = l` and `0` otherwise.
The substitution `x ↦ x + l` (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.integral_add_right_eq_self`) reduces it to
`Daubechies.integral_scalingFun_translate_mul_conj` for `k - l`.

Daubechies.integral_scalingFun_translate.name: Daubechies.integral_scalingFun_translate_mul_conj
Daubechies.integral_scalingFun_translate.docstring:
**Orthonormality of the integer translates of the scaling function**: for a mask of order
`N ≥ 2` and every `k ∈ ℤ`, `∫ φ(x - k) conj φ(x) dx` is `1` for `k = 0` and `0` otherwise.
Parseval's identity (`Real.integral_mul_conj_eq_integral_fourier`; `φ` is continuous and
integrable, with integrable transform `𝓕 φ = Φ` by `Daubechies.fourier_scalingFun`) and the
translation rule `𝓕[φ(· - k)](ξ) = e^(-2πikξ) Φ(ξ)` (`Real.fourier_comp_sub_right_apply`) turn the
integral into `∫ e^(-2πikξ) |Φ(ξ)|² dξ`, which is
`Daubechies.integral_normSq_symbolProduct_mul_expFreq`.

Daubechies.integral_scalingFun.name: Daubechies.integral_scalingFun
Daubechies.integral_scalingFun.docstring:
**The scaling function has integral `1`**: `∫ φ = 𝓕 φ(0) = Φ(0) = 1` for `N ≥ 2`
(`Real.real_fourier_apply_zero`, `Daubechies.fourier_scalingFun`,
`Daubechies.symbolProduct_zero`).

Daubechies.integral_scaledFun_mul_conj.name: Daubechies.integral_scaledFun_mul_conj
Daubechies.integral_scaledFun_mul_conj.docstring:
**Orthonormality at every level**: if the integer translates of `g` are orthonormal,
`∫ g(x - k) conj g(x - l) dx = δ_{kl}` for all `k, l ∈ ℤ`, then so are the generators of every
level `j`: `∫ g_{j,k}(x) conj g_{j,l}(x) dx = δ_{kl}`. The substitution `u = 2^j x`
(`Daubechies.integral_eq_two_pow_mul_integral_comp`) cancels the factor `2^j` of
`Daubechies.scaledFun_mul_conj`.

Daubechies.integral_prod_daubFun.name: Daubechies.integral_prod_daubFun
Daubechies.integral_prod_daubFun.docstring:
**The dyadic products integrate to the iterates of the transfer operator**: for every `n`,
`∫_{-2^n/2}^{2^n/2} ∏_{j<n} P(ξ/2^(j+1)) dξ = ∫_{-1/2}^{1/2} (T^n 1)(η) dη`. The substitution
`ξ = 2^n η` (Mathlib's `intervalIntegral.smul_integral_comp_mul_left`) turns the left side into
`2^n ∫_{-1/2}^{1/2} ∏_{j<n} P(2^n η/2^(j+1)) dη = 2^n ∫_{-1/2}^{1/2} ∏_{i<n} P(2^i η) dη`, which is
`Daubechies.integral_iterate_transferOp_one`.

Daubechies.integral_periodic_mul_normSq_.name: Daubechies.integral_periodic_mul_normSq_truncProduct
Daubechies.integral_periodic_mul_normSq_.docstring:
**The integral identity for the truncated products**: for every continuous `1`-periodic
`w : ℝ → ℂ` and every `n`, `∫ w(ξ) |Φ_n(ξ)|² dξ = ∫_0^1 w(ξ) dξ`. Induction on `n`, for all such
`w` at once. The case `n = 0` is `Daubechies.integral_mul_normSq_truncProduct_zero`. For the step,
the substitution `ξ = 2ζ` (`Daubechies.integral_mul_normSq_truncProduct_succ`) and the induction
hypothesis for the continuous `1`-periodic function `ζ ↦ w(2ζ) |m_0(ζ)|²`
(`Daubechies.periodic_comp_two_mul_mul_normSq_symbol`) give `2 ∫_0^1 w(2ζ) |m_0(ζ)|² dζ`, which
is `∫_0^1 w` (`Daubechies.two_mul_intervalIntegral_comp_two_mul_mul_normSq_symbol`).

Daubechies.integral_periodic_mul_normSq_.name: Daubechies.integral_periodic_mul_normSq_symbolProduct
Daubechies.integral_periodic_mul_normSq_.docstring:
**The integral identity for the symbol product**: for a mask of order `N ≥ 2` and every
continuous `1`-periodic `w : ℝ → ℂ`, `∫ w(ξ) |Φ(ξ)|² dξ = ∫_0^1 w(ξ) dξ`. The integrands
`w |Φ_n|²` converge pointwise to `w |Φ|²` (`Daubechies.tendsto_truncProduct`) and are bounded by
`(B/κ²) |Φ|²` (`Daubechies.norm_truncProduct_le`), where `B` bounds the continuous periodic
function `|w|` (Mathlib's `Function.Periodic.isBounded_of_continuous`) and `κ > 0` bounds `|Φ|`
from below on `[-1/2, 1/2]`; this bound is integrable
(`Daubechies.integrable_normSq_symbolProduct`). Dominated convergence (Mathlib's
`MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence`) and `∫ w |Φ_n|² = ∫_0^1 w` for every
`n` (`Daubechies.integral_periodic_mul_normSq_truncProduct`) give the identity.

Daubechies.integral_normSq_symbolProduct.name: Daubechies.integral_normSq_symbolProduct_mul_expFreq
Daubechies.integral_normSq_symbolProduct.docstring:
**The Fourier coefficients of `|Φ|²` at the integers**: for a mask of order `N ≥ 2` and every
`k ∈ ℤ`, `∫ |Φ(ξ)|² e^(-2πikξ) dξ` is `1` for `k = 0` and `0` otherwise. This is the integral
identity `Daubechies.integral_periodic_mul_normSq_symbolProduct` for `w(ξ) = e^(-2πikξ)`,
together with `∫_0^1 e^(-2πikξ) dξ = δ_(k0)` (`Daubechies.integral_expFreq_intCast_mul`).

Daubechies.integral_mul_normSq_truncProd.name: Daubechies.integral_mul_normSq_truncProduct_zero
Daubechies.integral_mul_normSq_truncProd.docstring:
**The integral identity for `n = 0`**: `∫ w(ξ) |Φ_0(ξ)|² dξ = ∫_0^1 w(ξ) dξ` for every
`1`-periodic `w : ℝ → ℂ`. Since `|Φ_0|² = 1_[-1/2, 1/2)`, the left side is `∫_(-1/2)^(1/2) w`,
and the integral of a `1`-periodic function is the same over every interval of length `1`
(Mathlib's `Function.Periodic.intervalIntegral_add_eq`).

Daubechies.integral_mul_normSq_truncProd.name: Daubechies.integral_mul_normSq_truncProduct_succ
Daubechies.integral_mul_normSq_truncProd.docstring:
**The substitution step**: for every `w : ℝ → ℂ` and every `n`,
`∫ w(ξ) |Φ_(n+1)(ξ)|² dξ = 2 ∫ w(2ζ) |m_0(ζ)|² |Φ_n(ζ)|² dζ`, by the recursion
`|Φ_(n+1)(ξ)|² = |m_0(ξ/2)|² |Φ_n(ξ/2)|²` (`Daubechies.normSq_truncProduct_succ`) and the
substitution `ξ = 2ζ` (`Daubechies.integral_comp_div_two`).

Daubechies.integral_mul_conj_daubechiesE.name: Daubechies.integral_mul_conj_daubechiesExpand
Daubechies.integral_mul_conj_daubechiesE.docstring:
**Coefficients against a finite expansion**: let `N ≥ 2`, let `f` be locally integrable and
let the coefficients `v : ℤ → ℂ` vanish outside a finite set `T`. Then for every level `j`,
`∫ f conj(∑_n v_n φ_{j,n}) = ∑_{n ∈ T} conj(v_n) ⟨f, φ_{j,n}⟩`: the expansion is a finite sum, and
the integral is linear on the integrable terms
(`Daubechies.integrable_mul_conj_daubechiesScaled`).

Daubechies.integral_iterate_transferOp.name: Daubechies.integral_iterate_transferOp
Daubechies.integral_iterate_transferOp.docstring:
**The adjoint identity for the iterates**: for continuous `1`-periodic `h` and `g` and every
`n`, `∫_{-1/2}^{1/2} h(η) (T^n g)(η) dη = 2^n ∫_{-1/2}^{1/2} h(2^n η) ∏_{i<n} P(2^i η) g(η) dη`.
Induction on `n`: `T^(n+1) g = T (T^n g)`, `Daubechies.integral_transferOp` for `T^n g`, and the
induction hypothesis for the continuous `1`-periodic function `η ↦ h(2η) P(η)` in place of
`h`.

Daubechies.integral_finsum_mul_conj_fins.name: Daubechies.integral_finsum_mul_conj_finsum
Daubechies.integral_finsum_mul_conj_fins.docstring:
**Orthonormality of the exponentials `e^(-2πikξ)` on `[0, 1]`**, for coefficient sequences
`a, b : ℤ → ℂ` with finite support:
`∫_0^1 (∑_k a_k e^(-2πikξ)) conj (∑_k b_k e^(-2πikξ)) dξ = ∑_k a_k conj b_k`.

Daubechies.integral_expFreq_mul_normSq_s.name: Daubechies.integral_expFreq_mul_normSq_symbol_add_half
Daubechies.integral_expFreq_mul_normSq_s.docstring:
**Fourier coefficients of `|m_0(· + 1/2)|²`**: for every `n ∈ ℤ`,
`∫_0^1 e^(-2πinξ) |m_0(ξ + 1/2)|² dξ = (1/4) e^(πin) ∑_k c_(k-n) c_k`. The substitution
`η = ξ + 1/2` (Mathlib's `intervalIntegral.integral_comp_add_right`) gives the factor
`e^(-2πin(-1/2)) = e^(πin)` and the integral over `[1/2, 3/2]`, which is the integral over
`[0, 1]` since `η ↦ e^(-2πinη) |m_0(η)|²` has period `1`
(`Daubechies.periodic_expFreq_intCast_mul`, `Daubechies.symbol_periodic`, Mathlib's
`Function.Periodic.intervalIntegral_add_eq`); then `Daubechies.integral_expFreq_mul_normSq_symbol`
applies.

Daubechies.integral_expFreq_mul_normSq_s.name: Daubechies.integral_expFreq_mul_normSq_symbol
Daubechies.integral_expFreq_mul_normSq_s.docstring:
**Fourier coefficients of `|m_0|²`**: for every `n ∈ ℤ`,
`∫_0^1 e^(-2πinξ) |m_0(ξ)|² dξ = (1/4) ∑_k c_(k-n) c_k`.

Daubechies.integral_expFreq_mul_normSq_f.name: Daubechies.integral_expFreq_mul_normSq_finsum
Daubechies.integral_expFreq_mul_normSq_f.docstring:
**Fourier coefficients of `|T|²`** for a trigonometric polynomial
`T(ξ) = ∑_k a_k e^(-2πikξ)` with finitely many nonzero `a_k ∈ ℂ`:
`∫_0^1 e^(-2πinξ) |T(ξ)|² dξ = ∑_k a_(k-n) conj a_k` for every `n ∈ ℤ`.

Daubechies.integral_expFreq_intCast_mul.name: Daubechies.integral_expFreq_intCast_mul
Daubechies.integral_expFreq_intCast_mul.docstring:
**Integrals of the exponentials over a period**: `∫_0^1 e^(-2πinξ) dξ` is `1` for `n = 0`
and `0` for every other integer `n`.

Daubechies.integral_eq_two_pow_mul_integ.name: Daubechies.integral_eq_two_pow_mul_integral_comp
Daubechies.integral_eq_two_pow_mul_integ.docstring:
**The dyadic substitution**: `∫ g(u) du = 2^j ∫ g(2^j y) dy` for every `g : ℝ → ℂ` and every
`j ∈ ℕ`, by the substitution `u = 2^j y` (Mathlib's
`MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_comp_mul_left`). Both sides are `0` when `g` is not integrable.

Daubechies.integral_daubechiesExpand_mul.name: Daubechies.integral_daubechiesExpand_mul_conj_daubechiesExpand
Daubechies.integral_daubechiesExpand_mul.docstring:
**Parseval's identity for a finite expansion**: for `N ≥ 2`, every level `j`, all coefficients
`u : ℤ → ℂ` and all coefficients `v` vanishing outside a finite set `T`,
`∫ (∑_n u_n φ_{j,n}) conj(∑_n v_n φ_{j,n}) = ∑_{n ∈ T} u_n conj(v_n)`, by
`Daubechies.integral_mul_conj_daubechiesExpand` and coefficient recovery
(`Daubechies.coeffFun_daubechiesExpand_scalingFun`).

Daubechies.integral_comp_div_two_add_com.name: Daubechies.integral_comp_div_two_add_comp_add_one_div_two
Daubechies.integral_comp_div_two_add_com.docstring:
**The two branches of halving**: for a continuous `1`-periodic `f`,
`∫_{-1/2}^{1/2} (f(η/2) + f((η + 1)/2)) dη = 2 ∫_{-1/2}^{1/2} f(η) dη`. The substitutions
`u = η/2` and `u = (η + 1)/2` (Mathlib's `intervalIntegral.integral_comp_div` and
`intervalIntegral.integral_comp_div_add`) turn the two summands into `2 ∫_{-1/4}^{1/4} f` and
`2 ∫_{1/4}^{3/4} f`. Together they give `2 ∫_{-1/4}^{3/4} f`, and the integral of a `1`-periodic
function is the same over every interval of length `1`
(`Function.Periodic.intervalIntegral_add_eq`).

Daubechies.integral_comp_div_two.name: Daubechies.integral_comp_div_two
Daubechies.integral_comp_div_two.docstring:
**The doubling substitution on the line**: `∫ F(ξ/2) dξ = 2 ∫ F(ζ) dζ` for every
`F : ℝ → ℂ`, by the substitution `ξ = 2ζ` (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_comp_div`).
The identity holds for every `F`, integrable or not: Lean assigns the value `0` to the integral
of a non-integrable function, on both sides.

Daubechies.integral_cascade_mul_eq_zero.name: Daubechies.integral_cascade_mul_eq_zero
Daubechies.integral_cascade_mul_eq_zero.docstring:
`∫ η_n g = 0` for every `n` and every function `g : ℝ → ℂ` that vanishes on `[0, 2N - 1]`:
the product `η_n g` vanishes everywhere (`Daubechies.cascade_eq_zero`).

Daubechies.integral_annulus_normSq_le.name: Daubechies.integral_annulus_normSq_le
Daubechies.integral_annulus_normSq_le.docstring:
**The integral of `|Φ|²` over an annulus**: under a growth bound `T^n 1 ≤ C λ^n`,
`∫_{A_n} |Φ(ξ)|² dξ ≤ exp(C(2N - 1, N) π²/12) (4/(π 2^n))^(2N) C λ^n` for every `n ∈ ℕ`. The
pointwise bound `Daubechies.normSq_symbolProduct_le_of_mem_annulus` leaves the integral of
`∏_{j<n} P(ξ/2^(j+1))` over `A_n ⊆ [-2^n/2, 2^n/2]`, which is at most `C λ^n`
(`Daubechies.TransferGrowth.setIntegral_prod_daubFun_le`).

Daubechies.integrable_symbolProduct_of_g.name: Daubechies.integrable_symbolProduct_of_growth
Daubechies.integrable_symbolProduct_of_g.docstring:
**The symbol product is integrable under a growth bound**: if `T^n 1 ≤ C λ^n`
(`Daubechies.TransferGrowth`) and `N - log₄ λ - 1/2 > 0`, then `Φ` is integrable. This is the case
`a = 0` of the weighted bound `Daubechies.integrable_rpow_mul_norm`.

Daubechies.integrable_symbolProduct.name: Daubechies.integrable_symbolProduct
Daubechies.integrable_symbolProduct.docstring:
**The symbol product is integrable** for every Daubechies mask of order `N ≥ 2`: the crude
growth bound `T^n 1 ≤ (2 C(2N - 1, N))^n` (`Daubechies.transferGrowth_crude`) satisfies
`log₄(2 C(2N - 1, N)) < N - 1/2` (`Daubechies.logb_four_two_mul_choose_lt`), so
`Daubechies.integrable_symbolProduct_of_growth` applies.

Daubechies.integrable_scalingFun.name: Daubechies.integrable_scalingFun
Daubechies.integrable_scalingFun.docstring:
**The scaling function is integrable**, for `N ≥ 2`: it is continuous with compact support
(Mathlib's `Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport`).

Daubechies.integrable_scaledFun_mul_conj.name: Daubechies.integrable_scaledFun_mul_conj
Daubechies.integrable_scaledFun_mul_conj.docstring:
If `g` is continuous and vanishes outside `[a, b]`, then `y ↦ g_{j,l}(y) conj g_{j,k}(y)` is
integrable: it is continuous with compact support.

Daubechies.integrable_rpow_mul_normSq.name: Daubechies.integrable_rpow_mul_normSq
Daubechies.integrable_rpow_mul_normSq.docstring:
**The weighted `L²` bound on the symbol product**: under a growth bound `T^n 1 ≤ C λ^n`, the
function `ξ ↦ (1 + |ξ|)^(2s) |Φ(ξ)|²` is integrable for every real `s < N - log₄ λ`. On the
annulus `A_n` the weight is at most `4^|2s| 2^(2sn)`
(`Daubechies.one_add_abs_rpow_le_of_mem_annulus`) and
`∫_{A_n} |Φ|² ≤ exp(C(2N - 1, N) π²/12) (4/π)^(2N) C (λ/4^N)^n`
(`Daubechies.integral_annulus_normSq_le`), so the integrals over the annuli decay geometrically
with ratio `2^(2s) λ/4^N < 1` (`Daubechies.two_rpow_two_mul_mul_lt`,
`Daubechies.integrable_of_integral_annulus_le`).

Daubechies.integrable_rpow_mul_norm.name: Daubechies.integrable_rpow_mul_norm
Daubechies.integrable_rpow_mul_norm.docstring:
**The weighted `L¹` bound on the symbol product**: under a growth bound `T^n 1 ≤ C λ^n`, the
function `ξ ↦ (1 + |ξ|)^a |Φ(ξ)|` is integrable for every real `a < N - log₄ λ - 1/2`. Choose `b`
with `a + 1/2 < b < N - log₄ λ`; then
`(1 + |ξ|)^a |Φ(ξ)| ≤ (1 + |ξ|)^(-2(b - a)) + (1 + |ξ|)^(2b) |Φ(ξ)|²`
(`Daubechies.rpow_mul_le_rpow_add_rpow_mul_sq`), where the first summand is integrable since
`2(b - a) > 1` (Mathlib's `integrable_one_add_norm`) and the second by
`Daubechies.integrable_rpow_mul_normSq`.

Daubechies.integrable_pow_smul_scalingFu.name: Daubechies.integrable_pow_smul_scalingFun
Daubechies.integrable_pow_smul_scalingFu.docstring:
For `N ≥ 2` and every `n ∈ ℕ` the moment function `x ↦ x^n φ(x)` is integrable: it is
continuous with compact support. It is written with the real scalar multiplication
`x^n • φ(x)`, the form of the hypothesis of Mathlib's `Real.iteratedDeriv_fourier`.

Daubechies.integrable_of_integral_annulu.name: Daubechies.integrable_of_integral_annulus_le
Daubechies.integrable_of_integral_annulu.docstring:
**Integrability from geometric decay on the annuli**: a continuous `f : ℝ → E` with
`∫_{A_n} ‖f‖ ≤ M r^n` for every `n`, where `0 ≤ r < 1`, is integrable on `ℝ`. On `[-1/4, 1/4]` it
is integrable as a continuous function on a compact interval, on `⋃_n A_n` because the integrals
over the annuli are summable (Mathlib's `integrableOn_iUnion_of_summable_integral_norm`), and
these two sets cover `ℝ`.

Daubechies.integrable_norm_pow_mul_norm_.name: Daubechies.integrable_norm_pow_mul_norm_scalingFun
Daubechies.integrable_norm_pow_mul_norm_.docstring:
For `N ≥ 2` and every `n ∈ ℕ` the function `x ↦ |x|^n |φ(x)|` is integrable: it is
continuous and vanishes outside `[0, 2N - 1]` (`Daubechies.hasCompactSupport_scalingFun`).

Daubechies.integrable_normSq_symbolProdu.name: Daubechies.integrable_normSq_symbolProduct
Daubechies.integrable_normSq_symbolProdu.docstring:
**`|Φ|²` is integrable** for every mask of order `N ≥ 2`, since `Φ ∈ L²`
(`Daubechies.memLp_symbolProduct_two`).

Daubechies.integrable_mul_conj_daubechie.name: Daubechies.integrable_mul_conj_daubechiesScaled
Daubechies.integrable_mul_conj_daubechie.docstring:
**The coefficient integrands of locally integrable functions are integrable**: for `N ≥ 2`
and locally integrable `f`, the function `y ↦ f(y) conj φ_{j,k}(y)` is integrable, since
`φ_{j,k}` is continuous with compact support (Mathlib's
`MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrable.integrable_smul_right_of_hasCompactSupport`).

Daubechies.integrable_fourier_symbolProd.name: Daubechies.integrable_fourier_symbolProduct
Daubechies.integrable_fourier_symbolProd.docstring:
For `N ≥ 2` the Fourier transform `𝓕 Φ` of the symbol product is integrable:
`𝓕 Φ(ξ) = φ(-ξ)` (`Daubechies.fourier_symbolProduct_apply`), and `φ` is integrable.

Daubechies.integrable_expFreq_mul.name: Daubechies.integrable_expFreq_mul
Daubechies.integrable_expFreq_mul.docstring:
An integrable `f : ℝ → ℂ` stays integrable after multiplication by `e^(-2πiaξ)`, a continuous
function of modulus `1` (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Integrable.bdd_mul`).

Daubechies.integrable_const_mul_comp_two.name: Daubechies.integrable_const_mul_comp_two_mul_sub
Daubechies.integrable_const_mul_comp_two.docstring:
If `f : ℝ → ℂ` is integrable, then so is `x ↦ c f(2x - b)`, for all `c ∈ ℂ` and `b ∈ ℝ`
(Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Integrable.comp_sub_right` and
`MeasureTheory.Integrable.comp_mul_left'`).

Daubechies.integrable_conj_daubechiesSca.name: Daubechies.integrable_conj_daubechiesScaled
Daubechies.integrable_conj_daubechiesSca.docstring: `conj φ_{j,k}` is integrable for `N ≥ 2`: it is continuous with compact support.

Daubechies.integrable_cascade.name: Daubechies.integrable_cascade
Daubechies.integrable_cascade.docstring:
**The cascade functions are integrable**, by induction on `n`: `1_[0,1)` is integrable, and
`η_(n+1)` is a finite sum of the integrable functions `x ↦ c_k η_n(2x - k)`.

Daubechies.iUnion_Ico_div_two_pow.name: Daubechies.iUnion_Ico_div_two_pow
Daubechies.iUnion_Ico_div_two_pow.docstring:
**The dyadic cells of level `j` cover the line**: every `x ∈ ℝ` lies in the cell
`[k/2^j, (k + 1)/2^j)` with `k = ⌊2^j x⌋`.

Daubechies.higherDiff_scalingFun_eq_zero.name: Daubechies.higherDiff_scalingFun_eq_zero
Daubechies.higherDiff_scalingFun_eq_zero.docstring:
**The support of the differences of the scaling function**: for `N ≥ 2`, `r ∈ ℕ` and a step
`|h| ≤ 1`, `Δ_h^r φ(x) = 0` for every `x ∉ [-r, 2N - 1 + r]`. The scaling function vanishes
outside `[0, 2N - 1]` (`Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_zero`), so `Δ_h^r φ` vanishes outside
`[-r|h|, 2N - 1 + r|h|] ⊆ [-r, 2N - 1 + r]` (`Daubechies.iterate_fwdDiff_eq_zero_of_notMem`).

Daubechies.hasSum_sq_div_two_pow.name: Daubechies.hasSum_sq_div_two_pow
Daubechies.hasSum_sq_div_two_pow.docstring:
**The geometric series of the squared dyadic scalings**:
`∑_{j ≥ 0} (x/2^(j+1))² = x² ∑_{j ≥ 0} 4^(-(j+1)) = x²/3`.

Daubechies.hasProd_cos_div_two_pow.name: Daubechies.hasProd_cos_div_two_pow
Daubechies.hasProd_cos_div_two_pow.docstring:
**The cosine product as a `HasProd`**: `∏_{j ≥ 0} cos(x/2^(j+1)) = sinc(x)`. The partial
products `p_n` satisfy `sinc(x/2^n) p_n = sinc(x)`
(`Daubechies.sinc_div_two_pow_mul_prod_cos`); since `sinc(x/2^n) → sinc(0) = 1` and `p_n`
converges, the limit of `p_n` is `sinc(x)`.

Daubechies.hasProdUniformlyOn_symbolProd.name: Daubechies.hasProdUniformlyOn_symbolProduct
Daubechies.hasProdUniformlyOn_symbolProd.docstring:
**Uniform convergence on compact sets**: on every compact set `K ⊆ ℝ`, say `K ⊆ [-R, R]`, the
symbol product converges uniformly, since there `|m_0(ξ/2^(j+1)) - 1| ≤ (CR/2)/2^j` (Mathlib's
`Summable.hasProdUniformlyOn_nat_one_add`).

Daubechies.hasProdLocallyUniformly_symbo.name: Daubechies.hasProdLocallyUniformly_symbolProduct
Daubechies.hasProdLocallyUniformly_symbo.docstring:
**Locally uniform convergence**: the products `∏_{j ∈ s} m_0(ξ/2^(j+1))` over finite sets
`s ⊆ ℕ` converge to `Φ(ξ)` as `s` grows, locally uniformly in `ξ ∈ ℝ`: uniformly on every compact
set (`Daubechies.hasProdUniformlyOn_symbolProduct`, Mathlib's
`hasProdLocallyUniformly_of_forall_compact`).

Daubechies.hasCompactSupport_wavelet.name: Daubechies.hasCompactSupport_wavelet
Daubechies.hasCompactSupport_wavelet.docstring:
**The wavelet has compact support**, for `N ≥ 2`: it vanishes outside `[1 - N, N]`
(`Daubechies.wavelet_eq_zero`).

Daubechies.hasCompactSupport_scalingFun.name: Daubechies.hasCompactSupport_scalingFun
Daubechies.hasCompactSupport_scalingFun.docstring:
**The scaling function has compact support**, for `N ≥ 2`: it vanishes outside the compact
interval `[0, 2N - 1]` (`Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_zero`).

Daubechies.hasCompactSupport_scaledFun.name: Daubechies.hasCompactSupport_scaledFun
Daubechies.hasCompactSupport_scaledFun.docstring:
**`g_{j,k}` has compact support** if `g` vanishes outside `[a, b]`: it vanishes outside the
compact support window (`Daubechies.scaledFun_eq_zero`).

Daubechies.fwdDiff_scaledFun.name: Daubechies.fwdDiff_scaledFun
Daubechies.fwdDiff_scaledFun.docstring:
**Differences commute with dilation and translation**: for every `g : ℝ → ℂ`, level `j`,
position `k` and step `h`, `Δ_h g_{j,k} = (Δ_{2^j h} g)_{j,k}`, that is
`g_{j,k}(x + h) - g_{j,k}(x) = 2^(j/2) (g(2^j x - k + 2^j h) - g(2^j x - k))`, since
`2^j (x + h) - k = (2^j x - k) + 2^j h`.

Daubechies.fwdDiff_daubechiesExpand.name: Daubechies.fwdDiff_daubechiesExpand
Daubechies.fwdDiff_daubechiesExpand.docstring:
**A difference of an expansion**: if `g` vanishes outside `[a, b]`, then for every level `j`,
all coefficients `c : ℤ → ℂ` and every step `h`,
`Δ_h (∑_k c_k g_{j,k}) = ∑_k c_k (Δ_{2^j h} g)_{j,k}` at every point. At each point only finitely
many terms are nonzero (`Daubechies.summable_expand`), so the difference may be taken termwise
(`Daubechies.fwdDiff_scaledFun`).

Daubechies.fourier_symbolProduct_apply.name: Daubechies.fourier_symbolProduct_apply
Daubechies.fourier_symbolProduct_apply.docstring:
`𝓕 Φ(ξ) = φ(-ξ)` for every `ξ ∈ ℝ`, since `𝓕⁻ Φ(x) = 𝓕 Φ(-x)` (Mathlib's
`Real.fourierInv_eq_fourier_neg`).

Daubechies.fourier_scalingFun.name: Daubechies.fourier_scalingFun
Daubechies.fourier_scalingFun.docstring:
**The Fourier transform of the scaling function is the symbol product**: `𝓕 φ = Φ` for
`N ≥ 2`. The function `Φ` is continuous and integrable, and so is `𝓕 Φ`
(`Daubechies.integrable_fourier_symbolProduct`), so the inversion theorem `𝓕 (𝓕⁻ Φ) = Φ` applies
(Mathlib's `Continuous.fourier_fourierInv_eq`).

Daubechies.fourier_pow_mul_scalingFun_in.name: Daubechies.fourier_pow_mul_scalingFun_int
Daubechies.fourier_pow_mul_scalingFun_in.docstring:
**The Fourier transforms of the moments vanish at the nonzero integers**: for `N ≥ 2`,
`l < N` and every integer `j ≠ 0`, `𝓕[x^l φ](j) = 0`, since
`(-2πi)^l 𝓕[x^l φ](j) = Φ^(l)(j) = 0` (`Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_eq_fourier`,
`Daubechies.iteratedDeriv_symbolProduct_int`).

Daubechies.fourier_cascade_succ.name: Daubechies.fourier_cascade_succ
Daubechies.fourier_cascade_succ.docstring:
**The cascade recursion on the Fourier side**: `𝓕 η_(n+1)(ξ) = m_0(ξ/2) 𝓕 η_n(ξ/2)` for
every `ξ ∈ ℝ`. The transform of `x ↦ η_n(2x - k)` is `(1/2) e^(-2πik(ξ/2)) 𝓕 η_n(ξ/2)`
(`Real.fourier_comp_mul_sub_apply`), and `(1/2) ∑_k c_k e^(-2πik(ξ/2)) = m_0(ξ/2)`
(`Daubechies.symbol_eq_sum`).

Daubechies.fourier_cascade.name: Daubechies.fourier_cascade
Daubechies.fourier_cascade.docstring:
**The Fourier transform of the cascade**:
`𝓕 η_n(ξ) = ∏_{j<n} m_0(ξ/2^(j+1)) · 𝓕 η_0(ξ/2^n)` for every `n` and every `ξ ∈ ℝ`, by induction
with `Daubechies.fourier_cascade_succ` and the splitting of the first factor of the product
(`Daubechies.prod_range_succ_symbol`).

Daubechies.fourierInv_expFreq_mul_apply.name: Daubechies.fourierInv_expFreq_mul_apply
Daubechies.fourierInv_expFreq_mul_apply.docstring:
**Modulation by `e^(-2πiaξ)` is translation by `a`** for the inverse Fourier transform:
`𝓕⁻[ξ ↦ e^(-2πiaξ) f(ξ)](x) = 𝓕⁻ f(x - a)` for every `f : ℝ → ℂ` and all real `a`, `x`
(`Real.fourierInv_exp_mul_apply` with `b = -a`).

Daubechies.finsum_two_mul_add_finsum_two.name: Daubechies.finsum_two_mul_add_finsum_two_mul_add_one
Daubechies.finsum_two_mul_add_finsum_two.docstring:
**Splitting a sum over `ℤ` by parity**: `∑_i g(2i) + ∑_i g(2i + 1) = ∑_k g(k)` for every
function `g` with finite support.

Daubechies.finsum_two_mul_add_add_two_mu.name: Daubechies.finsum_two_mul_add_add_two_mul
Daubechies.finsum_two_mul_add_add_two_mu.docstring:
The sum `∑_i g(2i + r)` over one parity class depends only on the parity of `r`:
`∑_i g(2i + r + 2q) = ∑_i g(2i + r)` for all `r, q ∈ ℤ`.

Daubechies.finsum_two_mul_add_add_finsum.name: Daubechies.finsum_two_mul_add_add_finsum
Daubechies.finsum_two_mul_add_add_finsum.docstring:
Splitting a sum over `ℤ` by parity, shifted by `r ∈ ℤ`:
`∑_i g(2i + r) + ∑_i g(2i + r + 1) = ∑_k g(k)` for every function `g` with finite support.

Daubechies.finsum_mul_sub_two_mul.name: Daubechies.finsum_mul_sub_two_mul
Daubechies.finsum_mul_sub_two_mul.docstring:
**Reindexing a sum of products of shifted sequences**: for all `h, h' : ℤ → ℝ` and
`k, l ∈ ℤ`, `∑_n h_{n-2k} h'_{n-2l} = ∑_a h_a h'_{a+2(k-l)}`, by the substitution `n = a + 2k`.

Daubechies.finsum_eq_sum_range_of_eq_zer.name: Daubechies.finsum_eq_sum_range_of_eq_zero
Daubechies.finsum_eq_sum_range_of_eq_zer.docstring:
A sum over `k ∈ ℤ` of a function that vanishes outside `0 ≤ k < n` is the finite sum over
`k = 0, …, n - 1`.

Daubechies.finsum_eq_sum_range_of_daubec.name: Daubechies.finsum_eq_sum_range_of_daubechiesCoeff
Daubechies.finsum_eq_sum_range_of_daubec.docstring:
A sum over `k ∈ ℤ` of a function that vanishes wherever the filter coefficients vanish is the
finite sum over `k = 0, …, 2N - 1`.

Daubechies.finsum_dualCoeff_sub_two_mul_.name: Daubechies.finsum_dualCoeff_sub_two_mul_mul
Daubechies.finsum_dualCoeff_sub_two_mul_.docstring:
Reindexing a sum of products of dual filter coefficients over one parity class:
`∑_j g_(a-2j) g_(b-2j) = (-1)^(a+b) ∑_i c_(2i+(1-a)+(a-b)) c_(2i+(1-a))`.

Daubechies.finsum_daubechiesCoeff_sub_tw.name: Daubechies.finsum_daubechiesCoeff_sub_two_mul_mul
Daubechies.finsum_daubechiesCoeff_sub_tw.docstring:
Reindexing a sum of products of filter coefficients over one parity class:
`∑_j c_(a-2j) c_(b-2j) = ∑_i c_(2i+b+(a-b)) c_(2i+b)`.

Daubechies.finite_support_dualCoeff.name: Daubechies.finite_support_dualCoeff
Daubechies.finite_support_dualCoeff.docstring: The dual filter has finite support.

Daubechies.finite_support_daubechiesCoef.name: Daubechies.finite_support_daubechiesCoeff
Daubechies.finite_support_daubechiesCoef.docstring: The filter coefficients have finite support: they vanish outside `0 ≤ k < 2N`.

Daubechies.expandConst_ne_top.name: Daubechies.expandConst_ne_top
Daubechies.expandConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant `expandConst g a b p` is finite for every `g ∈ L_p`.

Daubechies.expandConst.name: Daubechies.expandConst
Daubechies.expandConst.docstring:
**The constant of the upper estimate** `Daubechies.eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand_le`:
`M^(1 - 1/p) ‖g‖_p` with the overlap number `M = ⌈b - a⌉ + 1`, which bounds the number of
generators of one level that are nonzero at a point. It is the same for every level.

Daubechies.expFreq_mul_eq_exp.name: Daubechies.expFreq_mul_eq_exp
Daubechies.expFreq_mul_eq_exp.docstring:
`e^(-2πiaξ) = exp(2π(-a)ξ i)`, the form of the exponential in the modulation rule
`Real.fourierInv_exp_mul_apply`.

Daubechies.expFreq_eq_exp_mul.name: Daubechies.expFreq_eq_exp_mul
Daubechies.expFreq_eq_exp_mul.docstring:
`e^(-2πiξ) = exp(cξ)` with the complex constant `c = -2πi`, the form in which `ξ` enters
linearly into the exponent.

Daubechies.expFreq.name: Daubechies.expFreq
Daubechies.expFreq.docstring:
**The point `e^(-2πiξ)` of the unit circle.** The symbol of a mask is its mask polynomial
evaluated at `z = e^(-2πiξ)`; the sign of the exponent is the one of Mathlib's Fourier transform
`𝓕 f(ξ) = ∫ e^(-2πixξ) f(x) dx`.

Daubechies.exists_pos_le_norm_symbolProd.name: Daubechies.exists_pos_le_norm_symbolProduct
Daubechies.exists_pos_le_norm_symbolProd.docstring:
**`|Φ|` is bounded below on `[-1/2, 1/2]`**: there is `κ > 0` with `κ ≤ |Φ(ξ)|` for all
`|ξ| ≤ 1/2`, namely the minimum of the continuous function `|Φ|` on the compact interval, which is
positive since `Φ` has no zeros there.

Daubechies.exists_poly_sum_pow_mul.name: Daubechies.exists_poly_sum_pow_mul
Daubechies.exists_poly_sum_pow_mul.docstring:
**The integer moments of the translates are polynomials**: for `N ≥ 2` and `l < N` there is
a polynomial `Q` of degree `≤ l` with coefficient `1` at `X^l` (so `Q` is monic of degree `l`)
such that `∑_{k ∈ ℤ} k^l φ(x - k) = Q(x)` for every `x ∈ ℝ`. The polynomial is
`Q = ∑_{i=0}^{l} C(l, i) (-1)^(l-i) μ_(l-i) X^i` with the moments `μ_r = ∫ y^r φ(y) dy`
(`Daubechies.tsum_intCast_pow_mul_scalingFun_sub`); its coefficient at `X^l` is
`μ_0 = ∫ φ = 1` (`Daubechies.integral_scalingFun`).

Daubechies.exists_poly_comp_two_pow_mul.name: Daubechies.exists_poly_comp_two_pow_mul
Daubechies.exists_poly_comp_two_pow_mul.docstring:
**Dilating a polynomial**: for every polynomial `Q` of degree `< N` and every `j ∈ ℕ` there is
a polynomial `R` of degree `< N` with `R(2^j y) = Q(y)` for every `y ∈ ℝ`, namely
`R(u) = Q(2^(-j) u)` (`Interval.comp_affine_mem_degreeLT`).

Daubechies.exists_mem_annulus.name: Daubechies.exists_mem_annulus
Daubechies.exists_mem_annulus.docstring:
**The annuli cover `{|ξ| > 1/4}`**: for `|ξ| > 1/4` the least `n` with `|ξ| ≤ 2^n/2`
satisfies `2^n/4 < |ξ|` (for `n = 0` by hypothesis, for `n ≥ 1` by minimality), so `ξ ∈ A_n`.

Daubechies.exists_div_two_pow_lt.name: Daubechies.exists_div_two_pow_lt
Daubechies.exists_div_two_pow_lt.docstring:
**Dyadic scales become small**: for every `c ∈ ℝ` and `δ > 0` there is a level `J` with
`c/2^J < δ`.

Daubechies.exists_coeff_poly_of_mem_degr.name: Daubechies.exists_coeff_poly_of_mem_degreeLT
Daubechies.exists_coeff_poly_of_mem_degr.docstring:
**Polynomials of degree `< n` as combinations of the translates, with polynomial
coefficients**: for `N ≥ 2`, `n ≤ N` and every polynomial `Q` of degree `< n` there is a
polynomial `a` of degree `< n` with `Q(x) = ∑_{k ∈ ℤ} a(k) φ(x - k)` for every `x ∈ ℝ`. Induction
on `n`. For `n = 0` the polynomial `Q` is zero. For the step, let `q_n` be the coefficient of
`X^n` in `Q` and let `P` be the monic polynomial of degree `n` with
`P(x) = ∑_k k^n φ(x - k)` (`Daubechies.exists_poly_sum_pow_mul`, since `n < N`). The polynomial
`Q - q_n P` has degree `< n` (`Daubechies.sub_C_coeff_mul_mem_degreeLT`), so by induction it is
`∑_k a'(k) φ(x - k)` with `a'` of degree `< n`, and `a = q_n X^n + a'` represents `Q`.

Daubechies.exists_coeff_poly.name: Daubechies.exists_coeff_poly
Daubechies.exists_coeff_poly.docstring:
**Every polynomial of degree `< N` is a combination of the integer translates of `φ` with
polynomial coefficients**: for `N ≥ 2` and every polynomial `Q` of degree `< N` there is a
polynomial `a` with `Q(x) = ∑_{k ∈ ℤ} a(k) φ(x - k)` for every `x ∈ ℝ`
(`Daubechies.exists_coeff_poly_of_mem_degreeLT` with `n = N`, which also gives `a` of
degree `< N`). For each `x` the sum has only finitely many nonzero terms.

Daubechies.eventually_mem_Ico_two_pow.name: Daubechies.eventually_mem_Ico_two_pow
Daubechies.eventually_mem_Ico_two_pow.docstring:
Every `ξ ∈ ℝ` lies in the cut-off interval `[-2^n/2, 2^n/2)` for all sufficiently large `n`,
since `2^n → ∞`.

Daubechies.eval_one_daubPoly.name: Daubechies.eval_one_daubPoly
Daubechies.eval_one_daubPoly.docstring:
**The value at `1`**: `P_N(1) = ∑_{k < N} C(N - 1 + k, k) = C(2N - 1, N)` for `N ≥ 1`, by the
symmetry `C(N - 1 + k, k) = C(N - 1 + k, N - 1)` (Mathlib's `Nat.choose_symm_add`) and the
hockey-stick identity `∑_{i ≤ n} C(i + m, m) = C(n + m + 1, m + 1)` (`Nat.sum_range_add_choose`).

Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_succ_eq_one_add.name: Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_succ_eq_one_add
Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_succ_eq_one_add.docstring:
The constant term of `P_{M+1}` is `1`:
`P_{M+1}(y) = 1 + ∑_{k < M} C(M + k + 1, k + 1) y^(k+1)`.

Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_nonneg.name: Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_nonneg
Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_nonneg.docstring: `P_N(y) ≥ 0` for `y ≥ 0`: all coefficients of `P_N` are nonnegative.

Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_le_eval_one.name: Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_le_eval_one
Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_le_eval_one.docstring: On `[0, 1]` the polynomial `P_N` is bounded by its value at `1`, since `y^k ≤ 1` there.

Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_le.name: Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_le
Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_le.docstring:
`P_N(y) ≤ 1 + C(2N - 1, N) y` for `0 ≤ y ≤ 1` and every `N`: the constant term is `1`, the
other terms satisfy `y^k ≤ y`, and their coefficients add up to `P_N(1) - 1 = C(2N - 1, N) - 1`
(for `N = 0` the left side is `0`).

Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_bezout_succ.name: Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_bezout_succ
Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_bezout_succ.docstring:
**The induction step of the Bézout identity**: for `N ≥ 1` the Bézout sum
`(1 - y)^N P_N(y) + y^N P_N(1 - y)` takes the same value at `N + 1` as at `N`. By the recurrence
the first summand changes by `y^N (1 - y)^N (C(2N - 1, N) - C(2N, N) y)` and the second by
`y^N (1 - y)^N (C(2N - 1, N) - C(2N, N) (1 - y))`; the changes add up to
`y^N (1 - y)^N (2 C(2N - 1, N) - C(2N, N)) = 0`.

Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_bezout.name: Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_bezout
Daubechies.eval_daubPoly_bezout.docstring:
**The Bézout identity of the Daubechies polynomials**, evaluated:
`(1 - y)^N P_N(y) + y^N P_N(1 - y) = 1` for `N ≥ 1` and every real `y`, by induction from
`P_1 = 1`, where it reads `(1 - y) + y = 1`.

Daubechies.eval_daubPoly.name: Daubechies.eval_daubPoly
Daubechies.eval_daubPoly.docstring: The value of `P_N` at a real number `y`: `P_N(y) = ∑_{k < N} C(N - 1 + k, k) y^k`.

Daubechies.enorm_sub_daubechiesProj_le_o.name: Daubechies.enorm_sub_daubechiesProj_le_of_continuous
Daubechies.enorm_sub_daubechiesProj_le_o.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality for a continuous representative**: for `N ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, every
`f ∈ L_p(ℝ)` that agrees almost everywhere with a continuous function `g`, and every level `j`,
`‖f - P_j f‖_p ≤ C_J ω_N(f, 2^(-j))_p` with `C_J = daubechiesJacksonConst m p`
(`Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le_smoothnessModulus` for `g`; both sides depend only on the class
of `f`, `Daubechies.projFun_congr_ae` and `Rd.smoothnessModulus_congr_ae`).

Daubechies.enorm_projFun_sub_le.name: Daubechies.enorm_projFun_sub_le
Daubechies.enorm_projFun_sub_le.docstring:
**A pointwise bound for `P_j f - f`**: let `N ≥ 2`, let `f` be locally integrable, let
`‖φ(t)‖ ≤ C` for all `t`, and let `η` bound `‖f(y) - f(x)‖` for all `y` with
`|y - x| ≤ (2N - 1)/2^j`. Then `‖P_j f(x) - f(x)‖ ≤ 2N C ‖φ‖_1 η`. The kernel form
(`Daubechies.projFun_sub_eq_tsum`) has at most `2N` nonzero terms at `x`
(`Daubechies.card_Icc_ceil_floor_le_two_mul`), each bounded by
`Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesScaled_mul_integral_sub_le`.

Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesScaled_mul_in.name: Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesScaled_mul_integral_sub_le
Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesScaled_mul_in.docstring:
**A local bound for one kernel term**: let `N ≥ 2`, `‖φ(t)‖ ≤ C` for all `t`, and let `η`
bound `‖f(y) - f(x)‖` for all `y` with `|y - x| ≤ (2N - 1)/2^j`. Then
`‖φ_{j,k}(x) ∫ (f(y) - f(x)) conj φ_{j,k}(y) dy‖ ≤ C ‖φ‖_1 η` for every position `k`. The term
vanishes unless `x` lies in the support window of `φ_{j,k}`; then every `y` of that window has
`|y - x| ≤ (2N - 1)/2^j` (`Daubechies.abs_sub_le_of_mem_supportWindow`), so the integral is at
most `η ‖φ_{j,k}‖_1 = η 2^(-j/2) ‖φ‖_1` (`Daubechies.eLpNorm_scaledFun`), while
`‖φ_{j,k}(x)‖ ≤ 2^(j/2) C` (`Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesScaled_le`).

Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesScaled_le.name: Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesScaled_le
Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesScaled_le.docstring:
**A pointwise bound of `φ_{j,k}`**: if `‖φ(t)‖ ≤ C` for every `t`, then
`‖φ_{j,k}(x)‖ ≤ 2^(j/2) C` for every level `j`, position `k` and point `x`.

Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesProj_zero_equ.name: Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesProj_zero_equiv
Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesProj_zero_equ.docstring:
**The norm of the projection of level `0` through the scaling coefficients**: for `N ≥ 2` and
`1 ≤ p < ∞` there are constants `K, M < ∞` with `‖(⟨f, φ_{0,k}⟩)_k‖_{ℓ_p} ≤ K ‖P_0 f‖_p` and
`‖P_0 f‖_p ≤ M ‖(⟨f, φ_{0,k}⟩)_k‖_{ℓ_p}` for every `f ∈ L_p`, where `φ_{0,k} = φ(· - k)`: the level
`j = 0` of `Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesProj_equiv`.

Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesProj_succ_sub.name: Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesProj_succ_sub_daubechiesProj
Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesProj_succ_sub.docstring:
**The norm of a block**: `‖P_{j+1} f - P_j f‖_p = ‖∑_k ⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩ ψ_{j,k}‖_p` for every
`f ∈ L_p` and every level `j` (`Daubechies.daubechiesProj_succ_sub_daubechiesProj`).

Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesProj_equiv.name: Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesProj_equiv
Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesProj_equiv.docstring:
**The norms of the projections through the scaling coefficients**: for `N ≥ 2` and
`1 ≤ p < ∞` there are constants `K, M < ∞` such that for every `f ∈ L_p` and every level `j`
`2^(j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖(⟨f, φ_{j,k}⟩)_k‖_{ℓ_p} ≤ K ‖P_j f‖_p` and
`‖P_j f‖_p ≤ M 2^(j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖(⟨f, φ_{j,k}⟩)_k‖_{ℓ_p}`, by the stability of the expansions
(`Daubechies.lqNorm_le_eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand`, `Daubechies.eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand_le`) for
`g = φ`.

Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesProj_eq.name: Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesProj_eq
Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesProj_eq.docstring:
**The norm of a projection**: `‖P_j f‖_p = ‖∑_k ⟨f, φ_{j,k}⟩ φ_{j,k}‖_p` for every
`f ∈ L_p` and every level `j` (`Daubechies.daubechiesProj_apply_ae`).

Daubechies.enorm_coeffFun_le.name: Daubechies.enorm_coeffFun_le
Daubechies.enorm_coeffFun_le.docstring:
**A single coefficient**: under the hypotheses of `Daubechies.eLpNorm_mul_conj_scaledFun_le`,
`|⟨f, g_{j,k}⟩| ≤ ‖1_W f‖_p ‖g_{j,k}‖_{p'}` with the support window
`W = {x : 2^j x - k ∈ [a, b]}`, since `|∫ h| ≤ ‖h‖_1`.

Daubechies.enorm_block_equiv.name: Daubechies.enorm_block_equiv
Daubechies.enorm_block_equiv.docstring:
**The norms of the blocks through the wavelet coefficients**: for `N ≥ 2` and `1 ≤ p < ∞`
there are constants `K, M < ∞` such that for every `f ∈ L_p` and every level `j`
`2^(j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖(⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩)_k‖_{ℓ_p} ≤ K ‖P_{j+1} f - P_j f‖_p` and
`‖P_{j+1} f - P_j f‖_p ≤ M 2^(j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖(⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩)_k‖_{ℓ_p}`. The block is the wavelet
expansion with the coefficients `⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩`
(`Daubechies.enorm_daubechiesProj_succ_sub_daubechiesProj`), so the lower and the upper stability of
the expansions (`Daubechies.lqNorm_le_eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand`, which uses the orthonormality of
the translates of `ψ`, and `Daubechies.eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand_le`) give the constants
`K = Daubechies.coeffConst` and `M = Daubechies.expandConst` for `g = ψ`.

Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_steklovSmooth_le_.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_steklovSmooth_le_smoothnessModulus
Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_steklovSmooth_le_.docstring:
**The smoothing is close to `f` on the whole line**: for continuous `f : ℝ → ℂ`, `r ∈ ℕ`,
`δ > 0` and `1 ≤ p < ∞`,
`‖f - S_δ f‖_{L_p(ℝ)} ≤ ω_r(f, rδ)_p`.
Indeed `f - S_δ f = (-1)^r avg_{v ∈ [0, δ]^r} Δ^r_{v_1 + ⋯ + v_r} f`
(`Interval.sub_steklovSmooth_eq`), and Minkowski's inequality for averages
(`Interval.eLpNorm_avgStepIter_le`, stated for `p < ∞`) bounds its norm by the supremum of
`‖Δ_h^r f‖_{L_p(ℝ)}` over `0 ≤ h ≤ rδ`.

Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_steklovSmooth_le_.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_steklovSmooth_le_dyadic
Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_steklovSmooth_le_.docstring:
**The smoothing at a dyadic scale is close to `f`**: for continuous `f : ℝ → ℂ`, `N ≥ 1`,
`j ∈ ℕ`, `1 ≤ p < ∞` and the step `δ = 1/(N 2^j)`,
`‖f - S_δ f‖_{L_p(ℝ)} ≤ ω_N(f, 2^(-j))_p`.
This is `eLpNorm_sub_steklovSmooth_le_smoothnessModulus` with `r = N`, since `Nδ = 2^(-j)`.

Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le_smooth.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le_smoothnessModulus
Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le_smooth.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality for continuous functions**: for `N ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, every continuous
`f : ℝ → ℂ` and every level `j`,
`‖f - P_j f‖_p ≤ C_J ω_N(f, 2^(-j))_p` with `C_J = daubechiesJacksonConst m p` and the modulus of
smoothness `ω_N(f, t)_p = sup_{|h| ≤ t} ‖Δ_h^N f‖_{L_p(ℝ)}` (`Rd.smoothnessModulus volume`). With
the Steklov smoothing `S = S_δ f` at the step `δ = 1/(N 2^j)`, which lies in `C^N`
(`Interval.contDiff_steklovSmooth`): `‖f - S‖_p ≤ ω_N(f, 2^(-j))_p`
(`Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_steklovSmooth_le_dyadic`), `‖S^(N)‖_p ≤ 2^N N^N 2^(jN) ω_N(f, 2^(-j))_p`
(`Daubechies.eLpNorm_iteratedDeriv_steklovSmooth_le_dyadic`), hence
`‖S - P_j S‖_p ≤ C_S 2^N N^N ω_N(f, 2^(-j))_p` (`Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le_of_contDiff`),
and `Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le_add` with `Daubechies.add_le_daubechiesJacksonConst_mul`
combines the two bounds. The inequality holds in `[0, ∞]` for every continuous `f`.

Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le_of_con.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le_of_contDiff
Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le_of_con.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality for smooth functions**: for `N ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `S ∈ C^N(ℝ)` and
every level `j`, `‖S - P_j S‖_p ≤ C_S 2^(-jN) ‖S^(N)‖_p` with `C_S = smoothJacksonConst m p`.
The cell bound `Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_cell_le` holds on every dyadic cell of level `j`,
the cells cover `ℝ` (`Daubechies.iUnion_Ico_div_two_pow`), and the windows satisfy the window
summation `Daubechies.tsum_eLpNorm_window_rpow_le`, so the summation lemma
`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_forall_eLpNorm_restrict_le` applies. The inequality holds in
`[0, ∞]` for every `S ∈ C^N(ℝ)`.

Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le_add.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le_add
Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le_add.docstring:
**Comparing the errors of two functions**: for `N ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, locally integrable
`f, S : ℝ → ℂ` and every level `j`,
`‖f - P_j f‖_p ≤ (1 + C) ‖f - S‖_p + ‖S - P_j S‖_p` with the uniform bound `C = projConst m p` of
the projections. Indeed `f - P_j f = (f - S) + (S - P_j S) + P_j (S - f)` by the linearity of
`P_j` (`Daubechies.projFun_sub`), and `‖P_j (S - f)‖_p ≤ C ‖S - f‖_p`
(`Daubechies.eLpNorm_projFun_le`).

Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le
Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le.docstring:
**The `L_p` error of `P_j f` for a continuous function with compact support**: let `N ≥ 2`,
let `f` be continuous with `f(x) = 0` for `|x| ≥ R`, let `‖φ(t)‖ ≤ C` for all `t`, and let `η`
bound `‖f(y) - f(x)‖` for all `x, y` with `|y - x| ≤ (2N - 1)/2^j`. Then for every exponent `p`,
`‖f - P_j f‖_p ≤ 2N C ‖φ‖_1 η |[-R - 2N, R + 2N]|^(1/p)`. The pointwise bound
`Daubechies.enorm_projFun_sub_le` holds everywhere, and `P_j f - f` vanishes for
`|x| > R + 2N`, where the same bound holds with `η = 0`.

Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_cell_le_o.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_cell_le_of_poly
Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_cell_le_o.docstring:
**The error on a cell through a polynomial**: let `N ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, let `S : ℝ → ℂ` be
locally integrable and `Q` a complex polynomial of degree `< N`. Then on the dyadic cell
`I = [k/2^j, (k + 1)/2^j)` with the window `W = [(k - (2N - 2))/2^j, (k + 2N - 1)/2^j]`,
`‖S - P_j S‖_{L_p(I)} ≤ (1 + C) ‖S - Q‖_{L_p(W)}` with the constant `C = cellConst m p` of the
local bound. Indeed `S - P_j S = (S - Q) - P_j (S - Q)`
(`Daubechies.sub_projFun_eq_sub_projFun_sub`), `I ⊆ W` (`Daubechies.Ico_subset_window`), and
`‖P_j (S - Q)‖_{L_p(I)} ≤ C ‖S - Q‖_{L_p(W)}` (`Daubechies.eLpNorm_projFun_cell_le`).

Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_cell_le.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_cell_le
Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_cell_le.docstring:
**The error on a cell for a smooth function**: let `N ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞` and `S ∈ C^N(ℝ)`.
Then on the dyadic cell `I = [k/2^j, (k + 1)/2^j)` with the window
`W = [(k - (2N - 2))/2^j, (k + 2N - 1)/2^j]`,
`‖S - P_j S‖_{L_p(I)} ≤ (1 + C) (4N - 3)^N 2^(-jN) ‖S^(N)‖_{L_p(W)}` with `C = cellConst m p`.
Taylor's theorem on `W` gives a polynomial `Q` of degree `< N` with
`‖S - Q‖_{L_p(W)} ≤ |W|^N ‖S^(N)‖_{L_p(W)}` (`Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le`), and
`|W| = (4N - 3)/2^j` (`Daubechies.ofReal_window_length_pow`); then
`Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_cell_le_of_poly` applies.

Daubechies.eLpNorm_scaledFun_conjExponen.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_scaledFun_conjExponent
Daubechies.eLpNorm_scaledFun_conjExponen.docstring:
**`L_{p'}` norms of the generators**: for `1 ≤ p` and the conjugate exponent `p'`,
`‖g_{j,k}‖_{p'} = 2^(-j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖g‖_{p'}`, since `1/2 - 1/p' = -(1/2 - 1/p)`
(`Daubechies.eLpNorm_scaledFun`, `Daubechies.one_div_toReal_conjExponent`).

Daubechies.eLpNorm_scaledFun.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_scaledFun
Daubechies.eLpNorm_scaledFun.docstring:
**`L_p` norms of the generators**: for every a.e. strongly measurable `g`, every level `j`,
position `k` and exponent `p`, `‖g_{j,k}‖_p = 2^(j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖g‖_p`
(`Daubechies.eLpNorm_comp_two_pow_mul_sub` and the factor `2^(j/2)`,
`enorm_two_rpow_half`). In particular
`‖g_{j,k}‖_2 = ‖g‖_2`.

Daubechies.eLpNorm_projFun_le.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_projFun_le
Daubechies.eLpNorm_projFun_le.docstring:
**The projections are bounded on `L_p`, uniformly in the level**: for `N ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`,
every a.e. strongly measurable `f` and every level `j`, `‖P_j f‖_p ≤ C ‖f‖_p` with
`C = projConst m p`, from the upper estimate of the expansions and the coefficient estimate,
whose dyadic weights cancel (`Daubechies.eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand_coeffFun_le`).

Daubechies.eLpNorm_projFun_cell_le.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_projFun_cell_le
Daubechies.eLpNorm_projFun_cell_le.docstring:
**The local bound on a dyadic cell**: for `N ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, every a.e. strongly measurable
`f`, every level `j` and every `k ∈ ℤ`, the projection on the dyadic cell
`I = [k/2^j, (k + 1)/2^j)` is controlled by `f` on the window
`W = [(k - (2N - 2))/2^j, (k + 2N - 1)/2^j]`:
`‖P_j f‖_{L_p(I)} ≤ (2N - 1) ‖φ‖_p ‖φ‖_{p'} ‖f‖_{L_p(W)}` (the constant `Daubechies.cellConst`
is the same for every `j` and `k`). On `I` only the `2N - 1` positions `k - (2N - 2) ≤ l ≤ k`
contribute (`Daubechies.projFun_eq_sum_of_mem_cell`), the support windows of their `φ_{j,l}` lie
in `W` (`Daubechies.supportWindow_subset_of_mem_Icc`), and each term is bounded by
`Daubechies.eLpNorm_coeffFun_mul_daubechiesScaled_le`.

Daubechies.eLpNorm_mul_conj_scaledFun_le.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_mul_conj_scaledFun_le
Daubechies.eLpNorm_mul_conj_scaledFun_le.docstring:
**Hölder's inequality on a support window**: let `g` be a.e. strongly measurable and vanish
outside `[a, b]`, let `1 ≤ p`, and let `f` be a.e. strongly measurable. Then
`‖f conj g_{j,k}‖_1 ≤ ‖1_W f‖_p ‖g_{j,k}‖_{p'}` with the support window
`W = {x : 2^j x - k ∈ [a, b]}` and the conjugate exponent `p'`, since `g_{j,k}` vanishes outside
`W` (`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_mul_conj_le_of_forall_notMem`).

Daubechies.eLpNorm_iteratedDeriv_steklov.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_iteratedDeriv_steklovSmooth_le_smoothnessModulus
Daubechies.eLpNorm_iteratedDeriv_steklov.docstring:
**The derivative of order `r` of the smoothing on the whole line**: for continuous
`f : ℝ → ℂ`, `r ∈ ℕ`, `δ > 0` and `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`,
`‖(S_δ f)^(r)‖_{L_p(ℝ)} ≤ 2^r δ^(-r) ω_r(f, rδ)_p`,
by the triangle inequality for `(S_δ f)^(r) = ∑_{k=1}^r (-1)^(k+1) C(r, k) (kδ)^(-r) Δ_{kδ}^r f`
and `∑_{k=1}^r C(r, k) ≤ 2^r` (`Interval.eLpNorm_sum_smoothCoeff_smul_le` for Lebesgue measure on
`ℝ`).

Daubechies.eLpNorm_iteratedDeriv_steklov.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_iteratedDeriv_steklovSmooth_le_dyadic
Daubechies.eLpNorm_iteratedDeriv_steklov.docstring:
**The derivative of the smoothing at a dyadic scale**: for continuous `f : ℝ → ℂ`, `N ≥ 1`,
`j ∈ ℕ`, `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞` and the step `δ = 1/(N 2^j)`,
`‖(S_δ f)^(N)‖_{L_p(ℝ)} ≤ 2^N N^N 2^(jN) ω_N(f, 2^(-j))_p`.
This is `eLpNorm_iteratedDeriv_steklovSmooth_le_smoothnessModulus` with `r = N`, since
`δ^(-N) = N^N 2^(jN)` (`Daubechies.ofReal_one_div_mul_two_pow_inv_pow`) and `Nδ = 2^(-j)`.

Daubechies.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_smoothn.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_smoothnessModulus_of_nonneg
Daubechies.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_smoothn.docstring:
**Differences with a nonnegative step are bounded by the modulus**: for `0 ≤ h ≤ t`,
`‖Δ_h^r f‖_{L_p(ℝ)} ≤ ω_r(f, t)_p`, where `ω_r(f, t)_p = sup_{|h| ≤ t} ‖Δ_h^r f‖_{L_p(ℝ)}` is the
modulus of smoothness of the line (`Rd.smoothnessModulus volume`).

Daubechies.eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand_le.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand_le
Daubechies.eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand_le.docstring:
**Upper stability of the expansions**: let `g` be a.e. strongly measurable and vanish outside
`[a, b]`, and let `1 ≤ p < ∞`. Then for every level `j` and all coefficients `c : ℤ → ℂ`,
`‖∑_k c_k g_{j,k}‖_p ≤ M^(1 - 1/p) ‖g‖_p 2^(j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖c‖_{ℓ_p}` with the overlap number
`M = ⌈b - a⌉ + 1`. The constant `M^(1 - 1/p) ‖g‖_p` (`Daubechies.expandConst`) is proportional to
`‖g‖_p`, depends on the support only through `b - a`, and is the same for every level `j` and
every `c`. At each point at most `M` terms are nonzero
(`Daubechies.card_le_of_forall_mem_supportWindow`), so
the bounded overlap inequality `‖∑_k F_k‖_p^p ≤ M^(p-1) ∑_k ‖F_k‖_p^p`
(`Rd.eLpNorm_rpow_le_of_overlap`) applies, and
`‖c_k g_{j,k}‖_p = |c_k| 2^(j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖g‖_p` (`Daubechies.eLpNorm_const_mul_scaledFun`).

Daubechies.eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand_coef.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand_coeffFun_le
Daubechies.eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand_coef.docstring:
**The expansion of the coefficients is bounded on `L_p`, uniformly in the level**: if `g` is
a.e. strongly measurable and vanishes outside `[a, b]` and `1 ≤ p < ∞`, then for every a.e.
strongly measurable `f` and every level `j`, `‖∑_k ⟨f, g_{j,k}⟩ g_{j,k}‖_p ≤ C C' ‖f‖_p` with the
constants `C = expandConst g a b p` and `C' = coeffConst g a b p`: the upper estimate
(`Daubechies.eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand_le`) and the coefficient estimate
(`Daubechies.dyadicWeight_mul_lqNorm_coeffFun_le`), whose dyadic weights cancel.

Daubechies.eLpNorm_const_mul_scaledFun.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_const_mul_scaledFun
Daubechies.eLpNorm_const_mul_scaledFun.docstring:
**`L_p` norm of a multiple of a generator**: `‖z g_{j,k}‖_p = |z| 2^(j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖g‖_p` for
every `z ∈ ℂ` (`Daubechies.eLpNorm_scaledFun`).

Daubechies.eLpNorm_comp_two_pow_mul_sub.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_comp_two_pow_mul_sub
Daubechies.eLpNorm_comp_two_pow_mul_sub.docstring:
**Dilation and translation in `L_p`**: for every a.e. strongly measurable `F : ℝ → ℂ`, every
`j ∈ ℕ`, `t ∈ ℝ` and every exponent `p`, `‖F(2^j · - t)‖_p = 2^(-j/p) ‖F‖_p`. The image of
Lebesgue measure under `x ↦ 2^j x` is `2^(-j)` times Lebesgue measure (Mathlib's
`Real.map_volume_mul_left`), and translations preserve Lebesgue measure. For `p = ∞` the factor
is `1`, since then `1/p.toReal = 0` in Lean.

Daubechies.eLpNorm_coeffFun_mul_daubechi.name: Daubechies.eLpNorm_coeffFun_mul_daubechiesScaled_le
Daubechies.eLpNorm_coeffFun_mul_daubechi.docstring:
**One term of the projection, bounded on a window**: let `N ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ p`, let `f` be a.e.
strongly measurable, and let the set `W` contain the support window of `φ_{j,l}`. Then
`‖⟨f, φ_{j,l}⟩ φ_{j,l}‖_p ≤ ‖φ‖_p ‖φ‖_{p'} ‖f‖_{L_p(W)}`, from Hölder's inequality on the support
window (`Daubechies.enorm_coeffFun_le`) and the norms `‖φ_{j,l}‖_p = 2^(j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖φ‖_p` and
`‖φ_{j,l}‖_{p'} = 2^(-j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖φ‖_{p'}` (`Daubechies.eLpNorm_const_mul_scaledFun`,
`Daubechies.eLpNorm_scaledFun_conjExponent`), whose dyadic weights cancel.

Daubechies.dyadicWeight_mul_lqNorm_coeff.name: Daubechies.dyadicWeight_mul_lqNorm_coeffFun_le
Daubechies.dyadicWeight_mul_lqNorm_coeff.docstring:
**The coefficient estimate, weighted form**:
`2^(j(1/2 - 1/p)) ‖(⟨f, g_{j,k}⟩)_k‖_{ℓ_p} ≤ C' ‖f‖_p` with `C' = coeffConst g a b p`, under the
hypotheses of `Daubechies.lqNorm_coeffFun_le`, since `2^(j(1/2 - 1/p)) 2^(-j(1/2 - 1/p)) = 1`.

Daubechies.dualCoeff_sub_eq_zero.name: Daubechies.dualCoeff_sub_eq_zero
Daubechies.dualCoeff_sub_eq_zero.docstring:
The shifted dual filter `n ↦ g_{n-2l}` vanishes outside `[2l + 2 - 2N, 2l + 1]`
(`Daubechies.dualCoeff_eq_zero`).

Daubechies.dualCoeff_eq_zero.name: Daubechies.dualCoeff_eq_zero
Daubechies.dualCoeff_eq_zero.docstring: The dual filter vanishes outside `2 - 2N ≤ k ≤ 1`.

Daubechies.dualCoeff.name: Daubechies.dualCoeff
Daubechies.dualCoeff.docstring:
**The dual filter** `g_k = (-1)^k c_(1-k)` of a mask, the coefficients of the refinement
equation `ψ(x) = ∑_k g_k φ(2x - k)` of the wavelet. They vanish outside `2 - 2N ≤ k ≤ 1`
(`Daubechies.dualCoeff_eq_zero`).

Daubechies.div_two_pow_add_succ.name: Daubechies.div_two_pow_add_succ
Daubechies.div_two_pow_add_succ.docstring:
`ξ/2^(n+j+1) = (ξ/2^n)/2^(j+1)`: the arguments of the tail of a dyadic product are the
arguments of the full product at the point `ξ/2^n`.

Daubechies.daubechiesScheme.name: Daubechies.daubechiesScheme
Daubechies.daubechiesScheme.docstring:
**The Daubechies scheme** in `L_p`, for `N ≥ 2` and `1 ≤ p < ∞`: `{0}` at complexity `0` and
the scaling space `V_{⌊log₂ n⌋}` at complexity `n ≥ 1`, so that `V_k` is the set of approximants
of complexity `2^k` (`ApproximationScheme.ofMonotoneSubmodules`).

Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_refine.name: Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_refine
Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_refine.docstring:
**The refinement relation between levels**: for `N ≥ 2`, every level `j`, position `k` and
point `x`, `φ_{j,k}(x) = ∑_{i=0}^{2N-1} (c_i/√2) φ_{j+1,2k+i}(x)`. This is the refinement
equation `φ(y) = ∑_i c_i φ(2y - i)` (`Daubechies.scalingFun_refine`) at `y = 2^j x - k`, with
`2(2^j x - k) - i = 2^(j+1) x - (2k + i)` and `2^(j/2) = 2^((j+1)/2)/√2`
(`Daubechies.two_rpow_succ_div_two`).

Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_mul_integral.name: Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_mul_integral_conj
Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_mul_integral.docstring:
**`φ_{j,k}` times its integral**: `φ_{j,k}(x) ∫ conj φ_{j,k} = φ(2^j x - k)` for `N ≥ 2`, every
level `j`, position `k` and point `x`. The scaling function is real with `∫ φ = 1`
(`Daubechies.conj_scalingFun`, `Daubechies.integral_scalingFun`), so the substitution `u = 2^j y`
(`Daubechies.integral_eq_two_pow_mul_integral_comp`) gives
`∫ conj φ_{j,k} = 2^(j/2) 2^(-j)`, and `2^(j/2) 2^(j/2) 2^(-j) = 1`.

Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_eq_zero_of_n.name: Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_eq_zero_of_notMem_Icc
Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_eq_zero_of_n.docstring:
**The positions contributing at a point**: for `N ≥ 2`, `φ_{j,k}(x) = 0` unless
`⌈2^j x - (2N - 1)⌉ ≤ k ≤ ⌊2^j x⌋` (`Daubechies.scaledFun_eq_zero`,
`Daubechies.mem_Icc_ceil_floor`).

Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_eq_zero_of_m.name: Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_eq_zero_of_mem_cell
Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_eq_zero_of_m.docstring:
**Only the positions `k - (2N - 2) ≤ l ≤ k` meet a dyadic cell**: for `N ≥ 2`, if `x` lies in
the dyadic cell `[k/2^j, (k + 1)/2^j)` and `l` lies outside `[k - (2N - 2), k]`, then
`φ_{j,l}(x) = 0`. Indeed `φ` vanishes outside the open interval `(0, 2N - 1)`
(`Daubechies.scalingFun_eq_zero_of_notMem_Ioo`), and `0 < 2^j x - l < 2N - 1` together with
`k ≤ 2^j x < k + 1` forces `k - (2N - 1) < l < k + 1`.

Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_eq_daubechie.name: Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_eq_daubechiesExpand
Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_eq_daubechie.docstring:
**`φ_{j,k}` is an expansion of level `j + 1`**: for `N ≥ 2`, every level `j`, position `k`
and point `x`, `φ_{j,k}(x) = ∑_{n ∈ ℤ} (c_{n-2k}/√2) φ_{j+1,n}(x)`. This is the refinement
relation `Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_refine` after the substitution `n = 2k + i`; the filter
coefficients `c_i` vanish outside `0 ≤ i ≤ 2N - 1` (`Daubechies.daubechiesCoeff_eq_zero`).

Daubechies.daubechiesScaled.name: Daubechies.daubechiesScaled
Daubechies.daubechiesScaled.docstring:
**The functions `φ_{j,k}` of the multiresolution analysis**:
`φ_{j,k}(x) = 2^(j/2) φ(2^j x - k)` for the scaling function `φ` (`Daubechies.scalingFun`), the
level `j ∈ ℕ` and the position `k ∈ ℤ`; this is the generic `Daubechies.scaledFun` for `g = φ`.

Daubechies.daubechiesProjectionScheme_on.name: Daubechies.daubechiesProjectionScheme_one
Daubechies.daubechiesProjectionScheme_on.docstring:
**The projection of complexity `1` of the Daubechies projection scheme is `P_0`**: the
case `k = 0` of `Daubechies.daubechiesProjectionScheme_two_pow`.

Daubechies.daubechiesProjectionScheme_bl.name: Daubechies.daubechiesProjectionScheme_block
Daubechies.daubechiesProjectionScheme_bl.docstring:
**The dyadic blocks of the Daubechies projection scheme**: for every `f ∈ L_p` and level `j`,
the block `P(2^(j+1)) f - P(2^j) f` of the projection scheme is `P_{j+1} f - P_j f`, since the
projection of complexity `2^j` is `P_j` (`Daubechies.daubechiesProjectionScheme_two_pow`).

Daubechies.daubechiesProjectionScheme.name: Daubechies.daubechiesProjectionScheme
Daubechies.daubechiesProjectionScheme.docstring:
**The projection scheme of the Daubechies scaling spaces** in `L_p`, for `N ≥ 2` and
`1 ≤ p < ∞`: the projection of complexity `n ≥ 1` is `P_{⌊log₂ n⌋}`, the one of complexity `0`
is `0` (the approximants of complexity `0` are `{0}`), and all are bounded by `projConst m p`.

Daubechies.daubechiesProj_succ_sub_daube.name: Daubechies.daubechiesProj_succ_sub_daubechiesProj
Daubechies.daubechiesProj_succ_sub_daube.docstring:
**The block identity on `L_p`**: for `N ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, every level `j` and every
`f ∈ L_p`, `P_{j+1} f - P_j f` is the class of the wavelet part
`∑_k ⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩ ψ_{j,k}` (`Daubechies.daubechiesDetailFun`, `Daubechies.projFun_succ_eq_add`).

Daubechies.daubechiesProj_succ_daubechie.name: Daubechies.daubechiesProj_succ_daubechiesProj
Daubechies.daubechiesProj_succ_daubechie.docstring:
**The projections of consecutive levels**: `P_{j+1} (P_j f) = P_j f` for every `f ∈ L_p`, for
`N ≥ 2` and `1 ≤ p < ∞` (`Daubechies.projFun_succ_projFun`).

Daubechies.daubechiesProj_mem_scalingSpa.name: Daubechies.daubechiesProj_mem_scalingSpace
Daubechies.daubechiesProj_mem_scalingSpa.docstring: The projection `P_j f` lies in the scaling space `V_j`.

Daubechies.daubechiesProj_eq_self_of_mem.name: Daubechies.daubechiesProj_eq_self_of_mem
Daubechies.daubechiesProj_eq_self_of_mem.docstring:
**The projection fixes the scaling space**: `P_j a = a` for every `a ∈ V_j`
(`Daubechies.daubechiesProj_daubechiesProj`).

Daubechies.daubechiesProj_daubechiesProj.name: Daubechies.daubechiesProj_daubechiesProj
Daubechies.daubechiesProj_daubechiesProj.docstring:
**`P_j` is a projection**: `P_j (P_j f) = P_j f` for every `f ∈ L_p`, for `N ≥ 2` and
`1 ≤ p < ∞` (`Daubechies.projFun_projFun`).

Daubechies.daubechiesProj_apply_ae.name: Daubechies.daubechiesProj_apply_ae
Daubechies.daubechiesProj_apply_ae.docstring:
**The projection is the pointwise projection almost everywhere**:
`P_j f = ∑_k ⟨f, φ_{j,k}⟩ φ_{j,k}` almost everywhere, for every `f ∈ L_p`.

Daubechies.daubechiesProj.name: Daubechies.daubechiesProj
Daubechies.daubechiesProj.docstring:
**The projection of level `j` on `L_p`**, for `N ≥ 2` and `1 ≤ p < ∞`:
`P_j f = ∑_{k ∈ ℤ} ⟨f, φ_{j,k}⟩ φ_{j,k}`, a bounded operator whose norm is at most
`projConst m p` for every level (`Daubechies.norm_daubechiesProj_le`).

Daubechies.daubechiesJacksonConst_ne_top.name: Daubechies.daubechiesJacksonConst_ne_top
Daubechies.daubechiesJacksonConst_ne_top.docstring:
The constant `daubechiesJacksonConst m p` is finite for `N ≥ 2`
(`Daubechies.smoothJacksonConst_ne_top`).

Daubechies.daubechiesJacksonConst.name: Daubechies.daubechiesJacksonConst
Daubechies.daubechiesJacksonConst.docstring:
**The constant of Jackson's inequality**: `C_J = 1 + C + C_S 2^N N^N` with the uniform bound
`C = projConst m p` of the projections and the constant `C_S = smoothJacksonConst m p` for smooth
functions (`Daubechies.eLpNorm_sub_projFun_le_smoothnessModulus`). It depends only on the mask and
on `p`.

Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_wavelet_eq_d.name: Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_wavelet_eq_daubechiesExpand_succ
Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_wavelet_eq_d.docstring:
**Wavelet expansions of level `j` are expansions of level `j + 1`**: for `N ≥ 2`, every level
`j`, coefficients `b : ℤ → ℂ` and point `x`, `∑_k b_k ψ_{j,k}(x) = ∑_n b'_n φ_{j+1,n}(x)` with the
refined coefficients `b'_n = ∑_k b_k g_{n-2k}/√2` (`Daubechies.waveletRefineCoeff`), by
`Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_eq_tsum_refine_of_filter` and
`Daubechies.waveletScaled_eq_daubechiesExpand`.

Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_eq_tsum_refi.name: Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_eq_tsum_refine_of_filter
Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_eq_tsum_refi.docstring:
**Refining an expansion through a filter**: if `N ≥ 2`, the real filter `h` vanishes outside
`[a, b]` and `g_{j,k} = ∑_n (h_{n-2k}/√2) φ_{j+1,n}` for every `k`, then
`∑_k c_k g_{j,k}(x) = ∑_n (∑_k c_k h_{n-2k}/√2) φ_{j+1,n}(x)` for all `c` and `x`; the two sums
may be exchanged (`Daubechies.summable_refine_of_filter`).

Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_eq_daubechie.name: Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_eq_daubechiesExpand_succ
Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_eq_daubechie.docstring:
**Expansions of level `j` are expansions of level `j + 1`**: for `N ≥ 2`, every level `j`,
coefficients `a : ℤ → ℂ` and point `x`, `∑_k a_k φ_{j,k}(x) = ∑_n a'_n φ_{j+1,n}(x)` with the
refined coefficients `a'_n = ∑_k a_k c_{n-2k}/√2` (`Daubechies.refineCoeff`), by
`Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_eq_tsum_refine_of_filter` and
`Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_eq_daubechiesExpand`.

Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_const_mul.name: Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_const_mul
Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_const_mul.docstring:
**Expansions are homogeneous in the coefficients**:
`∑_k (z c_k) g_{j,k}(x) = z ∑_k c_k g_{j,k}(x)` for every `z ∈ ℂ` and every point `x`.

Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_add.name: Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_add
Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_add.docstring:
**Expansions are additive in the coefficients**: if `g` vanishes outside `[a, b]`, then
`∑_k (c_k + d_k) g_{j,k}(x) = ∑_k c_k g_{j,k}(x) + ∑_k d_k g_{j,k}(x)` at every point `x`; both
sums are finite (`Daubechies.summable_expand`).

Daubechies.daubechiesExpand.name: Daubechies.daubechiesExpand
Daubechies.daubechiesExpand.docstring:
**The expansion** `∑_{k ∈ ℤ} c_k g_{j,k}(x)` of level `j` with coefficients `c : ℤ → ℂ`. If
`g` vanishes outside a bounded interval, only finitely many terms are nonzero at each point
(`Daubechies.daubechiesExpand_eq_sum`), so the sum is meaningful for every coefficient sequence.

Daubechies.daubechiesDetailFun.name: Daubechies.daubechiesDetailFun
Daubechies.daubechiesDetailFun.docstring:
**The wavelet part of level `j`, pointwise**: `Q_j f(x) = ∑_{k ∈ ℤ} ⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩ ψ_{j,k}(x)`
for every `f : ℝ → ℂ`, the expansion of level `j` in the wavelets with the coefficients
`⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩ = ∫ f(y) conj ψ_{j,k}(y) dy` (`Daubechies.coeffFun`). It is the difference
`P_{j+1} f - P_j f` of two consecutive projections (`Daubechies.projFun_succ_eq_add`).

Daubechies.daubechiesCoeff_natCast.name: Daubechies.daubechiesCoeff_natCast
Daubechies.daubechiesCoeff_natCast.docstring: For `k ∈ ℕ` the filter coefficient is `c_k = 2 [z^k] m(z)`.

Daubechies.daubechiesCoeff_eq_zero.name: Daubechies.daubechiesCoeff_eq_zero
Daubechies.daubechiesCoeff_eq_zero.docstring:
The filter coefficients vanish outside `0 ≤ k < 2N`: for `k < 0` by definition, for
`k ≥ 2N` since the mask polynomial has degree `< 2N`.

Daubechies.daubechiesCoeffNorm.name: Daubechies.daubechiesCoeffNorm
Daubechies.daubechiesCoeffNorm.docstring:
**The Daubechies coefficient quasi-norm** of `f : ℝ → ℂ`, for the exponents `p, q` and the
smoothness `s`:
