`‖(⟨f, φ(· - k)⟩)_k‖_{ℓ_p} + ‖(2^(j(s + 1/2 - 1/p)) ‖(⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩)_k‖_{ℓ_p})_j‖_{ℓ_q}`, with the
coefficients `⟨f, g_{j,k}⟩ = ∫ f(x) conj g_{j,k}(x) dx` (`Daubechies.coeffFun`) of the scaling
function `φ` at level `0` and of the wavelet `ψ` at the levels `j ∈ ℕ`. Its finiteness describes
`B^s_{p,q}(ℝ)` (`Daubechies.besov_iff_coeff`).

Daubechies.daubechiesCoeff.name: Daubechies.daubechiesCoeff
Daubechies.daubechiesCoeff.docstring:
**The filter coefficients** `c_k = 2 [z^k] m(z)` of a mask, for `k ∈ ℤ`: twice the
coefficients of the mask polynomial for `k ≥ 0`, and `0` for `k < 0`. They vanish outside
`0 ≤ k < 2N` (`Daubechies.daubechiesCoeff_eq_zero`) and add up to `2`
(`Daubechies.sum_daubechiesCoeff`).

Daubechies.daubechiesBernsteinConst_ne_t.name: Daubechies.daubechiesBernsteinConst_ne_top
Daubechies.daubechiesBernsteinConst_ne_t.docstring:
The constant of the Bernstein inequality is finite for `N ≥ 2`, since `φ` lies in every
`L_p` (`Daubechies.coeffConst_ne_top`).

Daubechies.daubechiesBernsteinConst.name: Daubechies.daubechiesBernsteinConst
Daubechies.daubechiesBernsteinConst.docstring:
**The constant of the Bernstein inequality**: `(2N + 2r)^(1 - 1/p) (2N)^(1/p) ‖φ‖_{p'}` with
the conjugate exponent `p'`. The first factor is the overlap factor of the upper estimate of
expansions (`Daubechies.eLpNorm_daubechiesExpand_le`) for the generators `Δ_H^r φ`, `|H| ≤ 1`, which
vanish outside `[-r, 2N - 1 + r]` (`Daubechies.natCeil_higherDiff_support_add_one`); the second is
the constant of the coefficient estimate (`Daubechies.coeffConst` for `φ` and its support
`[0, 2N - 1]`). It is the same for every level and every scale.

Daubechies.daubPoly.name: Daubechies.daubPoly
Daubechies.daubPoly.docstring:
**The Daubechies polynomial** of order `N`: `P_N(y) = ∑_{k < N} C(N - 1 + k, k) y^k`, the
first `N` terms of the binomial series `(1 - y)^(-N) = ∑_k C(N - 1 + k, k) y^k`. For `N = 0`
it is the zero polynomial.

Daubechies.daubFun_le_choose.name: Daubechies.daubFun_le_choose
Daubechies.daubFun_le_choose.docstring:
`P ≤ C(2N - 1, N)` for every `N`: for `N ≥ 1` this is the value of `P_N` at `1`, the maximum
of `P_N` on `[0, 1]`.

Daubechies.daubFun_le.name: Daubechies.daubFun_le
Daubechies.daubFun_le.docstring:
`P(ξ) ≤ 1 + C(2N - 1, N) π² ξ²`, from `P_N(y) ≤ 1 + C(2N - 1, N) y` on `[0, 1]` and
`sin²(πξ) ≤ π² ξ²` (Mathlib's `Real.sin_sq_le_sq`).

Daubechies.daubFun_bezout.name: Daubechies.daubFun_bezout
Daubechies.daubFun_bezout.docstring:
**The trigonometric Bézout identity**: `cos(πξ)^(2N) P(ξ) + sin(πξ)^(2N) P(ξ + 1/2) = 1` for
`N ≥ 1`. This is the Bézout identity at `y = sin²(πξ)`, where `cos²(πξ) = 1 - y` and
`P(ξ + 1/2) = P_N(1 - y)`; it gives the quadrature mirror filter identity
`|m_0(ξ)|² + |m_0(ξ + 1/2)|² = 1` of the Daubechies masks.

Daubechies.daubFun.name: Daubechies.daubFun
Daubechies.daubFun.docstring:
**The trigonometric Daubechies polynomial** of order `N`: `P(ξ) = P_N(sin²(πξ))`. A
Daubechies mask of order `N` has a polynomial factor `L` with `|L(e^(-2πiξ))|² = P(ξ)`.

Daubechies.continuous_wavelet.name: Daubechies.continuous_wavelet
Daubechies.continuous_wavelet.docstring:
**The wavelet is continuous**, for `N ≥ 2`: a finite sum of dilated and translated copies of
the continuous scaling function (`Daubechies.continuous_scalingFun`).

Daubechies.continuous_transferOp.name: Daubechies.continuous_transferOp
Daubechies.continuous_transferOp.docstring: `T` maps continuous functions to continuous functions.

Daubechies.continuous_symbolProduct.name: Daubechies.continuous_symbolProduct
Daubechies.continuous_symbolProduct.docstring:
**The symbol product is continuous**, as a locally uniform limit of the continuous partial
products.

Daubechies.continuous_scalingFun.name: Daubechies.continuous_scalingFun
Daubechies.continuous_scalingFun.docstring:
**The scaling function is continuous** for `N ≥ 2`: the inverse Fourier transform of the
integrable function `Φ` (`Daubechies.integrable_symbolProduct`) is continuous
(`Real.real_continuous_fourierInv_of_integrable`).

Daubechies.continuous_projFun.name: Daubechies.continuous_projFun
Daubechies.continuous_projFun.docstring:
**The projection is continuous**: for `N ≥ 2`, `P_j f` is continuous for every level `j` and
every `f`, as an expansion in the continuous functions `φ_{j,k}`
(`Daubechies.continuous_daubechiesExpand`).

Daubechies.continuous_prod_daubFun.name: Daubechies.continuous_prod_daubFun
Daubechies.continuous_prod_daubFun.docstring: The finite dyadic products `ξ ↦ ∏_{j<n} P(ξ/2^(j+1))` are continuous.

Daubechies.continuous_pow_mul_scalingFun.name: Daubechies.continuous_pow_mul_scalingFun
Daubechies.continuous_pow_mul_scalingFun.docstring: For `N ≥ 2` the moment function `x ↦ x^l φ(x)` is continuous.

Daubechies.continuous_one_add_abs_rpow.name: Daubechies.continuous_one_add_abs_rpow
Daubechies.continuous_one_add_abs_rpow.docstring: The weight `ξ ↦ (1 + |ξ|)^t` is continuous for every real `t`, since `1 + |ξ| > 0`.

Daubechies.continuous_iterate_transferOp.name: Daubechies.continuous_iterate_transferOp_one
Daubechies.continuous_iterate_transferOp.docstring: The iterates `T^n 1` of the constant function `1` are continuous.

Daubechies.continuous_iterate_transferOp.name: Daubechies.continuous_iterate_transferOp
Daubechies.continuous_iterate_transferOp.docstring: The iterates `T^n g` of a continuous `g` are continuous.

Daubechies.continuous_iterate_fwdDiff.name: Daubechies.continuous_iterate_fwdDiff
Daubechies.continuous_iterate_fwdDiff.docstring:
The differences `Δ_h^r f` of a continuous `f : ℝ → ℂ` are continuous, for every `r ∈ ℕ` and
every `h ∈ ℝ`: by induction on `r`, since `Δ_h g = g(· + h) - g`.

Daubechies.continuous_fourier_cascade.name: Daubechies.continuous_fourier_cascade
Daubechies.continuous_fourier_cascade.docstring:
The Fourier transform of every cascade function is continuous, since `η_n` is integrable
(`Real.real_continuous_fourier_of_integrable`).

Daubechies.continuous_expFreq_mul.name: Daubechies.continuous_expFreq_mul
Daubechies.continuous_expFreq_mul.docstring: `ξ ↦ e^(-2πicξ)` is continuous for every `c ∈ ℝ`.

Daubechies.continuous_daubechiesExpand_u.name: Daubechies.continuous_daubechiesExpand_uncurry
Daubechies.continuous_daubechiesExpand_u.docstring:
**Expansions are jointly continuous in the coefficients and the point**: if `g` is continuous
and vanishes outside `[a, b]`, then `(c, x) ↦ ∑_k c_k g_{j,k}(x)` is continuous on
`(ℤ → ℂ) × ℝ`, with the product topology on the coefficient sequences. Near `(c, x)`, at all
`(c', y)` with `|2^j y - 2^j x| < 1`, the expansion is the same finite sum over
`⌈2^j x - b - 1⌉ ≤ k ≤ ⌊2^j x - a + 1⌋`, continuous in `(c', y)`.

Daubechies.continuous_daubechiesExpand.name: Daubechies.continuous_daubechiesExpand
Daubechies.continuous_daubechiesExpand.docstring:
**Expansions are continuous**: if `g` is continuous and vanishes outside `[a, b]`, then
`x ↦ ∑_k c_k g_{j,k}(x)` is continuous for every level `j` and all coefficients `c`, the
restriction of the jointly continuous map `(c, x) ↦ ∑_k c_k g_{j,k}(x)`
(`Daubechies.continuous_daubechiesExpand_uncurry`).

Daubechies.contDiff_symbolProduct.name: Daubechies.contDiff_symbolProduct
Daubechies.contDiff_symbolProduct.docstring:
**The symbol product is smooth** for `N ≥ 2`: `Φ = 𝓕 φ` (`Daubechies.fourier_scalingFun`)
is `C^∞`, since every moment `∫ |x|^n |φ(x)| dx` is finite (Mathlib's
`Real.contDiff_fourier`).

Daubechies.contDiff_symbol.name: Daubechies.contDiff_symbol
Daubechies.contDiff_symbol.docstring:
**The symbol is smooth**: `C^n` for every `n`, including `n = ∞` and the analytic case
`n = ω`, as a polynomial (Mathlib's `Polynomial.contDiff_aeval`) composed with the smooth map
`ξ ↦ e^(-2πiξ)`.

Daubechies.contDiff_nat_symbolProduct.name: Daubechies.contDiff_nat_symbolProduct
Daubechies.contDiff_nat_symbolProduct.docstring:
For `N ≥ 2` the symbol product is `C^n` for every `n ∈ ℕ`
(`Daubechies.contDiff_symbolProduct`).

Daubechies.contDiff_expFreq.name: Daubechies.contDiff_expFreq
Daubechies.contDiff_expFreq.docstring:
`ξ ↦ e^(-2πiξ)` is smooth: it is `C^n` for every `n`, including `n = ∞` and the analytic
case `n = ω`.

Daubechies.conj_scalingFun.name: Daubechies.conj_scalingFun
Daubechies.conj_scalingFun.docstring:
**The scaling function is real**: `conj φ(x) = φ(x)` for every `x ∈ ℝ`. Conjugation turns the
inverse transform into the transform of the conjugate (`Real.conj_fourierInv`),
`conj Φ(ξ) = Φ(-ξ)` (`Daubechies.symbolProduct_neg`), and `𝓕[Φ(-·)] = 𝓕⁻ Φ` (Mathlib's
`Real.fourierInv_eq_fourier_comp_neg`).

Daubechies.coeff_iterate_X_mul_derivativ.name: Daubechies.coeff_iterate_X_mul_derivative
Daubechies.coeff_iterate_X_mul_derivativ.docstring:
The `l`-th iterate of the Euler operator `p ↦ X p'` multiplies the `k`-th coefficient by
`k^l`.

Daubechies.coeff_X_mul_derivative.name: Daubechies.coeff_X_mul_derivative
Daubechies.coeff_X_mul_derivative.docstring:
**The Euler operator on coefficients**: the `k`-th coefficient of `X p'` is `k` times the
`k`-th coefficient of `p`.

Daubechies.coeffFun_wavelet_eq_tsum.name: Daubechies.coeffFun_wavelet_eq_tsum
Daubechies.coeffFun_wavelet_eq_tsum.docstring:
**The wavelet coefficients of level `j` through the scaling coefficients of level `j + 1`**:
for `N ≥ 2` and locally integrable `f`, `⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩ = ∑_n (g_{n-2k}/√2) ⟨f, φ_{j+1,n}⟩`
(`Daubechies.coeffFun_eq_tsum_of_filter`, `Daubechies.waveletScaled_eq_daubechiesExpand`).

Daubechies.coeffFun_scalingFun_eq_tsum.name: Daubechies.coeffFun_scalingFun_eq_tsum
Daubechies.coeffFun_scalingFun_eq_tsum.docstring:
**The scaling coefficients of level `j` through those of level `j + 1`**: for `N ≥ 2` and
locally integrable `f`, `⟨f, φ_{j,k}⟩ = ∑_n (c_{n-2k}/√2) ⟨f, φ_{j+1,n}⟩`
(`Daubechies.coeffFun_eq_tsum_of_filter`, `Daubechies.daubechiesScaled_eq_daubechiesExpand`).

Daubechies.coeffFun_eq_tsum_of_filter.name: Daubechies.coeffFun_eq_tsum_of_filter
Daubechies.coeffFun_eq_tsum_of_filter.docstring:
**The coefficients of a refinable generator through those of the next level**: if `N ≥ 2`,
the real filter `h` vanishes outside `[a, b]`, `f` is locally integrable and
`g_{j,k} = ∑_n (h_{n-2k}/√2) φ_{j+1,n}`, then `⟨f, g_{j,k}⟩ = ∑_n (h_{n-2k}/√2) ⟨f, φ_{j+1,n}⟩`
(`Daubechies.integral_mul_conj_daubechiesExpand` for the finite expansion; the filter is real).

Daubechies.coeffFun_daubechiesExpand_sca.name: Daubechies.coeffFun_daubechiesExpand_scalingFun
Daubechies.coeffFun_daubechiesExpand_sca.docstring:
**Coefficient recovery for the scaling function**: for `N ≥ 2`, every level `j`, every
coefficient sequence `c : ℤ → ℂ` and every `k ∈ ℤ`, `⟨∑_l c_l φ_{j,l}, φ_{j,k}⟩ = c_k`
(`Daubechies.coeffFun_daubechiesExpand` for `g = φ`, with `a = 0` and `b = 2N - 1`).

Daubechies.coeffFun_daubechiesExpand.name: Daubechies.coeffFun_daubechiesExpand
Daubechies.coeffFun_daubechiesExpand.docstring:
**Coefficient recovery**: let `g` be continuous, vanish outside `[a, b]`, and have
orthonormal integer translates. Then for every level `j`, every coefficient sequence
`c : ℤ → ℂ` and every `k ∈ ℤ`, `⟨∑_l c_l g_{j,l}, g_{j,k}⟩ = c_k`. Only the positions `l` with
`|l - k| ≤ ⌈b - a⌉` contribute to the integrand (`Daubechies.scaledFun_mul_conj_eq_zero`), so it
is a finite sum, and orthonormality at level `j` (`Daubechies.integral_scaledFun_mul_conj`) leaves
the term `l = k`. The sequence `c` is arbitrary: at each point the sum over `l` is finite.

Daubechies.coeffFun_const_mul.name: Daubechies.coeffFun_const_mul
Daubechies.coeffFun_const_mul.docstring:
**The coefficients are homogeneous in `f`**: `⟨z f, g_{j,k}⟩ = z ⟨f, g_{j,k}⟩` for every
`z ∈ ℂ` (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.integral_const_mul`).

Daubechies.coeffFun_congr_ae.name: Daubechies.coeffFun_congr_ae
Daubechies.coeffFun_congr_ae.docstring:
**The coefficients depend only on the class of `f` almost everywhere**: if `f = f'` almost
everywhere, then `⟨f, g_{j,k}⟩ = ⟨f', g_{j,k}⟩` (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.integral_congr_ae`).

Daubechies.coeffFun_add.name: Daubechies.coeffFun_add
Daubechies.coeffFun_add.docstring:
**The coefficients are additive in `f`**: `⟨f + f', g_{j,k}⟩ = ⟨f, g_{j,k}⟩ + ⟨f', g_{j,k}⟩`
when both integrands are integrable (for instance for `f, f' ∈ L_p`,
`Daubechies.integrable_mul_conj_scaledFun`).

Daubechies.coeffFun.name: Daubechies.coeffFun
Daubechies.coeffFun.docstring:
**The coefficient functional** `⟨f, g_{j,k}⟩ = ∫ f(y) conj g_{j,k}(y) dy` of level `j` and
position `k`. For an orthonormal system it recovers the coefficients of an expansion
(`Daubechies.coeffFun_daubechiesExpand`).

Daubechies.coeffConst_ne_top.name: Daubechies.coeffConst_ne_top
Daubechies.coeffConst_ne_top.docstring:
The constant `coeffConst g a b p` is finite for every `g ∈ L_{p'}`, `p'` the conjugate
exponent.

Daubechies.coeffConst.name: Daubechies.coeffConst
Daubechies.coeffConst.docstring:
**The constant of the coefficient estimate** `Daubechies.lqNorm_coeffFun_le`:
`M^(1/p) ‖g‖_{p'}` with the overlap number `M = ⌈b - a⌉ + 1` and the conjugate exponent
`p' = p/(p - 1)` (Mathlib's `ENNReal.conjExponent`). It is the same for every level.

Daubechies.closure_iUnion_scalingSpace.name: Daubechies.closure_iUnion_scalingSpace
Daubechies.closure_iUnion_scalingSpace.docstring:
**The scaling spaces are dense** in `L_p`, for `N ≥ 2` and `1 ≤ p < ∞`: the closure of
`⋃_j V_j` is all of `L_p`. Approximate `F ∈ L_p` by a continuous function `g` with compact
support (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.MemLp.exists_hasCompactSupport_eLpNorm_sub_le`), and `g` by
`P_j g ∈ V_j` (`Daubechies.tendsto_eLpNorm_sub_projFun`).

Daubechies.closure_iUnion_daubechiesSche.name: Daubechies.closure_iUnion_daubechiesScheme
Daubechies.closure_iUnion_daubechiesSche.docstring:
**The Daubechies scheme is dense** in `L_p`, for `N ≥ 2` and `1 ≤ p < ∞`: the closure of the
union of its approximants is all of `L_p`, since `V_j` is the set of approximants of complexity
`2^j` (`Daubechies.mem_daubechiesScheme_two_pow`, `Daubechies.closure_iUnion_scalingSpace`).

Daubechies.choose_two_mul_eq_two_mul_cho.name: Daubechies.choose_two_mul_eq_two_mul_choose
Daubechies.choose_two_mul_eq_two_mul_cho.docstring:
`C(2N, N) = 2 C(2N - 1, N)` for `N ≥ 1`: Pascal's rule
`C(2N, N) = C(2N - 1, N - 1) + C(2N - 1, N)` and the symmetry `C(2N - 1, N - 1) = C(2N - 1, N)`
(Mathlib's `Nat.choose_symm_half`).

Daubechies.choose_lt_four_pow.name: Daubechies.choose_lt_four_pow
Daubechies.choose_lt_four_pow.docstring:
`C(2N - 1, N) < 4^(N - 1)` for `N ≥ 2`. With `N = M + 1`, `C(2M + 1, M + 1) = C(2M + 1, M)`
is a term of `∑_{i ≤ M} C(2M + 1, i) = 4^M` (Mathlib's `Nat.sum_range_choose_halfway`), and so is
`C(2M + 1, 0) = 1` since `M ≥ 1`. Equivalently `N - log₄(2 C(2N - 1, N)) > 1/2`.

Daubechies.cellConst_ne_top.name: Daubechies.cellConst_ne_top
Daubechies.cellConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of the local bound is finite for `N ≥ 2`, since `φ` lies in every `L_p`.

Daubechies.cellConst.name: Daubechies.cellConst
Daubechies.cellConst.docstring:
**The constant of the local bound**: `(2N - 1) ‖φ‖_p ‖φ‖_{p'}` with the conjugate exponent
`p'` (`Daubechies.eLpNorm_projFun_cell_le`).

Daubechies.cascade_succ_apply.name: Daubechies.cascade_succ_apply
Daubechies.cascade_succ_apply.docstring:
**The cascade recursion** `η_(n+1)(x) = ∑_{k=0}^{2N-1} c_k η_n(2x - k)` for every
`x ∈ ℝ`.

Daubechies.cascade_succ.name: Daubechies.cascade_succ
Daubechies.cascade_succ.docstring:
The cascade recursion as an identity of functions:
`η_(n+1) = (x ↦ ∑_{k=0}^{2N-1} c_k η_n(2x - k))`.

Daubechies.cascade_eq_zero.name: Daubechies.cascade_eq_zero
Daubechies.cascade_eq_zero.docstring:
**The cascade functions vanish outside `[0, 2N - 1]`**: `η_n(x) = 0` for every `n` and every
`x ∉ [0, 2N - 1]`. By induction on `n`: `[0, 1) ⊆ [0, 2N - 1]` since `N ≥ 1`
(`Daubechies.Mask.one_le`), and for `x ∉ [0, 2N - 1]` no point `2x - k` with `0 ≤ k ≤ 2N - 1`
lies in `[0, 2N - 1]` (`Daubechies.mem_Icc_of_two_mul_sub_mem_Icc`).

Daubechies.cascade.name: Daubechies.cascade
Daubechies.cascade.docstring:
**The cascade algorithm** of a mask with filter coefficients `c_k`: `η_0 = 1_[0,1)` is the
indicator function of `[0, 1)`, and `η_(n+1)(x) = ∑_{k=0}^{2N-1} c_k η_n(2x - k)`. For `N ≥ 2`
the functions `η_n` converge to the scaling function `φ` against every Schwartz function
(`Daubechies.tendsto_integral_cascade_mul`).

Daubechies.card_le_of_forall_mem_window.name: Daubechies.card_le_of_forall_mem_window
Daubechies.card_le_of_forall_mem_window.docstring:
**Bounded overlap of the windows**: for `N ≥ 1`, every point `x` lies in at most `4N - 2`
of the windows `[(k - (2N - 2))/2^j, (k + 2N - 1)/2^j]`, `k ∈ ℤ`, of one level `j`. The windows
are the support windows of an interval of length `4N - 3`
(`Daubechies.card_le_of_forall_mem_supportWindow`).

Daubechies.card_le_of_forall_mem_support.name: Daubechies.card_le_of_forall_mem_supportWindow
Daubechies.card_le_of_forall_mem_support.docstring:
**Bounded overlap of the support windows**: every point `x` lies in at most `⌈b - a⌉ + 1`
of the windows `{x : 2^j x - k ∈ [a, b]}`, `k ∈ ℤ`, of one level `j`: such `k` satisfy
`⌈2^j x - b⌉ ≤ k ≤ ⌊2^j x - a⌋` (`Daubechies.mem_Icc_ceil_floor`,
`Daubechies.card_Icc_ceil_floor_le`).

Daubechies.card_Icc_sub_two_mul_sub_two.name: Daubechies.card_Icc_sub_two_mul_sub_two
Daubechies.card_Icc_sub_two_mul_sub_two.docstring:
The number of positions meeting a cell: `[k - (2N - 2), k]` contains `2N - 1` integers, for
`N ≥ 1`.

Daubechies.card_Icc_ceil_floor_le_two_mu.name: Daubechies.card_Icc_ceil_floor_le_two_mul
Daubechies.card_Icc_ceil_floor_le_two_mu.docstring:
**Counting the contributing positions**: for `N ≥ 1` and every `t ∈ ℝ`, the interval
`[⌈t - (2N - 1)⌉, ⌊t⌋]` contains at most `2N` integers (`Daubechies.card_Icc_ceil_floor_le`).

Daubechies.card_Icc_ceil_floor_le.name: Daubechies.card_Icc_ceil_floor_le
Daubechies.card_Icc_ceil_floor_le.docstring:
**Counting integers in an interval of length `b - a`**: the integers `k` with
`⌈t - b⌉ ≤ k ≤ ⌊t - a⌋` number at most `⌈b - a⌉ + 1`, for all real `t`, `a`, `b`.

Daubechies.approxError_daubechiesScheme_.name: Daubechies.approxError_daubechiesScheme_le_daubechiesJacksonConst_mul
Daubechies.approxError_daubechiesScheme_.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality for the Daubechies scheme, with its constant**: for `N ≥ 2`,
`1 ≤ p < ∞`, every `f ∈ L_p(ℝ)` and every level `j`, the error of best approximation from the
scaling space `V_j` (the approximants of complexity `2^j`,
`Daubechies.mem_daubechiesScheme_two_pow`) satisfies `E_{2^j}(f)_p ≤ C_J ω_N(f, 2^(-j))_p` with
`C_J = daubechiesJacksonConst m p`. For `f` with a bounded continuous representative, `P_j f ∈ V_j`
gives `E_{2^j}(f)_p ≤ ‖f - P_j f‖_p` (`Daubechies.enorm_sub_daubechiesProj_le_of_continuous`); these
`f` are dense in `L_p` (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Lp.boundedContinuousFunction_dense`), and both
sides are controlled by `‖f‖_p` (`Rd.lpModulus_add_le`, `Rd.lpModulus_le`), so the bound extends to
all of `L_p` (`ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_of_dense`).

Daubechies.annulus_subset_Icc.name: Daubechies.annulus_subset_Icc
Daubechies.annulus_subset_Icc.docstring: The annulus `A_n` lies in the interval `[-2^n/2, 2^n/2]`.

Daubechies.annulus.name: Daubechies.annulus
Daubechies.annulus.docstring:
**The dyadic annulus** `A_n = {ξ ∈ ℝ : 2^n/4 < |ξ| ≤ 2^n/2}` for `n ∈ ℕ`. The annuli
`A_0, A_1, …` cover `{|ξ| > 1/4}` (`Daubechies.exists_mem_annulus`).

Daubechies.aestronglyMeasurable_scaledFu.name: Daubechies.aestronglyMeasurable_scaledFun
Daubechies.aestronglyMeasurable_scaledFu.docstring:
The generators `g_{j,k}` of an a.e. strongly measurable `g` are a.e. strongly measurable
(`Daubechies.aestronglyMeasurable_comp_two_pow_mul_sub`).

Daubechies.aestronglyMeasurable_daubechi.name: Daubechies.aestronglyMeasurable_daubechiesExpand
Daubechies.aestronglyMeasurable_daubechi.docstring:
**Expansions are a.e. strongly measurable** for every a.e. strongly measurable `g` and all
coefficients `c`: a countable sum of a.e. strongly measurable functions (Mathlib's
`MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable.tsum`).

Daubechies.aestronglyMeasurable_comp_two.name: Daubechies.aestronglyMeasurable_comp_two_pow_mul_sub
Daubechies.aestronglyMeasurable_comp_two.docstring:
**Dilation and translation preserve measurability**: for every a.e. strongly measurable
`F : ℝ → ℂ`, `j ∈ ℕ` and `t ∈ ℝ`, the function `x ↦ F(2^j x - t)` is a.e. strongly measurable
(`Daubechies.aestronglyMeasurable_comp_sub_map`).

Daubechies.aestronglyMeasurable_comp_sub.name: Daubechies.aestronglyMeasurable_comp_sub_map
Daubechies.aestronglyMeasurable_comp_sub.docstring:
For every a.e. strongly measurable `F : ℝ → ℂ`, `j ∈ ℕ` and `t ∈ ℝ`, the translate
`u ↦ F(u - t)` is a.e. strongly measurable for the image of Lebesgue measure under `x ↦ 2^j x`.
That image is `2^(-j)` times Lebesgue measure (Mathlib's `Real.map_volume_mul_left`), and
translations preserve Lebesgue measure.

Daubechies.add_le_daubechiesJacksonConst.name: Daubechies.add_le_daubechiesJacksonConst_mul
Daubechies.add_le_daubechiesJacksonConst.docstring:
**Combining the two bounds of Jackson's inequality**: for all `A, B, ω ∈ [0, ∞]` and every
level `j`, if `A ≤ ω` and `B ≤ 2^N N^N 2^(jN) ω`, then
`(1 + C) A + C_S 2^(-jN) B ≤ C_J ω` with `C = projConst m p`, `C_S = smoothJacksonConst m p` and
`C_J = daubechiesJacksonConst m p`: the factors `2^(-jN)` and `2^(jN)` cancel.

Daubechies.abs_transferOp_le.name: Daubechies.abs_transferOp_le
Daubechies.abs_transferOp_le.docstring:
**The crude bound**: if `|g(x)| ≤ B` for every `x`, then `|(T g)(ξ)| ≤ 2 C(2N - 1, N) B` for
every `ξ`, since `0 ≤ P ≤ C(2N - 1, N)` (`Daubechies.daubFun_le_choose`).

Daubechies.abs_sub_le_of_mem_supportWind.name: Daubechies.abs_sub_le_of_mem_supportWindow
Daubechies.abs_sub_le_of_mem_supportWind.docstring:
**Points of one support window are close**: if `x` and `y` both lie in the support window
`{t : 2^j t - k ∈ [a, b]}`, then `|y - x| ≤ (b - a)/2^j`.

Daubechies.abs_sinc_le_inv_abs.name: Daubechies.abs_sinc_le_inv_abs
Daubechies.abs_sinc_le_inv_abs.docstring:
`|sinc x| ≤ 1/|x|` for `x ≠ 0`, since `sinc x = sin x / x` and `|sin x| ≤ 1`. Mathlib's
`Real.sinc_le_inv_abs` is the one-sided bound `sinc x ≤ 1/|x|`.

Daubechies.abs_iterate_transferOp_le.name: Daubechies.abs_iterate_transferOp_le
Daubechies.abs_iterate_transferOp_le.docstring:
If `|g(x)| ≤ B` for every `x`, then `|(T^n g)(ξ)| ≤ (2 C(2N - 1, N))^n B` for every `n` and
`ξ`, by induction from `Daubechies.abs_transferOp_le`.

Daubechies.X_add_one_pow_dvd_maskPoly.name: Daubechies.X_add_one_pow_dvd_maskPoly
Daubechies.X_add_one_pow_dvd_maskPoly.docstring:
The mask polynomial is divisible by `(z + 1)^N`: `m(z) = (z + 1)^N · 2^(-N) L(z)`. This is the
source of the sum rules of the filter coefficients.

Daubechies.TransferGrowth.setIntegral_pr.name: Daubechies.TransferGrowth.setIntegral_prod_daubFun_le
Daubechies.TransferGrowth.setIntegral_pr.docstring:
Under a growth bound `T^n 1 ≤ C λ^n`, the integral of `∏_{j<n} P(ξ/2^(j+1))` over every set
`s ⊆ [-2^n/2, 2^n/2]` is at most `C λ^n`: the integrand is nonnegative, so the integral over `s`
is at most the integral over the whole interval, which is at most `C λ^n`
(`Daubechies.TransferGrowth.integral_prod_daubFun_le`).

Daubechies.TransferGrowth.integral_prod_.name: Daubechies.TransferGrowth.integral_prod_daubFun_le
Daubechies.TransferGrowth.integral_prod_.docstring:
Under a growth bound `T^n 1 ≤ C λ^n`, the dyadic products satisfy
`∫_{-2^n/2}^{2^n/2} ∏_{j<n} P(ξ/2^(j+1)) dξ ≤ C λ^n` (`Daubechies.integral_prod_daubFun`).

Daubechies.TransferGrowth.integral_itera.name: Daubechies.TransferGrowth.integral_iterate_transferOp_one_le
Daubechies.TransferGrowth.integral_itera.docstring:
Under a growth bound `T^n 1 ≤ C λ^n`, the integral of `T^n 1` over one period is at most
`C λ^n`.

Daubechies.TransferGrowth.name: Daubechies.TransferGrowth
Daubechies.TransferGrowth.docstring:
**A growth bound for the transfer operator** of order `N`, with rate `λ` (the argument `lam`)
and constant `C`: `λ > 0`, and `(T^n 1)(ξ) ≤ C λ^n` for every `n ∈ ℕ` and every `ξ ∈ ℝ`. Such a
bound controls the decay of the symbol product `Φ` of a Daubechies mask of order `N`:
`∫ (1 + |ξ|)^(2s) |Φ(ξ)|² dξ < ∞` for `s < N - log₄ λ`. It is a hypothesis; it is proved with
`λ = 4` for `N = 2`, `λ = 9` for `N = 3` (`Daubechies.transferGrowth_two`,
`Daubechies.transferGrowth_three`) and with a crude rate for every `N`
(`Daubechies.transferGrowth_crude`).

Daubechies.Mask.one_le.name: Daubechies.Mask.one_le
Daubechies.Mask.one_le.docstring: Every mask has order `N ≥ 1`: the degree of `L` is a natural number `< N`.

Daubechies.Mask.name: Daubechies.Mask
Daubechies.Mask.docstring:
**A Daubechies mask of order `N`**, given by its polynomial factor: a real polynomial `L` of
degree `< N` with `L(1) = 1` and `|L(e^(-2πiξ))|² = P(ξ) = P_N(sin²(πξ))` for every `ξ ∈ ℝ`
(`Daubechies.daubFun`). The mask polynomial is `m(z) = ((1 + z)/2)^N L(z)`
(`Daubechies.maskPoly`). Every mask has order `N ≥ 1` (`Daubechies.Mask.one_le`).

Daubechies.Ico_subset_window.name: Daubechies.Ico_subset_window
Daubechies.Ico_subset_window.docstring:
**A cell lies in its window**: for `N ≥ 1`, the dyadic cell `[k/2^j, (k + 1)/2^j)` lies in
the window `[(k - (2N - 2))/2^j, (k + 2N - 1)/2^j]`.

Daubechies.BernsteinBound.name: Daubechies.BernsteinBound
Daubechies.BernsteinBound.docstring:
**A Bernstein bound of order `θ`** for the scaling function `φ` in `L_p`, with differences
of order `r`: there is a finite constant `K` with `ω_r(φ, t)_p ≤ K t^θ` for all `0 < t ≤ 1`.
It is a hypothesis on the mask; the regularity theorems for `φ` prove it
(`Daubechies.bernsteinBound_of_le_two`, `Daubechies.bernsteinBound_interp`), for instance for
`N = 2` and `N = 3` with `p ≤ 2` and for D4 with `p ≥ 2` (`Daubechies.bernsteinBound_order_two`,
`Daubechies.bernsteinBound_order_three`, `Daubechies.bernsteinBound_d4`), and a Bernstein bound
gives the inverse inequality of the Daubechies scheme (`Daubechies.inverse_daubechiesScheme`).

Cube.update_mem_listRegion_iff.name: Cube.update_mem_listRegion_iff
Cube.update_mem_listRegion_iff.docstring: The box region of a list does not depend on the coordinates outside the list.

Cube.unitVol_restrict_Icc_of_subset.name: Cube.unitVol_restrict_Icc_of_subset
Cube.unitVol_restrict_Icc_of_subset.docstring:
On `[a, b] ⊆ [0, 1]`, Lebesgue measure on `[0, 1]` restricted to `[a, b]` is Lebesgue measure
on `[a, b]`.

Cube.toNat_lt_of_mem_qiIdx.name: Cube.toNat_lt_of_mem_qiIdx
Cube.toNat_lt_of_mem_qiIdx.docstring:
The interval `J(n) = I_{k, max(n, 0)}` of a coefficient `λ_n`, `-r < n < 2^k`, lies in
`[0, 1)`.

Cube.sub_cubeSteklovSmooth_eq.name: Cube.sub_cubeSteklovSmooth_eq
Cube.sub_cubeSteklovSmooth_eq.docstring:
**`f - S^{(i)}_δ f` is an averaged coordinate difference**:
`f(x) - S^{(i)}_δ f(x) = (-1)^r avg_h Δ^r_{h e_i} f(x)`, the average over the steps only.

Cube.splineSubmodule.name: Cube.splineSubmodule
Cube.splineSubmodule.docstring:
The **splines** of order `r` and level `j` on `[0, 1)`, as a subspace of the functions on
`ℝ`.

Cube.splineExponent_nonneg.name: Cube.splineExponent_nonneg
Cube.splineExponent_nonneg.docstring: The gain exponents of splines are nonnegative.

Cube.splineExponent.name: Cube.splineExponent
Cube.splineExponent.docstring:
The gain exponent of a difference of order `m` of splines of order `r`: `m` for `m < r`,
`r - 1 + 1/p` for `m = r`.

Cube.slice_update.name: Cube.slice_update
Cube.slice_update.docstring: A slice does not depend on the coordinate `i` of the point.

Cube.slice_sub_slicewise.name: Cube.slice_sub_slicewise
Cube.slice_sub_slicewise.docstring: The slices of `f - T^{(i)} f` in coordinate `i` are the errors of `T` on the slices of `f`.

Cube.slice_reflectCoord.name: Cube.slice_reflectCoord
Cube.slice_reflectCoord.docstring: The slice of a reflected function is the reflected slice.

Cube.slice_cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv.name: Cube.slice_cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv
Cube.slice_cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv.docstring: The slices of the derivative are the derivatives of the smoothed slices.

Cube.slice_cubeSteklovSmooth.name: Cube.slice_cubeSteklovSmooth
Cube.slice_cubeSteklovSmooth.docstring: The slices of the smoothing are the smoothings of the slices.

Cube.slice_cubeMixedDiff_mem.name: Cube.slice_cubeMixedDiff_mem
Cube.slice_cubeMixedDiff_mem.docstring:
**Slices of mixed differences stay in a subspace**: if every slice of `f` in coordinate `i`
lies in a subspace `V` of functions of one variable, so does every slice in coordinate `i` of a
mixed difference along a list of coordinates `≠ i`.

Cube.slice_cubeDiff_of_ne.name: Cube.slice_cubeDiff_of_ne
Cube.slice_cubeDiff_of_ne.docstring:
**Slices of coordinate differences in other coordinates**: for `c ≠ i`, the slice in
coordinate `i` of `Δ^m_{t e_c} G` is a combination of slices of `G` in coordinate `i`.

Cube.slice_cubeDiff.name: Cube.slice_cubeDiff
Cube.slice_cubeDiff.docstring: The slice of a coordinate difference in its own coordinate is the difference of the slice.

Cube.slice.name: Cube.slice
Cube.slice.docstring:
The **slice** of `f` through `x` in coordinate `i`: `t ↦ f(x₁, …, t, …, x_d)`, with `t` in
place `i`.

Cube.regionVol.name: Cube.regionVol
Cube.regionVol.docstring: The cube measure restricted to the region `{x ∈ Q : x_i ∈ [a, b]}`.

Cube.reflectCoord.name: Cube.reflectCoord
Cube.reflectCoord.docstring: The **reflection in coordinate `i`**, `x ↦ x` with `x_i` replaced by `1 - x_i`.

Cube.qiKernel_kernelCoef.name: Cube.qiKernel_kernelCoef
Cube.qiKernel_kernelCoef.docstring:
The coefficients of the kernel operator are the quasi-interpolant coefficients, for `g`
integrable on `[0, 1]`.

Cube.qiKernel_apply.name: Cube.qiKernel_apply
Cube.qiKernel_apply.docstring:
**The kernel operator is the quasi-interpolant**: `(qiKernel hr k).apply g = Q_k g` for `g`
integrable on `[0, 1]`.

Cube.qiKernel.name: Cube.qiKernel
Cube.qiKernel.docstring:
The **quasi-interpolant of level `k` as a kernel operator**, indexed by the B-splines
`-r < n < 2^k`: the kernel `κ_n = ∑_i β_{n,i} κ_{J(n),i}` combines the kernels of the local
projection on `J(n)` (`Cube.ppKernel`), and `φ_n` is the B-spline `N_r(2^k x - n)` on `[0, 1)`.

Cube.ppSubmodule.name: Cube.ppSubmodule
Cube.ppSubmodule.docstring:
The **piecewise polynomials** of level `j` and degree `< r` on `[0, 1)`, as a subspace of the
functions on `ℝ`.

Cube.ppKernel_rangeFn_eq_sum.name: Cube.ppKernel_rangeFn_eq_sum
Cube.ppKernel_rangeFn_eq_sum.docstring:
**Refinement**: the functions of level `k` are combinations of those of level `k + 1`,
`φ^{(k)}_j = P_{k+1} φ^{(k)}_j = ∑_{j'} (∫_0^1 φ^{(k)}_j κ^{(k+1)}_{j'}) φ^{(k+1)}_{j'}`.

Cube.ppKernel_rangeFn_eq_ppFun.name: Cube.ppKernel_rangeFn_eq_ppFun
Cube.ppKernel_rangeFn_eq_ppFun.docstring:
The function `φ_{n,l}` of level `k` is the piecewise polynomial with the single piece
`d_l(2^k t - n)` on `I_{k,n}`.

Cube.ppKernel_kernelCoef.name: Cube.ppKernel_kernelCoef
Cube.ppKernel_kernelCoef.docstring: The coefficients of the kernel operator are the local coefficients.

Cube.ppKernel_apply_ppFun.name: Cube.ppKernel_apply_ppFun
Cube.ppKernel_apply_ppFun.docstring: The local projection reproduces the piecewise polynomials of its level.

Cube.ppKernel_apply.name: Cube.ppKernel_apply
Cube.ppKernel_apply.docstring: **The kernel operator is the local projection**: `(ppKernel r k).apply g = P_k g`.

Cube.ppKernel.name: Cube.ppKernel
Cube.ppKernel.docstring:
The **local projection onto piecewise polynomials of level `k`** as a kernel operator, indexed
by `(n, l)`: `κ_{n,l}(s) = 1_{I_{k,n}}(s) 2^k b_l(2^k s - n)`, `φ_{n,l}(t) = 1_{I_{k,n}}(t) d_l(2^k t - n)`.

Cube.ppExponent_nonneg.name: Cube.ppExponent_nonneg
Cube.ppExponent_nonneg.docstring: The gain exponents of piecewise polynomials are nonnegative.

Cube.ppExponent.name: Cube.ppExponent
Cube.ppExponent.docstring:
The gain exponent of a difference of order `m` of piecewise polynomials: `0` for `m = 0`,
`1/p` otherwise.

Cube.norm_indicator_polyFun_le.name: Cube.norm_indicator_polyFun_le
Cube.norm_indicator_polyFun_le.docstring:
The polynomials `b_l(2^k s - n)` and `d_l(2^k t - n)` on `I_{k,n}` are bounded by the bound of the
bases on `[0, 1]`.

Cube.mem_cubeSplineScheme_two_pow.name: Cube.mem_cubeSplineScheme_two_pow
Cube.mem_cubeSplineScheme_two_pow.docstring: The approximants of complexity `2^k` are the splines of level `k`.

Cube.mem_cubePPScheme_two_pow.name: Cube.mem_cubePPScheme_two_pow
Cube.mem_cubePPScheme_two_pow.docstring: The approximants of complexity `2^k` are the piecewise polynomials of level `k`.

Cube.measurable_slice_uncurry.name: Cube.measurable_slice_uncurry
Cube.measurable_slice_uncurry.docstring: The slices of a measurable function are jointly measurable in the point and the variable.

Cube.measurable_slice.name: Cube.measurable_slice
Cube.measurable_slice.docstring: The slices of a measurable function are measurable.

Cube.measurable_eLpNorm_slice.name: Cube.measurable_eLpNorm_slice
Cube.measurable_eLpNorm_slice.docstring: The `L_p` norms of the slices of a measurable function are measurable in the point.

Cube.measurable_cubeMixedDiff.name: Cube.measurable_cubeMixedDiff
Cube.measurable_cubeMixedDiff.docstring: Mixed differences of measurable functions are measurable.

Cube.measurable_cubeDiff.name: Cube.measurable_cubeDiff
Cube.measurable_cubeDiff.docstring: Coordinate differences of measurable functions are measurable.

Cube.lpIsoModulus_le_of_exponents.name: Cube.lpIsoModulus_le_of_exponents
Cube.lpIsoModulus_le_of_exponents.docstring:
**The isotropic inverse inequality from estimates in one variable**: let `V` be a subspace of
functions of one variable with `‖Δ_t^m u‖_{L_p(J(m,t))} ≤ C (2^j |t|)^{θ_m} ‖u‖_{L_p[0,1]}` for
`u ∈ V`, `m ≤ r` and `|t| ≤ 2^(-j)`, where `θ_m ≥ 0` and `0 ≤ Θ ≤ ∑_i θ_{m_i}` whenever
`∑_i m_i = r`. If `a ∈ L_p(Q)`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, is represented by a measurable `g` whose slices all
lie in `V`, then for every `k`
`ω_r(a, 2^(-k))_p ≤ (d^r C^d + 2^r) 2^(-(k-j)Θ) ‖a‖_p`, with `k - j` truncated
at `0` (`Cube.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_of_exponents` for `k ≥ j`, `Cube.isoModulus_le` for
`k < j`).

Cube.lpIsoModulus_le.name: Cube.lpIsoModulus_le
Cube.lpIsoModulus_le.docstring: `ω_r(f, t)_p ≤ 2^r ‖f‖_p` in `L_p(Q)`, for the isotropic modulus.

Cube.lpIsoModulus_add_le.name: Cube.lpIsoModulus_add_le
Cube.lpIsoModulus_add_le.docstring: The isotropic modulus on `L_p(Q)` is subadditive.

Cube.lpIsoModulus.name: Cube.lpIsoModulus
Cube.lpIsoModulus.docstring: The isotropic modulus of an element of `L_p(Q)` at the dyadic scale `2^(-k)`.

Cube.lpCubeModulus_anti.name: Cube.lpCubeModulus_anti
Cube.lpCubeModulus_anti.docstring: The modulus at the dyadic scales decreases with the level.

Cube.lpCubeModulus.name: Cube.lpCubeModulus
Cube.lpCubeModulus.docstring:
The modulus of an element of `L_p(Q)` at the dyadic scale `2^(-k)`,
`ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p` on the cube.

Cube.listRegion_nil.name: Cube.listRegion_nil
Cube.listRegion_nil.docstring: The box region of the empty list is everything.

Cube.listRegion.name: Cube.listRegion
Cube.listRegion.docstring:
The **box region** of a mixed difference along a list: the points `x` with
`x_i + m_i h_i ∈ [0, 1]` for the coordinates `i` of the list.

Cube.lintegral_region_eq_slice.name: Cube.lintegral_region_eq_slice
Cube.lintegral_region_eq_slice.docstring:
**Integrating out one coordinate over a region** `{x ∈ Q : x_i ∈ S}`:
`∫_{x_i ∈ S} G = ∫_Q (∫_{S ∩ [0,1]} G(update x i t) dt) dx`, the case `R = ℝ^d` of
`Cube.lintegral_inter_eq_slice`.

Cube.lintegral_inter_eq_slice.name: Cube.lintegral_inter_eq_slice
Cube.lintegral_inter_eq_slice.docstring:
**Integrating out one coordinate under a constraint that does not depend on it**: if the
measurable set `R` does not depend on the coordinate `i`, then
`∫_{R ∩ {x_i ∈ S}} G = ∫_R (∫_{S ∩ [0,1]} G(x with t in place i) dt) dx`.

Cube.lintegral_cubeVol_eq_slice.name: Cube.lintegral_cubeVol_eq_slice
Cube.lintegral_cubeVol_eq_slice.docstring:
**Integrating out one coordinate**: for measurable `G ≥ 0` on the cube and every
coordinate `i`, `∫_Q G = ∫_Q (∫_0^1 G(update x i t) dt) dx`; the inner integral does not depend
on `x_i`.

Cube.letterCount_le.name: Cube.letterCount_le
Cube.letterCount_le.docstring: The multiplicities of a word are at most its length.

Cube.le_sum_splineExponent.name: Cube.le_sum_splineExponent
Cube.le_sum_splineExponent.docstring:
**Every word of order `r` gains `r - 1 + 1/p` for splines of order `r`**: either one
coordinate carries all `r` differences, or all orders are `< r` and add up to `r`.

Cube.le_sum_ppExponent.name: Cube.le_sum_ppExponent
Cube.le_sum_ppExponent.docstring:
**Every word of positive order gains `1/p` for piecewise polynomials**: if `∑_i m_i = r ≥ 1`,
some `m_i ≥ 1`.

Cube.isoRegion_inter_cubeSet.name: Cube.isoRegion_inter_cubeSet
Cube.isoRegion_inter_cubeSet.docstring:
**The isotropic region on the cube is a step set**: `{x ∈ Q : x + rh ∈ Q}` is the set `Q_{rh}`
of the points `x` with `x, x + h, …, x + rh ∈ Q` (`Rd.diffStepSet`).

Cube.isoRegion.name: Cube.isoRegion
Cube.isoRegion.docstring:
The **region of the isotropic difference** of order `r` and step `h`: the points `x` with
`x + rh ∈ [0, 1]^d`. Together with `x ∈ Q` (the cube measure lives on `Q`) all points `x + kh`,
`k ≤ r`, lie in `Q`.

Cube.isoModulus_eq_iSup.name: Cube.isoModulus_eq_iSup
Cube.isoModulus_eq_iSup.docstring:
**The isotropic modulus through the isotropic regions**:
`ω_r(f, t)_p = sup_{‖h‖_∞ ≤ t} ‖Δ_h^r f‖_{L_p({x ∈ Q : x + rh ∈ Q})}`.

Cube.isoModulus_congr_ae.name: Cube.isoModulus_congr_ae
Cube.isoModulus_congr_ae.docstring:
**The isotropic modulus depends only on the class in `L_p(Q)`** (`Rd.modulusOn_congr_ae`,
with Mathlib's `ae_eq_restrict_iff_indicator_ae_eq`).

Cube.isoModulus.name: Cube.isoModulus
Cube.isoModulus.docstring:
The **isotropic modulus of smoothness** on the cube, the modulus on the set `Q` of
`Rd.modulusOn`: `ω_r(f, t)_p = sup_{‖h‖_∞ ≤ t} ‖Δ_h^r(f, ·, Q)‖_p`.

Cube.isCubeSpline_zero_fun.name: Cube.isCubeSpline_zero_fun
Cube.isCubeSpline_zero_fun.docstring: The zero function is a spline on the cube.

Cube.isCubeSpline_of_isForm.name: Cube.isCubeSpline_of_isForm
Cube.isCubeSpline_of_isForm.docstring:
**The forms of the quasi-interpolant are splines on the cube**: a bounded measurable function
with the form of `Q_k` in every coordinate has slices that are combinations of B-splines.

Cube.isCubeSpline_cubeQI.name: Cube.isCubeSpline_cubeQI
Cube.isCubeSpline_cubeQI.docstring:
**The tensor quasi-interpolant is a spline on the cube**: it has the form of `Q_k` in every
coordinate, so its slices are combinations of B-splines.

Cube.isCubePP_zero.name: Cube.isCubePP_zero
Cube.isCubePP_zero.docstring: The zero function is a piecewise polynomial.

Cube.isCubePP_cubeProj.name: Cube.isCubePP_cubeProj
Cube.isCubePP_cubeProj.docstring:
The tensor projection of a bounded measurable function is a piecewise polynomial on the
cube.

Cube.higherDiff_single.name: Cube.higherDiff_single
Cube.higherDiff_single.docstring:
**Isotropic differences in a coordinate direction** are the coordinate differences: the
isotropic difference with step `t e_i` is the difference `Cube.cubeDiff r t i` in coordinate `i`.

Cube.higherDiff_eq_sum.name: Cube.higherDiff_eq_sum
Cube.higherDiff_eq_sum.docstring:
**The isotropic difference as a sum of mixed coordinate differences**:
`Δ_h^r f(x) = ∑_α M_{m(α)} f(x + s_α)`, summed over the words `α : Fin r → Fin d`, with the
multiplicities `m_i(α)` and the shifts `s_α`.

Cube.exists_right_cubeSmoothing.name: Cube.exists_right_cubeSmoothing
Cube.exists_right_cubeSmoothing.docstring:
**Smoothing on a right region**: the same as `Cube.exists_left_cubeSmoothing` on
`{x_i ≥ 1 - w}`, by the reflection in coordinate `i`.

Cube.exists_left_cubeSmoothing.name: Cube.exists_left_cubeSmoothing
Cube.exists_left_cubeSmoothing.docstring:
**Smoothing on a left region**: for continuous `f`, `r ≥ 1`, a scale `L > 0` and
`w + L ≤ 1`, the smoothing `G = S^{(i)}_δ f`, `δ = L/r²`, and `D = ∂_i^r G` satisfy
`‖f - G‖_{L_p({x_i ≤ w})} ≤ ω_r^{(i)}(f, L)_p` and
`‖D‖_{L_p({x_i ≤ w})} ≤ L^(-r) 2^r r^(2r) ω_r^{(i)}(f, L)_p`, and every slice of `G` has Taylor
polynomials `‖G - T‖_{L_p[u,v]} ≤ (v - u)^r ‖D‖_{L_p[u,v]}` on the slice.

Cube.exists_inverse_cubeSplineScheme_iso.name: Cube.exists_inverse_cubeSplineScheme_iso
Cube.exists_inverse_cubeSplineScheme_iso.docstring:
**The inverse inequality for tensor splines on the cube with the isotropic modulus**, of
order `θ = r - 1 + 1/p`.

Cube.exists_inverse_cubePPScheme_iso.name: Cube.exists_inverse_cubePPScheme_iso
Cube.exists_inverse_cubePPScheme_iso.docstring:
**The inverse inequality for piecewise polynomials on the cube with the isotropic
modulus**, of order `θ = 1/p`.

Cube.exists_eLpNorm_sub_slicewise_qiKern.name: Cube.exists_eLpNorm_sub_slicewise_qiKernel_le
Cube.exists_eLpNorm_sub_slicewise_qiKern.docstring:
**Jackson's estimate for splines in one coordinate**: there is `B < ∞` with
`‖f - Q_k^{(i)} f‖_{L_p(Q)} ≤ B ω_r^{(i)}(f, 2^(-k))_p` for every continuous `f`, every
coordinate `i` and every `k ≥ r + 2`.

Cube.exists_eLpNorm_sub_slicewise_ppKern.name: Cube.exists_eLpNorm_sub_slicewise_ppKernel_zero_le
Cube.exists_eLpNorm_sub_slicewise_ppKern.docstring:
**Whitney's estimate in one coordinate**: for `0 < t ≤ 1/3` there is `W < ∞` with
`‖f - P_0^{(i)} f‖_{L_p(Q)} ≤ W ω_r^{(i)}(f, t)_p` for every continuous `f` and every
coordinate `i`, where `P_0` is the projection onto the polynomials of degree `< r` in one
variable. On every slice, the Taylor polynomials of the smoothings on `{x_i ≤ 1 - t}` and on
`{x_i ≥ t}` are glued as in Whitney's inequality on `[0, 1]`
(`Cube.exists_eLpNorm_sub_ppKernel_zero_apply_le`).

Cube.exists_eLpNorm_sub_ppKernel_zero_ap.name: Cube.exists_eLpNorm_sub_ppKernel_zero_apply_le
Cube.exists_eLpNorm_sub_ppKernel_zero_ap.docstring:
**Whitney's estimate for the projection of level `0`**: there is `K < ∞` such that for `u`
integrable on `[0, 1]` and polynomials `T₁, T₂` of degree `< r`,
`‖u - P_0 u‖_{L_p[0,1]} ≤ K (‖u - T₁‖_{L_p[0,2/3]} + ‖u - T₂‖_{L_p[1/3,1]})`: the projection is
quasi-optimal (`Cube.eLpNorm_sub_ppKernel_apply_le`), and `T₁` and `T₂` are glued as in Whitney's
inequality (`Interval.exists_eLpNorm_sub_polyFun_le_glue`).

Cube.exists_eLpNorm_qiKernel_apply_le.name: Cube.exists_eLpNorm_qiKernel_apply_le
Cube.exists_eLpNorm_qiKernel_apply_le.docstring:
**The quasi-interpolant is bounded on `L_p[0, 1]`** as a kernel operator, uniformly in the
level: there is `C < ∞` with `‖Q_k u‖_{L_p[0,1]} ≤ C ‖u‖_{L_p[0,1]}` for all `k` and all
measurable `u`.

Cube.exists_eLpNorm_higherDiff_stepRegio.name: Cube.exists_eLpNorm_higherDiff_stepRegion_spline_le
Cube.exists_eLpNorm_higherDiff_stepRegio.docstring:
**Splines, steps of either sign**: there is `C` such that for every level `j`, every spline
`u` of order `r` and level `j`, every order `m ≤ r` and `|t| ≤ 2^(-j)`,
`‖Δ_t^m u‖_{L_p(J(m,t))} ≤ C (2^j |t|)^{θ_m} ‖u‖_p` with the exponent
`θ_m = Cube.splineExponent p r m`.

Cube.exists_eLpNorm_higherDiff_stepRegio.name: Cube.exists_eLpNorm_higherDiff_stepRegion_pp_le
Cube.exists_eLpNorm_higherDiff_stepRegio.docstring:
**Piecewise polynomials, steps of either sign**: there is `C` such that for every level `j`,
every piecewise polynomial `u` of level `j` and degree `< r`, every order `m ≤ r` and
`|t| ≤ 2^(-j)`, `‖Δ_t^m u‖_{L_p(J(m,t))} ≤ C (2^j |t|)^{θ_m} ‖u‖_p` with the exponent
`θ_m = Cube.ppExponent p m`.

Cube.exists_approxError_cubeSplineScheme.name: Cube.exists_approxError_cubeSplineScheme_le
Cube.exists_approxError_cubeSplineScheme.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality for tensor splines on the cube**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞` and `r ≥ 1` there is
`C_J < ∞` with `E_{2^k}(f)_p ≤ C_J ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p` for every `f ∈ L_p(Q)` and every `k ≥ 0`:
the tensor quasi-interpolant for `k ≥ r + 2`, Whitney's inequality for `k ≤ r + 1`.

Cube.exists_approxError_cubePPScheme_one.name: Cube.exists_approxError_cubePPScheme_one_le
Cube.exists_approxError_cubePPScheme_one.docstring:
**Whitney's inequality on the cube**: for `m ≥ 2` there is `W < ∞` with
`E_1(f)_p ≤ W ω_r(f, 2^(-m))_p` for every `f ∈ L_p(Q)`; the approximants of complexity `1` are the
polynomials of degree `< r` in each variable.

Cube.exists_approxError_cubePPScheme_le.name: Cube.exists_approxError_cubePPScheme_le
Cube.exists_approxError_cubePPScheme_le.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality for piecewise polynomials on the cube at every level**: for
`1 ≤ p < ∞` and `r ≥ 1` there is `C_J < ∞` with `E_{2^k}(f)_p ≤ C_J ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p` for every
`f ∈ L_p(Q)` and every `k ≥ 0`; level `0` is Whitney's inequality.

Cube.eLpNorm_sub_slicewise_ppKernel_le.name: Cube.eLpNorm_sub_slicewise_ppKernel_le
Cube.eLpNorm_sub_slicewise_ppKernel_le.docstring:
**Jackson's estimate in one coordinate**: for continuous `f`, `r ≥ 1` and `k ≥ 0`,
`‖f - P_{k+1}^{(i)} f‖_{L_p(Q)} ≤ (1 + C_r) 2 (1 + 2^r r^(2r)) ω_r^{(i)}(f, 2^(-(k+1)))_p`.

Cube.eLpNorm_sub_slicewise_le_of_smoothi.name: Cube.eLpNorm_sub_slicewise_le_of_smoothing
Cube.eLpNorm_sub_slicewise_le_of_smoothi.docstring:
**Jackson's estimate in one coordinate from the smoothings**: let `f` be continuous, `r ≥ 1`,
`L > 0` and `w + L ≤ 1`. Suppose that in one variable the error of `T` on every continuous `u` is
bounded through any functions `g₁, g₂` that are approximated on every interval `[a, b]` by
polynomials of degree `< r` up to `(b - a)^r ‖D_ν‖_{L_p[a,b]}`:
`‖u - T u‖_{L_p[0,1]} ≤ c ((‖u - g₁‖_{L_p[0,w]} + M ‖D₁‖_{L_p[0,w]})`
`+ (‖u - g₂‖_{L_p[1-w,1]} + M ‖D₂‖_{L_p[1-w,1]}))`.
If `a + M b ≤ J ω` whenever `a ≤ ω` and `b ≤ L^(-r) 2^r r^(2r) ω`, then
`‖f - T^{(i)} f‖_{L_p(Q)} ≤ c (2 J) ω_r^{(i)}(f, L)_p`: apply the bound on every slice to the
smoothings of `f` in coordinate `i` (`Cube.exists_left_cubeSmoothing`,
`Cube.exists_right_cubeSmoothing`) and pass to the cube as in `Cube.cube_eLpNorm_le_of_slice_le`.
The constants `c, M, J` may be any elements of `[0, ∞]`.

Cube.eLpNorm_sub_ppKernel_apply_le.name: Cube.eLpNorm_sub_ppKernel_apply_le
Cube.eLpNorm_sub_ppKernel_apply_le.docstring:
**Lebesgue's inequality for the local projection**: for `u` integrable on `[0, 1]` and every
piecewise polynomial `S` of level `k` and degree `< r`,
`‖u - P_k u‖_{L_p[0,1]} ≤ (1 + C_r) ‖u - S‖_{L_p[0,1]}`. Since `P_k S = S`, the error is
`u - P_k u = (u - S) - P_k (u - S)`.

Cube.eLpNorm_sub_cubeSteklovSmooth_le_of.name: Cube.eLpNorm_sub_cubeSteklovSmooth_le_of_cubeDiff_le
Cube.eLpNorm_sub_cubeSteklovSmooth_le_of.docstring:
**The smoothing is close to `f`, for every measure**: let `f` be continuous, `r ∈ ℕ`,
`δ > 0`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `μ` an s-finite measure on `ℝ^d`, and let
`‖Δ^r_{h e_i} f‖_{L_p(μ)} ≤ B` for every step `0 ≤ h ≤ rδ`. Then
`‖f - S^{(i)}_δ f‖_{L_p(μ)} ≤ B`: the difference is `(-1)^r` times an average of these
coordinate differences (`Cube.sub_cubeSteklovSmooth_eq`), and Minkowski's inequality for averages
(`Interval.eLpNorm_avgStepIter_le`) bounds it by the largest of their norms.

Cube.eLpNorm_sub_cubeSteklovSmooth_le.name: Cube.eLpNorm_sub_cubeSteklovSmooth_le
Cube.eLpNorm_sub_cubeSteklovSmooth_le.docstring:
**The smoothing is close to `f`**: on `{x_i ≤ w}` with `w + r² δ ≤ 1`,
`‖f - S^{(i)}_δ f‖_p ≤ ω_r^{(i)}(f, rδ)_p` (`Cube.eLpNorm_sub_cubeSteklovSmooth_le_of_cubeDiff_le`
with `Cube.eLpNorm_cubeDiff_regionVol_le`).

Cube.eLpNorm_sub_cubeProj_le_of_coord.name: Cube.eLpNorm_sub_cubeProj_le_of_coord
Cube.eLpNorm_sub_cubeProj_le_of_coord.docstring:
**From one coordinate to all, for the tensor projection**: if
`‖f - P_k^{(i)} f‖_{L_p(Q)} ≤ B ω_r^{(i)}(f, t)_p` in every coordinate, then
`‖f - P_k^d f‖_{L_p(Q)} ≤ (1 + C_r)^d B ω_r(f, t)_p`.

Cube.eLpNorm_sub_cubeProj_le.name: Cube.eLpNorm_sub_cubeProj_le
Cube.eLpNorm_sub_cubeProj_le.docstring:
**Jackson's estimate for continuous functions on the cube**: for bounded continuous `f`,
`r ≥ 1` and `k ≥ 0`, the tensor projection satisfies
`‖f - P_{k+1}^d f‖_{L_p(Q)} ≤ (1 + C_r)^(d+1) 2 (1 + 2^r r^(2r)) ω_r(f, 2^(-(k+1)))_p`.

Cube.eLpNorm_shift_cubeMixedDiff_le.name: Cube.eLpNorm_shift_cubeMixedDiff_le
Cube.eLpNorm_shift_cubeMixedDiff_le.docstring:
**The translated terms**: on the isotropic region the translate of the mixed difference of
a word `α` by its shift `s_α` stays in the cube, and lands in the box of the mixed difference, so
`‖M f(· + s_α)‖_{L_p(Q_{rh})} ≤ ‖M f‖_{L_p(box)}`.

Cube.eLpNorm_rpow_region_eq_slice.name: Cube.eLpNorm_rpow_region_eq_slice
Cube.eLpNorm_rpow_region_eq_slice.docstring:
**`L_p` norms over a region through slices**: for measurable `f`, `0 < p < ∞`,
`‖f‖_{L_p({x_i ∈ S})}^p = ∫_Q ‖slice f x i‖_{L_p(S)}^p dx`.

Cube.eLpNorm_rpow_cubeDiff_eq_slice.name: Cube.eLpNorm_rpow_cubeDiff_eq_slice
Cube.eLpNorm_rpow_cubeDiff_eq_slice.docstring:
**Coordinate differences through slices**: for measurable `f`, `h ≥ 0` and `0 < p < ∞`,
`‖Δ^r_{h e_i} f‖_{L_p({x_i ≤ 1 - rh})}^p = ∫_Q ‖Δ_h^r (slice f x i)‖_{L_p[0, 1-rh]}^p dx`.

Cube.eLpNorm_regionVol_eq_slice.name: Cube.eLpNorm_regionVol_eq_slice
Cube.eLpNorm_regionVol_eq_slice.docstring:
**`L_p` norms over a region as mixed norms of slices**: for measurable `f`, `0 < p < ∞` and
`[a, b] ⊆ [0, 1]`, `‖f‖_{L_p({x_i ∈ [a, b]})} = ‖x ↦ ‖slice f x i‖_{L_p[a, b]}‖_{L_p(Q)}`
(`Cube.eLpNorm_inter_eq_slice`).

Cube.eLpNorm_ppKernel_apply_le.name: Cube.eLpNorm_ppKernel_apply_le
Cube.eLpNorm_ppKernel_apply_le.docstring: The kernel operator is bounded on `L_p[0, 1]` by the bound of the local projections.

Cube.eLpNorm_inter_le_of_slice_le.name: Cube.eLpNorm_inter_le_of_slice_le
Cube.eLpNorm_inter_le_of_slice_le.docstring:
**Bounds through slices**: let the measurable set `R` not depend on the coordinate `i`. For
measurable `F, G`, `0 < p < ∞`, measurable `S, S' ⊆ ℝ` and `C ∈ [0, ∞]`, if
`‖slice F x i‖_{L_p(S ∩ [0, 1])} ≤ C ‖slice G x i‖_{L_p(S' ∩ [0, 1])}` for every point `x`, then
`‖F‖_{L_p(R ∩ {x_i ∈ S})} ≤ C ‖G‖_{L_p(R ∩ {x_i ∈ S'})}` (`Cube.eLpNorm_inter_eq_slice`).

Cube.eLpNorm_inter_eq_slice.name: Cube.eLpNorm_inter_eq_slice
Cube.eLpNorm_inter_eq_slice.docstring:
**`L_p` norms as mixed norms of slices**: let the measurable set `R` not depend on the
coordinate `i`. For measurable `f` and `0 < p < ∞`,
`‖f‖_{L_p(R ∩ {x_i ∈ S})} = ‖x ↦ ‖slice f x i‖_{L_p(S ∩ [0, 1])}‖_{L_p(R)}`, by integrating out the
coordinate `i` in `|f|^p` (`Cube.lintegral_inter_eq_slice`).

Cube.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_sum.name: Cube.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_sum
Cube.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_sum.docstring:
**Isotropic differences of functions with slices in a class**: if the differences of order
`m ≤ r` of the functions in `V` with the steps `h_i` are bounded by `β(m, h_i)` on the step regions,
and every slice of `f` lies in `V`, then
`‖Δ_h^r f‖_{L_p(Q_{rh})} ≤ (∑_α ∏_i β(m_i(α), h_i)) ‖f‖_{L_p(Q)}`, summed over the words
`α : Fin r → Fin d`.

Cube.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_of_exponents.name: Cube.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_of_exponents
Cube.eLpNorm_higherDiff_le_of_exponents.docstring:
**Isotropic differences with gains in the coordinates**: let the differences of order
`m ≤ r` of the functions in `V` satisfy `‖Δ_t^m u‖_{L_p(J(m,t))} ≤ C (2^j |t|)^{θ_m} ‖u‖_p` for
`|t| ≤ 2^(-j)`, with `θ_m ≥ 0`, and let `Θ ≤ ∑_i θ_{m_i}` whenever `∑_i m_i = r`. Then for every
`f` with slices in `V` and `‖h‖_∞ ≤ 2^(-j)`,
`‖Δ_h^r f‖_{L_p(Q_{rh})} ≤ d^r C^d (2^j ‖h‖_∞)^Θ ‖f‖_{L_p(Q)}`.

Cube.eLpNorm_higherDiff_isoRegion_eq.name: Cube.eLpNorm_higherDiff_isoRegion_eq
Cube.eLpNorm_higherDiff_isoRegion_eq.docstring:
The isotropic difference on the cube is the restricted difference on the set `Q`:
`‖Δ_h^r f‖_{L_p(Q_{rh})} = ‖Δ_h^r(f, ·, Q)‖_p`.

Cube.eLpNorm_cubeVol_le_of_slice_le.name: Cube.eLpNorm_cubeVol_le_of_slice_le
Cube.eLpNorm_cubeVol_le_of_slice_le.docstring:
**Bounds through slices on the whole cube**: for measurable `F, G`, `0 < p < ∞` and
`C ∈ [0, ∞]`, if `‖slice F x i‖_{L_p[0,1]} ≤ C ‖slice G x i‖_{L_p[0,1]}` for every point `x`,
then `‖F‖_{L_p(Q)} ≤ C ‖G‖_{L_p(Q)}`.

Cube.eLpNorm_cubeVol_eq_slice.name: Cube.eLpNorm_cubeVol_eq_slice
Cube.eLpNorm_cubeVol_eq_slice.docstring:
**`L_p` norms on the cube as mixed norms of slices**: for measurable `f` and `0 < p < ∞`,
`‖f‖_{L_p(Q)} = ‖x ↦ ‖slice f x i‖_{L_p[0, 1]}‖_{L_p(Q)}` (`Cube.eLpNorm_inter_eq_slice`).

Cube.eLpNorm_cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv_le.name: Cube.eLpNorm_cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv_le
Cube.eLpNorm_cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv_le.docstring:
**The derivative of the smoothing**: on `{x_i ≤ w}` with `w + r² δ ≤ 1`,
`‖∂_i^r S^{(i)}_δ f‖_p ≤ 2^r δ^(-r) ω_r^{(i)}(f, rδ)_p`.

Cube.eLpNorm_cubeMixedDiff_le.name: Cube.eLpNorm_cubeMixedDiff_le
Cube.eLpNorm_cubeMixedDiff_le.docstring:
**Mixed differences on boxes**: if every slice of `f` in every coordinate lies in `V`, and
the differences of order `m_i` and step `h_i` of the functions in `V` are bounded by `β_i` on the
step regions, then the mixed difference along a list of distinct coordinates satisfies
`‖M f‖_{L_p(box)} ≤ (∏_{i ∈ l} β_i) ‖f‖_{L_p(Q)}`.

Cube.eLpNorm_cubeDiff_regionVol_le.name: Cube.eLpNorm_cubeDiff_regionVol_le
Cube.eLpNorm_cubeDiff_regionVol_le.docstring:
**Coordinate differences on a region are bounded by the modulus**: for `w + r (rδ) ≤ 1` and
`0 ≤ h ≤ rδ`, `‖Δ^r_{h e_i} f‖_{L_p({x_i ≤ w})} ≤ ω_r^{(i)}(f, rδ)_p`, since the region
`{0 ≤ x_i ≤ w}` lies in `{0 ≤ x_i ≤ 1 - rh}`.

Cube.eLpNorm_cubeDiff_le_of_slice_le.name: Cube.eLpNorm_cubeDiff_le_of_slice_le
Cube.eLpNorm_cubeDiff_le_of_slice_le.docstring:
**Coordinate differences bounded through slices**: for measurable `f`, `0 < p < ∞`,
`h ≥ 0` and `B ∈ [0, ∞]`, if `‖Δ_h^r (slice f x i)‖_{L_p[0, 1-rh]} ≤ B ‖slice f x i‖_{L_p[0,1]}`
for every point `x`, then `‖Δ^r_{h e_i} f‖_{L_p({x_i ≤ 1 - rh})} ≤ B ‖f‖_{L_p(Q)}`
(`Cube.eLpNorm_inter_le_of_slice_le`).

Cube.eLpNorm_cubeDiff_le.name: Cube.eLpNorm_cubeDiff_le
Cube.eLpNorm_cubeDiff_le.docstring:
**`‖Δ^r_{h e_i} f‖_{L_p({x_i ≤ 1 - rh})} ≤ 2^r ‖f‖_{L_p(Q)}`** for `h ≥ 0`, from the bound in
one variable on every slice.

Cube.eLpNorm_cubeDiff_inter_le.name: Cube.eLpNorm_cubeDiff_inter_le
Cube.eLpNorm_cubeDiff_inter_le.docstring:
**One coordinate step**: let `R` not depend on the coordinate `i`, and let every slice of `F`
in coordinate `i` satisfy `‖Δ_t^m u‖_{L_p(J(m,t))} ≤ β ‖u‖_{L_p[0,1]}`. Then
`‖Δ^m_{t e_i} F‖_{L_p(R ∩ {x_i + mt ∈ [0,1]})} ≤ β ‖F‖_{L_p(R)}`, by Tonelli in coordinate `i`
(`Cube.eLpNorm_inter_le_of_slice_le`).

Cube.eLpNorm_comp_add_le.name: Cube.eLpNorm_comp_add_le
Cube.eLpNorm_comp_add_le.docstring:
**Translation inside the cube**: if `x + v ∈ R' ∩ Q` for all `x ∈ R ∩ Q`, then
`‖G(· + v)‖_{L_p(R ∩ Q)} ≤ ‖G‖_{L_p(R' ∩ Q)}`, by the translation invariance of Lebesgue measure
(Mathlib's `measurePreserving_add_right`).

Cube.diffRegion_eq_isoRegion.name: Cube.diffRegion_eq_isoRegion
Cube.diffRegion_eq_isoRegion.docstring:
The region of a coordinate difference is the isotropic region of the step `s e_i`, on the
cube.

Cube.diffRegion.name: Cube.diffRegion
Cube.diffRegion.docstring:
The region `{x ∈ Q : x_i ≤ 1 - r h}` of the differences of step `h` in coordinate `i`, as a
restriction of the cube measure.

Cube.diffAct_list_prod.name: Cube.diffAct_list_prod
Cube.diffAct_list_prod.docstring: **Products of coordinate elements act by mixed differences**.

Cube.diffAct_coordElem_pow.name: Cube.diffAct_coordElem_pow
Cube.diffAct_coordElem_pow.docstring: `(δ_{h_i e_i} - 1)^m` acts by the coordinate difference `Δ^m_{h_i e_i}`.

Cube.cube_eLpNorm_le_of_slice_le.name: Cube.cube_eLpNorm_le_of_slice_le
Cube.cube_eLpNorm_le_of_slice_le.docstring:
**From slices to the cube, on two regions**: if every slice of `F` in coordinate `i` satisfies
`‖F_{x,i}‖_{L_p[0,1]} ≤ c ((‖(G₁)_{x,i}‖_{L_p[a₁,b₁]} + M ‖(D₁)_{x,i}‖_{L_p[a₁,b₁]}) + (‖(G₂)_{x,i}‖_{L_p[a₂,b₂]} + M ‖(D₂)_{x,i}‖_{L_p[a₂,b₂]}))`,
then the same bound holds for the norms on the cube and on the regions `{x_i ∈ [a_ν, b_ν]}`: the
norms are mixed norms of the slices (`Cube.eLpNorm_cubeVol_eq_slice`,
`Cube.eLpNorm_regionVol_eq_slice`), and Minkowski's inequality in `L_p` over the point applies.

Cube.cubeVol_restrict_congr.name: Cube.cubeVol_restrict_congr
Cube.cubeVol_restrict_congr.docstring: The cube measure restricted to two sets that agree on the cube.

Cube.cubeVol_eq_restrict.name: Cube.cubeVol_eq_restrict
Cube.cubeVol_eq_restrict.docstring:
The cube measure is Lebesgue measure restricted to the cube (Mathlib's
`Measure.restrict_pi_pi`).

Cube.cubeVol.name: Cube.cubeVol
Cube.cubeVol.docstring:
**Lebesgue measure on the unit cube** `[0, 1]^d`, the product of Lebesgue measure on
`[0, 1]`.

Cube.cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv_eq_sum_smul.name: Cube.cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv_eq_sum_smul
Cube.cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv_eq_sum_smul.docstring:
**The derivative of the smoothing as a sum of functions**:
`∂_i^r S^{(i)}_δ f = ∑_{k=1}^r (-1)^(k+1) C(r,k) (kδ)^(-r) Δ^r_{kδ e_i} f` as an identity of
functions on `ℝ^d` (`Cube.cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv_eq` at every point), written as a sum
`∑_k c_k • g_k`, the form to which the triangle inequality in `L_p` applies.

Cube.cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv_eq.name: Cube.cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv_eq
Cube.cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv_eq.docstring:
**The derivative of the smoothing is a combination of coordinate differences**:
`∂_i^r S^{(i)}_δ f = ∑_{k=1}^r (-1)^(k+1) C(r,k) (kδ)^(-r) Δ^r_{kδ e_i} f`.

Cube.cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv.name: Cube.cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv
Cube.cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv.docstring:
The **derivative of order `r` in coordinate `i`** of the smoothing,
`∂_i^r S^{(i)}_δ f(x) = (S_δ (slice f x i))^(r)(x_i)`.

Cube.cubeSteklovSmooth.name: Cube.cubeSteklovSmooth
Cube.cubeSteklovSmooth.docstring: The **Steklov smoothing in coordinate `i`**: `S^{(i)}_δ f(x) = S_δ (slice f x i)(x_i)`.

Cube.cubeSplineSpace_mono.name: Cube.cubeSplineSpace_mono
Cube.cubeSplineSpace_mono.docstring: The spline spaces on the cube increase with the level.

Cube.cubeSplineSpace.name: Cube.cubeSplineSpace
Cube.cubeSplineSpace.docstring: The space of **splines of order `r` and level `k` in each variable** in `L_p(Q)`.

Cube.cubeSplineScheme.name: Cube.cubeSplineScheme
Cube.cubeSplineScheme.docstring:
The **scheme of tensor splines on the cube**: `{0}` at complexity `0` and the splines of
level `⌊log₂ n⌋` in each variable at complexity `n ≥ 1`.

Cube.cubeSplineIsoModulusData.name: Cube.cubeSplineIsoModulusData
Cube.cubeSplineIsoModulusData.docstring:
The **isotropic modulus** `ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p` on the cube is compatible with the scheme of
tensor splines of order `r`, with inverse order `θ = r - 1 + 1/p`.

Cube.cubeQI.name: Cube.cubeQI
Cube.cubeQI.docstring:
The **tensor quasi-interpolant**: the quasi-interpolant `Q_k` applied in all coordinates,
`Q_k^{(0)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ Q_k^{(d-1)}`.

Cube.cubeProj.name: Cube.cubeProj
Cube.cubeProj.docstring:
The **tensor projection**: the local projection `P_k` applied in all coordinates,
`P_k^{(0)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ P_k^{(d-1)}`.

Cube.cubePPSpace_mono.name: Cube.cubePPSpace_mono
Cube.cubePPSpace_mono.docstring: The spaces `V_k^d` increase with the level.

Cube.cubePPSpace.name: Cube.cubePPSpace
Cube.cubePPSpace.docstring:
The space `V_k^d` of **piecewise polynomials of level `k` and degree `< r` in each variable**
in `L_p(Q)`.

Cube.cubePPScheme.name: Cube.cubePPScheme
Cube.cubePPScheme.docstring:
The **scheme of dyadic piecewise polynomials on the cube**: `{0}` at complexity `0` and
`V_{⌊log₂ n⌋}^d` at complexity `n ≥ 1`.

Cube.cubePPIsoModulusData.name: Cube.cubePPIsoModulusData
Cube.cubePPIsoModulusData.docstring:
The **isotropic modulus** `ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p` on the cube is compatible with the scheme of
piecewise polynomials, with inverse order `θ = 1/p` and Jackson's inequality at every level.

Cube.cubeModulus_mono.name: Cube.cubeModulus_mono
Cube.cubeModulus_mono.docstring: The modulus on the cube increases in `t`.

Cube.cubeModulus_le_isoModulus.name: Cube.cubeModulus_le_isoModulus
Cube.cubeModulus_le_isoModulus.docstring: **The modulus on the cube is bounded by the isotropic modulus**: `ω_cube ≤ d ω_iso`.

Cube.cubeModulus_congr_ae.name: Cube.cubeModulus_congr_ae
Cube.cubeModulus_congr_ae.docstring: The modulus on the cube depends only on the class in `L_p(Q)`.

Cube.cubeModulus_add_le.name: Cube.cubeModulus_add_le
Cube.cubeModulus_add_le.docstring: The modulus on the cube is subadditive.

Cube.cubeModulus.name: Cube.cubeModulus
Cube.cubeModulus.docstring: The **modulus of smoothness on the cube**, `ω_r(f, t)_p = ∑_i ω_r^{(i)}(f, t)_p`.

Cube.cubeMixedDiff_nil.name: Cube.cubeMixedDiff_nil
Cube.cubeMixedDiff_nil.docstring: The mixed difference along the empty list is the function itself.

Cube.cubeMixedDiff.name: Cube.cubeMixedDiff
Cube.cubeMixedDiff.docstring:
The **mixed coordinate difference** along a list of coordinates: the difference of order
`m_i` with step `h_i` in each coordinate `i` of the list, the last one first.

Cube.cubeJacksonConst_ne_top.name: Cube.cubeJacksonConst_ne_top
Cube.cubeJacksonConst_ne_top.docstring: The Jackson constant on the cube is finite.

Cube.cubeJacksonConst.name: Cube.cubeJacksonConst
Cube.cubeJacksonConst.docstring:
The constant of Jackson's inequality on the cube, `(1 + C_r)^(d+1) 2 (1 + 2^r r^(2r))`, with
the bound `C_r` of the local projections.

Cube.cubeDiff_eq.name: Cube.cubeDiff_eq
Cube.cubeDiff_eq.docstring: The coordinate difference as a sum: `Δ^r_{h e_i} f(x) = ∑_k (-1)^(r-k) C(r,k) f(x + k h e_i)`.

Cube.cubeDiff.name: Cube.cubeDiff
Cube.cubeDiff.docstring:
The **difference of order `r` and step `h` in coordinate `i`**,
`Δ^r_{h e_i} f(x) = Δ_h^r (slice f x i)(x_i)`.

Cube.coordModulus_reflectCoord.name: Cube.coordModulus_reflectCoord
Cube.coordModulus_reflectCoord.docstring:
**Reflection preserves the coordinate modulus**: `ω_r^{(i)}(f(reflect_i ·), t) = ω_r^{(i)}(f, t)`,
slice by slice (`Interval.eLpNorm_higherDiff_reflect`, `Cube.coordModulus_eq_of_slice`).

Cube.coordModulus_le_isoModulus.name: Cube.coordModulus_le_isoModulus
Cube.coordModulus_le_isoModulus.docstring:
**Coordinate moduli are bounded by the isotropic modulus**: steps `s e_i`, `0 ≤ s ≤ t`, are
isotropic steps with `‖s e_i‖_∞ = s`.

Cube.coordModulus_eq_of_slice.name: Cube.coordModulus_eq_of_slice
Cube.coordModulus_eq_of_slice.docstring:
**Equal coordinate moduli through slices**: for measurable `f, g` and `0 < p < ∞`, if for
every step `0 ≤ s ≤ t` and almost every point `x` the differences of the slices have equal norms,
`‖Δ_s^r (slice f x i)‖_{L_p[0, 1-rs]} = ‖Δ_s^r (slice g x i)‖_{L_p[0, 1-rs]}`, then
`ω_r^{(i)}(f, t)_p = ω_r^{(i)}(g, t)_p` (`Cube.eLpNorm_rpow_cubeDiff_eq_slice`).

Cube.coordModulus_congr_ae.name: Cube.coordModulus_congr_ae
Cube.coordModulus_congr_ae.docstring:
**The coordinate modulus depends only on the class in `L_p(Q)`**: measurable functions that
agree almost everywhere on the cube have almost everywhere equal slices, hence equal
differences.

Cube.coordModulus.name: Cube.coordModulus
Cube.coordModulus.docstring:
The **modulus of smoothness in coordinate `i`** on the cube:
`ω_r^{(i)}(f, t)_p = sup_{0 ≤ h ≤ t} ‖Δ^r_{h e_i} f‖_{L_p({x ∈ Q : x_i ≤ 1 - rh})}`.

Cube.continuous_slice.name: Cube.continuous_slice
Cube.continuous_slice.docstring: The slices of a continuous function are continuous.

Cube.continuous_cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv.name: Cube.continuous_cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv
Cube.continuous_cubeSteklovSmoothDeriv.docstring: The derivative of the smoothing of a continuous function is continuous.

Cube.continuous_cubeSteklovSmooth.name: Cube.continuous_cubeSteklovSmooth
Cube.continuous_cubeSteklovSmooth.docstring: The smoothing of a continuous function is continuous.

Cube.continuous_cubeDiff_uncurry.name: Cube.continuous_cubeDiff_uncurry
Cube.continuous_cubeDiff_uncurry.docstring:
Coordinate differences of a continuous function are jointly continuous in the step and the
point.

Cube.continuous_cubeDiff.name: Cube.continuous_cubeDiff
Cube.continuous_cubeDiff.docstring: Coordinate differences of a continuous function are continuous.

Cube.bddMeas_zero.name: Cube.bddMeas_zero
Cube.bddMeas_zero.docstring: The zero function is bounded and measurable.

Cube.bddMeas_sum.name: Cube.bddMeas_sum
Cube.bddMeas_sum.docstring: Finite sums of bounded measurable functions are bounded and measurable.

Cube.bddMeas_ppFun.name: Cube.bddMeas_ppFun
Cube.bddMeas_ppFun.docstring:
Piecewise polynomials are bounded and measurable (`Interval.measurable_ppFun`,
`Interval.exists_norm_ppFun_le`).

Cube.approxError_le_of_continuous.name: Cube.approxError_le_of_continuous
Cube.approxError_le_of_continuous.docstring:
**From continuous functions to `L_p(Q)` by density**: a bound
`E_n(g) ≤ C ω_r(g, 2^(-k))_p` for every bounded continuous `g`, given by an approximant
`u ∈ A_n` of `g`, holds for every `f ∈ L_p(Q)`, `p < ∞`, as in one variable
(`Interval.interval_approxError_le_of_continuous`).

Cube.approxError_cubeSplineScheme_one_le.name: Cube.approxError_cubeSplineScheme_one_le
Cube.approxError_cubeSplineScheme_one_le.docstring:
At complexity `1` the tensor splines contain the polynomials of degree `< r` in each
variable, so their error is at most that of the piecewise polynomials.

Cube.approxError_cubePPScheme_le.name: Cube.approxError_cubePPScheme_le
Cube.approxError_cubePPScheme_le.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality for piecewise polynomials on the cube**: for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, `r ≥ 1` and
`k ≥ 1`, `E_{2^k}(f)_p ≤ (1 + C_r)^(d+1) 2 (1 + 2^r r^(2r)) ω_r(f, 2^(-k))_p` for every
`f ∈ L_p(Q)`; first for bounded continuous functions with the tensor projection
(`Cube.eLpNorm_sub_cubeProj_le`), then by density.

Cube.ae_slice_ae_eq.name: Cube.ae_slice_ae_eq
Cube.ae_slice_ae_eq.docstring:
**Slices of almost equal functions**: if `f = g` almost everywhere on the cube, then for
almost every `x` the slices of `f` and `g` through `x` in coordinate `i` agree almost
everywhere on `[0, 1]`.

Cube.add_smul_mem_cubeSet.name: Cube.add_smul_mem_cubeSet
Cube.add_smul_mem_cubeSet.docstring: For `x` in the isotropic region of the cube and `0 ≤ n ≤ r`, `x + nh` lies in the cube.

Cube.add_mul_mem_Icc.name: Cube.add_mul_mem_Icc
Cube.add_mul_mem_Icc.docstring:
**Convexity of intervals**: if `a, a + R b ∈ [0, 1]` and `0 ≤ n ≤ R`, then
`a + n b ∈ [0, 1]`.

Cube.KernelOp.slicewise_sub.name: Cube.KernelOp.slicewise_sub
Cube.KernelOp.slicewise_sub.docstring: **The slicewise action is linear** on bounded measurable functions.

Cube.KernelOp.slicewise_eq.name: Cube.KernelOp.slicewise_eq
Cube.KernelOp.slicewise_eq.docstring: The slicewise action as a sum: `T^{(i)} g(x) = ∑_j (∫_0^1 g(x with s in place i) κ_j(s) ds) φ_j(x_i)`.

Cube.KernelOp.slicewise.name: Cube.KernelOp.slicewise
Cube.KernelOp.slicewise.docstring: The **slicewise action in coordinate `i`**: `T^{(i)} g(x) = T(slice g x i)(x_i)`.

Cube.KernelOp.slice_slicewise.name: Cube.KernelOp.slice_slicewise
Cube.KernelOp.slice_slicewise.docstring: The slices of `T^{(i)} g` in coordinate `i` are the images of the slices under `T`.

Cube.KernelOp.norm_kernelCoef_le.name: Cube.KernelOp.norm_kernelCoef_le
Cube.KernelOp.norm_kernelCoef_le.docstring: `|∫_0^1 g κ_j| ≤ M B` for `|g| ≤ M` and `|κ_j| ≤ B`.

Cube.KernelOp.measurable_slicewise.name: Cube.KernelOp.measurable_slicewise
Cube.KernelOp.measurable_slicewise.docstring: The slicewise action of a measurable function is measurable.

Cube.KernelOp.measurable_kernelCoef_slic.name: Cube.KernelOp.measurable_kernelCoef_slice
Cube.KernelOp.measurable_kernelCoef_slic.docstring: The coefficients of the slices are measurable in the point.

Cube.KernelOp.kernelCoef_sum.name: Cube.KernelOp.kernelCoef_sum
Cube.KernelOp.kernelCoef_sum.docstring: The coefficients of finite sums of functions integrable on `[0, 1]`.

Cube.KernelOp.kernelCoef_sub.name: Cube.KernelOp.kernelCoef_sub
Cube.KernelOp.kernelCoef_sub.docstring: The coefficients of a difference of functions integrable on `[0, 1]`.

Cube.KernelOp.isForm_zero.name: Cube.KernelOp.isForm_zero
Cube.KernelOp.isForm_zero.docstring: The zero function has the form of every operator.

Cube.KernelOp.isForm_slicewise.name: Cube.KernelOp.isForm_slicewise
Cube.KernelOp.isForm_slicewise.docstring:
**The slicewise action produces the form**: `T^{(i)} g` has the form of `T` in coordinate `i`
for bounded measurable `g`, with the coefficients `c_j(x) = ∫_0^1 g(x with s in place i) κ_j`.

Cube.KernelOp.isForm_foldSlicewise.name: Cube.KernelOp.isForm_foldSlicewise
Cube.KernelOp.isForm_foldSlicewise.docstring: **The action in all coordinates of a list gives the form in each of them.**

Cube.KernelOp.integrableOn_mul_kernel.name: Cube.KernelOp.integrableOn_mul_kernel
Cube.KernelOp.integrableOn_mul_kernel.docstring: The products `g κ_j` of a function `g` integrable on `[0, 1]` are integrable on `[0, 1]`.

Cube.KernelOp.foldSlicewise_cons.name: Cube.KernelOp.foldSlicewise_cons
Cube.KernelOp.foldSlicewise_cons.docstring: The action in the coordinates of `i :: l` is `T^{(i)}` after the action in those of `l`.

Cube.KernelOp.foldSlicewise.name: Cube.KernelOp.foldSlicewise
Cube.KernelOp.foldSlicewise.docstring:
The action of `T` in the coordinates of a list, the last coordinate first:
`T^{(l_1)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ T^{(l_m)}`.

Cube.KernelOp.eLpNorm_sub_foldSlicewise_.name: Cube.KernelOp.eLpNorm_sub_foldSlicewise_le_of_coord
Cube.KernelOp.eLpNorm_sub_foldSlicewise_.docstring:
**From one coordinate to all**: if `‖T u‖_{L_p[0,1]} ≤ C ‖u‖_{L_p[0,1]}` and
`‖f - T^{(i)} f‖_{L_p(Q)} ≤ B ω_r^{(i)}(f, t)_p` in every coordinate, then
`‖f - T^{(0)} ⋯ T^{(d-1)} f‖_{L_p(Q)} ≤ (1 + C)^d B ω_r(f, t)_p`, by telescoping
(`Cube.KernelOp.eLpNorm_sub_foldSlicewise_le`).

Cube.KernelOp.eLpNorm_sub_foldSlicewise_.name: Cube.KernelOp.eLpNorm_sub_foldSlicewise_le
Cube.KernelOp.eLpNorm_sub_foldSlicewise_.docstring:
**Telescoping over the coordinates of a list**: if `‖T u‖_{L_p[0,1]} ≤ C ‖u‖_{L_p[0,1]}`,
then `‖g - T^{(l_1)} ⋯ T^{(l_m)} g‖_{L_p(Q)} ≤ (1 + C)^m ∑_{i ∈ l} ‖g - T^{(i)} g‖_{L_p(Q)}` for
bounded measurable `g`. The step is `g - T^{(i)} h = (g - T^{(i)} g) + T^{(i)} (g - h)`.

Cube.KernelOp.eLpNorm_slicewise_le.name: Cube.KernelOp.eLpNorm_slicewise_le
Cube.KernelOp.eLpNorm_slicewise_le.docstring:
**Slicewise bounds**: if `‖T u‖_{L_p[0,1]} ≤ C ‖u‖_{L_p[0,1]}` for all measurable `u`, then
`‖T^{(i)} g‖_{L_p(Q)} ≤ C ‖g‖_{L_p(Q)}` for measurable `g` with measurable `T^{(i)} g`.

Cube.KernelOp.bddMeas_slicewise.name: Cube.KernelOp.bddMeas_slicewise
Cube.KernelOp.bddMeas_slicewise.docstring: The slicewise action keeps functions bounded and measurable.

Cube.KernelOp.bddMeas_foldSlicewise.name: Cube.KernelOp.bddMeas_foldSlicewise
Cube.KernelOp.bddMeas_foldSlicewise.docstring: The action in the coordinates of a list keeps functions bounded and measurable.

Cube.KernelOp.apply_sub.name: Cube.KernelOp.apply_sub
Cube.KernelOp.apply_sub.docstring:
**Kernel operators are linear** on functions integrable on `[0, 1]`:
`T(g - h) = T g - T h`.

Cube.KernelOp.apply.name: Cube.KernelOp.apply
Cube.KernelOp.apply.docstring: The operator `T g = ∑_j (∫_0^1 g κ_j) φ_j`.

Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.slicewise.name: Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.slicewise
Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.slicewise.docstring:
**The form is kept by the action in another coordinate**: if `g` has the form of `T` in
coordinate `i` and `j ≠ i`, then `S^{(j)} g` has the form of `T` in coordinate `i`, with the
coefficients `S^{(j)} c_a`.

Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.slice_eq.name: Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.slice_eq
Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.slice_eq.docstring: The slices of a function of the form of `T` in coordinate `i` are combinations of the `φ_j`.

Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.refine.name: Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.refine
Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.refine.docstring:
**Refinement of forms**: if every `φ_j` of `T` is a combination of the `φ'_{j'}` of `T'`,
then the form of `T` in a coordinate is a form of `T'`.

Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.const_mul.name: Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.const_mul
Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.const_mul.docstring: Functions of the form of `T` in a coordinate form a linear space: constant multiples.

Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.add.name: Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.add
Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.add.docstring: Functions of the form of `T` in a coordinate form a linear space: sums.

Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.name: Cube.KernelOp.IsForm
Cube.KernelOp.IsForm.docstring:
`g` has the **form of `T` in coordinate `i`**: `g(x) = ∑_j c_j(x) φ_j(x_i)` with bounded
measurable coefficients `c_j` that do not depend on `x_i`.

Cube.KernelOp.name: Cube.KernelOp
Cube.KernelOp.docstring:
A **finite-rank kernel operator** on functions on `[0, 1]`: `T g = ∑_j (∫_0^1 g κ_j) φ_j`
with bounded measurable kernels `κ_j` and functions `φ_j`.

Cube.IsCubeSpline.succ.name: Cube.IsCubeSpline.succ
Cube.IsCubeSpline.succ.docstring: Splines of level `k` are splines of level `k + 1`.

Cube.IsCubeSpline.slice_mem_splineSubmod.name: Cube.IsCubeSpline.slice_mem_splineSubmodule
Cube.IsCubeSpline.slice_mem_splineSubmod.docstring: The slices of a spline on the cube are splines.

Cube.IsCubeSpline.const_mul.name: Cube.IsCubeSpline.const_mul
Cube.IsCubeSpline.const_mul.docstring: Constant multiples of splines on the cube.

Cube.IsCubeSpline.add.name: Cube.IsCubeSpline.add
Cube.IsCubeSpline.add.docstring: Sums of splines on the cube.

Cube.IsCubeSpline.name: Cube.IsCubeSpline
Cube.IsCubeSpline.docstring:
A function on the cube is a **spline of order `r` and level `k` in each variable**: bounded
and measurable, and every slice in every coordinate is a dyadic spline of order `r` and level `k`
on `[0, 1]`.

Cube.IsCubePP.succ.name: Cube.IsCubePP.succ
Cube.IsCubePP.succ.docstring: Piecewise polynomials of level `k` are piecewise polynomials of level `k + 1`.

Cube.IsCubePP.slice_mem_ppSubmodule.name: Cube.IsCubePP.slice_mem_ppSubmodule
Cube.IsCubePP.slice_mem_ppSubmodule.docstring: The slices of a piecewise polynomial on the cube are piecewise polynomials.

Cube.IsCubePP.isCubeSpline_zero.name: Cube.IsCubePP.isCubeSpline_zero
Cube.IsCubePP.isCubeSpline_zero.docstring: **At level `0` the piecewise polynomials are splines**: there are no interior knots.

Cube.IsCubePP.exists_slice_eq_ppFun.name: Cube.IsCubePP.exists_slice_eq_ppFun
Cube.IsCubePP.exists_slice_eq_ppFun.docstring:
**The slices of a piecewise polynomial on the cube** are piecewise polynomials of the same
level and degree on `[0, 1]`.

Cube.IsCubePP.name: Cube.IsCubePP
Cube.IsCubePP.docstring:
A function on the cube is a **piecewise polynomial of level `k` and degree `< r` in each
variable**: bounded and measurable with the form of the local projection `P_k` in every
coordinate, so that on every dyadic cube of level `k` it is a polynomial of degree `< r` in each
variable separately.

Cube.BddMeas.slice.name: Cube.BddMeas.slice
Cube.BddMeas.slice.docstring: The slices of a bounded measurable function are bounded and measurable.

Cube.BddMeas.memLp.name: Cube.BddMeas.memLp
Cube.BddMeas.memLp.docstring: A bounded measurable function lies in every `L_p` of a finite measure.

Cube.BddMeas.integrableOn_Icc.name: Cube.BddMeas.integrableOn_Icc
Cube.BddMeas.integrableOn_Icc.docstring: A bounded measurable function is integrable on `[0, 1]`.

Cube.BddMeas.const_mul.name: Cube.BddMeas.const_mul
Cube.BddMeas.const_mul.docstring: Bounded measurable functions are closed under constant multiples.

Cube.BddMeas.add.name: Cube.BddMeas.add
Cube.BddMeas.add.docstring: Bounded measurable functions are closed under sums.

ContinuousLinearMap.norm_iteratedFDeriv_.name: ContinuousLinearMap.norm_iteratedFDeriv_le_one_add_norm_sq_rpow
ContinuousLinearMap.norm_iteratedFDeriv_.docstring:
**Continuous linear maps are symbols of order `1`**: `‖D^j L(x)‖ ≤ ‖L‖ (1 + ‖x‖²)^{(1-j)/2}`
for every `j`, since `L` grows like the Japanese bracket, its derivative is the constant `L` and
its higher derivatives vanish. Mirrored from TauCeti
(`Analysis/SpecialFunctions/JapaneseBracket/Deriv.lean`, commit `b61a90d`, Apache-2.0).

ContinuousLinearMap.exists_norm_iterated.name: ContinuousLinearMap.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_smul_le_one_add_norm_sq_rpow
ContinuousLinearMap.exists_norm_iterated.docstring:
**A bracket bound times a linear map**: if the derivatives of order `i ≤ k` of a smooth
real function `g` satisfy `‖D^i g(x)‖ ≤ C (1 + ‖x‖²)^{ρ - i/2}`, then the `k`-th derivative of
`x ↦ g(x) L(x)`, for a continuous linear map `L`, satisfies the bracket bound of order
`ρ + 1/2`, by the Leibniz rule (Mathlib's `norm_iteratedFDeriv_smul_le`). Mirrored from TauCeti
(`Analysis/SpecialFunctions/JapaneseBracket/Deriv.lean`, commit `b61a90d`, Apache-2.0).

ContDiffOn.exists_norm_iteratedFDerivWit.name: ContDiffOn.exists_norm_iteratedFDerivWithin_le
ContDiffOn.exists_norm_iteratedFDerivWit.docstring:
**Bounded derivatives on a compact set**: if `f` is smooth on a set `s` of unique
differentiability and `K ⊆ s` is compact, then the derivatives of `f` within `s` of the orders
`i ≤ r` are bounded on `K` by one constant (their norms are continuous on `K`).

Complex.contDiffOn_ofReal_rpow_const.name: Complex.contDiffOn_ofReal_rpow_const
Complex.contDiffOn_ofReal_rpow_const.docstring: The function `t ↦ t^τ`, as a complex-valued function, is smooth on `(0, ∞)`.

BoundedContinuousFunction.toReal_eLpNorm.name: BoundedContinuousFunction.toReal_eLpNorm_top_le_norm
BoundedContinuousFunction.toReal_eLpNorm.docstring:
**The real form of the sup-norm bound in `L_∞`**: `(‖a‖_{L_∞(μ)}).toReal ≤ sup |a|` for every
measure `μ` (`BoundedContinuousFunction.eLpNorm_top_le_enorm`, with `‖a‖ₑ < ∞`).

BoundedContinuousFunction.norm_toLp_top.name: BoundedContinuousFunction.norm_toLp_top
BoundedContinuousFunction.norm_toLp_top.docstring:
For a measure that charges every nonempty open set, the `L_∞` norm of a bounded
continuous function is its sup norm.

BoundedContinuousFunction.norm_toLp_eq_t.name: BoundedContinuousFunction.norm_toLp_eq_toReal_eLpNorm
BoundedContinuousFunction.norm_toLp_eq_t.docstring:
The `L_p` norm of the class of a bounded continuous function is its `eLpNorm`: the bounded
continuous analogue of Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Lp.norm_toLp`, proved from
`MeasureTheory.Lp.norm_def` with the class `toLp p μ 𝕜 a` equal to `a` almost everywhere
(`BoundedContinuousFunction.coeFn_toLp`).

BoundedContinuousFunction.isometry_toLp_.name: BoundedContinuousFunction.isometry_toLp_top
BoundedContinuousFunction.isometry_toLp_.docstring: For a measure that charges every nonempty open set, `toLp ∞` is an isometry.

BoundedContinuousFunction.isClosed_range.name: BoundedContinuousFunction.isClosed_range_toLp_top
BoundedContinuousFunction.isClosed_range.docstring:
For a measure that charges every nonempty open set, the bounded continuous functions form
a closed subspace of `L_∞`.

BoundedContinuousFunction.inclusionOfExp.name: BoundedContinuousFunction.inclusionOfExponentLe_toLp
BoundedContinuousFunction.inclusionOfExp.docstring: The `L_p` class of `a` is the inclusion of its `L_r` class.

BoundedContinuousFunction.inclusionOfExp.name: BoundedContinuousFunction.inclusionOfExponentLeLinear_toLp
BoundedContinuousFunction.inclusionOfExp.docstring:
The `L_p` class of `a` is the image of its `L_r` class under the linear inclusion
`MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionOfExponentLeLinear`, which agrees with the bounded inclusion for
`1 ≤ p` (`MeasureTheory.Lp.inclusionOfExponentLe_apply`).

BoundedContinuousFunction.eLpNorm_top_le.name: BoundedContinuousFunction.eLpNorm_top_le_enorm
BoundedContinuousFunction.eLpNorm_top_le.docstring:
**The `L_∞` norm of a bounded continuous function is at most its sup norm**:
`‖a‖_{L_∞(μ)} ≤ sup |a|` in `[0, ∞]` for every measure `μ`, since `|a(x)| ≤ ‖a‖` for every
`x`.

BesselPotentialSpace.enorm_toLp_eq.name: BesselPotentialSpace.enorm_toLp_eq
BesselPotentialSpace.enorm_toLp_eq.docstring:
`‖J_s U‖_p = ‖U‖` in `ℝ≥0∞`, for `U ∈ H^{s,p}(E, F)`: the norm of the Bessel potential space
is the norm of the `L_p` function `J_s U` (Mathlib's `BesselPotentialSpace.norm_toLp_eq`).

ApproximationScheme.zero_mem.name: ApproximationScheme.zero_mem
ApproximationScheme.zero_mem.docstring: `0` is an approximant of every complexity.

ApproximationScheme.tsum_dyadicWeight_mu.name: ApproximationScheme.tsum_dyadicWeight_mul_add_tolerance_ne_top
ApproximationScheme.tsum_dyadicWeight_mu.docstring:
For `τ ≤ σ` and `‖(2^(kτ) E_{2^k}(f))_k‖_{ℓ_1} < ∞`, the series
`∑_k 2^(kτ) (E_{2^k}(f) + t_k)` with the tolerances `t_k = tolerance f σ k` is finite.

ApproximationScheme.tsum_dyadicWeight_mu.name: ApproximationScheme.tsum_dyadicWeight_mul_add_tolerance_le
