ApproximationScheme.tsum_dyadicWeight_mu.docstring:
**Splitting off the tolerances**: for `τ ≤ σ`,
`∑_k 2^(kτ) (E_{2^k}(f) + t_k) ≤ ‖(2^(kτ) E_{2^k}(f))_k‖_{ℓ_1} + 2 ‖f‖`, with the tolerances
`t_k = tolerance f σ k`.

ApproximationScheme.tolerance.name: ApproximationScheme.tolerance
ApproximationScheme.tolerance.docstring:
The tolerances `t_k = ‖f‖ 2^(-k(σ+1))`: positive and finite for `f ≠ 0`, decreasing for
`σ ≥ -1`, and small against every weight `2^(kτ)` with `τ ≤ σ`.

ApproximationScheme.tendsto_approxError_.name: ApproximationScheme.tendsto_approxError_zero_of_pow
ApproximationScheme.tendsto_approxError_.docstring: Since the errors decrease, they tend to zero as soon as the dyadic errors `E_{2^k}` do.

ApproximationScheme.tendsto_approxError_.name: ApproximationScheme.tendsto_approxError_zero_iff
ApproximationScheme.tendsto_approxError_.docstring:
The errors tend to zero exactly for the elements of the closure of `⋃ n, A n`: the
decreasing errors tend to their infimum, the distance from `f` to `⋃ n, A n`.

ApproximationScheme.tendsto_approxError_.name: ApproximationScheme.tendsto_approxError_pow_zero_of_memApprox
ApproximationScheme.tendsto_approxError_.docstring: For `f ∈ A^s_q` with `s > 0` and `0 < q ≤ ∞`, the dyadic errors `E_{2^k}(f)` tend to zero.

ApproximationScheme.sum_range_mem.name: ApproximationScheme.sum_range_mem
ApproximationScheme.sum_range_mem.docstring:
The partial sums of a block decomposition are approximants: `∑_{j<k} g_j ∈ A (2^k)`, since
`∑_{j<k} 2^j < 2^k` (Mathlib's `Nat.geomSum_lt`).

ApproximationScheme.sum_mem.name: ApproximationScheme.sum_mem
ApproximationScheme.sum_mem.docstring: A finite sum of approximants has at most the sum of the complexities.

ApproximationScheme.sub_mem_pow_add_two.name: ApproximationScheme.sub_mem_pow_add_two
ApproximationScheme.sub_mem_pow_add_two.docstring:
The difference of consecutive dyadic approximants, `a ∈ A (2 ^ (k + 1))` and
`b ∈ A (2 ^ k)`, lies in `A (2 ^ (k + 2))`.  This is the inclusion that every telescoping
argument uses.

ApproximationScheme.sub_mem.name: ApproximationScheme.sub_mem
ApproximationScheme.sub_mem.docstring: `a - b ∈ A_{m+n}` for `a ∈ A_m` and `b ∈ A_n`.

ApproximationScheme.smul_set_eq.name: ApproximationScheme.smul_set_eq
ApproximationScheme.smul_set_eq.docstring: Multiplying by a nonzero scalar maps `A n` onto itself.

ApproximationScheme.shiftSeq_of_lt.name: ApproximationScheme.shiftSeq_of_lt
ApproximationScheme.shiftSeq_of_lt.docstring: The levels below `γ` of the moved sequence are `0`.

ApproximationScheme.shiftSeq_mem.name: ApproximationScheme.shiftSeq_mem
ApproximationScheme.shiftSeq_mem.docstring: **Moving approximants up**: if `a_j ∈ A_{2^(j+γ)}`, then `(shiftSeq γ a)_i ∈ A_{2^i}`.

ApproximationScheme.shiftSeq.name: ApproximationScheme.shiftSeq
ApproximationScheme.shiftSeq.docstring: The sequence `a` moved up by `γ` levels: `a_{i-γ}` at the levels `i ≥ γ`, and `0` below.

ApproximationScheme.reprUpperConst_ne_to.name: ApproximationScheme.reprUpperConst_ne_top
ApproximationScheme.reprUpperConst_ne_to.docstring: The constant `reprUpperConst r s q` is finite for `0 < s < r`.

ApproximationScheme.reprUpperConst.name: ApproximationScheme.reprUpperConst
ApproximationScheme.reprUpperConst.docstring:
The constant `kMethodUpperConst (s/r) r q · devorePopovConst r s` of the bound of the
continuous K-norm of `(X, A^r_∞)` by the dyadic quasi-norm of `A^s_q`.

ApproximationScheme.reprLowerConst_ne_to.name: ApproximationScheme.reprLowerConst_ne_top
ApproximationScheme.reprLowerConst_ne_to.docstring: The constant `reprLowerConst r s q` is finite for `r > 0`.

ApproximationScheme.reprLowerConst.name: ApproximationScheme.reprLowerConst
ApproximationScheme.reprLowerConst.docstring:
The constant `2 · 2^s (1 + 2 · 2^r) 2^s (r log 2)^(-1/q)` of the bound of the dyadic
quasi-norm of `A^s_q` by the continuous K-norm of `(X, A^r_∞)`.

ApproximationScheme.reprCouple.name: ApproximationScheme.reprCouple
ApproximationScheme.reprCouple.docstring:
The **couple `(X, A^r_∞)`** of the scheme, `leftApproxCouple r ∞`: the norm `‖f‖` of `X` and
the dyadic quasi-norm `‖f‖ + sup_k 2^(kr) E_{2^k}(f)` of `A^r_∞`.  Its interpolation spaces are
the approximation spaces `A^s_q`, `0 < s < r` (`memApprox_iff_memKMethod_reprCouple`).

ApproximationScheme.reprConst_ne_top.name: ApproximationScheme.reprConst_ne_top
ApproximationScheme.reprConst_ne_top.docstring: The constant of the representation theorem is finite for `s < r`.

ApproximationScheme.reprConst.name: ApproximationScheme.reprConst
ApproximationScheme.reprConst.docstring:
The constant of Bernstein's half of the representation theorem,
`3 + (3 C + 2 K) (1 - 2^(-(r-s)))⁻¹` with `K = liftConst C r`.

ApproximationScheme.reiterationExponent_.name: ApproximationScheme.reiterationExponent_pos
ApproximationScheme.reiterationExponent_.docstring:
**The reiteration exponent is positive**: for `0 < s₀ < s₁` and `0 < η < 1`,
`0 < (1-η)s₀ + ηs₁`.

ApproximationScheme.reiterationExponent_.name: ApproximationScheme.reiterationExponent_lt
ApproximationScheme.reiterationExponent_.docstring:
**The reiteration exponent stays below every bound of `s₁`**: for `s₀ < s₁ < θ` and
`η < 1`, `(1-η)s₀ + ηs₁ = s₁ - (1-η)(s₁ - s₀)` is at most `s₁`, hence `< θ`.

ApproximationScheme.phiIntegrand_le_disc.name: ApproximationScheme.phiIntegrand_le_discretePhiSeq
ApproximationScheme.phiIntegrand_le_disc.docstring:
**Upper bound on a piece**: for an increasing `φ`, `θ ≥ 0` and
`t ∈ [2^(nρ), 2^((n+1)ρ))`, `t^(-θ) φ(t) ≤ 2^(ρθ) · 2^(-(n+1)ρθ) φ(2^((n+1)ρ))`.

ApproximationScheme.phiIntegrand_const_m.name: ApproximationScheme.phiIntegrand_const_mul
ApproximationScheme.phiIntegrand_const_m.docstring: The integrand of `a φ` is `a` times the integrand of `φ`.

ApproximationScheme.phiIntegrand_comp_mu.name: ApproximationScheme.phiIntegrand_comp_mul
ApproximationScheme.phiIntegrand_comp_mu.docstring:
The integrand of `φ(c ·)` at `t` is the integrand of `c^θ φ` at `c t`:
`t^(-θ) φ(c t) = (c t)^(-θ) c^θ φ(c t)`, for `0 < c < ∞`.

ApproximationScheme.phiIntegrand.name: ApproximationScheme.phiIntegrand
ApproximationScheme.phiIntegrand.docstring: The integrand `t ↦ t^(-θ) φ(t)` of `Φ_{θ,q}(φ)`, for `t : ℝ`.

ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_mono.name: ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_mono
ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_mono.docstring:
**Monotonicity of `Φ_{θ,q}`**: if `φ ≤ ψ` on `(0, ∞)` and `φ` is measurable, then
`Φ_{θ,q}(φ) ≤ Φ_{θ,q}(ψ)`.

ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_le_lqN.name: ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_le_lqNorm_discretePhiSeq
ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_le_lqN.docstring:
**The functional `Φ_{θ,q}` by its discrete version**: for an increasing `φ`, `θ ≥ 0` and
`ρ > 0`, `Φ_{θ,q}(φ) ≤ (ρ log 2)^(1/q) 2^(ρθ) ‖(2^(-nρθ) φ(2^(nρ)))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q}`.

ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_eq.name: ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_eq
ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_eq.docstring: `Φ_{θ,q}(φ)` is the `L_q(dt/t)` norm of `t ↦ t^(-θ) φ(t)`.

ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_const_.name: ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_const_mul
ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_const_.docstring:
**Homogeneity of `Φ_{θ,q}`**: `Φ_{θ,q}(a φ) = a Φ_{θ,q}(φ)` for every `a ∈ [0, ∞]` and
measurable `φ`, by the homogeneity of `L_q` norms of `[0, ∞]`-valued functions
(Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_const_mul_ennreal`).

ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_congr.name: ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_congr
ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_congr.docstring:
`Φ_{θ,q}(φ)` depends only on the values of `φ` on `(0, ∞)`: if `φ t = ψ t` for every
`t ≠ 0, ∞`, then `Φ_{θ,q}(φ) = Φ_{θ,q}(ψ)`.

ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_comp_m.name: ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_comp_mul
ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional_comp_m.docstring:
**`Φ_{θ,q}` under a dilation** (Bergh–Löfström (3.1.7)): for `0 < c < ∞` and measurable `φ`,
`Φ_{θ,q}(φ(c ·)) = c^θ Φ_{θ,q}(φ)`, by the invariance of `dt/t` under `t ↦ c t`.

ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional.name: ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional
ApproximationScheme.phiFunctional.docstring:
The functional `Φ_{θ,q}(φ) = (∫_0^∞ (t^(-θ) φ(t))^q dt/t)^(1/q)` of a function
`φ : [0, ∞] → [0, ∞]` (the essential supremum of `t^(-θ) φ(t)` for `q = ∞`).  The formula is
that of `EQuasinorm.phiFunctional` in the project *MultilinearInterpolation* (Bonn, Apache 2.0).

ApproximationScheme.pairwise_disjoint_dy.name: ApproximationScheme.pairwise_disjoint_dyadicPiece
ApproximationScheme.pairwise_disjoint_dy.docstring: The dyadic pieces are pairwise disjoint for `ρ ≥ 0`.

ApproximationScheme.ofSubmodules.name: ApproximationScheme.ofSubmodules
ApproximationScheme.ofSubmodules.docstring:
A scheme made of an increasing sequence of **linear subspaces** starting with `{0}`.  The
third axiom holds automatically, since `A m` and `A n` both lie in `A (m + n)`.

ApproximationScheme.ofReal_mul_log_two_r.name: ApproximationScheme.ofReal_mul_log_two_rpow_ne_zero
ApproximationScheme.ofReal_mul_log_two_r.docstring: The factor `(ρ log 2)^(1/q)` is nonzero for `ρ > 0`.

ApproximationScheme.ofReal_mul_log_two_n.name: ApproximationScheme.ofReal_mul_log_two_ne_zero
ApproximationScheme.ofReal_mul_log_two_n.docstring: The measure `ρ log 2` of a dyadic piece is nonzero for `ρ > 0`.

ApproximationScheme.ofReal_mem_Icc_of_me.name: ApproximationScheme.ofReal_mem_Icc_of_mem_dyadicPiece
ApproximationScheme.ofReal_mem_Icc_of_me.docstring:
A point `t` of the dyadic piece `[2^(nρ), 2^((n+1)ρ))` satisfies
`2^(nρ) ≤ t ≤ 2^((n+1)ρ)` as an element of `[0, ∞]`.

ApproximationScheme.ofReal_log_two_rpow_.name: ApproximationScheme.ofReal_log_two_rpow_ne_zero
ApproximationScheme.ofReal_log_two_rpow_.docstring:
The factor `(log 2)^(1/q)` is nonzero: the case `ρ = 1` of
`ofReal_mul_log_two_rpow_ne_zero`.

ApproximationScheme.ofMonotoneSubmodules.name: ApproximationScheme.ofMonotoneSubmodules
ApproximationScheme.ofMonotoneSubmodules.docstring:
The **dyadic scheme of an increasing sequence of subspaces** `V_0 ⊆ V_1 ⊆ ⋯`: `{0}` at
complexity `0` and `V_k`, `k = ⌊log₂ n⌋`, at complexity `n ≥ 1`, so that the level `V_k` is the
set of approximants of complexity `2^k`. Piecewise polynomials and splines on dyadic partitions
are schemes of this form.

ApproximationScheme.nonempty.name: ApproximationScheme.nonempty
ApproximationScheme.nonempty.docstring:
The sets of a scheme are nonempty.  This is the hypothesis under which
`Metric.infEDist` is finite, so the error of approximation is finite.

ApproximationScheme.nikolskiiConst.name: ApproximationScheme.nikolskiiConst
ApproximationScheme.nikolskiiConst.docstring:
The constant of the Nikolskii transfer theorem,
`3 C + 3 K (1 - 2^(-(s-α)))⁻¹ + 2 K` with `K = liftConst C α`.

ApproximationScheme.mul_add_mul_tsum_tol.name: ApproximationScheme.mul_add_mul_tsum_tolerance_le
ApproximationScheme.mul_add_mul_tsum_tol.docstring:
**The bound of a telescoping lift by the norm of `A^σ_1`**:
`c (2 ‖f‖ + ‖f‖) + K ∑_k 2^(kσ) (E_{2^k}(f) + t_k) ≤ (3 c + 3 K) ‖f‖_{A^σ_1}` with the
tolerances `t_k = tolerance f σ k`, for all `c, K ∈ [0, ∞]`.

ApproximationScheme.mem_of_le.name: ApproximationScheme.mem_of_le
ApproximationScheme.mem_of_le.docstring: The sets increase: `A_m ⊆ A_n` for `m ≤ n`.

ApproximationScheme.mem_ofSubmodules.name: ApproximationScheme.mem_ofSubmodules
ApproximationScheme.mem_ofSubmodules.docstring: Membership in the scheme of an increasing sequence of subspaces.

ApproximationScheme.mem_ofMonotoneSubmod.name: ApproximationScheme.mem_ofMonotoneSubmodules_zero
ApproximationScheme.mem_ofMonotoneSubmod.docstring: The dyadic scheme of a sequence of subspaces is `{0}` at complexity `0`.

ApproximationScheme.mem_ofMonotoneSubmod.name: ApproximationScheme.mem_ofMonotoneSubmodules_two_pow
ApproximationScheme.mem_ofMonotoneSubmod.docstring: The dyadic scheme of a sequence of subspaces is `V_k` at complexity `2^k`.

ApproximationScheme.mem_ofMonotoneSubmod.name: ApproximationScheme.mem_ofMonotoneSubmodules
ApproximationScheme.mem_ofMonotoneSubmod.docstring: The dyadic scheme of a sequence of subspaces is `V_⌊log₂ n⌋` at complexity `n ≥ 1`.

ApproximationScheme.mem_comap.name: ApproximationScheme.mem_comap
ApproximationScheme.mem_comap.docstring: Membership in the preimage scheme: `y ∈ ι⁻¹(A_n)` iff `ι y ∈ A_n`.

ApproximationScheme.mem_closure_iUnion_o.name: ApproximationScheme.mem_closure_iUnion_of_memApprox
ApproximationScheme.mem_closure_iUnion_o.docstring: **`A^s_q` lies in the closure of `⋃ A n`** for `s > 0` and `0 < q ≤ ∞`.

ApproximationScheme.memKMethod_iff_memAp.name: ApproximationScheme.memKMethod_iff_memApprox_of_two_sandwiches
ApproximationScheme.memKMethod_iff_memAp.docstring:
**The sandwich principle**: if `N₀` lies between two dyadic quasi-norms of smoothness `s₀`
and `N₁` between two of smoothness `s₁`, with `0 < s₀ < s₁`, finite constants and fine indices
`≥ 1`, then for `0 < η < 1` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `(N₀, N₁)_{η,q} = A^{(1-η)s₀+ηs₁}_q`.

ApproximationScheme.memKMethod_iff_memAp.name: ApproximationScheme.memKMethod_iff_memApprox_of_sandwich
ApproximationScheme.memKMethod_iff_memAp.docstring:
**The sandwich principle at the left endpoint**: if a function `N₁ : X → [0, ∞]` lies between
two dyadic quasi-norms of smoothness `r > 0`, `N₁ ≤ c ‖·‖_{A^r_{q'}}` and
`‖·‖_{A^r_{q''}} ≤ c' N₁` with finite `c, c'` and `q', q'' ≥ 1`, then for `0 < θ < 1` and
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `(X, N₁)_{θ,q} = A^{θr}_q`.  Smaller norms give larger interpolation spaces
(`InterpCouple.MemKMethod.of_le`), and both outer spaces are `A^{θr}_q`
(`memKMethod_approxCouple_zero_iff`).

ApproximationScheme.memKMethod_approxCou.name: ApproximationScheme.memKMethod_approxCouple_zero_iff
ApproximationScheme.memKMethod_approxCou.docstring:
**The reiteration theorem for approximation spaces at the left endpoint**: for `s₁ > 0`,
`0 < η < 1` and `1 ≤ q₁, q ≤ ∞`, `(X, A^{s₁}_{q₁})_{η,q} = A^{ηs₁}_q`, for the couple
`leftApproxCouple s₁ q₁` of the norm of `X` and the dyadic quasi-norm of `A^{s₁}_{q₁}`.

ApproximationScheme.memApprox_iff_lqNorm.name: ApproximationScheme.memApprox_iff_lqNorm_dyadic_lt_top'
ApproximationScheme.memApprox_iff_lqNorm.docstring: For `s ≥ 0` and every `q ≠ 0`, `f ∈ A^s_q` iff `(2^(ks) E_{2^k}(f))_k ∈ ℓ_q`.

ApproximationScheme.memApprox_iff_approx.name: ApproximationScheme.memApprox_iff_approxNormDyadic_lt_top'
ApproximationScheme.memApprox_iff_approx.docstring: For `s ≥ 0` and every `q ≠ 0`, `f ∈ A^s_q` iff its dyadic quasi-norm is finite.

ApproximationScheme.memApprox_iff_approx.name: ApproximationScheme.memApprox_iff_approxNormDyadic_lt_top
ApproximationScheme.memApprox_iff_approx.docstring: For `s ≥ 0` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `f ∈ A^s_q` iff its dyadic quasi-norm is finite.

ApproximationScheme.measurePreserving_mu.name: ApproximationScheme.measurePreserving_mul_left_kMethodMeasure
ApproximationScheme.measurePreserving_mu.docstring:
**Dilations preserve `dt/t`**: for `c > 0`, `t ↦ c t` maps the measure `dt/t` on `(0, ∞)`
to itself, since Lebesgue measure scales by `c⁻¹` and the density `t⁻¹` by `c`.

ApproximationScheme.measurable_phiIntegr.name: ApproximationScheme.measurable_phiIntegrand_of_measurable
ApproximationScheme.measurable_phiIntegr.docstring: For a measurable `φ`, the integrand `t ↦ t^(-θ) φ(t)` is measurable.

ApproximationScheme.measurable_phiIntegr.name: ApproximationScheme.measurable_phiIntegrand
ApproximationScheme.measurable_phiIntegr.docstring: For an increasing `φ`, the integrand `t ↦ t^(-θ) φ(t)` is measurable.

ApproximationScheme.map.name: ApproximationScheme.map
ApproximationScheme.map.docstring: The **image of a scheme** under a linear map `T : X → Y`: the sets `T '' A n`.

ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_shiftSeq_le.name: ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_shiftSeq_le
ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_shiftSeq_le.docstring:
**The weighted norm of a moved sequence**:
`‖(2^(iσ) ‖(shiftSeq γ a)_i‖)_i‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ‖(2^((j+γ)σ) ‖a_j‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q}`.

ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_le_of_le_part.name: ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_le_of_le_partialSums
ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_le_of_le_part.docstring:
**The `ℓ_q` norm of a sequence bounded through partial sums**: for `q ≥ 1`, with the
tolerances `t_k = tolerance f s k`, if
`u_k ≤ (2^(ks) E_{2^k}(f) + 2^(ks) t_k) + (B 2^(-k(r-s)) + K 2^(-k(r-s)) ∑_{j ≤ k} 2^(jr)
(E_{2^j}(f) + t_j))` for every `k`, then `‖u‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ (D + 2 ‖f‖) + (B c + K c (D + 2 ‖f‖))`,
where `D = ‖(2^(ks) E_{2^k}(f))_k‖_{ℓ_q}` and `c = (1 - 2^(-(r-s)))⁻¹`, by Hardy's inequality
for partial sums (`ENNReal.hardy_sum_le`).  Both Bernstein halves, through lifts and through
the near-best approximants in `A^r_∞`, end with this bound.

ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_le_lqNorm_dis.name: ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_le_lqNorm_discretePhiSeq
ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_le_lqNorm_dis.docstring:
**The grid on `ℕ` is part of the grid on `ℤ`**:
`‖(2^(kρθ) φ(2^(-kρ)))_{k ∈ ℕ}‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ‖(2^(-nρθ) φ(2^(nρ)))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q}`.

ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_le_approxNorm.name: ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_le_approxNormDyadic
ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_le_approxNorm.docstring: The `ℓ_q` part of the dyadic quasi-norm is at most the quasi-norm.

ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_kFunctional_r.name: ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_kFunctional_reprCouple_le
ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_kFunctional_r.docstring:
**The `ℓ_q` part of the interpolation norm of `(X, A^r_∞)`**: for `0 ≤ s < r`, `q ≥ 1` and
near-best approximants with the tolerances `tolerance f s`,
`‖(2^(ks) K(2^(-kr), f))_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ (D + 2 ‖f‖) + 3 ‖f‖ c_{r-s} + 2 c_{r-s} (D + 2 ‖f‖)`, where
`D = ‖(2^(ks) E_{2^k}(f))_k‖_{ℓ_q}` and `c_{r-s} = (1 - 2^(-(r-s)))⁻¹`
(`lqNorm_le_of_le_partialSums` with `B = 3 ‖f‖` and `K = 2`).

ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_.name: ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_mul_enorm_le_approxNormDyadic
ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_dyadicWeight_.docstring:
**Blocks controlled by the errors**: for `s ≥ 0`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `M ≥ 1` and a sequence `b_j`
in a normed group with `‖b_j‖ ≤ C ‖f‖` for `j < M` and `‖b_{n+M}‖ ≤ C E_{2^n}(f)` for every `n`,
`‖(2^(js) ‖b_j‖)_j‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ M 2^(Ms) C ‖f‖^dyadic`.  For Littlewood–Paley blocks `b_j = Δ_j f`
this is the bound of the Littlewood–Paley quasi-norm by the approximation norm.

ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_discretePhiSe.name: ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_discretePhiSeq_le_phiFunctional
ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_discretePhiSe.docstring:
**The discrete version of `Φ_{θ,q}` by the functional**: for an increasing `φ`, `θ ≥ 0`
and `ρ > 0`, `(ρ log 2)^(1/q) 2^(-ρθ) ‖(2^(-nρθ) φ(2^(nρ)))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ Φ_{θ,q}(φ)`.

ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_discretePhiSe.name: ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_discretePhiSeq_le_inv_mul_phiFunctional
ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_discretePhiSe.docstring:
**The discrete version of `Φ_{θ,q}` by the functional, solved for the sequence**: for an
increasing `φ`, `θ ≥ 0` and `ρ > 0`,
`‖(2^(-nρθ) φ(2^(nρ)))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ((ρ log 2)^(1/q) 2^(-ρθ))⁻¹ Φ_{θ,q}(φ)`
(`lqNorm_discretePhiSeq_le_phiFunctional`).

ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_discretePhiSe.name: ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_discretePhiSeq_le
ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_discretePhiSe.docstring:
**The grid on `ℤ` by the grid on `ℕ`**: if `φ ≤ M` and `ρθ ≥ 0`, then
`‖(2^(-nρθ) φ(2^(nρ)))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ C_q γ (M + ‖(2^(kρθ) φ(2^(-kρ)))_{k ∈ ℕ}‖_{ℓ_q})` with
`γ = dyadicGeomConst (ρθ) q`, where `C_q` is Mathlib's constant `LpAddConst q` of the
quasi-triangle inequality (`1` for `q ≥ 1`).

ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_approxSeqDyad.name: ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_approxSeqDyadic_add_tolerance_le
ApproximationScheme.lqNorm_approxSeqDyad.docstring:
**The `ℓ_q` norm of the errors plus the tolerances**: for `q ≥ 1`,
`‖(2^(ks) E_{2^k}(f) + 2^(ks) t_k)_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ‖(2^(ks) E_{2^k}(f))_k‖_{ℓ_q} + 2 ‖f‖`, with the
tolerances `t_k = tolerance f s k`.

ApproximationScheme.liftConst.name: ApproximationScheme.liftConst
ApproximationScheme.liftConst.docstring: The constant `2 C 4^β` by which a lifted dyadic block exceeds `2^(kβ)` times its error.

ApproximationScheme.leftApproxCouple.name: ApproximationScheme.leftApproxCouple
ApproximationScheme.leftApproxCouple.docstring:
The **couple `(X, A^s_q)`** of the scheme: the norm `‖f‖` of `X` and the dyadic quasi-norm
`‖f‖ + ‖(2^(ks) E_{2^k}(f))_k‖_{ℓ_q}` of `A^s_q`.  Its interpolation spaces are the
approximation spaces `A^{ηs}_q`, `0 < η < 1` (`memKMethod_approxCouple_zero_iff`).

ApproximationScheme.le_mul_approxError_o.name: ApproximationScheme.le_mul_approxError_of_forall_mem
ApproximationScheme.le_mul_approxError_o.docstring:
To bound a quantity by `C · E_n(f)` with `C < ∞` it suffices to bound it by `C ‖f - a‖`
for every approximant `a`.  The finiteness of `C` is needed: for `C = ∞` and `f` in the
closure of `A n` outside `A n`, every `C ‖f - a‖` is `∞`, so the hypothesis holds for every
`e`, while `C · E_n(f) = ∞ · 0 = 0`.

ApproximationScheme.le_approxError_iff.name: ApproximationScheme.le_approxError_iff
ApproximationScheme.le_approxError_iff.docstring: `r ≤ E_n(f)` iff `r ≤ ‖f - a‖` for every `a ∈ A_n`.

ApproximationScheme.kMethodUpperConst_ne.name: ApproximationScheme.kMethodUpperConst_ne_top
ApproximationScheme.kMethodUpperConst_ne.docstring: The constant `kMethodUpperConst θ ρ q` is finite for `θ, ρ > 0`.

ApproximationScheme.kMethodUpperConst.name: ApproximationScheme.kMethodUpperConst
ApproximationScheme.kMethodUpperConst.docstring:
The constant `(ρ log 2)^(1/q) 2^(ρθ) C_q γ`, with `γ = dyadicGeomConst (ρθ) q`, of the bound
of the continuous K-norm by the discrete one on the grid `2^(-kρ)`.

ApproximationScheme.kMethodNorm_reprCoup.name: ApproximationScheme.kMethodNorm_reprCouple_le_approxNormDyadic
ApproximationScheme.kMethodNorm_reprCoup.docstring:
**The continuous K-norm of `(X, A^r_∞)` by the dyadic quasi-norm of `A^s_q`**: for
`0 < s < r` and `q ≥ 1`, `‖f‖_{K,s/r,q} ≤ reprUpperConst r s q · ‖f‖_{A^s_q}`.

ApproximationScheme.kMethodMeasure_dyadi.name: ApproximationScheme.kMethodMeasure_dyadicPiece
ApproximationScheme.kMethodMeasure_dyadi.docstring: **The measure `dt/t` of a dyadic piece** is `log 2^ρ = ρ log 2`, for `ρ ≥ 0`.

ApproximationScheme.kMethodMeasure_apply.name: ApproximationScheme.kMethodMeasure_apply
ApproximationScheme.kMethodMeasure_apply.docstring: The measure `dt/t` of a measurable set `s` is `∫ 1_{s ∩ (0, ∞)}(t) t⁻¹ dt`.

ApproximationScheme.kMethodMeasure.name: ApproximationScheme.kMethodMeasure
ApproximationScheme.kMethodMeasure.docstring:
The measure `dt/t` on `(0, ∞)`, as a measure on `ℝ`: Lebesgue measure with density `1/t`,
restricted to `t > 0`.

ApproximationScheme.isQuasiNormed_reprCo.name: ApproximationScheme.isQuasiNormed_reprCouple
ApproximationScheme.isQuasiNormed_reprCo.docstring: For `r ≥ 0` the couple `(X, A^r_∞)` is quasi-normed with constant `2 · 2^r`.

ApproximationScheme.isQuasiNormed_leftAp.name: ApproximationScheme.isQuasiNormed_leftApproxCouple
ApproximationScheme.isQuasiNormed_leftAp.docstring:
For `s ≥ 0` and `q ≥ 1` the couple `(X, A^s_q)` is quasi-normed with constant `2 · 2^s`
(`approxNormDyadic_add_le`).

ApproximationScheme.interpSeq_le_of_lift.name: ApproximationScheme.interpSeq_le_of_lift
ApproximationScheme.interpSeq_le_of_lift.docstring:
**The interpolation sequence at one scale from lifted approximants**: if `y_0` and `d_j`
lift near-best approximants `a_k` of `f`, `ι(y_0 + ∑_{j<k} d_j) = a_k`, with `‖y_0‖ ≤ B` and
`‖d_j‖ ≤ K b_j`, then for `r ≠ 0`
`2^(ks) K(2^(-kr), f) ≤ 2^(ks) (E_{2^k}(f) + t_k) + B 2^(-k(r-s)) + K 2^(-k(r-s)) ∑_{j ≤ k} b_j`,
from `K(2^(-kr), f) ≤ ‖f - a_k‖ + 2^(-kr) ‖y_0 + ∑_{j<k} d_j‖`.

ApproximationScheme.interpSeq.name: ApproximationScheme.interpSeq
ApproximationScheme.interpSeq.docstring: The dyadic sequence of the interpolation norm, `2^(kρθ) K(2^(-kρ), f)`.

ApproximationScheme.interpNorm_reprCoupl.name: ApproximationScheme.interpNorm_reprCouple_le_approxNormDyadic
ApproximationScheme.interpNorm_reprCoupl.docstring:
**Bernstein's half of `A^s_q = (X, A^r_∞)_{s/r,q}`** (DeVore–Popov, LNM 1302 (1988)): for
`0 ≤ s < r` and `q ≥ 1`,
`‖f‖ + ‖(2^(ks) K(2^(-kr), f))_k‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ devorePopovConst r s · ‖f‖_{A^s_q}`.  The near-best
approximants themselves lie in `A^r_∞` and take the place of the lifts of the representation
theorem (`enorm_add_le_mul_approxNormDyadic` with `B = 3` and `K = 2`).

ApproximationScheme.injective_neg_natCas.name: ApproximationScheme.injective_neg_natCast
ApproximationScheme.injective_neg_natCas.docstring: The map `k ↦ -k` from `ℕ` to `ℤ` is injective.

ApproximationScheme.injective_natCast_ad.name: ApproximationScheme.injective_natCast_add_one
ApproximationScheme.injective_natCast_ad.docstring: The map `k ↦ k + 1` from `ℕ` to `ℤ` is injective.

ApproximationScheme.indicator_preimage_m.name: ApproximationScheme.indicator_preimage_mul_left_inv
ApproximationScheme.indicator_preimage_m.docstring:
The density of `dt/t` under a dilation: for `c > 0`,
`1_{c⁻¹ s ∩ (0, ∞)}(t) t⁻¹ = c · 1_{s ∩ (0, ∞)}(c t) (c t)⁻¹`.

ApproximationScheme.inclKMethodNorm.name: ApproximationScheme.inclKMethodNorm
ApproximationScheme.inclKMethodNorm.docstring:
The norm of the **continuous K-method**, `‖f‖_{K,θ,q} = Φ_{θ,q}(K(·, f))`, that is
`(∫_0^∞ (t^(-θ) K(t, f))^q dt/t)^(1/q)` for `0 < q < ∞`, the essential supremum of
`t^(-θ) K(t, f)` for `q = ∞`, and `0` for `q = 0` (Bergh–Löfström, Section 3.1).

ApproximationScheme.inclKFunctional_le.name: ApproximationScheme.inclKFunctional_le
ApproximationScheme.inclKFunctional_le.docstring: Every `y ∈ Y` bounds the K-functional: `K(t, f) ≤ ‖f - ι y‖ + t ‖y‖`.

ApproximationScheme.inclKFunctional.name: ApproximationScheme.inclKFunctional
ApproximationScheme.inclKFunctional.docstring: The **Peetre K-functional** `K(t, f) = inf_y (‖f - ι y‖ + t ‖y‖)`.

ApproximationScheme.inclInterpNorm_le_ap.name: ApproximationScheme.inclInterpNorm_le_approxNormDyadic_of_bernstein
ApproximationScheme.inclInterpNorm_le_ap.docstring:
**Bernstein's half of the representation theorem**: for `0 < s < r`,
`‖f‖_{(X,Y)_{s/r,q}} ≤ reprConst C r s · ‖f‖_{A^s_q}` (dyadic quasi-norm).

ApproximationScheme.inclInterpNorm.name: ApproximationScheme.inclInterpNorm
ApproximationScheme.inclInterpNorm.docstring:
The norm of the **real interpolation space** `(X, Y)_{θ,q}` on the dyadic grid
`t = 2^(-kρ)`: `‖f‖ + ‖(2^(kρθ) K(2^(-kρ), f))_k‖_{ℓ_q}`.

ApproximationScheme.hasSum_shiftSeq.name: ApproximationScheme.hasSum_shiftSeq
ApproximationScheme.hasSum_shiftSeq.docstring: **Moving a series up keeps its sum.**

ApproximationScheme.ext.name: ApproximationScheme.ext
ApproximationScheme.ext.docstring: Two schemes with the same sets are equal.

ApproximationScheme.exists_preimage_of_l.name: ApproximationScheme.exists_preimage_of_liftBound
ApproximationScheme.exists_preimage_of_l.docstring:
**A lifting bound of exponent `β` gives `A^β_1 ↪ Y`**: if
`∑_k 2^(kβ) E_{2^k}(f) < ∞`, then `f = ι y` with
`‖y‖ ≤ (3 C + 3 K) (‖f‖ + ∑_k 2^(kβ) E_{2^k}(f))`, `K = liftConst C β`.  For a Bernstein
inequality this is the embedding of the approximation space into the smoothness space.

ApproximationScheme.exists_mem_enorm_sub.name: ApproximationScheme.exists_mem_enorm_sub_lt
ApproximationScheme.exists_mem_enorm_sub.docstring: If the error is below `r`, some approximant is closer than `r`.

ApproximationScheme.exists_mem_enorm_sub.name: ApproximationScheme.exists_mem_enorm_sub_le_add
ApproximationScheme.exists_mem_enorm_sub.docstring:
**Near-best approximants.** For every `ε > 0` there is `a ∈ A n` with
`‖f - a‖ ≤ E_n(f) + ε`.  A best approximant (`ε = 0`) need not exist.

ApproximationScheme.exists_dyadicApprox.name: ApproximationScheme.exists_dyadicApprox
ApproximationScheme.exists_dyadicApprox.docstring: Near-best approximants exist for every choice of positive tolerances.

ApproximationScheme.enorm_sub_apply_le_o.name: ApproximationScheme.enorm_sub_apply_le_of_apply_eq
ApproximationScheme.enorm_sub_apply_le_o.docstring:
**The Lebesgue inequality in extended norms**: if an additive map `P` with
`‖P x‖ ≤ C ‖x‖`, `C ∈ [0, ∞]`, fixes `a`, then `‖f - P f‖ ≤ (1 + C) ‖f - a‖`.

ApproximationScheme.enorm_add_le_mul_app.name: ApproximationScheme.enorm_add_le_mul_approxNormDyadic
ApproximationScheme.enorm_add_le_mul_app.docstring:
**Adding the norm**: if `L ≤ (D + 2 ‖f‖) + (B ‖f‖ c + K c (D + 2 ‖f‖))` with
`D = ‖(2^(ks) E_{2^k}(f))_k‖_{ℓ_q}`, then `‖f‖ + L ≤ (3 + (B + 2 K) c) ‖f‖_{A^s_q}`, since
`‖f‖` and `D` are at most the dyadic quasi-norm `‖f‖_{A^s_q} = ‖f‖ + D`.

ApproximationScheme.eNormPietsch_complex.name: ApproximationScheme.eNormPietsch_complexityCouple
ApproximationScheme.eNormPietsch_complex.docstring:
**Pietsch's form of the complexity couple is Pietsch's quasi-norm**: for an approximation
scheme `A`, `‖f‖^P_{s,q}` of its complexity couple is `‖f‖_{A^s_q}`, termwise since
`E(n, f) = E_n(f)` (`ApproximationScheme.eFunctional_complexityCouple`).

ApproximationScheme.eFunctional_complexi.name: ApproximationScheme.eFunctional_complexityCouple
ApproximationScheme.eFunctional_complexi.docstring:
**The E-functional of the complexity couple is the error of best approximation**:
`E(n, f) = E_n(f)` for every `n ∈ ℕ`.

ApproximationScheme.dyadicWeight_mul_kFu.name: ApproximationScheme.dyadicWeight_mul_kFunctional_reprCouple_le
ApproximationScheme.dyadicWeight_mul_kFu.docstring:
**One term of the interpolation norm of `(X, A^r_∞)` by near-best approximants**: for `s ≥ 0`,
`r ≠ 0` and near-best approximants `a_k` with the tolerances `t_k = tolerance f s k`,
`2^(ks) K(2^(-kr), f) ≤ (2^(ks) E_{2^k}(f) + 2^(ks) t_k) + 3 ‖f‖ 2^(-k(r-s))
+ 2 · 2^(-k(r-s)) ∑_{j ≤ k} 2^(jr) (E_{2^j}(f) + t_j)`, from
`K(2^(-kr), f) ≤ ‖f - a_k‖ + 2^(-kr) ‖a_k‖_{A^r_∞}`.

ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq_zero.name: ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq_zero
ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq_zero.docstring: The term of `(2^(-nρθ) φ(2^(nρ)))_{n ∈ ℤ}` with `n = 0` is `φ(1)`.

ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq_neg_n.name: ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq_neg_natCast
ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq_neg_n.docstring: The terms of `(2^(-nρθ) φ(2^(nρ)))_{n ∈ ℤ}` with `n = -k ≤ 0` are `2^(kρθ) φ(2^(-kρ))`.

ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq_natCa.name: ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq_natCast_add_one_le
ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq_natCa.docstring:
If `φ ≤ M`, the terms of `(2^(-nρθ) φ(2^(nρ)))_{n ∈ ℤ}` with `n = k + 1 > 0` are at most
`2^(-kρθ) M`, for `ρθ ≥ 0`.

ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq_le_ph.name: ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq_le_phiIntegrand
ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq_le_ph.docstring:
**Lower bound on a piece**: for an increasing `φ`, `θ ≥ 0` and
`t ∈ [2^(nρ), 2^((n+1)ρ))`, `2^(-ρθ) · 2^(-nρθ) φ(2^(nρ)) ≤ t^(-θ) φ(t)`.

ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq_le_ex.name: ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq_le_extend
ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq_le_ex.docstring:
**Splitting the grid on `ℤ`**: if `φ ≤ M` and `ρθ ≥ 0`, the sequence
`(2^(-nρθ) φ(2^(nρ)))_{n ∈ ℤ}` is at most the sequence `2^(kρθ) φ(2^(-kρ))` placed at
`n = -k ≤ 0` plus the sequence `2^(-kρθ) M` placed at `n = k + 1 > 0`.

ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq.name: ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq
ApproximationScheme.discretePhiSeq.docstring:
The sequence `(2^(-nρθ) φ(2^(nρ)))_{n ∈ ℤ}`: the function `φ` sampled on the grid
`t = 2^(nρ)` with the weight `t^(-θ)`.  For `ρ = 1` its `ℓ_q` norm is the formula of
`EQuasinorm.discretePhiFunctional θ q (n ↦ φ(2^n))` in the project *MultilinearInterpolation*.

ApproximationScheme.discreteKMethodNorm_.name: ApproximationScheme.discreteKMethodNorm_reprCouple_le_approxNormDyadic
ApproximationScheme.discreteKMethodNorm_.docstring:
**The discrete K-norm of `(X, A^r_∞)` on the grid `t = 2^n` by the dyadic quasi-norm of
`A^s_q`**: for `0 < s < r` and `q ≥ 1`,
`‖(2^(-ns/r) K(2^n, f))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q} ≤ ((log 2)^(1/q) 2^(-s/r))⁻¹ reprUpperConst r s q
‖f‖_{A^s_q}` (`InterpCouple.discreteKMethodNorm_le_mul_kMethodNorm`).

ApproximationScheme.devorePopovConst_ne_.name: ApproximationScheme.devorePopovConst_ne_top
ApproximationScheme.devorePopovConst_ne_.docstring: The constant `devorePopovConst r s` is finite for `s < r`.

ApproximationScheme.devorePopovConst.name: ApproximationScheme.devorePopovConst
ApproximationScheme.devorePopovConst.docstring:
The constant `3 + 7 (1 - 2^(-(r-s)))⁻¹` of the proof here of Bernstein's half of the theorem
`A^s_q = (X, A^r_∞)_{s/r,q}` of DeVore–Popov, LNM 1302 (1988).

ApproximationScheme.complexityCouple.name: ApproximationScheme.complexityCouple
ApproximationScheme.complexityCouple.docstring:
The **complexity couple** of an approximation scheme: the norm of `X` and the complexity
`min {n : b ∈ A n}`.

ApproximationScheme.comap.name: ApproximationScheme.comap
ApproximationScheme.comap.docstring:
The **preimage of a scheme** under an injective linear map `ι : Y → X`: the sets
`ι ⁻¹' A n`.  Injectivity is what makes `ι ⁻¹' {0} = {0}`.  This is the scheme on a smaller
space `Y` (for instance `L_r ⊆ L_p`) induced by a scheme on `X`.

ApproximationScheme.approxSeqDyadic_le_l.name: ApproximationScheme.approxSeqDyadic_le_lqNorm
ApproximationScheme.approxSeqDyadic_le_l.docstring:
Each term `2^(ks) E_{2^k}(f)` is at most the `ℓ_q` norm of the dyadic sequence, for every
`q ≠ 0`.

ApproximationScheme.approxSeqDyadic_eq_m.name: ApproximationScheme.approxSeqDyadic_eq_mul
ApproximationScheme.approxSeqDyadic_eq_m.docstring: Changing the smoothness index multiplies the dyadic terms by `2^(k(t-s))`.

ApproximationScheme.approxSeqDyadic_add_.name: ApproximationScheme.approxSeqDyadic_add_le_succ
ApproximationScheme.approxSeqDyadic_add_.docstring: The dyadic sequence of `f + g` at `k + 1` is controlled by those of `f` and `g` at `k`.

ApproximationScheme.approxNorm_le_approx.name: ApproximationScheme.approxNorm_le_approxNormDyadic'
ApproximationScheme.approxNorm_le_approx.docstring:
**Pietsch's quasi-norm is dominated by the dyadic one**, for every `q`: for `s ≥ 0`,
`‖f‖_{A^s_q} ≤ C_q 2^s (‖f‖ + ‖(2^(ks) E_{2^k}(f))_k‖_q)` with Mathlib's constant
`C_q = LpAddConst q` of the quasi-triangle inequality (`1` for `q ≥ 1`). This is the comparison
of Pietsch's weights with the dyadic ones for the decreasing sequence `E_n(f)`
(`ENNReal.lqNorm_pow_mul_le_dyadic`), whose first term is `E_0(f) = ‖f‖`.

ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_top.name: ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_top_le_of_mem
ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_top.docstring:
**The quasi-norm of `A^s_∞` of an approximant**: for `a ∈ A_{2^k}`, `E_{2^j}(a) = 0` for
`j ≥ k`, hence `‖a‖_{A^s_∞} ≤ ‖a‖ + ∑_{j<k} 2^(js) E_{2^j}(a)`.

ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_top.name: ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_top_le_of_jackson
ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_top.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality gives `ι(Y) ⊆ A^r_∞`**:
`‖ι y‖ + sup_k 2^(kr) E_{2^k}(ι y) ≤ (‖ι‖ + C) ‖y‖`.

ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.name: ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_of_tail
ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.docstring:
**The transfer estimate.**  Let `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `α ≤ s`, `t_k = tolerance f s k` and
`g_k = 2^(kα) (E_{2^k}(f) + t_k)`.  If an element `y` of `Y` and a scheme `B` in `Y` satisfy
`‖y‖ ≤ c (2 ‖f‖ + ‖f‖) + K ∑_k g_k` and `E^B_{2^k}(y) ≤ K ∑_{i ≥ 0} g_{k+i}` for every `k`, then
`‖y‖_{B^{s-α}_q} ≤ (3 c + 3 K (1 - 2^(-(s-α)))⁻¹ + 2 K) ‖f‖_{A^s_q}` in the dyadic
quasi-norms.  The constant is finite for `α < s` (`ENNReal.one_sub_two_rpow_neg_inv_ne_top`),
the case of both transfer theorems.  Hardy's inequality for tails (`ENNReal.hardy_tail_le`)
turns the tail bound into the bound of the `ℓ_q` part.  The Nikolskii transfer theorem and the
trace transfer theorem (`TraceBound.approxNormDyadic_limitTrace_le`) both end with this estimate.

ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.name: ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_of_lt
ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.docstring:
**Trading smoothness for the fine index**: for `t < s` and `1 ≤ q, r ≤ ∞`,
`‖f‖_{A^t_r} ≤ (1 - 2^(-(s-t)))⁻¹ ‖f‖_{A^s_q}` in the dyadic form.

ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.name: ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_of_hasSum
ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.docstring:
**A block decomposition controls the approximation norm**: for `s > 0`,
`‖f‖^dyadic ≤ 2 (1 - 2^(-s))⁻¹ ‖(2^(ks) ‖g_k‖)_k‖_q`.

ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.name: ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_kMethodNorm_reprCouple
ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.docstring:
**The dyadic quasi-norm of `A^s_q` by the continuous K-norm of `(X, A^r_∞)`**: for `s ≥ 0`,
`r > 0` and `q ≥ 1`, `‖f‖_{A^s_q} ≤ reprLowerConst r s q · ‖f‖_{K,s/r,q}`.

ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.name: ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_interpNorm_reprCouple
ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.docstring:
**Jackson's half of `A^s_q = (X, A^r_∞)_{s/r,q}`**: for `s ≥ 0`, `r ≠ 0` and `q ≥ 1`,
`‖f‖_{A^s_q} ≤ 2 · 2^s (‖f‖ + ‖(2^(ks) K(2^(-kr), f))_k‖_{ℓ_q})`, the dyadic quasi-norm against
the norm of the couple `(X, A^r_∞)` on the grid `t = 2^(-kr)`.

ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.name: ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_inclInterpNorm_of_jackson
ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.docstring:
**Jackson's half of the representation theorem**:
`‖f‖_{A^s_q} ≤ max(1, C) ‖f‖_{(X,Y)_{s/r,q}}` (dyadic quasi-norm), for `r ≠ 0`.

ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.name: ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_discreteKMethodNorm_reprCouple
ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.docstring:
**The dyadic quasi-norm of `A^s_q` by the discrete K-norm of `(X, A^r_∞)` on the grid
`t = 2^n`**: for `s ≥ 0`, `r > 0` and `q ≥ 1`,
`‖f‖_{A^s_q} ≤ reprLowerConst r s q (log 2)^(1/q) 2^(s/r) ‖(2^(-ns/r) K(2^n, f))_{n ∈ ℤ}‖_{ℓ_q}`
(`InterpCouple.kMethodNorm_le_mul_discreteKMethodNorm`).

ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.name: ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_approxNorm'
ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_.docstring:
**The dyadic quasi-norm is dominated by Pietsch's**, for every `q ≠ 0`: for `s ≥ 0`,
`‖f‖ + ‖(2^(ks) E_{2^k}(f))_k‖_q ≤ 4 C_q² 2^s ‖f‖_{A^s_q}` with Mathlib's constant
`C_q = LpAddConst q` of the quasi-triangle inequality (`1` for `q ≥ 1`). This is the comparison
of the dyadic weights with Pietsch's for the decreasing sequence `E_n(f)`
(`ENNReal.dyadic_le_lqNorm_pow_mul`), whose first term is `E_0(f) = ‖f‖`.

ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_add.name: ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_add_le
ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_add.docstring:
**Quasi-triangle inequality** for the dyadic quasi-norm, with constant `2 · 2^s`, for
`1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and `s ≥ 0`; for `s < 1` this constant is smaller than the constant `2 + 2^s` of
`ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic_add_le'` at `q ≥ 1`.

ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic.name: ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic
ApproximationScheme.approxNormDyadic.docstring:
The **dyadic quasi-norm** `‖f‖ + ‖(2^(ks) E_{2^k}(f))_k‖_{ℓ_q}`, equivalent to Pietsch's
quasi-norm for `s ≥ 0`.

ApproximationScheme.approxNorm.name: ApproximationScheme.approxNorm
ApproximationScheme.approxNorm.docstring: **Pietsch's quasi-norm** of `A^s_q`: the `ℓ_q` norm of `((n + 1)^(s - 1/q) E_n(f))_n`.

ApproximationScheme.approxError_smul.name: ApproximationScheme.approxError_smul
ApproximationScheme.approxError_smul.docstring: **Homogeneity**: `E_n(c f) = |c| E_n(f)`, because `c • A n = A n` for `c ≠ 0`.

ApproximationScheme.approxError_pow_le_d.name: ApproximationScheme.approxError_pow_le_dyadicWeight_mul
ApproximationScheme.approxError_pow_le_d.docstring: One term of the dyadic quasi-norm of `A^r_∞`: `E_{2^k}(b) ≤ 2^(-kr) ‖b‖_{A^r_∞}`.

ApproximationScheme.approxError_pow_le.name: ApproximationScheme.approxError_pow_le
ApproximationScheme.approxError_pow_le.docstring:
A bound on the dyadic quasi-norm gives the decay `E_{2^k}(f) ≤ 2^(-ks) ‖f‖^dyadic`, for every
`q ≠ 0`.

ApproximationScheme.approxError_ne_top.name: ApproximationScheme.approxError_ne_top
ApproximationScheme.approxError_ne_top.docstring: The errors are finite, since `A n` is nonempty.

ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_of_me.name: ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_of_mem
ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_of_me.docstring: Every approximant gives an upper bound: `E_n(f) ≤ ‖f - a‖` for `a ∈ A_n`.

ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_of_de.name: ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_of_dense
ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_of_de.docstring:
**Bounds by a modulus pass from a dense set to all of `X`**: if `ω` is subadditive with
`ω(f) ≤ C₀ ‖f‖` and `E_n(g) ≤ C ω(g)` for all `g` in a dense set, then `E_n(f) ≤ C ω(f)` for every
`f`, since both sides move by at most a multiple of `‖f - g‖`
(`ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_approxError_add_enorm`).

ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_kFunc.name: ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_kFunctional_reprCouple
ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_kFunc.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality for the couple `(X, A^r_∞)`**: `E_{2^(k+1)}(f) ≤ K(2^(-kr), f)`, since
`E_{2^(k+1)}(f) ≤ E_{2^k}(f - b) + E_{2^k}(b) ≤ ‖f - b‖ + 2^(-kr) ‖b‖_{A^r_∞}` for every `b`.

ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_inclK.name: ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_inclKFunctional_of_jackson
ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_inclK.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality controls the errors by the K-functional**:
`E_n(f) ≤ max(1, C) K(n^(-r), f)` for `n ≥ 1`.

ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_enorm.name: ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_enorm
ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_enorm.docstring: The error never exceeds the norm, since `0` is an approximant.

ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_appro.name: ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_approxError_add_enorm
ApproximationScheme.approxError_le_appro.docstring: `E_n(f) ≤ E_n(g) + ‖f - g‖`: the error is `1`-Lipschitz in `f`.

ApproximationScheme.approxError_anti.name: ApproximationScheme.approxError_anti
ApproximationScheme.approxError_anti.docstring: The error decreases as the complexity grows.

ApproximationScheme.approxError_add_le_p.name: ApproximationScheme.approxError_add_le_pow_succ
ApproximationScheme.approxError_add_le_p.docstring: The dyadic form of subadditivity: `E_{2^(k+1)}(f + g) ≤ E_{2^k}(f) + E_{2^k}(g)`.

ApproximationScheme.approxError_add_le_o.name: ApproximationScheme.approxError_add_le_of_add_mem
ApproximationScheme.approxError_add_le_o.docstring:
**Subadditivity** for any three complexities with `A m + A n ⊆ A k`:
`E_k(f + g) ≤ E_m(f) + E_n(g)`.

ApproximationScheme.approxError.name: ApproximationScheme.approxError
ApproximationScheme.approxError.docstring:
The **error of best approximation** `E_n(f) = inf_{a ∈ A n} ‖f - a‖ ∈ [0, ∞]` of `f` from
the approximants of complexity `n`, the extended distance from `f` to `A n`.

ApproximationScheme.approxCouple.name: ApproximationScheme.approxCouple
ApproximationScheme.approxCouple.docstring:
The **couple `(A^{s₀}_{q₀}, A^{s₁}_{q₁})`** of two approximation spaces, with their dyadic
quasi-norms.

ApproximationScheme.ae_pos_kMethodMeasur.name: ApproximationScheme.ae_pos_kMethodMeasure
ApproximationScheme.ae_pos_kMethodMeasur.docstring:
Almost every point for `dt/t` is positive, since `dt/t` is a restriction to `(0, ∞)`
(Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.ae_restrict_mem`).

ApproximationScheme.ae_mem_iUnion_dyadic.name: ApproximationScheme.ae_mem_iUnion_dyadicPiece
ApproximationScheme.ae_mem_iUnion_dyadic.docstring: For `ρ > 0`, almost every point for `dt/t` lies in a dyadic piece.

ApproximationScheme.add_mem_pow_succ.name: ApproximationScheme.add_mem_pow_succ
ApproximationScheme.add_mem_pow_succ.docstring: Two approximants of complexity `2 ^ k` add up to one of complexity `2 ^ (k + 1)`.

ApproximationScheme.add_mem.name: ApproximationScheme.add_mem
ApproximationScheme.add_mem.docstring: `a + b ∈ A_{m+n}` for `a ∈ A_m` and `b ∈ A_n`.

ApproximationScheme.SmoothnessSpace.exis.name: ApproximationScheme.SmoothnessSpace.exists_eq_of_lt
ApproximationScheme.SmoothnessSpace.exis.docstring:
**`A^s_q ⊆ W` for `s > r`**: more smoothness in the approximation sense than the order of
`W` gives an element of `W`, for every fine index.

ApproximationScheme.SmoothnessSpace.name: ApproximationScheme.SmoothnessSpace
ApproximationScheme.SmoothnessSpace.docstring:
A **smoothness space** of order `r` for the scheme `A`: a normed space `F` with an injective
bounded linear map `ι : F → E` satisfying Jackson's and Bernstein's inequalities of order `r`.
Sobolev spaces inside `L_p` are the motivating example.

ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.ten.name: ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.tendsto_of_dense
ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.ten.docstring: If `⋃ A n` is dense, the projections converge: `P n f → f` for every `f`.

ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.sum.name: ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.sum_block
ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.sum.docstring: The blocks telescope: `∑_{i < N} Δ_{k+i} f = P (2^(k+N)) f - P (2^k) f`.

ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.ofM.name: ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.ofMonotone_two_pow
ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.ofM.docstring: The projection of complexity `2^k` of `ProjectionScheme.ofMonotone` is `Q_k`.

ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.ofM.name: ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.ofMonotone
ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.ofM.docstring:
**The projection scheme of an increasing sequence of subspaces**: bounded linear projections
`Q_k` onto `V_k`, with `Q_k a = a` for `a ∈ V_k` and `‖Q_k‖ ≤ B`, give a projection scheme for the
dyadic scheme `ofMonotoneSubmodules V`, with `P_0 = 0` and `P_n = Q_⌊log₂ n⌋` for `n ≥ 1`.

ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.mem.name: ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.memApprox_iff_blockNorm_lt_top_of_dense
ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.mem.docstring:
**Characterisation of `A^s_q` by dyadic blocks**: for a projection scheme with dense
`⋃ A n`, `s > 0` and `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞`, `f ∈ A^s_q` iff
`‖P 1 f‖ + ‖(2^(ks) ‖Δ_k f‖)_k‖_q < ∞`.

ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.eno.name: ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.enorm_sub_le_tsum_block
ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.eno.docstring:
If `P n f → f`, the error of `P (2^k)` is the norm of the tail of the blocks:
`‖f - P (2^k) f‖ ≤ ∑_{i ≥ 0} ‖Δ_{k+i} f‖`.

ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.eno.name: ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.enorm_sub_le_approxError
ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.eno.docstring: **The Lebesgue inequality**: `‖f - P n f‖ ≤ (1 + M) E_n(f)`.

ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.eno.name: ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.enorm_block_le
ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.eno.docstring: A block is controlled by the error: `‖Δ_k f‖ ≤ 2 (1 + M) E_{2^k}(f)`.

ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.blo.name: ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.blockNorm_le_approxNormDyadic
ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.blo.docstring:
**The blocks are controlled by the approximation norm**:
`‖P 1 f‖ + ‖(2^(ks) ‖Δ_k f‖)_k‖_q ≤ (M + 2 (1 + M)) ‖f‖^dyadic`.

ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.blo.name: ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.block
ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.blo.docstring: The **dyadic block** `Δ_k f = P (2^(k+1)) f - P (2^k) f`.

ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.app.name: ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.approxNormDyadic_le_blockNorm
ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.app.docstring:
**The approximation norm is controlled by the blocks**: for `s > 0`, `1 ≤ q ≤ ∞` and
`P n f → f`, `‖f‖^dyadic ≤ (1 + 2 C_s) (‖P 1 f‖ + ‖(2^(ks) ‖Δ_k f‖)_k‖_q)` with
`C_s = (1 - 2^(-s))⁻¹`.

ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.app.name: ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.approxError_le_enorm_sub
ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.app.docstring: `P n f` is an approximant, so `E_n(f) ≤ ‖f - P n f‖`.

ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.name: ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme
ApproximationScheme.ProjectionScheme.docstring:
A **projection scheme**: bounded linear projections `P n` of `X` onto `A n`, uniformly
bounded by `M`.

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.ofExists.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.ofExists
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.ofExists.docstring:
A modulus compatible with the scheme from **existence statements** for the two constants:
the modulus with its subadditivity and the bound `ω(f) ≤ C₀ ‖f‖`, a Jackson inequality
`E_{2^k}(f) ≤ C_J ω(f, 2^(-k))` for `k ≥ k₀` with some finite `C_J`, and an inverse inequality
`ω(a, 2^(-k)) ≤ C_B 2^(-(k-j)θ) ‖a‖`, `a ∈ A_{2^j}`, with some finite `C_B`.  The constants
`C_J`, `C_B` are chosen with `Exists.choose`.

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.modulus_.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.modulus_sum_le
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.modulus_.docstring: The modulus is subadditive on finite sums (Mathlib's `Finset.le_sum_of_subadditive`).

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.modulus_.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.modulus_le_of_dyadicApprox
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.modulus_.docstring:
**The modulus at one scale from near-best approximants**: for near-best approximants
`a_k ∈ A_{2^k}` of `f` with an antitone tolerance `t` and `t_0 = ‖f‖`, the telescoping
`f = (f - a_k) + a_0 + ∑_{j<k} (a_{j+1} - a_j)` and the inverse inequality give
`ω(f, 2^(-k)) ≤ C₀ (E_{2^k}(f) + t_k) + 3 C_B 2^(-kθ) ‖f‖
  + ∑_{j<k} 2 C_B 4^θ 2^(-(k-j)θ) (E_{2^j}(f) + t_j)`.

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.modNorm_.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.modNorm_le_approxNormDyadic
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.modNorm_.docstring:
**The inverse direction**: for `0 ≤ s < θ`, `‖f‖^ω_{s,q} ≤ K ‖f‖_{A^s_q}` with
`K = M.inverseConst s`.

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.modCoupl.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.modCouple
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.modCoupl.docstring:
The **couple of two classical spaces** of a modulus `ω` compatible with the scheme: the
classical quasi-norms `‖f‖ + ‖(2^(ks_i) ω(f, 2^(-k)))_k‖_{ℓ_{q_i}}`, `i = 0, 1`.

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.memKMeth.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.memKMethod_modCouple_iff_memApprox
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.memKMeth.docstring:
**Classical spaces interpolate to approximation spaces**: for a modulus compatible with the
scheme of inverse order `θ`, `0 < s₀ < s₁ < θ`, `0 < η < 1` and `1 ≤ q₀, q₁, q ≤ ∞`, the real
interpolation space of the couple of the classical spaces of smoothness `s₀` and `s₁` is
`A^{(1-η)s₀+ηs₁}_q`.  The classical quasi-norms are equivalent to the dyadic quasi-norms
(`approxNormDyadic_le_modNorm`, `modNorm_le_approxNormDyadic`), so the sandwich principle
applies (`memKMethod_iff_memApprox_of_two_sandwiches`).

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.memKMeth.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.memKMethod_modCouple_iff
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.memKMeth.docstring:
**The interpolation spaces of two classical spaces**: for a modulus compatible with the
scheme of inverse order `θ`, `0 < s₀ < s₁ < θ`, `0 < η < 1` and `1 ≤ q₀, q₁, q ≤ ∞`, `f` lies in
the real interpolation space of the couple of the classical spaces of smoothness `s₀` and `s₁`
iff `‖f‖ + ‖(2^(ks) ω(f, 2^(-k)))_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞` with `s = (1-η)s₀ + ηs₁`.

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.memKMeth.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.memKMethod_leftModCouple_iff_memApprox
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.memKMeth.docstring:
**`X` and a classical space interpolate to approximation spaces**: for a modulus compatible
with the scheme of inverse order `θ`, `0 < s₁ < θ`, `0 < η < 1` and `1 ≤ q₁, q ≤ ∞`, the real
interpolation space of the couple of `X` and the classical space of smoothness `s₁` is
`A^{ηs₁}_q` (`memKMethod_iff_memApprox_of_sandwich`).

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.memKMeth.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.memKMethod_leftModCouple_iff
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.memKMeth.docstring:
**The interpolation spaces of `X` and a classical space**: for a modulus compatible with the
scheme of inverse order `θ`, `0 < s₁ < θ`, `0 < η < 1` and `1 ≤ q₁, q ≤ ∞`, `f` lies in the real
interpolation space of the couple of `X` and the classical space of smoothness `s₁` iff
`‖f‖ + ‖(2^(kηs₁) ω(f, 2^(-k)))_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`.

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.leftModC.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.leftModCouple
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.leftModC.docstring:
The **couple of `X` and a classical space** of a modulus `ω` compatible with the scheme: the
norm `‖f‖` of `X` and the classical quasi-norm `‖f‖ + ‖(2^(ks₁) ω(f, 2^(-k)))_k‖_{ℓ_{q₁}}`.

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.inverseC.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.inverseConst_ne_top
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.inverseC.docstring: The constant of the inverse direction is finite for `s < θ`.

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.inverseC.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.inverseConst
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.inverseC.docstring:
The constant of the inverse direction,
`1 + 3 C₀ + C_B (3 + 6 · 4^θ) (1 - 2^(-(θ-s)))⁻¹`.

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.dyadicWe.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.dyadicWeight_mul_modulus_le_of_dyadicApprox
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.dyadicWe.docstring:
**The weighted modulus at one scale**: with `E_k = 2^(ks) (E_{2^k}(f) + t_k)` and
`α = θ - s`, `ModulusData.modulus_le_of_dyadicApprox` multiplied by `2^(ks)` reads
`2^(ks) ω(f, 2^(-k)) ≤ C₀ E_k + 3 C_B ‖f‖ 2^(-kα) + 2 C_B 4^θ 2^(-kα) ∑_{j ≤ k} 2^(jα) E_j`.

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.directCo.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.directConst_ne_top
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.directCo.docstring: The constant of Jackson's direction is finite.

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.directCo.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.directConst
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.directCo.docstring: The constant of Jackson's direction, `1 + ∑_{k<k₀} 2^(ks) + C_J`.

ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.name: ApproximationScheme.ModulusData
ApproximationScheme.ModulusData.docstring:
A **modulus of smoothness compatible with the scheme `A`**, with inverse order `θ`: the
modulus at the dyadic scales `modulus f k = ω(f, 2^(-k))`, subadditive and bounded by `C₀ ‖f‖`, with a
Jackson inequality `E_{2^k}(f) ≤ C_J ω(f, 2^(-k))` for `k ≥ k₀` and an inverse inequality
`ω(a, 2^(-k)) ≤ C_B 2^(-(k-j)θ) ‖a‖` for `a ∈ A_{2^j}`.

ApproximationScheme.MemInterp.name: ApproximationScheme.MemInterp
ApproximationScheme.MemInterp.docstring:
`f` belongs to the **real interpolation space** `(X, Y)_{θ,q}` of the discrete K-method on
the grid `t = 2^(-kρ)`: `‖f‖ + ‖(2^(kρθ) K(2^(-kρ), f))_k‖_{ℓ_q} < ∞`.

ApproximationScheme.MemInclKMethod.name: ApproximationScheme.MemInclKMethod
ApproximationScheme.MemInclKMethod.docstring:
`f` belongs to the **real interpolation space** `(X, Y)_{θ,q}` of the continuous
K-method: `‖f‖_{K,θ,q} < ∞`.

ApproximationScheme.MemApprox.of_lt.name: ApproximationScheme.MemApprox.of_lt
ApproximationScheme.MemApprox.of_lt.docstring: `A^s_q ⊆ A^t_r` for `0 ≤ t < s` and all `1 ≤ q, r ≤ ∞`.

ApproximationScheme.MemApprox.lqNorm_one.name: ApproximationScheme.MemApprox.lqNorm_one_lt_top
ApproximationScheme.MemApprox.lqNorm_one.docstring:
For `0 ≤ t < s`, the dyadic series `∑ₖ 2^(kt) E_{2^k}(f)` converges for `f ∈ A^s_q`.  This
is the form in which telescoping arguments use membership.

ApproximationScheme.LiftBound.name: ApproximationScheme.LiftBound
ApproximationScheme.LiftBound.docstring:
A **lifting bound** of exponent `β` and constant `C` for `ι : Y → X`: every approximant
`a ∈ A n`, `n ≥ 1`, is `ι y` for some `y` with `‖y‖ ≤ C n^β ‖a‖`.  This is Bernstein's
inequality when `Y` is a smoothness space and Nikolskii's inequality when `Y ⊆ X` is a
smaller Lebesgue space.

ApproximationScheme.JacksonBound.name: ApproximationScheme.JacksonBound
ApproximationScheme.JacksonBound.docstring:
**Jackson's inequality** of order `r` with constant `C`: `E_n(ι y) ≤ C n^(-r) ‖y‖` for all
`y ∈ Y` and `n ≥ 1`, stated for the real number `E_n(ι y)` (the error is finite).

ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.tendsto.name: ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.tendsto
ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.tendsto.docstring: The approximants converge to `f` when the dyadic errors and the tolerances tend to `0`.

ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.sub_mem.name: ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.sub_mem
ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.sub_mem.docstring: Consecutive approximants differ by an approximant of complexity `2^(k+2)`.

ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.exists_.name: ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.exists_preimage_of_tsum_ne_top
ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.exists_.docstring:
**The telescoping lift.**  If `∑_k 2^(kβ) (E_{2^k}(f) + t_k) < ∞`, then `f = ι y` for some
`y ∈ Y` with

* `‖y‖ ≤ C (2 ‖f‖ + t_0) + K ∑_k 2^(kβ) (E_{2^k}(f) + t_k)`, and
* for every `k` some `z` with `ι z ∈ A (2^k)` and
  `‖y - z‖ ≤ K ∑_{i ≥ 0} 2^((k+i)β) (E_{2^(k+i)}(f) + t_{k+i})`,

where `K = liftConst C β`.

ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.exists_.name: ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.exists_lift_partial
ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.exists_.docstring:
**The lifted partial sums.**  There are `y_0` and `d_k` in `Y` whose partial sums
`z_n = y_0 + ∑_{j<n} d_j` lift the approximants, `ι z_n = a_n`, with
`‖y_0‖ ≤ C (2 ‖f‖ + t_0)` and `‖d_k‖ ≤ K 2^(kβ) (E_{2^k}(f) + t_k)`, `K = liftConst C β`.
No completeness of `Y` is needed.

ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.exists_.name: ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.exists_lift_of_liftBound
ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.exists_.docstring:
**Lifting the blocks**: `a_0 = ι y_0` and `a_{k+1} - a_k = ι d_k` with
`‖y_0‖ ≤ C ‖a_0‖` and `‖d_k‖ ≤ C 2^((k+2)β) ‖a_{k+1} - a_k‖`.

ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.enorm_z.name: ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.enorm_zero_le
ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.enorm_z.docstring: The first approximant is bounded: `‖a_0‖ ≤ 2 ‖f‖ + t_0`.

ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.enorm_s.name: ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.enorm_sub_succ_le
ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.enorm_s.docstring: The blocks are controlled by the errors: `‖a_{k+1} - a_k‖ ≤ 2 (E_{2^k}(f) + t_k)`.

ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.enorm_l.name: ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.enorm_le
ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.enorm_l.docstring: A near-best approximant of complexity `2^k` has norm at most `2 ‖f‖ + t_k`.

ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.approxN.name: ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.approxNormDyadic_top_le
ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.approxN.docstring:
**The quasi-norm of `A^r_∞` of a near-best approximant**: for decreasing tolerances with
`t_0 ≤ ‖f‖`, `‖a_k‖_{A^r_∞} ≤ 3 ‖f‖ + 2 ∑_{j ≤ k} 2^(jr) (E_{2^j}(f) + t_j)`.

ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.approxE.name: ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.approxError_le
ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.approxE.docstring:
**The errors of a near-best approximant**: for decreasing tolerances and `j ≤ k`,
`E_{2^j}(a_k) ≤ E_{2^j}(f) + ‖f - a_k‖ ≤ 2 (E_{2^j}(f) + t_j)`.

ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.name: ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox
ApproximationScheme.DyadicApprox.docstring:
A **dyadic sequence of near-best approximants** of `f` with tolerances `t`:
`a k ∈ A (2^k)` and `‖f - a k‖ ≤ E_{2^k}(f) + t k`.
